live.ecclesiasticus|24:12: And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|24:13: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:14: I was exalted like a palm tree in En-gaddi, and as a rose plant in Jericho, as a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, and grew up as a plane tree by the water.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:15: I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and aspalathus, and I yielded a pleasant odour like the best myrrh, as galbanum, and onyx, and sweet storax, and as the fume of frankincense in the tabernacle.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:16: As the turpentine tree I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honour and grace.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:17: As the vine brought I forth pleasant savour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:18: I am the mother of fair love, and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope: I therefore, being eternal, am given to all my children which are named of him.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:19: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:20: For my memorial is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than the honeycomb.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:21: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:22: He that obeyeth me shall never be confounded, and they that work by me shall not do amiss.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:23: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:24: Faint not to be strong in Yahuah (God); that he may confirm you, cleave to him: for Yahuah (God) Almighty is Yahuah (God) alone, and beside him there is no other Saviour.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:25: He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:26: He makes the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:27: He makes the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:28: The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:29: For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:30: I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:31: I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:32: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:33: I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.
live.ecclesiasticus|24:34: Behold that I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:1: In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before Yahuah (God) and men: the unity of brothers, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:2: Three sorts of men my soul hates, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:3: If you have gathered nothing in your youth, how can you find any thing in your age?
live.ecclesiasticus|25:4: O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel!
live.ecclesiasticus|25:5: O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honour.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:6: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of Yahuah (God) is their glory.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:7: There be nine things which I have judged in my heart to be happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: A man that has joy of his children; and he that lives to see the fall of his enemy:
live.ecclesiasticus|25:8: Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served a man more unworthy than himself:
live.ecclesiasticus|25:9: Well is him that has found prudence, and he that speaks in the ears of them that will hear:
live.ecclesiasticus|25:10: O how great is he that finds wisdom! yet is there none above him that fears Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|25:11: But the love of Yahuah (God) passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, to which shall he be likened?
live.ecclesiasticus|25:12: The fear of Yahuah (God) is the beginning of his love: and faith is the beginning of cleaving to him.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:13: Give me any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman:
live.ecclesiasticus|25:14: And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate me: and any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:15: There is no head above the head of a serpent; and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:16: I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:17: The wickedness of a woman changeth her face, and darkeneth her countenance like sackcloth.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:18: Her husband shall sit among his neighbours; and when he heareth it shall sigh bitterly.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:19: All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall upon her.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:20: As the climbing up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:21: Stumble not at the beauty of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:22: A woman, if she maintain her husband, is full of anger, impudence, and much reproach.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:23: A wicked woman abateth the courage, makes an heavy countenance and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distress makes weak hands and feeble knees.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:24: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:25: Give the water no passage; neither a wicked woman liberty to gad abroad.
live.ecclesiasticus|25:26: If she go not as you would have her, cut her off from your flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:1: Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:2: A virtuous woman rejoices her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:3: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|26:4: Whether a man be rich or poor, if he have a good heart toward Yahuah (God), he shall at all times rejoice with a cheerful countenance.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:5: There be three things that my heart fears; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:6: But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:7: An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that has hold of her is as though he held a scorpion.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:8: A drunken woman and a gadder abroad causeth great anger, and she will not cover her own shame.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:9: The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:10: If your daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly, lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:11: Watch over an impudent eye: and marvel not if she trespass against you.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:12: She will open her mouth, as a thirsty traveller when he has found a fountain, and drink of every water near her: by every hedge will she sit down, and open her quiver against every arrow.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:13: The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fatten his bones.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:14: A silent and loving woman is a gift of Yahuah (God); and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:15: A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:16: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:17: As the clear light is upon the holy candlestick; so is the beauty of the face in ripe age.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:18: As the golden pillars are upon the sockets of silver; so are the fair feet with a constant heart.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:19: My son, keep the flower of your age sound; and give not your strength to strangers.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:20: When you have gotten a fruitful possession through all the field, sow it with your own seed, trusting in the goodness of your stock.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:21: So your race which you leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:22: An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:23: A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that fears Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|26:24: A dishonest woman contemneth shame: but an honest woman will reverence her husband.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:25: A shameless woman shall be counted as a dog; but she that is shamefaced will fear Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|26:26: A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:27: A loud crying woman and a scold shall be sought out to drive away the enemies.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:28: There be two things that grieve my heart; and the third makes me angry: a man of war that suffers poverty; and men of understanding that are not set by; and one that returns from righteousness to sin; Yahuah (God) prepareth such an one for the sword.
live.ecclesiasticus|26:29: A merchant shall hardly keep himself from doing wrong; and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:1: Many have sinned for a small matter; and he that seeks for abundance will turn his eyes away.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:2: As a nail sticketh fast between the joinings of the stones; so does sin stick close between buying and selling.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:3: Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of Yahuah (God), his house shall soon be overthrown.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:4: As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:5: The furnace proves the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:6: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:7: Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:8: If you followest righteousness, you shall obtain her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:9: The birds will resort to their like; so will truth return to them that practise in her.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:10: As the lion lieth in wait for the prey; so sin for them that work iniquity.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:11: The discourse of a godly man is always with wisdom; but a fool changeth as the moon.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:12: If you be among the indiscreet, observe the time; but be continually among men of understanding.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:13: The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:14: The talk of him that sweareth much makes the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:15: The strife of the proud is bloodshedding, and their revilings are grievous to the ear.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:16: Whoso discovers secrets loses his credit; and shall never find friend to his mind.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:17: Love your friend, and be faithful to him: but if you betrayest his secrets, follow no more after him.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:18: For as a man has destroyed his enemy; so have you lost the love of your neighbor.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:19: As one that letteth a bird go out of his hand, so have you let your neighbour go, and shall not get him again
live.ecclesiasticus|27:20: Follow after him no more, for he is too far off; he is as a roe escaped out of the snare.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:21: As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement: but he that betrayeth secrets is without hope.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:22: He that winketh with the eyes works evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:23: When you are present, he will speak sweetly, and will admire your words: but at the last he will writhe his mouth, and slander your sayings.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:24: I have hated many things, but nothing like him; for Yahuah (God) will hate him.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:25: Whoso casteth a stone on high casteth it on his own head; and a deceitful stroke shall make wounds.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:26: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:27: He that works mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it comes.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:28: Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:29: They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.
live.ecclesiasticus|27:30: Malice and wrath, even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:1: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:2: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:3: One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?
live.ecclesiasticus|28:4: He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?
live.ecclesiasticus|28:5: If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?
live.ecclesiasticus|28:6: Remember your end, and let enmity cease; remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:7: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:8: Abstain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins: for a furious man will kindle strife,
live.ecclesiasticus|28:9: A sinful man disquieteth friends, and makes debate among them that be at peace.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:10: As the matter of the fire is, so it burneth: and as a man’s strength is, so is his wrath; and according to his riches his anger rises; and the stronger they are which contend, the more they will be inflamed.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:11: An hasty contention kindleth a fire: and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:12: If you blow the spark, it shall burn: if you spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of your mouth.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:13: Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:14: A backbiting tongue has disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities has it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:15: A backbiting tongue has cast out virtuous women, and deprived them of their labours.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:16: Whoso hearkeneth to it shall never find rest, and never dwell quietly.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:17: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:18: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:19: Well is he that is defended through the venom thereof; who has not drawn the yoke thereof, nor has been bound in her bands.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:20: For the yoke thereof is a yoke of iron, and the bands thereof are bands of brass.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:21: The death thereof is an evil death, the grave were better than it.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:22: It shall not have rule over them that fear Yahuah (God), neither shall they be burned with the flame thereof.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:23: Such as forsake Yahuah (God) shall fall into it; and it shall burn in them, and not be quenched; it shall be sent upon them as a lion, and devour them as a leopard.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:24: Look that you hedge your possession about with thorns, and bind up your silver and gold,
live.ecclesiasticus|28:25: And weigh your words in a balance, and make a door and bar for your mouth.
live.ecclesiasticus|28:26: Beware you slide not by it, lest you fall before him that lieth in wait.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:1: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:2: Lend to your neighbour in time of his need, and pay you your neighbour again in due season.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:3: Keep your word, and deal faithfully with him, and you shall always find the thing that is necessary for you.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:4: Many, when a thing was lent them, reckoned it to be found, and put them to trouble that helped them.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:5: Till he has received, he will kiss a man’s hand; and for his neighbour’s money he will speak submissly: but when he should repay, he will prolong the time, and return words of grief, and complain of the time.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:6: If he prevail, he shall hardly receive the half, and he will count as if he had found it: if not, he has deprived him of his money, and he has gotten him an enemy without cause: he payeth him with cursings and railings; and for honour he will pay him disgrace.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:7: Many therefore have refused to lend for other men’s ill dealing, fearing to be defrauded.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:8: Yet have you patience with a man in poor estate, and delay not to shew him mercy.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:9: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:10: Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and let it not rust under a stone to be lost.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:11: Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:12: Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:13: It shall fight for you against your enemies better than a mighty shield and strong spear.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:14: An honest man is surety for his neighbour: but he that is impudent will forsake him.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:15: Forget not the friendship of your surety, for he has given his life for you.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:16: A sinner will overthrow the good estate of his surety:
live.ecclesiasticus|29:17: And he that is of an unthankful mind will leave him in danger that delivered him.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:18: Suretiship has undone many of good estate, and shaken them as a wave of the sea: mighty men has it driven from their houses, so that they wandered among strange nations.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:19: A wicked man transgressing the commandments of Yahuah (God) shall fall into suretiship: and he that undertaketh and followeth other men’s business for gain shall fall into suits.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:20: Help your neighbour according to your power, and beware that you thyself fall not into the same.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:21: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:22: Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:23: Be it little or much, hold you contented, that you hear not the reproach of your house.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:24: For it is a miserable life to go from house to house: for where you are a stranger, you darest not open your mouth.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:25: You shall entertain, and feast, and have no thanks: moreover you shall hear bitter words:
live.ecclesiasticus|29:26: Come, you stranger, and furnish a table, and feed me of that you have ready.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:27: Give place, you stranger, to an honourable man; my brother comes to be lodged, and I have need of my house.
live.ecclesiasticus|29:28: These things are grievous to a man of understanding; the upbraiding of houseroom, and reproaching of the lender.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:1: He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:2: He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:3: He that teaches his son grieves the enemy: and before his friends he shall rejoice of him.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:4: Though his father die, yet he is as though he were not dead: for he has left one behind him that is like himself.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:5: While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: and when he died, he was not sorrowful.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:6: He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one that shall requite kindness to his friends.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:7: He that makes too much of his son shall bind up his wounds; and his bowels will be troubled at every cry.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:8: An horse not broken becometh headstrong: and a child left to himself will be wilful.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:9: Cocker your child, and he shall make you afraid: play with him, and he will bring you to heaviness.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:10: Laugh not with him, lest you have sorrow with him, and lest you gnash your teeth in the end.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:11: Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:12: Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient to you, and so bring sorrow to yours heart.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:13: Chastise your son, and hold him to labour, lest his lewd behaviour be an offence to you.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:14: Better is the poor, being sound and strong of constitution, than a rich man that is afflicted in his body.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:15: Health and good estate of body are above all gold, and a strong body above infinite wealth.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:16: There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:17: Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:18: Delicates poured upon a mouth shut up are as messes of meat set upon a grave.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:19: What good doeth the offering to an idol? for neither can it eat nor smell: so is he that is persecuted of Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|30:20: He seeth with his eyes and groaneth, as an eunuch that embraceth a virgin and sigheth.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:21: Give not over your mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in your own counsel.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:22: The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:23: Love your own soul, and comfort your heart, remove sorrow far from you: for sorrow has killed many, and there is no profit in it.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:24: Envy and wrath shorten the life, and carefulness brings age before the time.
live.ecclesiasticus|30:25: A cheerful and good heart will have a care of his meat and diet.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:1: Watching for riches consumeth the flesh, and the care thereof drives away sleep.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:2: Watching care will not let a man slumber, as a sore disease breaks sleep,
live.ecclesiasticus|31:3: The rich has great labour in gathering riches together; and when he resteth, he is filled with his delicates.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:4: The poor laboureth in his poor estate; and when he leaveth off, he is still needy.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:5: He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:6: Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:7: It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:8: Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:9: Who is he? and we will call him blessed: for wonderful things has he done among his people.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:10: Who has been tried thereby, and found perfect? then let him glory. Who might offend, and has not offended? or done evil, and has not done it?
live.ecclesiasticus|31:11: His goods shall be established, and the congregation shall declare his alms.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:12: If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:13: Remember that a wicked eye is an evil thing: and what is created more wicked than an eye? therefore it weeps upon every occasion.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:14: Stretch not yours hand whithersoever it looketh, and thrust it not with him into the dish.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:15: Judge not your neighbour by thyself: and be discreet in every point.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:16: Eat as it becometh a man, those things which are set before you; and devour not, lest you be hated.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:17: Leave off first for manners’ sake; and be not unsatiable, lest you offend.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:18: When you sittest among many, reach not yours hand out first of all.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:19: A very little is sufficient for a man well nurtured, and he fetcheth not his wind short upon his bed.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:20: Sound sleep comes of moderate eating: he rises early, and his wits are with him: but the pain of watching, and choler, and pangs of the belly, are with an unsatiable man.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:21: And if you have been forced to eat, arise, go forth, vomit, and you shall have rest.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:22: My son, hear me, and despise me not, and at the last you shall find as I told you: in all your works be quick, so shall there no sickness come to you.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:23: Whoso is liberal of his meat, men shall speak well of him; and the report of his good housekeeping will be believed.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:24: But against him that is a niggard of his meat the whole city shall murmur; and the testimonies of his niggardness shall not be doubted of.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:25: Shew not your valiantness in wine; for wine has destroyed many.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:26: The furnace proves the edge by dipping: so does wine the hearts of the proud by drunkeness.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:27: Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:28: Wine measurably drunk and in season brings gladness of the heart, and cheerfulness of the mind:
live.ecclesiasticus|31:29: But wine drunken with excess makes bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:30: Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminisheth strength, and makes wounds.
live.ecclesiasticus|31:31: Rebuke not your neighbour at the wine, and despise him not in his mirth: give him no despiteful words, and press not upon him with urging him to drink.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:1: If you be made the master of a feast, lift not thyself up, but be among them as one of the rest; take diligent care for them, and so sit down.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:2: And when you have done all your office, take your place, that you may be merry with them, and receive a crown for your well ordering of the feast.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:3: Speak, you that are the elder, for it becometh you, but with sound judgment; and hinder not musick.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:4: Pour not out words where there is a musician, and shew not forth wisdom out of time.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:5: A concert of musick in a banquet of wine is as a signet of carbuncle set in gold.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:6: As a signet of an emerald set in a work of gold, so is the melody of musick with pleasant wine.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:7: Speak, young man, if there be need of you: and yet scarcely when you are twice asked.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:8: Let your speech be short, comprehending much in few words; be as one that knoweth and yet holdeth his tongue.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:9: If you be among great men, make not thyself equal with them; and when ancient men are in place, use not many words.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:10: Before the thunder goes lightning; and before a shamefaced man shall go favour.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:11: Rise up betimes, and be not the last; but get you home without delay.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:12: There take your pastime, and do what you will: but sin not by proud speech.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:13: And for these things bless him that made you, and has replenished you with his good things.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:14: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) will receive his discipline; and they that seek him early shall find favour.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:15: He that seeks the law shall be filled with it: but the hypocrite will be offended thereat.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:16: They that fear Yahuah (God) shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:17: A sinful man will not be reproved, but finds an excuse according to his will.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:18: A man of counsel will be considerate; but a strange and proud man is not daunted with fear, even when of himself he has done without counsel.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:19: Do nothing without advice; and when you have once done, repent not.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:20: Go not in a way in which you may fall, and stumble not among the stones.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:21: Be not confident in a plain way.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:22: And beware of your own children.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:23: In every good work trust your own soul; for this is the keeping of the commandments.
live.ecclesiasticus|32:24: He that believes in Yahuah (God) takes heed to the commandment; and he that trusts in him shall fare never the worse.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:1: There shall no evil happen to him that fears Yahuah (God); but in temptation even again he will deliver him.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:2: A wise man hates not the law; but he that is an hypocrite in it is as a ship in a storm.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:3: A man of understanding trusts in the law; and the law is faithful to him, as an oracle.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:4: Prepare what to say, and so you shall be heard: and bind up instruction, and then make answer.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:5: The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; and his thoughts are like a rolling axletree.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:6: A stallion horse is as a mocking friend, he neigheth under every one that sits upon him.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:7: Why does one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun?
live.ecclesiasticus|33:8: By the knowledge of Yahuah (God) they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:9: Some of them has he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them has he made ordinary days.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:10: And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth:
live.ecclesiasticus|33:11: In much knowledge Yahuah (God) has divided them, and made their ways diverse.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:12: Some of them has he blessed and exalted and some of them he sanctified, and set near himself: but some of them has he cursed and brought low, and turned out of their places.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:13: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:14: Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:15: So look upon all the works of the Most High; and there are two and two, one against another.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:16: I awaked up last of all, as one that gathers after the grapegatherers: by the blessing of Yahuah (God) I profited, and tred my winepress like a gatherer of grapes.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:17: Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:18: Hear me, O you great men of the people, and hearken with your ears, you rulers of the congregation.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:19: Give not your son and wife, your brother and friend, power over you while you livest, and give not your goods to another: lest it repent you, and you intreat for the same again.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:20: As long as you livest and have breath in you, give not thyself over to any.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:21: For better it is that your children should seek to you, than that you should stand to their courtesy.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:22: In all your works keep to thyself the preeminence; leave not a stain in yours honour.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:23: At the time when you shall end your days, and finish your life, distribute your inheritance.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:24: Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the ass; and bread, correction, and work, for a servant.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:25: If you set your servant to labour, you shall find rest: but if you let him go idle, he shall seek liberty.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:26: A yoke and a collar do bow the neck: so are tortures and torments for an evil servant.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:27: Send him to labour, that he be not idle; for idleness teaches much evil.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:28: Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:29: But be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:30: If you have a servant, let him be to you as thyself, because you have bought him with a price.
live.ecclesiasticus|33:31: If you have a servant, entreat him as a brother: for you have need of him, as of your own soul: if you entreat him evil, and he run from you, which way will you go to seek him?
live.ecclesiasticus|34:1: The hopes of a man void of understanding are vain and false: and dreams lift up fools.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:2: Whoso regardeth dreams is like him that catches at a shadow, and followeth after the wind.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:3: The vision of dreams is the resemblance of one thing to another, even as the likeness of a face to a face.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:4: Of an unclean thing what can be cleansed? and from that thing which is false what truth can come?
live.ecclesiasticus|34:5: Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain: and the heart fancieth, as a woman’s heart in travail.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:6: If they be not sent from the Most High in your visitation, set not your heart upon them.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:7: For dreams have deceived many, and they have failed that put their trust in them.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:8: The law shall be found perfect without lies: and wisdom is perfection to a faithful mouth.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:9: A man that has travelled knoweth many things; and he that has much experience will declare wisdom.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:10: He that has no experience knoweth little: but he that has travelled is full of prudence.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:11: When I travelled, I saw many things; and I understand more than I can express.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:12: I was ofttimes in danger of death: yet I was delivered because of these things.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:13: The spirit of those that fear Yahuah (God) shall live; for their hope is in him that saves them.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:14: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:15: Blessed is the soul of him that fears Yahuah (God): to whom does he look? and who is his strength?
live.ecclesiasticus|34:16: For the eyes of Yahuah (God) are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, a preservation from stumbling, and an help from falling.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:17: He raiseth up the soul, and lighteneth the eyes: he gives health, life, and blessing.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:18: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:19: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:20: Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor doeth as one that killeth the son before his father’s eyes.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:21: The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:22: He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.
live.ecclesiasticus|34:23: When one buildeth, and another pulleth down, what profit have they then but labour?
live.ecclesiasticus|34:24: When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?
live.ecclesiasticus|34:25: He that washeth himself after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it again, what availeth his washing?
live.ecclesiasticus|34:26: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?
live.ecclesiasticus|35:1: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:2: He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:3: To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:4: You shall not appear empty before Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|35:5: For all these things are to be done because of the commandment.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:6: The offering of the righteous makes the altar fat, and the sweet savour thereof is before the Most High.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:7: The sacrifice of a just man is acceptable. and the memorial thereof shall never be forgotten.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:8: Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:9: In all your gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:10: Give to the Most High according as he has enriched you; and as you have gotten, give with a cheerful eye.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:11: For Yahuah (God) recompenseth, and will give you seven times as much.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:12: Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices; for Yahuah (God) is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:13: He will not accept any person against a poor man, but will hear the prayer of the oppressed.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:14: He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:15: Do not the tears run down the widow’s cheeks? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall?
live.ecclesiasticus|35:16: He that serveth Yahuah (God) shall be accepted with favour, and his prayer shall reach to the clouds.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:17: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the Most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:18: For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen; till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptre of the unrighteous;
live.ecclesiasticus|35:19: Till he have rendered to every man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their devices; till he have judged the cause of his people, and made them to rejoice in his mercy.
live.ecclesiasticus|35:20: Mercy is seasonable in the time of affliction, as clouds of rain in the time of drought.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:1: Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us:
live.ecclesiasticus|36:2: And send your fear upon all the nations that seek not after you.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:3: Lift up your hand against the strange nations, and let them see your power.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:4: As you were sanctified in us before them: so be you magnified among them before us.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:5: And let them know you, as we have known you, that there is no Yahuah (God) but only you, O Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|36:6: Shew new signs, and make other strange wonders: glorify your hand and your right arm, that they may set forth your wondrous works.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:7: Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath: take away the adversary, and destroy the enemy.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:8: Make the time short, remember the covenant, and let them declare your wonderful works.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:9: Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire; and let them perish that oppress the people.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:10: Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:11: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:12: O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:13: O be merciful to Jerusalem, your holy city, the place of your rest.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:14: Fill Sion with your unspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory:
live.ecclesiasticus|36:15: Give testimony to those that you have possessed from the beginning, and raise up prophets that have been in your name.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:16: Reward them that wait for you, and let your prophets be found faithful.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:17: O Yahuah (God), hear the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all they which dwell upon the earth may know that you are Yahuah (God), the eternal Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|36:18: The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:19: As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so does an heart of understanding false speeches.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:20: A froward heart causeth heaviness: but a man of experience will recompense him.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:21: A woman will receive every man, yet is one daughter better than another.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:22: The beauty of a woman cheereth the countenance, and a man loves nothing better.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:23: If there be kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, then is not her husband like other men.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:24: He that getteth a wife begins a possession, a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:25: Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled: and he that has no wife will wander up and down mourning.
live.ecclesiasticus|36:26: Who will trust a thief well appointed, that skippeth from city to city? so who will believe a man that has no house, and lodgeth wherever the night takes him?
live.ecclesiasticus|37:1: Every friend says, I am his friend also: but there is a friend, which is only a friend in name.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:2: Is it not a grief to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?
live.ecclesiasticus|37:3: O wicked imagination, whence camest you in to cover the earth with deceit?
live.ecclesiasticus|37:4: There is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:5: There is a companion, which helps his friend for the belly, and takes up the buckler against the enemy.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:6: Forget not your friend in your mind, and be not unmindful of him in your riches.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:7: Every counsellor extolleth counsel; but there is some that counselleth for himself.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:8: Beware of a counsellor, and know before what need he has; for he will counsel for himself; lest he cast the lot upon you,
live.ecclesiasticus|37:9: And say to you, Your way is good: and afterward he stand on the other side, to see what shall befall you.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:10: Consult not with one that suspecteth you: and hide your counsel from such as envy you.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:11: Neither consult with a woman touching her of whom she is jealous; neither with a coward in matters of war; nor with a merchant concerning exchange; nor with a buyer of selling; nor with an envious man of thankfulness; nor with an unmerciful man touching kindness; nor with the slothful for any work; nor with an hireling for a year of finishing work; nor with an idle servant of much business: hearken not to these in any matter of counsel.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:12: But be continually with a godly man, whom you know to keep the commandments of Yahuah (God), whose, mind is according to your mind, and will sorrow with you, if you shall miscarry.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:13: And let the counsel of your own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful to you than it.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:14: For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:15: And above all this pray to the Most High, that he will direct your way in truth.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:16: Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:17: The countenance is a sign of changing of the heart.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:18: Four manner of things appear: good and evil, life and death: but the tongue ruleth over them continually.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:19: There is one that is wise and teaches many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:20: There is one that sheweth wisdom in words, and is hated: he shall be destitute of all food.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:21: For grace is not given, him from Yahuah (God), because he is deprived of all wisdom.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:22: Another is wise to himself; and the fruits of understanding are commendable in his mouth.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:23: A wise man instructs his people; and the fruits of his understanding fail not.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:24: A wise man shall be filled with blessing; and all they that see him shall count him happy.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:25: The days of the life of man may be numbered: but the days of Yashar'el (Israel) are innumerable.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:26: A wise man shall inherit glory among his people, and his name shall be perpetual.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:27: My son, prove your soul in your life, and see what is evil for it, and give not that to it.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:28: For all things are not profitable for all men, neither has every soul pleasure in every thing.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:29: Be not unsatiable in any dainty thing, nor too greedy upon meats:
live.ecclesiasticus|37:30: For excess of meats brings sickness, and surfeiting will turn into choler.
live.ecclesiasticus|37:31: By surfeiting have many perished; but he that takes heed prolongeth his life.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:1: Honour a physician with the honour due to him for the uses which you may have of him: for Yahuah (God) has created him.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:2: For of the Most High comes healing, and he shall receive honour of the king.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:3: The skill of the physician shall lift up his head: and in the sight of great men he shall be in admiration.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:4: Yahuah (God) has created medicines out of the earth; and he that is wise will not abhor them.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:5: Was not the water made sweet with wood, that the virtue thereof might be known?
live.ecclesiasticus|38:6: And he has given men skill, that he might be honoured in his marvellous works.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:7: With such does he heal men, and takes away their pains.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:8: Of such does the apothecary make a confection; and of his works there is no end; and from him is peace over all the earth,
live.ecclesiasticus|38:9: My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:10: Leave off from sin, and order yours hands aright, and cleanse your heart from all wickedness.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:11: Give a sweet savour, and a memorial of fine flour; and make a fat offering, as not being.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:12: Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:13: There is a time when in their hands there is good success.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:14: For they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give for ease and remedy to prolong life.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:15: He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:16: My son, let tears fall down over the dead, and begin to lament, as if you had suffered great harm thyself; and then cover his body according to the custom, and neglect not his burial.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:17: Weep bitterly, and make great moan, and use lamentation, as he is worthy, and that a day or two, lest you be evil spoken of: and then comfort thyself for your heaviness.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:18: For of heaviness comes death, and the heaviness of the heart breaks strength.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:19: In affliction also sorrow remains: and the life of the poor is the curse of the heart.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:20: Take no heaviness to heart: drive it away, and remember the last end.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:21: Forget it not, for there is no turning again: you shall not do him good, but hurt thyself.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:22: Remember my judgment: for your also shall be so; yesterday for me, and to day for you.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:23: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; and be comforted for him, when his Spirit is departed from him.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:24: The wisdom of a learned man comes by opportunity of leisure: and he that has little business shall become wise.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:25: How can he get wisdom that holdeth the plough, and that glorieth in the goad, that drives oxen, and is occupied in their labours, and whose talk is of bullocks?
live.ecclesiasticus|38:26: He gives his mind to make furrows; and is diligent to give the kine fodder.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:27: So every carpenter and workmaster, that laboureth night and day: and they that cut and grave seals, and are diligent to make great variety, and give themselves to counterfeit imagery, and watch to finish a work:
live.ecclesiasticus|38:28: The smith also sitting by the anvil, and considering the iron work, the vapour of the fire wasteth his flesh, and he fighteth with the heat of the furnace: the noise of the hammer and the anvil is ever in his ears, and his eyes look still upon the pattern of the thing that he makes; he sets his mind to finish his work, and watcheth to polish it perfectly:
live.ecclesiasticus|38:29: So does the potter sitting at his work, and turning the wheel about with his feet, who is alway carefully set at his work, and makes all his work by number;
live.ecclesiasticus|38:30: He fashioneth the clay with his arm, and boweth down his strength before his feet; he applieth himself to lead it over; and he is diligent to make clean the furnace:
live.ecclesiasticus|38:31: All these trust to their hands: and every one is wise in his work.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:32: Without these cannot a city be inhabited: and they shall not dwell where they will, nor go up and down:
live.ecclesiasticus|38:33: They shall not be sought for in publick counsel, nor sit high in the congregation: they shall not sit on the judges’ seat, nor understand the sentence of judgment: they cannot declare justice and judgment; and they shall not be found where parables are spoken.
live.ecclesiasticus|38:34: But they will maintain the state of the world, and all their desire is in the work of their craft.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:1: But he that gives his mind to the law of the Most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:2: He will keep the sayings of the renowned men: and where subtil parables are, he will be there also.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:3: He will seek out the secrets of grave sentences, and be conversant in dark parables.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:4: He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes: he will travel through strange countries; for he has tried the good and the evil among men.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:5: He will give his heart to resort early to Yahuah (God) that made him, and will pray before the Most High, and will open his mouth in prayer, and make supplication for his sins.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:6: When the great Yahuah (God) will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks to Yahuah (God) in his prayer.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:7: He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:8: He shall shew forth that which he has learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|39:9: Many shall commend his understanding; and so long as the world endureth, it shall not be blotted out; his memorial shall not depart away, and his name shall live from generation to generation.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:10: Nations shall shew forth his wisdom, and the congregation shall declare his praise.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:11: If he die, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: and if he live, he shall increase it.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:12: Yet have I more to say, which I have thought upon; for I am filled as the moon at the full.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:13: Hearken to me, you holy children, and bud forth as a rose growing by the brook of the field:
live.ecclesiasticus|39:14: And give you a sweet savour as frankincense, and flourish as a lily, send forth a smell, and sing a song of praise, bless Yahuah (God) in all his works.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:15: Magnify his name, and shew forth his praise with the songs of your lips, and with harps, and in praising him you shall say after this manner:
live.ecclesiasticus|39:16: All the works of Yahuah (God) are exceeding good, and whatsoever he commands shall be accomplished in due season.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:17: And none may say, What is this? wherefore is that? for at time convenient they shall all be sought out: at his commandment the waters stood as an heap, and at the words of his mouth the receptacles of waters.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:18: At his commandment is done whatsoever pleaseth him; and none can hinder, when he will save.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:19: The works of all flesh are before him, and nothing can be hid from his eyes.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:20: He seeth from everlasting to everlasting; and there is nothing wonderful before him.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:21: A man need not to say, What is this? wherefore is that? for he has made all things for their uses.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:22: His blessing covered the dry land as a river, and watered it as a flood.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:23: As he has turned the waters into saltness: so shall the heathen inherit his wrath.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:24: As his ways are plain to the holy; so are they stumblingblocks to the wicked.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:25: For the good are good things created from the beginning: so evil things for sinners.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:26: The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:27: All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:28: There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:29: Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance;
live.ecclesiasticus|39:30: Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:31: They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth, when need is; and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:32: Therefore from the beginning I was resolved, and thought upon these things, and have left them in writing.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:33: All the works of Yahuah (God) are good: and he will give every needful thing in due season.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:34: So that a man cannot say, This is worse than that: for in time they shall all be well approved.
live.ecclesiasticus|39:35: And therefore praise you Yahuah (God) with the whole heart and mouth, and bless the name of Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|40:1: Great travail is created for every man, and an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, till the day that they return to the mother of all things.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:2: Their imagination of things to come, and the day of death, trouble their thoughts, and cause fear of heart;
live.ecclesiasticus|40:3: From him that sits on a throne of glory, to him that is humbled in earth and ashes;
live.ecclesiasticus|40:4: From him that wears purple and a crown, to him that is clothed with a linen frock.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:5: Wrath, and envy, trouble, and unquietness, fear of death, and anger, and strife, and in the time of rest upon his bed his night sleep, do change his knowledge.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:6: A little or nothing is his rest, and afterward he is in his sleep, as in a day of keeping watch, troubled in the vision of his heart, as if he were escaped out of a battle.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:7: When all is safe, he awakes, and marvelleth that the fear was nothing.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:8: Such things happen to all flesh, both man and beast, and that is sevenfold more upon sinners.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:9: Death, and bloodshed, strife, and sword, calamities, famine, tribulation, and the scourge;
live.ecclesiasticus|40:10: These things are created for the wicked, and for their sakes came the flood.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:11: All things that are of the earth shall turn to the earth again: and that which is of the waters does return into the sea.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:12: All bribery and injustice shall be blotted out: but true dealing shall endure for ever.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:13: The goods of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in rain.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:14: While he opens his hand he shall rejoice: so shall transgressors come to nought.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:15: The children of the ungodly shall not bring forth many branches: but are as unclean roots upon a hard rock.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:16: The weed growing upon every water and bank of a river shall be pulled up before all grass.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:17: Bountifulness is as a most fruitful garden, and mercifulness endureth for ever.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:18: To labour, and to be content with that a man has, is a sweet life: but he that finds a treasure is above them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:19: Children and the building of a city continue a man’s name: but a blameless wife is counted above them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:20: Wine and musick rejoice the heart: but the love of wisdom is above them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:21: The pipe and the psaltery make sweet melody: but a pleasant tongue is above them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:22: Your eye desires favour and beauty: but more than both corn while it is green.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:23: A friend and companion never meet amiss: but above both is a wife with her husband.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:24: Brothers and help are against time of trouble: but alms shall deliver more than them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:25: Gold and silver make the foot stand sure: but counsel is esteemed above them both.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:26: Riches and strength lift up the heart: but the fear of Yahuah (God) is above them both: there is no want in the fear of Yahuah (God), and it needeth not to seek help.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:27: The fear of Yahuah (God) is a fruitful garden, and covereth him above all glory.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:28: My son, lead not a beggar’s life; for better it is to die than to beg.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:29: The life of him that dependeth on another man’s table is not to be counted for a life; for he polluteth himself with other men’s meat: but a wise man well nurtured will beware thereof.
live.ecclesiasticus|40:30: Begging is sweet in the mouth of the shameless: but in his belly there shall burn a fire.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:1: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of you to a man that lives at rest in his possessions, to the man that has nothing to vex him, and that has prosperity in all things: yes, to him that is yet able to receive meat!
live.ecclesiasticus|41:2: O death, acceptable is your sentence to the needy, and to him whose strength fails, that is now in the last age, and is vexed with all things, and to him that despaireth, and has lost patience!
live.ecclesiasticus|41:3: Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before you, and that come after; for this is the sentence of Yahuah (God) over all flesh.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:4: And why art you against the pleasure of the Most High? there is no inquisition in the grave, whether you have lived ten, or an hundred, or a thousand years.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:5: The children of sinners are abominable children, and they that are conversant in the dwelling of the ungodly.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:6: The inheritance of sinners’ children shall perish, and their posterity shall have a perpetual reproach.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:7: The children will complain of an ungodly father, because they shall be reproached for his sake.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:8: Woe be to you, ungodly men, which have forsaken the law of the most high Yahuah (God)! for if you increase, it shall be to your destruction:
live.ecclesiasticus|41:9: And if you be born, you shall be born to a curse: and if you die, a curse shall be your portion.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:10: All that are of the earth shall turn to earth again: so the ungodly shall go from a curse to destruction.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:11: The mourning of men is about their bodies: but an ill name of sinners shall be blotted out.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:12: Have regard to your name; for that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:13: A good life has but few days: but a good name endureth for ever.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:14: My children, keep discipline in peace: for wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is in them both?
live.ecclesiasticus|41:15: A man that hideth his foolishness is better than a man that hideth his wisdom.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:16: Therefore be shamefaced according to my word: for it is not good to retain all shamefacedness; neither is it altogether approved in every thing.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:17: Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man;
live.ecclesiasticus|41:18: Of an offence before a judge and ruler; of iniquity before a congregation and people; of unjust dealing before your partner and friend;
live.ecclesiasticus|41:19: And of theft in regard of the place where you sojournest, and in regard of the truth of Yahuah (God) and his covenant; and to lean with your elbow upon the meat; and of scorning to give and take;
live.ecclesiasticus|41:20: And of silence before them that salute you; and to look upon an harlot;
live.ecclesiasticus|41:21: And to turn away your face from your kinsman; or to take away a portion or a gift; or to gaze upon another man’s wife.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:22: Or to be overbusy with his maid, and come not near her bed; or of upbraiding speeches before friends; and after you have given, upbraid not;
live.ecclesiasticus|41:23: Or of iterating and speaking again that which you have heard; and of revealing of secrets.
live.ecclesiasticus|41:24: So shall you be truly shamefaced and find favour before all men.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:1: Of these things be not you ashamed, and accept no person to sin thereby:
live.ecclesiasticus|42:2: Of the law of the Most High, and his covenant; and of judgment to justify the ungodly;
live.ecclesiasticus|42:3: Of reckoning with your partners and travellers; or of the gift of the heritage of friends;
live.ecclesiasticus|42:4: Of exactness of balance and weights; or of getting much or little;
live.ecclesiasticus|42:5: And of merchants’ indifferent selling; of much correction of children; and to make the side of an evil servant to bleed.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:6: Sure keeping is good, where an evil wife is; and shut up, where many hands are.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:7: Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that you give out, or receivest in.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:8: Be not ashamed to inform the unwise and foolish, and the extreme aged that contendeth with those that are young: thus shall you be truly learned, and approved of all men living.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:9: The father waketh for the daughter, when no man knoweth; and the care for her takes away sleep: when she is young, lest she pass away the flower of her age; and being married, lest she should be hated:
live.ecclesiasticus|42:10: In her virginity, lest she should be defiled and gotten with child in her father’s house; and having an husband, lest she should misbehave herself; and when she is married, lest she should be barren.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:11: Keep a sure watch over a shameless daughter, lest she make you a laughingstock to your enemies, and a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, and make you ashamed before the multitude.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:12: Behold not every body’s beauty, and sit not in the midst of women.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:13: For from garments comes a moth, and from women wickedness.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:14: Better is the churlishness of a man than a courteous woman, a woman, I say, which brings shame and reproach.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:15: I will now remember the works of Yahuah (God), and declare the things that I have seen: In the words of Yahuah (God) are his works.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:16: The sun that gives light looketh upon all things, and the work thereof is full of the glory of Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|42:17: Yahuah (God) has not given power to the saints to declare all his marvellous works, which the Almighty Yahuah (God) firmly settled, that whatsoever is might be established for his glory.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:18: He seeks out the deep, and the heart, and considereth their crafty devices: for Yahuah (God) knoweth all that may be known, and he beholds the signs of the world.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:19: He declareth the things that are past, and for to come, and revealeth the steps of hidden things.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:20: No thought escapeth him, neither any word is hidden from him.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:21: He has garnished the excellent works of his wisdom, and he is from everlasting to everlasting: to him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he has no need of any counsellor.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:22: Oh how desirable are all his works! and that a man may see even to a spark.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:23: All these things live and remain for ever for all uses, and they are all obedient.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:24: All things are double one against another: and he has made nothing imperfect.
live.ecclesiasticus|42:25: One thing establishes the good or another: and who shall be filled with beholding his glory?
live.ecclesiasticus|43:1: The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew;
live.ecclesiasticus|43:2: The sun when it appears, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the Most High:
live.ecclesiasticus|43:3: At noon it parcheth the country, and who can abide the burning heat thereof?
live.ecclesiasticus|43:4: A man blowing a furnace is in works of heat, but the sun burneth the mountains three times more; breathing out fiery vapours, and sending forth bright beams, it dimmeth the eyes.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:5: Great is Yahuah (God) that made it; and at his commandment runs hastily.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:6: He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:7: From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:8: The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven;
live.ecclesiasticus|43:9: The beauty of heaven, the glory of the stars, an ornament giving light in the highest places of Yahuah (God).
live.ecclesiasticus|43:10: At the commandment of the Holy One they will stand in their order, and never faint in their watches.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:11: Look upon the rainbow, and praise him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:12: It compasseth the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the Most High have bended it.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:13: By his commandment he makes the snow to fall aplace, and sends swiftly the lightnings of his judgment.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:14: Through this the treasures are opened: and clouds fly forth as fowls.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:15: By his great power he makes the clouds firm, and the hailstones are broken small.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:16: At his sight the mountains are shaken, and at his will the south wind bloweth.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:17: The noise of the thunder makes the earth to tremble: so does the northern storm and the whirlwind: as birds flying he scatters the snow, and the falling down thereof is as the lighting of grasshoppers:
live.ecclesiasticus|43:18: The eye marvelleth at the beauty of the whiteness thereof, and the heart is astonished at the raining of it.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:19: The hoarfrost also as salt he poureth on the earth, and being congealed, it lieth on the top of sharp stakes.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:20: When the cold north wind bloweth, and the water is congealed into ice, it abideth upon every gathering together of water, and clothes the water as with a breastplate.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:21: It devoureth the mountains, and burneth the wilderness, and consumeth the grass as fire.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:22: A present remedy of all is a mist coming speedily, a dew coming after heat refresheth.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:23: By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:24: They that sail on the sea tell of the danger thereof; and when we hear it with our ears, we marvel thereat.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:25: For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:26: By him the end of them has prosperous success, and by his word all things consist.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:27: We may speak much, and yet come short: wherefore in sum, he is all.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:28: How shall we be able to magnify him? for he is great above all his works.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:29: Yahuah (God) is terrible and very great, and marvellous is his power.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:30: When you glorify Yahuah (God), exalt him as much as you can; for even yet will he far exceed: and when you exalt him, put forth all your strength, and be not weary; for you can never go far enough.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:31: Who has seen him, that he might tell us? and who can magnify him as he is?
live.ecclesiasticus|43:32: There are yet hid greater things than these be, for we have seen but a few of his works.
live.ecclesiasticus|43:33: For Yahuah (God) has made all things; and to the godly has he given wisdom.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:1: Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:2: Yahuah (God) has wrought great glory by them through his great power from the beginning.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:3: Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies:
live.ecclesiasticus|44:4: Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions:
live.ecclesiasticus|44:5: Such as found out musical tunes, and recited verses in writing:
live.ecclesiasticus|44:6: Rich men furnished with ability, living peaceably in their habitations:
live.ecclesiasticus|44:7: All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:8: There be of them, that have left a name behind them, that their praises might be reported.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:9: And some there be, which have no memorial; who are perished, as though they had never been; and are become as though they had never been born; and their children after them.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:10: But these were merciful men, whose righteousness has not been forgotten.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:11: With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:12: Their seed stands fast, and their children for their sakes.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:13: Their seed shall remain for ever, and their glory shall not be blotted out.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:14: Their bodies are buried in peace; but their name lives for evermore.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:15: The people will tell of their wisdom, and the congregation will shew forth their praise.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:16: Enoch pleased Yahuah (God), and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:17: Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:18: An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:19: Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like to him;
live.ecclesiasticus|44:20: Who kept the law of the Most High, and was in covenant with him: he established the covenant in his flesh; and when he was proved, he was found faithful.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:21: Therefore he assured him by an oath, that he would bless the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, and from the river to the utmost part of the land.
live.ecclesiasticus|44:22: With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant,
live.ecclesiasticus|44:23: And made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:1: And he brought out of him a merciful man, which found favour in the sight of all flesh, even Moses, beloved of Yahuah (God) and men, whose memorial is blessed.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:2: He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:3: By his words he caused the wonders to cease, and he made him glorious in the sight of kings, and gave him a commandment for his people, and shewed him part of his glory.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:4: He sanctified him in his faithfuless and meekness, and chose him out of all men.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:5: He made him to hear his voice, and brought him into the dark cloud, and gave him commandments before his face, even the law of life and knowledge, that he might teach Jacob his covenants, and Yashar'el (Israel) his judgments.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:6: He exalted Aaron, an holy man like to him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:7: An everlasting covenant he made with him and gave him the priesthood among the people; he beautified him with comely ornaments, and clothed him with a robe of glory.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:8: He put upon him perfect glory; and strengthened him with rich garments, with breeches, with a long robe, and the ephod.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:9: And he compassed him with pomegranates, and with many golden bells round about, that as he went there might be a sound, and a noise made that might be heard in the temple, for a memorial to the children of his people;
live.ecclesiasticus|45:10: With an holy garment, with gold, and blue silk, and purple, the work of the embroiderer, with a breastplate of judgment, and with Urim and Thummim;
live.ecclesiasticus|45:11: With twisted scarlet, the work of the cunning workman, with precious stones graven like seals, and set in gold, the work of the jeweller, with a writing engraved for a memorial, after the number of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.ecclesiasticus|45:12: He set a crown of gold upon the mitre, in which was engraved Holiness, an ornament of honour, a costly work, the desires of the eyes, goodly and beautiful.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:13: Before him there were none such, neither did ever any stranger put them on, but only his children and his children’s children perpetually.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:14: Their sacrifices shall be wholly consumed every day twice continually.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:15: Moses consecrated him, and anointed him with holy oil: this was appointed to him by an everlasting covenant, and to his seed, so long as the heavens should remain, that they should minister to him, and execute the office of the priesthood, and bless the people in his name.
live.ecclesiasticus|45:16: He chose him out of all men living to offer sacrifices to Yahuah (God), incense, and a sweet savour, for a memorial, to make reconciliation for his people.
