live.2-maccabees|12:27: And after he had put to flight and destroyed them, Judas removed the host toward Ephron, a strong city, in which Lysias abode, and a great multitude of divers nations, and the strong young men kept the walls, and defended them mightily: in which also was great provision of engines and darts.
live.2-maccabees|12:28: But when Judas and his company had called upon Almighty Yahuah (God), who with his power breaks the strength of his enemies, they won the city, and slew twenty and five thousand of them that were within,
live.2-maccabees|12:29: From thence they departed to Scythopolis, which lieth six hundred furlongs from Jerusalem,
live.2-maccabees|12:30: But when the Yahudim (Jews) that dwelt there had testified that the Scythopolitans dealt lovingly with them, and entreated them kindly in the time of their adversity;
live.2-maccabees|12:31: They gave them thanks, desiring them to be friendly still to them: and so they came to Jerusalem, the feast of the weeks approaching.
live.2-maccabees|12:32: And after the feast, called Pentecost, they went forth against Gorgias the governor of Idumea,
live.2-maccabees|12:33: Who came out with three thousand men of foot and four hundred horsemen.
live.2-maccabees|12:34: And it happened that in their fighting together a few of the Yahudim (Jews) were slain.
live.2-maccabees|12:35: At which time Dositheus, one of Bacenor’s company, who was on horseback, and a strong man, was still upon Gorgias, and taking hold of his coat drew him by force; and when he would have taken that cursed man alive, a horseman of Thracia coming upon him struck off his shoulder, so that Gorgias fled to Marisa.
live.2-maccabees|12:36: Now when they that were with Gorgias had fought long, and were weary, Judas called upon Yahuah (God), that he would shew himself to be their helper and leader of the battle.
live.2-maccabees|12:37: And with that he began in his own language, and sung psalms with a loud voice, and rushing unawares upon Gorgias’ men, he put them to flight.
live.2-maccabees|12:38: So Judas gathered his host, and came into the city of Odollam, And when the seventh day came, they purified themselves, as the custom was, and kept the sabbath in the same place.
live.2-maccabees|12:39: And upon the day following, as the use had been, Judas and his company came to take up the bodies of them that were slain, and to bury them with their kinsmen in their fathers’ graves.
live.2-maccabees|12:40: Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Yahudim (Jews) by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
live.2-maccabees|12:41: All men therefore praising Yahuah (God), the righteous Judge, who had opened the things that were hid,
live.2-maccabees|12:42: Betook themselves to prayer, and besought him that the sin committed might wholly be put out of remembrance. Besides, that noble Judas exhorted the people to keep themselves from sin, forsomuch as they saw before their eyes the things that came to pass for the sins of those that were slain.
live.2-maccabees|12:43: And when he had made a gathering throughout the company to the sum of two thousand drachms of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sin offering, doing in it very well and honestly, in that he was mindful of the resurrection:
live.2-maccabees|12:44: For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should have risen again, it had been superfluous and vain to pray for the dead.
live.2-maccabees|12:45: And also in that he perceived that there was great favour laid up for those that died godly, it was an holy and good thought. Whereupon he made a reconciliation for the dead, that they might be delivered from sin.
live.2-maccabees|13:1: In the hundred forty and ninth year it was told Judas, that Antiochus Eupator was coming with a great power into Judea,
live.2-maccabees|13:2: And with him Lysias his protector, and ruler of his affairs, having either of them a Grecian power of footmen, an hundred and ten thousand, and horsemen five thousand and three hundred, and elephants two and twenty, and three hundred chariots armed with hooks.
live.2-maccabees|13:3: Menelaus also joined himself with them, and with great dissimulation encouraged Antiochus, not for the safeguard of the country, but because he thought to have been made governor.
live.2-maccabees|13:4: But the King of kings moved Antiochus’ mind against this wicked wretch, and Lysias informed the king that this man was the cause of all mischief, so that the king commanded to bring him to Berea, and to put him to death, as the manner is in that place.
live.2-maccabees|13:5: Now there was in that place a tower of fifty cubits high, full of ashes, and it had a round instrument which on every side hanged down into the ashes.
live.2-maccabees|13:6: And whoever was condemned of sacrilege, or had committed any other grievous crime, there did all men thrust him to death.
live.2-maccabees|13:7: Such a death it happened that wicked man to die, not having so much as burial in the earth; and that most justly:
live.2-maccabees|13:8: For inasmuch as he had committed many sins about the altar, whose fire and ashes were holy, he received his death in ashes.
live.2-maccabees|13:9: Now the king came with a barbarous and haughty mind to do far worse to the Yahudim (Jews), than had been done in his father’s time.
live.2-maccabees|13:10: Which things when Judas perceived, he commanded the multitude to call upon Yahuah (God) night and day, that if ever at any other time, he would now also help them, being at the point to be put from their law, from their country, and from the holy temple:
live.2-maccabees|13:11: And that he would not suffer the people, that had even now been but a little refreshed, to be in subjection to the blasphemous nations.
live.2-maccabees|13:12: So when they had all done this together, and besought the merciful Yahuah (God) with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness.
live.2-maccabees|13:13: And Judas, being apart with the elders, determined, before the king’s host should enter into Judea, and get the city, to go forth and try the matter in fight by the help of Yahuah (God).
live.2-maccabees|13:14: So when he had committed all to the Creator of the world, and exhorted his soldiers to fight manfully, even to death, for the laws, the temple, the city, the country, and the commonwealth, he camped by Modin:
live.2-maccabees|13:15: And having given the watchword to them that were about him, Victory is of Yahuah (God); with the most valiant and choice young men he went in into the king’s tent by night, and slew in the camp about four thousand men, and the chiefest of the elephants, with all that were upon him.
live.2-maccabees|13:16: And at last they filled the camp with fear and tumult, and departed with good success.
live.2-maccabees|13:17: This was done in the break of the day, because the protection of Yahuah (God) did help him.
live.2-maccabees|13:18: Now when the king had taken a taste of the manliness of the Yahudim (Jews), he went about to take the holds by policy,
live.2-maccabees|13:19: And marched toward Bethsura, which was a strong hold of the Yahudim (Jews): but he was put to flight, failed, and lost of his men:
live.2-maccabees|13:20: For Judas had conveyed to them that were in it such things as were necessary.
live.2-maccabees|13:21: But Rhodocus, who was in the Yahudim (Jews)’ host, disclosed the secrets to the enemies; therefore he was sought out, and when they had gotten him, they put him in prison.
live.2-maccabees|13:22: The king treated with them in Bethsum the second time, gave his hand, took their’s, departed, fought with Judas, was overcome;
live.2-maccabees|13:23: Heard that Philip, who was left over the affairs in Antioch, was desperately bent, confounded, intreated the Yahudim (Jews), submitted himself, and sware to all equal conditions, agreed with them, and offered sacrifice, honoured the temple, and dealt kindly with the place,
live.2-maccabees|13:24: And accepted well of Maccabeus, made him principal governor from Ptolemais to the Gerrhenians;
live.2-maccabees|13:25: Came to Ptolemais: the people there were grieved for the covenants; for they stormed, because they would make their covenants void:
live.2-maccabees|13:26: Lysias went up to the judgment seat, said as much as could be in defence of the cause, persuaded, pacified, made them well affected, returned to Antioch. Thus it went touching the king’s coming and departing.
live.2-maccabees|14:1: After three years was Judas informed, that Demetrius the son of Seleucus, having entered by the haven of Tripolis with a great power and navy,
live.2-maccabees|14:2: Had taken the country, and killed Antiochus, and Lysias his protector.
live.2-maccabees|14:3: Now one Alcimus, who had been high priest, and had defiled himself wilfully in the times of their mingling with the Gentiles, seeing that by no means he could save himself, nor have any more access to the holy altar,
live.2-maccabees|14:4: Came to king Demetrius in the hundred and one and fiftieth year, presenting to him a crown of gold, and a palm, and also of the boughs which were used solemnly in the temple: and so that day he held his peace.
live.2-maccabees|14:5: Howbeit having gotten opportunity to further his foolish enterprize, and being called into counsel by Demetrius, and asked how the Yahudim (Jews) stood affected, and what they intended, he answered to it:
live.2-maccabees|14:6: Those of the Yahudim (Jews) that he called Assideans, whose captain is Judas Maccabeus, nourish war and are seditious, and will not let the rest be in peace.
live.2-maccabees|14:7: Therefore I, being deprived of my ancestors’ honour, I mean the high priesthood, am now come hither:
live.2-maccabees|14:8: First, verily for the unfeigned care I have of things pertaining to the king; and secondly, even for that I intend the good of my own countrymen: for all our nation is in no small misery through the unadvised dealing of them aforersaid.
live.2-maccabees|14:9: Wherefore, O king, seeing knowest all these things, be careful for the country, and our nation, which is pressed on every side, according to the clemency that you readily shewest to all.
live.2-maccabees|14:10: For as long as Judas lives, it is not possible that the state should be quiet.
live.2-maccabees|14:11: This was no sooner spoken of him, but others of the king’s friends, being maliciously set against Judas, did more incense Demetrius.
live.2-maccabees|14:12: And forthwith calling Nicanor, who had been master of the elephants, and making him governor over Judea, he sent him forth,
live.2-maccabees|14:13: Commanding him to slay Judas, and to scatter them that were with him, and to make Alcimus high priest of the great temple.
live.2-maccabees|14:14: Then the heathen, that had fled out of Judea from Judas, came to Nicanor by flocks, thinking the harm and calamities of the Yahudim (Jews) to be their welfare.
live.2-maccabees|14:15: Now when the Yahudim (Jews) heard of Nicanor’s coming, and that the heathen were up against them, they cast earth upon their heads, and made supplication to him that had established his people for ever, and who always helps his portion with manifestation of his presence.
live.2-maccabees|14:16: So at the commandment of the captain they removed straightways from thence, and came near to them at the town of Dessau.
live.2-maccabees|14:17: Now Simon, Judas’ brother, had joined battle with Nicanor, but was somewhat discomfited through the sudden silence of his enemies.
live.2-maccabees|14:18: Nevertheless Nicanor, hearing of the manliness of them that were with Judas, and the courageousness that they had to fight for their country, durst not try the matter by the sword.
live.2-maccabees|14:19: Wherefore he sent Posidonius, and Theodotus, and Mattathias, to make peace.
live.2-maccabees|14:20: So when they had taken long advisement thereupon, and the captain had made the multitude acquainted with it, and it appeared that they were all of one mind, they consented to the covenants,
live.2-maccabees|14:21: And appointed a day to meet in together by themselves: and when the day came, and stools were set for either of them,
live.2-maccabees|14:22: Ludas placed armed men ready in convenient places, lest some treachery should be suddenly practised by the enemies: so they made a peaceable conference.
live.2-maccabees|14:23: Now Nicanor abode in Jerusalem, and did no hurt, but sent away the people that came flocking to him.
live.2-maccabees|14:24: And he would not willingly have Judas out of his sight: for he love the man from his heart
live.2-maccabees|14:25: He prayed him also to take a wife, and to beget children: so he married, was quiet, and took part of this life.
live.2-maccabees|14:26: But Alcimus, perceiving the love that was between them, and considering the covenants that were made, came to Demetrius, and told him that Nicanor was not well affected toward the state; for that he had ordained Judas, a traitor to his realm, to be the king’s successor.
live.2-maccabees|14:27: Then the king being in a rage, and provoked with the accusations of the most wicked man, wrote to Nicanor, signifying that he was much displeased with the covenants, and commanding him that he should send Maccabeus prisoner in all haste to Antioch.
live.2-maccabees|14:28: When this came to Nicanor’s hearing, he was much confounded in himself, and took it grievously that he should make void the articles which were agreed upon, the man being in no fault.
live.2-maccabees|14:29: But because there was no dealing against the king, he watched his time to accomplish this thing by policy.
live.2-maccabees|14:30: Notwithstanding, when Maccabeus saw that Nicanor began to be churlish to him, and that he entreated him more roughly than he was wont, perceiving that such sour behaviour came not of good, he gathered together not a few of his men, and withdrew himself from Nicanor.
live.2-maccabees|14:31: But the other, knowing that he was notably prevented by Judas’ policy, came into the great and holy temple, and commanded the priests, that were offering their usual sacrifices, to deliver him the man.
live.2-maccabees|14:32: And when they sware that they could not tell where the man was whom he sought,
live.2-maccabees|14:33: He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If you will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of Yahuah (God) even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple to Bacchus.
live.2-maccabees|14:34: After these words he departed. Then the priests lifted up their hands toward heaven, and besought him that was ever a defender of their nation, saying in this manner;
live.2-maccabees|14:35: You, O Yahuah (God) of all things, who have need of nothing, were pleased that the temple of yours habitation should be among us:
live.2-maccabees|14:36: Therefore now, O holy Yahuah (God) of all holiness, keep this house ever undefiled, which lately was cleansed, and stop every unrighteous mouth.
live.2-maccabees|14:37: Now was there accused to Nicanor one Razis, one of the elders of Jerusalem, a lover of his countrymen, and a man of very good report, who for his kindness was called a father of the Yahudim (Jews).
live.2-maccabees|14:38: For in the former times, when they mingled not themselves with the Gentiles, he had been accused of Judaism, and did boldly jeopard his body and life with all vehemency for the religion of the Yahudim (Jews).
live.2-maccabees|14:39: So Nicanor, willing to declare the hate that he bare to the Yahudim (Jews), sent above five hundred men of war to take him:
live.2-maccabees|14:40: For he thought by taking him to do the Yahudim (Jews) much hurt.
live.2-maccabees|14:41: Now when the multitude would have taken the tower, and violently broken into the outer door, and told that fire should be brought to burn it, he being ready to be taken on every side fell upon his sword;
live.2-maccabees|14:42: Choosing rather to die manfully, than to come into the hands of the wicked, to be abused otherwise than beseemed his noble birth:
live.2-maccabees|14:43: But missing his stroke through haste, the multitude also rushing within the doors, he ran boldly up to the wall, and cast himself down manfully among the thickest of them.
live.2-maccabees|14:44: But they quickly giving back, and a space being made, he fell down into the midst of the void place.
live.2-maccabees|14:45: Nevertheless, while there was yet breath within him, being inflamed with anger, he rose up; and though his blood gushed out like spouts of water, and his wounds were grievous, yet he ran through the midst of the throng; and standing upon a steep rock,
live.2-maccabees|14:46: When as his blood was now quite gone, he plucked out his bowels, and taking them in both his hands, he cast them upon the throng, and calling upon Yahuah (God) of life and spirit to restore him those again, he thus died.
live.2-maccabees|15:1: But Nicanor, hearing that Judas and his company were in the strong places about Samaria, resolved without any danger to set upon them on the sabbath day.
live.2-maccabees|15:2: Nevertheless the Yahudim (Jews) that were compelled to go with him said, O destroy not so cruelly and barbarously, but give honour to that day, which he, that seeth all things, has honoured with holiness above all other days.
live.2-maccabees|15:3: Then the most ungracious wretch demanded, if there were a Mighty one in heaven, that had commanded the sabbath day to be kept.
live.2-maccabees|15:4: And when they said, There is in heaven a living Yahuah (God), and mighty, who commanded the seventh day to be kept:
live.2-maccabees|15:5: Then said the other, And I also am mighty upon earth, and I command to take arms, and to do the king’s business. Yet he obtained not to have his wicked will done.
live.2-maccabees|15:6: So Nicanor in exceeding pride and haughtiness determined to set up a publick monument of his victory over Judas and them that were with him.
live.2-maccabees|15:7: But Maccabeus had ever sure confidence that Yahuah (God) would help him:
live.2-maccabees|15:8: Wherefore he exhorted his people not to fear the coming of the heathen against them, but to remember the help which in former times they had received from heaven, and now to expect the victory and aid, which should come to them from the Almighty.
live.2-maccabees|15:9: And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.
live.2-maccabees|15:10: And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithall the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.
live.2-maccabees|15:11: Thus he armed every one of them, not so much with defence of shields and spears, as with comfortable and good words: and beside that, he told them a dream worthy to be believed, as if it had been so indeed, which did not a little rejoice them.
live.2-maccabees|15:12: And this was his vision: That Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken also, and exercised from a child in all points of virtue, holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Yahudim (Jews).
live.2-maccabees|15:13: This done, in like manner there appeared a man with gray hairs, and exceeding glorious, who was of a wonderful and excellent majesty.
live.2-maccabees|15:14: Then Onias answered, saying, This is a lover of the brothers, who prayeth much for the people, and for the holy city, to wit, Jeremias the prophet of Yahuah (God).
live.2-maccabees|15:15: Whereupon Jeremias holding forth his right hand gave to Judas a sword of gold, and in giving it spoke thus,
live.2-maccabees|15:16: Take this holy sword, a gift from Yahuah (God), with the which you shall wound the adversaries.
live.2-maccabees|15:17: Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas, which were very good, and able to stir them up to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men, they determined not to pitch camp, but courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict, because the city and the sanctuary and the temple were in danger.
live.2-maccabees|15:18: For the care that they took for their wives, and their children, their brothers, and folks, was in least account with them: but the greatest and principal fear was for the holy temple.
live.2-maccabees|15:19: Also they that were in the city took not the least care, being troubled for the conflict abroad.
live.2-maccabees|15:20: And now, when as all looked what should be the trial, and the enemies were already come near, and the army was set in array, and the beasts conveniently placed, and the horsemen set in wings,
live.2-maccabees|15:21: Maccabeus seeing the coming of the multitude, and the divers preparations of armour, and the fierceness of the beasts, stretched out his hands toward heaven, and called upon Yahuah (God) that works wonders, knowing that victory comes not by arms, but even as it seemeth good to him, he gives it to such as are worthy:
live.2-maccabees|15:22: Therefore in his prayer he said after this manner; O Yahuah (God), you did send your angel in the time of Ezekias king of Judea, and did slay in the host of Sennacherib an hundred fourscore and five thousand:
live.2-maccabees|15:23: Wherefore now also, O Yahuah (God) of heaven, send a good angel before us for a fear and dread to them;
live.2-maccabees|15:24: And through the might of your arm let those be stricken with terror, that come against your holy people to blaspheme. And he ended thus.
live.2-maccabees|15:25: Then Nicanor and they that were with him came forward with trumpets and songs.
live.2-maccabees|15:26: But Judas and his company encountered the enemies with invocation and prayer.
live.2-maccabees|15:27: So that fighting with their hands, and praying to Yahuah (God) with their hearts, they slew no less than thirty and five thousand men: for through the appearance of Yahuah (God) they were greatly cheered.
live.2-maccabees|15:28: Now when the battle was done, returning again with joy, they knew that Nicanor lay dead in his harness.
live.2-maccabees|15:29: Then they made a great shout and a noise, praising the Almighty in their own language.
live.2-maccabees|15:30: And Judas, who was ever the chief defender of the citizens both in body and mind, and who continued his love toward his countrymen all his life, commanded to strike off Nicanor’s head, and his hand with his shoulder, and bring them to Jerusalem.
live.2-maccabees|15:31: So when he was there, and called them of his nation together, and set the priests before the altar, he sent for them that were of the tower,
live.2-maccabees|15:32: And shewed them vile Nicanor’s head, and the hand of that blasphemer, which with proud brags he had stretched out against the holy temple of the Almighty.
live.2-maccabees|15:33: And when he had cut out the tongue of that ungodly Nicanor, he commanded that they should give it by pieces to the fowls, and hang up the reward of his madness before the temple.
live.2-maccabees|15:34: So every man praised toward the heaven the glorious Yahuah (God), saying, Blessed be he that has kept his own place undefiled.
live.2-maccabees|15:35: He hanged also Nicanor’s head upon the tower, an evident and manifest sign to all of the help of Yahuah (God).
live.2-maccabees|15:36: And they ordained all with a common decree in no case to let that day pass without solemnity, but to celebrate the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which in the Syrian tongue is called Adar, the day before Mardocheus’ day.
live.2-maccabees|15:37: Thus went it with Nicanor: and from that time forth the Hebrews had the city in their power. And here will I make an end.
live.2-maccabees|15:38: And if I have done well, and as is fitting the story, it is that which I desired: but if slenderly and meanly, it is that which I could attain to.
live.2-maccabees|15:39: For as it is hurtful to drink wine or water alone; and as wine mingled with water is pleasant, and delighteth the taste: even so speech finely framed delighteth the ears of them that read the story. And here shall be an end.
live.3-maccabees|1:1: Now Philopater, on learning from those who came back that Antiochus had made himself master of the places which belonged to himself, sent orders to all his footmen and horsemen, took with him his sister Arsinoe, and marched out as far as the parts of Raphia, where Antiochus and his forces encamped.
live.3-maccabees|1:2: And one Theodotus, intending to carry out his design, took with him the bravest of the armed men who had been before committed to his trust by Ptolemy, and got through at night to the tent of Ptolemy, to kill him on his own responsibility, and so to end the war.
live.3-maccabees|1:3: But Dositheus, called the son of Drimulus, by birth a Yahudi (Jew), afterward a renegade from the laws and observances of his country, conveyed Ptolemy away, and made an obscure person lie down in his stead in the tent. It befel this man to receive the fate which was meant for the other.
live.3-maccabees|1:4: A fierce battle then took place; and the men of Antiochus prevailing, Arsinoe continually went up and down the ranks, and with dishevelled hair, with tears and entreaties, begged the soldiers to fight manfully for themselves, their children, and wives; and promised that if they proved conquerors, she would give them two minæ of gold apiece.
live.3-maccabees|1:5: It thus fell out that their enemies were defeated in hand-to-hand encounter, and that many of them were taken prisoners.
live.3-maccabees|1:6: Having vanquished this attempt, the king then decided to proceed to the neighbouring cities, and encourage them.
live.3-maccabees|1:7: By doing this, and by making donations to their temples, he inspired his subjects with confidence.
live.3-maccabees|1:8: The Yahudim (Jews) also sent some of their council and of their elders to him. The greetings, guest-gifts, and congratulations on the past, bestowed by them, filled him with the greater eagerness to visit their city.
live.3-maccabees|1:9: Having arrived at Jerusalem, sacrificed, and offered thank-offerings to the Greatest Elohim (God), and done whatever else was suitable to the sanctity of the place, and entered the inner court,
live.3-maccabees|1:10: he was so struck with the exact magnificence of the place, and so wondered at the orderly arrangements of the temple, that he conceived the purpose of entering the sanctuary itself.
live.3-maccabees|1:11: And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
live.3-maccabees|1:12: Then they read the law to him; but he persisted in obtruding himself, exclaiming, that he ought to be allowed: and saying, Be it that they were deprived of this honour, I ought not to be.
live.3-maccabees|1:13: And he put the question, Why, when he entered all temples, none of the priests who were present forbad him?
live.3-maccabees|1:14: He was thoughtlessly answered by some one, That he did wrong to boast of this.
live.3-maccabees|1:15: Well; since I have done this, said he, be the cause what it may, shall I not enter with or without your consent?
live.3-maccabees|1:16: And when the priests fell down in their sacred vestments imploring the Greatest Elohim (God) to come and help in time of need, and to avert the violence of the fierce aggressor, and when they filled the temple with lamentations and tears,
live.3-maccabees|1:17: then those who had been left behind in the city were scared, and rushed forth, uncertain of the event.
live.3-maccabees|1:18: Virgins, who had been shut up within their chambers, came out with their mothers, scattering dust and ashes on their heads, and filling the streets with outcries.
live.3-maccabees|1:19: Women, but recently separated off, left their bridal chambers, left the reserve that befitted them, and ran about the city in a disorderly manner.
live.3-maccabees|1:20: Newborn babes were deserted by the mothers or nurses who waited upon them; some here, some there, in houses, or in fields; these now, with an ardour which could not be checked, swarmed into the El Elyon (Most High) temple.
live.3-maccabees|1:21: Various were the prayers offered up by those who assembled in this place, on account of the unholy attempt of the king.
live.3-maccabees|1:22: Along with these there were some of the citizens who took courage, and would not submit to his obstinacy, and his intention of carrying out his purpose.
live.3-maccabees|1:23: Calling out to arms, and to die bravely in defence of the law of their fathers, they created a great uproar in the place, and were with difficulty brought back by the aged and the elders to the station of prayer which they had occupied before.
live.3-maccabees|1:24: During this time the multitude kept on praying.
live.3-maccabees|1:25: The elders who surrounded the king strove in many ways to divert his haughty mind from the design which he had formed.
live.3-maccabees|1:26: He, in his hardened mood, insensible to all persuasion, was going onwards, with the view of carrying out this design.
live.3-maccabees|1:27: Yet even his own officers, when they saw this, joined the Yahudim (Jews) in an appeal to Him who has all power, to aid in the present crisis, and not wink at such overweening lawlessness.
live.3-maccabees|1:28: Such was the frequency and the vehemence of the cry of the assembled crowd, that an indescribable noise ensued.
live.3-maccabees|1:29: Not the men only, the very walls and floor seemed to sound forth; all things preferring dissolution rather than to see the place defiled.
live.3-maccabees|2:1: Now was it that the high priest Simon bowed his knees over against the holy place, and spread out his hands in reverent form, and uttered the following supplication:
live.3-maccabees|2:2: O Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord), King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who exulteth in his confidence and strength.
live.3-maccabees|2:3: It is thou, the Creator of all, Yahuah (Lord) of the universe, who art a righteous Governor, and judgest all who act with pride and insolence.
live.3-maccabees|2:4: It was thou who didst destroy the former workers of unrighteousness, among whom were the giants, who trusted in their strength and hardihood, by covering them with a measureless flood.
live.3-maccabees|2:5: It was thou who didst make the Sodomites, those workers of exceeding iniquity, men notorious for their vices, an example to after generations, when thou didst consume them with fire and brimstone.
live.3-maccabees|2:6: Thou didst make known thy power when thou causedst the bold Pharaoh, the enslaver of thy people, to pass through the ordeal of many and diverse inflictions.
live.3-maccabees|2:7: And thou rolledst the depths of the sea over him, when he made pursuit with chariots, and with a multitude of followers, and gavest a safe passage to those who put their trust in thee, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation.
live.3-maccabees|2:8: These saw and felt the works of thine hands, and praised thee the Almighty.
live.3-maccabees|2:9: Thou, O King, when thou createdst the illimitable and measureless earth, didst choose out this city: thou didst make this place sacred to thy name, albeit thou needest nothing: thou didst glorify it with thy illustrious presence, after constructing it to the glory of thy great and honourable name.
live.3-maccabees|2:10: And thou didst promise, out of love to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that should we fall away from thee, and become afflicted, and then come to this house and pray, thou wouldest hear our prayer.
live.3-maccabees|2:11: Verily thou art faithful and true.
live.3-maccabees|2:12: And whereas thou didst often aid our fathers when hard pressed, and in low estate, and deliveredst them out of great dangers,
live.3-maccabees|2:13: see now, holy King, how through our many and great sins we are borne down, and made subject to our enemies, and are become weak and powerless.
live.3-maccabees|2:14: We being in this low condition, this bold and profane man seeks to dishonour this thy holy place, consecrated out of the earth to the name of thy Majesty.
live.3-maccabees|2:15: Thy dwelling-place, the heaven of heavens, is indeed unapproachable to men.
live.3-maccabees|2:16: But since it seemed good to thee to exhibit thy glory among thy people Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst sanctify this place.
live.3-maccabees|2:17: Punish us not by means of the uncleanness of their men, nor chastise us by means of their profanity; lest the lawless ones should boast in their rage, and exult in exuberant pride of speech, and say,
live.3-maccabees|2:18: We have trampled upon the holy house, as idolatrous houses are trampled upon.
live.3-maccabees|2:19: Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and shew forth thy compassion in this hour.
live.3-maccabees|2:20: Let thy mercies quickly go before us. Grant us peace, that the cast down and broken hearted may praise thee with their mouth.
live.3-maccabees|2:21: At that time Elohim (God), who seeth all things, who is beyond all Holy among the holy, heard that prayer, so suitable; and scourged the man greatly uplifted with scorn and insolence.
live.3-maccabees|2:22: Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech.
live.3-maccabees|2:23: His friends and body-guards, beholding the swift recompense which had suddenly overtaken him, struck with exceeding terror, and fearing that he would die, speedily removed him.
live.3-maccabees|2:24: When in course of time he had come to himself, this severe check caused no repentance within him, but he departed with bitter threatenings.
live.3-maccabees|2:25: He proceeded to Egypt, grew worse in wickedness through his beforementioned companions in wine, who were lost to all goodness;
live.3-maccabees|2:26: and not satisfied with countless acts of impiety, his audacity so increased that he raised evil reports there, and many of his friends, watching his purpose attentively, joined in furthering his will.
live.3-maccabees|2:27: His purpose was to inflict a public stigma upon our race; wherefore he erected a pillar at the tower-porch, and caused the following inscription to be engraven upon it:
live.3-maccabees|2:28: That entrance to their own temple was to be refused to all those who would not sacrifice; that all the Yahudim (Jews) were to be registered among the common people; that those who resisted were to be forcibly seized and put to death;
live.3-maccabees|2:29: that those who were thus registered, were to be marked on their persons by the ivy-leaf symbol of Dionysus, and to be set apart with these limited rights.
live.3-maccabees|2:30: To do away with the appearance of hating them all, he had it written underneath, that if any of them should elect to enter the community of those initiated in the rites, these should have equal rights with the Alexandrians.
live.3-maccabees|2:31: Some of those who were over the city, therefore, abhorring any approach to the city of piety, unhesitatingly gave in to the king, and expected to derive some great honour from a future connection with him.
live.3-maccabees|2:32: A nobler spirit, however, prompted the majority to cling to their religious observances, and by paying money that they might live unmolested, these sought to escape the registration:
live.3-maccabees|2:33: cheerfully looking forward to future aid, they abhorred their own apostates, considering them to be national foes, and debarring them from the common usages of social intercourse.
live.3-maccabees|3:1: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Yahudim (Jews) in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
live.3-maccabees|3:2: While this was going on, an invidious rumour was uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Yahudi (Jewish) race. The purport of their charge was, that the Yahudim (Jews) kept them away from the ordinances of the law.
live.3-maccabees|3:3: Now, while the Yahudim (Jews) always maintained a feeling of unswerving loyalty towards the kings,
live.3-maccabees|3:4: yet, as they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium;
live.3-maccabees|3:5: although, as they adorned their conversation with works of righteousness, they had established themselves in the good opinion of the world.
live.3-maccabees|3:6: What all the rest of mankind said, was, however, made of no account by the foreigners;
live.3-maccabees|3:7: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Yahudim (Jews) with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them.
live.3-maccabees|3:8: Nor was this unexpected uproar and sudden conflux of people unobserved by the Greeks who lived in the city, concerning men who had never harmed them: yet to aid them was not in their power, since all was oppression around; but they encouraged the Yahudim (Jews) by sympathizing with them in their troubles, and expected a favourable turn of affairs:
live.3-maccabees|3:9: He who knoweth all things, will not, said they , disregard so great a people.
live.3-maccabees|3:10: Some of the neighbours, friends, and fellow dealers of the Yahudim (Jews), even called them secretly to an interview, pledged them their assistance, and promised to do their very utmost for them.
live.3-maccabees|3:11: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of Elohim (God), but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Yahudim (Jews).
live.3-maccabees|3:12: King Ptolemy Philopater, to the commanders and soldiers in Egypt, and in all places, health and happiness!
live.3-maccabees|3:13: I am right well; and so, too, are my affairs.
live.3-maccabees|3:14: Since our Asiatic campaign, the particulars of which ye know, and which by the aid of the gods, not lightly given, and by our own vigour, has been brought to a successful issue according to our expectation,
live.3-maccabees|3:15: we resolved, not with strength of spear, but with gentleness and much humanity, as it were to nurse the inhabitants of Cœle-Syria and Phœnicia, and to be their willing benefactors.
live.3-maccabees|3:16: So, having bestowed considerable sums of money upon the temples of the several cities, we proceeded even as far as Jerusalem; and went up to honour the temple of these wretched beings who never cease from their folly.
live.3-maccabees|3:17: To outward appearance they received us willingly; but belied that appearance by their deeds. When we were eager to enter their temple, and to honour it with the most beautiful and exquisite gifts,
live.3-maccabees|3:18: they were so carried away by their old arrogance, as to forbid us the entrance; while we, out of our forbearance toward all men, refrained from exercising our power upon them.
live.3-maccabees|3:19: And thus, exhibiting their enmity against us, they alone among the nations lift up their heads against kings and benefactors, as men unwilling to submit to any thing reasonable.
live.3-maccabees|3:20: We then, having endeavoured to make allowance for the madness of these persons, and on our victorious return treating all people in Egypt courteously, acted in a manner which was befitting.
live.3-maccabees|3:21: Accordingly, bearing no ill-will against their kinsmen [at Jerusalem], but rather remembering our connection with them, and the numerous matters with sincere heart from a remote period entrusted to them, we wished to venture a total alteration of their state, by bestowing upon them the rights of citizens of Alexandria, and to admit them to the everlasting rites of our solemnities.
live.3-maccabees|3:22: All this, however, they have taken in a very different spirit. With their innate malignity, they have spurned the fair offer; and constantly inclining to evil,
live.3-maccabees|3:23: have rejected the inestimable rights. Not only so, but by using speech, and by refraining from speech, they abhor the few among them who are heartily disposed towards us; ever deeming that their ignoble course of procedure will force us to do away with our reform.
live.3-maccabees|3:24: Having then, received certain proofs that these Yahudim (Jews) bear us every sort of ill-will, we must look forward to the possibility of some sudden tumult among ourselves, when these impious men may turn traitors and barbarous enemies.
live.3-maccabees|3:25: As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Yahudim (Jews) who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected.
live.3-maccabees|3:26: For by the punishment of them in one body we perceive that we have found the only means of establishing our affairs for the future on a firm and satisfactory basis.
live.3-maccabees|3:27: Whoever shall shield a Yahudi (Jew), whether it be old man, child, or suckling, shall with his whole house be tortured to death.
live.3-maccabees|3:28: Whoever shall inform against the Yahudim (Jews) , besides receiving the property of the person charged, shall be presented with two thousand drachmæ from the royal treasury, shall be made free, and shall be crowned.
live.3-maccabees|3:29: Whatever place shall shelter a Yahudi (Jew), shall, when he is hunted forth, be put under the ban of fire, and be for ever rendered useless to every living being for all time to come.
live.3-maccabees|3:30: Such was the purport of the king's letter.
live.3-maccabees|4:1: Wherever this decree was received, the people kept up a revelry of joy and shouting; as if their long-pent-up, hardened hatred, were now to shew itself openly.
live.3-maccabees|4:2: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
live.3-maccabees|4:3: What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation?
live.3-maccabees|4:4: They were sent out unanimously by the generals in the several cities, with such stern and pitiless feeling, that the exceptional nature of the infliction moved even some of their enemies. These, influenced by sentiments of common humanity, and reflecting upon the uncertain issue of life, shed tears at this their miserable expulsion.
live.3-maccabees|4:5: A multitude of aged hoary-haired men, were driven along with halting bending feet, urged onward by the impulse of a violent, shameless force to quick speed.
live.3-maccabees|4:6: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled, and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn.
live.3-maccabees|4:7: Bound, and exposed to public gaze, they were hurried violently on board ship.
live.3-maccabees|4:8: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand.
live.3-maccabees|4:9: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
live.3-maccabees|4:10: The planks of the deck above them barred out the light, and shut out the day on every side, so that they might be treated like traitors during the whole voyage.
live.3-maccabees|4:11: They were conveyed accordingly in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces; nay, were deemed unworthy of any civilized accommodation.
live.3-maccabees|4:12: When this was done, the king, hearing that their brethren in the city often went out and lamented the melancholy distress of these victims,
live.3-maccabees|4:13: was full of rage, and commanded that they should be carefully subjected to the same (and not one whit milder) treatment.
live.3-maccabees|4:14: The whole nation was now to be registered. Every individual was to be specified by name; not for that hard servitude of labour which we have a little before mentioned, but that he might expose them to the before-mentioned tortures; and finally, in the short space of a day, might extirpate them by his cruelties.
live.3-maccabees|4:15: The registering of these men was carried on cruelly, zealously, assiduously, from the rising of the sun to its going down, and was not brought to an end in forty days.
live.3-maccabees|4:16: The king was filled with great and constant joy, and celebrated banquets before the temple idols. His erring heart, far from the truth, and his profane mouth, gave glory to idols, deaf and incapable of speaking or aiding, and uttered unworthy speech against the Greatest Elohim (God).
live.3-maccabees|4:17: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Yahudim (Jews) was too great for registration,
live.3-maccabees|4:18: inasmuch as there were many still left in the land, of whom some were in inhabited houses, and others were scattered about in various places; so that all the commanders in Egypt were insufficient for the work.
live.3-maccabees|4:19: The king threatened them, and charged them with taking bribes, in order to contrive the escape of the Yahudim (Jews) : but was clearly convinced of the truth of what had been said.
live.3-maccabees|4:20: They said, and proved, that paper and pens had failed them for the carrying out of their purpose.
live.3-maccabees|4:21: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
live.3-maccabees|5:1: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
live.3-maccabees|5:2: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine and handfuls of incense [infused] to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious draughts of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Yahudim (Jews).
live.3-maccabees|5:3: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Yahudim (Jews) the most.
live.3-maccabees|5:4: The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually.
live.3-maccabees|5:5: The underlings appointed for the purpose went out about eventide and bound the hands of the miserable victims, and took other precautions for their security at night, thinking that the whole race would perish together.
live.3-maccabees|5:6: The heathen believed the Yahudim (Jews) to be destitute of all protection; for chains fettered them about.
live.3-maccabees|5:7: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah (Lord), and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim (God) and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah (Lord) of every power,
live.3-maccabees|5:8: to overthrow the evil purpose which was gone out against them, and to deliver them by extraordinary manifestation from that death which was in store for them.
live.3-maccabees|5:9: Their litany so earnest went up to heaven.
live.3-maccabees|5:10: Then Hermon, who had filled his merciless elephants with copious draughts of mingled wine and frankincense, came early to the palace to certify the king thereof.
live.3-maccabees|5:11: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time, by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion thereof [now] upon the king.
live.3-maccabees|5:12: By this sweet and profound influence of Yahuah (Lord) he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.
live.3-maccabees|5:13: But the Yahudim (Jews), having escaped the hour which had been fixed, praised their holy Elohim (God), and again prayed him who is easily reconciled to display the power of his powerful hand to the overweening Gentiles.
live.3-maccabees|5:14: The middle of the tenth hour had well nigh arrived, when the master-bidder, seeing the guests who were bidden collected, came and shook the king.
live.3-maccabees|5:15: He gained his attention with difficulty, and hinting that the mealtime was getting past, talked the matter over with him.
live.3-maccabees|5:16: The king listened to this, and then turning aside to his potations, commanded the guests to sit down before him.
live.3-maccabees|5:17: This done, he asked them to enjoy themselves, and to indulge in mirth at this somewhat late hour of the banquet.
live.3-maccabees|5:18: Conversation grew on, and the king sent for Hermon, and enquired of him, with fierce denunciations, why the Yahudim (Jews) had been allowed to outlive that day.
live.3-maccabees|5:19: Hermon explained that he had done his bidding over night; and in this he was confirmed by his friends.
live.3-maccabees|5:20: The king, then, with a barbarity exceeding that of Phalaris, said, That they might thank his sleep of that day. Lose no time, and get ready the elephants against to-morrow, as you did before, for the destruction of these accursed Yahudim (Jews).
live.3-maccabees|5:21: When the king said this, the company present were glad, and approved; and then each man went to his own home.
live.3-maccabees|5:22: Nor did they employ the night in sleep, so much as in contriving cruel mockeries for those deemed miserable.
live.3-maccabees|5:23: The morning cock had just crowed, and Hermon, having harnessed the brutes, was stimulating them in the great colonnade.
live.3-maccabees|5:24: The city crowds were collected together to see the hideous spectacle, and waited impatiently for the dawn.
live.3-maccabees|5:25: The Yahudim (Jews), breathless with momentary suspense, stretched forth their hands, and prayed the Greatest Elohim (God), in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.
live.3-maccabees|5:26: The sun's rays were not yet shed abroad, and the king was waiting for his friends, when Hermon came to him, calling him out, and saying, That his desires could now be realized.
live.3-maccabees|5:27: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unwonted exit; and, overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, enquired the object of this earnest preparation.
live.3-maccabees|5:28: But this was the working of that El Shaddai (Almighty God) who had made him forget all his purpose.
live.3-maccabees|5:29: Hermon, and all his friends, pointed out the preparation of the animals. They are ready, O king, according to your own strict injunction.
live.3-maccabees|5:30: The king was filled with fierce anger at these words; for, by the Providence of Elohim (God) regarding these things, his mind had become entirely confused. He looked hard at Hermon, and threatened him as follows:
live.3-maccabees|5:31: Your parents, or your children, were they here, to these wild beasts a large repast they should have furnished; not these innocent Yahudim (Jews), who me and my forefathers loyally have served.
live.3-maccabees|5:32: Had it not been for familiar friendship, and the claims of your office, your life should have gone for theirs.
live.3-maccabees|5:33: Hermon, being threatened in this unexpected and alarming manner, was troubled in visage, and depressed in countenance.
live.3-maccabees|5:34: The friends, too, stole out one by one, and dismissed the assembled multitudes to their occupations.
live.3-maccabees|5:35: The Yahudim (Jews), having heard of these events, praised the glorious Elohim (God) and King of kings, because they had obtained this help, too, from him.
live.3-maccabees|5:36: Now the king arranged another banquet after the same manner, and proclaimed an invitation to mirth.
live.3-maccabees|5:37: And he summoned Hermon to his presence, and said, with threats, How often, O wretch, must I repeat my orders to thee about these same persons?
live.3-maccabees|5:38: Once more, arm the elephants against the morrow for the extermination of the Yahudim (Jews).
live.3-maccabees|5:39: His kinsmen, who were reclining with him, wondered at his instability, and thus expressed themselves:
live.3-maccabees|5:40: O king, how long dost thou make trial of us, as of men bereft of reason? This is the third time that thou hast ordered their destruction. When the thing is to be done, thou changest thy mind, and recallest thy instructions.
live.3-maccabees|5:41: For this cause the feeling of expectation causes tumult in the city: it swarms with factions; and is continually on the point of being plundered.
live.3-maccabees|5:42: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Yahudim (Jews). He swore a fruitless oath, and determined forthwith to send them to Hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.
live.3-maccabees|5:43: He would also invade Judea, and level its towns with fire and the sword; and destroy that temple which the heathen might not enter, and prevent sacrifices ever after being offered up there.
live.3-maccabees|5:44: Joyfully his friends broke up, together with his kinsmen; and, trusting in his determination, arranged their forces in guard at the most convenient places of the city.
live.3-maccabees|5:45: And the master of the elephants urged the beasts into an almost maniacal state, drenched them with incense and wine, and decked them with frightful instruments.
live.3-maccabees|5:46: About early morning, when the city was now filled with an immense number of people at the hippodrome, he entered the palace, and called the king to the business in hand.
live.3-maccabees|5:47: The king's heart teemed with impious rage; and he rushed forth with the mass, along with the elephants. With feelings unsoftened, and eyes pitiless, he longed to gaze at the hard and wretched doom of the above-mentioned Yahudim (Jews) .
live.3-maccabees|5:48: But the Yahudim (Jews) , when the elephants went out at the gate, followed by the armed force; and when they saw the dust raised by the throng, and heard the loud cries of the crowd,
live.3-maccabees|5:49: thought that they had come to the last moment of their lives, to the end of what they had tremblingly expected. They gave way, therefore, to lamentations and moans: they kissed each other: those nearest of kin to each other hung about one another's necks: fathers about their sons, mothers their daughters: other women held their infants to their breasts, which drew what seemed their last milk.
live.3-maccabees|5:50: Nevertheless, when they reflected upon the succour before granted them from heaven, they prostrated themselves with one accord; removed even the sucking children from the breast, and
live.3-maccabees|5:51: sent up an exceeding great cry, entreating Yahuah (Lord) of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of Hades.
live.3-maccabees|6:1: And Eleazar, an illustrious priest of the country, who had attained to length of days, and whose life had been adorned with virtue, caused the presbyters who were about him to cease to cry out to the holy Elohim (God), and prayed thus:
live.3-maccabees|6:2: O King, mighty in power, most high, El Shaddai (Almighty God), who regulatest the whole creation with thy tender mercy,
live.3-maccabees|6:3: look upon the seed of Abraham, upon the children of the sanctified Jacob, thy sanctified inheritance, O Father, now being wrongfully destroyed as strangers in a strange land.
live.3-maccabees|6:4: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.
live.3-maccabees|6:5: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah (Lord), didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.
live.3-maccabees|6:6: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.
live.3-maccabees|6:7: It was thou who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, didst bring him back again unhurt to light.
live.3-maccabees|6:8: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
live.3-maccabees|6:9: And now, thou who hatest insolence; thou who dost abound in mercy; thou who art the protector of all things; appear quickly to those of the race of Yashar'el (Israel), who are insulted by abhorred, lawless Gentiles.
live.3-maccabees|6:10: If our life has during our exile been stained with iniquity, deliver us from the hand of the enemy, and destroy us, O Yahuah (Lord), by the death which thou preferrest.
live.3-maccabees|6:11: Let not the vain-minded congratulate vain idols at the destruction of thy beloved, saying, Neither did their Elohim (God) deliver them.
live.3-maccabees|6:12: Thou who art All-powerful and Almighty, O Eternal One, behold! have mercy upon us who are being withdrawn from life, like traitors, by the unreasoning insolence of lawless men.
live.3-maccabees|6:13: Let the heathen cower before thy invincible might to-day, O glorious One, who hast all power to save the race of Jacob.
live.3-maccabees|6:14: The whole band of infants and their parents with tears beseech thee.
live.3-maccabees|6:15: Let it be shewn to all the nations that thou art with us, O Yahuah (Lord), and hast not turned thy face away from us; but as thou saidst that thou wouldst not forget them even in the land of their enemies, so do thou fulfil this saying, O Yahuah (Lord).
live.3-maccabees|6:16: Now, at the time that Eleazar had ended his prayer, the king came along to the hippodrome, with the wild beasts, and with his tumultuous power.
live.3-maccabees|6:17: When the Yahudim (Jews) saw this, they uttered a loud cry to heaven, so that the adjacent valleys resounded, and caused an irrepressible lamentation throughout the army.
live.3-maccabees|6:18: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
live.3-maccabees|6:19: And they stood opposite, and filled the enemies' host with confusion and cowardice; and bound them with immoveable fetters.
live.3-maccabees|6:20: And a cold shudder came over the person of the king, and oblivion paralysed the vehemence of his spirit.
live.3-maccabees|6:21: They turned back the animals upon the armed forces which followed them; and the animals trod them down, and destroyed them.
live.3-maccabees|6:22: The king's wrath was converted into compassion; and he wept at his own machinations.
live.3-maccabees|6:23: For when he heard the cry, and saw them all on the verge of destruction, with tears he angrily threatened his friends, saying,
live.3-maccabees|6:24: Ye have governed badly; and have exceeded tyrants in cruelty; and me your benefactor ye have laboured to deprive at once of my dominion and my life, by secretly devising measures injurious to the kingdom.
live.3-maccabees|6:25: Who has gathered here, unreasonably removing each from his home, those who, in fidelity to us, had held the fortresses of the country?
live.3-maccabees|6:26: Who has thus consigned to unmerited punishments those who in good will towards us from the beginning have in all things surpassed all nations, and who often have engaged in the most dangerous undertakings?
live.3-maccabees|6:27: Loose, loose the unjust bonds; send them to their homes in peace, and deprecate what has been done.
live.3-maccabees|6:28: Release the sons of the almighty living Elohim (God) of heaven, who from our ancestors' times until now has granted a glorious and uninterrupted prosperity to our affairs.
live.3-maccabees|6:29: These things he said: and they, released the same moment, having now escaped death, praised Elohim (God) their holy Saviour.
live.3-maccabees|6:30: The king then departed to the city, and called his financier to him, and bade him provide a seven days' quantity of wine and other materials for feasting for the Yahudim (Jews). He decided that they should keep a gladsome festival of deliverance in the very place in which they expected to meet with their destruction.
live.3-maccabees|6:31: Then they who were before despised and nigh unto Hades, yea, rather advanced into it, partook of the cup of salvation, instead of a grievous and lamentable death. Full of exultation, they parted out the place intended for their fall and burial into banqueting booths.
live.3-maccabees|6:32: Ceasing their miserable strain of woe, they took up the subject of their fatherland, hymning in praise Elohim (God) their wonder-working Saviour. All groans, all wailing, were laid aside: they formed dances in token of serene joy.
live.3-maccabees|6:33: So, also, the king collected a number of guests for the occasion, and returned unceasing thanks with much magnificence for the unexpected deliverance afforded him.
live.3-maccabees|6:34: Those who had marked them out as for death and for carrion, and had registered them with joy, howled aloud, and were clothed with shame, and had the fire of their rage ingloriously put out.
live.3-maccabees|6:35: But the Yahudim (Jews), as we just said, instituted a dance, and then gave themselves up to feasting, glad thanksgivings, and psalms.
live.3-maccabees|6:36: They made a public ordinance to commemorate these things for generations to come, as long as they should be sojourners. They thus established these days as days of mirth, not for the purpose of drinking or luxury, but because Elohim (God) had saved them.
live.3-maccabees|6:37: They requested the king to send them back to their homes.
live.3-maccabees|6:38: They were being enrolled from the twenty-fifth of Pachon to the fourth of Epiphi, a period of forty days: the measures taken for their destruction lasted from the fifth of Epiphi till the seventh, that is, three days.
live.3-maccabees|6:39: The Ruler over all did during this time manifest forth his mercy gloriously, and did deliver them all together unharmed.
live.3-maccabees|6:40: They feasted upon the king's provision up to the fourteenth day, and then asked to be sent away.
live.3-maccabees|6:41: The king commended them, and wrote the subjoined letter, of magnanimous import for them, to the commanders of every city.
live.3-maccabees|7:1: King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders throughout Egypt, and to all who are set over affairs, joy and strength.
live.3-maccabees|7:2: We, too, and our children are well; and Elohim (God) has directed our affairs as we wish.
live.3-maccabees|7:3: Certain of our friends did of malice vehemently urge us to punish the Yahudim (Jews) of our realm in a body, with the infliction of a monstrous punishment.
live.3-maccabees|7:4: They pretended that our affairs would never be in a good state till this took place. Such, they said, was the hatred borne by the Yahudim (Jews) to all other people.
live.3-maccabees|7:5: They brought them fettered in grievous chains as slaves, nay, as traitors. Without enquiry or examination they endeavoured to annihilate them. They buckled themselves with a savage cruelty, worse than Scythian custom.
live.3-maccabees|7:6: For this cause we severely threatened them; yet, with the clemency which we are wont to extend to all men, we at length permitted them to live. Finding that the Elohim (God) of heaven cast a shield of protection over the Yahudim (Jews) so as to preserve them, and that he fought for them as a father always fights for his sons;
live.3-maccabees|7:7: and taking into consideration their constancy and fidelity towards us and towards our ancestors, we have, as we ought, acquitted them of every sort of charge.
live.3-maccabees|7:8: And we have dismissed them to their several homes; bidding all men everywhere to do them no wrong, or unrighteously revile them about the past.
live.3-maccabees|7:9: For know ye, that should we conceive any evil design against, or in any manner aggrieve them, we shall ever have as our opposite, not man, but the highest Elohim (God), the ruler of all might. From Him there will be no escape, as the avenger of such deeds. Fare ye well.
live.3-maccabees|7:10: When they had received this letter, they were not forward to depart immediately. They petitioned the king to be allowed to inflict fitting punishment upon those of their race who had willingly transgressed the holy Elohim (God), and the law of Elohim (God).
live.3-maccabees|7:11: They alleged that men who had for their bellies' sake transgressed the ordinances of Elohim (God), would never be faithful to the interests of the king.
live.3-maccabees|7:12: The king admitted the truth of this reasoning, and commended them. Full power was given them, without warrant or special commission, to destroy those who had transgressed the law of Elohim (God) boldly in every part of the king's dominions.
live.3-maccabees|7:13: Their priests, then, as it was meet, saluted him with good wishes, and all the people echoed with the Hallelujah. They then joyfully departed.
live.3-maccabees|7:14: Then they punished and destroyed with ignominy every polluted Yahudi (Jew) that fell in their way;
live.3-maccabees|7:15: slaying thus, in that day, above three hundred men, and esteeming this destruction of the wicked a season of joy.
live.3-maccabees|7:16: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
live.3-maccabees|7:17: Having arrived at Ptolemais, called from the specialty of that district Rose-bearing, where the fleet, in accordance with the general wish, waited for them seven days,
live.3-maccabees|7:18: they partook of a banquet of deliverance, for the king generously granted them severally the means of securing a return home.
live.3-maccabees|7:19: They were accordingly brought back in peace, while they gave utterance to becoming thanks; and they determined to keep these days during their sojourn as days of joyfulness.
live.3-maccabees|7:20: These they registered as sacred upon a pillar, when they had dedicated the place of their festivity to be one of prayer. They departed unharmed, free, abundant in joy, preserved by the king's command, by land, by sea, and by river, each to his own home.
live.3-maccabees|7:21: They had more weight than before among their enemies; and were honoured and feared, and no one in any way robbed them of their goods.
live.3-maccabees|7:22: Every man received back his own, according to inventory; those who had obtained their goods, giving them up with the greatest terror. For the greatest Elohim (God) wrought with perfectness wonders for their salvation.
live.3-maccabees|7:23: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) unto everlasting. Amen.

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | No man... but he hath dealt wickedly — the universal verdict pre-Paul
cards.s_text: For in truth them is no man among them that be born, but he has dealt wickedly; and among the faithful there is none which has not done amiss.
cards.t_text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God);

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | Who is there alive that hath not sinned — the leveling baseline before Paul
cards.s_text: I answered then and said, This is my first and last saying, that it had been better not to have given the earth to Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.
cards.t_text: As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one:

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | How did they not sooner find out Yahuah (the Lord) — without-excuse, source argument
cards.s_text: For if they were able to know so much, that they could aim at the world; how did they not sooner find out Yahuah (God) thereof?
cards.t_text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned — the Romans 1 argument before Romans 1
cards.s_text: Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned.
cards.t_text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | We are all worthy of punishment — the universal verdict in wisdom register
cards.s_text: Reproach not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
cards.t_text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God);

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | Righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces — Baruch echoes Daniel verbatim
cards.s_text: And you shall say, To Yahuah (God), our Elohim (God) belongeth righteousness, but to us the confusion of faces, as it is come to pass this day, to them of Juda, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
cards.t_text: O Adonai (Lord), righteousness belongs unto you, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Yahudah (Judah), and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Yashar'el (Israel), that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither you have driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against you.

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | Forgive me, I humbly beseech thee — Manasseh's confession in Daniel-style posture
cards.s_text: I have sinned, O Yahuah (God), I have sinned, and I acknowledge my iniquities:
cards.t_text: We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from your precepts and from your judgments:

cards.note: thread:effort-over-accomplishment | I have sinned, I acknowledge mine iniquities — the model return-prayer matches the new heart's loathing
cards.s_text: Now therefore I bow the knee of my heart, beseeching you of grace.
cards.t_text: Then shall you remember your own evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and shall lothe yourselves in your own sight for your iniquities and for your abominations.

cards.note: *Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.* Ecclesiasticus 44's *Praise of Famous Men* walks the Hebrew library's celebration of the same genealogical line — Avraham (Abraham), Yitschaq (Isaac), Ya'aqov (Jacob), Mosheh (Moses), down through David and the prophets. The Hebrew library knew the line as a thing to praise; Matthew opens his gospel with the same line restored and crowned.
cards.s_text: The book of the generation of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), the son of David, the son of Abraham.
cards.t_text: Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.

cards.note: *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:1). *In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea,* (Matthew 3:1). Sirach opens his praise of Elijah with fire: he stood up as fire and his word burned like a lamp. Matthew opens John's ministry in the wilderness, and the fire is already there in what he says, *O generation of vipers* and *he shall baptize you with the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Ghost), and with fire* (Matthew 3:7, 11). The angel had told Zacharias his son would go before Yahuah (God) in the spirit and power of Elias (Luke 1:17), and Yahusha (Jesus) later says it plainly, *this is Elias, which was for to come* (Matthew 11:14). The prophet who stood up as fire has stood up again in the wilderness of Judaea.
cards.s_text: In those days came John the Baptist, preaching in the wilderness of Judaea,
cards.t_text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.

cards.note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of Yahuah (Lord), make his paths straight.* (Matthew 3:3). Sirach is drawing on Malachi, *he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children* (Malachi 4:6), and then he says what Malachi's Elijah is for: to restore the tribes of Jacob. Not Yahudah (Judah) only, the tribes. That is the errand John steps into when he stands in the wilderness as the voice Isaiah heard, preparing the way of Yahuah (Lord). Preparing the way is the beginning of the Elijah work; the end of it is the scattered tribes of Jacob brought home, and the one whose way John prepared is the one who gathers them.
cards.s_text: For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare you the way of Yahuah (Lord), make his paths straight.
cards.t_text: Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

cards.note: *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* The fire-baptism Yochanan (John) announces at Matt 3:11 — *he shall immerse you with the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), and with fire* — sits inside the Hebrew library's prophet-as-fire register. Ecclesiasticus reads Eliyahu (Elijah) as fire and his word as a burning lamp; Yochanan (John) names the one mightier than he as bringing the Ruach-and-fire register the Eliyahu (Elijah)-pattern had carried in shadow.
cards.s_text: I indeed baptize you with water unto repentance: but he that comes after me is mightier than I, whose shoes I am not worthy to bear: he shall baptize you with the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), and with fire:
cards.t_text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.

cards.note: *Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: while he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:12). *Then cometh Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.* (Matthew 3:13). The whirlwind took Elijah at the Jordan, and Elisha came back across the same river carrying his spirit (2 Kings 2:8–15). Sirach adds that no prince could move Elijah while he lived. Now Yahusha (Jesus) comes from Galilee to the Jordan, to a man no prince could move either, the John who would shortly tell Herod his marriage was unlawful. At that river the heavens open and the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) comes down on him (Matthew 3:16). The Jordan is where the prophetic spirit passed from Elijah to Elisha, and it is where the Spirit rests on the one Elijah's successor was sent to announce.
cards.s_text: Then comes Yahusha (Jesus) from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him.
cards.t_text: Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: while he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.

cards.note: *For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled...* Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 begins the Hebrew library's longest single Spirit-characterization — twenty-one attributes of the Ruach (Spirit) in three verses. The Spirit Matthew names descending dove-form at Matt 3:16 is the same Ruach the Hebrew library had been characterizing in the Wisdom literature for centuries before the gospel.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
cards.t_text: For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good,

cards.note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* Wisdom 7:25 names the Spirit as *the breath of the power of Yahuah* — the Ruach in the literal Hebrew-breath sense, the divine animating presence proceeding from the Father. The dove-descent at Matt 3:16 is the visible form of this breath landing on the Formed in flesh. The Hebrew library's framework — the Ruach as Yahuah's own breath, not as a third co-equal person of a later Trinitarian grid — is the framework the gospel inherits.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
cards.t_text: For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.
