cards.note: *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon them...* 2 Baruch 35:1 — the same eschatological-harvest-of-the-age verse also anchors Matt 9:38's *pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers.* The Lord-of-the-harvest is the Mighty One the apocalyptic-stream had named; the labourers being prayed-for are about to be commissioned at Matt 10:1.
cards.s_text: Pray you therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.
cards.t_text: Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.

cards.note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). The souls of the righteous in their chambers ask how long, and when comes the fruit of the floor, the threshing floor where the reward is given. The King looks out over the multitudes and says the harvest is plenteous and the labourers few. Both speak of one harvest. The souls are asking when the floor will be filled; the King is sending men into the field to fill it, and the next verse in 2 Esdras gives the answer the souls received, when the number of seeds is filled. The waiting dead and the working living are looking toward the same floor from opposite sides of it.
cards.s_text: Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
cards.t_text: Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?

cards.note: *And to these things Uriel the archangel gave them answer, and said, Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* (2 Esdras 4:36). *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38). Uriel's answer to the waiting souls is a number: the harvest comes when the number of seeds is filled, and he has weighed the world in the balance. The King's answer to a plenteous harvest with few labourers is a prayer: ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest to send forth labourers. The number is his and the timing is his, but the gathering is done by hands he sends, and the labourers he sends are how the seeds are filled up to the number. Esdras was shown why the end waits; the disciples were told what to do while it does.
cards.s_text: Pray you therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.
cards.t_text: And to these things Uriel the archangel gave them answer, and said, Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.

cards.note: *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* 2 Baruch 38:4 names the twelve-tribes-bound-by-one-bond architecture in the wisdom-stream's apocalyptic register — all the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, born from one father. The framework's gathering-thesis holds the twelve-tribe-restoration as the load-bearing prophetic substance; Matt 9:36's *sheep having no shepherd* multitudes are the same twelve-tribe-bound-by-one-bond body the wisdom-stream had named.
cards.s_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
cards.t_text: And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.

cards.note: *He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* 2 Baruch 38:7 (epistle to the nine-and-a-half scattered tribes across the Euphrates) names the wisdom-stream's gathering-of-the-dispersed-with-much-mercy architecture explicitly. The much-mercy register at 2 Baruch 38:7 is the same mercy-substance Hosea 6:6 names at Matt 9:13; the gathering-of-the-dispersed IS the mercy-architecture of the kingdom-at-hand.
cards.s_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
cards.t_text: For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Ezra is told plainly who the peaceable multitude of his vision is: the ten tribes Shalmaneser carried out of their own land and over the waters, who never came back. Those are the people the King means when he sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). A sheep is lost when it has wandered where the shepherd cannot see it, and the northern house had been lost in another land for seven centuries by the time Yahusha (Jesus) spoke these words. The mission of the twelve was aimed at the same body Ezra was shown.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.* (2 Esdras 13:41–42). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). The tribes did not simply vanish into the heathen. Ezra is told they took counsel to leave the multitude and go further out, into a country where no one lived, so that they could keep the statutes they had never kept in their own land. The carrying away became, for a remnant of them, a going out to keep Torah. Centuries later the King sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same body, in the lands it went out to. The commandments they carried into the far country are what the sheep are being called back to, and Yahusha (Jesus) sends his messengers after them rather than waiting for them to find the way home alone.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,

cards.note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). The Most High stayed the river once so the tribes could cross out, and Ezra is promised he will stay it again so they can cross back, in the latter time. That return is the end of the story the vision tells. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve they will not finish going over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) before the Son of Adam comes; the work he sends them on is not completed in their lifetime but runs until his coming. Set together, the two say the same thing: the going after the lost sheep and the gathering of the ten tribes are one work, begun with the sending and finished when the Highest opens the way home and the King returns.
cards.s_text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee you into another: for verily I say unto you, You shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.
cards.t_text: The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.

cards.note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Tobit lays out the whole order in one breath: Yahuah (God) scourges his people for their iniquities, has mercy again, and gathers them out of all the nations he scattered them into. The scourge was the scattering. The mercy is the gathering. When Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve, he points them at the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the very people Tobit said would be gathered, and the sending is that mercy beginning to move. The gathering Tobit prayed for as a thing still to come is the mission the King commissions.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

cards.note: *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them. There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Elohim (God), and he is Yahuah (God) our Father for ever.* (Tobit 13:3–4). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Tobit sings this from the land of the captivity, and the instruction is not to hide among the Gentiles but to confess Yahuah (God) in front of them, to declare his greatness in the very places he scattered his children into. Yahusha (Jesus) is sending the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in this same chapter, and he gives them the same charge with a promise attached: confess me before men, and I will confess you before my Father. The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King names them before the Father. The confession Tobit called for and the confession Yahusha (Jesus) rewards are one confession, made by the same scattered people in the same territories.
cards.s_text: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
cards.t_text: Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.

cards.note: *And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Yahuah (God) shall be built in it for ever with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.* (Tobit 14:5). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). Tobit, dying, tells his son there will be two returns, not one. First a return to the land and a temple not like the first, which is the house Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah raised after Babylon, a return of Yahudah (Judah) only. Then, after the time of that age is fulfilled, a return from all places of the captivity, Jerusalem built gloriously and the house of Yahuah (God) built in it for ever, as the prophets spoke. That second return has not happened. Between the two stands the work Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve into, and he tells them it will not be finished before the Son of Adam comes. The mission to the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) runs through this age toward the return Tobit saw at the end of it.
cards.s_text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee you into another: for verily I say unto you, You shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.
cards.t_text: And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Yahuah (God) shall be built in it for ever with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.

cards.note: *My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:1). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Sirach opens his second chapter by telling the one who comes to serve Yahuah (God) to expect temptation and get his soul ready for it, and the next line says how: set your heart aright, and constantly endure. Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve out with the same preparation. They will be hated for his name, and the one who endures to the end is the one who is saved. Neither voice promises the servant an easy road; both tie the outcome to endurance. The disciple's endurance is not something new the gospel invented; it is what serving Yahuah (God) has always asked, and Sirach had been saying so for generations before the twelve were sent.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Sirach says the furnace is where acceptable men are proved, the way fire proves gold. Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve into that furnace with his eyes open: hated of all men for his name, and saved by enduring to the end. The hatred is not a sign the mission failed; it is the fire doing what fire does, and the disciple who comes through it is shown to be what Sirach calls acceptable. Adversity in the service of Yahuah (God) is the trial, not the verdict.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:18). *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28). Those who fear Yahuah (God), Sirach says, would rather fall into his hands than into the hands of men, because his mercy is as great as his majesty. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the twelve the same choice with the stakes spelled out: men can kill the body and no more, while Yahuah (God) is able to destroy both soul and body in hell, so fear him and not them. Both verses move the fear off men and onto Yahuah (God), and both find that the safer place. The one whose hands hold the final judgment is the same one whose mercy matches his majesty, which is why falling into his hands is the choice of the one who fears him.
cards.s_text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
cards.t_text: Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28). Men can kill the body. Wisdom says what they cannot touch: the souls of the righteous, which are in the hand of Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same thing before sending them out among wolves — do not fear the ones who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul. The persecutor's reach stops where the Father's hand begins. The righteous who died under the ungodly in Wisdom 2 were not lost; they were kept.
cards.s_text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5). *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22). Wisdom calls the suffering of the righteous a proving: Yahuah (God) chastens a little, tests the metal, and finds them worthy of himself. Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples the same thing from the other side — you will be hated of all men for my name's sake, and the one who endures to the end will be saved. The hatred is the furnace; the enduring is what the furnace proves. The reward is great because the trial was real, and the Father is the one who did the proving.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.

cards.note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Wisdom looks to the day when the righteous man, whose labours his afflicters counted as nothing, stands in front of them in great boldness. The King gives his disciples the way into that day: confess him before men now, and he will confess them before the Father then. The confession is made in the face of the same people doing the afflicting, and the boldness Solomon saw is the boldness of the one being named by the Son in front of the Father while those who despised him look on.
cards.s_text: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
cards.t_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.

cards.note: *Therefore if ye have any engine of torment, apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.* 4 Maccabees (edition chapter 8, verses 4-5; standard 4 Macc 9:4-5) names the Hebrew library's most direct verbal-anchor for Matt 10:28's *fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.* The third son of the seven, under Antiochus's torture, names the diagnostic explicitly: the body can be reached by the engine of torment; the soul cannot. The framework reads the Matt 10:28 fear-redirect as the King naming the operative-fact the Hebrew library had already named at the martyrdom-witness. The persecutors reach the body; the soul is in another hand entirely.
cards.s_text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
cards.t_text: bond of brotherhood. Therefore if ye have any engine of torment, apply it to this body of mine; for

cards.note: *Her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God).* 4 Maccabees (edition chapter 11, verse 3; standard 4 Macc 15:3) names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture: the seven sons chose religion-which-saveth-unto-eternal-life over the tyrant's present-life-saving-promise. Matt 10:28's fear-redirect to the Father who-is-able-to-destroy-both-soul-and-body is the inverse-naming of the same priority: the kingdom-citizens choose the One who holds the eternal-stakes over the persecutors who hold only the present-life-stakes. The wisdom-stream had named the priority at the martyrdom-witness; the King at Matt 10:28 names it at the commissioning.
cards.s_text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
cards.t_text: her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal

cards.note: *For on that day virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* 4 Maccabees (edition chapter 13, verse 13; standard 4 Macc 17:13) names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture of the endurance-prize: virtue proves the martyrs through endurance, and the prize of victory is incorruption in everlasting life. Matt 10:22's *he that endureth to the end shall be saved* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens level. The endurance is the proving-substance; the prize is the everlasting-life-resurrection at the King's recognition. The wisdom-stream and the King name the same diagnostic.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: But the first in the fight was Eleazar, and the mother of the seven sons played her part, and the brethren fought.

cards.note: *The tyrant himself and his whole council admired their endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* 4 Maccabees (edition chapter 13, verse 18; standard 4 Macc 17:18) names the wisdom-stream's post-martyrdom-architecture explicitly: the endurance of the seven sons led to their standing beside the throne of Yahuah (God) and living the blessed age. The framework reads the verse against the Red Line #11 first-resurrection architecture: the martyrs who endure to the end are among the first-resurrection-firstfruits at the King's coming. Matt 10:22's endure-to-the-end and the Hebrews 11:39-40 *they without us should not be made perfect* and the Revelation 20:4-6 first-resurrection-of-the-beheaded all name the same architecture at different angles; 4 Macc 13:18 names it from the wisdom-stream side at the martyrdom-witness.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.

cards.note: *Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.* 4 Maccabees (edition chapter 8, verse 18; standard 4 Macc 9:18) names the wisdom-stream's direct architecture for Matt 10:20's *Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.* The third son under torture names the operative-fact: even with his tongue cut out, Yahuah (God) hears the speechless — the Father's direct-hearing of the persecuted-disciple does not depend on the disciple's organ of speech. Matt 10:19-20's *take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you* walks the same architecture at the kingdom-citizens persecution-encounter level. The Father's direct-presence in the persecution-hour does not depend on the disciple's pre-prepared-words.
cards.s_text: For it is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaks in you.
cards.t_text: But he said, ‘Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.

cards.note: *Then I answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?* (2 Esdras 4:33). *And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?* (Matthew 11:3). Esdras, shown the end and the threshing, asks the question anyone in distress asks: how, and when, and why are our years few and evil. John, in Herod's prison, sends to ask Yahusha (Jesus), art thou he that should come, or do we look for another. John had preached the axe at the root and the fan in the hand, and the fire had not fallen while he sat in chains. Neither question is unbelief. Both are the faithful asking the one who knows the times why the times are not yet what he said they would be.
cards.s_text: And said unto him, Are you he that should come, or do we look for another?
cards.t_text: Then I answered and said, How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?

cards.note: *And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.* (2 Esdras 4:34). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The angel's answer to Esdras is not a date; it is, do not hasten above the Most High, the times are his and your hurry cannot move them. The King's answer to John is not a date either; after naming the works being done he adds, blessed is he who is not offended in me. Both answers ask the same thing of the one waiting: that he not stumble over the gap between what was promised and what he can see from where he sits. The blessing is on the one who trusts the timing of Yahuah (God) when the timing is the hardest part.
cards.s_text: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
cards.t_text: And he answered me, saying, Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him, for you have much exceeded.

cards.note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). *And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.* (Matthew 11:6). The righteous dead ask from their chambers how long they must hope this way. John saw the same souls under the altar asking how long, O Yahuah (Lord), and they were told to rest a little while longer (Revelation 6:9–11). The King's word to John the Baptist in his prison is the word for everyone who waits: blessed is he who is not offended in me. The dead wait in their chambers, the living wait in their chains, and the blessing is on both for not letting the length of the wait turn into offense at the one who set its length.
cards.s_text: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
cards.t_text: Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?

cards.note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). When Yahusha (Jesus) says John is the Elias who was to come, he is pointing at a job description everyone in the crowd knew. Sirach had written it out: Elijah is ordained to reprove, to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. All of Jacob, all twelve tribes, the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah) together. John began that work at the Jordan; the full restoring of the tribes waits on the great and dreadful day Malachi set it beside (Malachi 4:5). *If ye will receive it* is the hard part, because receiving it means receiving that the gathering of a scattered people is what Elijah comes to do.
cards.s_text: And if you will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
cards.t_text: Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

cards.note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* (1 Maccabees 2:58). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). Mattathias remembers Elijah (Elias) for one thing: he was zealous and fervent for the law, and he was taken up into heaven. That is how the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) remembered him, as the man who stood for the commandments of Yahuah (God) against a kingdom that had traded them for Baal. When Yahusha (Jesus) says of John, this is Elijah (Elias) which was for to come, the likeness is that same zeal: John in the wilderness calling the leadership a generation of vipers, John in prison for telling Herod his marriage was unlawful. Elijah's zeal for the law is what Malachi promised would come before the great day, and it came first in John.
cards.s_text: And if you will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
cards.t_text: Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.

cards.note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The system faulted John for fasting and Yahusha (Jesus) for eating, which tells you the complaints were not the reason. Wisdom of Solomon gave the reason long before: the righteous one is clean contrary to our doings and upbraids us with our offending the law, so let us lie in wait for him. The glutton and winebibber charge is a cover for the grievance the ungodly admit among themselves, that his life exposes their departure from the Torah. *Wisdom is justified of her children* because wisdom's own book had already written the accusers' script.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.

cards.note: *He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:15). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom cannot even stand to look at the righteous man, because his life is cut to another pattern than theirs. That is the complaint behind the slander in Matthew: the Son of Adam sat at table with publicans and sinners, and the religious system of his day could only read a life of another fashion as gluttony and drunkenness. The charge changes its words from one age to the next, but it is the same offense — a righteous life reproves the ones watching it, and they answer by calling it unrighteous. Wisdom is justified of her children all the same.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: He is grievous to us even to behold: for his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.

cards.note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). The ungodly in Wisdom finish where they were always headed: condemn him to a shameful death. In Matthew 11 they are only at the beginning — calling him a glutton and a winebibber for sitting with sinners. The road runs from there to Matthew 12, where his works are credited to Beelzebub, and on to the trial and the cross in Matthew 26 and 27. A system that cannot deny what it sees moves from slander to false accusation to execution. Wisdom had named the end of that road before the gospel showed its first step.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.

cards.note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Wisdom calls out: come to me, all you who desire me, and fill yourselves with my fruits. Yahusha (Jesus) came eating and drinking, and the ones who came to him were the publicans and the sinners, while the system called him a glutton and a winebibber — and then he says wisdom is justified of her children. The children of wisdom are the ones who heard the call and came to be filled. The invitation Sirach wrote down is the one the Son of Adam spoke in Galilee, and his table was where the filling happened.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* (Baruch 3:36). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch says the whole way of knowledge was found out by Elohim (God) and then given, not to the world at large but to Jacob his servant and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved. Wisdom has a people she was given to. Yahusha (Jesus), reproached for eating with publicans and sinners, says wisdom is justified of her children: the ones who recognize her are her own. The children of wisdom in Matthew 11 are the covenant seed Baruch names, the people the knowledge was given to, and when the one who gave it stood among them in flesh they knew his voice even when the leaders did not. Her children are the proof she was given to Jacob.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.

cards.note: *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* (Baruch 4:1). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch names what the wisdom given to Jacob is: the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), the law that endures for ever, which gives life to those who keep it and death to those who leave it. Wisdom is not a mood or a philosophy; she is the Torah. So when Yahusha (Jesus) says wisdom is justified of her children, her children are the ones who keep the commandments. John says the same thing from the other side: *He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him* (1 John 2:4). The law that endureth for ever has not been set aside by the one who spoke it at Sinai and walked in Galilee; wisdom's children are known by keeping it.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

cards.note: *Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:5). *Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.* (Matthew 11:21). A sharp judgment belongs to those in high places. Chorazin and Bethsaida were set in a high place: the mighty works were done in their streets, and they did not repent. Tyre and Sidon, cities the prophets thundered against, would have been in sackcloth long ago if they had seen the same works. The more that is shown to a city or a man, the sharper the reckoning, and Solomon had written that rule before the King applied it to the towns he had been healing in.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, Chorazin! woe unto you, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
cards.t_text: Horribly and speedily shall he come upon you: for a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.

cards.note: *For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:6). *But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.* (Matthew 11:22). Mercy soon pardons the lowly; the mighty are mightily tormented. The King says it over the towns that saw his works: more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for you. The judgment is real and it has degrees. Those who were shown little answer for little; those who were shown the kingdom working in their own streets answer for that. It is not one flat torment for everyone and it is not nothing; it is weighed.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.
cards.t_text: For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.

cards.note: *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:8). *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23). A sore trial comes upon the mighty. Capernaum was mighty in the one way that counts in this chapter: it was exalted unto heaven, the King's own city where he lived and healed and taught. The sore trial for a city like that is to be brought down to hell, the grave, the place of the dead, lower than Sodom. The hell here is the pit the city goes down into, not the endless fire the pulpit reads into the word. Sodom would have stood if it had seen what Capernaum saw.
cards.s_text: And you, Capernaum, which are exalted unto heaven, shall be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in you, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.
cards.t_text: But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.

cards.note: *Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:7). *But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.* (Matthew 11:24). The waste land still smoking, the fruit that never ripens, the pillar of salt standing as a monument of an unbelieving soul: Sodom was still preaching in Solomon's day. The King uses that monument as the floor. If the works done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, Sodom would still be standing, and so it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for the town that saw the kingdom at work in its own streets and did not turn. The smoking land is the witness against the unbelieving soul; the city with the mighty works has a sharper witness against it.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for you.
cards.t_text: Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.

cards.note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Sirach says favour before Yahuah (God) runs toward the one who humbles himself, and the greater he is, the lower he should go. Yahusha (Jesus) thanks the Father for the same thing working: these things hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The wise and prudent are the ones who did not humble themselves, who came to the Father with their standing in hand, and the revelation went past them to the ones with nothing to defend. Sirach names the principle; the prayer in Matthew 11 shows it happening.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.
cards.t_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:19). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Sirach says it as plainly as it can be said: many are in high place and of renown, but mysteries are revealed to the meek. Yahusha (Jesus) prays the same pairing to the Father, hidden from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes. The meek in Sirach and the babes in Matthew are the same people, the ones with nothing to defend when the Father speaks, and the high and renowned are the same people as the wise and prudent, the ones whose standing fills the space where the hearing would be. The two verses line up in their shape, high against low, hidden against revealed, and they name one rule of how Yahuah (God) gives understanding.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.
cards.t_text: Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.

cards.note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:7). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Solomon prayed, and understanding was given him; he called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came. The King thanks the Father that these things were hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The two agree on where understanding comes from: it is given. Solomon asked and it was given him; the babes had nothing in hand and it was revealed to them; the wise and prudent, sure they already had it, were passed over.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank you, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because you have hid these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them unto babes.
cards.t_text: Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.

cards.note: *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:23). *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28). Sirach ends his book with an invitation: draw near, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning. Yahusha (Jesus) issues the same one, come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden. Sirach was pointing people toward Wisdom; the one who speaks in Matthew is the Wisdom who stood beside the Maker before the world was (Ecclesiasticus 24:9; Proverbs 8:22–30), now speaking in his own voice. The load his hearers carried was the burden the scribes bound on them, *heavy burdens and grievous to be borne* (Matthew 23:4), not the Torah itself. The rest he offers is in the house of learning, not outside it.
cards.s_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.t_text: Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.

cards.note: *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:26). *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* (Matthew 11:29). Sirach's yoke is instruction, and he tells the soul to receive it, so the rest he found was not rest from the yoke but rest under it. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same thing in the same order: take my yoke, learn of me, and you will find rest for your souls. He is quoting Jeremiah, *ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls* (Jeremiah 6:16). His yoke is not the absence of a yoke; it is the old path, his Father's commandments as he teaches and walks them, set in place of the heavy burdens the scribes had bound on men's shoulders (Matthew 23:4). Sirach put his neck under it and called it rest.
cards.s_text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and you shall find rest unto your souls.
cards.t_text: Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.

cards.note: *Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:27). *For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* (Matthew 11:30). Sirach is not theorizing; he points to his own life and says look, little labour, much rest, and his neck is still under the yoke when he says it. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same of his yoke: easy, and the burden light. Neither man is describing a life without commandments. Moses said the commandment *is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off* (Deuteronomy 30:11), and John says *his commandments are not grievous* (1 John 5:3). The heavy thing was never the Torah; it was what men added to it, and the one who gave it carries it lightly.
cards.s_text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
cards.t_text: Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.

cards.note: *For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:28). *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* (Matthew 11:29). Sirach's sixth chapter is about putting the neck under wisdom's yoke; her fetters look like bondage at first, and at the last you find her rest, and the rest is turned to joy. Yahusha (Jesus) offers his yoke in the same words: take it, learn of me, and ye shall find rest unto your souls. The yoke is not the opposite of the rest; it is the road to it, in Sirach and in the Messiah alike. The pulpit offers a rest with no yoke in it, and the other side of the aisle calls the yoke a burden; both have lost what Sirach and the Messiah say in the same breath, that the rest is found at the end of wearing it.
cards.s_text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and you shall find rest unto your souls.
cards.t_text: For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.

cards.note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28). Wisdom has been calling this way all through Ecclesiasticus, and here she says it outright: come to me, all of you who want me, and be filled. When Yahusha (Jesus) stood in Galilee and said *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*, it was not a new voice. It was the same one, the Wisdom who sat beside the Maker in Ecclesiasticus 24, now speaking in flesh, and the ones he calls are the ones Sirach's Wisdom had already called, the weary who want her and have not yet been fed.
cards.s_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: *At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brothers that were murdered in the secret places.* (1 Maccabees 2:41). *How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.* (Matthew 12:12). After a thousand of their brothers were slaughtered in the caves rather than lift a hand on the sabbath, Mattathias and his men decreed that they would fight whoever came against them on that day. They were not setting the sabbath aside; they were refusing to let the heathen use the sabbath to root the people who kept it out of the earth. Yahusha (Jesus) makes the same judgment when he asks whether a man is worth more than a sheep pulled from a pit on the sabbath and answers that it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The sabbath was given for life; to preserve life on it is to keep it, not to break it.
cards.s_text: How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
cards.t_text: At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brothers that were murdered in the secret places.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Sirach says keeping the law is bringing offerings enough, and heeding the commandment is itself a peace offering. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes Hosea, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, against men who condemned the guiltless for picking grain on the Sabbath. Nothing in either verse loosens the Sabbath or the altar. What both say is that the man who holds the form of the commandment while condemning the hungry has not kept the commandment at all, and his sacrifice counts for nothing, while the one who shows mercy has brought the offering.
cards.s_text: But if you had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:18). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Sirach says the offering of a thing wrongfully gotten is laughable before Yahuah (God), and the gifts of unjust men are not received. Yahusha (Jesus) told the Pharisees that if they had understood I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, they would not have condemned his hungry disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath. Both lines say the same thing about the altar: it does not wash the hands that bring to it. A sacrifice offered while mercy is withheld from the guiltless is the unjust man's gift, and Yahuah (God) does not take it.
cards.s_text: But if you had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless.
cards.t_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.

cards.note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Tobit gives mercy its full weight: alms deliver from death and keep a man from the darkness. Mercy is not the soft side of the Torah, something to be set aside when the rules get strict. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same to the Pharisees on the Sabbath: if you had known what Hosea meant by mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless. The system that condemned hungry disciples had lost the thing Tobit's household had kept, and the King names the loss in Hosea's own words.
cards.s_text: But if you had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless.
cards.t_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.

cards.note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The council that went out to plan his destruction was the system rendering its verdict on the righteous man. It had started by faulting his disciples, moved to calling him a drunkard and a friend of sinners, and now it was planning his death. Wisdom had already written the end of that story: the one the system condemned stands in great boldness before the faces of those who condemned him. The third day was the first installment of that standing, and the day of judgment is the rest of it, when the verdict rendered in this age is reversed in front of the men who rendered it.
cards.s_text: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.
cards.t_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.

cards.note: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour:* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The men who held a council to destroy him accounted his life madness; before long they will say he casts out devils by Beelzebub. Wisdom puts their own confession in their mouths at the judgment: we fools, we accounted his life madness and his end without honour. The council of Matthew 12:14 is the first step of that story, and the verse that follows in Wisdom is its last, when they see him numbered among the children of Yahuah (God). The same reversal waits for everyone the system counts a fool for walking in his commandments now.
cards.s_text: Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.
cards.t_text: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour:

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:1). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach tells his son not to defraud the poor and not to make the needy eyes wait long; the next line adds not to make a hungry soul sorrowful or provoke a man in his distress. That is a description of handling the bruised reed without breaking it and the smoking flax without quenching it, which is what Isaiah said of the Messiah and what Matthew says Yahusha (Jesus) fulfilled. The disposition Sirach asks of a son is the disposition the Son carried. A system that sorts the bruised and the smoldering into categories and dismisses them has lost both the counsel and the Messiah who kept it.
cards.s_text: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:4). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach is describing a face that stays turned toward the one in need, and Matthew 12:20 describes the Messiah's: a bruised reed he will not break, smoking flax he will not quench. The supplication of the afflicted is the bruised reed, and the poor man at the door is the smoking flax, easy to snap and easy to snuff. What Sirach asked of every son of Yashar'el (Israel), Yahusha (Jesus) did. A religious system that turns its face from the afflicted has abandoned the counsel and parted ways with the Messiah in the same motion.
cards.s_text: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
cards.t_text: Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.

cards.note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint. Do not the tears run down the widow’s cheeks? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall?* (Ecclesiasticus 35:14–15). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach says Yahuah (God) does not despise the fatherless when they plead or the widow when she pours out her complaint. Matthew is quoting Isaiah about the servant who will not break a bruised reed or put out a smoking wick, and he says it of Yahusha (Jesus) in the same chapter where the Pharisees are plotting to destroy him. The ones who cause the tears and the one who hears them stand side by side. The widow's cry Sirach speaks of is heard by the same one who would not break a reed already bent.
cards.s_text: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
cards.t_text: He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.

cards.note: *But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). *And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on the Canaanites little by little and gave them place of repentance, knowing all the while that their malice was bred in them and their cogitation would never be changed; the next verse calls them a cursed seed from the beginning. The King speaks of a sin that will not be forgiven in this world or the one to come, the word spoken against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by men who had just watched the Spirit cast out devils and called it Beelzebub. Both passages describe a disposition that does not change: room to repent is given, and the heart that was never going to turn uses the room to harden. He said of such hearers that they believe not because they are not of his sheep (John 10:26).
cards.s_text: And whosoever speaks a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaks against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.
cards.t_text: But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.

cards.note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* (Matthew 12:34). Sirach puts the two halves side by side: the fruit shows how the tree was kept, and what a man says shows the conceit of his heart. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same two things in one breath to the Pharisees, that a tree is known by its fruit and that the mouth speaks out of the abundance of the heart. Words are fruit. Bad fruit means a bad tree, and bad speech means a bad heart, and no amount of religious credential changes what the mouth gives away.
cards.s_text: O generation of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
cards.t_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.

cards.note: *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:7). *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* (Matthew 12:36). Sirach says a man is tried when he speaks, so hear him before you praise him. Yahusha (Jesus) carries the same trial all the way to the end: every idle word men speak will be given account of in the day of judgment. What Sirach says a wise listener does now, the Judge will do then. The words are the evidence of the heart, and the heart is what the judgment weighs.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
cards.t_text: Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.

cards.note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:11). *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* (Matthew 12:36). Wisdom of Solomon says no word is so secret that it goes for nothing, and that a lying mouth kills the soul that owns it. Yahusha (Jesus) says every idle word will be accounted for in the day of judgment, and the next verse says what the accounting looks like: *by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (Matthew 12:37). Murmuring and backbiting feel like small, private sins. Both books say there is nothing private about them; the ear of jealousy hears everything, and the words are kept for the day.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
cards.t_text: Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.

cards.note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40). The Father holds both doors: he leads down to the gates of hell and he brings up again. Yahusha (Jesus) gave that generation one sign, the sign of Jonah — three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, and then up. The resurrection was not a new idea arriving in Galilee; the library already knew that the one who has power of life and death brings up from the grave, and the King walked that road in his own body so the sign would stand in front of everyone.
cards.s_text: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
cards.t_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.

cards.note: *O you Adam, what have you done? for though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.* (2 Esdras 7:48). *Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.* (Matthew 12:45). Ezra cries out to Adam that his fall did not stay with him; everyone who comes of him fell with him, carrying the grain of evil seed sown in Adam's heart from the beginning (2 Esdras 4:30). Yahusha (Jesus) describes a house swept clean of its unclean spirit but left empty, so that the spirit returns with seven worse and the last state is worse than the first. A son of Adam cleaned out but not given a new heart is that empty house; the inherited pattern comes back to fill what was only swept. The remedy is not a cleaner house but a different heart in it (Ezekiel 36:26).
cards.s_text: Then goes he, and takes with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.
cards.t_text: O you Adam, what have you done? for though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.

cards.note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The righteous one in Wisdom of Solomon calls himself the child of Yahuah (God), and two verses later the ungodly say why they believe him enough to hate him: his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion. Yahusha (Jesus) names the family of the Father the same way, whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, sister, mother. The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life that does the Father's will; that is how the Father's children are recognised. The ungodly recognised it too, and it was the recognising that made them lie in wait.
cards.s_text: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
cards.t_text: He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The ungodly have a test for who is the son of Yahuah (God): will the Father step in and deliver him? Yahusha (Jesus) gives the Father's own test for who belongs to his family: whoever does the will of my Father in heaven. One measures sonship by rescue, the other by obedience. Wisdom shows the just man already living by the second standard before the first is ever applied to him, and that is exactly why his life was grievous to them.
cards.s_text: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
cards.t_text: For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.

cards.note: *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:10). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). Sirach says the man who fathers the fatherless and stands in for the widow's husband shall be as the son of the Most High, loved by him more than a mother loves. Yahusha (Jesus) says whoever does the will of his Father is his brother, sister, and mother. In both, the family of Elohim (God) is known by the doing of the Father's will, which in Sirach's example is the Torah's own care for the orphan and widow. The doing does not manufacture the sonship; it shows it, the way a son is known by bearing his father's likeness, and that is why Yahusha (Jesus) names his kin by it.
cards.s_text: For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
cards.t_text: Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.

cards.note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber, And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied upon earth.* (2 Esdras 5:9–10). *He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.* (Matthew 13:11). Esdras is shown a day when understanding withdraws into its secret chamber and is sought by many and not found. The King tells his disciples why he speaks in parables: to you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom, to them it is not given. Understanding does not vanish from the earth; it withdraws from those who would not have it and is given to those who hear. The many who seek and do not find in Esdras are the ones who, in Matthew, hear and do not understand, because what is withdrawn from one is a gift to the other, and the hearing reveals which is which.
cards.s_text: He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.
cards.t_text: And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber,

cards.note: *For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:4). *Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13). Wisdom will not move into a soul that is set against her. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in parables for the same reason he gives in the next lines, quoting Isaiah: *this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed* (Matthew 13:15). The parable did not shut them out; the closed eyes were their own doing, and wisdom does not force the door. In the same breath he tells the disciples their eyes are blessed because they see (Matthew 13:16). The teaching was one teaching; what differed was the soul it met.
cards.s_text: Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
cards.t_text: For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.

cards.note: *When the great Yahuah (God) will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks to Yahuah (God) in his prayer.* (Ecclesiasticus 39:6). *But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.* (Matthew 13:16). Sirach says the scribe is filled with the spirit of understanding when the great Yahuah (God) wills it; the man does not work it up out of his own study, he is filled. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples their eyes and ears are blessed, and the verse before explains why: *it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom* (Matthew 13:11). The seeing and the hearing are given the same way the scribe's understanding is given. The hand that fills the scribe is the hand that opens the disciple's eyes, and both of them answer with thanks.
cards.s_text: But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.
cards.t_text: When the great Yahuah (God) will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks to Yahuah (God) in his prayer.

cards.note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Uriel says a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, that it has brought up ungodliness ever since, and that it will go on bearing until the time of threshing. Yahusha (Jesus) opens his parable with a man sowing good seed in his field, and the verses that follow tell of the enemy's seed and the harvest when the two are separated. Esdras and the King both speak of seed, of two kinds of seed in one ground, and of a threshing that ends the matter. The evil seed is not the last word in either book; the threshing is.
cards.s_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:
cards.t_text: For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?

cards.note: *For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.* (2 Esdras 3:21). *But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25). Esdras says the first Adam bore a wicked heart, transgressed, and was overcome, and so are all who are born of him. The parable says that while men slept an enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat. These are two different facts about one field. The sons of Adam carry the wicked heart, and the law was given to bring fruit out of them in spite of it; the tares are another seed, planted by an enemy, not born of Adam at all. The wheat is wounded, the tares are not wheat, and the harvest will tell them apart.
cards.s_text: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.
cards.t_text: For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God), if you suffer not your servant, that we may pray before you, and you give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; how shall each man live that is corrupt, who bears the place of a man?* (2 Esdras 8:6). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Ezra prays for seed to the heart and culture to the understanding, so that fruit may come, because a corrupt man cannot live any other way. The kingdom parable answers that prayer with a sower: a man goes out and sows good seed in his field. The seed to the heart Ezra begs for is what the sower is sowing; the fruit Ezra hopes for is what the good ground brings forth (Matthew 13:23). The prayer and the parable meet in the same field.
cards.s_text: Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God), if you suffer not your servant, that we may pray before you, and you give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; how shall each man live that is corrupt, who bears the place of a man?

cards.note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom puts the shining of the righteous at a set time — the time of their visitation — and sets it in a harvest scene: sparks running among the stubble. Yahusha (Jesus) puts it at the same moment in the parable of the tares: when the field is reaped and the tares are bundled for the fire, then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun. The stubble burning and the sparks flying are the same picture as the tares burning and the wheat shining. The shining is not yet; it waits on the harvest.
cards.s_text: Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who has ears to hear, let him hear.
cards.t_text: And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.

cards.note: *As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:22). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35).
