Parents brought their children to Yahusha (Jesus) and he laid his hands on them. The library shows a father passing covenant life to the next generation; the gospel shows the King receiving the children their parents bring to him. The two belong together at the household, where the covenant has always been handed down.
cards.s_text: And he laid his hands on them, and departed thence.
cards.t_text: And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.

cards.note: *Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:11). *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* (Matthew 19:17). Sirach calls the law a law of life, given for an heritage along with knowledge. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the young man that if he would enter into life he should keep the commandments. The law of life and entering into life are the same road. Moses set life and good before Yashar'el (Israel) in the commandments, Sirach calls that inheritance by its name, and the King does not amend it when the question is put to him directly.
cards.s_text: And he said unto him, Why callest you me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if you will enter into life, keep the commandments.
cards.t_text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.

cards.note: *He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:1). *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* (Matthew 19:17). Sirach says the merciful man lends to his neighbour, and the one who strengthens his hand keeps the commandments; mercy and commandment are one act. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the young man who asks about life to keep the commandments, and when the young man says he has kept them all, the King tests him with the poor: sell and give. The test did not change the subject. Mercy to the neighbour is what keeping the commandments looks like with a full purse in hand, and the young man's grief showed where his keeping had stopped. Sirach would have told him the same thing.
cards.s_text: And he said unto him, Why callest you me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if you will enter into life, keep the commandments.
cards.t_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.

cards.note: *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:11). *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21). Sirach says lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it will outprofit gold. Yahusha (Jesus) says it to the young man who has kept the commandments from his youth: sell, give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. The King's word was a test for one heart, not a command that every disciple become penniless; it found the place where this man's love of neighbour stopped, which was his own possessions. Giving to the poor was never new; the Torah had always commanded it (Deuteronomy 15:7–8), and Sirach is only saying that treasure laid up that way is the kind that lasts.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If you will be perfect, go and sell that you have, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
cards.t_text: Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.

cards.note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21). The young ruler asked what he still lacked, and the King told him: sell, give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven. Tobit had told his son the same thing long before — alms are a good treasure laid up against the day of necessity. The Torah already commanded the open hand to the poor brother, and the library carried it forward as treasure laid up. Yahusha (Jesus) was not raising the bar on the young man; he was reading him the library, and the young man went away sorrowful because he could not walk it.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If you will be perfect, go and sell that you have, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
cards.t_text: For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve that in the regeneration, when the Son of Adam sits on the throne of his glory, they will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). Twelve thrones for twelve tribes means the twelve tribes are there to be judged: gathered, whole, as from the beginning. What Sirach asked for in prayer the King states as the shape of the kingdom when it comes.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Wisdom says the righteous shall judge the nations; Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve they shall sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). These are two views of one kingdom. The gathered twelve tribes sit under the apostles' thrones, and that gathered people is the kingdom of priests the Father promised at Sinai — *ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests* (Exodus 19:6) — who judge and teach the nations left alive in the reign. The priesthood toward the nations begins when the kingdom is set up, not before. Wisdom saw the outer ring; the King named the inner one.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.

cards.note: *So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).* (Ecclesiasticus 24:8). *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1). Wisdom was commanded by the Creator to pitch her tent in Jacob and take her inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel). Isaiah had already said that the vineyard of Yahuah (God) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and Jeremiah mourned the pastors who destroyed it. When Yahusha (Jesus) opens the parable with a householder hiring labourers into his vineyard, that is the vineyard he means — the covenant people the Father planted and in whom Wisdom made her dwelling. The householder is the Father, and the labourers are the ones he calls into it through the hours of the day.
cards.s_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.t_text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 24:12). *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1). Wisdom says she took root in an honourable people, in the portion that is Yahuah's (God's) own inheritance. That people is the vineyard of the parable — the householder's own ground, into which he goes out to hire labourers through the day. The vineyard is Yashar'el (Israel), and so are the labourers called into it, whether called early or late: the covenant line from Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the children of that line who grew up scattered among the nations and are being called home. The honourable people Wisdom rooted in is the inheritance the Father is still gathering.
cards.s_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.t_text: And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.* (Ecclesiasticus 33:13). *Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good?* (Matthew 20:15). Sirach says man is in the hand of his Maker as clay is in the hand of the potter, to render to each as seems best to him, and the verse before it says he has blessed and exalted some and brought others low. The householder in the parable asks the grumbling labourers the same thing: is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own? The one who made the clay owes it no explanation for how he shapes it. An eye that goes evil because the Maker has been good to another has forgotten whose hand it is in.
cards.s_text: Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with my own? Is your eye evil, because I am good?
cards.t_text: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.

cards.note: *And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:* (2 Esdras 5:23). *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1). Ezra, praying, names what the Most High did with the whole earth: out of every wood and every tree he chose one vine. When Yahusha (Jesus) opens the parable of the labourers, the householder's vineyard is not a new field; it is that one vine, the vineyard Isaiah had already named as the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Isaiah 5:7). Labourers are hired into it at different hours, but the vineyard itself was chosen long before the morning began. Whoever is brought in at the eleventh hour is brought into that same vineyard, not into a different one planted beside it.
cards.s_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.t_text: And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:

cards.note: *Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.* (2 Esdras 9:22). *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16). The Most High tells Ezra he will let the multitude born in vain perish and keep his grape and his plant, made perfect with great labour. The parable ends the same way: many called, few chosen. The grape kept out of the cluster is the few; the great labour is the Father's long keeping of his seed through all the scattering until the gathering. He does not lose what he laboured over, and he does not keep what he never planted.
cards.s_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.t_text: Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain; and let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.

cards.note: *And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* (2 Esdras 8:1). *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16). Ezra asks why so many are made for so little, and the answer is plain: this world was made for many, the world to come for few. Yahusha (Jesus) closes the parable of the labourers with the same count: many are called, few chosen. The call goes out broadly because the sheep are scattered among many and no one can tell them by sight; the few are the ones who hear and come in and bear fruit. The many and the few are not two peoples set against each other; they are the whole field and the harvest that comes out of it.
cards.s_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.t_text: And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.

cards.note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:3). *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16). The angel gives Ezra the plainest form of it: many created, few saved. Yahusha (Jesus) says many called, few chosen. The few are not those who saved themselves by effort, nor a number chosen apart from how they walked; they are the ones whose names were written from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), who hear because they are his sheep, and whose walk bears the fruit that keeps a name from being blotted out (Revelation 3:5). Being created does not make a man one of the few, and neither does being called. Hearing and keeping do, and those come from what he already was.
cards.s_text: So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
cards.t_text: There be many created, but few shall be saved.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22). James and John asked for thrones and were handed a cup. Yahusha (Jesus) asked whether they could drink what he was about to drink, and they said they could, not knowing what they were agreeing to. James was put to the sword by Herod (Acts 12:2); John outlived them all and was on Patmos for the testimony. The cup was real suffering, and Wisdom tells where it ends: the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there no torment touches them. James drank the cup to the bottom and lies down in that hand, kept and asleep until the Father raises him; the sword reached his body and could not follow him there.
cards.s_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, You know not what you ask. Are you able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* (Matthew 20:23). The sons of Zebedee asked for the seats; the King promised them the cup. They would drink what he drank and be baptized with what he was baptized with, and the seats would be the Father's to assign. Wisdom puts the order the same way: the righteous man's labours are made no account of first, and the standing in great boldness comes after. The cup is the afflicting; the boldness before the afflicters is what follows it, and who sits where on that day is in the Father's hand, not seized along the road.
cards.s_text: And he says unto them, You shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not my to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.
cards.t_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.

cards.note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.* (Matthew 20:23). The righteous live for evermore and their reward is with Yahuah (God). It is kept in his hand, which is what the King tells the sons of Zebedee when they ask for the seats: to sit at his right hand and his left is not his to give, it is given to those for whom it is prepared of his Father. The reward is real and it is the Father's to give. It is not seized by flesh and it is not handed out regardless of the walk; it is held for the righteous by the one who sees their labours when no one else does.
cards.s_text: And he says unto them, You shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not my to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.
cards.t_text: But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.

cards.note: *But I, as my brothers, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching Yahuah (God) that he would speedily be merciful to our nation; and that you by torments and plagues may confess, that he alone is Yahuah (God);* (2 Maccabees 7:37). *But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.* (Matthew 20:22). The youngest brother offers his body and life for the laws of his fathers and prays that in him and his brothers the wrath on the nation would cease (2 Maccabees 7:38). When James and John ask for the chief seats, Yahusha (Jesus) asks whether they can drink the cup he is about to drink, and they say they are able. The brothers under Antiochus had drunk a cup like that, giving their lives for the Torah and for mercy on their people. Only the King's cup carries the remission of sins; his death is the one no martyr could die. But the cost of following him is real, and the seven brothers show what the sons of Zebedee were agreeing to, James by the sword (Acts 12:2) and John in exile on Patmos (Revelation 1:9).
cards.s_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, You know not what you ask. Are you able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.
cards.t_text: But I, as my brothers, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching Yahuah (God) that he would speedily be merciful to our nation; and that you by torments and plagues may confess, that he alone is Yahuah (God);

cards.note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;* (Matthew 20:26). The kingdoms of the world run on domination; Yahusha (Jesus) has just said so of the princes of the Gentiles, and then he says it shall not be so among you. Whoever will be great among you, let him be your minister, the one who waits the table. Sirach had set the same direction centuries earlier: the greater you are, the more humble yourself, and favour before Yahuah (God) follows the humbling. In the kingdom greatness flows downward into service, the exact reverse of the kingdoms around it, and the Messiah is not introducing that reversal; he is restoring what the fathers had already taught and then living it out with a towel.
cards.s_text: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;
cards.t_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Therefore they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms to him that had given them good success in cleansing his place.* (2 Maccabees 10:7). *And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.* (Matthew 21:8). When the temple was cleansed, the people carried branches and fair boughs and palms and sang psalms to the one who had given them success in cleansing his place, keeping eight days with gladness like the feast of tabernacles (2 Maccabees 10:6). When Yahusha (Jesus) rode into Jerusalem, the multitude cut down branches and strewed them in the way and cried Hosanna from Psalm 118, and the next thing he did was walk into the temple and cleanse it. Branches, psalms, and a cleansed temple belong together in both books. The people at the gate were doing what their fathers had done after Judas's victory, whether they knew it or not, and the King they welcomed went straight to his Father's house as the Maccabees had gone to theirs.
cards.s_text: And a very great multitude spread their garments in the way; others cut down branches from the trees, and strawed them in the way.
cards.t_text: Therefore they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms to him that had given them good success in cleansing his place.

cards.note: *Fill Sion with your unspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory:* (Ecclesiasticus 36:14). *And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest.* (Matthew 21:9). Sirach prays for Sion to be filled with the oracles of Yahuah (God) and his people with his glory, in the same prayer that asks for the tribes to be gathered and for mercy on Jerusalem. When Yahusha (Jesus) rode into the city the multitudes cried Hosanna to the Son of David and Blessed is he that cometh in the name of Yahuah (Lord), and the next verse says all the city was moved. The glory Sirach asked to fill Sion came through its gate on a colt. The city was moved and did not know by whom; the prayer was being answered in its streets.
cards.s_text: And the multitudes that went before, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the Son of David: Blessed is he that comes in the name of Yahuah (Lord); Hosanna in the highest.
cards.t_text: Fill Sion with your unspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory:

cards.note: *Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.* (1 Maccabees 4:43). *And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,* (Matthew 21:12). The priests Judas chose carried the defiled stones out of the sanctuary to an unclean place. Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God) and carried out the sellers, the buyers, the tables, and the seats. What defiled the house in Judas's day was an idol the Greeks had set on the altar; what defiled it in the King's day was trade the priesthood had set in the court of prayer. Both were put out. Cleansing the sanctuary is what faithful men do when the house of Yahuah (God) has been made to serve something other than him.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,
cards.t_text: Who cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.

cards.note: *And having cleansed the temple they made another altar, and striking stones they took fire out of them, and offered a sacrifice after two years, and set forth incense, and lights, and shewbread.* (2 Maccabees 10:3). *And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,* (Matthew 21:12). Judas and his men cleansed what Antiochus had defiled: they pulled down the heathen altars, built a new altar, struck fresh fire from stones, and brought back the sacrifice, the incense, the lamps, and the shewbread after two years without them. Yahusha (Jesus) also walked into the temple and cleansed it, but the defilement he drove out had not come from a foreign king. It came from the house's own leadership, who had let the courts become a market, and he answered them with Jeremiah's words: *My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves* (Matthew 21:13; Jeremiah 7:11). The Maccabees cleansed the temple of a defilement pressed on it from outside; the King cleansed it of the one that grew up inside, in the very priesthood their victory had restored. Both cleansings say the same thing about whose house it is.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) went into the temple of Elohim (God), and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the moneychangers, and the seats of them that sold doves,
cards.t_text: And having cleansed the temple they made another altar, and striking stones they took fire out of them, and offered a sacrifice after two years, and set forth incense, and lights, and shewbread.

cards.note: *Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices; for Yahuah (God) is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:12). *And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.* (Matthew 21:13). Sirach says do not think to corrupt Yahuah (God) with gifts, for he will not take them, and do not trust in unrighteous sacrifices, for he is judge and shows no favour to persons. Yahusha (Jesus) walked into the temple courts and found the house of prayer turned into a den of thieves; the gifts and the sacrifices had become a trade. The leaders who ran that trade trusted that the sacrifices would still cover them. Sirach had already told them the judge does not take bribes, and the King overturning the tables was the judge saying it in person.
cards.s_text: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but you have made it a den of thieves.
cards.t_text: Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices; for Yahuah (God) is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.

cards.note: *And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.* (1 Maccabees 4:46). *And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.* (Matthew 21:13). Judas's priests did not know what to do with the stones of the profaned altar, so they laid them up on the temple mount until a prophet should come to say. Yahusha (Jesus) came into that temple as the prophet the crowds had just named him, the prophet of Nazareth (Matthew 21:11), and the word he gave about the house was from the prophets already written: it is written, my house shall be called the house of prayer. The Maccabees waited for a prophet to tell them what the house required. When he came, he told them, and what it required was that it be a house of prayer and not a den of thieves.
cards.s_text: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but you have made it a den of thieves.
cards.t_text: And laid up the stones in the mountain of the temple in a convenient place, until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.

cards.note: *For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:4). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom describes the brood of the ungodly as branches that flourish for a while with nothing under them; the wind shakes them and finally roots them out. Yahusha (Jesus) came to a fig tree in full leaf, found no fruit, and it withered. Leaves without fruit is the same picture as branches without roots — a show of life with nothing feeding it. The tree stands for the religious leadership of that day, which had the look of the covenant and none of its fruit; it does not stand for the people of Yashar'el (Israel) as a whole. What flourishes without a root does not stand when the wind comes.
cards.s_text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
cards.t_text: For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.

cards.note: *The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:5). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom is describing branches that flourish for a season, bear nothing worth eating, and are broken off. The fig tree the King met on the road the morning after he cleansed the Temple was all leaves and no fruit, and he spoke its end on the spot. The tree was not the people of Yashar'el (Israel); it was the leadership standing in that Temple with every show of foliage and nothing to feed anyone, the same men he answers with seven woes in Matthew 23 before the week is out. The test he had already given his disciples was fruit, not leaves (Matthew 7:16), and Solomon had written the same verdict long before.
cards.s_text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
cards.t_text: The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing.

cards.note: *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:25). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Sirach says of the adulterous woman that her children will not take root and her branches will bring forth no fruit — what grows from unfaithfulness has nothing underneath it, and nothing comes of it. Yahusha (Jesus) came to the fig tree, found leaves and no fruit, and spoke the same sentence over it: let no fruit grow on you from now on. The tree stands for the leadership that held the vineyard in trust and gave the Father leaves instead of fruit, as the parable of the husbandmen later in the same chapter says plainly. No root, no fruit, and then no fruit forever — the judgment reads the same in both books.
cards.s_text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
cards.t_text: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.

cards.note: *But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:24). *He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.* (Matthew 21:29). Sirach says Yahuah (God) grants return to them that repent and comforts those who failed in patience. The first son in the parable said I will not, then repented and went — and he is the one who did the father's will. The publicans and harlots Yahusha (Jesus) names a few lines later walked the same road: a no at first, and then a return. Return is granted to the one who turns, not to the one who said the right word and stayed where he was.
cards.s_text: He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went.
cards.t_text: But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.

cards.note: *Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:28). *And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.* (Matthew 21:30). The second son in the parable says yes with his mouth and no with his feet. Sirach had already named that man: the one who comes to Yahuah (God) with a double heart, one heart for what he says and another for what he does. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the parable to the chief priests and elders, who had answered the Father's call through John with the words of obedience and none of the walking, and the double heart is what he is exposing. A yes that does not go is not a weaker obedience; it is the thing Sirach warns against, and the Father does not receive it.
cards.s_text: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.
cards.t_text: Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.

cards.note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:29). *And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.* (Matthew 21:30). Sirach's warning is against being a hypocrite in the sight of men, and against careless speech, and the second son in the parable fails both at once. He speaks the right words, I go, sir, where men can hear them, and then does not go. Yahusha (Jesus) is telling the parable to the chief priests and elders, who had given the Father the public yes and withheld the obedience, which is hypocrisy as Sirach defines it: a performance for the watching crowd with nothing behind it. Take good heed what you speak, Sirach says, because the Father holds a man to what his mouth promised.
cards.s_text: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not.
cards.t_text: Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.

cards.note: *My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:1). *For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.* (Matthew 21:32). Sirach opens the chapter with the whole of repentance in one line: stop doing it, and ask pardon for what is past. That is what John came preaching in the wilderness, and Yahusha (Jesus) names who actually did it — the publicans and the harlots believed him and turned, while the chief priests and elders saw it and repented not. The ones with the least standing walked Sirach's counsel; the ones holding the office refused it. Sonship is shown by the turning, not by the title.
cards.s_text: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and you believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and you, when you had seen it, repented not afterward, that you might believe him.
cards.t_text: My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.

cards.note: *And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it;* (2 Esdras 9:11). *For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.* (Matthew 21:32). The Most High describes those who loathed his law while they still had liberty, while a place of repentance stood open to them, and despised it. The chief priests and elders are told the same about themselves: John came in the way of righteousness, which is the law's own way, and they did not believe him, and even after watching publicans and harlots repent they did not repent afterward. The open place of repentance was John at the Jordan; they walked past it. Ezra's lament and the King's rebuke describe the same men in the same posture.
cards.s_text: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and you believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and you, when you had seen it, repented not afterward, that you might believe him.
cards.t_text: And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it;

cards.note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.* (Matthew 21:35). Yahuah (God) says he sent his servants the prophets and the people took them, slew them, and tore their bodies in pieces, and he will require their blood. In the parable the husbandmen take the owner's servants and beat one, kill another, and stone another. The servants are the prophets, the husbandmen are the men set over the vineyard, and the owner who sent them is going to require the blood. The parable is not a new story; the King is telling the leadership of his day the history already written against their fathers, and daring them to finish it.
cards.s_text: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
cards.t_text: I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.* (Matthew 21:39). The sentence in 2 Esdras follows directly on the slaying of the prophets: your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble. The parable follows the same order. After the servants are beaten and killed the son is sent, and the husbandmen cast him out of the vineyard and slay him, and the King asks his hearers what the owner will do to them. The desolate house is the answer. Killing the prophets brought the sentence near; killing the son brought it down, and within a generation not one stone of that house was left on another.
cards.s_text: And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him.
cards.t_text: Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* (Matthew 21:43). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the chief priests the kingdom will be taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits; a nation, one, not the nations. That one nation is the gathered tribes of Jacob bearing fruit, the very people Sirach prayed for. It is not the church put in the place of Yashar'el (Israel), and it is not whoever keeps Torah regardless of seed; it is Jacob's own tribes, gathered home and bearing the fruit their leaders in that day would not bring.
cards.s_text: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God);* (2 Esdras 2:38). *Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.* (Matthew 22:9). Esdras is told to stand and look at the number of those sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God). In the parable the first guests would not come, so the king sends his servants into the highways to bid as many as they find to the marriage. The ones found on the highways are not strangers to the king; they are the scattered children whose number he already knows, sealed before the servants ever went out. The feast of Yahuah (God) in 2 Esdras and the marriage in Matthew are the same table, and the guests are gathered in from wherever they were scattered.
cards.s_text: Go you therefore into the highways, and as many as you shall find, bid to the marriage.
cards.t_text: Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God);

cards.note: *I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* (2 Esdras 2:42). *So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.* (Matthew 22:10). Esdras sees on mount Sion a great people he could not number, all praising Yahuah (God) with songs. The parable ends with the wedding furnished with guests, gathered from the highways, both bad and good. John saw the same crowd in Revelation 7, a great multitude no man could number, out of all nations. Esdras saw the gathered on the mountain, the parable shows the gathering on the roads, and the next verse in each shows the King coming among them to see who is wearing what.
cards.s_text: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.
cards.t_text: I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.

cards.note: *And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.* (2 Esdras 2:43). *And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:* (Matthew 22:11). In the midst of the gathered crowd on mount Sion a young man taller than all the rest sets a crown on every head, and the angel tells Esdras a few verses on that this is the Son of Elohim (God) whom they confessed in the world. In the parable the king comes in to see the guests and finds a man with no wedding garment. Both scenes have the King walking among the gathered, and in both what he does depends on what they are wearing; in 2 Esdras the verses before say the gathered have received glorious garments, and these receive crowns. The man without the garment at the marriage receives nothing and is put out. The garment is the righteousness of the saints, and the King himself inspects it.
cards.s_text: And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment:
cards.t_text: And in the midst of them there was a young man of a high stature, taller than all the rest, and upon every one of their heads he set crowns, and was more exalted; which I marvelled at greatly.

cards.note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.* (Matthew 22:12). The guest came in without a wedding garment and had nothing to say. Wisdom shows what the garment was for: those who receive a glorious kingdom and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God) receive them clothed. The fine linen of the bride is the righteousness of saints (Revelation 19:8), granted to her and then worn, and the man at the feast had neither put it on nor walked in it. The crown is given from the Father's hand to those who came dressed for the feast; the one who came in his own clothes receives the silence and the door.
cards.s_text: And he says unto him, Friend, how came you in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless.
cards.t_text: Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.

cards.note: *He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,* (Ecclesiasticus 17:3). *And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?* (Matthew 22:20). Sirach says the Maker made men according to his image, with strength of their own, carrying Genesis 1 forward. Yahusha (Jesus) held up the coin and asked whose image and superscription it bore. The coin bears Caesar's image and goes back to Caesar; the man bears the Father's image and belongs to the Father. The question about the tribute was a question about ownership, and Sirach had already said who stamped the man.
cards.s_text: And he says unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?
cards.t_text: He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,

cards.note: *Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:11). *They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).* (Matthew 22:21). Sirach says the law of life was given as an heritage — set on the people along with the image. Yahusha (Jesus) says to render to Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's). What is Elohim's (God's) is what he put on the man: his image, and the law he gave for the man's inheritance. Rendering it back is not a burden laid on a free man; it is the heir keeping his inheritance.
cards.s_text: They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then says he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).
cards.t_text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:23). *And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?* (Matthew 22:20). Yahusha (Jesus) asked whose image was on the coin, and the answer settled where the coin belonged. Wisdom tells us whose image is on the man: Yahuah (God) made him an image of his own eternity. Caesar's stamp is on the money, so the money goes back to Caesar; the Father's stamp is on the one holding it, so the one holding it goes back to the Father. The coin is perishable and so is its owner. The man was made for immortality, and the image he bears tells him whose he is.
cards.s_text: And he says unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). *They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).* (Matthew 22:21). Caesar's face on the coin makes the coin Caesar's. Solomon's prayer tells you what makes everything else the Father's: he made all things with his word, and the next verse adds that he ordained man through his wisdom to rule over what was made. So when the King says render unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God's), the things in question are all things, man first, because man carries the Maker's image the way the denarius carries Caesar's. The Word the Father made all things with is the one standing in the court holding the coin and asking whose image is on it.
cards.s_text: They say unto him, Cæsar’s. Then says he unto them, Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto Elohim (God) the things that are Elohim's (God’s).
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,

cards.note: *And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.* (2 Maccabees 7:9). *Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 22:29). The second of the seven brothers, dying under Antiochus for refusing to break the Torah, said with his last breath that the King of the world would raise him up to everlasting life. He did not hold a philosophy about the afterlife; he held a hope in the resurrection, and he paid for it with his body. When the Sadducees, who said there is no resurrection (Acts 23:8), came to trap Yahusha (Jesus), he told them they erred because they knew neither the scriptures nor the power of Elohim (God). The brothers in 2 Maccabees 7 knew both. The resurrection the King defended in the temple was the resurrection a family had already confessed under torture, for his laws.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto them, You do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.

cards.note: *But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.* (2 Maccabees 7:23). *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* (Matthew 22:32). The mother tells her sons where life comes from: she did not give them breath, the Creator did, and the one who formed man at the beginning can give breath and life again. That is her whole comfort as they die. Yahusha (Jesus) makes the same argument from the same ground: Elohim (God) names himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and he is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living, so the fathers must rise. Neither the mother nor the King speaks of souls already in heaven; both look to the Creator giving breath again to those who sleep. The seven sons and their mother lie down in that hope, waiting with the fathers for the day their breath is given back.
cards.s_text: I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.
cards.t_text: But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.

cards.note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* 2 Esdras 7:32 carries forward the resurrection of the asleep that Daniel named at Daniel 12:2 (*many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake*). It stands beside Matt 22:31's *but as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by Elohim (God)* — the King reads to the Sadducees what the library already held: the earth, the dust and the secret places giving back the asleep. In Esdras this restoring comes after the Messiah's reign and the seven days of silence (2 Esdras 7:28-31) — the great resurrection, when the dead are judged — while the righteous seed are raised first, at his coming (Revelation 20:4-6). The dead sleep awaiting the resurrection; they are not carried off at death as disembodied souls.
cards.s_text: But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have you not read that which was spoken unto you by Elohim (God), saying,
cards.t_text: And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* (Matthew 22:32). Read this verse with the rest of its chapter and it is not souls flying off to heaven. The righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God) — kept, at rest, waiting; a few verses on, *in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7), and that visitation has not come yet. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living. The fathers are asleep and held, and the Father counts them living because he is going to raise them. That is why Paul can tell the grieving not to sorrow as those who have no hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13), and it is the only reason.
cards.s_text: I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:30). *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.* (Matthew 22:37). Sirach is carrying the Shema forward: love him that made you with all your strength, the strength Deuteronomy 6:5 names and that Yahusha (Jesus) renders heart, soul, and mind when he gives the great commandment in Matthew 22:37. The Messiah is not replacing the commandments with love; he is quoting the commandment, the same one Sirach's readers recited twice a day. Sirach's next clause keeps love and Torah together, forsake not his ministers, and the verses around it give the priests their portion as it is commanded; loving Yahuah (God) with all your strength shows up as keeping what he commanded. That is the love written on the heart the prophets promised, not a feeling that excuses the walk.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, You shall love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.
cards.t_text: Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.

cards.note: *And he said to them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:14). *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). Sirach says the commandment concerning the neighbour was given to every man, in the same breath as the warning against all unrighteousness — this is Sinai, where their eyes saw his glory and their ears heard his voice. When Yahusha (Jesus) names the second great commandment he is quoting the Torah, the commandment Sirach is describing. The King added nothing. He put his finger on what was given at the beginning.
cards.s_text: And the second is like unto it, You shall love your neighbour as thyself.
cards.t_text: And he said to them, Beware of all unrighteousness; and he gave every man commandment concerning his neighbour.

cards.note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:2). *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). Sirach says forgive your neighbour the hurt he did you, and your own sins will be forgiven. Yahusha (Jesus) names the second great commandment as love your neighbour as yourself, quoting Leviticus 19:18, and that verse in the Torah begins by forbidding vengeance and grudges before it ever says love. Forgiving the hurt is what loving the neighbour looks like when he has wronged you. Sirach is not adding to the commandment; he is reading it, and the King's answer to the lawyer stands on the same verse.
cards.s_text: And the second is like unto it, You shall love your neighbour as thyself.
cards.t_text: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.

cards.note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:7). *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40). Sirach binds the commandments and the covenant together with bearing no malice and overlooking ignorance, all in one breath. When Yahusha (Jesus) says all the law and the prophets hang on loving Yahuah (God) and loving your neighbour, he is doing the same thing, not the opposite: he is saying what the whole Torah is for, not cutting it down to two lines. A man cannot hang a coat on a peg and then throw the coat away. Remember the commandments, and the love of the neighbour is what keeping them looks like; the heart Jeremiah 31:33 and Ezekiel 36:26–27 promise is the heart that does both at once.
cards.s_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.t_text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.

cards.note: *And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption;* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:18). *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* (Matthew 22:40). Love is the keeping of her laws. The King hangs all the law and the prophets on two commandments, love of Yahuah (God) and love of neighbour, and the pulpit has used that sentence for centuries to say love replaced the law. Solomon says the opposite: love is what keeping the law looks like, and heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption. John says it the same way, that this is the love of Elohim (God), that we keep his commandments (1 John 5:3). The two commandments are not a shorter list; they are the heart the whole Torah hangs from, the heart Ezekiel promised would be new so the statutes could be walked (Ezekiel 36:27).
cards.s_text: On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
cards.t_text: And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption;

cards.note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:14). *And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.* (Matthew 23:12). Sirach says the throne itself changes hands: the proud prince loses it and the meek receive it. Yahusha (Jesus) states the rule behind the history — exalt yourself and you are abased, humble yourself and you are exalted — and he says it in the middle of his rebuke of the scribes and Pharisees who loved the chief seats. This is not piety literature sitting beside the gospel; it is the same voice. What the Father does to kingdoms he does to men.
cards.s_text: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.

cards.note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.* (Matthew 23:11). Sirach's counsel runs opposite to how religious status works: the greater you are, the more humble yourself. In Matthew 23 Yahusha (Jesus) is describing a leadership that had reversed it, loving the chief seats and the greetings and the titles, and in the middle of the woes he states the kingdom's rule: he that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Any system that climbs as it grows holy has walked Sirach backward. The favour before Yahuah (God) that Sirach promises goes to the one who goes down, and the Messiah says the same of greatness.
cards.s_text: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant.
cards.t_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Seek not of Yahuah (God) preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:4). *And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,* (Matthew 23:6). Sirach tells his son not to ask Yahuah (God) for preeminence or the king for the seat of honour. Matthew 23:6 describes a religious leadership that loved exactly those things, the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues. The counsel and the woe are the same measure applied twice, once as a warning and once as a diagnosis, and the seat of honour is the tell in both. A system that wants the chief seat has made its religion a way of climbing, which is what Sirach said not to do with it.
cards.s_text: And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
cards.t_text: Seek not of Yahuah (God) preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.

cards.note: *If you be made the master of a feast, lift not thyself up, but be among them as one of the rest; take diligent care for them, and so sit down.* (Ecclesiasticus 32:1). *And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,* (Matthew 23:6). Sirach's rule for the master of a feast is to be among the guests as one of the rest and to take diligent care for them before he sits down. Yahusha (Jesus) names the scribes and Pharisees by the opposite habit: they love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues. Sirach put the care of the company first and the seat last; the leaders of that day had put the seat first and the company nowhere. The one who washed his disciples' feet on the night he was betrayed was keeping Sirach's rule to the letter.
cards.s_text: And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues,
cards.t_text: If you be made the master of a feast, lift not thyself up, but be among them as one of the rest; take diligent care for them, and so sit down.

cards.note: *Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God);* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:4). *But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.* (Matthew 23:13). Wisdom addresses men who hold office as ministers of his kingdom and have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after his counsel. The King addresses the same office in the Temple court: men who hold the keys of the kingdom of heaven, do not go in themselves, and shut the door on those who are entering. The test is the one John gives plainly, that he who says he knows him and keeps not his commandments is a liar (1 John 2:4), and a ministry that sets aside the law it was given to keep fails it in whatever century it stands. The woe is on the office and the system; the men in it had the lie handed to them, and the people under them are the ones being shut out.
cards.s_text: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for you neither go in yourselves, neither suffer you them that are entering to go in.
cards.t_text: Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God);

cards.note: *Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:9). *Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!* (Matthew 23:16). Sirach's counsel is simple: do not get your mouth used to swearing or to naming the Holy One. The tradition Yahusha (Jesus) is answering had gone the other way — it had built grades of oath, where swearing by the temple meant nothing but swearing by the gold of the temple bound you. The Torah knows no such grades; every vow binds and every oath counts. Sirach stood with the Torah on this, and the blind guides are the office that built the ladder of evasions, not the people who were taught to climb it.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, you blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor!
cards.t_text: Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.

cards.note: *A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:11). *And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of Elohim (God), and by him that sitteth thereon.* (Matthew 23:22). Sirach says the man who swears much is filled with iniquity and his house is full of calamities — he takes every oath seriously, because every one of them counts. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same against the tradition that had sorted oaths into binding and empty: to swear by heaven is to swear by the throne of Elohim (God) and by him who sits on it, so there is no empty oath. Sirach and Yahusha (Jesus) stand together on the Torah here; the grading of oaths was the invention of the system, not of Moses.
cards.s_text: And he that shall swear by heaven, swears by the throne of Elohim (God), and by him that sits thereon.
cards.t_text: A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.

cards.note: *The talk of him that sweareth much makes the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:14). *And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.* (Matthew 23:18). Sirach says the talk of a man who swears constantly makes the hair stand on end, and their quarrels make you cover your ears. Yahusha (Jesus) met a whole religion of that: a system that had ruled an oath by the altar was nothing but an oath by the gift on the altar was binding. That is the much swearing Sirach warned of, dressed up as law, a maze of oaths that let a man say anything and be bound by none of it. The teaching that hedges every oath is what the King names blind, and his own word on the matter was let your yes be yes.
cards.s_text: And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever swears by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty.
cards.t_text: The talk of him that sweareth much makes the hair stand upright; and their brawls make one stop his ears.

cards.note: *Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:28). *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.* (Matthew 23:25). A double heart is a clean outside and a different inside. Sirach warns the one who comes to Yahuah (God) not to come that way; Yahusha (Jesus) names the religious leadership of his day as having done exactly that, the cup scrubbed where men can see and full of extortion and excess where only Elohim (God) sees. The two verses are the same diagnosis from two directions, the counsel before the fault and the woe after it. Yahuah (God) has always looked on the heart, so a system that polishes the outside and leaves the inside alone has misjudged who is doing the inspecting.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
cards.t_text: Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.

cards.note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:29). *Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.* (Matthew 23:28). The word Yahusha (Jesus) uses, hypocrite, is the word for a stage actor, a man playing a part for an audience, and Sirach had warned against that very thing two centuries earlier: be not an hypocrite in the sight of men. Matthew 23:28 is where the seven woes land, outward righteousness for men to see, hypocrisy and iniquity underneath. The counsel in Sirach and the woe in Matthew describe one man, the one whose righteousness is aimed at human eyes. Yahuah (God) is not in the audience for that performance; he is reading the inside.
cards.s_text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
cards.t_text: Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.

cards.note: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8). *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.* (Matthew 23:25). The pride and the riches were real; so was the vaunting. What Wisdom records is their worth on the day, which is nothing. The cup the King points at in the Temple court is the same lesson in a dish: clean on the outside where men can see it, extortion and excess on the inside where only the judgment will look. What has pride profited us is the question the inside of that cup will have to answer when the day of the righteous turns it over.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess.
cards.t_text: What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?

cards.note: *I gathered you together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings: but now, what shall I do to you? I will cast you out from my face.* (2 Esdras 1:30). *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37). The voice in 2 Esdras is Yahuah (God) speaking to Yashar'el (Israel): I gathered you as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not stay gathered. In the temple Yahusha (Jesus) says the same words over Jerusalem in the first person, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. He is not borrowing a figure of speech; he is the one who did the gathering the figure describes, the one who spoke to the fathers and now stands in the city that killed the prophets he sent. The hen is the same hen, the children are the same children, and the refusal is the same refusal.
cards.s_text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto you, how often would I have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, and you would not!
cards.t_text: I gathered you together, as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings: but now, what shall I do to you? I will cast you out from my face.

cards.note: *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).* (2 Esdras 1:32). *Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:* (Matthew 23:34). The pattern in 2 Esdras is past tense: I sent my servants the prophets, you slew them, I will require their blood. In Matthew 23 the King turns it to the future: behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes, and some of them ye shall kill. He is the sender in both. The same voice that sent Jeremiah and Zechariah to be rejected now sends apostles to be scourged in the synagogues and chased from city to city, and the next verses say the blood of all of them, from Abel onward, will be required of that generation. What Yahuah (God) promised through Esdras, Yahusha (Jesus) pronounces in the temple.
cards.s_text: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them you shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall you scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city:
cards.t_text: I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands, says Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* (2 Esdras 1:33). *Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38). The words are nearly the same in both books. Yahuah (God) Almighty says through Esdras, your house is desolate; Yahusha (Jesus) says in the temple, behold, your house is left unto you desolate, and walks out of it. Jeremiah had said it of the first house before Babylon burned it, and Ezekiel watched the glory leave it. Now the one whose glory it was leaves the second house on his own feet, and the house was desolate from that hour whatever the priests kept doing in it. The leadership that killed the prophets lost the house; the children the hen would have gathered are still being gathered.
cards.s_text: Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
cards.t_text: Thus says the Almighty Yahuah (God), Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.

cards.note: *Nevertheless as concerning the tokens, behold, the days shall come, that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.* (2 Esdras 5:1). *And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.* (Matthew 24:10). The first sign Esdras is given of the end is not war or famine but this: the way of truth hidden and the land barren of faith. The King gives the same sign in the same order in Matthew 24, many offended, betraying one another, hating one another, and two verses on, because lawlessness abounds the love of many grows cold. Faith does not die by itself; it dies when the way of truth, which is the law of Yahuah (God), is hidden from the people, and lawlessness fills the place it left. Esdras saw the land barren; the King explains what made it so.
cards.s_text: And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.
cards.t_text: Nevertheless as concerning the tokens, behold, the days shall come, that they which dwell upon earth shall be taken in a great number, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith.

cards.note: *But if the Most High grant you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night, and the moon thrice in the day:* (2 Esdras 5:4). *Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:* (Matthew 24:29). Esdras is told that those who live to see it will see the sun shine in the night and the moon by day, after the third trumpet. The King says that immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give her light, and the stars will fall. The prophets had said the same of the day of Yahuah (LORD): Isaiah, Joel, Amos, Zephaniah.
