In both books the disordered heavens come after the trouble, not before it, and in both they are seen by people still standing on the earth. A teaching that has his people carried away before those days has to set 2 Esdras 5 and Matthew 24 both aside to stand.
cards.s_text: Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken:
cards.t_text: But if the Most High grant you to live, you shall see after the third trumpet that the sun shall suddenly shine again in the night, and the moon thrice in the day:

cards.note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber,* (2 Esdras 5:9). *And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.* (Matthew 24:10). Among the signs Esdras is given is that all friends shall destroy one another. The King names the same thing among his: many shall be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. The pressure of the last days does not only come from outside; it turns friend on friend and brother on brother inside the house, and Paul tasted it when Demas forsook him and no man stood with him at his first answer. Esdras and Matthew both put the betrayal of friends on the list of signs, so the reader will not mistake it for proof that the way was wrong.
cards.s_text: And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.
cards.t_text: And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber,

cards.note: *And the time shall be when these things shall come to pass, and the signs shall happen which I shewed you before, and then shall my Son be declared, whom you sawest as a man ascending.* (2 Esdras 13:32). *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30). Ezra sees a man come up out of the sea and is told that when the signs have happened, the Most High's Son will be declared. Yahusha (Jesus) sets the same order on the Mount of Olives: after the tribulation the sign of the Son of Adam appears in heaven and all the tribes of the earth see him coming in the clouds with power and great glory. The signs come first, then the Son is shown openly to all. Ezra was given the sequence; Matthew names the one it is about.
cards.s_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.t_text: And the time shall be when these things shall come to pass, and the signs shall happen which I shewed you before, and then shall my Son be declared, whom you sawest as a man ascending.

cards.note: *And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him; Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:39–40). *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). Ezra asks about the peaceable multitude the man from the sea gathers to himself, and the Most High tells him outright who they are: the ten tribes carried out of their own land by Salmanasar of Assyria and taken over the waters into another land. The elect gathered from the four winds at the sound of the trumpet are that multitude. The gathering Yahusha (Jesus) describes is not the assembling of whoever has decided to believe; it is the homecoming of a scattered people the Most High kept, named here by tribe. Ezra tells us whom the angels are sent to gather.
cards.s_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.t_text: And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him;

cards.note: *For it is an easy thing to Yahuah (God) in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways.* (Ecclesiasticus 11:26). *Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.* (Matthew 24:46). Sirach says the reward according to a man's ways is an easy thing for Yahuah (God) at the day of death. Yahusha (Jesus) blesses the servant found so doing when the lord returns — found at the work, not found having once begun it. The reward follows the ways walked through the whole delay. The day of death and the day of the lord's coming come to the same servant, and what he is found doing is the whole question.
cards.s_text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he comes shall find so doing.
cards.t_text: For it is an easy thing to Yahuah (God) in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways.

cards.note: *Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.* (Ecclesiasticus 16:14). *Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.* (Matthew 24:47). Sirach says every man shall find according to his works. The faithful and wise servant of Matthew 24 found more — ruler over all his goods — because he was found faithful with the household he had. The one-time confession that the pulpits treat as the whole account is not what either verse describes. The finding is according to the walking, and the servant is rewarded for what he was found doing through the long wait.
cards.s_text: Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.
cards.t_text: Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.

cards.note: *As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:4). *And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 24:51). Shake a sieve and what stays behind is the refuse; so a man's talk shows what is left in him once everything else falls through. The servant in Matthew 24 was trusted with his lord's household, and his talk and his conduct while the lord delayed showed what he was, so that when the lord came he was cut asunder and given his portion with the hypocrites. That is a sifting of the household, not of strangers; the one being sifted had been given a stewardship. Ezekiel says the same about the righteous man who turns from his righteousness, that none of his righteousness will be remembered (Ezekiel 18:24), and John the Baptist saw the fan in the Messiah's hand purging his own floor (Matthew 3:12). The sieve finds the refuse among the servants.
cards.s_text: And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
cards.t_text: As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk.

cards.note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.* (Matthew 24:46). Wisdom sets the shining of the righteous at the time of their visitation — the day the Master comes to look in on his house. Yahusha (Jesus) describes that same day from the servant's side: blessed is that servant whom his lord, when he comes, finds so doing. The visitation is the coming. The servant found at his work when the Master arrives is the one who shines, which is what Daniel saw as well — *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament* (Daniel 12:3).
cards.s_text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he comes shall find so doing.
cards.t_text: And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.

cards.note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:* (Matthew 25:31). The time of the righteous' visitation in Wisdom is the day Yahusha (Jesus) describes at the opening of the sheep and the goats: the Son of Adam coming in his glory with all the holy angels, and sitting on the throne of his glory. That is the visitation. The righteous who were killed in the sight of men shine on that day and not before, the way Daniel saw it — *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament* (Daniel 12:3). The throne and the shining arrive together.
cards.s_text: When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory:
cards.t_text: And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.

cards.note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:* (Matthew 25:32). Before the righteous judge the nations there is a gathering and a sorting. Yahusha (Jesus) says all nations are gathered before him and he separates them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats — the seed brought out of every nation and sifted, the way Ezekiel saw it pass under the rod. Then the sifted remnant, his brethren of Matthew 25:40, does what Wisdom says: judges the nations and has dominion over the people. Daniel saw the same order — *judgment was given to the saints of the El Elyon (most High); and the time came that the saints possessed the kingdom* (Daniel 7:22). The gathering comes first, the reign after.
cards.s_text: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats:
cards.t_text: They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.

cards.note: *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). *Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:* (Matthew 25:34). At the judgment his afflicters discover that the man they despised is numbered among the children of Yahuah (God) and has his lot among the saints. The King says where that lot came from: a kingdom prepared for the blessed from the foundation of the world. It was not assigned on the day; it was prepared before there was a world, and the day only reveals whose it was. Names were written in the Lamb's book from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), and on that day the sheep hear the Shepherd say come, because they were his before they ever heard him.
cards.s_text: Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world:
cards.t_text: How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!

cards.note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:* (Matthew 25:41). Wisdom and the King are describing the same day from two sides. On that day the righteous stand in great boldness, and the next verse in Wisdom has their afflicters troubled with terrible fear and amazed at a salvation they never looked for, which is exactly the astonishment of those on the left hand asking when they ever saw him hungry or thirsty (Matthew 25:44). Notice what the King says about the fire: it was prepared for the devil and his angels, the fallen ones Jude and Peter say are kept in chains for judgment (Jude 6; 2 Peter 2:4), and John sees the devil himself cast into that lake of fire (Revelation 20:10). The goats are sent toward a place that was not made for them. They are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted before the reign, not the nations being judged for entry.
cards.s_text: Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, you cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:
cards.t_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.

cards.note: *Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.* (Ecclesiasticus 11:21). *His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:21). Sirach tells the labourer not to marvel at how sinners get on, but to trust Yahuah (God) and stay at the work, because he can make a poor man rich in a moment. The faithful servant of the parable did exactly that — did not look sideways, did not stop, traded what he was given — and heard well done. The commendation is for the faithfulness, not the size of the return; the servant with two talents heard the same words as the one with five.
cards.s_text: His lord said unto him, Well done, you good and faithful servant: you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things: enter you into the joy of your lord.
cards.t_text: Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.

cards.note: *A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:1). *His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:* (Matthew 25:26). Sirach's picture is blunt: a slothful man is a filthy stone, and everyone hisses him out to his disgrace. The lord in the parable is just as blunt with the servant who buried his talent — wicked and slothful, he calls him, because the servant knew what his master expected and did nothing. The fault in both is the same: not wickedness done, but the work left undone. Sloth is treated as disgrace in the wisdom book and as judgment in the parable, and it is the same sin in both.
cards.s_text: His lord answered and said unto him, You wicked and slothful servant, you knew that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed:
cards.t_text: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.

cards.note: *Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.* (Ecclesiasticus 33:28). *Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury.* (Matthew 25:27). Sirach's counsel for a servant is to set him to work fit for him, and if he will not obey, to bind him tighter; idleness, the verse before says, teaches much evil. The master in the parable judges his servant by the same measure. The servant was not condemned for losing the money; he was condemned for doing nothing with it, when even handing it to the exchangers would have been work enough. The one who was given a charge and buried it is the one Sirach's heavier fetters were written for.
cards.s_text: You oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received my own with usury.
cards.t_text: Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.

cards.note: *Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:30). *His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.* (Matthew 25:23). Sirach's last word is a word about timing: do your work early, and the reward comes in his time, not yours. The faithful servant in the parable did exactly that; he worked while the master was away and was paid when the master came back, rule over many things and entry into his lord's joy. The reward is not handed out along the way. Yahusha (Jesus) says *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works* (Matthew 16:27), and the reigning with him that follows the first resurrection is that reward (Revelation 20:4–6). The work is now; the wages are at his coming.
cards.s_text: His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a few things, I will make you ruler over many things: enter you into the joy of your lord.
cards.t_text: Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.

cards.note: *And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* (2 Esdras 8:1). *And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.* (Matthew 25:10). Ten virgins went out to meet the bridegroom, and all ten were called to the wedding; only those who were ready went in before the door was shut. That is Ezra's answer told as a story: this world is made for many, the world to come for few. The five who found the door shut were not strangers; they were virgins with lamps who had gone out to meet him. The few are those found ready when he comes, which is why readiness matters more than having once set out.
cards.s_text: And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.
cards.t_text: And he answered me, saying, The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.

cards.note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:3). *But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.* (Matthew 25:12). Many created, few saved: Ezra receives it as the hard rule of the age. The foolish virgins knock at the shut door and hear I know you not, the same word spoken to those who say Lord, Lord and work iniquity (Matthew 7:23). They were among the called and they were not among the few. Ezra's few saved and the bridegroom's I know you not are the two ends of one sentence.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.
cards.t_text: There be many created, but few shall be saved.

cards.note: *And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.* (2 Esdras 7:35). *And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 25:30). Ezra is told that at the judgment the work follows and the reward is shown, that good deeds are of force and wicked ones bear no rule. The servant in the parable was given a talent and called a servant; he belonged to the house. What condemned him was not that he was never the master's, but that his work did not follow, and so he is cast into the outer darkness. The warning here is to those inside the household whose deeds bore no fruit, which is why it is so sharp.
cards.s_text: And cast you the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
cards.t_text: And the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed, and the good deeds shall be of force, and wicked deeds shall bear no rule.

cards.note: *And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end:* (2 Esdras 7:33). The seat of judgment Esdras sees comes after the old silence of seven days (2 Esdras 7:30), at the judgment of the dead after the reign. The throne of glory of Matthew 25:31-32 comes first, at his coming, where the gathered are sifted, the sheep from the goats; and Joel's valley of Jehoshaphat, where he pleads with the nations *for my people and for my heritage Yashar'el (Israel)* (Joel 3:2), is the Day on the scatterers. One King, two sittings, the reign between them.
cards.s_text: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats:
cards.t_text: And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end:

cards.note: *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.* (Tobit 4:16). *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* (Matthew 25:35). Bread to the hungry, garments to the naked, alms according to abundance, no envious eye — Tobit gives his son two of the very things the King names at the judgment: *I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat ... naked, and ye clothed me.* Isaiah had said the same, to deal bread to the hungry and cover the naked. This is not a charity program for the world in general; the King says it is mercy done to his brethren, and it is the measure by which the sheep are told from the goats. The library had been teaching that measure in the exile household all along.
cards.s_text: For I was an hungred, and you gave me meat: I was thirsty, and you gave me drink: I was a stranger, and you took me in:
cards.t_text: Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.

cards.note: *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32). *Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.* (Matthew 25:36). Sirach says the hand stretched to the poor is what perfects the blessing — the blessing is not finished until it has gone out the door to someone in need. Yahusha (Jesus) sets the same thing as the measure at his judgment seat: the naked clothed, the sick visited, the prisoner visited, and he counts it as done to himself. Sirach keeps going in the next verses — be with them that weep, be not slow to visit the sick — and the list reads like the King's own. This is the fruit of the new heart Ezekiel promised, a heart that keeps his judgments because it has been made able to; a confession that never stretches out its hand has not yet been perfected into a blessing.
cards.s_text: Naked, and you clothed me: I was sick, and you visited me: I was in prison, and you came unto me.
cards.t_text: And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.

cards.note: *Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:9). *And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* (Matthew 25:40). Sirach says help the poor because the commandment says so, and do not turn him away because he is poor. At the judgment the King says that whatever was done to the least of his brethren was done to him. The mercy Sirach commands is not a charity program; it is the commandment kept, and the King counts it as done to himself because the least of these are his own kin, his brethren, the household of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered and poor. Help the poor for the commandment's sake and you have served the King without knowing his face.
cards.s_text: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as you have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, you have done it unto me.
cards.t_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:1). *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* (Matthew 25:35). Sirach's command not to defraud the poor and not to keep needy eyes waiting is what the sheep in Matthew 25 are found to have done: I was hungry and you gave me meat, thirsty and you gave me drink, a stranger and you took me in. The judgment does not ask whether a man knew the right words; it asks what he did when the needy eyes were on him, and Sirach's chapter goes on to name the failure the goats are judged for, turn not away your eye from the needy (verse 5). This is not earning anything; it is what covenant life with Yahuah (God) looks like from the outside. The King recognizes his own by it because it was always his way.
cards.s_text: For I was an hungred, and you gave me meat: I was thirsty, and you gave me drink: I was a stranger, and you took me in:
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.* (Matthew 25:40). Tobit promises that the face of Yahuah (God) stays turned toward the man who does not turn his face from the poor. Yahusha (Jesus) says it more sharply: what you did to the least of my brethren you did to me. The giver meets the King in the one he feeds, and the King's face toward him is the Father's face toward him. The same thing was said to Saul on the Damascus road, that to persecute the brethren was to persecute him (Acts 9:4–5). It is personal: mercy toward the King's brethren is mercy the King himself receives.
cards.s_text: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as you have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, you have done it unto me.
cards.t_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.

cards.note: *Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.* (1 Maccabees 1:63). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). Under Antiochus the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) chose death over unclean meat because eating it would profane the holy covenant, and so they died. At the table Yahusha (Jesus) names his own blood the blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The covenant the Maccabean faithful died for and the covenant he died to seal are not two covenants with two laws; Jeremiah says the new covenant is the law written in the inward parts and on the heart, the same law those men would not break. They gave their lives rather than profane it; he gave his to write it where it could not be taken from them.
cards.s_text: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
cards.t_text: Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.

cards.note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* (1 Maccabees 2:50). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). Mattathias, dying, charges his sons to be zealous for the law and to give their lives for the covenant of their fathers. The King does both. His zeal for his Father's house and his Father's commandments runs through the gospels, and at the table he gives his life, his blood of the new covenant shed for many. The covenant of the fathers and the new covenant are one covenant; what is new in Jeremiah 31 is where the law is written, on the heart, not whether it stands. So the zeal Mattathias asked of his sons is not a different thing from what Yahusha (Jesus) poured out; it is the same love of the same law, carried to the same end.
cards.s_text: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.

cards.note: *For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.* (2 Maccabees 7:36). *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). The youngest brother says his brothers are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life. They died for his laws, and their deaths are held inside a covenant that promises them life again. At the last supper Yahusha (Jesus) names his blood as the blood of the new covenant, shed for many for the remission of sins. The covenant the martyrs died under and the covenant the King's blood seals are not two covenants; the brothers trusted a promise of everlasting life, and the King's death and third-day rising are where that promise was made good. Their short pain and his cup end in the same resurrection, and the Torah they died for is the Torah the new covenant writes on the heart (Jeremiah 31:33).
cards.s_text: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
cards.t_text: For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.

cards.note: *Why dost thou delay, O tyrant? We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.* 4 Maccabees 6:29 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the ready-to-die-rather-than-transgress-the-commandments substance — the Maccabean-seven-brothers' one-voice declaration to Antiochus-Epiphanes. The framework reads the verse against Matt 26:39's *O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.* The Maccabean-faithful-servants walk-the-substantial-ready-to-die-rather-than-transgress-the-commandments-substance against the substantial-tyrant-substance; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-substantively-the-substantial-cup-of-suffering-substance the substantial Tanakh-cup-of-Yahuah's-wrath-cluster (Psalm 75:8 + Isaiah 51:17-22 + Jeremiah 25:15-29 + Ezekiel 23:31-34) the King drinks-as-the-substantial-Pesach-lamb-substance for-the-substantial-remission-of-sins-substance. The framework reads this carefully — the Gethsemane-cup-substance is NOT-substantially-the-categorical-physical-suffering-only-substance the modern-Christian-collapse walks-from; the substantial-cup is the substantial-Father's-cup-of-Yahuah's-wrath-substance the King-as-the-Suffering-Servant-substance drinks-substantively the substantial Isaiah 53:10 substance the prophet-Yeshayahu (Isaiah) walked walks-into (*yet it pleased Yahuah (the LORD) to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin*). The Maccabean-prefiguring-substance walks-the-pattern; the King walks-the-substantial-fulfillment-at-the-categorically-greater-substance.
cards.s_text: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as you will.
cards.t_text: 'Why dost thou delay, O tyrant? We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.

cards.note: *And righteousness won the victory, and gave the crown to her athletes.* 4 Maccabees 13:13 names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the righteousness-won-the-victory + the prize-of-victory-in-incorruption-everlasting-life substance the Maccabean-seven-brothers walked-out-substantively faithful-unto-death. The framework reads the verse against Matt 26:42's second-Gethsemane-prayer (*O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done*). The Maccabean-faithful-walked-the-endurance-substance-into-the-substantial-prize-of-victory-in-incorruption-everlasting-life; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-substantively-the-substantial-drinking-of-the-cup-into-the-substantial-resurrection-of-the-third-day-substance. The substantial *thy will be done* substance walks the substantial-Formless-Source-and-Formed-Expression-substance — the substantial-Father-substance is-the-substantial-Formless-Source-substance, the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) is-the-substantial-Formed-Expression-substance walking-eternally-submitted-to-the-Formless-Source-substance the apostle-Yochanan (John) walks at John 5:30 and John 8:28-29 walks-substantively. The substantial-substance walks-the-substantial-direct-rule-out of three-inherited-collapses-of-the-substantial-nature-of-Elohim-substance: (a) the Trinitarian-three-co-equal-persons-substance (three-co-equal-persons-substance does-NOT-walk the Gethsemane-substance the Son-submits-to-the-Father); (b) the modalist-collapse-substance (the substantial-distinction-between-the-Father-substance and the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-as-the-Son-of-Adam-substance walks-substantively-the-Gethsemane-substance); (c) the Arian-created-being-substance (the substantial-King-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-as-the-Formed-Expression-substance walks-the-substantial-eternal-Word-substance, NOT-a-created-being-substance).
cards.s_text: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, your will be done.
cards.t_text: But the first in the fight was Eleazar, and the mother of the seven sons played her part, and the brethren fought.

cards.note: *They having as it were become a ransom for our nation's sin; and through the blood of these righteous men and the propitiation of their death, the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel) that before was evil entreated.* 4 Maccabees 13:18 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the ransom-for-our-nation's-sin + propitiation-of-their-death-delivered-Yashar'el (Israel) substance — the Maccabean-faithful-servants' faithful-unto-death-as-the-substantial-prefiguring-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 26:46's *Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me* — the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-substantively into-the-substantial-arrest + the substantial-passion + the substantial-Cross + the substantial-third-day-resurrection. The substantial-Maccabean-prefiguring-substance walks-the-substantial-ransom-and-propitiation-substance at-the-substantial-Maccabean-faithful-servants-substance; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel)-as-the-Pesach-lamb-substance walks-the-substantial-fulfillment-substance at-the-substantial-categorically-greater-substance the substantial Matthew 20:28 substance the King had-walked walks-into (*the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many*). The framework reads this carefully — the substantial *ransom* (Greek *lytron* + Greek *antallagma*) substance and the substantial *propitiation* (Greek *hilasterion* + Greek *hilasmos*) substance the King walks-out is NOT-substantially-the-forensic-substitutionary-juridical-transaction-substance the inherited-Anselmian-Reformation-Calvinist-collapse walks-from; the substantial-substance is the substantial-Pesach-lamb-fulfillment-substance the Tanakh-Exodus-12-Pesach-substance + the substantial Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement) substance the prophet-Mosheh (Moses) walked at Leviticus 16 walks-into directly + the substantial-Isaiah-53-Suffering-Servant-bearing-the-iniquities-of-the-many-substance walks-into. The Maccabean-prefiguring-substance walks-the-pattern; the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-the-substantial-fulfillment-at-the-categorically-greater-substance.
cards.s_text: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that does betray me.
cards.t_text: whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.

cards.note: *Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:1). *Then Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said.* (Matthew 26:25). Sirach warns against two things in one verse, the friend who turns enemy and the sinner with a double tongue, and Judas is both at the table. He had already sold his Master for thirty pieces of silver, and he asks, Master, is it I?, with the bargain in his pocket; that is the double tongue, one voice at the supper and another with the priests. Yahusha (Jesus) answers, thou hast said, and lets the man's own mouth carry the verdict. The betrayal served the Father's purpose and was Judas's own choice at the same time; the devil put it in his heart, John says, and Judas walked it out, and Sirach's warning stands over him as the shame and reproach of a friend who became an enemy.
cards.s_text: Then Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, You have said.
cards.t_text: Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.

cards.note: *An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit: he will weep with his eyes, but if he find opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.* (Ecclesiasticus 12:16). *And forthwith he came to Yahusha (Jesus), and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.* (Matthew 26:49). Sirach draws the enemy who speaks sweetly with his lips while planning the pit, who weeps with his eyes and is not satisfied with blood. Judas came with Hail, master, and a kiss. The sweet lips and the pit were never far apart in the Hebrew library, and Yahusha (Jesus) knew the pattern before the kiss landed. The betrayer is the old enemy of the proverbs with a face.
cards.s_text: And forthwith he came to Yahusha (Jesus), and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.
cards.t_text: An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit: he will weep with his eyes, but if he find opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.

cards.note: *Is it not a grief to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?* (Ecclesiasticus 37:2). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Yahusha (Jesus), and took him.* (Matthew 26:50). Sirach asks whether it is not a grief unto death when a companion and friend turns enemy. In the garden Yahusha (Jesus) called Judas Friend as the kiss was given and the hands were laid on him. He had just said his soul was exceeding sorrowful, even unto death, which is Sirach's own measure of it. The friend who had eaten his bread lifted up his heel against him, and the King named him Friend to the last; that is the grief Sirach meant.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Friend, wherefore are you come? Then came they, and laid hands on Yahusha (Jesus), and took him.
cards.t_text: Is it not a grief to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?

cards.note: *My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:1). *Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.* (Matthew 26:41). In Gethsemane Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples to watch and pray so they do not enter into temptation, and they fall asleep. Sirach had said what they needed to hear before they ever came to the garden: if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation. The flesh is weak, the Messiah says; what Sirach adds is that a servant can get his soul ready for that weakness instead of being surprised by it. The disciples were willing in spirit and unprepared in soul, and the night proved Sirach right.
cards.s_text: Watch and pray, that you enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
cards.t_text: My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). *And Peter remembered the word of Yahusha (Jesus), which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.* (Matthew 26:75). Peter went into the furnace that night and came out weeping. He had denied his Master three times, the cock crowed, the word came back to him, and he went out and wept bitterly. Sirach says acceptable men are tried in the furnace of adversity the way gold is tried in the fire, and the bitter weeping is the fire working. Caiaphas had rent his garments a few verses earlier (v.65); Peter rent his heart, which is the tearing Yahuah (God) asks for, and it carried him to the restoration by the shore in John 21. A disciple can fail, and a failed disciple is neither finished nor safe; he repents, and the furnace is what shows whether he is gold.
cards.s_text: And Peter remembered the word of Yahusha (Jesus), which said unto him, Before the cock crow, you shall deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.* 2 Baruch (Charles edition seq #3, verse 7; standard 2 Baruch 6:7) names the wisdom-stream's direct external-witness articulation of the heavenly-angel-descending-into-the-Holy-of-Holies-and-taking-the-veil substance — the wisdom-stream had named the veil-architecture at the heavenly-register (the angel-from-above acting upon the veil), and Matt 27:51's *the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom* names the operative-fulfillment at the earthly-pivot. The framework reads the verses together: the *from the top to the bottom* direction names the Father-from-above tearing-the-veil-from-the-heavenly-side, opening-the-way-back-into-the-Most-Holy-Place per Hebrews 10:19-22's *boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus), by a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh.* This is the door-home opening architecturally per the *Grace, the Way, the New Heart, and the Mercy of Depart* exposition in framework-deep.md — grace as the means of return-to-the-Father's-house, NOT the inherited-Christian-replacement-theology reading that the temple-system-is-now-replaced-by-the-church (the framework rejects the abolition-of-the-Father's-house reading; the framework reads the veil-rent as Yahuah-opening-the-Way-back-into-the-Father's-house, not as Yahuah-abolishing-the-Father's-house). FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.

The King COULD save-himself-substantively per Matt 26:53 + John 10:17-18 (*no man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself*); he chooses the Pesach (Passover)-lamb-substance per the Father's-purpose-substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:43's mockers' *he trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* The mockers' challenge is the inverse of the architecture the wisdom-stream named: the live-unto-Elohim substance does NOT require the present-deliverance-from-the-cross-substance the mockers demand; the deliverance-architecture is the resurrection-after-the-third-day per Hosheia (Hosea) 6:2 + the patriarchs-sleeping-awaiting-the-first-resurrection per Hebrews 11:39-40 (*they without us should not be made perfect*). The wisdom-stream had named the architecture; the cross walks-out the King's-own-walking-into-the-patriarchs'-pattern.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:50's *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost* — the King's-voluntary-laying-down-of-the-life is the supreme-walking-out of the endurance-architecture the wisdom-stream named at the seven-sons-and-the-mother martyrdom-witness. The Greek *aphēken to pneuma* — *yielded up the spirit* — names the voluntary-substance per John 10:17-18 (*no man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself*); the prize-of-victory-in-incorruption is the resurrection-on-the-third-day + the first-resurrection-at-the-King's-coming per Red Line #11. cards.note: *After these years shall my son Messiah (Christ) die, and all men that have life. And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* (2 Esdras 7:29–30). *Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.* (Matthew 27:45). Ezra is told that the Messiah will die, and that the world will then be turned back into the old silence, as in the former judgments, before the raising up that follows (2 Esdras 7:31–32). When Yahusha (Jesus) hung on the tree, darkness lay over all the land from the sixth hour to the ninth, as if creation had drawn back toward its first dark. The three hours were not the seven days; they were a small showing of them, the world going quiet at the death of the Messiah (Christ) before the graves gave up their dead (Matthew 27:52). Amos had said *I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day* (Amos 8:9); Ezra was told the Messiah's death brings the old silence; the cross carried both for three hours.
cards.s_text: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

cards.note: *And the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment, and misery shall pass away, and the long suffering shall have an end:* (2 Esdras 7:33). *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). In Ezra's order, once the earth has given back her dead the Most High appears upon the seat of judgment, and misery and long suffering come to an end. At the moment Yahusha (Jesus) died the veil of the temple tore from top to bottom, the earth quaked, the rocks split, and the graves were opened (Matthew 27:52). The signs that belong to the day of the Most High's appearing broke through for a moment at the cross. It was not that day, but it carried the marks of it, the way a first shaking tells of the one still to come (Haggai 2:6–7).

cards.note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). Ezra is told that the earth will restore those asleep in her, that the dust will give back those that dwell in silence. At the cross the earth quaked and the graves were opened, and many bodies of the saints that slept arose. The earth was doing in small measure what Ezra was told she will do fully: giving back what was sleeping in her. The saints who came out of their graves that day are a first showing of the resurrection the fathers are still waiting for, the first resurrection in which the faithful who fell asleep are raised (Revelation 20:4–6; Hebrews 11:39–40).

cards.note: *But those who have been saved by their works, And to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence, Shall wonders appear in their time. For they shall behold the world which is now invisible to them, And they shall behold the time which is now hidden from them.* 2 Baruch (Charles edition seq #21, verse 1; standard 2 Baruch 51:1-8) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the saved-by-their-works-shall-behold-the-world-now-invisible substance — the apocalyptic-stream's resurrection-glory architecture. The framework reads the verse against Matt 27:52-53's *and the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose, and came out of the graves after his resurrection, and went into the holy city, and appeared unto many* — the saints-arising-and-appearing-in-the-holy-city substance is the historical-pivot-foretaste of the broader-architecture 2 Baruch 51 names: the faithful-righteous-shall-behold-the-world-now-invisible + shall-be-made-like-unto-the-angels + shall-be-equal-to-the-stars. The framework reads the saved-by-their-works language CAREFULLY — NOT the inherited-Reformation-merit-doctrine collapse; the framework reads works as the fruit-of-the-Spirit-internalized-Torah per Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 36:26-27 + Yirmeyahu (Jeremiah) 31:31-34 + James 2:14-26's *faith without works is dead*; the works are the Spirit-empowered-walking-in-the-Way the framework's *Grace, the Way, the New Heart, and the Mercy of Depart* exposition unfolds. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-resurrection-glory; the saints-arising-at-the-cross substance is the historical-foretaste.

cards.note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). The angel at the tomb announced the first man to pass through Wisdom's time of visitation: He is not here, for he is risen. The righteous who are held in the Father's hand shine when he visits them, and the empty tomb is the firstfruits of that day — *Messiah (Christ) the firstfruits; afterward they that are Messiah's (Christ's) at his coming* (1 Corinthians 15:23). Daniel saw the rest of them still sleeping in the dust until they awake and shine (Daniel 12:2–3). One has risen; the others rest and wait for the same visitation.

cards.t_text: And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.

cards.note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). Wisdom sees the righteous judging the nations and ruling the people under an Elohim (God) who reigns for ever — the reign John saw on the earth, where *they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years* (Revelation 20:4). That reign needs risen saints, and the empty tomb is where the rising began: He is not here, for he is risen. The first to rise is the one who will seat the rest. This is not souls escaping to heaven while the earth burns; it is the dead raised to rule on the earth with their King, the way Daniel said the saints of the most High would take the kingdom.

cards.note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9). The righteous live for evermore. The women at the tomb found out what that looks like: they held him by the feet. He had a body they could grip, flesh and bones he would show the disciples that evening (Luke 24:39), and that risen body is the firstfruits of what Wisdom promises the righteous. The righteous dead are not disembodied souls already in heaven; they are asleep, their reward kept with Yahuah (God), waiting for the day the one who rose first raises them (1 Thessalonians 4:16). The care of them is with the Most High the whole time they wait.

cards.note: *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God): for with his right hand shall he cover them, and with his arm shall he protect them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:16). *And as they went to tell his disciples, behold, Yahusha (Jesus) met them, saying, All hail. And they came and held him by the feet, and worshipped him.* (Matthew 28:9). The women held the risen King by the feet and worshipped him. He is the first of the righteous to receive the glorious kingdom from the Father's hand, and the crown Wisdom speaks of is the one Paul expects at his appearing (2 Timothy 4:8) and the one the King promises to the faithful unto death (Revelation 2:10). The right hand that covers the righteous is the hand he will name a few verses later when he says all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth (Matthew 28:18). What the women touched that morning was the first of the resurrected righteous, crowned.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). Set these two side by side and the Great Commission stops reading as a change of audience. Ezra was shown the ten tribes carried over the waters into another land, and that land is among the nations; the scattered house lives there, mixed in and unrecognizable, the people Hosea called not my people (Hosea 1:9). So the King who said he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) now sends his disciples to all nations, because that is where the sheep are. The scope widened to every nation because the flock is scattered through every nation, not because the flock was replaced. We do not know those sheep by sight, so the word goes out broadly, and the ones who hear are revealed to be his (John 10:27).

cards.note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). Ezra sees the ten tribes come back through the stream the Most High stays for them; the peaceable multitude of his vision is the scattered house coming home, and it is the Highest who does the gathering. Yahusha (Jesus) sends his disciples to all nations, and these two verses explain each other: the disciples go out into the nations because that is where the tribes were carried, and the Father brings them back. Isaiah had already said he would set his hand the second time to recover the remnant of his people from the four corners of the earth (Isaiah 11:11–12); James wrote to the twelve tribes scattered abroad (James 1:1), and Peter to the strangers scattered through the provinces (1 Peter 1:1). The proclamation to all nations is that second recovery going out to find them.

cards.note: *For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.* (2 Esdras 9:31). *And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.* (Mark 4:20). The law is spoken of here as seed: I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you. The good ground in the parable is those who hear the word, receive it, and bring forth fruit, thirty, sixty, a hundredfold. The word sown in Mark is the law sown in Ezra, and the fruit is the same fruit, a people keeping what was put in them. Ezra goes on to say that the fathers who received it and kept it not perished (2 Esdras 9:32–33), which is the other soils of the parable.
cards.s_text: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

cards.note: *But as concerning the things of which you ask me, I will tell you; for the evil is sown, but the destruction thereof is not yet come.* (2 Esdras 4:28, with 4:32 — *And when the ears shall be cut down, which are without number, how great a floor shall they fill?*) The sown-evil awaits its appointed harvest-floor. Mark 4:29's *when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come* names the same appointed threshing 2 Esdras 4 names: the seed grows of itself by the Father's clock until the cutting-down of the ears, the harvest-floor of the age.

cards.t_text: But as concerning the things of which you ask me, I will tell you; for the evil is sown, but the destruction thereof is not yet come.

cards.note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.* (Mark 4:15). The evil seed in the heart of Adam has been bearing ungodliness since the beginning, Uriel says, and will until the threshing. In the parable of the sower the word is sown and Satan comes at once and takes it out of the heart before it can root. The heart is the ground in both; in one the evil seed is sown into it, in the other the good seed is stolen out of it. Mark's four soils are the field Esdras was shown, and the adversary works the same ground the same way until the harvest.
cards.s_text: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan comes immediately, and takes away the word that was sown in their hearts.

cards.note: *For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders.* What a man brings forth reveals the heart that bore it: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 27:6) The Hebrew library makes the utterance the disclosure of the heart's tending; the King's catalogue of what proceeds from within is the same diagnostic — the fruit declares the tree, and the heart's contents declare the man.
cards.s_text: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
cards.t_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.

cards.note: *And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.* The defilement proceeds from the man's own heart because the man was made a free agent over his own counsel: *He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel.* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 15:14) The Hebrew library locates the source of evil in the man's own choosing, not in what enters from without; the King names the same — the heart, not the unwashen hand, is where defilement begins.
cards.s_text: And he said, That which comes out of the man, that defiles the man.

cards.note: *For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:9). *Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.* (Mark 7:13). Sirach says a father's blessing establishes the houses of children and a mother's curse roots out foundations, so honour toward parents is not a courtesy; it is what a house stands on. Yahusha (Jesus) says the tradition that voided the fifth commandment made the word of Elohim (God) of none effect, and Sirach tells you what that costs: the blessing forfeited and the foundation uprooted. A tradition that teaches sons to withhold from their parents is pulling the house down on them while calling it devotion. The Messiah names the voiding; Sirach had already named the price.
cards.s_text: Making the word of Elohim (God) of none effect through your tradition, which you have delivered: and many such like things do you.
cards.t_text: For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children; but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.

cards.note: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:8). *And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;* (Mark 7:12). Mark 7:12 is the deed being forbidden: once the vow was spoken, the tradition suffered a man no more to do anything for his father or his mother. Sirach had said honour is both in word and deed, and the corban ruling kept the word, a vow formula that profited the system, and outlawed the deed. Measured by Sirach's own standard, the tradition did not merely fall short of the commandment; it subtracted half of it and called the remainder righteousness. Yahusha (Jesus) is not bringing a new standard against the elders, only the old one they had cut in two.
cards.s_text: And you suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;
cards.t_text: Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.

cards.note: *He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father, and will do service to his parents, as to his masters.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:7). *For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:* (Mark 7:10). Sirach binds honouring one's father to the fear of Yahuah (God): the man who fears him will serve his parents the way a servant serves his masters. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes the commandment behind that, for Moses said, honour thy father and thy mother, and then shows how the corban tradition severed what Sirach had joined, letting a man withhold from his parents what he vowed to the altar and call it devotion. A fear of Yahuah (God) that excuses a man from his parents is not the fear Sirach knew. The tradition had split the two apart; the Messiah puts Moses back on the table.
cards.s_text: For Moses said, Honour your father and your mother; and, Whoso curses father or mother, let him die the death:
cards.t_text: He that fears Yahuah (God) will honour his father, and will do service to his parents, as to his masters.

cards.note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). *And as touching the dead, that they rise: have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush Elohim (God) spake unto him, saying, I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob?* (Mark 12:26). Wisdom admits the plain fact: the righteous are punished in the sight of men, and men watch them die. Then it names what the watchers cannot see — a hope full of immortality. Yahusha (Jesus) puts the same hope on the record of Moses: at the bush, generations after the patriarchs were buried, Elohim (God) still called himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Their death was in the sight of men; their life is in his sight. The resurrection is the shape that hope takes when it is kept.
cards.s_text: And as touching the dead, that they rise: have you not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush Elohim (God) spake unto him, saying, I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob?
cards.t_text: For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *He is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.* (Mark 12:27). The Sadducees denied the resurrection, and Yahusha (Jesus) answered them from the bush: Elohim (God) named himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob long after they were buried, and he is not the Elohim (God) of the dead. Wisdom explains how the fathers can be counted living while they lie in the ground — their souls are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and no torment touches them there. They rest, held against the day he raises them. To deny that is to err greatly, as he told the Sadducees to their faces.
cards.s_text: He is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but the Elohim (God) of the living: you therefore do greatly err.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *And they which did gainsay your promises, and believed not your covenants, have trodden them down.* (2 Esdras 5:29). *What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.* (Mark 12:9). In Ezra's prayer the ones who trod the people down are the ones who gainsaid the promises and did not believe the covenants, the many nations the one people had been given over to (2 Esdras 5:28). In the parable the same unbelief shows up inside the hedge: the husbandmen entrusted with the vineyard beat the servants and kill the heir, acting as though the owner's word about returning were empty. Ezra asks why the Most High lets his people be trodden down; the parable answers with what the lord of the vineyard will do when he comes. Those who tread down what the covenants cover, whether from outside the hedge or from within it, meet the same owner.
cards.s_text: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.
cards.t_text: And they which did gainsay your promises, and believed not your covenants, have trodden them down.

cards.note: *And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* (2 Esdras 5:27). *What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.* (Mark 12:9). Ezra names what the vineyard is before the parable ever has to explain it: one people gotten out of all the multitudes, loved, and given a law. The lord of the vineyard in the parable owns it because he chose it; the husbandmen only hold it. When they beat his servants and kill his heir, what he takes from them is the stewardship, and that is what he gives to others. The one people the Most High loved and gave his law to is still his vineyard; it was never the keepers' to lose.
cards.s_text: What shall therefore the lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard unto others.
cards.t_text: And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.

cards.note: *And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:* (2 Esdras 5:23). *And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.* (Mark 12:1). The vineyard of the parable is not a figure Yahusha (Jesus) invents on the spot; Ezra had already prayed it back to the Most High, who out of all the trees of the earth chose one only vine. In the parable that chosen vine is hedged, given a winefat and a tower, and let out to husbandmen while the owner goes into a far country. Everything the husbandmen later do, they do to a vineyard that was never theirs. The one vine remains the owner's choice; the keepers were only ever entrusted with it.
cards.s_text: And he began to speak unto them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set an hedge about it, and digged a place for the winefat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.
cards.t_text: And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:

cards.note: *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:7). *It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Mark 10:25). Sirach says gold is a stumblingblock to those who sacrifice to it, and every fool is taken by it, taken as a bird is taken in a snare. Yahusha (Jesus) says the rich man passes into the kingdom about as easily as a camel through a needle's eye. The two sayings are one picture: a man held by what he sacrifices to cannot get through the narrow door, because the thing holding him will not fit. It is not the gold that stops at the needle's eye; it is the man who will not let go of it.
cards.s_text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.

cards.note: *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:6). *And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Yahusha (Jesus) answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!* (Mark 10:24). Sirach does not say gold is evil; he says it has ruined many, and that their destruction was standing right beside them while they held it. Yahusha (Jesus) puts his finger on the same spot: not the riches, but the trusting in them. The hand that closes around gold is the hand that cannot take hold of the kingdom, and the disciples were astonished because the whole world around them measured blessing by that very gold.
cards.s_text: And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Yahusha (Jesus) answers again, and says unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!
cards.t_text: Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.

cards.note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:5). *And Yahusha (Jesus) looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!* (Mark 10:23). Sirach says the man who loves gold will not be justified. Yahusha (Jesus) looks round at his disciples after the rich young man walks away and says how hard it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of Elohim (God). It is the same man in both verses: the one Sirach says will not be justified is the one the King says hardly enters. Not because riches are a sin, but because gold tends to own the man who has it, and a man owned by gold does not come in.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) looked round about, and says unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of Elohim (God)!
cards.t_text: He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.

cards.note: *Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:8). *Then Yahusha (Jesus) beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.* (Mark 10:21). Sirach calls the rich man blessed who is found without blemish and has not gone after gold, and the next verse asks, who is he? as if such a man were rare enough to go looking for. Yahusha (Jesus) looked at a rich young man, loved him, and put Sirach's question to him in the flesh: sell what you have, give to the poor, and come. The man went away grieved, because his great possessions had him. The blessing Sirach names was offered to him on the road and he could not take it, because he had gone after gold and the gold had gone after him.
cards.s_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing you lackest: go your way, sell whatsoever you have, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.

cards.note: *Woe to the nations that rise up against my kindred! Yahuah (God) Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment, in putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.* Judith 16:17 names the fire-and-worms judgment register in the same breath the gospel uses at Mark 9:48 — *where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.* The Hebrew library's victory-song already pairs the unquenched fire with the deathless worm and the everlasting feeling of it; the King reads the same Tanakh-rooted Gehenna-image (Isaiah 66:24) that Judith's song carries. The day-of-judgment frame and the *weep for ever* duration are the architecture Mark 9:48 walks.
cards.s_text: Where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched.
cards.t_text: Woe to the nations that rise up against my kindred! Yahuah (God) Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment, in putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.

cards.note: *For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.* (2 Maccabees 7:36). *And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.* (Mark 14:24). Dying under Antiochus, the youngest brother names where his brothers now lie: dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life. They were faithful to the covenant unto death, and the covenant holds them. At the table Yahusha (Jesus) lifts the cup and calls it his blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The martyrs of 2 Maccabees 7 died trusting a covenant of everlasting life whose promise had not yet been made good; Mark 14:24 is the King's own blood put to that same covenant. The many it is shed for include the seven who went before it, and their everlasting life waits on the resurrection the King's own rising opened.
cards.s_text: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.
cards.t_text: For our brothers, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under the covenant of Yahuah (God) of everlasting life: but you, through the judgment of Yahuah (God), shall receive just punishment for your pride.

cards.note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.* (1 Maccabees 2:50). *And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.* (Mark 14:24). A dying father tells his sons to give their lives for the covenant of their fathers, and the sons do it, one after another, through the rest of the book. Mark records the King doing the same thing with his own blood, the blood of the new covenant, shed for many. The many he died for are the people whose fathers cut that covenant at Sinai and whose sons died for it under Antiochus. Mattathias asked his sons for what Yahusha (Jesus) gave, and the covenant both were given for is the same covenant, now written on the heart.
cards.s_text: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.

cards.note: *Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.* 1 Maccabees 1:63 names the faithful who chose death rather than profane the holy covenant. Mark 14:24's *this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many* names the covenant sealed in blood — the King's own blood given for the covenant. The Hebrew library had named the faithful dying for the covenant; the King names the covenant itself sealed by the blood he is about to shed.
cards.s_text: And he said unto them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.
cards.t_text: Wherefore they chose rather to die, that they might not be defiled with meats, and that they might not profane the holy covenant: so then they died.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and given back their inheritance as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam will send his angels and gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the earth to the other. The four winds are where the tribes were scattered; the elect gathered out of them are the tribes Sirach prayed home. The prayer names who; the gospel names how and when.
cards.s_text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 5:5). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). Baruch 4:37 brought the children from east to west; here they come from west to east. Between the two verses the gathering comes from every direction. Mark 13:27 says it the same way: the Son of Adam sends his angels to gather his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth.
