Jerusalem's children in Baruch and the elect in Mark are one people, the scattered seed, brought home by the word of the Holy One and the hand of the Son of Adam at the end of the age. Jerusalem is told to stand on high and watch, because the homecoming is something she will see.
cards.s_text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
cards.t_text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 4:37 names the four-quarters gathering directly — the sons who were sent away come *from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One.* Mark 13:27's *gather together his elect from the four winds* walks the same Hebrew library architecture: the gathering is of those who were sent away (the scattered), and it is accomplished by the word of the Holy One — the Son of Adam who has just been named coming in the clouds (13:26).
cards.s_text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
cards.t_text: Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). The ten tribes did not find their own way home in Ezra's vision. The Highest stayed the springs of the stream for them, as he had once held the waters when they went out, and the multitude came through in peace. Mark 13:27 is the same homecoming seen from the gospel side: when the Son of Adam comes, he sends his angels to gather his elect from the four winds, from one end of the earth to the other. The gathering is his act in both books. The scattered seed is brought back by the hand of the Most High, not by its own contriving, and the elect of Mark 13 are the people Ezra watched cross the stream.
cards.s_text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
cards.t_text: The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 13:40 names the ten tribes of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) by the precise history of their scattering — the Assyrian captivity under Hoshea and Shalmaneser. Mark 13:27's gathering *from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven* is the answering-act to this scattering: the same tribes the Hebrew library traced into the further country are the elect the angels gather at the end.
cards.s_text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him; Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:39–40). *And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.* (Mark 13:27). The man who comes up from the sea gathers a peaceable multitude to himself, and Ezra is told in the next breath who they are: the ten tribes Salmanasar of Assyria carried away captive over the waters into another land. When Yahusha (Jesus) says the angels will gather his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth, that is the multitude he means. The elect are not a people assembled out of whoever chose to join; they are the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) brought home from where they were carried. Ezra puts a name on the ones the four winds give back.
cards.s_text: And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
cards.t_text: And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him;

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *He hath holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy;* (Luke 1:54). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Mary, carrying the child, sings that he has helped his servant Yashar'el (Israel) in remembrance of his mercy. The help she sings is the beginning of the answer to Sirach's prayer: mercy remembered toward the whole servant Yashar'el (Israel), all the tribes, not a figure of speech for some other people. The gathering was being set in motion in her womb.
cards.s_text: He has holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy;
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). *He hath holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy;* (Luke 1:54). Sirach asks mercy for the people called by the name of Yahuah (God), for Yashar'el (Israel) his firstborn. Mary sings that he has helped his servant Yashar'el (Israel) in remembrance of his mercy. The mercy prayed for and the mercy remembered fall on the same people, the firstborn son, the servant, and both are tied to the gathering: Sirach's verse before asks for all the tribes of Jacob, and Mary's next lines name the oath sworn to Abraham. The firstborn is remembered, not replaced.
cards.s_text: He has holpen his servant Yashar'el (Israel), in remembrance of his mercy;
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.

cards.note: *O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 4:36). *As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.* (Luke 1:55). Jerusalem is told to turn east, the direction her children were carried, and watch the joy coming back to her from Yahuah (God); the next verse says what the joy is, her sons gathered from east to west. Mary ends her song on the ground that joy stands on: Yahuah (God) spoke to the fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. The gathering is how the oath to Abraham is kept. Baruch's song and Mary's are singing one thing, a seed promised to the fathers, scattered, and now being brought home because he remembers what he said.
cards.s_text: As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.
cards.t_text: O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 4:37). *As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.* (Luke 1:55). Here is what Jerusalem sees when she looks east: her sons, the ones she sent away, coming gathered from east to west by the word of the Holy One. Mary's song ends with the seed those sons belong to; Yahuah (God) spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed for ever. The sons gathered in Baruch are Abraham's seed, scattered by exile and brought back because the oath was for ever. The Magnificat names the promise; Baruch names its fulfillment walking home.
cards.s_text: As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.
cards.t_text: Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) has appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Yashar'el (Israel) may go safely in the glory of Yahuah (God),* (Baruch 5:7). *Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;* (Luke 3:5). Baruch gives the reason the hills come down and the valleys fill: so that Yashar'el (Israel) may walk home safely in the glory of Yahuah (God). The leveled road is a road for the gathering. John the Baptist preached from Isaiah 40, every valley filled, every mountain brought low, the rough ways made smooth, and Luke tells us who was walking that road: the people coming out to him to be baptized, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) being called back. Baruch read Isaiah's highway as the road the scattered seed comes home on; John stood at the head of that road and opened it.
cards.s_text: Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; and the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough ways shall be made smooth;
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) has appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Yashar'el (Israel) may go safely in the glory of Yahuah (God),

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* (Baruch 5:9). *And all flesh shall see the salvation of Elohim (God).* (Luke 3:6). Baruch ends his gathering song with Yahuah (God) himself leading Yashar'el (Israel) home with joy, in the light of his glory, in mercy and righteousness. Luke ends his quotation of Isaiah 40 with all flesh seeing the salvation of Elohim (God). The two endings belong together: the road is leveled so Yashar'el (Israel) can walk it, and when Yahuah (God) leads them home in his glory the whole earth watches. The salvation all flesh sees is the gathering of the scattered seed; the nations see it done, and Yashar'el (Israel) walks it.
cards.s_text: And all flesh shall see the salvation of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.

cards.note: *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:1 names Eliyahu (Elias) the prophet who stood up as fire — the prophet the King names at Natsareth (Nazareth) when he points to *the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months* (Luke 4:25). The Hebrew library's praise-of-Elias is the witness behind the contrast case: it was to none of the many widows in Yashar'el (Israel) that this fire-prophet was sent, but to the widow of Tsarephath (Zarephath) — individual mercy without absorption into the seed-of-promise.
cards.s_text: But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
cards.t_text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.

cards.note: *By the word of Yahuah (God) he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:3 names Eliyahu (Elias) shutting up the heaven by the word of Yahuah — the exact famine the King names at Luke 4:25, *when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land.* The Hebrew library carries the heaven-shut famine as the setting; the King carries it as the frame for the individual-mercy contrast: in that famine the prophet was sent to one Tsidonian (Sidonian) widow, not to the many widows of Yashar'el — mercy to the foreign-origin individual without the covenant-absorption the marriage-mechanism alone confers.
cards.s_text: But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;
cards.t_text: By the word of Yahuah (God) he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire.

cards.note: *Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: while he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:12 names Eliseus (Elisha) filled with the spirit of Eliyahu (Elias) — the prophet the King names in the second contrast case at Luke 4:27, *many lepers were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.* The Hebrew library names the Elisha who carried the double-portion spirit and did the wonders; the King names the Syrian commander cleansed by that prophet — individual mercy to the foreign-origin man without absorption into the seed-of-promise. Naaman receives the cleansing; he is not thereby made covenant-seed. The contrast case proves the directional non-symmetry the framework holds against the false-inclusion gospel.
cards.s_text: And many lepers were in Yashar'el (Israel) in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
cards.t_text: Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: while he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.

cards.note: *Yet they that received it perished, because they kept not the thing that was sown in them.* (2 Esdras 9:33). *But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.* (Luke 8:15). Ezra says why the fathers perished: they received what was sown and did not keep it. The good ground in the parable is the opposite in every word, an honest and good heart that hears the word, keeps it, and brings forth fruit with patience. Receiving is not the dividing line; keeping is. The fruit is the keeping, and the perishing is the not keeping.
cards.s_text: But that on the good ground are they, which in an honest and good heart, having heard the word, keep it, and bring forth fruit with patience.
cards.t_text: Yet they that received it perished, because they kept not the thing that was sown in them.

cards.note: *For as the husbandman sows much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees, and yet the thing that is sown good in his season comes not up, neither does all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are sown in the world; they shall not all be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:41). *They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.* (Luke 8:13). Ezra is told the husbandman's experience: much seed sown, many trees planted, and not all of it comes up or takes root. Yahusha (Jesus) names the rocky ground the same way: hearers who receive the word with joy, have no root, believe for a while, and fall away when tried. Springing up is not the same as taking root. Ezra's not all saved and the parable's fall away are the same plant dying for the same reason.
cards.s_text: They on the rock are they, which, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root, which for a while believe, and in time of temptation fall away.
cards.t_text: For as the husbandman sows much seed upon the ground, and planteth many trees, and yet the thing that is sown good in his season comes not up, neither does all that is planted take root: even so is it of them that are sown in the world; they shall not all be saved.

cards.note: *For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.* (2 Esdras 9:31). *Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of Elohim (God).* (Luke 8:11). When Yahusha (Jesus) explains the parable, he says the seed is the word of Elohim (God). Ezra had already heard the Most High say what that seed is: I sow my law in you. The law is the word sown, and it is sown into the hearer to bring fruit there, not handed to him as a weight to carry. There is no gap between the word of Elohim (God) in the gospel and the law in Ezra; they are one seed.
cards.s_text: Now the parable is this: The seed is the word of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.

cards.note: *Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:18). *But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.* (Luke 6:49). Sirach says pales set on a high place never stand against the wind, and the fool's fearful heart stands against nothing. Luke names the fool: he heard and did not do, and built his house on the earth with no foundation, and when the stream beat on it the house fell at once and the ruin was great. Hearing without doing is the house without a foundation. The wind finds it, and there is nothing underneath to hold.
cards.s_text: But he that hears, and does not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.
cards.t_text: Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.

cards.note: *As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* (Ecclesiasticus 22:16). *He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.* (Luke 6:48). Sirach's picture is timber bound together in a building that cannot be loosed with shaking; the heart established by counsel is like that. Luke adds a detail Matthew does not: the wise builder dug deep and laid his foundation on a rock, and when the flood beat on the house it could not shake it. The digging deep is the doing — the hearer who does the sayings is driving his foundation down to rock. That is how a heart is established so that it fears at no time.
cards.s_text: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.
cards.t_text: As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.

cards.note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Sirach 27:6) Luke 6:44 names the fruit-test as the means of knowing: *for every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.* The Hebrew library's Sirach 27:6 names the same architecture — the fruit declares the husbandry, the utterance declares the heart. The tree is known by what it brings forth; the heart by what its mouth speaks.
cards.s_text: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.
cards.t_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.

cards.note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.* (Luke 6:43). Sirach says the fruit tells whether the tree was dressed and the speech tells what the heart has conceived. Luke's record of Yahusha (Jesus) holds both together: a good tree does not bear corrupt fruit, a corrupt tree does not bear good, and two verses later, of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaks. The fruit is the tree's utterance and the mouth is the heart's. The wise had named the test long before; the King made it the way his disciples would know one another and know a teacher.
cards.s_text: For a good tree brings not forth corrupt fruit; neither does a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.
cards.t_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.

cards.note: *If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add to it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:15). *Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.* (Luke 11:52). Sirach describes two hearers: the skilful man hears a wise word and commends it and adds to it, while the man of no understanding is displeased by it and throws it behind his back. The lawyers in Luke are the second man — they heard the Word, refused it, and then took the key away so that those entering were hindered too. Casting the word behind your back is bad enough; shutting the door from the outside against others is what draws the woe. The system that does this is what Yahusha (Jesus) names; the people kept from the door are the ones he came for.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, lawyers! for you have taken away the key of knowledge: you entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in you hindered.
cards.t_text: If a skilful man hear a wise word, he will commend it, and add to it: but as soon as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behind his back.

cards.note: *The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:14). *Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.* (Luke 11:52). Sirach pictures the fool's inward parts as a broken vessel: pour knowledge in and it runs out, so he holds none his whole life. Yahusha (Jesus) says the lawyers had taken away the key of knowledge — they had not entered themselves and were hindering those who were entering. A man who holds no knowledge cannot open the door for anyone else. The key that was taken away is the Torah read plainly, and the fences the office built around it are what kept the people outside; the woe is on the office that did it, not on the people it shut out.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, lawyers! for you have taken away the key of knowledge: you entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in you hindered.
cards.t_text: The inner parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, and he will hold no knowledge as long as he lives.

cards.note: *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:12). *And he said, Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.* (Luke 11:46). Sirach locates the beginning of pride in a heart turned away from its Maker. The lawyers Yahusha (Jesus) rebukes have built a weight of rules on top of the Torah and will not lift a finger under it themselves; the hand that adds to the commandment has already turned from the one who gave it. Voiding the commandment by addition is as much a departure as voiding it by subtraction, and both wear the robe of the law while they do it.
cards.s_text: And he said, Woe unto you also, you lawyers! for you lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and you yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
cards.t_text: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.

cards.note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:13). *Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.* (Luke 11:43). Sirach traces sin to pride, and the overthrow of nations to the abomination pride pours out. The woe Yahusha (Jesus) pronounces falls on the love of the uppermost seats and the greetings in the markets — pride in a religious dress. The library had named the disease centuries before the Pharisee's table; the King names it at the table. The woe is on the man who loves the seat; the love of the uppermost place is the pride Sirach said sin begins in.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for you love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
cards.t_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

cards.note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.* (Luke 10:18). The one whose envy let death into the world is the one Yahusha (Jesus) saw fall like lightning. When the seventy came back rejoicing that the devils were subject to them, he told them what they had been watching: the enemy who brought death in was being thrown down, and in the next verse he gives them power to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy. Wisdom names the door death came through; Luke shows the one who opened it losing his footing.
cards.s_text: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.
cards.t_text: Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.

cards.note: *Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth, and shew mercy to them: for I am merciful, says Yahuah (God) Almighty.* (2 Esdras 2:31). *For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.* (Luke 15:24). Yahuah (God) tells the mother to remember her children that sleep, because he will bring them out of the sides of the earth and show them mercy. The father in the parable says of his returned son, this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. The son came out of a far country, and the children in 2 Esdras come out of the sides of the earth, and in both the mercy belongs to the father and the merriment follows the return. The ones who sleep are brought out because he is merciful; that is the resurrection hope, and the prodigal's homecoming is a picture of it, the lost child of the house gathered home and counted alive.
cards.s_text: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
cards.t_text: Remember your children that sleep, for I shall bring them out of the sides of the earth, and shew mercy to them: for I am merciful, says Yahuah (God) Almighty.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.* (Luke 15:6). The sheep in the parable was lost, and the shepherd went after it until he found it, then called his neighbours to rejoice. Ezra was told who the lost are: the ten tribes carried over the waters into another land, where they dwelt until the latter time, *and now when they shall begin to come* (2 Esdras 13:46). The joy Yahusha (Jesus) describes is the joy of that homecoming. A lost sheep is still the shepherd's sheep the whole time it is lost; the ten tribes were still the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in the far country, and the finding is the gathering the prophets promised.
cards.s_text: And when he comes home, he calls together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:13). *And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.* (Luke 15:5). Sirach says the mercy of Yahuah (God) does what a shepherd does: it reproves, it nurtures, it teaches, and it brings the flock back again. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the same thing as a story — one sheep lost, the shepherd going after it until he finds it, and the sheep carried home on his shoulders with rejoicing. The bringing again is the gathering of the lost, and the mercy that gathers is wider than the mercy of man, which reaches only as far as his neighbour.
cards.s_text: And when he has found it, he lays it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
cards.t_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Luke 13:29). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says they will come from east, west, north and south and sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God). Four directions is where the tribes went; four directions is where they come back from. The ones sitting down are the tribes Sirach prayed for, the firstborn his next verse names, not a substitute people set at their table.
cards.s_text: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God). For they departed from you on foot, and were led away of their enemies: but Yahuah (God) brings them to you exalted with glory, as children of the kingdom.* (Baruch 5:5–6). *And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).* (Luke 13:29). Jerusalem is told to stand up high and watch her children come home from the west to the east, and the next verse says who they are: the ones who left her on foot, led away by their enemies, now brought back by Yahuah (God) exalted with glory as children of the kingdom. Yahusha (Jesus) says they shall come from the east and the west and the north and the south and sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God). The ones who come from every quarter in Luke 13 are the same children of the kingdom Baruch watches return, not strangers streaming in, but Jerusalem's own sons who were led away and are being brought home.
cards.s_text: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* Baruch 4:37 names the gathering directly: the sons whom Jerusalem *sentest away* — the scattered into exile — *come gathered together from the east to the west.* Luke 13:29's *they shall come from the east, and from the west* walks the same architecture. The ones gathered are the sent-away sons coming home, not strangers added; the Hebrew library names them as Jerusalem's own scattered children regathered by the word of the Holy One.
cards.s_text: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).* Baruch 4:36 turns Jerusalem's face toward the east to behold the gathering-joy — the prophetic-gathering register the King names at Luke 13:29's *they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).* The Hebrew library names the direction of the coming; the gospel names the four quarters the scattered seed comes from to sit down in the kingdom. This is not categorical-Gentile-inclusion — it is the gathering of the dispersed children of Yashar'el (Israel) from the territories of their scattering.
cards.s_text: And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: O Jerusalem, look about you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29:12 names the storehouse-of-alms architecture — the treasure laid up against affliction. Luke 12:33's *a treasure in the heavens that faileth not* walks the same Hebrew library architecture: the kingdom-citizen who lays up alms in the heavenly storehouse holds what the earthly storehouse cannot keep. The next verse seals it — *for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also* (Luke 12:34).
cards.s_text: Sell that you have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that fails not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
cards.t_text: Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.

cards.note: *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:11). *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* (Luke 12:33). Sirach says lay up your treasure the way the commandments of the Most High direct, and it will profit you more than gold; two verses earlier he said help the poor for the commandment's sake. Yahusha (Jesus) says sell, give alms, and provide yourselves bags that do not wear out, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail. The treasure of the man who opens his hand because the commandment says so is laid up where gold cannot go and thieves cannot follow. That is why it outlasts gold.
cards.s_text: Sell that you have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that fails not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
cards.t_text: Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.

cards.note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* (Luke 12:33). Tobit says alms deliver from death and keep the giver out of darkness; the open hand protects the one who opens it. Yahusha (Jesus) says to sell, give alms, and have a treasure in the heavens that does not fail, where no thief approaches and no moth corrupts. Both are saying that what is given away is the one thing that cannot be taken away. The library names the deliverance; the gospel names the storehouse no thief can reach.
cards.s_text: Sell that you have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that fails not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
cards.t_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.

cards.note: *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* (Tobit 4:9). *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* (Luke 12:33). Tobit's charge to give alms comes with a reason: the giver is laying up a good treasure against the day of necessity. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same thing with a picture — sell, give alms, and you have bags that do not wear out, a treasure in the heavens that does not fail. What is given now is what is stored for then. The library names the treasure the open hand lays up; the gospel names where it is kept and why no thief or moth can reach it.
cards.s_text: Sell that you have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that fails not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.
cards.t_text: For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.

cards.note: *There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:* (Ecclesiasticus 11:18). *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). Sirach describes the man who grows rich by wariness and pinching and says, dryly, that this is the portion of his reward — the heap is all he gets. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same man his night: the soul is required, and the goods pass to someone else. Hoarding is not a sin with no consequence. The consequence is that the hoard was the whole reward.
cards.s_text: But Elohim (God) said unto him, You fool, this night your soul shall be required of you: then whose shall those things be, which you have provided?
cards.t_text: There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:

cards.note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.* (Luke 12:19). Sirach writes the rich fool's speech before the parable: I have found rest, I will eat continually of my goods. Yahusha (Jesus) puts nearly the same words in his mouth — take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. Sirach had also named the two things the man never reckons with: he does not know what time is coming on him, and he must leave it all to others and die. The barns come down the same night.
cards.s_text: And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have much goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* (Luke 19:10). Sirach asks mercy for Yashar'el (Israel), the firstborn called by the name of Yahuah (God). Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came to seek and to save that which was lost. The firstborn had been scattered until he was lost, Hosea's not my people, and the mercy Sirach prayed for arrived as a Shepherd out looking for him. The one sought is the firstborn; the seeking is the mercy.
cards.s_text: For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* (Luke 19:10). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came to seek and to save that which was lost. What was lost was the house, the tribes scattered until they forgot who they were, and seeking them is the gathering Sirach prayed for. He said it in the house of Zacchaeus, a son of Abraham his neighbours had written off, which is what a found tribe looks like one man at a time.
cards.s_text: For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.* (Luke 16:31). Ezra names where the dead wait: asleep in the earth, in the dust, in secret places that hold the souls committed to them until the day they are delivered. When Abraham tells the rich man that his brothers would not be persuaded even if one rose from the dead, he is speaking from inside that same expectation: the dead are held, and one coming back from among them is a thing that could happen. What the brothers have now is Moses and the prophets. If those are not heard, a voice come back from the secret places will not be heard either.
cards.s_text: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
cards.t_text: And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.

cards.note: *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:7). *No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Luke 16:13). Sirach calls gold a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it. He is describing worship, an offering brought and a devotion given, and he says that devotion takes its devotee. Yahusha (Jesus) names the same thing when he calls mammon a master. To serve mammon is to sacrifice to the stumblingblock; the servant does not own it, it owns him, and Sirach had already said where that ends.
cards.s_text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.
cards.t_text: It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it, and every fool shall be taken with it.

cards.note: *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:6). *No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Luke 16:13). Sirach had already watched gold ruin many before Yahusha (Jesus) said no servant can serve two masters. The ruin Sirach names is what happens to the man who takes mammon for a master; it does not share him, it destroys him, and the destruction is already present while he thinks he is being served. The steward in the parable just before this verse was called wise because he treated money as a thing that perishes and used it, instead of bowing to it.
cards.s_text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.
cards.t_text: Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.

cards.note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:5). *No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* (Luke 16:13). Sirach says the man who loves gold will not be justified. Luke sets the King's verdict at the end of the parable of the unjust steward, a story about using mammon shrewdly before the books are called, and then closes it: you cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon. The divided heart that holds to gold has chosen its master, and Sirach already said where that leaves it. The setting is different from the Sermon on the Mount, but the verdict is the same, and it was the wisdom of Yashar'el (Israel) before the King spoke it.
cards.s_text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. You cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.
cards.t_text: He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.

cards.note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26). On the road to Emmaus the King asks the two disciples whether the Messiah (Christ) ought not to have suffered these things and then enter his glory. Wisdom had already written the glory half: the righteous man, condemned in chapter 2 to a shameful death, now standing in great boldness before the faces of the men who did it. Suffering first, then the standing, is the shape he then shows them in Moses and all the prophets, and the Hebrew library had the same shape in Solomon's hand long before Luke wrote it down.
cards.s_text: Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?
cards.t_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.

cards.note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?* (Luke 24:26). On the road to Emmaus Yahusha (Jesus) asked the slow of heart why they were surprised. Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered? The suffering was written — in Moses, in the prophets, and here in Wisdom, where the just man who calls Yahuah (God) his father is sentenced to a shameful death by the men who lay in wait for him. The disciples had read the glory and skipped the suffering. The whole library had both halves on the page, and the King opened their eyes to read them together.
cards.s_text: Ought not Messiah (Christ) to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?
cards.t_text: Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.

cards.note: *And of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit: and of all the flowers thereof one lily:* (2 Esdras 5:24). *He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, Elohim (God) forbid.* (Luke 20:16). Ezra's prayer counts the Most High's choices one by one: one vine, one pit, one lily, one river, one city, one dove, one sheep, and at last one people (2 Esdras 5:23–27). When the parable ends with the vineyard given to others, those who heard it cried out against it, as though the chosen vine itself were being handed to a different people. But it is the husbandmen who are destroyed, not the vineyard. What passes to others is the keeping of the one vine; the vine the Most High chose out of all the lands of the whole world remains the one he chose.
cards.s_text: He shall come and destroy these husbandmen, and shall give the vineyard to others. And when they heard it, they said, Elohim (God) forbid.
cards.t_text: And of all lands of the whole world you have chosen you one pit: and of all the flowers thereof one lily:

cards.note: *And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.* (2 Esdras 5:27). *Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.* (Luke 20:9). The vineyard a certain man plants and lets out is the one people Ezra names, loved out of all the multitudes and given a law that is approved of all. The fruit the owner later sends his servants to collect is the fruit that law was given to bring, a people keeping what they were given. The husbandmen hold the vineyard while refusing its fruit; that is a leadership that keeps the title to the people while setting aside the law the people were planted under. The prayer and the parable agree on what the vineyard is and what it was planted for.
cards.s_text: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.
cards.t_text: And among all the multitudes of people you have gotten you one people: and to this people, whom you lovedst, you gavest a law that is approved of all.

cards.note: *And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine.* (2 Esdras 5:23) The Hebrew library names the vineyard as Yashar'el (Israel) explicitly — the one only vine the Most High chose out of all the trees of the earth. *A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time* (Luke 20:9): the vineyard the King's parable names is the same one-only-vine Ezra names — Yashar'el planted by the Master, let out to the keeping of the husbandmen who beat the servants and kill the heir. The parable is not against the people the vine is; it is against the husbandmen-leadership entrusted with the keeping.
cards.s_text: Then began he to speak to the people this parable; A certain man planted a vineyard, and let it forth to husbandmen, and went into a far country for a long time.
cards.t_text: And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:

cards.note: *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail* (Ecclesiasticus 24:9). Wisdom created/begotten before the world, sent to dwell in the inheritance of Yahuah (God), stands behind John 1:11's *he came unto his own, and his own received him not.* The one who was before the world came to the very people Wisdom was sent to tabernacle among — and his own received him not. The Hebrew library names the sending; the gospel names the refusal.
cards.s_text: He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
cards.t_text: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.

cards.note: *So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ecclesiasticus 24:8). Wisdom's tabernacle caused to rest, her dwelling set in Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel), is the architecture John 1:14's *dwelt among us* — the Greek *eskēnōsen,* tabernacled — walks. The Word made flesh pitched his tabernacle among the covenant people the Hebrew library said Wisdom was sent to dwell with.
cards.s_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
cards.t_text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud* (Ecclesiasticus 24:3). Wisdom proceeding from the mouth of the Most High is the same procession John 1:1-14 walks — the Word with Elohim (God) in the beginning, who *was made flesh, and dwelt among us.* The Word came out of the Formless source as Wisdom came out of the mouth of the Most High; the gospel names where she came to rest: in flesh, tabernacling among us.
cards.s_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
cards.t_text: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.

cards.note: *For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:22). Wisdom as *the worker of all things* is the maker-Word of John 1:3, *all things were made by him*; the holy understanding spirit in her is the Formed one full of *grace and truth* (John 1:14). The deuterocanon names the worker; the gospel names the worker made flesh.
cards.s_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
cards.t_text: For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good,

cards.note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). The Formed is the breath of the power and the pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty — the Formless source, the glory of the Almighty, expressing itself in the Formed. *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father)* (John 1:14): the glory beheld in flesh is the glory the breath flows from.
cards.s_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
cards.t_text: For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.

cards.note: *For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26). The Formed drawn from the Formless is named here as the brightness/effulgence of the everlasting light and the image of the Most High's goodness — the exact architecture of John 1:4's *in him was life; and the life was the light of men.* The light of men is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the One no eye sees.
cards.s_text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
cards.t_text: For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness.

cards.note: *And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9). Wisdom present with the Most High at the making of the world is the same architecture John 1:1-3 walks: *the same was in the beginning with Elohim (God) ... all things were made by him.* The Formed was with the Formless before the world was, and the world was made through him.
cards.s_text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
cards.t_text: And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). The Hebrew library names the Word as the agent through whom the Most High made all things — the same naming John 1:1-3 opens with: *In the beginning was the Word ... All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.* The Word is not a late Greek import into the gospel; the deuterocanon was already confessing the Most High's creating-Word.
cards.s_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,

cards.note: *But the altars which the heathen had built in the open street, and also the chapels, they pulled down.* (2 Maccabees 10:2) The rededication tears down what defiled the holy ground. *And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple* (John 2:15) walks the same architecture: the casting-out of the defilement that had encroached on the house of prayer. The Hebrew library's pulling-down of the heathen altars is the prior enacted purging the Formed one recapitulates with the scourge, reclaiming the gathering-court for the gathering it was built for.
cards.s_text: And when he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen; and poured out the changers’ money, and overthrew the tables;
cards.t_text: But the altars which the heathen had built in the open street, and also the chapels, they pulled down.

cards.note: *Then said Judas and his brothers, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.* (1 Maccabees 4:36). *And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.* (John 2:16). Judas and his brothers, with the enemy beaten back, go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary the heathen had defiled. Generations later Yahusha (Jesus) walks into the same house and drives out the sellers, saying make not my Father's house an house of merchandise. The Maccabees cleansed what Antiochus had polluted with his idol; the King cleansed what the priests had polluted with their market. It is the same motion, the house of Yahuah (God) purged of what does not belong in it, and the second time it is done by the Son whose Father's house it is.
cards.s_text: And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.
cards.t_text: Then said Judas and his brothers, Behold, our enemies are discomfited: let us go up to cleanse and dedicate the sanctuary.

cards.note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 24:23) The Hebrew library identifies wisdom as the Torah given as a heritage to the congregations of Ya'aqov (Jacob) — the covenant-knowledge the house of the covenant carries. *Salvation is of the Yahudim (Jews)* (John 4:22) names the same thing to the woman of Samaria: the wisdom, the covenant, the heritage was kept in the line of Yahudah (Judah), and the well of living water now offered to the scattered northern house flows from that kept inheritance, not from a rival mountain.
cards.s_text: You worship you know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.

cards.note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 24:19) Wisdom calls the desirous to come and be filled — the same invitation Yahusha (Jesus) extends at the well: *if thou knewest the gift of Elohim (God) ... thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water* (John 4:10). The Hebrew library's *come to me ... and fill yourselves* is the wisdom-call the living-water offer fulfils; the gift of Elohim (God) the woman did not yet know is the wisdom-fountain standing at Ya'aqov's (Jacob's) well asking her for a drink.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said unto her, If you knew the gift of Elohim (God), and who it is that says to you, Give me to drink; you would have asked of him, and he would have given you living water.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: *They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:21). *But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.* (John 4:14). Wisdom tells the truth about herself: the one who drinks of her will be thirsty again, and the student goes back to the well as long as he lives. The woman at the well was told of water that would end that going back, because the well itself would be set inside the one who drank it. Yahusha (Jesus) is not the abolition of the wisdom that left the drinker thirsty; he is what that wisdom was drawing the thirsty toward, the Word the Torah kept sending a man back to, now a spring in him that does not run dry.
cards.s_text: But whosoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
cards.t_text: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.

cards.note: *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* (Baruch 4:1) The wisdom Baruch 3 says no man could ascend to fetch is here named plainly as the Torah, *the law that endureth for ever.* Yahusha's (Jesus') rebuke at John 3:12 — *if I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?* — falls on a *master of Yashar'el (Israel)* who held the book of the commandments yet could not see the heavenly thing the book pointed toward. The Torah endures for ever; the One who came down from heaven is the wisdom it was always carrying.
cards.s_text: If I have told you earthly things, and you believe not, how shall you believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?
cards.t_text: This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

cards.note: *Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.* (Baruch 3:37). *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13). Baruch closes his search for wisdom with a sentence most Bibles no longer carry: afterward he shewed himself upon earth, and conversed with men. The one who alone knows the way of knowledge came down and walked among men. John 3:13 is the same event from the inside; the Son of Adam who came down from heaven is the only one who was ever up there. Baruch said the descent would come; Nicodemus was sitting across from it. The wisdom no man could fetch down from the clouds was in the room, talking with him.
cards.s_text: And no man has ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.
cards.t_text: Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.

cards.note: *Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?* (Baruch 3:30). *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13). Baruch piles up the impossibility. No one has gone up to heaven to bring wisdom down, and no one has crossed the sea to find her and buy her with pure gold; *No man knoweth her way, nor thinketh of her path* (Baruch 3:31). Yahusha (Jesus) tells Nicodemus that no man has ascended to heaven but the one who came down from it. The reaching Baruch rules out, upward or outward, is answered from the other direction. The Son of Adam did not have to search for wisdom over the sea, because he came down from where she dwells, and he sat in front of Nicodemus as the thing no gold could buy.
cards.s_text: And no man has ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.
cards.t_text: Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?

cards.note: *Who has gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?* (Baruch 3:29). *And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.* (John 3:13). Baruch asks a question meant to have no answer: who has gone up into heaven and taken wisdom and brought her down? No one, is the expected reply; wisdom is beyond the reach of any son of Adam. Then Yahusha (Jesus) tells Nicodemus that no man has ascended to heaven except the one who came down from it, the Son of Adam. He is the answer Baruch's question was waiting for. The wisdom no man could climb to fetch came down herself, in flesh; Wisdom of Solomon 9 and Ecclesiasticus 24 had already set her beside the Maker, and John 3:13 names the one who was there and came down.
cards.s_text: And no man has ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of Adam which is in heaven.
cards.t_text: Who has gone up into heaven, and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?

cards.note: *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:9 — Wisdom's own testimony, *I came out of the mouth of the Most High* (24:3), created before the world and never failing — names the from-eternity register John 8:58 walks: *Before Abraham was, I am.* The Hebrew library's Wisdom speaks her own before-the-world existence and her dwelling in Ya'aqov (Jacob) and Yashar'el (Israel) (24:8); the Formed Word names the same eternity in the first person, the *I am* who is before Avraham (Abraham), come to tabernacle among his own.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.
cards.t_text: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.

cards.note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.* (2 Esdras 1:19). *For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* (John 6:33). The manna was angels' bread, 2 Esdras says, given out of the Father's pity. In John, Yahusha (Jesus) tells the crowd that the bread of Elohim (God) is he which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world, and a few verses on he says it outright, I am the bread of life. The fathers ate angels' bread in the wilderness and died; the bread the Father sends now is a person, and the life he gives does not end at the edge of the wilderness. The manna was real bread and a real sign, and the one it signified stood in the synagogue at Capernaum and said so.
cards.s_text: For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which comes down from heaven, and gives life unto the world.
cards.t_text: Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.

cards.note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:26). *Then Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.* (John 6:32). The manna was teaching that it is the word of Yahuah (God), not the harvest, that keeps his children alive. Yahusha (Jesus) says Moses did not give the bread from heaven; the Father did, and the Father is now giving the true bread. The word that preserved the wilderness generation is standing in front of the crowd in flesh, the Word made flesh who is himself the bread. What the manna said in a picture, he says in person.
cards.s_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
cards.t_text: That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.

cards.note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). *Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.* (John 6:31). The crowd at Capernaum quotes the manna back at him as the high mark of what heaven has ever given. The library agrees with them about the manna: it was angels' food, sent from heaven without their labour, fitted to every taste. Yahusha (Jesus) does not take a word of it back; he says the Father who sent that bread is now giving the true bread, and the true bread is himself (John 6:32, 35). The manna was real and it was heaven's, and it was pointing past itself to the one who came down.
cards.s_text: Our fathers did eat manna in the desert; as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat.
cards.t_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. John says Yahusha (Jesus) would die not for that nation only but to gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. The scattered children are Jacob's tribes among the nations; the one nation in the land was Yahudah (Judah). Sirach prayed for the gathering, and John names the death that pays for it; Caiaphas said more than he knew.
cards.s_text: And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.* (Baruch 5:9). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Baruch's song ends with the gathering complete: Yahuah (God) leads Yashar'el (Israel) home with joy in the light of his glory. John names what the death of Yahusha (Jesus) accomplished in the same terms, gathering into one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. The scattered children and Yashar'el (Israel) led home are one people; John's into one is Baruch's led with joy. The mercy and righteousness that come from him in Baruch came in the flesh in John, and the gathering they promised runs through the cross.
cards.s_text: And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.

cards.note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 5:5). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Baruch says it twice, once in chapter 4 and again here, so no one misses it: Jerusalem's children are gathered by the word of the Holy One, from the east and from the west. John says the death of Yahusha (Jesus) was to gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. Scattered abroad is where Baruch's children went; gathered into one is where they are going. The homecoming Baruch sang from the captivity is the homecoming John says the cross was for.
cards.s_text: And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.
cards.t_text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).* (Baruch 4:37). *And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.* (John 11:52). Baruch sees the sons Jerusalem sent away coming gathered from east to west by the word of the Holy One. John explains the death of Yahusha (Jesus) in the same terms: not for that nation only, but to gather into one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad. The scattered children are not the nations; they are Jerusalem's own sons, sent away in the scattering, the ones Hosea said would be called sons of the living Elohim (God) in the very place they were called not his people (Hosea 1:10). Baruch names the gathering by the word of the Holy One; John names the death that does the gathering.
cards.s_text: And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of Elohim (God) that were scattered abroad.
cards.t_text: Lo, your sons come, whom you sentest away, they come gathered together from the east to the west by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). *Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.* (John 11:24). Martha, grieving, says what the Hebrew library had taught her: her brother will rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Ezra was told the same thing in fuller words, that the earth will restore those asleep in her and the secret places will deliver the souls committed to them. Martha's hope is not a vague comfort; it is this promise. And the one standing in front of her is about to call Lazarus out of the grave (John 11:43–44), a first sign of the day Ezra was shown.
cards.s_text: Martha says unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.
cards.t_text: And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.

cards.note: *And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.* (2 Esdras 13:33). *My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:* (John 10:27). When the Son is declared, Ezra is told, all the people hear his voice and every man leaves his battle in his own land. Yahusha (Jesus) says his sheep hear his voice, and he knows them, and they follow him. The hearing is what shows who they are; the ones who leave their fighting when he speaks are the ones who were his. His voice does not make sheep; it calls the sheep out of the battle they were in.
cards.s_text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:
cards.t_text: And when all the people hear his voice, every man shall in their own land leave the battle they have one against another.

cards.note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* 2 Esdras 13:47 names the gathering-home of the scattered ten tribes — the Most High staying the river so the carried-away may cross back.
