cards.note: Isaiah 44:17 — *And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.* The multitude 'allured by the grace of the work' who take the image for a god (Wisdom of Solomon 14:20) is Isaiah's man bowing to the leftover block and calling it his god.
cards.s_text: And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god, which a little before was but honoured.
cards.t_text: And the residue thereof he makes a god, even his graven image: he falls down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and says, Deliver me; for you are my god.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:13 — *The carpenter stretcheth out his rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and maketh it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.* Isaiah's craftsman shaping a beautiful man-figure is the very 'singular diligence of the artificer' that sets forward superstition in Wisdom of Solomon 14:18.
cards.s_text: Also the singular diligence of the artificer did help to set forward the ignorant to more superstition.
cards.t_text: The carpenter stretcheth out his rule; he marketh it out with a line; he fitteth it with planes, and he marketh it out with the compass, and makes it after the figure of a man, according to the beauty of a man; that it may remain in the house.

cards.note: Habakkuk 2:19 — *Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.* The flattering image of the absent king in Wisdom of Solomon 14:17 is Habakkuk's gilded wood and stone with no breath at all.
cards.s_text: Whom men could not honour in presence, because they dwelt far off, they took the counterfeit of his visage from far, and made an express image of a king whom they honoured, to the end that by this their forwardness they might flatter him that was absent, as if he were present.
cards.t_text: Woe unto him that says to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.

cards.note: Daniel 3:18 — *But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.* When 'graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings' (Wisdom of Solomon 14:16), Daniel's three refuse the king's golden image at the cost of the furnace.
cards.s_text: Thus in process of time an ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings.
cards.t_text: But if not, be it known unto you, O king, that we will not serve your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.

cards.note: Jeremiah 10:14 — *Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.* The artisan's image worshipped by kings' command in Wisdom of Solomon 14:16 is Jeremiah's molten falsehood with no breath in it.
cards.s_text: Thus in process of time an ungodly custom grown strong was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings.
cards.t_text: Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

cards.note: Jeremiah 10:5 — *They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good.* The dead image honoured as a god in Wisdom of Solomon 14:15 is Jeremiah's breathless idol that can neither speak nor walk.
cards.s_text: For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he has made an image of his child soon taken away, now honoured him as a god, which was then a dead man, and delivered to those that were under him ceremonies and sacrifices.
cards.t_text: They are upright as the palm tree, but speak not: they must needs be borne, because they cannot go. Be not afraid of them; for they cannot do evil, neither also is it in them to do good.

cards.note: Exodus 20:3 — *Thou shalt have no other gods before me.* The first word of the covenant is the standard against which Wisdom of Solomon 14:12 measures the devising of idols as fornication.
cards.s_text: For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.
cards.t_text: You shall have no other gods before me.

cards.note: Ezekiel 23:37 — *That they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands, and with their idols have they committed adultery, and have also caused their sons to pass through the fire, unto them to devour them.* Ezekiel names idolatry the very 'spiritual fornication' Wisdom of Solomon 14:12 calls its beginning, joined as here to child-sacrifice.
cards.s_text: For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.
cards.t_text: That they have committed adultery, and blood is in their hands, and with their idols have they committed adultery, and have also caused their sons, whom they bare unto me, to pass for them through the fire, to devour them.

cards.note: Exodus 20:4 — *Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:* the second commandment is the law Solomon traces idolatry's whole corruption back to in Wisdom of Solomon 14:12.
cards.s_text: For the devising of idols was the beginning of spiritual fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.
cards.t_text: You shall not make unto you any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 4:28 — *And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.* Wisdom 15:15's idols that cannot see, breathe, or hear are Moses' wood-and-stone gods that 'neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell' — the curse of forgetting the living Elohim.
cards.s_text: For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle; and as for their feet, they are slow to go.
cards.t_text: And there you shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:19 — *And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire... and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?* Wisdom 15:10's idolater whose 'heart is ashes' is Isaiah's man feeding on ashes, unable to consider the folly of bowing to a block of wood.
cards.s_text: His heart is ashes, his hope is more vile than earth, and his life of less value than clay:
cards.t_text: And none considereth in his heart, neither is there knowledge nor understanding to say, I have burned part of it in the fire; yea, also I have baked bread upon the coals thereof; I have roasted flesh, and eaten it: and shall I make the residue thereof an abomination? shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:8 — *But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.* Wisdom 15:13's craftsman who 'knoweth himself to offend above all others' is the same self-condemned maker the book has just cursed in chapter 14.
cards.s_text: For this man, that of earthly matter makes brittle vessels and graven images, knoweth himself to offend above all others.
cards.t_text: But that which is made with hands is cursed, as well it, as he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god.

cards.note: Romans 1:25 — *Who changed the truth of Elohim (God) into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.* Wisdom 15:17's mortal who 'is better than the things which he worshippeth' yet worships them is Paul's man serving the creature above the Creator.
cards.s_text: For being mortal, he works a dead thing with wicked hands: for he himself is better than the things which he worshippeth: whereas he lived once, but they never.
cards.t_text: Who changed the truth of Elohim (God) into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

cards.note: Romans 1:23 — *And changed the glory of the uncorruptible Elohim (God) into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.* Wisdom 15:18's worship of 'those beasts also that are most hateful' is Paul's exchange of the Creator's glory for the image of beasts.
cards.s_text: Yea, they worshipped those beasts also that are most hateful: for being compared together, some are worse than others.
cards.t_text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible Elohim (God) into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

cards.note: Romans 1:20 — *For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse.* Wisdom 15:11's idolater who 'knew not his Maker' is the very man Paul leaves without excuse for not knowing the Creator the creation declares.
cards.s_text: Forasmuch as he knew not his Maker, and him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed in a living spirit.
cards.t_text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

cards.note: Habakkuk 2:18 — *What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?* Wisdom 15:5's 'dead image, that has no breath' is Habakkuk's dumb idol — a teacher of lies that profits nothing.
cards.s_text: The sight of which enticeth fools to lust after it, and so they desire the form of a dead image, that has no breath.
cards.t_text: What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof has graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusts therein, to make dumb idols?

cards.note: Psalm 115:8 — *They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.* Wisdom 15:16's 'no man can make a god like to himself' is the obverse of the Psalm's verdict — the maker sinks to the deadness of the thing he made.
cards.s_text: For man made them, and he that borrowed his own spirit fashioned them: but no man can make a god like to himself.
cards.t_text: They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusts in them.

cards.note: Psalm 115:7 — *They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat.* Wisdom 15:15's idol with fingers that cannot handle and feet 'slow to go' is the Psalmist's catalogue of the silver-and-gold idol that cannot move.
cards.s_text: For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle; and as for their feet, they are slow to go.
cards.t_text: They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat.

cards.note: Genesis 2:7 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.* Wisdom 15:8's man 'made of earth himself' who 'returns to the same' is the Adam of the dust — the creature presuming to fashion a creator.
cards.s_text: And employing his labours lewdly, he makes a vain god of the same clay, even he which a little before was made of earth himself, and within a little while after returns to the same, out when his life which was lent him shall be demanded.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

cards.note: Isaiah 45:9 — *Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?* The clay declaring itself god in Wisdom 15:8 is the very woe Isaiah pronounces on the potsherd that contends with its Maker.
cards.s_text: For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashioneth every vessel with much labour for our service: yes, of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for clean uses, and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge.
cards.t_text: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What make you? or your work, He has no hands?

cards.note: Romans 9:21 — *Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?* Wisdom 15:7's one clay shaped into clean and contrary vessels is exactly Paul's lump made into honour and dishonour — the Potter's sovereign right.
cards.s_text: For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashioneth every vessel with much labour for our service: yes, of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for clean uses, and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge.
cards.t_text: Has not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

cards.note: Jeremiah 18:6 — *O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? saith Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).* Wisdom 15:2's 'if we sin, we are yours, knowing your power' rests on the same potter-claim — Israel is clay held in the Maker's own hand.
cards.s_text: For if we sin, we are yours, knowing your power: but we will not sin, knowing that we are counted yours.
cards.t_text: O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? says Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: John 17:3 — *And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom thou hast sent.* Wisdom 15:3 names knowing the living Elohim 'the root of immortality'; Yahusha names that same knowing as life eternal itself.
cards.s_text: For to know you is perfect righteousness: yes, to know your power is the root of immortality.
cards.t_text: And this is life eternal, that they might know you the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom you have sent.

cards.note: Numbers 21:6 — *And the LORD sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Israel died.* These are the 'venomous dragons' Wisdom of Solomon 16:10 says could not overcome Yahuah's sons, for His mercy healed them.
cards.s_text: But your sons not the very teeth of venomous dragons overcame: for your mercy was ever by them, and healed them.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and much people of Yashar'el (Israel) died.

cards.note: Numbers 11:31 — *And there went forth a wind from the LORD, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, as it were a day's journey on this side, and as it were a day's journey on the other side, round about the camp, and as it were two cubits high upon the face of the earth.* These are the 'quails to stir up their appetite' of Wisdom of Solomon 16:2.
cards.s_text: Instead of which punishment, dealing graciously with your own people, you preparedst for them meat of a strange taste, even quails to stir up their appetite:
cards.t_text: And there went forth a wind from Yahuah (LORD), and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, as it were a day’s journey on this side, and as it were a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and as it were two cubits high upon the face of the earth.

cards.note: Matthew 4:4 — *But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.* Yahusha wields the truth Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 confesses — the word, not the growing of fruits, sustains the children of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.
cards.t_text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:3 — *And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 distils this Torah lesson: not fruits but His word nourisheth and preserveth.
cards.s_text: That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.
cards.t_text: And he humbled you, and suffered you to hunger, and fed you with manna, which you knew not, neither did your fathers know; that he might make you know that man does not live by bread only, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of Yahuah (LORD) does man live.

cards.note: *For your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:21). *For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* (John 6:33). The manna carried the Father's sweetness to his children and fitted itself to every one who ate it. John names the bread of Elohim (God) as a person — he who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. The sweetness the wilderness tasted was a foretaste of the one who came down; the manna fed a generation, and the Bread who came down gives life.
cards.s_text: For your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.
cards.t_text: For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which comes down from heaven, and gives life unto the world.

cards.note: John 6:32 — *Then Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven.* The manna 'tempered itself to every man's liking' (Wisdom of Solomon 16:21) was the shadow; Yahusha is the true bread from heaven.
cards.s_text: For your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.
cards.t_text: Then Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.

cards.note: Psalm 78:25 — *Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full.* The Psalm and Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 use the same phrase — 'angels' food' — for the manna that filled every taste.
cards.s_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.
cards.t_text: Man did eat angels’ food: he sent them meat to the full.

cards.note: Exodus 16:4 — *Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.* This is the manna Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 calls 'bread prepared without their labour' sent from heaven.
cards.s_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.
cards.t_text: Then said Yahuah (LORD) unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 2:6 — *The LORD killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up.* Hannah's song is Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 word for word: He 'leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.'
cards.s_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) kills, and makes alive: he brings down to the grave, and brings up.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:39 — *See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.* The song of Moses says exactly what Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 says — power of life and death, none escaping His hand (Wisdom 16:15).
cards.s_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.
cards.t_text: See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.

cards.note: Psalm 107:20 — *He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.* This is the same confession as Wisdom of Solomon 16:12 — not herb nor plaister but the sent word of Yahuah heals all things.
cards.s_text: For it was neither herb, nor mollifying plaister, that restored them to health: but your word, O Yahuah (God), which healeth all things.
cards.t_text: He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions.

cards.note: John 3:15 — *That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.* The believing look of Wisdom of Solomon 16:7 — saved 'by thee, that art the Saviour of all' — finds its fullness in the lifted-up Messiah.
cards.s_text: For he that turned himself toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by you, that are the Saviour of all.
cards.t_text: That whosoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

cards.note: John 3:14 — *And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up.* Yahusha names the type Wisdom of Solomon 16:7 already saw — the look toward the lifted-up One, not the bronze, is what saves.
cards.s_text: For he that turned himself toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by you, that are the Saviour of all.
cards.t_text: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Adam be lifted up:

cards.note: Numbers 21:9 — *And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:7 reads this scene precisely: the beholder 'was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by thee, that art the Saviour of all.'
cards.s_text: For he that turned himself toward it was not saved by the thing that he saw, but by you, that are the Saviour of all.
cards.t_text: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.

cards.note: Numbers 21:8 — *And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live.* This is the very 'sign of salvation' Wisdom of Solomon 16:6 says was set up to put Yashar'el in remembrance of the commandment of the law.
cards.s_text: But they were troubled for a small season, that they might be admonished, having a sign of salvation, to put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Make you a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looks upon it, shall live.

cards.note: John 3:20 — *For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.* The conscience pressed and forecasting grievous things (Wisdom 17:11) flees the light lest its deeds be reproved.
cards.s_text: For wickedness, condemned by her own witness, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, always forecasteth grievous things.
cards.t_text: For every one that does evil hates the light, neither comes to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.

cards.note: John 3:19 — *And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.* The wickedness condemned by her own witness (Wisdom 17:11) is the love of darkness that is its own judgment.
cards.s_text: For wickedness, condemned by her own witness, is very timorous, and being pressed with conscience, always forecasteth grievous things.
cards.t_text: And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.

cards.note: 1 Enoch 10:5 — *And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light.* Azâzêl covered in darkness till the judgment matches the one chain of darkness from which the prisoners of Wisdom 17:17 could not escape.
cards.s_text: For whether he were husbandman, or shepherd, or a labourer in the field, he was overtaken, and endured that necessity, which could not be avoided: for they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
cards.t_text: And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light.

cards.note: 1 Enoch 10:4 — *And again Yahuah (God) said to Raphael: ’Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein.* The bound watcher of Enoch is the prison without iron bars (Wisdom 17:16) that Jude 6 inherits.
cards.s_text: So then whoever there fell down was straitly kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars,
cards.t_text: And again Yahuah (Lord) said to Raphael: ‘Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein.

cards.note: Jude 1:6 — *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* Jude's everlasting chains under darkness are Wisdom 17:17's one chain of darkness that bound every man of Egypt.
cards.s_text: For whether he were husbandman, or shepherd, or a labourer in the field, he was overtaken, and endured that necessity, which could not be avoided: for they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
cards.t_text: And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.

cards.note: Isaiah 60:2 — *For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but Yahuah (LORD) shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.* The heavy night that received the wicked (Wisdom 17:21) is the gross darkness from which the elect alone are spared.
cards.s_text: Over them only was spread an heavy night, an image of that darkness which should afterward receive them: but yet were they to themselves more grievous than the darkness.
cards.t_text: For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but Yahuah (LORD) shall arise upon you, and his glory shall be seen upon you.

cards.note: Isaiah 60:1 — *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee.* The clear light over the holy nation (Wisdom 17:20) is the prophetic light risen upon redeemed Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: For the whole world shined with clear light, and none were hindered in their labour:
cards.t_text: Arise, shine; for your light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon you.

cards.note: Exodus 10:23 — *They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) had light in their dwellings.* The very separation Wisdom 17:20 frames — the whole world shined for the righteous while night held the oppressor.
cards.s_text: For the whole world shined with clear light, and none were hindered in their labour:
cards.t_text: They saw not one another, neither rose any from his place for three days: but all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) had light in their dwellings.

cards.note: Psalm 105:28 — *He sent darkness, and made it dark; and they rebelled not against his word.* The Psalm names Yahuah's own hand behind the night that fettered Egypt in Wisdom 17:2.
cards.s_text: For when unrighteous men thought to oppress the holy nation; they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, and fettered with the bonds of a long night, lay there exiled from the eternal providence.
cards.t_text: He sent darkness, and made it dark; and they rebelled not against his word.

cards.note: Exodus 10:22 — *And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days* — the thick night against which no fire nor star could give light (Wisdom 17:5).
cards.s_text: No power of the fire might give them light: neither could the bright flames of the stars endure to lighten that horrible night.
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:

cards.note: Exodus 10:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Stretch out thine hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.* The plague Wisdom 17:2 expounds: a darkness so dense it imprisons, the bonds of a long night.
cards.s_text: For when unrighteous men thought to oppress the holy nation; they being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, and fettered with the bonds of a long night, lay there exiled from the eternal providence.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Stretch out your hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.

cards.note: Exodus 28:36 — *And thou shalt make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE Yahuah (LORD).* Your Majesty upon the diadem of his head (Wisdom 18:24) — the Name on the golden plate that the destroyer dares not pass.
cards.s_text: For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and your Majesty upon the diadem of his head.
cards.t_text: And you shall make a plate of pure gold, and grave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Exodus 28:29 — *And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before Yahuah (LORD) continually.* The glory of the fathers graven on the garment (Wisdom 18:24) — all twelve tribes carried before the throne for a memorial.
cards.s_text: For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and your Majesty upon the diadem of his head.
cards.t_text: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goes in unto the holy place, for a memorial before Yahuah (LORD) continually.

cards.note: Exodus 28:17 — *And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this shall be the first row.* The four rows of stones of Wisdom 18:24 — the high priest's breastplate, the glory of the fathers graven.
cards.s_text: For in the long garment was the whole world, and in the four rows of the stones was the glory of the fathers graven, and your Majesty upon the diadem of his head.
cards.t_text: And you shall set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this shall be the first row.

cards.note: Hebrews 4:12 — *For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.* The blameless man subdues the destroyer with a word (Wisdom 18:22) — intercession in the power of the living Word.
cards.s_text: For then the blameless man made haste, and stood forth to defend them; and bringing the shield of his proper ministry, even prayer, and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your servant.
cards.t_text: For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.

cards.note: Exodus 12:13 — *And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.* The oaths and covenants made with the fathers, by which the blameless man subdues the destroyer (Wisdom 18:22) — the same blood-token that turns the plague aside.
cards.s_text: So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, nor force of arms, but with a word subdued him that punished, alleging the oaths and covenants made with the fathers.
cards.t_text: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where you are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Numbers 16:48 — *And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.* The very posture of Wisdom 18:23 — Aaron standing between, staying the wrath, parting the way to the living.
cards.s_text: For when the dead were now fallen down by heaps one upon another, standing between, he stayed the wrath, and parted the way to the living.
cards.t_text: And he stood between the dead and the living; and the plague was stayed.

cards.note: Numbers 16:46 — *And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a censer, and put fire therein from off the altar, and put on incense, and go quickly unto the congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from Yahuah (LORD); the plague is begun.* The propitiation of incense Wisdom 18:21 names — the priest's shield of his proper ministry against the wrath.
cards.s_text: For then the blameless man made haste, and stood forth to defend them; and bringing the shield of his proper ministry, even prayer, and the propitiation of incense, set himself against the wrath, and so brought the calamity to an end, declaring that he was your servant.
cards.t_text: And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a censer, and put fire therein from off the altar, and put on incense, and go quickly unto the congregation, and make an atonement for them: for there is wrath gone out from Yahuah (LORD); the plague is begun.

cards.note: *And brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:16). *For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.* (Hebrews 4:12). In Egypt the word came as a sharp sword that filled the land with death, touching heaven and standing on the earth. Hebrews says the same word is still a sword, sharper than any two-edged blade, and it now cuts where no Egyptian saw it fall — between soul and spirit, into the thoughts and intents of the heart. The sword is the same; the field it works has moved inward. The one who judged Egypt in a night reads the heart of the one who reads him.
cards.s_text: And brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.
cards.t_text: For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.

cards.note: Revelation 19:15 — *And out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God).* The unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword filling all things with death (Wisdom 18:16) — the Word's blade that smites the nations.
cards.s_text: And brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.
cards.t_text: And out of his mouth goes a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations: and he shall rule them with a rod of iron: and he treads the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God).

cards.note: Revelation 19:13 — *And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of Elohim (God).* The very name Wisdom 18:15 gives the warrior — the Almighty Word — borne by the rider into the land of destruction.
cards.s_text: Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,
cards.t_text: And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Revelation 19:11 — *And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war.* The fierce man of war leaping from heaven (Wisdom 18:15) rides out of opened heaven to judge and make war.
cards.s_text: Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,
cards.t_text: And I saw heaven opened, and behold a white horse; and he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he does judge and make war.

cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The Almighty Word that leaped from the throne in Wisdom 18:15 is the Logos made flesh — heaven touched, earth stood upon.
cards.s_text: Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: Exodus 12:14 — *And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.* The holy law the righteous children consented to in Wisdom 18:9 — the Passover kept by ordinance forever, Torah standing.
cards.s_text: For the righteous children of good men did sacrifice secretly, and with one consent made a holy law, that the saints should be like partakers of the same good and evil, the fathers now singing out the songs of praise.
cards.t_text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and you shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; you shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

cards.note: Exodus 12:13 — *And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.* The blood-token behind the oaths the fathers were certified by (Wisdom 18:6) — the lamb that turns the destroyer aside.
cards.s_text: Of that night were our fathers certified afore, that assuredly knowing to what oaths they had given credence, they might afterwards be of good cheer.
cards.t_text: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where you are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 12:30 — *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.* Wisdom 18:11-12's innumerable dead and lamentable cry, with none left to bury — master and king and common person alike.
cards.s_text: So they all together had innumerable dead with one kind of death; neither were the living sufficient to bury them: for in one moment the noblest offspring of them was destroyed.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

cards.note: Exodus 12:29 — *And it came to pass, that at midnight Yahuah (LORD) smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.* The destruction of the firstborn that, in Wisdom 18:13, made Egypt confess Israel to be the sons of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: For whereas they would not believe any thing by reason of the enchantments; upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged this people to be the sons of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, that at midnight Yahuah (LORD) smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.

cards.note: Exodus 12:42 — *It is a night to be much observed unto Yahuah (LORD) for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of Yahuah (LORD) to be observed of all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in their generations.* The night by which the uncorrupt light of the law (Wisdom 18:4) was given through Israel to the world.
cards.s_text: For they were worthy to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, who had kept your sons shut up, by whom the uncorrupt light of the law was to be given to the world.
cards.t_text: It is a night to be much observed unto Yahuah (LORD) for bringing them out from the land of Egypt: this is that night of Yahuah (LORD) to be observed of all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in their generations.

cards.note: Exodus 14:20 — *And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Yashar'el (Israel); and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night.* The one fire is light to Israel and darkness to Egypt — Wisdom 18:3-4's two-edged mercy-in-judgment.
cards.s_text: Instead of which you gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably.
cards.t_text: And it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Yashar'el (Israel); and it was a cloud and darkness to them, but it gave light by night to these: so that the one came not near the other all the night.

cards.note: Exodus 13:22 — *He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.* The unfailing presence that, in Wisdom 18:3, entertains the saints honourably as an harmless sun.
cards.s_text: Instead of which you gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably.
cards.t_text: He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.

cards.note: Exodus 13:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:* The very pillar Wisdom 18:3 names as the burning guide of the unknown journey.
cards.s_text: Instead of which you gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

cards.note: Numbers 11:31 — *And there went forth a wind from the LORD, and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp.* The quails 'from the sea for their contentment' in Wisdom 19:12 are the wilderness quail-provision of Numbers 11.
cards.s_text: For quails came up to them from the sea for their contentment.
cards.t_text: And there went forth a wind from Yahuah (LORD), and brought quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, as it were a day’s journey on this side, and as it were a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and as it were two cubits high upon the face of the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 8:3 — *And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into thine house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed.* Wisdom 19:10's river casting up frogs instead of fishes is the second plague of the Torah.
cards.s_text: For they were yet mindful of the things that were done while they sojourned in the strange land, how the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, and how the river cast up a multitude of frogs instead of fishes.
cards.t_text: And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber, and upon your bed, and into the house of your servants, and upon your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneadingtroughs:

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 16:8 — *Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.* Yeshua ben Sira, like Wisdom 19:14, recalls Sodom's pride and inhospitality as the pattern of judgment on those who despise the stranger.
cards.s_text: For the Sodomites did not receive those, whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserved of them.
cards.t_text: Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.

cards.note: Matthew 10:15 — *Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than for that city.* Wisdom 19:14 makes Egypt's mistreatment of the stranger worse than Sodom's; Yahusha likewise weighs the inhospitable city below Sodom in judgment.
cards.s_text: For the Sodomites did not receive those, whom they knew not when they came: but these brought friends into bondage, that had well deserved of them.
cards.t_text: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

cards.note: Genesis 19:11 — *And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great: so that they wearied themselves to find the door.* Wisdom 19:17's blindness at the doors of the righteous man, every one seeking his own door, is the smiting of the Sodomites at Lot's house.
cards.s_text: Therefore even with blindness were these stricken, as those were at the doors of the righteous man: when, being compassed about with horrible great darkness, every one sought the passage of his own doors.
cards.t_text: And they smote the men that were at the door of the house with blindness, both small and great: so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

cards.note: Exodus 13:21 — *And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night.* The cloud shadowing the camp in Wisdom 19:7 is the pillar that was cloud by day and fire by night — element bent to guard His people.
cards.s_text: As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field:
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night:

cards.note: Exodus 9:24 — *So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.* Wisdom 19:20's fire having power in the water is the Torah's hail mingled with fire — the elements set against their own nature.
cards.s_text: The fire had power in the water, forgetting his own virtue: and the water forgat his own quenching nature.
cards.t_text: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

cards.note: Revelation 21:1 — *And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.* The elements re-harmonized in Wisdom 19:18 anticipate the final re-creation John beholds, where the sea itself is gone.
cards.s_text: For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, like as in a psaltery notes change the name of the tune, and yet are always sounds; which may well be perceived by the sight of the things that have been done.
cards.t_text: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea.

cards.note: Romans 8:19 — *For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.* The 'whole creature' re-fashioned to keep His children unhurt (Wisdom 19:6) is the very creature Paul says waits for the revealing of the sons of God.
cards.s_text: For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given to them, that your children might be kept without hurt:
cards.t_text: For the earnest expectation of the creature waits for the manifestation of the sons of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Isaiah 43:16 — *Thus saith the LORD, which maketh a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters.* Wisdom 19:7's 'way without impediment' out of the Red sea is exactly the LORD who makes a path in the mighty waters.
cards.s_text: As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field:
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), which makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters;

cards.note: Isaiah 43:19 — *Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall ye not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.* The creature 'fashioned again anew' in Wisdom 19:6 is Isaiah's 'new thing' — a way made where there was none, for His people.
cards.s_text: For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given to them, that your children might be kept without hurt:
cards.t_text: Behold, I will do a new thing; now it shall spring forth; shall you not know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:6 — *For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* Wisdom's final word that Yahuah magnified and glorified His people rests on the Torah's doctrine of election.
cards.s_text: For in all things, O Yahuah (God), you did magnify your people, and glorify them, neither did you lightly regard them: but did assist them in every time and place.
cards.t_text: For you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has chosen you to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 15:13 — *Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation.* The closing magnifying of His people in Wisdom 19:22 echoes the song's confession that mercy led the redeemed to the holy habitation.
cards.s_text: For in all things, O Yahuah (God), you did magnify your people, and glorify them, neither did you lightly regard them: but did assist them in every time and place.
cards.t_text: You in your mercy have led forth the people which you have redeemed: you have guided them in your strength unto your holy habitation.

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* The leaping, horse-like praise of Wisdom 19:9 is the Song of the Sea — Israel's first worship after the crossing.
cards.s_text: For they went at large like horses, and leaped like lambs, praising you, O Yahuah (God), who hadst delivered them.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: Exodus 14:28 — *And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.* The pursuers of Wisdom 19:2-3, drawn by their destiny, find in the same sea the 'strange death' (19:5) — a grave where Israel found a road.
cards.s_text: For while they were yet mourning and making lamentation at the graves of the dead, they added another foolish device, and pursued them as fugitives, whom they had intreated to be gone.
cards.t_text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

cards.note: Exodus 14:22 — *And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.* Wisdom 19:8's people who 'went' through, defended by Yahuah's hand, are Israel walled in by the waters.
cards.s_text: Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with your hand, seeing your marvellous strange wonders.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

cards.note: Exodus 14:21 — *And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.* The dry land and the way through the Red sea Wisdom 19:7 names is the very dividing of the waters in the Torah.
cards.s_text: As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field:
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Yahuah (LORD) caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 — *For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.* The sister-book seals Sir 1:30: the deceitful, secret-laden heart cannot house wisdom.
cards.s_text: Exalt not thyself, lest you fall, and bring dishonour upon your soul, and so Yahuah (God) discover your secrets, and cast you down in the midst of the congregation, because you camest not in truth to the fear of Yahuah (God), but your heart is full of deceit.
cards.t_text: For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.

cards.note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:29). *Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.* (Matthew 23:28). Sirach gives the counsel; Yahusha (Jesus) delivers the indictment of the men who ignored it. To be a hypocrite in the sight of men is to appear righteous unto men while being something else within, which is exactly how Matthew 23:28 reads. The warning came first, in a book the Reformation later cut from the library, and the Messiah's woe assumes his hearers should have known better. The religious system of his day had built itself on appearance; Sirach had told Yashar'el (Israel) long before that appearance is not what Yahuah (God) is weighing.
cards.s_text: Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.
cards.t_text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

cards.note: James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him.* James, the closest NT sibling, crowns the undivided heart that Sir 1:28 demands when poor and tried.
cards.s_text: Distrust not the fear of Yahuah (God) when you are poor: and come not to him with a double heart.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that endures temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to them that love him.

cards.note: Matthew 5:5 — *Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.* The faith and meekness that are Yahuah's delight (Sir 1:27) are the Beatitude's meek who inherit.
cards.s_text: For the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom and instruction: and faith and meekness are his delight.
cards.t_text: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.

cards.note: Matthew 6:33 — *But seek ye first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.* The Sermon's order matches Sir 1:26: seek the kingdom first, and what you desire is added.
cards.s_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.
cards.t_text: But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

cards.note: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:26). *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.* (Ecclesiastes 12:13). Sirach puts wisdom on the far side of the commandments: keep them, and Yahuah (God) gives her. Solomon ends his whole book in the same place, fear Elohim (God) and keep his commandments, and calls that the whole duty of man. Neither writer knows a wisdom that stands apart from the commandments or a fear of Yahuah (God) that outgrows them. The commandments are not the beginner's course a wise man leaves behind; they are the door wisdom comes through, and the conclusion the wisest man in Yashar'el (Israel) arrived at.
cards.s_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.
cards.t_text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:18 — *And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption;* The sister-book grounds Wisdom's everlasting foundation (Sir 1:15) in the keeping of her laws — Torah stands.
cards.s_text: She has built an everlasting foundation with men, and she shall continue with their seed.
cards.t_text: And love is the keeping of her laws; and the giving heed to her laws is the assurance of incorruption;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 6:2 — *That thou mightest fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to keep all his statutes and his commandments, which I command thee, thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son, all the days of thy life; and that thy days may be prolonged.* The long-life branches of Sir 1:20 are the Torah promise: the fear of Yahuah prolongs days.
cards.s_text: The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life.
cards.t_text: That you might fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to keep all his statutes and his commandments, which I command you, you, and your son, and your son’s son, all the days of your life; and that your days may be prolonged.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:18 — *She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her.* The root-and-branches of Sir 1:20 is Wisdom as the tree of life.
cards.s_text: The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life.
cards.t_text: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her.

cards.note: Job 28:28 — *And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of Yahuah (Lord), that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.* The crown of wisdom of Sir 1:18 is Job's verdict: the fear of Yahuah, that is wisdom.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is a crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish; both which are the gifts of Yahuah (God): and it enlargeth their rejoicing that love him.
cards.t_text: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of Adonai (Lord), that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

cards.note: Psalm 111:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.* The Psalter ties the fear-of-Yahuah wisdom of Sir 1:16 to doing his commandments — Torah stands.
cards.s_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is fulness of wisdom, and filleth men with her fruits.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endures for ever.

cards.note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* Word for word the maxim Ben Sira builds on in Sir 1:14.
cards.s_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* Sir 1:14 quotes the spine of Proverbs: the fear of Yahuah is the beginning.
cards.s_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:26 — *For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness.* The sister-book frames the same pre-created Wisdom of Sir 1:4 as the brightness of the everlasting light.
cards.s_text: Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
cards.t_text: For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness.

cards.note: John 1:3 — *All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.* The Wisdom poured out upon all his works (Sir 1:9) is the Word by whom all things were made.
cards.s_text: He created her, and saw her, and numbered her, and poured her out upon all his works.
cards.t_text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:23 — *I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.* The understanding from everlasting (Sir 1:4) is Wisdom set up before the earth.
cards.s_text: Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
cards.t_text: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:22 — *Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.* Sir 1:4's wisdom created before all things is the Wisdom of Proverbs 8, possessed from the beginning.
cards.s_text: Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:7 — *For the Spirit of Yahuah (God) filleth the world: and that which containeth all things has knowledge of the voice.* The sister wisdom-book names the same fountain: the Spirit of Yahuah filling the world is the fountain of wisdom of Sir 1:5.
cards.s_text: The word of Yahuah (God) most high is the fountain of wisdom; and her ways are everlasting commandments.
cards.t_text: For the Spirit of Yahuah (God) filleth the world: and that which containeth all things has knowledge of the voice.

cards.note: 1 Corinthians 1:30 — *But of him are ye in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus), who of Elohim (God) is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:* The wisdom that is with Yahuah for ever (Sir 1:1) is made ours in the Messiah.
cards.s_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.
cards.t_text: But of him are you in HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus), who of Elohim (God) is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:

cards.note: James 1:5 — *If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.* James, Sirach's closest NT sibling, echoes 1:1: all wisdom comes down from Yahuah, freely, to those who ask.
cards.s_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.
cards.t_text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that gives to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

cards.note: James 1:2 — *My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations;* James, the closest NT sibling to Sirach, echoes ben Sira's call to brace the soul for trial as joy.
cards.s_text: My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.
cards.t_text: My brethren, count it all joy when you fall into divers temptations;

cards.note: James 1:3 — *Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience.* The serving of Yahuah is met with testing that, as in Sirach 2:1-4, produces patient endurance.
cards.s_text: My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.
cards.t_text: Knowing this, that the trying of your faith works patience.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):* (1 Peter 1:7). Peter writes to the scattered strangers with Sirach's figure in his hand: faith tried with fire, more precious than gold that perishes. Sirach had said gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity, and Peter, who had been through that furnace himself the night the cock crowed, hands the picture on to the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) he is writing to. The trial is not a sign of being forsaken; it is the proving, and what is proved is found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ). The Apocrypha and the apostle are describing the same furnace.
cards.s_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
cards.t_text: That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perishes, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):

cards.note: Job 23:10 — *But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold.* Job is the Tanakh root of the acceptable man coming forth as gold from the furnace (Sirach 2:5).
cards.s_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
cards.t_text: But he knows the way that I take: when he has tried me, I shall come forth as gold.

cards.note: *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6). *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). Two wisdom books, one furnace. Sirach says gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity; Wisdom says Yahuah (God) tried the righteous as gold in the furnace and received them as a burnt offering. The fire does not destroy the gold; it shows what the gold is. The righteous who were tormented and killed in Wisdom 2 were being refined, not discarded, and what came through the fire was received at the altar.
cards.s_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
cards.t_text: As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.

cards.note: James 1:4 — *But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.* The constant endurance ben Sira commands (Sirach 2:2) is James's perfecting patience.
cards.s_text: Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.
cards.t_text: But let patience have her perfect work, that you may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

cards.note: Matthew 4:1 — *Then was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.* The Messiah Himself enters the prepared-for temptation of Sirach 2:1 and answers it by the word.
cards.s_text: My son, if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.
cards.t_text: Then was Yahusha (Jesus) led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:2 — *And thou shalt remember all the way which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no.* The low estate borne patiently (Sirach 2:4) is Israel proved in the wilderness.
cards.s_text: Whatsoever is brought upon you take cheerfully, and be patient when you are changed to a low estate.
cards.t_text: And you shall remember all the way which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, and to prove you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or no.

cards.note: Romans 5:3 — *And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience;* Sha'ul's glorying in tribulation is ben Sira's 'trust in him' through the time of trouble (Sirach 2:6).
cards.s_text: Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.
cards.t_text: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation works patience;

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* Ben Sira's triple 'ye that fear Yahuah' (Sirach 2:7-9) rests on the wisdom foundation of Proverbs.
cards.s_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Psalm 34:9 — *O fear Yahuah (LORD), ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.* The fearer of Yahuah who waits for mercy (Sirach 2:7) lacks no good thing.
cards.s_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall.
cards.t_text: O fear Yahuah (LORD), you his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.

cards.note: Psalm 25:3 — *Yea, let none that wait on thee be ashamed: let them be ashamed which transgress without cause.* To wait for His mercy and not go aside (Sirach 2:7) is to be kept from shame.
cards.s_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall.
cards.t_text: Yea, let none that wait on you be ashamed: let them be ashamed which transgress without cause.

cards.note: Revelation 2:10 — *Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.* The reward that shall not fail (Sirach 2:8) is the crown of life to the faithful-unto-death.
cards.s_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), believe him; and your reward shall not fail.
cards.t_text: Fear none of those things which you shall suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that you may be tried; and you shall have tribulation ten days: be you faithful unto death, and I will give you a crown of life.

cards.note: Psalm 22:4 — *Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them.* The generations of old who trusted and were not confounded (Sirach 2:10) are the delivered fathers of the Psalm.
cards.s_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?
cards.t_text: Our fathers trusted in you: they trusted, and you did deliver them.

cards.note: Psalm 22:5 — *They cried unto thee, and were delivered: they trusted in thee, and were not confounded.* The exact 'trusted and was not confounded' that ben Sira asks of the generations (Sirach 2:10).
cards.s_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?
cards.t_text: They cried unto you, and were delivered: they trusted in you, and were not confounded.

cards.note: Exodus 34:6 — *And Yahuah (LORD) passed by before him, and proclaimed, Yahuah (LORD), Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God), merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth,* The Sinai proclamation of the Name is the source of ben Sira's 'full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering' (Sirach 2:11).
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) passed by before him, and proclaimed, Yahuah (LORD), Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God), merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth,

cards.note: Lamentations 3:22 — *It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.* The compassions that fail not are ben Sira's mercy that saves in time of affliction (Sirach 2:11).
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction.
cards.t_text: It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.

cards.note: James 1:8 — *A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.* James's double-minded man is precisely ben Sira's 'sinner that goes two ways' (Sirach 2:12).
cards.s_text: Woe be to fearful hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goes two ways!
cards.t_text: A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.

cards.note: James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him.* The blessing on the endurer answers ben Sira's woe on the fainthearted who believes not (Sirach 2:13).
cards.s_text: Woe to him that is fainthearted! for he believes not; therefore shall he not be defended.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that endures temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to them that love him.

cards.note: Hebrews 12:5 — *And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of Yahuah (Lord), nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:* The lost-patience and faint hands of Sirach 2:14 are the fainting under chastening Hebrews warns against.
cards.s_text: Woe to you that have lost patience! and what will you do when Yahuah (God) shall visit you?
cards.t_text: And you have forgotten the exhortation which speaks unto you as unto children, My son, despise not you the chastening of Yahuah (Lord), nor faint when you are rebuked of him:

cards.note: John 14:15 — *If ye love me, keep my commandments.* The Messiah's measure of love is ben Sira's 'they that love him will keep his ways' (Sirach 2:15).
cards.s_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways.
cards.t_text: If you love me, keep my commandments.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:9 — *They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.* The companion wisdom book joins the truth-seeking, law-filled fearers of Sirach 2:16 to the faithful-in-love elect.
cards.s_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) will seek that which is well, pleasing to him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law.
cards.t_text: They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.
