cards.note: 2 Samuel 24:14 — *And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of Yahuah (LORD); for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.* David's choice is ben Sira's closing word verbatim in figure — to fall into the hands of Yahuah, not men (Sirach 2:18).
cards.s_text: Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.
cards.t_text: And David said unto Gad, I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of Yahuah (LORD); for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man.

cards.note: Romans 8:28 — *And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.* Because His mercy matches His majesty, all that is brought upon the lovers of Yahuah works to good (Sirach 2:18).
cards.s_text: Saying, We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men: for as his majesty is, so is his mercy.
cards.t_text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:30). Two books of the library say one thing in two pictures. Tobit's open hand keeps the face of Yahuah (God) turned toward the giver; Sirach says alms put out sin the way water puts out fire. Neither is buying anything. Alms is mercy, mercy is what the Torah asks of a man, and the one who walks in it walks in the light of the Father's face.
cards.s_text: Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.
cards.t_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.

cards.note: Matthew 6:4 — *That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.* The Sermon takes up Ben Sira's almsdeed that maketh atonement and hides it from man's eye (Ecclesiasticus 3:30).
cards.s_text: Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.
cards.t_text: That your alms may be in secret: and your Father which sees in secret himself shall reward you openly.

cards.note: Daniel 4:37 — *Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.* The king who learned that the stubborn heart fares evil at the last is living proof of Ben Sira's word (Ecclesiasticus 3:26).
cards.s_text: A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last; and he that loves danger shall perish in it.
cards.t_text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:18 — *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.* The wisdom-saying behind Ben Sira's verdict that for the punishment of the proud there is no remedy (Ecclesiasticus 3:28).
cards.s_text: In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy; for the plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
cards.t_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

cards.note: Daniel 12:10 — *Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.* As Ben Sira warns that many are deceived by vain opinion, Daniel divides the wise who understand from the wicked who never will (Ecclesiasticus 3:24).
cards.s_text: For many are deceived by their own vain opinion; and an evil suspicion has overthrown their judgment.
cards.t_text: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.

cards.note: Micah 6:8 — *He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* The modest, reverent walk Micah requires is Ben Sira's mind set on what is commanded rather than the hidden (Ecclesiasticus 3:22).
cards.s_text: But what is commanded you, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for you to see with your eyes the things that are in secret.
cards.t_text: He has shewed you, O man, what is good; and what does Yahuah (LORD) require of you, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your Elohim (God)?

cards.note: Deuteronomy 29:29 — *The secret things belong unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God): but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.* Moses' division of secret and revealed is exactly Ben Sira's: think on what is commanded, not on the things in secret (Ecclesiasticus 3:22).
cards.s_text: But what is commanded you, think thereupon with reverence, for it is not needful for you to see with your eyes the things that are in secret.
cards.t_text: The secret things belong unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God): but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:34 — *Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he giveth grace unto the lowly.* The Tanakh's wisdom that grace goes to the lowly underwrites Ben Sira's word that the lowly honour the great power of Yahuah (Ecclesiasticus 3:20).
cards.s_text: For the power of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.
cards.t_text: Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he gives grace unto the lowly.

cards.note: James 4:6 — *But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.* Ya'aqob, the closest NT sibling of this book, echoes that Yahuah is honoured of the lowly (Ecclesiasticus 3:20).
cards.s_text: For the power of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.
cards.t_text: But he gives more grace. Wherefore he says, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.

cards.note: Luke 18:14 — *I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.* The publican who humbled himself found the favour before Yahuah that Ben Sira promises the lowly (Ecclesiasticus 3:18).
cards.s_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

cards.note: Luke 14:11 — *For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.* The Messiah's law of the Kingdom is Ben Sira's counsel that the greater one is, the more he should humble himself (Ecclesiasticus 3:18).
cards.s_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

cards.note: Ephesians 6:3 — *That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.* The promise attached to honouring parents reaches into their old age, where Ben Sira bids the strong have patience (Ecclesiasticus 3:13).
cards.s_text: And if his understanding fail, have patience with him; and despise him not when you are in your full strength.
cards.t_text: That it may be well with you, and you may live long on the earth.

cards.note: Tobit 12:9 — *For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:* The sister wisdom-book confirms that the relief of one's father, counted instead of sins to build a man up, is an almsdeed (Ecclesiasticus 3:14).
cards.s_text: For the relieving of your father shall not be forgotten: and instead of sins it shall be added to build you up.
cards.t_text: For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:

cards.note: Matthew 15:6 — *And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition.* The corban loophole is precisely the forsaking of the father Ben Sira likens to blasphemy (Ecclesiasticus 3:16).
cards.s_text: He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have you made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition.

cards.note: Matthew 15:4 — *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* The Messiah holds the same commandment Ben Sira presses, rebuking the tradition that voided it (Ecclesiasticus 3:5).
cards.s_text: Whoso honoureth his father shall have joy of his own children; and when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
cards.t_text: For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour your father and mother: and, He that curses father or mother, let him die the death.

cards.note: Ephesians 6:2 — *Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)* Sha'ul names as the first commandment with promise the very duty Ben Sira urges in word and deed (Ecclesiasticus 3:8).
cards.s_text: Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)

cards.note: Deuteronomy 5:16 — *Honour thy father and thy mother, as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* The same long-life promise Ben Sira repeats: he that honoureth his father shall have a long life (Ecclesiasticus 3:6).
cards.s_text: He that honoureth his father shall have a long life; and he that is obedient to Yahuah (God) shall be a comfort to his mother.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and your mother, as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has commanded you; that your days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with you, in the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you.

cards.note: Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* The Sinai command Ben Sira unfolds when he says Yahuah has given the father honour over the children (Ecclesiasticus 3:2).
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) has given the father honour over the children, and has confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and your mother: that your days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you.

cards.note: *Strive for the truth to death, and Yahuah (God) shall fight for you.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:28). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Sirach tells his son to strive for the truth to death, and promises that Yahuah (God) will do the fighting. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve that whoever confesses him before men will be confessed before the Father. Confessing him before men is the striving for the truth, carried all the way to death if it comes to that, and the confession before the Father is Yahuah (God) fighting for the one who did not let go. The promise in Sirach and the promise in Matthew are the same promise: the man who holds the truth in front of men is not left to hold it alone.
cards.s_text: Strive for the truth to death, and Yahuah (God) shall fight for you.
cards.t_text: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.

cards.note: 1 John 1:9 — *If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.* The unashamed confession Sirach 4:26 commands meets the gospel's pledge of a faithful and just forgiveness.
cards.s_text: Be not ashamed to confess your sins; and force not the course of the river.
cards.t_text: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

cards.note: Proverbs 28:13 — *He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.* Ben Sira's charge not to be ashamed to confess your sins (Sirach 4:26) is the Proverb's open road to mercy through confession and forsaking.
cards.s_text: Be not ashamed to confess your sins; and force not the course of the river.
cards.t_text: He that covers his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.

cards.note: Hebrews 12:6 — *For whom Yahuah (Lord) loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.* The fear, dread, and discipline by which wisdom proves him in Sirach 4:17 is the scourging Hebrews reads as the proof of sonship, not rejection.
cards.s_text: For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.
cards.t_text: For whom Yahuah (Lord) loves he chastens, and scourgeth every son whom he receives.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:11 — *My son, despise not the chastening of Yahuah (LORD); neither be weary of his correction:* Wisdom's tormenting discipline in Sirach 4:17, which tries the soul by her laws, is the loving correction Proverbs tells the son not to despise.
cards.s_text: For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.
cards.t_text: My son, despise not the chastening of Yahuah (LORD); neither be weary of his correction:

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yes, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* Sirach's apocryphal sister-book speaks the same lady Wisdom whom to love is to love life, found of all who seek her early.
cards.s_text: He that loves her loves life; and they that seek to her early shall be filled with joy.
cards.t_text: Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yes, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.

cards.note: Proverbs 4:6 — *Forsake her not, and she shall preserve thee: love her, and she shall keep thee.* The mutual hold of Sirach 4:11, where wisdom layeth hold of them that seek her, is Proverbs' counsel to love her and be kept.
cards.s_text: Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.
cards.t_text: Forsake her not, and she shall preserve you: love her, and she shall keep you.

cards.note: *He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:13). *That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.* (Proverbs 8:21). Wisdom speaks for herself in Proverbs: she causes those who love her to inherit, and she fills their treasures. Sirach describes the same inheritance from the receiving end: the one who holds her fast inherits glory, and wherever she enters, Yahuah (God) blesses. Both verses give wisdom an estate to leave, and both leave it to the ones who love her and will not let her go. Holding her fast is the inheritance's condition and its proof.
cards.s_text: He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless.
cards.t_text: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:17 — *I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.* Lady Wisdom's own promise stands behind Sirach 4:12: he that loves her loves life, and they that seek her early are filled with joy.
cards.s_text: He that loves her loves life; and they that seek to her early shall be filled with joy.
cards.t_text: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

cards.note: Isaiah 58:6 — *Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?* Delivering the one who suffers wrong from the oppressor, the charge of Sirach 4:9, is the very fast Yahuah declares He has chosen.
cards.s_text: Deliver him that suffers wrong from the hand of the oppressor; and be not fainthearted when you sittest in judgment.
cards.t_text: Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that you break every yoke?

cards.note: James 1:27 — *Pure religion and undefiled before Elohim (God) and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.* James, Sirach's nearest NT kin, makes care for the fatherless and widow the mark of pure religion, just as Sirach 4:10 makes it the mark of the son of the Most High.
cards.s_text: Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.
cards.t_text: Pure religion and undefiled before Elohim (God) and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

cards.note: Psalm 68:5 — *A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is Elohim (God) in his holy habitation.* To be a father to the fatherless, as Sirach 4:10 urges, is to mirror Yahuah Himself, who is the orphan's Father and the widow's Judge.
cards.s_text: Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.
cards.t_text: A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is Elohim (God) in his holy habitation.

cards.note: James 2:16 — *And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit?* The hollow word that leaves the hungry sorrowful is exactly what Sirach 4:2 forbids.
cards.s_text: Make not an hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress.
cards.t_text: And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be you warmed and filled; notwithstanding you give them not those things which are needful to the body; what does it profit?

cards.note: James 2:15 — *If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,* James, the wisdom-book of the New Testament nearest to Sirach, sets the same hungry brother before us whom Ben Sira says we must not provoke in his distress.
cards.s_text: Make not an hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress.
cards.t_text: If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food,

cards.note: Isaiah 58:7 — *Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?* Isaiah's chosen fast is the opposite of turning the face away from a poor man that Sirach 4:4 condemns.
cards.s_text: Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.
cards.t_text: Is it not to deal your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor that are cast out to your house? when you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you hide not thyself from your own flesh?

cards.note: Matthew 25:35 — *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* The Messiah identifies with the hungry soul Ben Sira forbids us to make sorrowful, counting mercy to the least as mercy to Himself.
cards.s_text: Make not an hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress.
cards.t_text: For I was an hungred, and you gave me meat: I was thirsty, and you gave me drink: I was a stranger, and you took me in:

cards.note: Proverbs 19:17 — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again.* Sirach's plea not to defraud the poor rests on the same accounting: mercy to the needy is a loan made to Yahuah Himself.
cards.s_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.
cards.t_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:9 — *Beware that there be not a thought in thy wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and thine eye be evil against thy poor brother, and thou givest him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee.* The very curse Sirach 4:6 dreads — the poor man's cry reaching his Maker as sin against the giver — is Moses' own warning.
cards.s_text: For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.
cards.t_text: Beware that there be not a thought in your wicked heart, saying, The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand; and your eye be evil against your poor brother, and you give him nought; and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against you, and it be sin unto you.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:8 — *But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.* The open hand of Deuteronomy is the answer to Sirach's needy eyes that must not be made to wait long.
cards.s_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.
cards.t_text: But you shall open your hand wide unto him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:7 — *If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren within any of thy gates in thy land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother:* The Torah forbids the very hardening Ben Sira warns against when he says defraud not the poor of his living.
cards.s_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.
cards.t_text: If there be among you a poor man of one of your brethren within any of your gates in your land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you, you shall not harden your heart, nor shut your hand from your poor brother:

cards.note: Proverbs 17:28 — *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.* The proverb commends the "lay thy hand upon thy mouth" restraint of Ecclesiasticus 5:12.
cards.s_text: If you have understanding, answer your neighbour; if not, lay your hand upon your mouth.
cards.t_text: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shuts his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.

cards.note: James 1:19 — *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:* Ya'aqov all but quotes Ecclesiasticus 5:11 — "be swift to hear... with patience give answer" — the closest NT echo of ben Sira.
cards.s_text: Be swift to hear; and let your life be sincere; and with patience give answer.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

cards.note: Proverbs 10:19 — *In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.* The proverb commends the steadfast, single word Ben Sira urges in Ecclesiasticus 5:10.
cards.s_text: Be stedfast in your understanding; and let your word be the same.
cards.t_text: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refrains his lips is wise.

cards.note: James 3:5 — *Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!* Ya'aqov, Sirach's nearest sibling, takes up the same peril of the double tongue named in Ecclesiasticus 5:9.
cards.s_text: Winnow not with every wind, and go not into every way: for so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
cards.t_text: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!

cards.note: Luke 12:20 — *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* He who is at ease "in your security" (Ecclesiasticus 5:7) is the fool whose soul is suddenly required.
cards.s_text: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) said unto him, You fool, this night your soul shall be required of you: then whose shall those things be, which you have provided?

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 6:2 — *For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.* Sha'ul presses the same "make no tarrying" of Ecclesiasticus 5:7 — the day to turn is now.
cards.s_text: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
cards.t_text: (For he says, I have heard you in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured you: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)

cards.note: Proverbs 27:1 — *Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.* The proverb against presuming on tomorrow undergirds Ben Sira's "put not off from day to day" (Ecclesiasticus 5:7).
cards.s_text: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
cards.t_text: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for you know not what a day may bring forth.

cards.note: Romans 2:5 — *But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim (God);* He who presumes "His mercy is great" (Ecclesiasticus 5:6) forgets that wrath also rests on the impenitent.
cards.s_text: And say not His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners.
cards.t_text: But after your hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim (God);

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The space for repentance is the very propitiation Ecclesiasticus 5:5 says to fear adding sin against.
cards.s_text: Concerning propitiation, be not without fear to add sin to sin:
cards.t_text: But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 11:23 — *But you have mercy upon all; for you can do all things, and winkest at the sins of men, because they should amend.* The companion book confirms the mercy of Ecclesiasticus 5:6 is real, but given that men should amend — not that they may add sin to sin.
cards.s_text: And say not His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners.
cards.t_text: But you have mercy upon all; for you can do all things, and winkest at the sins of men, because they should amend.

cards.note: Romans 2:5 — *But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim (God);* The man who says "what harm" (Ecclesiasticus 5:4) is in fact treasuring up wrath against the day of vengeance.
cards.s_text: Say not, I have sinned, and what harm has happened to me? for Yahuah (God) is longsuffering, he will in no wise let you go.
cards.t_text: But after your hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of Elohim (God);

cards.note: Romans 2:4 — *Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of Elohim (God) leadeth thee to repentance?* Sha'ul shows the longsuffering of Ecclesiasticus 5:4 is mercy unto repentance, not permission to add sin.
cards.s_text: Say not, I have sinned, and what harm has happened to me? for Yahuah (God) is longsuffering, he will in no wise let you go.
cards.t_text: Or despisest you the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of Elohim (God) leads you to repentance?

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 8:11 — *Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.* The Preacher names the very self-deceit of "I have sinned, and what harm" in Ecclesiasticus 5:4.
cards.s_text: Say not, I have sinned, and what harm has happened to me? for Yahuah (God) is longsuffering, he will in no wise let you go.
cards.t_text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:8 — *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* The companion wisdom-book voices the dead man's regret over the goods that did not profit in the day of calamity (Ecclesiasticus 5:8).
cards.s_text: Set not yours heart upon goods unjustly gotten, for they shall not profit you in the day of calamity.
cards.t_text: What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?

cards.note: Matthew 6:19 — *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:* The Master forbids the heart set on goods that Ecclesiasticus 5:1 calls vain.
cards.s_text: Set your heart upon your goods; and say not, I have enough for my life.
cards.t_text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust does corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

cards.note: Luke 12:20 — *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* The rich fool who said "I have enough for my life" is the very man Ecclesiasticus 5:1 warns against.
cards.s_text: Set your heart upon your goods; and say not, I have enough for my life.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) said unto him, You fool, this night your soul shall be required of you: then whose shall those things be, which you have provided?

cards.note: Psalm 1:3 — *And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.* He who cleaves to the wise elders of Sirach 6:34 becomes the fruitful, unwithering tree — the opposite of the dry tree of Sirach 6:3.
cards.s_text: Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave to him that is wise.
cards.t_text: And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that brings forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he does shall prosper.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* The mind fixed on Yahuah's ordinances in Sirach 6:37 receives wisdom because the fear of Yahuah is where all knowledge begins.
cards.s_text: Let your mind be upon the ordinances of Yahuah (God) and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish yours heart, and give you wisdom at your owns desire.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 6:6 — *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:* The Shema's charge to carry Yahuah's words in the heart is the established heart Ben Sira promises in Sirach 6:37.
cards.s_text: Let your mind be upon the ordinances of Yahuah (God) and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish yours heart, and give you wisdom at your owns desire.
cards.t_text: And these words, which I command you this day, shall be in your heart:

cards.note: Psalm 1:2 — *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night.* Ben Sira's command to meditate continually in His commandments in Sirach 6:37 is the delight and day-and-night meditation of the blessed man.
cards.s_text: Let your mind be upon the ordinances of Yahuah (God) and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish yours heart, and give you wisdom at your owns desire.
cards.t_text: But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law does he meditate day and night.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.* The sibling book turns Wisdom's chains into the same treasure and robe of glory as Sirach 6:29 — and back to the friendship theme of the chapter.
cards.s_text: Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for you, and her chains a robe of glory.
cards.t_text: For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.

cards.note: Matthew 11:30 — *For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* Ben Sira's promise that Wisdom's bonds need not grieve you in Sirach 6:25 is the Messiah's easy yoke and light burden.
cards.s_text: Bow down your shoulder, and bear her, and be not grieved with her bonds.
cards.t_text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

cards.note: Matthew 11:29 — *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* The bowed shoulder bearing Wisdom's bonds in Sirach 6:25 is the Messiah's yoke that gives rest to the soul.
cards.s_text: Bow down your shoulder, and bear her, and be not grieved with her bonds.
cards.t_text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and you shall find rest unto your souls.

cards.note: James 1:5 — *If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.* James makes the youthful gathering of instruction in Sirach 6:18 a matter of asking the Giver who upbraids not.
cards.s_text: My son, gather instruction from your youth up: so shall you find wisdom till your old age.
cards.t_text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that gives to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:14 — *Whoso seeks her early shall have no great travail: for he shall find her sitting at his doors.* The sibling wisdom book echoes Sirach 6:19 verse for verse — the early seeker toils little and finds her near at hand.
cards.s_text: Come to her as one that ploweth and sows, and wait for her good fruits: for you shall not toil much in labouring about her, but you shall eat of her fruits right soon.
cards.t_text: Whoso seeks her early shall have no great travail: for he shall find her sitting at his doors.

cards.note: Proverbs 2:4 — *If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as for hid treasures;* Solomon's command to search for wisdom as for hid treasure is Ben Sira's "Search, and seek" and "let her not go" of Sirach 6:27.
cards.s_text: Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you: and when you have got hold of her, let her not go.
cards.t_text: If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hid treasures;

cards.note: Proverbs 8:17 — *I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.* Wisdom herself answers the plower and sower of Sirach 6:19 — those who seek her early eat of her fruits soon.
cards.s_text: Come to her as one that ploweth and sows, and wait for her good fruits: for you shall not toil much in labouring about her, but you shall eat of her fruits right soon.
cards.t_text: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

cards.note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* Ben Sira anchors right friendship in the fear of Yahuah in Sirach 6:17 — the same fear Proverbs calls the beginning of wisdom.
cards.s_text: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: John 15:15 — *Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.* He who fears the Father names His own as friends — the faithful friend that those who fear Yahuah shall find in Sirach 6:16.
cards.s_text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.
cards.t_text: Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knows not what his lord does: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.

cards.note: John 15:13 — *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* The Messiah's laid-down life is the medicine-of-life friendship of Sirach 6:16 carried to its fullest measure.
cards.s_text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.
cards.t_text: Greater love has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

cards.note: Proverbs 17:17 — *A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.* Solomon's friend who loves at all times is Ben Sira's "strong defence" and "treasure" — the faithful friend of Sirach 6:14.
cards.s_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.
cards.t_text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:20 — *He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.* The fair-weather "friend for his own occasion" of Sirach 6:8 is the companion of fools who is destroyed in the day of trouble.
cards.s_text: For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.
cards.t_text: He that walks with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

cards.note: Proverbs 27:6 — *Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.* Proverbs gives the test Ben Sira commands in Sirach 6:7 — prove a friend by whether his honest wounds outlast a flatterer's kisses.
cards.s_text: If you would get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him.
cards.t_text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

cards.note: *Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:6). *A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.* (Proverbs 18:24). Solomon's proverb has two kinds of friend in it: the many a friendly man gathers, and the one who sticks closer than a brother. Sirach draws the same line and tells you how to count: be at peace with many, but take one counsellor out of a thousand. The crowd of friends is not the problem; letting the crowd counsel you is. Both writers are pointing at the rare one, the friend whose word you can build on, and both say you will not find him by being friendly to everyone but by proving him.
cards.s_text: Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.
cards.t_text: A man that has friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.

cards.note: Matthew 12:35 — *A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.* The Messiah roots the "sweet language" of Sirach 6:5 where Ben Sira does — in the treasure of the heart that the tongue spends.
cards.s_text: Sweet language will multiply friends: and a fairspeaking tongue will increase kind greetings.
cards.t_text: A good man out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure brings forth evil things.

cards.note: James 3:10 — *Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.* James names the very double-mouthedness of the "double tongue" of Sirach 6:1 — blessing and cursing cannot share one tongue.
cards.s_text: Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.
cards.t_text: Out of the same mouth proceeds blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.

cards.note: James 3:8 — *But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.* The Messiah's brother frames the untamed tongue exactly as Ben Sira does in Sirach 6:1 — the instrument that breeds shame and reproach.
cards.s_text: Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.
cards.t_text: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

cards.note: Psalm 12:2 — *They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.* The double heart of David's psalm is Ben Sira's "double tongue" that turns a friend into an enemy in Sirach 6:1.
cards.s_text: Instead of a friend become not an enemy; for thereby you shall inherit an ill name, shame, and reproach: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.
cards.t_text: They speak vanity every one with his neighbour: with flattering lips and with a double heart do they speak.

cards.note: Hebrews 13:7 — *Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of Elohim (God): whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation* — Hebrews bids us follow the faithful "considering the end," the same remembrance Sirach 7:36 commands.
cards.s_text: Whatsoever you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amiss.
cards.t_text: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of Elohim (God): whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.

cards.note: Psalm 90:12 — *So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom* — numbering our days is to "remember the end" of Sirach 7:36, that we never do amiss.
cards.s_text: Whatsoever you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amiss.
cards.t_text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:29 — *O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!* — the considered "end" of Sirach 7:36 is Moses' very plea, the wisdom of the latter end.
cards.s_text: Whatsoever you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amiss.
cards.t_text: O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32). Tobit tells his son to turn his face toward the poor; Sirach tells his to stretch out his hand to them so that his blessing may be perfected. The face and the hand together are the whole posture of the righteous man in the library: see the need and move toward it. The blessing is not finished until the hand is open.
cards.s_text: And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.
cards.t_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.

cards.note: Matthew 25:36 — *Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me* — the King names visiting the sick, the very work Sirach 7:35 commands: "Be not slow to visit the sick."
cards.s_text: Be not slow to visit the sick: for that shall make you to be beloved.
cards.t_text: Naked, and you clothed me: I was sick, and you visited me: I was in prison, and you came unto me.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:17 — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again* — the perfected blessing of the open hand Sirach 7:32 promises.
cards.s_text: And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.
cards.t_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.

cards.note: *Fear Yahuah (God), and honor the priest; and give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:31). *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:* (Proverbs 3:9). Sirach puts the priest's portion under the fear of Yahuah (God) and says it is given as it is commanded — the firstfruits, the trespass offering, the shoulder, the holy things. Solomon had already said where that honor is going: the firstfruits of all the increase honor Yahuah (LORD) himself, and the priest is the hand that receives them for him. Neither verse treats the gift as a tax. It is the first and the best handed back to the one who gave the whole, and the Torah's instruction for the priest's due is where that honor lands in practice.
cards.s_text: Fear Yahuah (God), and honor the priest; and give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.
cards.t_text: Honour Yahuah (LORD) with your substance, and with the firstfruits of all your increase:

cards.note: Hebrews 13:17 — *Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you* — the honouring of the priest "as it is commanded you" that Sirach 7:31 details.
cards.s_text: Fear Yahuah (God), and honor the priest; and give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.
cards.t_text: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

cards.note: Hebrews 13:7 — *Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of Elohim (God): whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation* — the reverencing of Yahuah's ministers that Sirach 7:29 commands.
cards.s_text: Fear Yahuah (God) with all your soul, and reverence his priests.
cards.t_text: Remember them which have the rule over you, who have spoken unto you the word of Elohim (God): whose faith follow, considering the end of their conversation.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:6 — *Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it* — the instructing of children Sirach 7:23 commands: "instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth."
cards.s_text: Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.
cards.t_text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

cards.note: Ephesians 6:2 — *Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)* — Paul names as covenant-promise the very honour Sirach 7:27 commands.
cards.s_text: Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)

cards.note: Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee* — the Decalogue word Sirach 7:27 expounds "with your whole heart."
cards.s_text: Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and your mother: that your days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you.

cards.note: James 1:19 — *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath* — the slow-to-speak restraint Sirach 7:14 urges against "much babbling."
cards.s_text: Use not many words in a multitude of elders, and make not much babbling when you prayest.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

cards.note: James 1:26 — *If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain* — the same bridling of lying speech Sirach 7:13 calls for, for "the custom thereof is not good."
cards.s_text: Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.
cards.t_text: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.

cards.note: James 4:10 — *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* — the One who "humbleth and exalteth" of Sirach 7:11 is the same Yahuah who lifts up the humble.
cards.s_text: Laugh no man to scorn in the bitterness of his soul: for there is one which humbleth and exalteth.
cards.t_text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

cards.note: James 4:10 — *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* — the command form of Sirach 7:17's "Humble thyself greatly."
cards.s_text: Humble thyself greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and worms.
cards.t_text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

cards.note: James 4:6 — *But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* — James draws the very Proverb Sirach 7:17 dramatizes with "the vengeance of the ungodly."
cards.s_text: Humble thyself greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and worms.
cards.t_text: But he gives more grace. Wherefore he says, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:34 — *Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he giveth grace unto the lowly* — the same exalting of the lowly that Sirach 7:17's "humble thyself greatly" commands.
cards.s_text: Humble thyself greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and worms.
cards.t_text: Surely he scorneth the scorners: but he gives grace unto the lowly.

cards.note: James 1:27 — *Pure religion and undefiled before Elohim (God) and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world* — the same departing-from-iniquity that Sirach 7:2 urges, framed as undefiled religion.
cards.s_text: Depart from the unjust, and iniquity shall turn away from you.
cards.t_text: Pure religion and undefiled before Elohim (God) and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction* — the wisdom of which Sirach 7:1's "do no evil" is the first lived obedience.
cards.s_text: Do no evil, so shall no harm come to you.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:14 — *Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.* Sirach 8:17 says consult not with a fool who cannot keep counsel — but Proverbs keeps the door open to the safety found in many wise counsellors.
cards.s_text: Consult not with a fool; for he cannot keep counsel.
cards.t_text: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

cards.note: Proverbs 25:9 — *Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:* The exact caution of Sirach 8:18 — do no secret thing before a stranger; keep the matter between the two concerned.
cards.s_text: Do no secret thing before a stranger; for you know not what he will bring forth.
cards.t_text: Debate your cause with your neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another:

cards.note: Proverbs 11:13 — *A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.* Why open not your heart to every man (Sirach 8:19) — the talebearer reveals what the faithful conceal.
cards.s_text: Open not yours heart to every man, lest he requite you with a shrewd turn.
cards.t_text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:11 — *Wherefore set your affection upon my words; desire them, and you shall be instructed.* The sister wisdom-book echoes Sirach 8:8 — do not despise the discourse of the wise but set your affection on it and be instructed.
cards.s_text: Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs: for of them you shall learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.
cards.t_text: Wherefore set your affection upon my words; desire them, and you shall be instructed.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:34 — *Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave to him that is wise.* Ben Sira's own earlier charge, repeated here in Sirach 8:8-9 — keep company with the wise and the elders and learn.
cards.s_text: Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs: for of them you shall learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.
cards.t_text: Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave to him that is wise.

cards.note: Job 12:12 — *With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.* Why miss not the discourse of the elders (Sirach 8:9) — they learned of their fathers, and length of days carries understanding.
cards.s_text: Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learn understanding, and to give answer as need requires.
cards.t_text: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:5 — *A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:* The teachableness Sirach 8:8 commands — acquaint yourself with the proverbs of the wise and your learning increases.
cards.s_text: Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint thyself with their proverbs: for of them you shall learn instruction, and how to serve great men with ease.
cards.t_text: A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:

cards.note: Proverbs 24:17 — *Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:* The exact restraint of Sirach 8:7 — no gloating over the fallen foe, for we die all.
cards.s_text: Rejoice not over your greatest enemy being dead, but remember that we die all.
cards.t_text: Rejoice not when your enemy falls, and let not your heart be glad when he stumbleth:

cards.note: Proverbs 16:31 — *The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.* Why dishonour not old age (Sirach 8:6) — the grey head is a crown, not a thing to be despised.
cards.s_text: Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us wax old.
cards.t_text: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:32 — *Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).* Torah itself underwrites Sirach 8:6 — honour the aged, for the fear of Yahuah binds it.
cards.s_text: Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us wax old.
cards.t_text: You shall rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear your Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Galatians 6:1 — *Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.* The restoring meekness of Sirach 8:5 — handle the one who turns from sin gently, remembering your own frailty.
cards.s_text: Reproach not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
cards.t_text: Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, you which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest you also be tempted.

cards.note: Matthew 7:1 — *Judge not, that ye be not judged.* The Messiah commands what Sirach 8:5 counsels — refuse the reproach that forgets you too stand under judgment.
cards.s_text: Reproach not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
cards.t_text: Judge not, that you be not judged.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 7:20 — *For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.* The ground of Sirach 8:5 — do not reproach the one turning from sin, for there is no sinless man to cast the stone.
cards.s_text: Reproach not a man that turns from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
cards.t_text: For there is not a just man upon earth, that does good, and sins not.

cards.note: Matthew 5:25 — *Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison.* The Sermon on the Mount carries Sirach 8:11's wisdom — do not rise up to be entrapped in words; settle quickly before judgment falls.
cards.s_text: Rise not up in anger at the presence of an injurious person, lest he lie in wait to entrap you in your words
cards.t_text: Agree with your adversary quickly, whiles you are in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:20 — *Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.* The very image of Sirach 8:3,10 — withhold the wood, refuse to kindle the coals, and the sinner's fire dies down.
cards.s_text: Strive not with a man that is full of tongue, and heap not wood upon his fire.
cards.t_text: Where no wood is, there the fire goes out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceases.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:20 — *He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.* The traveling-companion warning of Sirach 8:15-16 is the same: walk with the bold and angry and you perish with them through their folly.
cards.s_text: Strive not with an angry man, and go not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no help, he will overthrow you.
cards.t_text: He that walks with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:25 — *Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.* Why not walk into a solitary place with the angry man of Sirach 8:16 — his ways become a snare and overthrow you where there is no help.
cards.s_text: Strive not with an angry man, and go not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no help, he will overthrow you.
cards.t_text: Lest you learn his ways, and get a snare to your soul.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:24 — *Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:* The same charge Ben Sira gives in Sirach 8:1,16 — keep no fellowship with the violent or the powerful who will overpower you.
cards.s_text: Strive not with a mighty man’ lest you fall into his hands.
cards.t_text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man you shall not go:

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 37:12 — *But be continually with a godly man, whom you know to keep the commandments of Yahuah (God), whose, mind is according to your mind, and will sorrow with you, if you shall miscarry.* Ben Sira's own counsel to keep company with the law-keeping wise, as in Sirach 9:15-16.
cards.s_text: Let your talk be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the Most High.
cards.t_text: But be continually with a godly man, whom you know to keep the commandments of Yahuah (God), whose, mind is according to your mind, and will sorrow with you, if you shall miscarry.

cards.note: *As near as you can, guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:14). *He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.* (Proverbs 13:20). Sirach says to take the measure of your neighbour as best you can and to take counsel from the wise, and in the next verse he says to let all your communication be in the law of the Most High. Solomon had said the same about company: walk with the wise and you grow wise, keep company with fools and you share their ruin. Who sits at your table shapes who you become.
cards.s_text: As near as you can, guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.
cards.t_text: He that walks with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

cards.note: *Let your talk be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the Most High.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:15). *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night.* (Psalm 1:2). Sirach puts the whole of the wise man's conversation inside the law of the Most High. David's blessed man delights in the law of Yahuah (LORD) and meditates in it day and night. The one who delights in it will talk about it; the man whose speech is in the Torah is the man whose heart has been there first.
cards.s_text: Let your talk be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the Most High.
cards.t_text: But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law does he meditate day and night.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:17 — *Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of Yahuah (LORD) all the day long.* the same pairing Sirach 9:11-16 makes — no envy of sinners, but the fear of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Envy not the glory of a sinner: for you know not what shall be his end.
cards.t_text: Let not your heart envy sinners: but be you in the fear of Yahuah (LORD) all the day long.

cards.note: Psalm 37:1 — *Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.* the very envy of the sinner's glory Sirach 9:11 forbids.
cards.s_text: Envy not the glory of a sinner: for you know not what shall be his end.
cards.t_text: Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be you envious against the workers of iniquity.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:14 — *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* the treasure of the old friend Sirach 9:10 ranks above the new.
cards.s_text: Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.
cards.t_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:16 — *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.* Ben Sira's own praise of the tried friend that Sirach 9:10 says not to forsake.
cards.s_text: Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.
cards.t_text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.

cards.note: Proverbs 27:10 — *Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.* the same command Sirach 9:10 gives not to forsake the old friend.
cards.s_text: Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.
cards.t_text: Your own friend, and your father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into your brother’s house in the day of your calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

cards.note: James 1:14 — *But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.* the inclined desire by which Sirach 9:9 says a man falls into destruction.
cards.s_text: Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in your arms, and spend not your money with her at the wine; lest yours heart incline to her, and so through your desire you fall into destruction.
cards.t_text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:31 — *Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.* the deceiving cup Sirach 9:9 says not to share with another man's wife.
cards.s_text: Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in your arms, and spend not your money with her at the wine; lest yours heart incline to her, and so through your desire you fall into destruction.
cards.t_text: Look not you upon the wine when it is red, when it gives his colour in the cup, when it moves itself aright.

cards.note: Proverbs 6:29 — *So he that goeth in to his neighbour's wife; whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.* the guilt Ben Sira would have a man avoid by not sitting with another man's wife in Sirach 9:9.
cards.s_text: Sit not at all with another man’s wife, nor sit down with her in your arms, and spend not your money with her at the wine; lest yours heart incline to her, and so through your desire you fall into destruction.
cards.t_text: So he that goes in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever touches her shall not be innocent.

cards.note: 2 Peter 2:14 — *Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children:* the very deception by beauty Sirach 9:8 warns has deceived many.
cards.s_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.
cards.t_text: Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children:

cards.note: *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:8). *But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* (Matthew 5:28). Sirach tells the eye to turn away before love is kindled as a fire, because the deception begins in the looking. Yahusha (Jesus) follows the same line to its root: the look that lusts has already committed the adultery in the heart. Neither is adding a new commandment to the seventh. Both are reading it where it was always meant to be read, at the eye and the heart, before the body ever moves.
cards.s_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

cards.note: Proverbs 6:25 — *Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.* the inward guard against the beauty Sirach 9:5 says not to gaze upon.
cards.s_text: Gaze not on a maid, that you fall not by those things that are precious in her.
cards.t_text: Lust not after her beauty in your heart; neither let her take you with her eyelids.

cards.note: Job 31:1 — *I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?* the eye-covenant Ben Sira enjoins when he says turn away the eye in Sirach 9:8.
cards.s_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.
cards.t_text: I made a covenant with my eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

cards.note: Proverbs 6:24 — *To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.* the Torah-light that does what Sirach 9:3 commands the prudent to do.
cards.s_text: Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares.
cards.t_text: To keep you from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.

cards.note: Proverbs 7:26 — *For she hath cast down many wounded: yea, many strong men have been slain by her.* the toll of the strange woman that Sirach 9:6 would have the wise escape.
cards.s_text: Give not your soul to harlots, that you lose not your inheritance.
cards.t_text: For she has cast down many wounded: yea, many strong men have been slain by her.

cards.note: Proverbs 6:26 — *For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.* the lost inheritance Ben Sira warns of in Sirach 9:6.
cards.s_text: Give not your soul to harlots, that you lose not your inheritance.
cards.t_text: For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread: and the adulteress will hunt for the precious life.

cards.note: Proverbs 5:5 — *Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.* the end of the harlot's path that makes Sirach 9:3's snare deadly.
cards.s_text: Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares.
cards.t_text: Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell.

cards.note: Proverbs 5:3 — *For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:* the honeyed lure Ben Sira calls a snare in Sirach 9:3.
cards.s_text: Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares.
cards.t_text: For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 1:14 — *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.* Ben Sira's own opening thesis grounds 10:22 — the fear of Yahuah is the glory of every estate.
cards.s_text: Whether he be rich, noble, or poor, their glory is the fear of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:2 — *The rich and poor meet together: Yahuah (LORD) is the maker of them all.* Rich, noble, or poor (Sirach 10:22) share one glory because they share one Maker.
cards.s_text: Whether he be rich, noble, or poor, their glory is the fear of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The rich and poor meet together: Yahuah (LORD) is the maker of them all.

cards.note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* None is greater than the man who fears Yahuah (Sirach 10:24) because that fear is wisdom's very beginning.
cards.s_text: Great men, and judges, and potentates, shall be honoured; yet is there none of them greater than he that fears Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* The glory Sirach 10:22 grants rich and poor alike is the reverence Proverbs makes the head of all knowledge.
cards.s_text: Whether he be rich, noble, or poor, their glory is the fear of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:8 — *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* The ungodly's too-late confession answers Sirach 10:9's question — pride and riches profit the earth-and-ashes man nothing.
cards.s_text: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one sets his own soul to sale; because while he lives he casteth away his bowels.
cards.t_text: What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?

cards.note: Luke 12:20 — *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* The rich fool is Sirach 10:9's covetous man — he sets his soul to sale and loses it overnight.
cards.s_text: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one sets his own soul to sale; because while he lives he casteth away his bowels.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) said unto him, You fool, this night your soul shall be required of you: then whose shall those things be, which you have provided?

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:7 — *For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.* The covetous man Sirach 10:9 sells his soul for what he cannot keep — Paul names the same emptiness.
cards.s_text: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one sets his own soul to sale; because while he lives he casteth away his bowels.
cards.t_text: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.

cards.note: Genesis 3:19 — *In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.* The Eden sentence is why the dead man inherits worms in Sirach 10:11 — ashes have no ground for pride.
cards.s_text: For when a man is dead, he shall inherit creeping things, beasts, and worms.
cards.t_text: In the sweat of your face shall you eat bread, till you return unto the ground; for out of it were you taken: for dust you are, and unto dust shall you return.

cards.note: Genesis 18:27 — *And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto Yahuah (Lord), which am but dust and ashes:* Abraham owns the very lowliness Sirach 10:9 asks the proud to remember — why is earth and ashes proud?
cards.s_text: Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one sets his own soul to sale; because while he lives he casteth away his bowels.
cards.t_text: And Abraham answered and said, Behold now, I have taken upon me to speak unto Adonai (Lord), which am but dust and ashes:

cards.note: Matthew 23:12 — *And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.* The Master's verdict on the proud matches Sirach 10:7 — pride is hateful, and it ends abased.
cards.s_text: Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.
cards.t_text: And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

cards.note: 1 Peter 5:5 — *Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.* The same proverb the apostles knew: the pride Sirach 10:7 calls hateful is what heaven sets itself against.
cards.s_text: Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.
cards.t_text: Likewise, you younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and gives grace to the humble.

cards.note: James 4:6 — *But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.* James, Sirach's closest NT sibling, turns 10:7's pride-is-hateful into the gospel of grace for the lowly.
cards.s_text: Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.
cards.t_text: But he gives more grace. Wherefore he says, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.

cards.note: Luke 14:11 — *For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.* Pride was not made for the born-of-woman (Sirach 10:18); the Master makes its undoing a law of the kingdom.
cards.s_text: Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are born of a woman.
cards.t_text: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

cards.note: Luke 1:52 — *He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.* Mariam's song is the very reversal of Sirach 10:14 — proud thrones down, the meek up.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.
cards.t_text: He has put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.
