cards.note: Daniel 4:37 — *Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.* The abased king's confession is Sirach 10:14 enacted in history.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.
cards.t_text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cards.note: Isaiah 14:14 — *I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the El Elyon (most High).* The self-exalting throne Isaiah taunts is precisely the proud throne Yahuah casts down in Sirach 10:14.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.
cards.t_text: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds; I will be like the El Elyon (most High).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:14 — *Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage;* the lifted-up heart forgetting its Maker is the very departure Sirach 10:12 calls the beginning of pride.
cards.s_text: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.
cards.t_text: Then your heart be lifted up, and you forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage;

cards.note: Proverbs 8:13 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.* The heart turned from its Maker (Sirach 10:12) is exactly the pride Yahuah names as hateful.
cards.s_text: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:2 — *When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.* Pride breeds the abomination Sirach 10:13 warns of, while lowliness is wisdom's home.
cards.s_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.
cards.t_text: When pride comes, then comes shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:18 — *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.* The wisdom-axiom Ben Sira distills: pride is the head that drags down everything after it, as in Sirach 10:13.
cards.s_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.
cards.t_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 7:1 — *A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.* Judge none blessed before his death (Sirach 11:28) — Qoheleth too weighs a life by its end, not its outward beginning.
cards.s_text: Judge none blessed before his death: for a man shall be known in his children.
cards.t_text: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

cards.note: Hebrews 9:27 — *And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:* In the day of death Yahuah rewards a man according to his ways (Sirach 11:26) — appointed once to die, and after, the judgment.
cards.s_text: For it is an easy thing to Yahuah (God) in the day of death to reward a man according to his ways.
cards.t_text: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:9 — *But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.* Say not 'I have enough' presuming on the hereafter (Sirach 11:24) — Paul names the snare that swallows those who will be rich.
cards.s_text: Again, say not, I have enough, and possess many things, and what evil shall I have hereafter?
cards.t_text: But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

cards.note: Luke 12:21 — *So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God).* The man who says 'I have enough, and possess many things' (Sirach 11:24) is the one not rich toward Elohim.
cards.s_text: Again, say not, I have enough, and possess many things, and what evil shall I have hereafter?
cards.t_text: So is he that lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God).

cards.note: Luke 12:20 — *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* Yahusha's rich fool is Sirach 11:19 verbatim — he says he will eat continually of his goods, yet must leave them to others and die.
cards.s_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) said unto him, You fool, this night your soul shall be required of you: then whose shall those things be, which you have provided?

cards.note: James 1:17 — *Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.* The gift and favour of Yahuah (Sirach 11:17) is James's every good and perfect gift from the Father of lights.
cards.s_text: The gift of Yahuah (God) remains with the ungodly, and his favour brings prosperity for ever.
cards.t_text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:18 — *But thou shalt remember Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.* Yahuah makes a poor man rich on the sudden (Sirach 11:21) — Moses anchors it: it is He that giveth power to get wealth.
cards.s_text: Marvel not at the works of sinners; but trust in Yahuah (God), and abide in your labour: for it is an easy thing in the sight of Yahuah (God) on the sudden to make a poor man rich.
cards.t_text: But you shall remember Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): for it is he that gives you power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto your fathers, as it is this day.

cards.note: Psalm 75:6 — *For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south.* Life and death and riches come of Yahuah (Sirach 11:14), not from any quarter of the earth.
cards.s_text: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: For promotion comes neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south.

cards.note: Psalm 75:7 — *But Elohim (God) is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another.* The Psalm's word for Sirach 11:14 — prosperity and adversity, poverty and riches, all come of Yahuah who alone sets up and casts down.
cards.s_text: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) is the judge: he puts down one, and sets up another.

cards.note: Psalm 127:1 — *Except Yahuah (LORD) build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except Yahuah (LORD) keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.* The eye of Yahuah that sets a man up from low estate (Sirach 11:12) — apart from that building hand all the labour is vain.
cards.s_text: Again, there is another that is slow, and has need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty; yet the eye of Yahuah (God) looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,
cards.t_text: Except Yahuah (LORD) build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except Yahuah (LORD) keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.

cards.note: Proverbs 28:20 — *A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.* Meddle much and you shall not be innocent (Sirach 11:10) is Proverbs' own verdict on the hasty.
cards.s_text: My son, meddle not with many matters: for if you meddle much, you shall not be innocent; and if you follow after, you shall not obtain, neither shall you escape by fleeing.
cards.t_text: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that makes haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 9:11 — *I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.* Qoheleth's word for Sirach 11:11 — the one who makes haste is so much the more behind, for the race is not to the swift.
cards.s_text: There is one that laboureth, and takes pains, and makes haste, and is so much the more behind.
cards.t_text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:4 — *Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.* The Tanakh command Sirach 11:11 dramatizes — he that makes haste is the more behind.
cards.s_text: There is one that laboureth, and takes pains, and makes haste, and is so much the more behind.
cards.t_text: Labour not to be rich: cease from your own wisdom.

cards.note: Luke 12:14 — *And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?* Yahusha himself keeps Sirach 11:9's rule — strive not in a matter that concerneth you not, sit not in judgment uninvited.
cards.s_text: Strive not in a matter that concerneth you not; and sit not in judgment with sinners.
cards.t_text: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?

cards.note: Proverbs 18:13 — *He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.* The exact proverb Sirach 11:8 expands — answer not before you have heard the cause.
cards.s_text: Answer not before you have heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talk.
cards.t_text: He that answers a matter before he hears it, it is folly and shame unto him.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:18 — *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.* Proverbs gives the proverb behind Sirach 11:4's warning not to exalt thyself in the day of honour.
cards.s_text: Boast not of your clothing and raiment, and exalt not thyself in the day of honour: for the works of Yahuah (God) are wonderful, and his works among men are hidden.
cards.t_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 10:12 — *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.* The proud heart that watcheth for your fall (11:30) is the heart already turned away from its Maker.
cards.s_text: Like as a partridge taken and kept in a cage, so is the heart of the proud; and like as a spy, watcheth he for your fall:
cards.t_text: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* Ben Sira self-links: the warning not to exalt thyself in the day of honour (11:4) rests on his own root-diagnosis that pride is the beginning of sin.
cards.s_text: Boast not of your clothing and raiment, and exalt not thyself in the day of honour: for the works of Yahuah (God) are wonderful, and his works among men are hidden.
cards.t_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

cards.note: James 1:10 — *But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.* The mighty greatly disgraced and the honourable delivered up (Sirach 11:6) is James's fading flower of the rich.
cards.s_text: Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced; and the honourable delivered into other men’s hands.
cards.t_text: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

cards.note: James 1:9 — *Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:* James echoes Sirach 11:5's reversal — the unregarded man wears the crown, the brother of low degree is the one exalted.
cards.s_text: Many kings have sat down upon the ground; and one that was never thought of has worn the crown.
cards.t_text: Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted:

cards.note: 1 Samuel 16:7 — *But Yahuah (LORD) said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for Yahuah (LORD) seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but Yahuah (LORD) looketh on the heart.* The Tanakh's anchor for Sirach 11:2 — abhor not a man by his outward appearance, for Yahuah weighs the heart.
cards.s_text: Commend not a man for his beauty; neither abhor a man for his outward appearance.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (LORD) said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for Yahuah (LORD) sees not as man sees; for man looks on the outward appearance, but Yahuah (LORD) looks on the heart.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:10 — *Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction.* the table-friend exposed by adversity, the very test Sirach 12:8 sets for knowing friend from enemy.
cards.s_text: A friend cannot be known in prosperity: and an enemy cannot be hidden in adversity.
cards.t_text: Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:8 — *For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.* ben Sira's own friendship-pack naming the companion of Sirach 12:15 who will not tarry once you begin to fall.
cards.s_text: For a while he will abide with you, but if you begin to fall, he will not tarry.
cards.t_text: For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.

cards.note: Matthew 26:49 — *And forthwith he came to Yahusha (Jesus), and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.* the feigned friend of Sirach 12:17 who 'pretends to help' yet undermines, fulfilled in the betrayer's kiss.
cards.s_text: If adversity come upon you, you shall find him there first; and though he pretend to help you, yet shall he undermine you.
cards.t_text: And forthwith he came to Yahusha (Jesus), and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.

cards.note: Psalm 41:9 — *Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.* David's table-betrayer is the archetype of Sirach 12:9's friend who departs in the day of adversity.
cards.s_text: In the prosperity of a man enemies will be grieved: but in his adversity even a friend will depart.
cards.t_text: Yea, my own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, has lifted up his heel against me.

cards.note: Micah 7:5 — *Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.* the prophet's last-days discernment matching Sirach 12:12's caution not to seat the enemy at your right hand.
cards.s_text: Set him not by you, lest, when he has overthrown you, he stand up in your place; neither let him sit at your right hand, lest he seek to take your seat, and you at the last remember my words, and be pricked with it.
cards.t_text: Trust you not in a friend, put you not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of your mouth from her that lies in your bosom.

cards.note: Proverbs 27:6 — *Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.* the proverbial blade behind Sirach 12:10's 'Never trust your enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.'
cards.s_text: Never trust your enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.
cards.t_text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:25 — *When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.* answers Sirach 12:11's warning that the crouching, humbled enemy's rust 'has not been altogether wiped away.'
cards.s_text: Though he humble himself, and go crouching, yet take good heed and beware of him, and you shall be to him as if you had wiped a lookingglass, and you shall know that his rust has not been altogether wiped away.
cards.t_text: When he speaks fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:24 — *He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;* the exact portrait of Sirach 12:16's enemy who speaks sweetly while imagining the pit.
cards.s_text: An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit: he will weep with his eyes, but if he find opportunity, he will not be satisfied with blood.
cards.t_text: He that hates dissembleth with his lips, and lays up deceit within him;

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:7 — *If you would get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him.* the same wisdom prudence ben Sira applies to charity in Sirach 12:6, that the Most High repays the ungodly, calls for proving a man before trusting him.
cards.s_text: For the Most High hates sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly, and keepeth them against the mighty day of their punishment.
cards.t_text: If you would get a friend, prove him first and be not hasty to credit him.

cards.note: Romans 12:20 — *Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head.* Sha'ul commands feeding the enemy; Sirach 12:4 is the guarded counterpart, 'Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.'
cards.s_text: Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.
cards.t_text: Therefore if your enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing you shall heap coals of fire on his head.

cards.note: Matthew 5:44 — *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* the Sermon presses doing-good outward to the enemy where Sirach 12:2 anchors the recompence in the Most High.
cards.s_text: Do good to the godly man, and you shall find a recompence; and if not from him, yet from the Most High.
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

cards.note: Proverbs 25:21 — *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:* the Tanakh root of beneficence that Sirach 12:1 frames with discernment of the recipient.
cards.s_text: When you will do good know to whom you do it; so shall you be thanked for your benefits.
cards.t_text: If your enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:

cards.note: Isaiah 3:15 — *What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) of hosts.* The rich eating up the poor in Sirach 13:19 is what Yahuah of hosts calls grinding the faces of the poor — and he enters judgment for it.
cards.s_text: As the wild ass is the lion’s prey in the wilderness: so the rich eat up the poor.
cards.t_text: What mean you that you beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) of hosts.

cards.note: Proverbs 14:20 — *The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich hath many friends.* When the rich man speaks all extol it but the poor man is dismissed (Sirach 13:23) — Proverbs already weighed this partiality of wealth.
cards.s_text: When a rich man speaks, every man holdeth his tongue, and, look, what he says, they extol it to the clouds: but if the poor man speak, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will help to overthrow him.
cards.t_text: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the rich has many friends.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:7 — *All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words, yet they are wanting to him.* The poor man rebuked and friendless in Sirach 13:22 is the very figure Proverbs describes — pursued with words, given no place.
cards.s_text: When a rich man is fallen, he has many helpers: he speaks things not to be spoken, and yet men justify him: the poor man slipped, and yet they rebuked him too; he spoke wisely, and could have no place.
cards.t_text: All the brethren of the poor do hate him: how much more do his friends go far from him? he pursueth them with words, yet they are wanting to him.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:4 — *Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.* The proverb behind Sirach 13:22 — the fallen rich man finds many helpers, the poor man is left alone.
cards.s_text: When a rich man is fallen, he has many helpers: he speaks things not to be spoken, and yet men justify him: the poor man slipped, and yet they rebuked him too; he spoke wisely, and could have no place.
cards.t_text: Wealth makes many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.

cards.note: Isaiah 65:25 — *The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent’s meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith Yahuah (LORD).* In the new creation the wolf and lamb of Sirach 13:17 finally have fellowship — Yahuah undoes the law of predatory kind.
cards.s_text: What fellowship has the wolf with the lamb? so the sinner with the godly.
cards.t_text: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent’s meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, says Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Isaiah 11:6 — *The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.* The wolf-and-lamb enmity Sirach 13:17 takes as fixed is exactly what the messianic mountain reverses.
cards.s_text: What fellowship has the wolf with the lamb? so the sinner with the godly.
cards.t_text: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 6:5 — *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* The Shema's first commandment stands behind Sirach 13:14 — love Yahuah all thy life, the one bond that never betrays.
cards.s_text: Love Yahuah (God) all your life, and call upon him for your salvation.
cards.t_text: And you shall love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.

cards.note: Habakkuk 2:6 — *Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!* The oppressor who lays up the poor man's words to hurt him (Sirach 13:12) has a woe laid up against his own increase.
cards.s_text: But cruelly he will lay up your words, and will not spare to do you hurt, and to put you in prison.
cards.t_text: Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increases that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!

cards.note: Proverbs 22:25 — *Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.* The snare of the powerful man's company in Proverbs is exactly the trap Sirach 13:11 names — his much communication is set to tempt and ensnare.
cards.s_text: Affect not to be made equal to him in talk, and believe not his many words: for with much communication will he tempt you, and smiling upon you will get out your secrets:
cards.t_text: Lest you learn his ways, and get a snare to your soul.

cards.note: Isaiah 3:14 — *Yahuah (LORD) will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.* Yahuah himself enters into judgment for the spoil of the poor — the answer to the rich man's wrong in Sirach 13:3.
cards.s_text: The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threateneth withal: the poor is wronged, and he must intreat also.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for you have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.

cards.note: Amos 5:11 — *Forasmuch therefore as your treading is upon the poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.* The prophetic sentence on the rich who tread the poor — the wrong of Sirach 13:3 does not go unjudged.
cards.s_text: The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threateneth withal: the poor is wronged, and he must intreat also.
cards.t_text: Forasmuch therefore as your treading is upon the poor, and you take from him burdens of wheat: you have built houses of hewn stone, but you shall not dwell in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink wine of them.

cards.note: James 2:6 — *But ye have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?* James, the NT's closest sibling to Sirach, indicts the very oppression Sirach 13:3 describes — the rich wrong and drag, the poor must plead.
cards.s_text: The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threateneth withal: the poor is wronged, and he must intreat also.
cards.t_text: But you have despised the poor. Do not rich men oppress you, and draw you before the judgment seats?

cards.note: Proverbs 22:7 — *The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.* The bare wisdom-fact behind Sirach 13:3 — the rich man rules, so he can wrong and still threaten while the poor must entreat.
cards.s_text: The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threateneth withal: the poor is wronged, and he must intreat also.
cards.t_text: The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 27:9 — *The birds will resort to their like; so will truth return to them that practise in her.* Ben Sira's own like-to-like principle elsewhere in his book — the same law of company that makes touching pitch (Sirach 13:1) defile.
cards.s_text: He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled with it; and he that has fellowship with a proud man shall be like to him.
cards.t_text: The birds will resort to their like; so will truth return to them that practise in her.

cards.note: Psalms 1:1 — *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* The blessing for the man who keeps clear of the scornful's seat — the positive of Sirach 13:1's warning against fellowship with the proud.
cards.s_text: He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled with it; and he that has fellowship with a proud man shall be like to him.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of the scornful.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:24 — *Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:* the Torah-wisdom Ben Sira inherits — avoid the proud and furious man's fellowship lest Sirach 13:1's defilement take hold.
cards.s_text: He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled with it; and he that has fellowship with a proud man shall be like to him.
cards.t_text: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man you shall not go:

cards.note: 1 Corinthians 15:33 — *Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.* Paul's one-line proverb is Ben Sira's pitch by another name — bad fellowship corrupts, so Sirach 13:1 warns it defiles.
cards.s_text: He that toucheth pitch shall be defiled with it; and he that has fellowship with a proud man shall be like to him.
cards.t_text: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Ben Sira's own personified Wisdom completes Sirach 14:27 — the man covered in her glory is welcomed to her fruits.
cards.s_text: By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:18 — *She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her.* The branches under which the seeker lodges in Sirach 14:26 are the tree of life that is Wisdom.
cards.s_text: He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches.
cards.t_text: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:34 — *Blessed is the man that heareth me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.* Wisdom's own beatitude on the watcher at her doors mirrors Sirach 14:23, who hearkens at her doors.
cards.s_text: He that prieth in at her windows shall also hearken at her doors.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that hears me, watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.

cards.note: Psalm 1:2 — *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night.* The blessed meditation in wisdom of Sirach 14:20 is the Torah-delight of the Psalter's blessed man.
cards.s_text: Blessed is the man that does meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.
cards.t_text: But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law does he meditate day and night.

cards.note: James 1:10 — *But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.* Sirach's nearest NT kin turns the waxing-old of all flesh (Sirach 14:17) on the rich man who hoards.
cards.s_text: All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death.
cards.t_text: But the rich, in that he is made low: because as the flower of the grass he shall pass away.

cards.note: 1 Peter 1:24 — *For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth away:* Peter echoes the same generation-of-flesh that comes to an end in Sirach 14:18.
cards.s_text: As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one comes to an end, and another is born.
cards.t_text: For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withereth, and the flower thereof falls away:

cards.note: Isaiah 40:6 — *The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:* the prophet's fading-flower of flesh matches the falling leaves of Sirach 14:18.
cards.s_text: As of the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one comes to an end, and another is born.
cards.t_text: The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:

cards.note: Genesis 3:19 — *In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.* This is the covenant from the beginning Ben Sira cites in Sirach 14:17 — you shall die the death.
cards.s_text: All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death.
cards.t_text: In the sweat of your face shall you eat bread, till you return unto the ground; for out of it were you taken: for dust you are, and unto dust shall you return.

cards.note: Matthew 6:20 — *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:* the Sermon turns Sirach 14:13's almsgiving-before-death into treasure stored past the grave.
cards.s_text: Do good to your friend before you die, and according to your ability stretch out your hand and give to him.
cards.t_text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

cards.note: Proverbs 11:25 — *The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.* The blessing on the outstretched hand of Sirach 14:13.
cards.s_text: Do good to your friend before you die, and according to your ability stretch out your hand and give to him.
cards.t_text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

cards.note: *My son, according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.* (Ecclesiasticus 14:11). *And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) hath taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Job 1:21). Sirach says to do good to yourself as you are able and to give Yahuah (God) his due offering, and his very next line is the reason: death will not be long in coming. Job said at the ash heap what Sirach is building on — a man comes naked and goes back naked, and what he had in between was Yahuah's (God's) to give and to take. Everything in the hand is on loan. Give the Giver his due while it is still in your hand to give.
cards.s_text: My son, according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.
cards.t_text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) has taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:7 — *For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.* Paul states the very ground of Sirach 14:16 — there is no seeking of dainties in the grave.
cards.s_text: Give, and take, and sanctify your soul; for there is no seeking of dainties in the grave.
cards.t_text: For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 5:15 — *As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.* Because nothing follows into the grave, Sirach 14:16 urges giving and sanctifying the soul now.
cards.s_text: Give, and take, and sanctify your soul; for there is no seeking of dainties in the grave.
cards.t_text: As he came forth of his mother’s womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:24 — *There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.* The generous opposite of the niggard who gathers only for others in Sirach 14:4.
cards.s_text: He that gathers by defrauding his own soul gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
cards.t_text: There is that scatters, and yet increases; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.

cards.note: Psalm 49:6 — *They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches;* the never-satisfied covetous eye of Sirach 14:9 is the soul that trusts in wealth that cannot redeem it.
cards.s_text: A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul.
cards.t_text: They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches;

cards.note: Luke 12:20 — *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* The wealth gathered by defrauding the soul (Sirach 14:4) passes to another the very night the hoarder dies.
cards.s_text: He that gathers by defrauding his own soul gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) said unto him, You fool, this night your soul shall be required of you: then whose shall those things be, which you have provided?

cards.note: Luke 12:19 — *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.* The rich fool gathers for others to spend, exactly the self-defrauding hoarder of Sirach 14:4.
cards.s_text: He that gathers by defrauding his own soul gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
cards.t_text: And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have much goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 5:10 — *He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.* Qoheleth names the same unsatisfied covetous eye Ben Sira condemns in Sirach 14:3,9.
cards.s_text: Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an envious man do with money?
cards.t_text: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.

cards.note: Psalm 1:1 — *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* The Psalter's opening beatitude on the man of clear conscience answers Ben Sira's blessing in Sirach 14:2.
cards.s_text: Blessed is he whose conscience has not condemned him, and who is not fallen from his hope in Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of the scornful.

cards.note: James 3:2 — *For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.* James, Sirach's nearest NT kin, makes the un-slipped tongue of Sirach 14:1 the mark of the perfect man.
cards.s_text: Blessed is the man that has not slipped with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sins.
cards.t_text: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:3 — *He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.* The same wisdom Ben Sira blesses in Sirach 14:1, the guarded mouth that does not slip into the multitude of sins.
cards.s_text: Blessed is the man that has not slipped with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sins.
cards.t_text: He that keeps his mouth keeps his life: but he that opens wide his lips shall have destruction.

cards.note: James 1:15 — *Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.* *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin* (Ecclesiasticus 15:20); sin is born of a man's own conceived lust, not of any divine warrant.
cards.s_text: He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.
cards.t_text: Then when lust has conceived, it brings forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, brings forth death.

cards.note: Romans 2:6 — *Who will render to every man according to his deeds.* Because Yahuah *knoweth every work of man* (Sirach 15:19), Paul says he renders to every man by those works.
cards.s_text: And his eyes are upon them that fear him, and he knoweth every work of man.
cards.t_text: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:

cards.note: *For the wisdom of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things:* (Ecclesiasticus 15:18). *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.* (Proverbs 15:3). Sirach says the wisdom of Yahuah (God) beholds all things and his power is great. Solomon put the same truth in one line: his eyes are in every place, on the evil and the good alike. The verses before this in Sirach say life and death are set before a man and he will be given what he chooses; the all-seeing eye is why the choice is weighed and not forgotten.
cards.s_text: For the wisdom of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things:
cards.t_text: The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

cards.note: Psalms 139:1 — *O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast searched me, and known me.* The Yahuah who *beholds all things* (Sirach 15:18) is David's God who has searched and known him.
cards.s_text: For the wisdom of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things:
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (LORD), you have searched me, and known me.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 11:26 — *Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse.* 'If you will, to keep the commandments' (Sirach 15:15) is the blessing-and-curse Moses sets before the keeper of the law.
cards.s_text: If you will, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.
cards.t_text: Behold, I set before you this day a blessing and a curse;

cards.note: Joshua 24:15 — *And if it seem evil unto you to serve Yahuah (LORD), choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahuah (LORD).* 'stretch forth your hand to whether you will' (Sirach 15:16) is Joshua's 'choose you this day' — fire and water before the will.
cards.s_text: He has set fire and water before you: stretch forth your hand to whether you will.
cards.t_text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve Yahuah (LORD), choose you this day whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Genesis 4:7 — *If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.* Man left *in the hand of his counsel* (Sirach 15:14) is Cain told he can yet rule over sin — the will is his.
cards.s_text: He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsel;
cards.t_text: If you do well, shall you not be accepted? and if you do not well, sin lies at the door. And unto you shall be his desire, and you shall rule over him.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.* 'whether him liketh shall be given him' (Sirach 15:17) is Moses' 'therefore choose life' — the will set free to choose.
cards.s_text: Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.
cards.t_text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both you and your seed may live:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil.* Sirach's 'Before man is life and death' (Sirach 15:17) is Moses' charge set before Israel verbatim in theme.
cards.s_text: Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.
cards.t_text: See, I have set before you this day life and good, and death and evil;

cards.note: Psalms 5:4 — *For thou art not a Elohim (God) that hath pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with thee.* Yahuah *hates all abomination* in Sirach 15:13 because no evil can dwell with him.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) hates all abomination; and they that fear Yahuah (God) love it not.
cards.t_text: For you are not a Elohim (God) that has pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with you.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 — *For Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* The companion wisdom book on the same restored shelf seals Sirach 15:11 — Yahuah is no author of the fall or of death.
cards.s_text: Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.

cards.note: James 1:14 — *But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.* Against Sirach's 'He has caused me to err' (Sirach 15:12), James names the true cause: a man's own lust, not Elohim.
cards.s_text: Say not you, He has caused me to err: for he has no need of the sinful man.
cards.t_text: But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.

cards.note: James 1:13 — *Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of Elohim (God): for Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man.* James's 'let no man say' is Ben Sira's 'Say not... it is through Yahuah that I fell away' (Sirach 15:11) — almost word for word.
cards.s_text: Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.
cards.t_text: Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of Elohim (God): for Elohim (God) cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man:

cards.note: Matthew 15:8 — *This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.* Praise unseemly in a sinner's mouth (Sirach 15:9) is the lip-honour without the heart that the Messiah rebukes.
cards.s_text: Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent him of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: This people draws nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:10 — *Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.* That the proud and the liars cannot remember her (Sirach 15:8) is Solomon's pairing of pride against wisdom.
cards.s_text: For she is far from pride, and men that are liars cannot remember her.
cards.t_text: Only by pride comes contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:18 — *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.* Wisdom is *far from pride* in Sirach 15:8 because pride is the very road to ruin Proverbs charts.
cards.s_text: For she is far from pride, and men that are liars cannot remember her.
cards.t_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

cards.note: James 1:5 — *If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.* Sirach's nursing-mother wisdom who feeds the seeker (Sirach 15:3) is James's wisdom freely given to whoever asks — Sirach's closest NT sibling.
cards.s_text: With the bread of understanding shall she feed him, and give him the water of wisdom to drink.
cards.t_text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that gives to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:13 — *Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, and the man that getteth understanding.* The man fed *the bread of understanding* in Sirach 15:3 is the happy man who finds wisdom in Proverbs.
cards.s_text: With the bread of understanding shall she feed him, and give him the water of wisdom to drink.
cards.t_text: Happy is the man that finds wisdom, and the man that gets understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 2:5 — *Then shalt thou understand the fear of Yahuah (LORD), and find the knowledge of Elohim (God).* Knowledge of the law in Sirach 15:1 yields the fear of Yahuah and the knowledge of Elohim.
cards.s_text: He that fears Yahuah (God) will do good, and he that has the knowledge of the law shall obtain her.
cards.t_text: Then shall you understand the fear of Yahuah (LORD), and find the knowledge of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* The fear of Yahuah that 'will do good' and obtains wisdom in Sirach 15:1 is the very beginning of wisdom in Proverbs.
cards.s_text: He that fears Yahuah (God) will do good, and he that has the knowledge of the law shall obtain her.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* Ben Sira's opening — he that fears Yahuah and knows the law obtains wisdom — is Solomon's own first principle (Sirach 15:1).
cards.s_text: He that fears Yahuah (God) will do good, and he that has the knowledge of the law shall obtain her.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:8 — *When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The ancient ordering of peoples whose proud breakers, like the wicked kindred of Sirach 16:4, become desolate.
cards.s_text: For by one that has understanding shall the city be replenished: but the kindred of the wicked shall speedily become desolate.
cards.t_text: When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:13). *Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.* (Ecclesiasticus 16:8). Sirach's own proof case for pride comes later in his book: the place where Lot sojourned was not spared, and the reason he gives is their pride. The verse here says pride pours out abomination and brings strange calamities; the later verse names the city it happened to. Sodom is not a story about one sin. It is where pride ends when it is left to pour.
cards.s_text: Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
cards.t_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:18 — *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.* Solomon's law of pride is precisely why Sodom was abhorred for its pride in Sirach 16:8.
cards.s_text: Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
cards.t_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

cards.note: Revelation 22:12 — *And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.* The returning King rewards as Sirach 16:14 promises: every man according to his works.
cards.s_text: Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.
cards.t_text: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.

cards.note: Matthew 16:27 — *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* Yahusha names the same judgment-by-works that Sirach 16:12 ascribes to Yahuah.
cards.s_text: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judges a man according to his works
cards.t_text: For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.

cards.note: Galatians 6:7 — *Be not deceived; Elohim (God) is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.* Paul's sowing-and-reaping matches Sirach 16:14: every man finds according to his works.
cards.s_text: Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.
cards.t_text: Be not deceived; Elohim (God) is not mocked: for whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap.

cards.note: Romans 9:18 — *Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.* Paul's conclusion matching Sirach 16:15's claim that Yahuah hardened Pharaoh to make his power known.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.
cards.t_text: Therefore has he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.

cards.note: Romans 9:17 — *For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.* Paul quoting the same purpose Sirach 16:15 reads in the hardening of Pharaoh.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.
cards.t_text: For the scripture says unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised you up, that I might shew my power in you, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 9:16 — *And in very deed for this cause have I raised thee up, for to shew in thee my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.* The Torah purpose behind Sirach 16:15's hardening of Pharaoh that his works be known.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerful works might be known to the world.
cards.t_text: And in very deed for this cause have I raised you up, for to shew in you my power; and that my name may be declared throughout all the earth.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:12 — *For who shall say, What have you done? or who shall withstand your judgment? or who shall accuse you for the nations that perish, whom you made? or who shall come to stand against you, to be revenged for the unrighteous men?* The live wisdom sibling pressing the same inescapable judgment Sirach 16:17 sets before the hidden soul.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will hide myself from Yahuah (God): shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?
cards.t_text: For who shall say, What have you done? or who shall withstand your judgment? or who shall accuse you for the nations that perish, whom you made? or who shall come to stand against you, to be revenged for the unrighteous men?

cards.note: Romans 1:20 — *For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:* the creation that makes Sirach 16:17's hiding impossible and leaves none excused.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will hide myself from Yahuah (God): shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?
cards.t_text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

cards.note: Psalm 139:11 — *If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.* No darkness conceals the man who imagines himself forgotten in Sirach 16:17.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will hide myself from Yahuah (God): shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?
cards.t_text: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me.

cards.note: Psalm 139:7 — *Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?* David's question is exactly the conceit Sirach 16:17 forbids — there is no hiding from Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will hide myself from Yahuah (God): shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembered among so many people: for what is my soul among such an infinite number of creatures?
cards.t_text: Whither shall I go from your spirit? or whither shall I flee from your presence?

cards.note: 1 Enoch 10:15 — *And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.* The decree of judgment behind Sirach 16:7's giants who fell away unpacified.
cards.s_text: He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness.
cards.t_text: And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.

cards.note: 1 Enoch 7:2 — *And they became pregnant, and they bare great giants, whose height was three thousand ells:* the live Watchers narrative supplying the begetting of the giants Sirach 16:7 names.
cards.s_text: He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness.
cards.t_text: And they became pregnant, and they bare great giants, whose height was three thousand ells:

cards.note: Genesis 6:4 — *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* The canonical root of Sirach 16:7's old giants.
cards.s_text: He was not pacified toward the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishness.
cards.t_text: There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:7 — *Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.* The Mosaic charge to recall the old judgments that Sirach 16:6 puts to use against the ungodly congregation.
cards.s_text: In the congregation of the ungodly shall a fire be kindled; and in a rebellious nation wrath is set on fire.
cards.t_text: Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask your father, and he will shew you; your elders, and they will tell you.

cards.note: Numbers 16:32 — *And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.* The hard-hearted multitude of Sirach 16:10 that perished in the wilderness rebellion.
cards.s_text: Nor the six hundred thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
cards.t_text: And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods.

cards.note: Genesis 19:24 — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* this is the place where Lot sojourned, abhorred for its pride in Sirach 16:8.
cards.s_text: Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
cards.t_text: Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;

cards.note: Genesis 1:26 — *And Elohim (God) said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.* Sirach 17:3-4 names the very image-and-dominion grant of the sixth day.
cards.s_text: He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 2:7 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.* Sirach 17:1 'created man of the earth, and turned him into it again' is Genesis 2:7 read with Genesis 3:19.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (God) created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

cards.note: Genesis 9:2 — *And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moveth upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.* Sirach 17:4 'put the fear of man upon all flesh' is the Noahic dominion-grant verbatim.
cards.s_text: And put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls.
cards.t_text: And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every fowl of the air, upon all that moves upon the earth, and upon all the fishes of the sea; into your hand are they delivered.

cards.note: Psalms 8:6 — *Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet:* the dominion Sirach 17:4 gives over beasts and fowls is the dominion David sings.
cards.s_text: And put the fear of man upon all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and fowls.
cards.t_text: You made him to have dominion over the works of your hands; you have put all things under his feet:

cards.note: Psalms 8:5 — *For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.* The man made 'according to his image' (Sirach 17:3) is the man crowned with glory and honour.
cards.s_text: He endued them with strength by themselves, and made them according to his image,
cards.t_text: For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and have crowned him with glory and honour.

cards.note: Exodus 19:5 — *Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:* the 'everlasting covenant' of Sirach 17:12 is the Sinai covenant offered to Israel.
cards.s_text: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, if you will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then you shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:

cards.note: Exodus 24:8 — *And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you concerning all these words.* The covenant Sirach 17:12 calls everlasting is the blood-ratified covenant of Sinai.
cards.s_text: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.
cards.t_text: And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) has made with you concerning all these words.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* the 'law of life' of Sirach 17:11 is Moses' choose-life Torah.
cards.s_text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
cards.t_text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both you and your seed may live:

cards.note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* The everlasting covenant of Sirach 17:12 is the law written on the heart — same Torah, kept inwardly.
cards.s_text: He made an everlasting covenant with them, and shewed them his judgments.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* Ben Sira's own crown-chapter identifies the 'law of life for an heritage' (Sirach 17:11) as the Torah and the book of the covenant.
cards.s_text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
cards.t_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.

cards.note: Romans 2:14 — *For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:* the heart 'shewed... good and evil' in Sirach 17:7 is Paul's law written in the conscience.
cards.s_text: Withal he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, and shewed them good and evil.
cards.t_text: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:

cards.note: Baruch 4:1 — *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* Baruch names the 'law of life for an heritage' (Sirach 17:11) the enduring commandment by which one lives.
cards.s_text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
cards.t_text: This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* the heart and counsel given to understand good and evil (Sirach 17:6) equip man for Moses' life-and-death choice.
cards.s_text: Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, gave he them to understand.
cards.t_text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both you and your seed may live:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:8 — *When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Sirach 17:17's division of the nations with Israel kept apart is the Song of Moses verbatim.
cards.s_text: For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Yashar'el (Israel) is the portion of Yahuah (God):
cards.t_text: When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:9 — *For the LORD'S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.* 'Israel is the portion of Yahuah' (Sirach 17:17) repeats Moses' word for word.
cards.s_text: For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Yashar'el (Israel) is the portion of Yahuah (God):
cards.t_text: For the LORD’S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.

cards.note: Acts 17:26 — *And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;* Paul preaches the same set bounds of the nations Sirach 17:17 names.
cards.s_text: For in the division of the nations of the whole earth he set a ruler over every people; but Yashar'el (Israel) is the portion of Yahuah (God):
cards.t_text: And has made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and has determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;

cards.note: Hebrews 4:13 — *Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.* Sirach 17:15 'their ways... shall not be hid from his eyes' is the same all-seeing scrutiny.
cards.s_text: Their ways are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.
cards.t_text: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

cards.note: Matthew 16:27 — *For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* The Messiah's coming recompense matches Sirach 17:23, 'render their recompence upon their heads.'
cards.s_text: Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads.
cards.t_text: For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.

cards.note: Revelation 22:12 — *And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.* The reward rendered upon every head in Sirach 17:23 is the reward carried at the Coming.
cards.s_text: Afterwards he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompence upon their heads.
cards.t_text: And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be.

cards.note: *Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:26). *Therefore I will judge you, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), every one according to his ways, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD). Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.* (Ezekiel 18:30). Sirach says to turn again to the Most High and away from iniquity, and promises light at the end of it. Ezekiel says the same to the house of Yashar'el (Israel): repent, turn from your transgressions, so iniquity shall not be your ruin. The turn is what keeps iniquity from being the end of the story. Judgment according to a man's ways and the open call to turn stand in the same verse because they are the same mercy.
cards.s_text: Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.
cards.t_text: Therefore I will judge you, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), every one according to his ways, says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD). Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.

cards.note: *But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:24). *For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD): wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.* (Ezekiel 18:32). Sirach says return is granted to them that repent. Ezekiel heard the heart behind it: Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) has no pleasure in the death of the one who dies, and so he calls, turn yourselves, and live. The granting of return is not reluctant. It is what he wanted all along.
cards.s_text: But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.
cards.t_text: For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dies, says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD): wherefore turn yourselves, and live you.

cards.note: 2 Peter 3:9 — *Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.* The great lovingkindness toward those that turn (Sirach 17:29) is Peter's longsuffering unto repentance.
cards.s_text: How great is the lovingkindness of Yahuah (God), our Elohim (God), and his compassion to such as turn to him in holiness!
cards.t_text: Yahuah (Lord) is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

cards.note: *Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:25). *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.* (James 4:8). Sirach says to return, forsake sins, pray before his face, and offend less. James says to draw nigh to Elohim (God) and he will draw nigh to you, and he says it to sinners with unclean hands and double minds. Both put the turning first and the nearness after. The prayer before his face and the drawing nigh are one movement, and both expect the hands to be cleansed on the way.
cards.s_text: Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less.
cards.t_text: Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners; and purify your hearts, you double minded.

cards.note: Luke 15:7 — *I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.* The return granted to them that repent (Sirach 17:24) is the heaven-joy over one sinner turning.
cards.s_text: But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.
cards.t_text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

cards.note: Psalms 6:5 — *For in death there is no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?* Sirach 17:27 'who shall praise the Most High in the grave' is David's question word for word.
cards.s_text: Who shall praise the Most High in the grave, instead of them which live and give thanks?
cards.t_text: For in death there is no remembrance of you: in the grave who shall give you thanks?

cards.note: Psalms 115:17 — *The dead praise not Yahuah (LORD), neither any that go down into silence.* Sirach 17:28 'thanksgiving perishes from the dead' is the same silence of the grave.
cards.s_text: Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart shall praise Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The dead praise not Yahuah (LORD), neither any that go down into silence.

cards.note: Romans 13:14 — *But put ye on the Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ), and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.* The borrowed banqueting that ensnares the soul in Sirach 18:33 is the flesh-provision Sha'ul forbids.
cards.s_text: Be not made a beggar by banqueting upon borrowing, when you have nothing in your purse: for you shall lie in wait for your own life, and be talked on.
cards.t_text: But put you on Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.

cards.note: *Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:30). *This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.* (Galatians 5:16). Sirach tells his son to refrain himself from his appetites rather than follow his lusts. Paul tells the Galatians how that refraining is done: walk in the Spirit, and the lust of the flesh will not be fulfilled. The Spirit does not loosen the standard Sirach set; he supplies the strength to keep it. Walking in the Spirit is the way a man refrains himself, and the commandments are where that walk goes.
cards.s_text: Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.
cards.t_text: This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and you shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.

cards.note: Luke 12:21 — *So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God).* Yahusha's verdict on the fool is Sirach 18:25's counsel: in riches think upon poverty and need.
cards.s_text: When you have enough, remember the time of hunger: and when you are rich, think upon poverty and need.
cards.t_text: So is he that lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God).

cards.note: Luke 12:19 — *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry.* The rich fool's ease is the very forgetfulness Sirach 18:25 warns against — when full, remember the time of hunger.
cards.s_text: When you have enough, remember the time of hunger: and when you are rich, think upon poverty and need.
cards.t_text: And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have much goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.

cards.note: Matthew 26:41 — *Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.* Preparing before prayer in Sirach 18:23 is Yahusha's watch-and-pray, not the presumption that tempts the LORD.
cards.s_text: Before you prayest, prepare thyself; and be not as one that tempteth Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Watch and pray, that you enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:13 — *He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.* Mishle is the source of Sirach 18:19's counsel to learn before you speak.
cards.s_text: Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.
cards.t_text: He that answers a matter before he hears it, it is folly and shame unto him.
