cards.note: *Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:19). *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:* (James 1:19). Sirach puts learning before speaking the way a wise man takes his medicine before the sickness comes — the order matters. James says the same in three strokes: swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. Both put the ear ahead of the mouth, and both treat it as wisdom you practice before the moment arrives, not after.
cards.s_text: Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 5:5 — *Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.* The unpaid vow Sirach 18:22 forbids is the very fault Qoheleth names worse than never vowing.
cards.s_text: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.
cards.t_text: Better is it that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay.

cards.note: *Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:22). *When thou vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.* (Ecclesiastes 5:4). Solomon wrote the rule: a vow made to Elohim (God) is to be paid without delay, because he has no pleasure in fools. Sirach is holding that rule when he tells his son to let nothing hinder the paying of a vow in due time, and he presses it one step further — do not put off until death the matter of being justified before Yahuah (God). The vow deferred and the turning deferred are the same folly.
cards.s_text: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.
cards.t_text: When you vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which you have vowed.

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when you give any thing.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:15). Tobit warns against the envious eye when giving; Sirach warns against the sour word. Both know that a gift can be spoiled by the spirit it comes in. The alms Yahuah (God) looks on is given gladly, without a grudging eye and without a hard word to the one who receives it.
cards.s_text: My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when you give any thing.
cards.t_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:21 — *Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.* A gracious word better than a gift in Sirach 18:17 trades on the tongue's life-and-death power Mishle weighs.
cards.s_text: Lo, is not a word better than a gift? but both are with a gracious man.
cards.t_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

cards.note: Matthew 6:3 — *But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth.* Yahusha's hidden alms is Sirach 18:15's unblemished giving without uncomfortable words.
cards.s_text: My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when you give any thing.
cards.t_text: But when you do alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand does:

cards.note: Matthew 6:2 — *Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men.* The trumpeted alms is the blemished good deed Sirach 18:15 warns against.
cards.s_text: My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when you give any thing.
cards.t_text: Therefore when you do your alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.

cards.note: Lamentations 3:22 — *It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.* The mercy upon all flesh in Sirach 18:13 is the unfailing compassion that keeps Yashar'el from being consumed.
cards.s_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.
cards.t_text: It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:12 — *For whom Yahuah (LORD) loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.* Mishle is the wellspring of Sirach 18:14's mercy on them that receive discipline.
cards.s_text: He has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.
cards.t_text: For whom Yahuah (LORD) loves he corrects; even as a father the son in whom he delights.

cards.note: Hebrews 12:6 — *For whom Yahuah (Lord) loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.* The discipline received in Sirach 18:14 is the Father's loving chastening, not curse — He has mercy on them that receive it.
cards.s_text: He has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seek after his judgments.
cards.t_text: For whom Yahuah (Lord) loves he chastens, and scourgeth every son whom he receives.

cards.note: Psalm 103:13 — *Like as a father pitieth his children, so Yahuah (LORD) pitieth them that fear him.* The shepherd-mercy of Sirach 18:13 is the Father's pity the Psalmist sings.
cards.s_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.
cards.t_text: Like as a father pitieth his children, so Yahuah (LORD) pitieth them that fear him.

cards.note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:13). *Yahuah (LORD) is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.* (Psalm 145:9). David sang it first: Yahuah (LORD) is good to all, and his tender mercies rest over everything he has made. Sirach sets the same truth beside the mercy of a man, which reaches only his neighbour, and shows how much wider the mercy of Yahuah (God) runs — over all flesh, as a shepherd over the whole flock. The psalm and the wisdom book are saying one thing in two voices.
cards.s_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.

cards.note: Psalm 103:16 — *For the wind passeth over it, and it is gone; and the place thereof shall know it no more.* Man's few days in Sirach 18:9 pass like grass over which the wind blows and is gone.
cards.s_text: The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.
cards.t_text: For the wind passes over it, and it is gone; and the place thereof shall know it no more.

cards.note: *The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:9). *As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.* (Psalm 103:15). Sirach puts the limit on a man's days at a hundred years at the most, and in the next verse calls a thousand years a drop of water to the sea beside eternity. David says man's days are as grass and he flourishes as a flower of the field. A hundred years and a flower's season are the same length against eternity, and both writers say it so the reader will spend them rightly.
cards.s_text: The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.
cards.t_text: As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.

cards.note: 2 Peter 3:8 — *But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.* Kepha carries Sirach 18:10's eternity-scale into the patience of the LORD before the day of judgment.
cards.s_text: As a drop of water to the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.
cards.t_text: But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with Yahuah (Lord) as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

cards.note: Psalm 90:4 — *For a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.* The Psalmist measures a thousand years against the Eternal exactly as Sirach 18:10 measures it a drop to the sea.
cards.s_text: As a drop of water to the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity.
cards.t_text: For a thousand years in your sight are but as yesterday when it is past, and as a watch in the night.

cards.note: Matthew 12:34 — *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* Sira's 'knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom' meets Yeshua's verdict: the evil heart cannot counterfeit good speech for long.
cards.s_text: The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, neither at any time the counsel of sinners prudence.
cards.t_text: O generation of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

cards.note: James 3:6 — *And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.* James names the 'exquisite subtilty that is unjust' for what it is — the unbridled tongue set on fire of hell, not wisdom.
cards.s_text: There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is unjust; and there is one that turns aside to make judgment appear; and there is a wise man that justifies in judgment.
cards.t_text: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

cards.note: *A man may be known by his look, and one that has understanding by his countenance, when you meetest him.* (Ecclesiasticus 19:29). *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?* (Matthew 7:16). Sirach says a man can be known by his look, and a man of understanding by his countenance, before he has said a word. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the surer test: you will know them by their fruits, because thorns do not yield grapes. Both say the same thing about the inward man — what is in him comes out where it can be seen, whether in the face or in the fruit.
cards.s_text: A man may be known by his look, and one that has understanding by his countenance, when you meetest him.
cards.t_text: You shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

cards.note: Baruch 4:1 — *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* Sira's 'performance of the law' as all wisdom is Baruch's enduring law that brings life to all who keep it.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
cards.t_text: This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 1:14 — *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.* Sira's own prologue self-witnesses the maxim he repeats here in chapter 19.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.* Sira's 'doctrine of life' and 'tree of immortality' are Moses' choose-life: keeping the commandments IS choosing life.
cards.s_text: The knowledge of the commandments of Yahuah (God) is the doctrine of life: and they that do things that please him shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.
cards.t_text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both you and your seed may live:

cards.note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* Word for word the maxim Sira states as 'the fear of Yahuah (God) is all wisdom.'
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* Sira's 'first step to be accepted of him' is Solomon's 'beginning of knowledge' — the fear of Yahuah as the door.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is the first step to be accepted of him, and wisdom obtaineth his love.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Proverbs 17:9 — *He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.* Sira's 'believe not every tale' and private admonition is Solomon's covering, not repeating, of a matter.
cards.s_text: Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.
cards.t_text: He that covers a transgression seeks love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

cards.note: Matthew 18:15 — *Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.* Yeshua's order of reproof is Sira's 'admonish a friend' — go to him first, privately.
cards.s_text: Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.
cards.t_text: Moreover if your brother shall trespass against you, go and tell him his fault between you and him alone: if he shall hear you, you have gained your brother.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:17 — *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.* The 'law of the Most High' Sira sends you back to: rebuke the neighbour rather than harbour the grudge.
cards.s_text: Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him; and not being angry, give place to the law of the Most High.
cards.t_text: You shall not hate your brother in your heart: you shall in any wise rebuke your neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 10:20 — *Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.* As Sira warns 'he heard and observed you,' Qoheleth warns that even secret speech is carried back.
cards.s_text: For he heard and observed you, and when time comes he will hate you.
cards.t_text: Curse not the king, no not in your thought; and curse not the rich in your bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:16 — *Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The Torah-command behind Sira's counsel not to talk of other men's lives.
cards.s_text: Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men’s lives; and if you can without offence, reveal them not.
cards.t_text: You shall not go up and down as a talebearer among your people: neither shall you stand against the blood of your neighbour: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 11:13 — *A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.* Sira's 'reveal them not' is Solomon's faithful spirit that conceals.
cards.s_text: Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other men’s lives; and if you can without offence, reveal them not.
cards.t_text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:28 — *A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.* The very harm Sira heads off by 'rehearse not' — the rehearsed tale that cleaves friend from friend.
cards.s_text: Rehearse not to another that which is told to you, and you shall fare never the worse.
cards.t_text: A froward man sows strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends.

cards.note: James 1:26 — *If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.* James names the unbridled tongue as Sira does, making rule of the mouth the test of true religion.
cards.s_text: He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife; and he that hates babbling shall have less evil.
cards.t_text: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.

cards.note: Matthew 12:36 — *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* Why let a word die with you? Because each idle one is answered for — Yeshua raises Sira's discretion to a day of reckoning.
cards.s_text: If you have heard a word, let it die with you; and be bold, it will not burst you.
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 10:12 — *The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.* Babbling devours its own speaker, exactly the 'less evil' Sira promises the man who hates it.
cards.s_text: He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife; and he that hates babbling shall have less evil.
cards.t_text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:21 — *Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.* The same weight Sira puts on ruling the tongue, Solomon hangs life and death upon.
cards.s_text: He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife; and he that hates babbling shall have less evil.
cards.t_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:5 — *Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.* The necessary patience in seeking Yahuah that Ben Sira commends in Sirach 20:32, over the man without a guide, is Solomon's trust in Yahuah rather than one's own understanding.
cards.s_text: Necessary patience in seeking Yahuah (God) is better than he that leadeth his life without a guide.
cards.t_text: Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all your heart; and lean not unto your own understanding.

cards.note: Matthew 25:18 — *But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.* The treasure hoarded up to no profit in Sirach 20:30 is the buried talent of the slothful servant in the Messiah's parable.
cards.s_text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
cards.t_text: But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money.

cards.note: Matthew 5:15 — *Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house.* The hidden wisdom that yields no profit in Sirach 20:30 is the Messiah's candle that must not be put under a bushel.
cards.s_text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
cards.t_text: Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it gives light unto all that are in the house.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 9:7 — *Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver.* Against the grudging giver of Sirach 20:15 who gives little and upbraideth much, Paul sets the cheerful giver Yahuah loves.
cards.s_text: He gives little, and upbraideth much; he opens his mouth like a crier; to day he lendeth, and to morrow will he ask it again: such an one is to be hated of Yahuah (God) and man.
cards.t_text: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for Elohim (God) loves a cheerful giver.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:6 — *Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:* the envious giver of Sirach 20:14, who looketh to receive many things for one, is Solomon's man of the evil eye whose gift profits nothing.
cards.s_text: The gift of a fool shall do you no good when you have it; neither yet of the envious for his necessity: for he looketh to receive many things for one.
cards.t_text: Eat you not the bread of him that has an evil eye, neither desire you his dainty meats:

cards.note: Revelation 21:27 — *And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.* The thief and the liar who in Sirach 20:25 have destruction to heritage are barred from the New Jerusalem, where no maker of a lie enters.
cards.s_text: A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.
cards.t_text: And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defiles, neither whatsoever works abomination, or makes a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

cards.note: Proverbs 12:22 — *Lying lips are abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but they that deal truly are his delight.* The liar's dishonourable disposition and ever-present shame in Sirach 20:26 is the abomination Solomon sets against Yahuah's delight in the truthful.
cards.s_text: The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.
cards.t_text: Lying lips are abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but they that deal truly are his delight.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:11 — *Ye shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.* The foul blot of the lie in Sirach 20:24 is forbidden in the same Holiness Code that frames Ben Sira's whole ethic of the tongue.
cards.s_text: A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught.
cards.t_text: You shall not steal, neither deal falsely, neither lie one to another.

cards.note: Proverbs 10:19 — *In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise.* The man who useth many words and is abhorred in Sirach 20:8 is the multitude-of-words wherein sin is not wanting.
cards.s_text: He that useth many words shall be abhorred; and he that takes to himself authority in it shall be hated.
cards.t_text: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refrains his lips is wise.

cards.note: Proverbs 25:11 — *A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.* The fitness of speech that Solomon prizes is the due season Ben Sira's fool fails in Sirach 20:20, rejecting even a wise sentence by speaking it untimely.
cards.s_text: A wise sentence shall be rejected when it comes out of a fool’s mouth; for he will not speak it in due season.
cards.t_text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:23 — *A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!* Solomon's praise of the timely word is Ben Sira's wise man of Sirach 20:7 who holds his tongue till he see opportunity.
cards.s_text: A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time.
cards.t_text: A man has joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!

cards.note: James 1:19 — *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:* James inherits Ben Sira's wisdom of the bridled tongue against the much babbling that becometh hateful in Sirach 20:5.
cards.s_text: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 3:7 — *A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;* the Preacher's appointed season for silence is exactly the man who in Sirach 20:6 keepeth silence, knowing his time.
cards.s_text: Some man holdeth his tongue, because he has not to answer: and some keepeth silence, knowing his time.
cards.t_text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

cards.note: *There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.* (Ecclesiasticus 20:5). *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.* (Proverbs 17:28). Solomon noticed that even a fool who holds his peace is counted wise. Sirach says it from the other side: one man keeps silence and is found wise, another babbles and makes himself hateful. Both are telling the same thing — the mouth gives a man away, and the one who can shut it is already halfway to understanding.
cards.s_text: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.
cards.t_text: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shuts his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:13 — *A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.* The babbling lips against the weighed words of the understanding (Ecclesiasticus 21:25).
cards.s_text: The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertain not to them: but the words of such as have understanding are weighed in the balance.
cards.t_text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

cards.note: James 3:6 — *And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.* The defiling fire of the tongue, the same self-defilement Ben Sira warns of (Ecclesiasticus 21:28).
cards.s_text: A whisperer defiles his own soul, and is hated wherever he dwells.
cards.t_text: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:22 — *The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.* The whisperer whose words wound, as Ben Sira says he defiles his own soul (Ecclesiasticus 21:28).
cards.s_text: A whisperer defiles his own soul, and is hated wherever he dwells.
cards.t_text: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:16 — *Thou shalt not go up and down as a talebearer among thy people: neither shalt thou stand against the blood of thy neighbour: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The Torah command against the very whisperer Ben Sira condemns (Ecclesiasticus 21:28).
cards.s_text: A whisperer defiles his own soul, and is hated wherever he dwells.
cards.t_text: You shall not go up and down as a talebearer among your people: neither shall you stand against the blood of your neighbour: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 17:28 — *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.* The weighed restraint that makes men seek the wise man's words in the congregation (Ecclesiasticus 21:17).
cards.s_text: They enquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.
cards.t_text: Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shuts his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 10:14 — *Wise men lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish is near destruction.* The laid-up wisdom against the fool's burdensome talk Ben Sira contrasts (Ecclesiasticus 21:16).
cards.s_text: The talking of a fool is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.
cards.t_text: Wise men lay up knowledge: but the mouth of the foolish is near destruction.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:23 — *The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.* The wise man whose mouth is governed from within his heart, as Ben Sira frames it (Ecclesiasticus 21:26).
cards.s_text: The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
cards.t_text: The heart of the wise teaches his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.

cards.note: Proverbs 29:11 — *A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterwards.* The fool whose heart is all in his mouth, where the wise keeps it in his heart (Ecclesiasticus 21:26).
cards.s_text: The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
cards.t_text: A fool utters all his mind: but a wise man keeps it in till afterwards.

cards.note: Matthew 12:34 — *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* Yahusha's word that the mouth pours out the heart, the very turn of Ben Sira's proverb (Ecclesiasticus 21:26).
cards.s_text: The heart of fools is in their mouth: but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
cards.t_text: O generation of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:24 — *The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.* The wise man's upward road against the sinner's pit, the same contrast Ben Sira draws (Ecclesiasticus 21:10).
cards.s_text: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell.
cards.t_text: The way of life is above to the wise, that he may depart from hell beneath.

cards.note: Psalm 1:1 — *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* The way of sinners Ben Sira says ends in the pit of hell (Ecclesiasticus 21:10).
cards.s_text: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the seat of the scornful.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil.* The two ways Moses set before Yashar'el, which Ben Sira draws as the smooth road to the pit versus the fountain of life (Ecclesiasticus 21:10,13).
cards.s_text: The way of sinners is made plain with stones, but at the end thereof is the pit of hell.
cards.t_text: See, I have set before you this day life and good, and death and evil;

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 24:23 — *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.* Ben Sira's own crown chapter names Wisdom as the Torah of Moses — the very law whose keeping is wisdom in 21:11.
cards.s_text: He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.
cards.t_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* The fear-of-Yahuah foundation Ben Sira sets under understanding (Ecclesiasticus 21:11).
cards.s_text: He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Psalm 111:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.* Wisdom bound to doing the commandments, exactly as Ben Sira binds it to keeping the law (Ecclesiasticus 21:11).
cards.s_text: He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endures for ever.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:11). *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* (Proverbs 9:10). Solomon set the foundation: the fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom. Sirach shows where it goes — the one who keeps the law of Yahuah (God) gets understanding of it, and the fear of Yahuah (God) brought to its perfection is wisdom itself. Fear is the beginning, keeping the law is the road, and wisdom is the crown of it. Understanding comes to the one who keeps, not to the one who only studies.
cards.s_text: He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: *My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:1). *Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.* (Proverbs 9:6). Wisdom's call in Proverbs is to forsake the foolish and live, and to walk in the way of understanding. Sirach opens his chapter with the same turn, put as a father puts it to a son — if you have sinned, do so no more, and ask pardon. Forsaking and turning are one motion; the way of understanding begins where the former sins are left behind.
cards.s_text: My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.
cards.t_text: Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.

cards.note: James 4:7 — *Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.* The way to flee the serpent Ben Sira describes (Ecclesiasticus 21:2).
cards.s_text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if you come too near it, it will bite you: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
cards.t_text: Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

cards.note: Genesis 4:7 — *If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.* The crouching sin Ben Sira bids us flee is the very beast the LORD set Cain to master (Ecclesiasticus 21:2).
cards.s_text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if you come too near it, it will bite you: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
cards.t_text: If you do well, shall you not be accepted? and if you do not well, sin lies at the door. And unto you shall be his desire, and you shall rule over him.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:32 — *At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.* The same serpent-bite figure Ben Sira uses for sin (Ecclesiasticus 21:2).
cards.s_text: Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent: for if you come too near it, it will bite you: the teeth thereof are as the teeth of a lion, slaying the souls of men.
cards.t_text: At the last it bites like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.

cards.note: James 3:8 — *But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.* Because no man can tame the tongue, Sirach 22:27 prays for a watch and a seal of wisdom from above.
cards.s_text: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?
cards.t_text: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

cards.note: James 3:5 — *Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!* The tongue Ben Sira fears will destroy him (Sirach 22:27) is James's little member that kindles a great fire.
cards.s_text: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?
cards.t_text: Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!

cards.note: Psalm 141:3 — *Set a watch, O Yahuah (LORD), before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.* Ben Sira's prayer in Sirach 22:27 is David's same plea for a guard set over the mouth.
cards.s_text: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?
cards.t_text: Set a watch, O Yahuah (LORD), before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 6:14 — *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* Ben Sira had already named the treasure that the upbraiding of Sirach 22:20 puts at risk.
cards.s_text: Whoso casteth a stone at the birds frayeth them away: and he that upbraideth his friend breaks friendship.
cards.t_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.

cards.note: Matthew 5:24 — *Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.* The returning to favour Ben Sira urges in Sirach 22:21 the Master sets before the very altar.
cards.s_text: Though you drewest a sword at your friend, yet despair not: for there may be a returning to favour.
cards.t_text: Leave there your gift before the altar, and go your way; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:19 — *A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.* The treacherous wound past which every friend departs (Sirach 22:22) is Solomon's offended brother, harder to win than a walled city.
cards.s_text: If you have opened your mouth against your friend, fear not; for there may be a reconciliation: except for upbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound: for for these things every friend will depart.
cards.t_text: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.

cards.note: Proverbs 27:6 — *Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.* Where Sirach 22:20 warns that upbraiding breaks friendship, Solomon distinguishes the faithful wound from the treacherous kiss.
cards.s_text: Whoso casteth a stone at the birds frayeth them away: and he that upbraideth his friend breaks friendship.
cards.t_text: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:14 — *As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.* The same disgraced sluggard of Sirach 22:1 turns idly on his bed in Solomon's proverb.
cards.s_text: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.
cards.t_text: As the door turns upon his hinges, so does the slothful upon his bed.

cards.note: Proverbs 6:11 — *So shall thy poverty come as one that travelleth, and thy want as an armed man.* The dunghill-filth of the sluggard in Sirach 22:2 ends in this ambush of want.
cards.s_text: A slothful man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: every man that takes it up will shake his hand.
cards.t_text: So shall your poverty come as one that travelleth, and your want as an armed man.

cards.note: Proverbs 6:6 — *Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise.* The slothful man hissed out as a filthy stone (Sirach 22:1) is sent to the ant to learn diligence.
cards.s_text: A slothful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hiss him out to his disgrace.
cards.t_text: Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

cards.note: Proverbs 27:3 — *A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath is heavier than them both.* The same scales of stone and sand weigh the unbearable fool of Sirach 22:15.
cards.s_text: Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, than a man without understanding.
cards.t_text: A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool’s wrath is heavier than them both.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:12 — *Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.* The same wisdom that bids Sirach 22:13 beware of the fool measures the deeper folly of self-conceit.
cards.s_text: Talk not much with a fool, and go not to him that has no understanding: beware of him, lest you have trouble, and you shall never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and you shall find rest, and never be disquieted with madness.
cards.t_text: See you a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:11 — *As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.* The fool is incorrigible, so Sirach 22:13 counsels: talk not much with him and depart from him.
cards.s_text: Talk not much with a fool, and go not to him that has no understanding: beware of him, lest you have trouble, and you shall never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and you shall find rest, and never be disquieted with madness.
cards.t_text: As a dog returns to his vomit, so a fool returns to his folly.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:1 — *As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.* Solomon and Ben Sira agree that the fool is past honour, his life worse than death (Sirach 22:11).
cards.s_text: Weep for the dead, for he has lost the light: and weep for the fool, for he wanteth understanding: make little weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: but the life of the fool is worse than death.
cards.t_text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:20 — *That thou mayest love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which Yahuah (LORD) sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.* Moses names the obedient cleaving as life and length of days — the same long life Sirach 23:28 promises the one received of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: It is great glory to follow Yahuah (God), and to be received of him is long life.
cards.t_text: That you may love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and that you may obey his voice, and that you may cleave unto him: for he is your life, and the length of your days: that you may dwell in the land which Yahuah (LORD) sware unto your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.

cards.note: Proverbs 12:3 — *A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.* Solomon names the very contrast of Sirach 23:25: the wicked take no root, but the righteous cannot be moved.
cards.s_text: Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.
cards.t_text: A man shall not be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be moved.

cards.note: Job 34:21 — *For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.* The same beholding eye brings the secret adulteress of Sirach 23:23, who disobeyed the law of the Most High, into the congregation for inquisition.
cards.s_text: For first, she has disobeyed the law of the Most High; and secondly, she has trespassed against her own husband; and thirdly, she has played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.
cards.t_text: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, and he sees all his goings.

cards.note: Job 31:1 — *I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?* Job is the man who refuses the adulterer's reasoning of Sirach 23:18 — guarding the eye before the heart ever thinks.
cards.s_text: A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins:
cards.t_text: I made a covenant with my eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

cards.note: Matthew 5:28 — *But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* Yahusha sees the secret thought of Sirach 23:18 itself as the act — the heart is never hidden.
cards.s_text: A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins:
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

cards.note: Psalm 139:7 — *Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?* David knows there is no darkness to compass oneself about, against the adulterer's boast of Sirach 23:18.
cards.s_text: A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins:
cards.t_text: Whither shall I go from your spirit? or whither shall I flee from your presence?

cards.note: Proverbs 15:3 — *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.* No wall hides from the eye that Sirach 23:19 calls brighter than the sun.
cards.s_text: Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.
cards.t_text: The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.

cards.note: Proverbs 5:21 — *For the ways of man are before the eyes of Yahuah (LORD), and he pondereth all his goings.* Solomon sets the all-seeing eye in his own chapter against the strange woman — the very ground of Sirach 23:19.
cards.s_text: Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.
cards.t_text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Yahuah (LORD), and he pondereth all his goings.

cards.note: Matthew 12:36 — *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* The sinner taken in his own speech of Sirach 23:8 stands before the reckoning Yahusha names for every idle word.
cards.s_text: The sinner shall be left in his foolishness: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.

cards.note: James 3:2 — *For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.* James makes Sirach 23:7's kept mouth the measure of the perfect man.
cards.s_text: Hear, O you children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips.
cards.t_text: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man, and able also to bridle the whole body.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 28:17 — *The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.* Ben Sira's own later word measures the ruin of the opprobrious mouth of Sirach 23:15 — the tongue wounds deeper than the whip.
cards.s_text: The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words will never be reformed all the days of his life.
cards.t_text: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:21 — *Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.* The stakes of Sirach 23:7's discipline: the tongue holds death and life.
cards.s_text: Hear, O you children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips.
cards.t_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:3 — *He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction.* Proverbs says in a line what Sirach 23:7 names the discipline of the mouth — to keep it is to keep one's life.
cards.s_text: Hear, O you children, the discipline of the mouth: he that keepeth it shall never be taken in his lips.
cards.t_text: He that keeps his mouth keeps his life: but he that opens wide his lips shall have destruction.

cards.note: James 5:12 — *But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.* James warns of the condemnation that Sirach 23:11 calls the plague that never departs the swearer's house.
cards.s_text: A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: if he shall offend, his sin shall be upon him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offence: and if he swear in vain, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.
cards.t_text: But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest you fall into condemnation.

cards.note: Matthew 5:37 — *But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.* The plain speech that needs no oath is the mouth Sirach 23:9 sought to discipline.
cards.s_text: Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these comes of evil.

cards.note: Matthew 5:34 — *But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is Elohim's (God's) throne.* On the mount Yahusha presses Sirach 23:9 to its root: not careless swearing tempered, but the oath forsworn altogether.
cards.s_text: Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is Elohim's (God’s) throne:

cards.note: Leviticus 19:12 — *And ye shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).* The holiness code names the false oath as a profaning of the Name — exactly the swearing Sirach 23:9 forbids.
cards.s_text: Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: And you shall not swear by my name falsely, neither shall you profane the name of your Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Exodus 20:7 — *Thou shalt not take the name of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in vain; for Yahuah (LORD) will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.* Sinai's third word stands behind Sirach 23:9's charge not to accustom the mouth to naming the Holy One.
cards.s_text: Accustom not your mouth to swearing; neither use thyself to the naming of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: You shall not take the name of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in vain; for Yahuah (LORD) will not hold him guiltless that takes his name in vain.

cards.note: James 1:26 — *If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man's religion is vain.* James echoes Sirach 23:1's prayer not to be left to one's own counsels — the unbridled tongue undoes all religion.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (God), Father and Governor of all my whole life, leave me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them.
cards.t_text: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.

cards.note: Psalm 139:4 — *For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Yahuah (LORD), thou knowest it altogether.* David's psalm answers the plea of Sirach 23:2: the One who would discipline the heart already knows the word before it is uttered.
cards.s_text: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart? that they spare me not for my ignorances, and it pass not by my sins:
cards.t_text: For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Yahuah (LORD), you know it altogether.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 22:27 — *Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?* The chapter before voices the very prayer Sirach 23:2 opens with — a seal upon the lips.
cards.s_text: Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over my heart? that they spare me not for my ignorances, and it pass not by my sins:
cards.t_text: Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seal of wisdom upon my lips, that I fall not suddenly by them, and that my tongue destroy me not?

cards.note: Colossians 1:15 — *Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature.* Wisdom who alone compassed the circuit of heaven (Sirach 24:5) is the image of the invisible Elohim, the firstborn of all creation.
cards.s_text: I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep.
cards.t_text: Who is the image of the invisible Elohim (God), the firstborn of every creature:

cards.note: Hebrews 1:3 — *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high.* The Wisdom enthroned in the cloudy pillar (Sirach 24:4) is the Son who is the brightness of the Father's glory, upholding all things.
cards.s_text: I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
cards.t_text: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;

cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* Wisdom serving in the holy tabernacle (Sirach 24:10) is the Word who pitched his tabernacle in flesh and showed his glory.
cards.s_text: In the holy tabernacle I served before him; and so was I established in Sion.
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 33:3 — *Yea, he loved the people; all his saints are in thy hand: and they sat down at thy feet; every one shall receive of thy words.* Wisdom rooting in the honourable people, the portion of Yahuah's inheritance (Sirach 24:12), is the people Yahuah loved and holds in his hand.
cards.s_text: And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Yea, he loved the people; all his saints are in your hand: and they sat down at your feet; every one shall receive of your words.

cards.note: Exodus 19:5 — *Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine.* The covenant-election that makes Jacob the peculiar treasure is why Wisdom is told to dwell in Jacob in Sirach 24:8.
cards.s_text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Now therefore, if you will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then you shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:

cards.note: Revelation 22:17 — *And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.* The canon's last call to the thirsty answers the thirst Wisdom awakens in Sirach 24:21.
cards.s_text: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.
cards.t_text: And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that hears say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.

cards.note: Isaiah 55:1 — *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.* Isaiah's free invitation to eat and drink stands behind Wisdom's Come to me and fill yourselves in Sirach 24:19.
cards.s_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
cards.t_text: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come you to the waters, and he that has no money; come you, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

cards.note: Matthew 11:28 — *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* Yahusha's call repeats Wisdom's own — Come to me, all you that be desirous of me (Sirach 24:19).
cards.s_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
cards.t_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

cards.note: John 6:35 — *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.* Yahusha answers the hunger and thirst Wisdom stirs up in Sirach 24:21 — in him alone is it filled.
cards.s_text: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.
cards.t_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that comes to me shall never hunger; and he that believes on me shall never thirst.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 1:1 — *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.* Sirach's own opening confession undergirds 24:8, where the Creator commands Wisdom to dwell in Jacob.
cards.s_text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.

cards.note: Baruch 3:9 — *Hear, Yashar'el (Israel), the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom.* Baruch equates the commandments of life with wisdom, the same identity Sirach 24:23 makes between Wisdom and the law of Moses.
cards.s_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.
cards.t_text: Hear, Yashar'el (Israel), the commandments of life: give ear to understand wisdom.

cards.note: Baruch 4:1 — *This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.* Baruch matches Sirach 24:23: Wisdom is the book of the covenant, the law that endureth.
cards.s_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.
cards.t_text: This is the book of the commandments of Yahuah (God), and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 33:4 — *Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.* This is the very phrase Wisdom claims for herself in Sirach 24:23 — the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.
cards.s_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.
cards.t_text: Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob.

cards.note: Colossians 1:16 — *For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him.* Wisdom that alone compassed the circuit of heaven (Sirach 24:5) is the One by whom all things were created.
cards.s_text: I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottom of the deep.
cards.t_text: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:

cards.note: Proverbs 8:30 — *Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him.* Wisdom that shall never fail (Sirach 24:9) is the One brought up with Yahuah before the world was.
cards.s_text: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.
cards.t_text: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;

cards.note: Proverbs 8:22 — *Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.* Wisdom created from the beginning before the world (Sirach 24:9) is the same Wisdom possessed before his works of old.
cards.s_text: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The Wisdom whose throne is in the cloudy pillar (Sirach 24:4) is the Word that tabernacled among us.
cards.s_text: I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: John 1:1 — *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* The Word that was with Elohim is the Wisdom that came out of the mouth of the Most High in Sirach 24:3.
cards.s_text: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.
cards.t_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 26:1 — *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.* Ben Sira's own next chapter carries the blessing of the wife of understanding straight into the praise of the virtuous wife.
cards.s_text: Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served a man more unworthy than himself:
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.

cards.note: Proverbs 31:30 — *Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth Yahuah (LORD), she shall be praised.* Ben Sira's wife of understanding, like Proverbs' praised woman, is measured by the fear of Yahuah, not by beauty.
cards.s_text: Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served a man more unworthy than himself:
cards.t_text: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that fears Yahuah (LORD), she shall be praised.

cards.note: Proverbs 31:10 — *Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.* The dwelling with a wife of understanding Ben Sira calls blessed is the rare treasure Proverbs prices above rubies.
cards.s_text: Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served a man more unworthy than himself:
cards.t_text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

cards.note: Proverbs 12:4 — *A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.* The wife of understanding who makes a man blessed is the crowning virtuous woman of Proverbs.
cards.s_text: Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not served a man more unworthy than himself:
cards.t_text: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that makes ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:19 — *It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.* The wife full of words who wearies the quiet man is the contentious woman Proverbs would flee to the wilderness to escape.
cards.s_text: As the climbing up a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
cards.t_text: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, than with a contentious and an angry woman.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:9 — *It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.* Proverbs' 'better the housetop' is Ben Sira's 'rather the lion and dragon' — the same flight from a wicked woman's house.
cards.s_text: I had rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, than to keep house with a wicked woman.
cards.t_text: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

cards.note: Romans 5:12 — *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:* Ben Sira's 'through her we all die' is the universal death Paul traces from the fall to every man.
cards.s_text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

cards.note: 1 Timothy 2:14 — *And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.* Paul, like Ben Sira, marks the woman as the door of the first transgression.
cards.s_text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
cards.t_text: And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.

cards.note: Genesis 3:16 — *Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.* The sentence on Eve is the sorrow and death Ben Sira says came through her.
cards.s_text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
cards.t_text: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception; in sorrow you shall bring forth children; and your desire shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you.

cards.note: Genesis 3:6 — *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* The eating in the garden is the beginning of sin Ben Sira traces to the woman.
cards.s_text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
cards.t_text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

cards.note: Job 12:12 — *With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.* Job binds wisdom to age as Ben Sira binds it to old men and counsel.
cards.s_text: O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honour.
cards.t_text: With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 20:29 — *The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head.* The beauty of old men is their gray head — the wisdom Ben Sira calls comely in men of honour.
cards.s_text: O how comely is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men of honour.
cards.t_text: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head.

cards.note: Proverbs 16:31 — *The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.* Proverbs crowns the gray head Ben Sira deems comely for counsel.
cards.s_text: O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel!
cards.t_text: The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:32 — *Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).* The Torah commands the very honour for gray hairs that Ben Sira calls comely.
cards.s_text: O how comely a thing is judgment for gray hairs, and for ancient men to know counsel!
cards.t_text: You shall rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear your Elohim (God): I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 1:14 — *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.* Ben Sira's own prologue founds the whole book on the fear chapter 25 names the glory of the aged.
cards.s_text: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of Yahuah (God) is their glory.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: Job 28:28 — *And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of Yahuah (Lord), that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.* The Almighty's own definition matches Ben Sira's: the fear of Yahuah is the beginning of his love and of cleaving to him.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is the beginning of his love: and faith is the beginning of cleaving to him.
cards.t_text: And unto man he said, Behold, the fear of Adonai (Lord), that is wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* Ben Sira sets none above the one who fears Yahuah because that fear is wisdom's own beginning.
cards.s_text: O how great is he that finds wisdom! yet is there none above him that fears Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* The reverence Ben Sira calls the glory of old men is what Proverbs names the very beginning of knowledge.
cards.s_text: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of Yahuah (God) is their glory.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:21 — *Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.* The wicked merchant of Sirach 26:29 'shall not be freed from sin,' yet the righteous seed is delivered.
cards.s_text: A merchant shall hardly keep himself from doing wrong; and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.
cards.t_text: Though hand join in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall be delivered.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 2:14 — *And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.* Paul's Eden allusion echoes the same beginning-of-sin reading that shadows Sirach 26:22.
cards.s_text: An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
cards.t_text: And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.

cards.note: Genesis 3:6 — *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* Eden is the 'beginning of sin' Sirach reads behind the woman who is a tower of death or life to her husband in Sirach 26:22.
cards.s_text: An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
cards.t_text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 25:24 — *Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.* Ben Sira's own Eve-allusion grounds Sirach 26:22's harlot-versus-wife weighing of the woman's power for death or for life.
cards.s_text: An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
cards.t_text: Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.

cards.note: Proverbs 27:15 — *A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.* The ceaseless dropping of the contentious woman is the unrelenting 'grief of heart' Sirach 26:6 sets beside the scourge of the tongue.
cards.s_text: But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.
cards.t_text: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:9 — *It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.* The brawling woman one flees to the rooftop is the loud-crying scold of Sirach 26:27.
cards.s_text: A loud crying woman and a scold shall be sought out to drive away the enemies.
cards.t_text: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a wide house.

cards.note: James 3:8 — *But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.* James names the untameable poisonous tongue that is Sirach 26:6's 'scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.'
cards.s_text: But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.
cards.t_text: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

cards.note: Proverbs 5:18 — *Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.* The blessed fountain kept to the wife of youth answers Sirach 26:19's charge to keep the flower of one's age sound and not give one's strength to strangers.
cards.s_text: My son, keep the flower of your age sound; and give not your strength to strangers.
cards.t_text: Let your fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of your youth.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:22 — *As a jewel of gold in a swine's snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.* The fair-but-indiscreet woman of Proverbs is the haughty-eyed one Sirach 26:9 warns marks whoredom.
cards.s_text: The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.
cards.t_text: As a jewel of gold in a swine’s snout, so is a fair woman which is without discretion.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 9:8 — *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.* Ben Sira's own earlier counsel on the deceiving eye undergirds Sirach 26:9's reading of whoredom in haughty looks and eyelids.
cards.s_text: The whoredom of a woman may be known in her haughty looks and eyelids.
cards.t_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.

cards.note: Matthew 5:28 — *But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* The Sermon traces lust to the eye and heart, the very inward purity Sirach 26:19 guards as 'the flower of your age.'
cards.s_text: My son, keep the flower of your age sound; and give not your strength to strangers.
cards.t_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

cards.note: Proverbs 12:4 — *A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that maketh ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.* The crown-versus-rottenness contrast matches Sirach 26:26's wife judged wise for honouring versus ungodly for dishonouring her husband.
cards.s_text: A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.
cards.t_text: A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but she that makes ashamed is as rottenness in his bones.

cards.note: Proverbs 31:11 — *The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.* The husband's safe trust answers Sirach 26:16's good wife who lights and orders his whole house.
cards.s_text: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
cards.t_text: The heart of her husband does safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
