cards.note: Proverbs 31:30 — *Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth Yahuah (LORD), she shall be praised.* The fear of Yahuah, not beauty, marks the godly woman 'given to him that fears Yahuah' in Sirach 26:23.
cards.s_text: A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that fears Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that fears Yahuah (LORD), she shall be praised.

cards.note: Proverbs 31:10 — *Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.* The virtuous woman beyond price is the good wife whose beauty in ordering her house shines like the sun in Sirach 26:16.
cards.s_text: As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
cards.t_text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.

cards.note: James 1:17 — *Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.* James names the down-from-above grammar of every gift, of which Sirach 26:14's silent loving woman 'a gift of Yahuah' is one.
cards.s_text: A silent and loving woman is a gift of Yahuah (God); and there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed.
cards.t_text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:14 — *House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from Yahuah (LORD).* The prudent wife given from Yahuah is the same gift Sirach 26:3 calls a good portion bestowed.
cards.s_text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 18:22 — *Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of Yahuah (LORD).* The good wife is favour obtained of Yahuah, exactly Ben Sira's 'portion of them that fear Yahuah' in Sirach 26:3.
cards.s_text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Whoso finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favour of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: 1 Peter 5:8 — *Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.* Vengeance lying in wait as a lion for the proud (Sirach 27:28) is the roaring lion Kepha bids the watchful resist.
cards.s_text: Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.
cards.t_text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walks about, seeking whom he may devour:

cards.note: Genesis 4:7 — *And if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.* The lion that lieth in wait as sin for the iniquitous (Sirach 27:10) is the beast couching at Cain's door.
cards.s_text: As the lion lieth in wait for the prey; so sin for them that work iniquity.
cards.t_text: If you do well, shall you not be accepted? and if you do not well, sin lies at the door. And unto you shall be his desire, and you shall rule over him.

cards.note: Galatians 6:7 — *Be not deceived; Elohim (God) is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.* The stone cast on high returning on its own head (Sirach 27:25) is Sha'ul's law of sowing and reaping.
cards.s_text: Whoso casteth a stone on high casteth it on his own head; and a deceitful stroke shall make wounds.
cards.t_text: Be not deceived; Elohim (God) is not mocked: for whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap.

cards.note: Psalm 7:16 — *His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.* Sirach 27:27 says the mischief falls upon its worker; David says it returns upon his own head and pate.
cards.s_text: He that works mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it comes.
cards.t_text: His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.

cards.note: Psalm 7:15 — *He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.* The mischief that falls on the worker who knows not whence it comes (Sirach 27:27) is the pit-digger fallen into his own ditch.
cards.s_text: He that works mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it comes.
cards.t_text: He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:27 — *Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.* Sirach 27:25-26 is the same twin proverb — the high-cast stone and the digged pit both fall back on the one who launched them.
cards.s_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it.
cards.t_text: Whoso digs a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:19 — *A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.* The betrayer of secrets is without hope (Sirach 27:21) because the offended friend is harder to win than a walled city.
cards.s_text: As for a wound, it may be bound up; and after reviling there may be reconcilement: but he that betrayeth secrets is without hope.
cards.t_text: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.

cards.note: Proverbs 17:9 — *He that covereth a transgression seeketh love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.* To betray a friend's secrets and follow no more (Sirach 27:17) is the repeating of a matter that separates very friends.
cards.s_text: Love your friend, and be faithful to him: but if you betrayest his secrets, follow no more after him.
cards.t_text: He that covers a transgression seeks love; but he that repeateth a matter separateth very friends.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:13 — *A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.* The man who discovers secrets and loses his credit in Sirach 27:16 is the talebearer the proverb contrasts with the faithful spirit.
cards.s_text: Whoso discovers secrets loses his credit; and shall never find friend to his mind.
cards.t_text: A talebearer revealeth secrets: but he that is of a faithful spirit concealeth the matter.

cards.note: Matthew 12:33 — *Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.* The Master ties the tree-and-fruit of Sirach 27:6 directly to the words a heart brings forth.
cards.s_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
cards.t_text: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit.

cards.note: Matthew 7:17 — *Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit.* The dressed tree showing its fruit in Sirach 27:6 is the good tree that cannot help but bear good fruit.
cards.s_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
cards.t_text: Even so every good tree brings forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree brings forth evil fruit.

cards.note: Matthew 7:16 — *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?* Sirach 27:6 already said the fruit declares the tree, and the man's utterance declares his heart.
cards.s_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
cards.t_text: You shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:6 — *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.* The trial-furnace of Sirach 27:5 is, in its sister wisdom-book, the proving that makes the righteous an offering — testing, not cursing.
cards.s_text: The furnace proves the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.
cards.t_text: As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.

cards.note: Matthew 12:37 — *For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.* Sirach 27:7 says hear a man speak before you praise him; the Master makes his words the very ground of his judgment.
cards.s_text: Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.
cards.t_text: For by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned.

cards.note: Matthew 12:34 — *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* The sieve leaving the refuse in a man's talk (Sirach 27:4) is the mouth speaking out of the heart's abundance.
cards.s_text: As when one sifteth with a sieve, the refuse remains; so the filth of man in his talk.
cards.t_text: O generation of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

cards.note: Proverbs 27:21 — *As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.* The same furnace-image that proves the potter's vessels in Sirach 27:5 already weighed the man in Proverbs.
cards.s_text: The furnace proves the potter’s vessels; so the trial of man is in his reasoning.
cards.t_text: As the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so is a man to his praise.

cards.note: Proverbs 12:18 — *There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.* The sword-piercing speech is Sira's stroke of the tongue in 28:17 that *breaks the bones*.
cards.s_text: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.
cards.t_text: There is that speaks like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.

cards.note: Proverbs 18:21 — *Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.* Solomon weighs the very deadliness Sirach 28:18 names — more fallen by the tongue than the sword.
cards.s_text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.
cards.t_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.

cards.note: James 3:8 — *But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.* The untameable poison answers Sirach 28:14's backbiting tongue that *pulled down* cities and houses.
cards.s_text: A backbiting tongue has disquieted many, and driven them from nation to nation: strong cities has it pulled down, and overthrown the houses of great men.
cards.t_text: But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.

cards.note: James 3:6 — *And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.* James's tongue-as-fire is Sira's spark of 28:12 that, blown, *shall burn*.
cards.s_text: If you blow the spark, it shall burn: if you spit upon it, it shall be quenched: and both these come out of your mouth.
cards.t_text: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity: so is the tongue among our members, that it defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.

cards.note: Proverbs 12:17 — *He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.* The false witness feeds the hasty contention that Sirach 28:11 says *kindleth a fire*.
cards.s_text: An hasty contention kindleth a fire: and an hasty fighting sheddeth blood.
cards.t_text: He that speaks truth shows forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.

cards.note: Proverbs 26:20 — *Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.* Solomon's talebearer is Sira's sinful man of 28:9 who *disquieteth friends*.
cards.s_text: A sinful man disquieteth friends, and makes debate among them that be at peace.
cards.t_text: Where no wood is, there the fire goes out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceases.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:1 — *A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.* The soft answer is the opposite of Sirach 28:8's *furious man* who kindles strife.
cards.s_text: Abstain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins: for a furious man will kindle strife,
cards.t_text: A soft answer turns away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.

cards.note: Ephesians 4:32 — *And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as Elohim (God) for Messiah's (Christ’s) sake hath forgiven you.* Kindness in place of malice fulfils Sirach 28:7's *bear no malice to your neighbour*.
cards.s_text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
cards.t_text: And be you kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as Elohim (God) for Messiah's (Christ’s) sake has forgiven you.

cards.note: Colossians 3:13 — *Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Messiah (Christ) forgave you, so also do ye.* Bearing no malice and forgiving the quarrel is the Torah-rooted command Sira gives in 28:7.
cards.s_text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.
cards.t_text: Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Messiah (Christ) forgave you, so also do you.

cards.note: Psalm 90:12 — *So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.* Numbering one's days is exactly Sirach 28:6's call to *remember your end* so that enmity ceases.
cards.s_text: Remember your end, and let enmity cease; remember corruption and death, and abide in the commandments.
cards.t_text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 27:28 — *Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.* Sira's own previous chapter sets the lion of vengeance that 28:1 and 28:23 will loose on the unforgiving.
cards.s_text: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
cards.t_text: Mockery and reproach are from the proud; but vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.

cards.note: Romans 12:17 — *Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.* Refusing to repay evil answers Sira's rebuke in 28:3 of the man who bears hatred yet seeks pardon.
cards.s_text: One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?
cards.t_text: Recompense to no man evil for evil. Provide things honest in the sight of all men.

cards.note: Romans 12:19 — *Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith Yahuah (Lord).* Paul cites the same principle as Sirach 28:1 — the avenger usurps a vengeance that is Yahuah's alone.
cards.s_text: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
cards.t_text: Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, says Yahuah (Lord).

cards.note: *He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?* (Ecclesiasticus 28:4). *Then came Peter to him, and said, Adonai (Lord), how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?* (Matthew 18:21). Peter's question is about a brother, a man like himself, sinning against him over and over. Sirach had already asked what becomes of a man who shows no mercy to one made like himself and then asks forgiveness for his own sins. Peter is standing right at that question, counting toward a limit, and the King's answer in the next verse takes the limit away. The mercy owed to an equal is the mercy Sirach demands, and it is the mercy a disciple must give before he asks his own.
cards.s_text: He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?
cards.t_text: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?

cards.note: Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The Torah's ban on vengeance and grudge is the root Sirach 28:1 grows from.
cards.s_text: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.
cards.t_text: You shall not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Mark 11:25 — *And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.* Forgiveness at the moment of prayer is precisely Sirach 28:2's *when you prayest*.
cards.s_text: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.
cards.t_text: And when you stand praying, forgive, if you have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.

cards.note: Matthew 18:35 — *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* The unforgiving servant is condemned by exactly Sira's logic in 28:3 — bearing hatred while seeking pardon.
cards.s_text: One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?
cards.t_text: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if you from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.

cards.note: Matthew 6:14 — *For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:* Yahusha makes the very bargain of Sirach 28:2 — forgive the neighbour's hurt and your own sins are forgiven.
cards.s_text: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.
cards.t_text: For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:

cards.note: Hebrews 13:5 — *Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.* 'Hold you contented' (Sirach 29:23) is the apostolic word of contentment grounded in Yahuah's faithfulness.
cards.s_text: Be it little or much, hold you contented, that you hear not the reproach of your house.
cards.t_text: Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as you have: for he has said, I will never leave you, nor forsake you.

cards.note: Proverbs 17:1 — *Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife.* Sirach 29:22's poor man's cottage over delicate fare in another's house echoes the dry morsel with peace.
cards.s_text: Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.
cards.t_text: Better is a dry morsel, and quietness therewith, than an house full of sacrifices with strife.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:16 — *Better is little with the fear of Yahuah (LORD) than great treasure and trouble therewith.* The 'better-is-little' wisdom of Sirach 29:22's poor cottage is straight from Proverbs.
cards.s_text: Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.
cards.t_text: Better is little with the fear of Yahuah (LORD) than great treasure and trouble therewith.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:8 — *And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.* Paul's 'food and raiment' is Sirach 29:21's water, bread, clothing and house — the chief things for life.
cards.s_text: The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame.
cards.t_text: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:17 — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again.* Against the wicked who 'transgressing the commandments of Yahuah' falls into suretiship (Sirach 29:19), Wisdom sets the merciful lender repaid by Yahuah.
cards.s_text: A wicked man transgressing the commandments of Yahuah (God) shall fall into suretiship: and he that undertaketh and followeth other men’s business for gain shall fall into suits.
cards.t_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:26 — *Be not thou one of them that strike hands, or of them that are sureties for debts.* The peril of standing surety in Sirach 29:18 is Wisdom's own caution.
cards.s_text: Suretiship has undone many of good estate, and shaken them as a wave of the sea: mighty men has it driven from their houses, so that they wandered among strange nations.
cards.t_text: Be not you one of them that strike hands, or of them that are sureties for debts.

cards.note: Proverbs 6:1 — *My son, if thou be surety for thy friend, if thou hast stricken thy hand with a stranger,* Proverbs' warning is the same sober counsel as Sirach 29:18, that suretiship has undone many.
cards.s_text: Suretiship has undone many of good estate, and shaken them as a wave of the sea: mighty men has it driven from their houses, so that they wandered among strange nations.
cards.t_text: My son, if you be surety for your friend, if you have stricken your hand with a stranger,

cards.note: John 15:13 — *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* The surety who 'has given his life for you' (Sirach 29:15) is a shadow of the Messiah's own laid-down life.
cards.s_text: Forget not the friendship of your surety, for he has given his life for you.
cards.t_text: Greater love has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:24 — *There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.* Wisdom's paradox underwrites Sirach 29:11: giving treasure away brings 'more profit than gold.'
cards.s_text: Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.
cards.t_text: There is that scatters, and yet increases; and there is that withholdeth more than is meet, but it tendeth to poverty.

cards.note: Tobit 4:9 — *For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Tobit's 'good treasure laid up' is the same storehouse of alms Sirach 29:12 says shall deliver.
cards.s_text: Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.
cards.t_text: For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.

cards.note: Tobit 4:10 — *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The live sister-book teaches Sirach 29:12 word for word: alms in store deliver you from affliction.
cards.s_text: Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.
cards.t_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.

cards.note: Matthew 6:19 — *Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal.* Sirach 29:10's money that should not 'rust under a stone to be lost' is the earthly treasure the Messiah warns against hoarding.
cards.s_text: Lose your money for your brother and your friend, and let it not rust under a stone to be lost.
cards.t_text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust does corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

cards.note: Matthew 6:20 — *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal.* The Messiah's heavenly treasure is Sirach 29:11's 'lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High.'
cards.s_text: Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High, and it shall bring you more profit than gold.
cards.t_text: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust does corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:10 — *Thou shalt surely give him, and thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest unto him: because that for this thing Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in all thy works, and in all that thou puttest thine hand unto.* 'Help the poor for the commandment's sake' (Sirach 29:9) cites this Torah blessing on the ungrudging giver.
cards.s_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.
cards.t_text: You shall surely give him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him: because that for this thing Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.

cards.note: Matthew 5:42 — *Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.* 'Turn him not away because of his poverty' (Sirach 29:9) is the same refusal to turn the borrower away.
cards.s_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.
cards.t_text: Give to him that asks you, and from him that would borrow of you turn not you away.

cards.note: Luke 6:34 — *And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.* The very fear of loss Sirach 29:7 names is the sinner's reckoning the Messiah calls us above.
cards.s_text: Many therefore have refused to lend for other men’s ill dealing, fearing to be defrauded.
cards.t_text: And if you lend to them of whom you hope to receive, what thank have you? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

cards.note: Luke 6:35 — *But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.* The Messiah's 'lend hoping for nothing again' is Sirach 29:8's patience with the poor debtor.
cards.s_text: Yet have you patience with a man in poor estate, and delay not to shew him mercy.
cards.t_text: But love you your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and you shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

cards.note: *Lend to your neighbour in time of his need, and pay you your neighbour again in due season.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:2). *Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.* (Matthew 5:42). Sirach says lend to your neighbour when he needs it, and pay back your neighbour when the time comes. Yahusha (Jesus) on the mount says give to him who asks, and do not turn away the one who wants to borrow. The Sermon takes Sirach's line and opens the hand wider, but it is the same hand. Lending to a neighbour in his need was already the commandment in Yashar'el (Israel); the King was telling his disciples to keep it without flinching.
cards.s_text: Lend to your neighbour in time of his need, and pay you your neighbour again in due season.
cards.t_text: Give to him that asks you, and from him that would borrow of you turn not you away.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:17 — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again.* Sirach 29:1's lending to a neighbour is, in Wisdom's eyes, lending to Yahuah Himself.
cards.s_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.
cards.t_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.

cards.note: Psalm 37:21 — *The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous sheweth mercy, and giveth.* The same righteous/wicked contrast over lending that frames Sirach 29:1-2.
cards.s_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.
cards.t_text: The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous shows mercy, and gives.

cards.note: Psalm 37:26 — *He is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed.* The Psalmist makes the merciful lender of Sirach 29:1 the very portrait of the blessed righteous.
cards.s_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.
cards.t_text: He is ever merciful, and lendeth; and his seed is blessed.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 15:8 — *But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.* The Torah command Sirach 29:1 calls keeping the commandments: the merciful man lends.
cards.s_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.
cards.t_text: But you shall open your hand wide unto him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:15 — *All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast.* 'No joy above the joy of the heart' (30:16) is the merry heart's continual feast — wealth no body can buy (Ecclesiasticus 30:16).
cards.s_text: There is no riches above a sound body, and no joy above the joy of the heart.
cards.t_text: All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart has a continual feast.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:13 — *A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.* Ben Sira's envy and wrath that 'shorten the life' (30:24) are Solomon's sorrow of heart that breaks the spirit (Ecclesiasticus 30:24).
cards.s_text: Envy and wrath shorten the life, and carefulness brings age before the time.
cards.t_text: A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.

cards.note: Proverbs 17:22 — *A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones.* 'The gladness of the heart is the life of man' (30:22) is Solomon's merry heart that heals like medicine, against the heaviness that shortens days (Ecclesiasticus 30:22).
cards.s_text: The gladness of the heart is the life of man, and the joyfulness of a man prolongeth his days.
cards.t_text: A merry heart does good like a medicine: but a broken spirit dries the bones.

cards.note: Proverbs 17:21 — *He that begetteth a fool doeth it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool hath no joy.* The troubled bowels and grief of the over-indulgent father in 30:7 are Solomon's sorrowing father of a fool (Ecclesiasticus 30:7).
cards.s_text: He that makes too much of his son shall bind up his wounds; and his bowels will be troubled at every cry.
cards.t_text: He that begetteth a fool does it to his sorrow: and the father of a fool has no joy.

cards.note: Ephesians 6:4 — *And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of Yahuah (Lord).* Paul's balance answers both of Sirach's warnings — no liberty to folly (30:11) yet no provoking wound (30:7) (Ecclesiasticus 30:11).
cards.s_text: Give him no liberty in his youth, and wink not at his follies.
cards.t_text: And, you fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

cards.note: Revelation 3:19 — *As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.* The Messiah to Laodicea speaks the same wisdom Ben Sira teaches the household: love rebukes (Ecclesiasticus 30:2).
cards.s_text: He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.
cards.t_text: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:12 — *For whom Yahuah (LORD) loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.* Sirach 30:1's loving father who applies the rod is the very image Solomon uses for Yahuah's love (Ecclesiasticus 30:1).
cards.s_text: He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end.
cards.t_text: For whom Yahuah (LORD) loves he corrects; even as a father the son in whom he delights.

cards.note: Hebrews 12:7 — *If ye endure chastening, Elohim (God) dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?* Ben Sira's rejoicing chastener (30:2) is the human picture Hebrews lifts to the Father of spirits (Ecclesiasticus 30:2).
cards.s_text: He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.
cards.t_text: If you endure chastening, Elohim (God) deals with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chastens not?

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:5 — *Thou shalt also consider in thine heart, that, as a man chasteneth his son, so Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) chasteneth thee.* The joy of the chastening father in 30:2 mirrors Yahuah's own fatherly correction of Yashar'el (Ecclesiasticus 30:2).
cards.s_text: He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.
cards.t_text: You shall also consider in your heart, that, as a man chastens his son, so Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) chastens you.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:14 — *Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.* 'Beat him on the sides while he is a child' (30:12) is Solomon's deliverance of the soul from death, not mere severity (Ecclesiasticus 30:12).
cards.s_text: Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient to you, and so bring sorrow to yours heart.
cards.t_text: You shall beat him with the rod, and shall deliver his soul from hell.

cards.note: Proverbs 29:17 — *Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.* Against the heaviness the cockered child brings (30:9), the corrected son brings rest and delight — the opposite outcome from the opposite cause (Ecclesiasticus 30:9).
cards.s_text: Cocker your child, and he shall make you afraid: play with him, and he will bring you to heaviness.
cards.t_text: Correct your son, and he shall give you rest; yea, he shall give delight unto your soul.

cards.note: Proverbs 29:15 — *The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.* The exact phrase of Sirach 30:8 — the 'child left to himself' who turns wilful — is lifted straight from Solomon (Ecclesiasticus 30:8).
cards.s_text: An horse not broken becometh headstrong: and a child left to himself will be wilful.
cards.t_text: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself brings his mother to shame.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:18 — *Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.* The Tanakh and Ben Sira agree: chasten while youth is pliable, not after the heart has set (Ecclesiasticus 30:13).
cards.s_text: Chastise your son, and hold him to labour, lest his lewd behaviour be an offence to you.
cards.t_text: Chasten your son while there is hope, and let not your soul spare for his crying.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:13 — *Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.* Sirach's 'Chastise your son' is the Proverb verbatim in spirit: correction is not cruelty but the saving of his life (Ecclesiasticus 30:13).
cards.s_text: Chastise your son, and hold him to labour, lest his lewd behaviour be an offence to you.
cards.t_text: Withhold not correction from the child: for if you beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.

cards.note: Proverbs 22:15 — *Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.* The 'rod' Ben Sira names in 30:1 is the same instrument that drives folly out of the young heart (Ecclesiasticus 30:1).
cards.s_text: He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end.
cards.t_text: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:24 — *He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.* Solomon's headline is Ben Sira's first verse: the father's love is proved by the rod, not denied by it (Ecclesiasticus 30:1).
cards.s_text: He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end.
cards.t_text: He that spareth his rod hates his son: but he that loves him chastens him betimes.

cards.note: Luke 21:34 — *And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.* The Master's warning against the overcharged heart is Ben Sira's drunkenness that diminisheth strength in Sirach 31:30.
cards.s_text: Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminisheth strength, and makes wounds.
cards.t_text: And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.

cards.note: Ephesians 5:18 — *And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.* Paul names the very wine drunken with excess Sira warns of in Sirach 31:29 and points past it to the fuller cup.
cards.s_text: But wine drunken with excess makes bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling.
cards.t_text: And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit;

cards.note: 1 Corinthians 6:10 — *Nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of Elohim (God).* Paul shuts the drunkard out of the kingdom, the fool whose rage drunkenness increaseth in Sirach 31:30.
cards.s_text: Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminisheth strength, and makes wounds.
cards.t_text: Nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Proverbs 23:32 — *At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.* The serpent's sting at the cup's bottom is the wounds drunkenness makes in Sirach 31:30.
cards.s_text: Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminisheth strength, and makes wounds.
cards.t_text: At the last it bites like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:29 — *Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?* Solomon's catalogue of woe is the bitterness, brawling and quarrelling of excess in Sirach 31:29.
cards.s_text: But wine drunken with excess makes bitterness of the mind, with brawling and quarrelling.
cards.t_text: Who has woe? who has sorrow? who has contentions? who has babbling? who has wounds without cause? who has redness of eyes?

cards.note: Proverbs 21:17 — *He that loveth pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loveth wine and oil shall not be rich.* Solomon's counterweight to the cup balances Ben Sira's if it be drunk moderately in Sirach 31:27.
cards.s_text: Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.
cards.t_text: He that loves pleasure shall be a poor man: he that loves wine and oil shall not be rich.

cards.note: Psalm 104:15 — *And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man’s heart.* The wine that maketh glad the heart is the very gladness of the heart Sira names in Sirach 31:27-28, wine made to make men glad.
cards.s_text: Wine is as good as life to a man, if it be drunk moderately: what life is then to a man that is without wine? for it was made to make men glad.
cards.t_text: And wine that makes glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man’s heart.

cards.note: Proverbs 23:21 — *For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.* The glutton's poverty is the unsatiable man Sira warns will give offence in Sirach 31:17.
cards.s_text: Leave off first for manners’ sake; and be not unsatiable, lest you offend.
cards.t_text: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.

cards.note: Proverbs 25:16 — *Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.* Eat only what is sufficient, lest you vomit, is exactly Sira's eat as becometh a man, and devour not in Sirach 31:16.
cards.s_text: Eat as it becometh a man, those things which are set before you; and devour not, lest you be hated.
cards.t_text: Have you found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for you, lest you be filled therewith, and vomit it.

cards.note: *If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:12). *And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.* (Proverbs 23:2). Solomon tells the man given to appetite to put a knife to his own throat when he sits at a ruler's table; Sirach tells him not to be greedy at a bountiful table or to say, There is much meat here. It is the same instruction in two voices, generations apart. A full table is a test of the eye and the hand, and both wisdom writers lay the restraint on the guest, not on the host.
cards.s_text: If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it.
cards.t_text: And put a knife to your throat, if you be a man given to appetite.

cards.note: Job 31:24 — *If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, Thou art my confidence.* Job's oath that he never made gold his hope is the proof of the rich man who has not gone after gold in Sirach 31:10.
cards.s_text: Who has been tried thereby, and found perfect? then let him glory. Who might offend, and has not offended? or done evil, and has not done it?
cards.t_text: If I have made gold my hope, or have said to the fine gold, You are my confidence;

cards.note: Job 1:1 — *There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared Elohim (God), and eschewed evil.* Job is the wealthy man tried thereby and found perfect that Sirach 31:10 asks after.
cards.s_text: Who has been tried thereby, and found perfect? then let him glory. Who might offend, and has not offended? or done evil, and has not done it?
cards.t_text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared Elohim (God), and eschewed evil.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:17 — *Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living Elohim (God), who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.* Paul's charge to the rich is Ben Sira's blessing on the rich found without blemish in Sirach 31:8.
cards.s_text: Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.
cards.t_text: Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living Elohim (God), who gives us richly all things to enjoy;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 8:14 — *Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.* The forgetting heart lifted up by wealth is the blemish Sira's blessed rich man has escaped in Sirach 31:8.
cards.s_text: Blessed is the rich that is found without blemish, and has not gone after gold.
cards.t_text: Then your heart be lifted up, and you forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage;

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 8:2 — *Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he overweigh you: for gold has destroyed many, and perverted the hearts of kings.* Ben Sira's own self-witness — gold has destroyed many — doubles the ruin of many in Sirach 31:6.
cards.s_text: Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.
cards.t_text: Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he overweigh you: for gold has destroyed many, and perverted the hearts of kings.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 5:10 — *He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this is also vanity.* The never-satisfied lover of silver is Ben Sira's man who loves gold and shall not be justified in Sirach 31:5.
cards.s_text: He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.
cards.t_text: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 5:12 — *The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.* The Preacher's sleepless rich man is exactly the watching care that drives away sleep in Sirach 31:1.
cards.s_text: Watching for riches consumeth the flesh, and the care thereof drives away sleep.
cards.t_text: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:9 — *But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.* The snare that drowns men echoes the riches-care that consumeth the flesh in Sirach 31:1.
cards.s_text: Watching for riches consumeth the flesh, and the care thereof drives away sleep.
cards.t_text: But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 6:10 — *For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.* Paul's most-quoted line on greed is Ben Sira's verdict on him that loves gold in Sirach 31:5.
cards.s_text: He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.
cards.t_text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:23 — *A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!* The favour that goes before the shamefaced man in Sirach 32:10 is the joy of the well-timed, well-ordered word.
cards.s_text: Before the thunder goes lightning; and before a shamefaced man shall go favour.
cards.t_text: A man has joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!

cards.note: Proverbs 18:12 — *Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility.* The master of the feast who lifts not himself up in Sirach 32:1 walks the proverb's road where humility goes before honour.
cards.s_text: If you be made the master of a feast, lift not thyself up, but be among them as one of the rest; take diligent care for them, and so sit down.
cards.t_text: Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility.

cards.note: James 1:25 — *But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.* 'This is the keeping of the commandments' in Sirach 32:23 is the doer of the work, blessed in his deed.
cards.s_text: In every good work trust your own soul; for this is the keeping of the commandments.
cards.t_text: But whoso looks into the perfect law of liberty, and continues therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.

cards.note: James 1:22 — *But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.* Taking heed to the commandment in Sirach 32:24 is James's call to be a doer, not a hearer only.
cards.s_text: He that believes in Yahuah (God) takes heed to the commandment; and he that trusts in him shall fare never the worse.
cards.t_text: But be you doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

cards.note: Romans 2:13 — *For not the hearers of the law are just before Elohim (God), but the doers of the law shall be justified.* He that takes heed to the commandment in Sirach 32:24 is Paul's doer of the law who shall be justified.
cards.s_text: He that believes in Yahuah (God) takes heed to the commandment; and he that trusts in him shall fare never the worse.
cards.t_text: (For not the hearers of the law are just before Elohim (God), but the doers of the law shall be justified.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:14 — *But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it.* Sirach 32:23's trust shown in good work is Moses' word very nigh, that thou mayest do it.
cards.s_text: In every good work trust your own soul; for this is the keeping of the commandments.
cards.t_text: But the word is very nigh unto you, in your mouth, and in your heart, that you may do it.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:11 — *For this commandment which I command thee this day, it is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off.* 'The keeping of the commandments' in Sirach 32:23 is Moses' commandment that is not hidden nor far off.
cards.s_text: In every good work trust your own soul; for this is the keeping of the commandments.
cards.t_text: For this commandment which I command you this day, it is not hidden from you, neither is it far off.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 19:20 — *The fear of Yahuah (God) is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.* Sirach binds the fear of 32:16 directly to the performance of the law.
cards.s_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 1:14 — *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.* Ben Sira's own opening makes the fear of Yahuah that finds judgment in Sirach 32:16 the beginning of wisdom.
cards.s_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) shall find judgment, and shall kindle justice as a light.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: Psalm 119:2 — *Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and that seek him with the whole heart.* 'They that seek him early shall find favour' in Sirach 32:14 is the blessing of those who seek him with the whole heart.
cards.s_text: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) will receive his discipline; and they that seek him early shall find favour.
cards.t_text: Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, and that seek him with the whole heart.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* The fearing soul that receives discipline in Sirach 32:14 is the proverb's beginning of knowledge.
cards.s_text: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) will receive his discipline; and they that seek him early shall find favour.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: James 4:14 — *Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.* The self-confident man of Sirach 32:18 forgets that his morrow is not his own.
cards.s_text: A man of counsel will be considerate; but a strange and proud man is not daunted with fear, even when of himself he has done without counsel.
cards.t_text: Whereas you know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appears for a little time, and then vanishes away.

cards.note: James 4:13 — *Go to now, ye that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain.* The proud man who acts without counsel in Sirach 32:18 is James's presumptuous planner.
cards.s_text: A man of counsel will be considerate; but a strange and proud man is not daunted with fear, even when of himself he has done without counsel.
cards.t_text: Go to now, you that say, To day or to morrow we will go into such a city, and continue there a year, and buy and sell, and get gain:

cards.note: Proverbs 11:14 — *Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.* 'Do nothing without advice' in Sirach 32:19 is the proverb of safety in the multitude of counsellors.
cards.s_text: Do nothing without advice; and when you have once done, repent not.
cards.t_text: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 3:7 — *A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak.* Sirach 32:4's 'shew not forth wisdom out of time' is the Preacher's time to keep silence.
cards.s_text: Pour not out words where there is a musician, and shew not forth wisdom out of time.
cards.t_text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;

cards.note: Proverbs 18:13 — *He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.* The short, knowing speech that holds its tongue in Sirach 32:8 is the wisdom against the hasty answer.
cards.s_text: Let your speech be short, comprehending much in few words; be as one that knoweth and yet holdeth his tongue.
cards.t_text: He that answers a matter before he hears it, it is folly and shame unto him.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:23 — *A man hath joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!* The elder's seasoned speech in Sirach 32:3 is Proverbs' word in due season.
cards.s_text: Speak, you that are the elder, for it becometh you, but with sound judgment; and hinder not musick.
cards.t_text: A man has joy by the answer of his mouth: and a word spoken in due season, how good is it!

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 7:21 — *Let your soul love a good servant, and defraud him not of liberty.* Ben Sira's own command tempers Sirach 33:30 — the bought servant, held as thyself, loved and not defrauded.
cards.s_text: If you have a servant, let him be to you as thyself, because you have bought him with a price.
cards.t_text: Let your soul love a good servant, and defraud him not of liberty.

cards.note: Proverbs 13:24 — *He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes.* The disciplined correction Sirach 33:28 sets to the idle servant — work and chastening as love, not malice.
cards.s_text: Set him to work, as is fit for him: if he be not obedient, put on more heavy fetters.
cards.t_text: He that spareth his rod hates his son: but he that loves him chastens him betimes.

cards.note: Proverbs 29:21 — *He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.* The servant who becomes a son — the very arc of Sirach 33:31's servant entreated as a brother.
cards.s_text: If you have a servant, entreat him as a brother: for you have need of him, as of your own soul: if you entreat him evil, and he run from you, which way will you go to seek him?
cards.t_text: He that delicately brings up his servant from a child shall have him become his son at the length.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:5 — *Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.* The wisdom behind Sirach 33:19's counsel to keep one's own governance and not surrender it to another.
cards.s_text: Give not your son and wife, your brother and friend, power over you while you livest, and give not your goods to another: lest it repent you, and you intreat for the same again.
cards.t_text: Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all your heart; and lean not unto your own understanding.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 42:24 — *All things are double one against another: and he has made nothing imperfect.* Ben Sira's own later word echoes Sirach 33:15 — two and two, one against another, all by perfect design.
cards.s_text: So look upon all the works of the Most High; and there are two and two, one against another.
cards.t_text: All things are double one against another: and he has made nothing imperfect.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil.* Moses sets before Israel the very pair Sirach 33:14 names — good against evil, life against death.
cards.s_text: Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
cards.t_text: See, I have set before you this day life and good, and death and evil;

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 15:7 — *For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashioneth every vessel with much labour for our service: yes, of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for clean uses, and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge.* Sirach's companion wisdom-book carries the same potter, the same clay, the same sovereign Judge as Sirach 33:13.
cards.s_text: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
cards.t_text: For the potter, tempering soft earth, fashioneth every vessel with much labour for our service: yes, of the same clay he makes both the vessels that serve for clean uses, and likewise also all such as serve to the contrary: but what is the use of either sort, the potter himself is the judge.

cards.note: Genesis 2:7 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.* The clay itself — Sirach 33:10 says all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth.
cards.s_text: And all men are from the ground, and Adam was created of earth:
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

cards.note: Isaiah 45:9 — *Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?* The clay that submits in Sirach 33:13 is the clay that must not strive with its Maker.
cards.s_text: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
cards.t_text: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What make you? or your work, He has no hands?

cards.note: Romans 9:21 — *Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?* The same sovereign sorting of Sirach 33:12 — some blessed and exalted, some brought low.
cards.s_text: Some of them has he blessed and exalted and some of them he sanctified, and set near himself: but some of them has he cursed and brought low, and turned out of their places.
cards.t_text: Has not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

cards.note: Romans 9:20 — *Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against Elohim (God)? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?* Paul forbids the vessel to dispute the hand that fashions it, as Sirach 33:13 sets man in the potter's hand.
cards.s_text: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
cards.t_text: Nay but, O man, who are you that repliest against Elohim (God)? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why have you made me thus?

cards.note: Jeremiah 18:6 — *O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? saith Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).* The exact figure of Sirach 33:13 — clay in the potter's hand, fashioned at his pleasure.
cards.s_text: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.
cards.t_text: O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? says Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 20:8 — *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.* The chief of the high days Sirach 33:9 says Yahuah hallowed above the ordinary days.
cards.s_text: Some of them has he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them has he made ordinary days.
cards.t_text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

cards.note: Genesis 1:14 — *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years.* The very distinguishing of seasons and feasts Sirach 33:8 says Yahuah altered, fixed in the lights of creation.
cards.s_text: By the knowledge of Yahuah (God) they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:

cards.note: Psalm 119:165 — *Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.* The opposite of Sirach 33:2's hypocrite who is as a ship in a storm — the law-lover rides unoffended.
cards.s_text: A wise man hates not the law; but he that is an hypocrite in it is as a ship in a storm.
cards.t_text: Great peace have they which love your law: and nothing shall offend them.

cards.note: Proverbs 1:7 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.* Sirach 33:1 likewise grounds deliverance in the fear of Yahuah, the root of all wisdom.
cards.s_text: There shall no evil happen to him that fears Yahuah (God); but in temptation even again he will deliver him.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.

cards.note: Romans 7:12 — *Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.* Paul confirms Sirach 33:2-3 that the wise man hates not the law, for the law is holy and faithful.
cards.s_text: A man of understanding trusts in the law; and the law is faithful to him, as an oracle.
cards.t_text: Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

cards.note: Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple.* The same trust Sirach 33:3 places in the faithful law that stands sure as an oracle.
cards.s_text: A man of understanding trusts in the law; and the law is faithful to him, as an oracle.
cards.t_text: The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:8 — *The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.* against the unheard curser of Sirach 34:24 stands the upright prayer that is Yahuah's delight.
cards.s_text: When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?
cards.t_text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

cards.note: Isaiah 1:16 — *Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil;* the futile washing of the man who touches the dead again in Sirach 34:25-26 is mended only by Isaiah's true cleansing — ceasing to do evil.
cards.s_text: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?
cards.t_text: Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil;

cards.note: Isaiah 1:15 — *And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.* the question of whose voice Yahuah will hear in Sirach 34:24 is answered by Isaiah's hidden eyes over blood-stained hands.
cards.s_text: When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?
cards.t_text: And when you spread forth your hands, I will hide my eyes from you: yea, when you make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

cards.note: Proverbs 28:9 — *He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.* the unheard prayer of the relapsing faster in Sirach 34:26 is the abomination-prayer of him who shuts his ear to the law.
cards.s_text: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?
cards.t_text: He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.

cards.note: *Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor doeth as one that killeth the son before his father’s eyes.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:20). *He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.* (Proverbs 28:8). Sirach says the man who brings an offering out of the goods of the poor is like one who kills a son in front of his father. Solomon says the man who grows rich by usury and unjust gain is only gathering it up for someone who will pity the poor. Both are talking about the same money. Taken from the poor and carried to the altar it is an abomination; held by the one who took it, it will not stay, for by the hand of Yahuah (God) it ends up with the merciful, and the one who gathered it is left with nothing but the blood on his hands.
cards.s_text: Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor doeth as one that killeth the son before his father’s eyes.
cards.t_text: He that by usury and unjust gain increases his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 24:14 — *Thou shalt not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of thy brethren, or of thy strangers that are in thy land within thy gates:* the bread of the needy that is their life in Sirach 34:21 is what Torah forbids oppressing.
cards.s_text: The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.
cards.t_text: You shall not oppress an hired servant that is poor and needy, whether he be of your brethren, or of your strangers that are in your land within your gates:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 24:15 — *At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it: lest he cry against thee unto Yahuah (LORD), and it be sin unto thee.* the Torah's same-day wage answers Sirach 34:22's defrauded labourer.
cards.s_text: He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.
cards.t_text: At his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and sets his heart upon it: lest he cry against you unto Yahuah (LORD), and it be sin unto you.

cards.note: James 5:4 — *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* the labourer defrauded of his hire whom Sirach 34:22 calls a bloodshed-victim is James' crying wage.
cards.s_text: He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.
cards.t_text: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, cries: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 35:12 — *Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices; for Yahuah (God) is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.* Ben Sira's own next chapter restates Sirach 34:19 — the unrighteous sacrifice Yahuah will not receive.
cards.s_text: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.
cards.t_text: Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive: and trust not to unrighteous sacrifices; for Yahuah (God) is judge, and with him is no respect of persons.

cards.note: Amos 5:21 — *I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies.* Yahuah's displeasure with the offerings of the wicked in Sirach 34:19 is Amos' hatred of feasts divorced from justice.
cards.s_text: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.
cards.t_text: I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies.

cards.note: Isaiah 1:11 — *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith Yahuah (LORD): I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.* the *multitude of sacrifices* that cannot pacify in Sirach 34:19 is Isaiah's wearisome multitude.
cards.s_text: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.
cards.t_text: To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? says Yahuah (LORD): I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats.

cards.note: Proverbs 15:8 — *The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.* the unaccepted gift of unjust men in Sirach 34:18 is set against the upright prayer Yahuah delights in.
cards.s_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.
cards.t_text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:27 — *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?* the *ridiculous* offering of the wrongdoer in Sirach 34:18 is Proverbs' abomination.
cards.s_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.
cards.t_text: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he brings it with a wicked mind?

cards.note: Psalm 34:8 — *O taste and see that Yahuah (LORD) is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.* the blessed soul that fears Yahuah in Sirach 34:15 is the man the Psalm calls blessed for trusting.
cards.s_text: Blessed is the soul of him that fears Yahuah (God): to whom does he look? and who is his strength?
cards.t_text: O taste and see that Yahuah (LORD) is good: blessed is the man that trusts in him.

cards.note: Psalm 34:7 — *The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.* the fearer who *shall not fear nor be afraid* (Sirach 34:14) is the one the Psalmist's angel encamps about.
cards.s_text: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.
cards.t_text: The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivers them.

cards.note: Proverbs 3:5 — *Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.* the hope that *saves them* in Sirach 34:13 is the trust that refuses to lean on self.
cards.s_text: The spirit of those that fear Yahuah (God) shall live; for their hope is in him that saves them.
cards.t_text: Trust in Yahuah (LORD) with all your heart; and lean not unto your own understanding.

cards.note: Jeremiah 23:28 — *The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat? saith Yahuah (LORD).* the chaff-and-wheat test sorts the failed dreams of Sirach 34:7 from the faithful word.
cards.s_text: For dreams have deceived many, and they have failed that put their trust in them.
cards.t_text: The prophet that has a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that has my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat? says Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Jeremiah 23:25 — *I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.* the dreams that *have deceived many* (Sirach 34:7) are Jeremiah's lying-prophet dreams.
cards.s_text: For dreams have deceived many, and they have failed that put their trust in them.
cards.t_text: I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 13:3 — *Thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) proveth you, to know whether ye love Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) with all your heart and with all your soul.* the dreamer is the proving Sirach 34:6 warns not to set the heart upon unless sent of the Most High.
cards.s_text: If they be not sent from the Most High in your visitation, set not your heart upon them.
cards.t_text: You shall not hearken unto the words of that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) proves you, to know whether you love Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) with all your heart and with all your soul.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 18:12 — *For all that do these things are an abomination unto Yahuah (LORD): and because of these abominations Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) doth drive them out from before thee.* the divination Sirach 34:5 dismisses is what Yahuah names abomination.
cards.s_text: Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain: and the heart fancieth, as a woman’s heart in travail.
cards.t_text: For all that do these things are an abomination unto Yahuah (LORD): and because of these abominations Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) does drive them out from before you.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 18:10 — *There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,* the Torah's flat ban on the soothsaying Sirach 34:5 calls vain.
cards.s_text: Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain: and the heart fancieth, as a woman’s heart in travail.
cards.t_text: There shall not be found among you any one that makes his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,

cards.note: Psalm 9:8 — *And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.* David's righteous Judge of the world is the One Sirach 35:18-19 waits on to render to every man according to his deeds.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen; till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptre of the unrighteous;
cards.t_text: And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.

cards.note: Luke 18:8 — *I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of Adam cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?* The speedy avenging answers Sirach 35:18's promise that Yahuah will not be slack to repay vengeance and break the sceptre of the unrighteous.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen; till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptre of the unrighteous;
cards.t_text: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of Adam comes, shall he find faith on the earth?

cards.note: Luke 18:7 — *And shall not Elohim (God) avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?* The Messiah's parable of the persistent widow resolves Sirach 35:19 — Yahuah will judge the cause of His people who cry to Him.
cards.s_text: Till he have rendered to every man according to his deeds, and to the works of men according to their devices; till he have judged the cause of his people, and made them to rejoice in his mercy.
cards.t_text: And shall not Elohim (God) avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them?

cards.note: Psalm 9:9 — *Yahuah (LORD) also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.* David's refuge for the oppressed is the same hearing ear Sirach 35:13 promises to the poor man's prayer.
cards.s_text: He will not accept any person against a poor man, but will hear the prayer of the oppressed.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble.

cards.note: James 5:4 — *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* James echoes Sirach 35:14 — the cry of the wronged reaches the ears of Yahuah, no respecter of persons.
cards.s_text: He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.
