cards.t_text: And like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to Yahuah (LORD) with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.

cards.note: Jeremiah 1:5 — *Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.* Sirach 49:7's prophet sanctified in his mother's womb is Jeremiah, known and set apart before birth.
cards.s_text: For they entreated him evil, who nevertheless was a prophet, sanctified in his mother’s womb, that he might root out, and afflict, and destroy; and that he might build up also, and plant.
cards.t_text: Before I formed you in the belly I knew you; and before you came forth out of the womb I sanctified you, and I ordained you a prophet unto the nations.

cards.note: Jeremiah 1:10 — *See, I have this day set thee over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.* Sirach 49:7's charge to root out, afflict, destroy, build and plant is Jeremiah's own commission quoted almost exactly.
cards.s_text: For they entreated him evil, who nevertheless was a prophet, sanctified in his mother’s womb, that he might root out, and afflict, and destroy; and that he might build up also, and plant.
cards.t_text: See, I have this day set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, to build, and to plant.

cards.note: Jeremiah 1:2 — *To whom the word of Yahuah (LORD) came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Yahudah (Judah), in the thirteenth year of his reign.* The prophet by whose word Sirach 49:6 says the city was burnt began to prophesy under Josiah, binding this thread to the praise of Josiah just before.
cards.s_text: They burnt the chosen city of the sanctuary, and made the streets desolate, according to the prophecy of Jeremias.
cards.t_text: To whom the word of Yahuah (LORD) came in the days of Josiah the son of Amon king of Yahudah (Judah), in the thirteenth year of his reign.

cards.note: Ezekiel 1:4 — *And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.* This is the opening of the glorious vision Sirach 49:8 says Ezekiel saw.
cards.s_text: It was Ezekiel who saw the glorious vision, which was shewed him upon the chariot of the cherubims.
cards.t_text: And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber, out of the midst of the fire.

cards.note: Ezekiel 1:16 — *The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.* The chariot of the cherubim in Sirach 49:8 is this wheel within a wheel beneath the living creatures.
cards.s_text: It was Ezekiel who saw the glorious vision, which was shewed him upon the chariot of the cherubims.
cards.t_text: The appearance of the wheels and their work was like unto the colour of a beryl: and they four had one likeness: and their appearance and their work was as it were a wheel in the middle of a wheel.

cards.note: Ezekiel 1:28 — *As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahuah (LORD). And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake.* The glorious vision Ezekiel saw in Sirach 49:8 is the very likeness of the glory of Yahuah enthroned above the chariot.
cards.s_text: It was Ezekiel who saw the glorious vision, which was shewed him upon the chariot of the cherubims.
cards.t_text: As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahuah (LORD). And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake.

cards.note: Hosea 1:1 — *The word of Yahuah (LORD) that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Yahudah (Judah), and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Yashar'el (Israel).* Hosea heads the twelve prophets Sirach 49:10 blesses, the first of the company sent to comfort and regather scattered Jacob.
cards.s_text: And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope.
cards.t_text: The word of Yahuah (LORD) that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Yahudah (Judah), and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Zechariah 1:3 — *Therefore say thou unto them, Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); Turn ye unto me, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and I will turn unto you, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* The twelve who comforted Jacob in Sirach 49:10 spoke this turning-and-return that is the heart of the gathering.
cards.s_text: And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope.
cards.t_text: Therefore say you unto them, Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); Turn you unto me, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and I will turn unto you, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).

cards.note: Zechariah 1:17 — *Cry yet, saying, Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); My cities through prosperity shall yet be spread abroad; and Yahuah (LORD) shall yet comfort Zion, and shall yet choose Jerusalem.* The assured hope by which the twelve delivered Jacob in Sirach 49:10 is this promise that Yahuah will yet comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem.
cards.s_text: And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope.
cards.t_text: Cry yet, saying, Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); My cities through prosperity shall yet be spread abroad; and Yahuah (LORD) shall yet comfort Zion, and shall yet choose Jerusalem.

cards.note: Haggai 2:23 — *In that day, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith Yahuah (LORD), and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* Sirach 49:11's Zerubbabel "as a signet on the right hand" quotes Yahuah's own word making him a signet.
cards.s_text: How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand:
cards.t_text: In that day, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), will I take you, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, says Yahuah (LORD), and will make you as a signet: for I have chosen you, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).

cards.note: Zechariah 4:9 — *The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it; and thou shalt know that Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) hath sent me unto you.* The house builded in Sirach 49:12 by Zerubbabel and Jeshua is this temple whose foundation and finishing Zechariah foretold.
cards.s_text: So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory.
cards.t_text: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house; his hands shall also finish it; and you shall know that Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) has sent me unto you.

cards.note: Ezra 3:8 — *Now in the second year of their coming unto the house of Elohim (God) at Jerusalem, in the second month, began Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the remnant of their brethren the priests and the Levites, and all they that were come out of the captivity unto Jerusalem; and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to set forward the work of the house of Yahuah (LORD).* The "Jesus the son of Josedec" of Sirach 49:12 is Jeshua son of Jozadak the high priest here — not the Messiah — who with Zerubbabel began the house.
cards.s_text: So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory.
cards.t_text: Now in the second year of their coming unto the house of Elohim (God) at Jerusalem, in the second month, began Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the remnant of their brethren the priests and the Levites, and all they that were come out of the captivity unto Jerusalem; and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to set forward the work of the house of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Nehemiah 2:17 — *Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.* Nehemiah, who in Sirach 49:13 raised up the fallen walls and set up the gates, calls Israel to rebuild Jerusalem's wall and gates.
cards.s_text: And among the elect was Neemias, whose renown is great, who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again.
cards.t_text: Then said I unto them, You see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lies waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach.

cards.note: Genesis 5:24 — *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.* This is the taking from the earth Sirach 49:14 says no other man was like.
cards.s_text: But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch; for he was taken from the earth.
cards.t_text: And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.

cards.note: 1 Enoch 71:5 — *And he translated my spirit into the heaven of heavens, And I saw there as it were a structure built of crystals, And between those crystals tongues of living fire.* Enoch's own book unfolds the translation Sirach 49:14 remembers, his spirit carried up to the heaven of heavens.
cards.s_text: But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch; for he was taken from the earth.
cards.t_text: And he translated my spirit into the heaven of heavens, And I saw there as it were a structure built of crystals, And between those crystals tongues of living fire.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:23 — *And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.* Jubilees tells where Enoch went when, as Sirach 49:14 says, he was taken from the earth — into Eden in majesty and honour.
cards.s_text: But upon the earth was no man created like Enoch; for he was taken from the earth.
cards.t_text: And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writes down the condemnation and judgment of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men.

cards.note: Genesis 50:25 — *And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.* Joseph's bones were regarded of Yahuah in Sirach 49:15 because of this dying oath laid on Israel.
cards.s_text: Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brothers, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from hence.

cards.note: Exodus 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* The bones Sirach 49:15 says were regarded of Yahuah were carried up at the Exodus exactly as Joseph had sworn.
cards.s_text: Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brothers, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and you shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:5 — *And he commanded the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.* Jubilees carries the same charge regarding Joseph's bones that Sirach 49:15 honours.
cards.s_text: Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brothers, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* Seth, honoured among men in Sirach 49:16, is the appointed seed through whom the line was kept.
cards.s_text: Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.
cards.t_text: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, has appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:29 — *And at the close of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week in the sixth year thereof, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.* Adam, set above every living thing in creation in Sirach 49:16, is here the first father of all, buried in the land of his own creation.
cards.s_text: Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.
cards.t_text: And at the close of the nineteenth jubilee, in the seventh week in the sixth year thereof, Adam died, and all his sons buried him in the land of his creation, and he was the first to be buried in the earth.

cards.note: Matthew 11:28 — *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* The congregation bowing to receive a blessing from the Most High (Sirach 50:21) finds its fulfilment in the wisdom-call of the Messiah, who opens His arms to give rest to all who come.
cards.s_text: And they bowed themselves down to worship the second time, that they might receive a blessing from the Most High.
cards.t_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

cards.note: Numbers 6:27 — *And they shall put my name upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and I will bless them.* Simon rejoicing in the Name as he blesses the people (Sirach 50:20) places that very Name upon Israel, as the blessing was ordained to do.
cards.s_text: Then he went down, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to give the blessing of Yahuah (God) with his lips, and to rejoice in his name.
cards.t_text: And they shall put my name upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and I will bless them.

cards.note: Numbers 6:25 — *Yahuah (LORD) make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:* the blessing of Yahuah Simon spoke with his lips over the congregation (Sirach 50:20) is the word of the shining face the priests were given to pronounce.
cards.s_text: Then he went down, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to give the blessing of Yahuah (God) with his lips, and to rejoice in his name.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) make his face shine upon you, and be gracious unto you:

cards.note: Numbers 6:23 — *Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying, On this wise ye shall bless the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying unto them,* Simon lifting his hands to give the blessing of Yahuah (Sirach 50:20) is performing the very Aaronic blessing Yahuah commanded the priests to speak over the people.
cards.s_text: Then he went down, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to give the blessing of Yahuah (God) with his lips, and to rejoice in his name.
cards.t_text: Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying, On this wise you shall bless the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying unto them,

cards.note: Hebrews 7:24 — *But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.* The sons of Aaron with the oblations in their hands (Sirach 50:13) were many priests who passed by death, the shadow of the one Priest whose priesthood does not pass.
cards.s_text: So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory, and the oblations of Yahuah (God) in their hands, before all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: But this man, because he continues ever, has an unchangeable priesthood.

cards.note: Hebrews 7:11 — *If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek), and not be called after the order of Aaron?* The sons of Aaron in their glory (Sirach 50:13) are the Levitical priesthood whose very glory Hebrews shows pointed beyond itself to another priest.
cards.s_text: So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory, and the oblations of Yahuah (God) in their hands, before all the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek), and not be called after the order of Aaron?

cards.note: *He stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour to the most high King of all.* (Ecclesiasticus 50:15). *Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.* (Hebrews 9:12). Simon the high priest finishes the altar service by pouring the blood of the grape at the foot of the altar, a sweet savour to the most high King. Yahusha (Jesus) took that same cup of the vine on his last night and said *this is my blood of the new testament* (Matthew 26:28). Hebrews says he then entered the holy place once, not with the blood of goats and calves but with his own. The wine poured at the altar's foot was showing in the fruit of the grape what the Messiah (Christ) would do in his own blood; Simon poured the picture, and the high priest after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) poured out the thing itself.
cards.s_text: He stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour to the most high King of all.
cards.t_text: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.

cards.note: Hebrews 9:7 — *But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:* Simon pouring out the blood of the grape at the foot of the altar (Sirach 50:15) enacts the once-a-year, not-without-blood service Hebrews names as the figure of the true.
cards.s_text: He stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour to the most high King of all.
cards.t_text: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:

cards.note: Leviticus 16:16 — *And he shall make an atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and because of their transgressions in all their sins: and so shall he do for the tabernacle of the congregation, that remaineth among them in the midst of their uncleanness.* Simon finishing the service at the altar (Sirach 50:14) is the high priest performing the atonement Aaron was commanded to make for the holy place.
cards.s_text: And finishing the service at the altar, that he might adorn the offering of the most high Almighty,
cards.t_text: And he shall make an atonement for the holy place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and because of their transgressions in all their sins: and so shall he do for the tabernacle of the congregation, that remains among them in the midst of their uncleanness.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 24:14 — *I was exalted like a palm tree in En-gaddi, and as a rose plant in Jericho, as a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, and grew up as a plane tree by the water.* Simon as a fair olive tree budding forth fruit (Sirach 50:10) echoes Wisdom's self-portrait as the fair olive tree and palm planted by the waters.
cards.s_text: And as a fair olive tree budding forth fruit, and as a cypress tree which grows up to the clouds.
cards.t_text: I was exalted like a palm tree in En-gaddi, and as a rose plant in Jericho, as a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, and grew up as a plane tree by the water.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 24:13 — *I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon.* Simon compassed about as a young cedar in Libanus (Sirach 50:12) is robed in the very tree-imagery Wisdom used of herself in this same book.
cards.s_text: When he took the portions out of the priests’ hands, he himself stood by the hearth of the altar, compassed about, as a young cedar in Libanus; and as palm trees compassed they him round about.
cards.t_text: I was exalted like a cedar in Libanus, and as a cypress tree upon the mountains of Hermon.

cards.note: 2 Peter 1:19 — *We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:* the priest as the morning star in the midst of a cloud (Sirach 50:6) foreshadows the day star Peter says will arise in the hearts of the faithful.
cards.s_text: He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full:
cards.t_text: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto you do well that you take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts:

cards.note: Revelation 4:3 — *And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald.* The rainbow about the glory of Simon at the altar (Sirach 50:7) is a glimpse of the rainbow John saw encircling the throne itself.
cards.s_text: As the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, and as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds:
cards.t_text: And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald.

cards.note: Genesis 9:13 — *I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.* The high priest as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds (Sirach 50:7) wears the very covenant-sign Yahuah set in the cloud.
cards.s_text: As the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, and as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds:
cards.t_text: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

cards.note: Malachi 4:2 — *But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.* Simon as the sun shining upon the temple (Sirach 50:7) is the priestly shadow of the Sun of righteousness the prophet promised to rise over those who fear the Name.
cards.s_text: As the sun shining upon the temple of the Most High, and as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds:
cards.t_text: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and you shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.

cards.note: Hebrews 8:2 — *A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which Yahuah (Lord) pitched, and not man.* Simon building the high fortress of the wall about the temple (Sirach 50:2) is the made-with-hands figure of the true tabernacle pitched by Yahuah Himself.
cards.s_text: And by him was built from the foundation the double height, the high fortress of the wall about the temple:
cards.t_text: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.

cards.note: Hebrews 8:1 — *Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;* the earthly high priest who repaired the temple (Sirach 50:1) is the shadow of the better High Priest enthroned in the true heavens.
cards.s_text: Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple:
cards.t_text: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;

cards.note: Exodus 28:2 — *And thou shalt make holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.* Simon repairing the house and serving in priestly office (Sirach 50:1) stands in the line of Aaron, the first robed for glory and beauty.
cards.s_text: Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple:
cards.t_text: And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother for glory and for beauty.

cards.note: Psalm 18:5 — *The sorrows of hell compassed me about: the snares of death prevented me.* The snare of the slandering tongue that drew Ben Sira's soul near to death is David's same snare of death encompassing him.
cards.s_text: By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue my soul drew near even to death, my life was near to the hell beneath.
cards.t_text: The sorrows of hell compassed me about: the snares of death prevented me.

cards.note: Psalm 18:6 — *In my distress I called upon Yahuah (LORD), and cried unto my Elohim (God): he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.* As Ben Sira's life drew near to the hell beneath, the righteous one's cry rises to Yahuah's temple and is heard.
cards.s_text: By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue my soul drew near even to death, my life was near to the hell beneath.
cards.t_text: In my distress I called upon Yahuah (LORD), and cried unto my Elohim (God): he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.

cards.note: Psalm 116:3 — *The sorrows of death compassed me, and the pains of hell gat hold upon me: I found trouble and sorrow.* The very nearness to death that Ben Sira describes is sung word-for-thought in the deliverance psalm.
cards.s_text: By an accusation to the king from an unrighteous tongue my soul drew near even to death, my life was near to the hell beneath.
cards.t_text: The sorrows of death compassed me, and the pains of hell gat hold upon me: I found trouble and sorrow.

cards.note: Psalm 34:6 — *This poor man cried, and Yahuah (LORD) heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.* Ben Sira's defender and helper who preserved his body is the same Yahuah who hears the poor man's cry and saves him from every trouble.
cards.s_text: For you are my defender and helper, and has preserved my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lips that forge lies, and has been my helper against my adversaries:
cards.t_text: This poor man cried, and Yahuah (LORD) heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.

cards.note: Psalm 34:19 — *Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but Yahuah (LORD) delivereth him out of them all.* Ben Sira's recollection that Yahuah delivers such as wait for him out of the hands of the enemies is this psalm's plain promise to the righteous.
cards.s_text: Then thought I upon your mercy, O Yahuah (God), and upon your acts of old, how you deliverest such as wait for you, and savest them out of the hands of the enemies.
cards.t_text: Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but Yahuah (LORD) delivers him out of them all.

cards.note: Psalm 34:17 — *The righteous cry, and Yahuah (LORD) heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.* Ben Sira lifting his supplications from the earth and praying for deliverance from death is exactly the cry that Yahuah hears.
cards.s_text: Then lifted I up my supplications from the earth, and prayed for deliverance from death.
cards.t_text: The righteous cry, and Yahuah (LORD) hears, and delivers them out of all their troubles.

cards.note: Psalm 116:17 — *I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* The thanksgiving and singing of praise that answers the heard prayer is David's same sacrifice of thanksgiving for deliverance.
cards.s_text: I will praise your name continually, and will sing praises with thanksgiving; and so my prayer was heard:
cards.t_text: I will offer to you the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Psalm 116:7 — *Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for Yahuah (LORD) hath dealt bountifully with thee.* As Ben Sira's heard prayer turns to continual praise, the rescued soul of the psalm is called back to its rest in Yahuah's bounty.
cards.s_text: I will praise your name continually, and will sing praises with thanksgiving; and so my prayer was heard:
cards.t_text: Return unto your rest, O my soul; for Yahuah (LORD) has dealt bountifully with you.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:17 — *I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.* Ben Sira seeking wisdom from his youth up, from the flower till the grape was ripe, is the early seeker whom Wisdom promises to be found by.
cards.s_text: Even from the flower till the grape was ripe has my heart delighted in her: my foot went the right way, from my youth up sought I after her.
cards.t_text: I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.

cards.note: Proverbs 2:4 — *If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as for hid treasures.* Praying for wisdom before the temple and seeking her out even to the end is the searching for hid treasure that Solomon commands.
cards.s_text: I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.
cards.t_text: If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hid treasures;

cards.note: Proverbs 2:6 — *For Yahuah (LORD) giveth wisdom: out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.* Ben Sira ascribing glory to him that gives him wisdom names Yahuah as the giver, just as Solomon does.
cards.s_text: I profited in it, therefore will I ascribe glory to him that gives me wisdom.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (LORD) gives wisdom: out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Ben Sira desiring wisdom openly in prayer from his youth is the same temple-prayer his apocryphal brother prays — the deuterocanon's own self-witness.
cards.s_text: When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer.
cards.t_text: Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.

cards.note: James 1:5 — *If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.* Ben Sira's lifelong asking for wisdom in prayer is exactly the asking James promises Elohim answers liberally.
cards.s_text: When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer.
cards.t_text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that gives to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:1 — *Doth not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?* Ben Sira opening his mouth to call the unlearned to the house of learning is Wisdom herself crying out for hearers.
cards.s_text: Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.
cards.t_text: Does not wisdom cry? and understanding put forth her voice?

cards.note: Proverbs 8:4 — *Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.* The teacher's summons to draw near and dwell in learning is Wisdom's universal call to the sons of man.
cards.s_text: Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.
cards.t_text: Unto you, O men, I call; and my voice is to the sons of man.

cards.note: Isaiah 55:1 — *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.* Ben Sira's cry to the thirsty soul to buy wisdom without money is Isaiah's free invitation almost word for word.
cards.s_text: I opened my mouth, and said, Buy her for yourselves without money.
cards.t_text: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come you to the waters, and he that has no money; come you, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

cards.note: Isaiah 55:3 — *Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.* To the thirsty souls Ben Sira chides, Isaiah promises that coming and hearing makes the soul live in everlasting covenant.
cards.s_text: Wherefore are you slow, and what say you to these things, seeing your souls are very thirsty?
cards.t_text: Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.

cards.note: Matthew 11:28 — *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* Ben Sira's *put your neck under the yoke* and *much rest* is the very invitation the Messiah takes up, calling the labouring to come to Him for rest.
cards.s_text: Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.
cards.t_text: Come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

cards.note: Matthew 11:29 — *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* Where Ben Sira says put your neck under the yoke and receive instruction, Yahusha makes the wisdom-yoke His own and gives rest unto the soul.
cards.s_text: Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.
cards.t_text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and you shall find rest unto your souls.

cards.note: Matthew 11:30 — *For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* Ben Sira's testimony that the yoke of wisdom brings but little labour and much rest is fulfilled in the Messiah's easy yoke and light burden.
cards.s_text: Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.
cards.t_text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:5 — *O ye simple, understand wisdom: and, ye fools, be ye of an understanding heart.* Ben Sira bidding the unlearned receive instruction under the yoke is Wisdom's same appeal to the simple to gain an understanding heart.
cards.s_text: Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.
cards.t_text: O you simple, understand wisdom: and, you fools, be you of an understanding heart.

cards.note: Matthew 5:6 — *Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.* The thirsty soul Ben Sira sends to labour for wisdom is the hungering, thirsting one the Messiah promises shall be filled.
cards.s_text: Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.
cards.t_text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.

cards.note: Matthew 5:12 — *Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.* Ben Sira's promise that in his time Yahuah will give the worker his reward is the Sermon's great reward in heaven for the faithful.
cards.s_text: Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.
cards.t_text: Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.

cards.note: Proverbs 8:35 — *For whoso findeth me findeth life, and shall obtain favour of Yahuah (LORD).* Ben Sira's call to rejoice in Yahuah's mercy and await the reward rests on the truth that whoso finds wisdom finds life and Yahuah's favour.
cards.s_text: Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise.
cards.t_text: For whoso finds me finds life, and shall obtain favour of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 21:23 — *His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God);) that thy land be not defiled, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee for an inheritance.* Tobit's secret burial of the slain in Tobit 1:17-18 keeps this very Torah command not to leave a body exposed.
cards.s_text: And my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.
cards.t_text: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but you shall in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God);) that your land be not defiled, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you for an inheritance.

cards.note: Tobit 12:9 — *For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:* Raphael's word later in the book weighs the worth of the many alms Tobit gives his brothers in Tobit 1:16.
cards.s_text: And in the time of Enemessar I gave many alms to my brothers, and gave my bread to the hungry,
cards.t_text: For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:

cards.note: Matthew 25:35 — *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:* The King's reckoning of mercy at the judgment names the very deeds Tobit does for his nation in Tobit 1:17.
cards.s_text: And my clothes to the naked: and if I saw any of my nation dead, or cast about the walls of Nineve, I buried him.
cards.t_text: For I was an hungred, and you gave me meat: I was thirsty, and you gave me drink: I was a stranger, and you took me in:

cards.note: Isaiah 58:7 — *Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?* This is the fast Yahuah chooses, lived out exactly in Tobit's bread to the hungry and clothes to the naked in Tobit 1:16-17.
cards.s_text: And in the time of Enemessar I gave many alms to my brothers, and gave my bread to the hungry,
cards.t_text: Is it not to deal your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor that are cast out to your house? when you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you hide not thyself from your own flesh?

cards.note: Daniel 1:8 — *But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.* Daniel's refusal of the king's defiling food in Babylon is the twin of Tobit keeping himself from the bread of the Gentiles in Tobit 1:11.
cards.s_text: But I kept myself from eating;
cards.t_text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And the third I gave to them to whom it was meet, as Debora my father’s mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphan by my father.* (Tobit 1:8). Tobit 1:8 shows the old man doing as a young man what he later teaches: the third tithe given to those to whom it was meet, as his grandmother Debora had commanded him. Three generations carry it, Debora to Tobit, Tobit to Tobias. The alms he charges on his son in chapter 4 is a tithe he had been paying since he was an orphan.
cards.s_text: And the third I gave to them to whom it was meet, as Debora my father’s mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphan by my father.
cards.t_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.

cards.note: Numbers 18:21 — *And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Yashar'el (Israel) for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.* This is the first tenth Tobit gives to the priests, the children of Aaron, at the altar in Tobit 1:6.
cards.s_text: But I alone went often to Jerusalem at the feasts, as it was ordained to all the people of Yashar'el (Israel) by an everlasting decree, having the firstfruits and tenths of increase, with that which was first shorn; and them gave I at the altar to the priests the children of Aaron.
cards.t_text: And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Yashar'el (Israel) for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 14:23 — *And thou shalt eat before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks; that thou mayest learn to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) always.* This is the second tenth Tobit carries up and spends every year at Jerusalem in Tobit 1:7.
cards.s_text: The first tenth part of all increase I gave to the sons of Aaron, who ministered at Jerusalem: another tenth part I sold away, and went, and spent it every year at Jerusalem:
cards.t_text: And you shall eat before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of your corn, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstlings of your herds and of your flocks; that you may learn to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) always.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 14:22 — *Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed, that the field bringeth forth year by year.* This is the very tithe of increase Tobit faithfully renders in Tobit 1:7.
cards.s_text: The first tenth part of all increase I gave to the sons of Aaron, who ministered at Jerusalem: another tenth part I sold away, and went, and spent it every year at Jerusalem:
cards.t_text: You shall truly tithe all the increase of your seed, that the field brings forth year by year.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 12:11 — *Then there shall be a place which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall choose to cause his name to dwell there; thither shall ye bring all that I command you; your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, and the heave offering of your hand, and all your choice vows which ye vow unto Yahuah (LORD):* This is the one chosen house of Jerusalem from which Naphtali fell in Tobit 1:4.
cards.s_text: And when I was in my own country, in the land of Yashar'el (Israel) being but young, all the tribe of Nephthali my father fell from the house of Jerusalem, which was chosen out of all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), that all the tribes should sacrifice there, where the temple of the habitation of the Most High was consecrated and built for all ages.
cards.t_text: Then there shall be a place which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall choose to cause his name to dwell there; thither shall you bring all that I command you; your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, your tithes, and the heave offering of your hand, and all your choice vows which you vow unto Yahuah (LORD):

cards.note: 1 Kings 12:28 — *Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.* Jeroboam's calf is the very 'heifer Baal' Tobit's tribe sacrificed to in Tobit 1:5.
cards.s_text: Now all the tribes which together revolted, and the house of my father Nephthali, sacrificed to the heifer Baal.
cards.t_text: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold your gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Ezekiel 37:21 — *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* The scattered tribe of Naphtali named in Tobit 1:1 is exactly the people Yahuah promises to regather, not to replace.
cards.s_text: The book of the words of Tobit, son of Tobiel, the son of Ananiel, the son of Aduel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asael, of the tribe of Nephthali;
cards.t_text: And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 28:64 — *And Yahuah (LORD) shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.* Tobit's captivity in Tobit 1:2 is Moses' covenant warning come to pass upon the house of Israel.
cards.s_text: Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians was led captive out of Thisbe, which is at the right hand of that city, which is called properly Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) shall scatter you among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there you shall serve other gods, which neither you nor your fathers have known, even wood and stone.

cards.note: 2 Kings 17:23 — *Until Yahuah (LORD) removed Yashar'el (Israel) out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Yashar'el (Israel) carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.* Tobit of the tribe of Naphtali in Tobit 1:1 is one of the very exiles this verse buries in the nations.
cards.s_text: The book of the words of Tobit, son of Tobiel, the son of Ananiel, the son of Aduel, the son of Gabael, of the seed of Asael, of the tribe of Nephthali;
cards.t_text: Until Yahuah (LORD) removed Yashar'el (Israel) out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets. So was Yashar'el (Israel) carried away out of their own land to Assyria unto this day.

cards.note: 2 Kings 17:6 — *In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.* This is the same Assyrian deportation that swept Tobit of Naphtali into Nineveh in Tobit 1:2.
cards.s_text: Who in the time of Enemessar king of the Assyrians was led captive out of Thisbe, which is at the right hand of that city, which is called properly Nephthali in Galilee above Aser.
cards.t_text: In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

cards.note: Matthew 6:4 — *That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.* Tobit's hidden alms and righteous deeds, mocked by his wife, are exactly the secret giving the Father sees and openly rewards.
cards.s_text: But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.
cards.t_text: That your alms may be in secret: and your Father which sees in secret himself shall reward you openly.

cards.note: Tobit 4:10 — *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Though Tobit sits afflicted in darkness, his alms are the treasure that, by the book's own teaching, delivers from death.
cards.s_text: But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.
cards.t_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.* (Tobit 2:14). Blind and poor, Tobit is mocked by his own wife: where are your alms and your righteous deeds now? He does not answer her reproach by giving up the practice. Two chapters later he hands the same practice to his son as the way to keep the face of Yahuah (God) toward him. The reproach did not move him, because alms were never a trade for comfort; they were covenant life, kept in blindness as in sight.
cards.s_text: But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.
cards.t_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.

cards.note: Job 2:10 — *But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of Elohim (God), and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.* Tobit, abashed yet not cursing Yahuah, answers his wife's reproach with the same steadfastness Job showed his.
cards.s_text: But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.
cards.t_text: But he said unto her, You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. What? shall we receive good at the hand of Elohim (God), and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

cards.note: Job 2:9 — *Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse Elohim (God), and die.* As Job's wife reproached him in his suffering, so Anna reproaches Tobit, taunting the alms and righteous deeds that seem to have gained him nothing.
cards.s_text: But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.
cards.t_text: Then said his wife unto him, Do you still retain your integrity? curse Elohim (God), and die.

cards.note: Job 2:7 — *So went Satan forth from the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.* As Job's body was smitten head to foot, so Tobit's eyes are struck with whiteness — the just man afflicted in the flesh.
cards.s_text: And I knew not that there were sparrows in the wall, and my eyes being open, the sparrows muted warm dung into my eyes, and a whiteness came in my eyes: and I went to the physicians, but they helped me not: moreover Achiacharus did nourish me, until I went into Elymais.
cards.t_text: So went Satan forth from the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

cards.note: Job 1:1 — *There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared Elohim (God), and eschewed evil.* Tobit, like Job, is a God-fearing and upright man, so his sudden blindness raises the same question of why the righteous suffer.
cards.s_text: And I knew not that there were sparrows in the wall, and my eyes being open, the sparrows muted warm dung into my eyes, and a whiteness came in my eyes: and I went to the physicians, but they helped me not: moreover Achiacharus did nourish me, until I went into Elymais.
cards.t_text: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared Elohim (God), and eschewed evil.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 16:10 — *And thou shalt keep the feast of weeks unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with a tribute of a freewill offering of thine hand, which thou shalt give unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), according as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath blessed thee:* Tobit keeps this same feast of weeks even in the captivity of Nineveh, the appointed time held fast in exile.
cards.s_text: Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored to me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks, there was a good dinner prepared me, in the which I sat down to eat.
cards.t_text: And you shall keep the feast of weeks unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with a tribute of a freewill offering of your hand, which you shall give unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), according as Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has blessed you:

cards.note: Amos 8:10 — *And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring up sackcloth upon all loins, and baldness upon every head; and I will make it as the mourning of an only son, and the end thereof as a bitter day.* Tobit quotes this prophecy by name, watching his feast of Pentecost turn to mourning over the slain brother in fulfilment of Amos.
cards.s_text: Remembering that prophecy of Amos, as he said, Your feasts shall be turned into mourning, and all your mirth into lamentation.
cards.t_text: And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will bring up sackcloth upon all loins, and baldness upon every head; and I will make it as the mourning of an only son, and the end thereof as a bitter day.

cards.note: Tobit 12:13 — *And when you did not delay to rise up, and leave your dinner, to go and cover the dead, your good deed was not hid from me: but I was with you.* Raphael reveals that the angel of Yahuah stood beside Tobit in this very burial of chapter 2, his good deed not hid.
cards.s_text: Therefore I wept: and after the going down of the sun I went and made a grave, and buried him.
cards.t_text: And when you did not delay to rise up, and leave your dinner, to go and cover the dead, your good deed was not hid from me: but I was with you.

cards.note: Matthew 8:22 — *But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.* The neighbours mock Tobit's burying as folly, yet the kindness to the dead he renders is the very faithfulness that following requires.
cards.s_text: But my neighbours mocked me, and said, This man is not yet afraid to be put to death for this matter: who fled away; and yet, lo, he burieth the dead again.
cards.t_text: But Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.

cards.note: Genesis 23:19 — *And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.* As Abraham labored to bury his own dead in dignity, so Tobit digs a grave for a brother of his nation at his own risk.
cards.s_text: Therefore I wept: and after the going down of the sun I went and made a grave, and buried him.
cards.t_text: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same is Hebron in the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 21:23 — *His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God);) that thy land be not defiled, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee for an inheritance.* Tobit buries before sunset and the same night precisely to keep this command that the land not be defiled by an unburied body.
cards.s_text: Therefore I wept: and after the going down of the sun I went and made a grave, and buried him.
cards.t_text: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but you shall in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God);) that your land be not defiled, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you for an inheritance.

cards.note: Revelation 20:2 — *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.* Raphael sent *to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit* (3:17) is the seed-war in miniature — the angel laying hold on and binding the adversary.
cards.s_text: And Raphael was sent to heal them both, that is, to scale away the whiteness of Tobit’s eyes, and to give Sara the daughter of Raguel for a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit; and to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit; because she belonged to Tobias by right of inheritance. The selfsame time came Tobit home, and entered into his house, and Sara the daughter of Raguel came down from her upper chamber.
cards.t_text: And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years,

cards.note: Luke 1:13 — *But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.* The angel sent because the prayer is heard (3:16-17) is the same word Gabriel brings Zacharias at the altar of incense.
cards.s_text: And Raphael was sent to heal them both, that is, to scale away the whiteness of Tobit’s eyes, and to give Sara the daughter of Raguel for a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit; and to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit; because she belonged to Tobias by right of inheritance. The selfsame time came Tobit home, and entered into his house, and Sara the daughter of Raguel came down from her upper chamber.
cards.t_text: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for your prayer is heard; and your wife Elisabeth shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.

cards.note: Daniel 9:21 — *Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation.* Raphael sent in answer to the prayers (3:17) matches Gabriel dispatched to Daniel in the very act of praying.
cards.s_text: And Raphael was sent to heal them both, that is, to scale away the whiteness of Tobit’s eyes, and to give Sara the daughter of Raguel for a wife to Tobias the son of Tobit; and to bind Asmodeus the evil spirit; because she belonged to Tobias by right of inheritance. The selfsame time came Tobit home, and entered into his house, and Sara the daughter of Raguel came down from her upper chamber.
cards.t_text: Yea, whiles I was speaking in prayer, even the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning, being caused to fly swiftly, touched me about the time of the evening oblation.

cards.note: Psalm 34:17 — *The righteous cry, and Yahuah (LORD) heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.* Tobit and Sarah cry and are heard (3:16) — delivered out of their troubles exactly as the psalm promises.
cards.s_text: So the prayers of them both were heard before the majesty of the great Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The righteous cry, and Yahuah (LORD) hears, and delivers them out of all their troubles.

cards.note: Psalm 34:15 — *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry.* Both prayers *heard before the majesty of the great Yahuah* (3:16) prove the psalm true: His ears are open to the afflicted righteous.
cards.s_text: So the prayers of them both were heard before the majesty of the great Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are upon the righteous, and his ears are open unto their cry.

cards.note: Psalm 25:17 — *The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.* Sarah's *Take me out of the earth, that I may hear no more the reproach* (3:13) is the same cry to be brought out of an unbearable distress.
cards.s_text: And say, Take me out of the earth, that I may hear no more the reproach.
cards.t_text: The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring you me out of my distresses.

cards.note: Psalm 25:15 — *Mine eyes are ever toward Yahuah (LORD); for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.* Sarah's eyes fixed toward Yahuah (3:12) trust, like David, to be plucked out of the snare that has taken her seven husbands.
cards.s_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), I set my eyes and my face toward you,
cards.t_text: My eyes are ever toward Yahuah (LORD); for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.

cards.note: Psalm 25:1 — *Unto thee, O Yahuah (LORD), do I lift up my soul.* Sarah setting *my eyes and my face toward you* (3:12) lifts her soul exactly as the psalmist does in his distress.
cards.s_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), I set my eyes and my face toward you,
cards.t_text: Unto you, O Yahuah (LORD), do I lift up my soul.

cards.note: Daniel 9:14 — *Therefore hath Yahuah (LORD) watched upon the evil, and brought it upon us: for Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice.* Tobit confessing Yahuah *just... in all your works* (3:2) speaks Daniel's confession that He is righteous in all His works.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (God), you are just, and all your works and all your ways are mercy and truth, and you judgest truly and justly for ever.
cards.t_text: Therefore has Yahuah (LORD) watched upon the evil, and brought it upon us: for Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) is righteous in all his works which he does: for we obeyed not his voice.

cards.note: Daniel 9:7 — *O Yahuah (Lord), righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day.* Tobit's *your judgments are many and true: deal with me according to my sins* (3:5) is Daniel's same self-condemning vindication of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And now your judgments are many and true: deal with me according to my sins and my fathers’: because we have not kept your commandments, neither have walked in truth before you.
cards.t_text: O Adonai (Lord), righteousness belongs unto you, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Yahudah (Judah), and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Yashar'el (Israel), that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither you have driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against you.

cards.note: Psalm 25:10 — *All the paths of Yahuah (LORD) are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.* Tobit's *all your ways are mercy and truth* (3:2) quotes the psalter's verdict on the covenant-keeping God almost word for word.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (God), you are just, and all your works and all your ways are mercy and truth, and you judgest truly and justly for ever.
cards.t_text: All the paths of Yahuah (LORD) are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:2 — *And the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.* Tobit's *we have not kept your commandments* (3:5) is the same confession the returning remnant makes in Nehemiah.
cards.s_text: And now your judgments are many and true: deal with me according to my sins and my fathers’: because we have not kept your commandments, neither have walked in truth before you.
cards.t_text: And the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins, and the iniquities of their fathers.

cards.note: Lamentations 5:1 — *Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproach.* Tobit dispersed *for a proverb of reproach to all the nations* (3:4) prays Lamentations' own appeal over the reproach of the scattered.
cards.s_text: For they obeyed not your commandments: wherefore you have delivered us for a spoil, and to captivity, and to death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.
cards.t_text: Remember, O Yahuah (LORD), what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproach.

cards.note: Lamentations 5:7 — *Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities.* Tobit asks not to be punished for *the sins of my fathers, who have sinned before you* (3:3) — the very weight Lamentations names.
cards.s_text: Remember me, and look on me, punish me not for my sins and ignorances, and the sins of my fathers, who have sinned before you:
cards.t_text: Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities.

cards.note: Daniel 9:11 — *Yea, all Yashar'el (Israel) have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of Elohim (God), because we have sinned against him.* Tobit's *they obeyed not your commandments: wherefore you have delivered us... to captivity* (3:4) is Daniel's identical reckoning of the exile as the law's own sworn oath.
cards.s_text: For they obeyed not your commandments: wherefore you have delivered us for a spoil, and to captivity, and to death, and for a proverb of reproach to all the nations among whom we are dispersed.
cards.t_text: Yea, all Yashar'el (Israel) have transgressed your law, even by departing, that they might not obey your voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of Elohim (God), because we have sinned against him.

cards.note: Psalm 25:18 — *Look upon mine affliction and my pain; and forgive all my sins.* Tobit, weighed by reproach and sin alike (3:6), asks the same: that Yahuah look on his affliction and forgive.
cards.s_text: Now therefore deal with me as seemeth best to you, and command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be dissolved, and become earth: for it is profitable for me to die rather than to live, because I have heard false reproaches, and have much sorrow: command therefore that I may now be delivered out of this distress, and go into the everlasting place: turn not your face away from me.
cards.t_text: Look upon my affliction and my pain; and forgive all my sins.

cards.note: Psalm 25:16 — *Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.* Tobit's *turn not your face away from me* (3:6) is the obverse of David's prayer that Yahuah turn toward the desolate.
cards.s_text: Now therefore deal with me as seemeth best to you, and command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be dissolved, and become earth: for it is profitable for me to die rather than to live, because I have heard false reproaches, and have much sorrow: command therefore that I may now be delivered out of this distress, and go into the everlasting place: turn not your face away from me.
cards.t_text: Turn you unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.

cards.note: Psalm 6:4 — *Return, O Yahuah (LORD), deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake.* Tobit's plea to be delivered out of his distress (3:6) is David's plea for deliverance for mercy's sake.
cards.s_text: Now therefore deal with me as seemeth best to you, and command my spirit to be taken from me, that I may be dissolved, and become earth: for it is profitable for me to die rather than to live, because I have heard false reproaches, and have much sorrow: command therefore that I may now be delivered out of this distress, and go into the everlasting place: turn not your face away from me.
cards.t_text: Return, O Yahuah (LORD), deliver my soul: oh save me for your mercies’ sake.

cards.note: Psalm 6:1 — *O Yahuah (LORD), rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure.* Tobit weeping in his sorrow (3:1) takes up David's opening cry of the chastened afflicted.
cards.s_text: Then I being grieved did weep, and in my sorrow prayed, saying,
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (LORD), rebuke me not in your anger, neither chasten me in your hot displeasure.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 24:18 — *But thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in Egypt, and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) redeemed thee thence: therefore I command thee to do this thing.* The 'remember and do my commandments' refrain that closes Tobit's charge echoes Moses' own ground for mercy: remember redemption, therefore keep the command.
cards.s_text: Bless Yahuah (God), your Elohim (God) alway, and desire of him that your ways may be directed, and that all your paths and counsels may prosper: for every nation has not counsel; but Yahuah (God) himself gives all good things, and he humbleth whom he will, as he will; now therefore, my son, remember my commandments, neither let them be put out of your mind.
cards.t_text: But you shall remember that you were a bondman in Egypt, and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) redeemed you thence: therefore I command you to do this thing.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:3 — *The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.* The directed ways Tobit prays for his son are the very guidance Proverbs grants the upright in heart.
cards.s_text: Bless Yahuah (God), your Elohim (God) alway, and desire of him that your ways may be directed, and that all your paths and counsels may prosper: for every nation has not counsel; but Yahuah (God) himself gives all good things, and he humbleth whom he will, as he will; now therefore, my son, remember my commandments, neither let them be put out of your mind.
cards.t_text: The integrity of the upright shall guide them: but the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them.

cards.note: Proverbs 10:17 — *He is in the way of life that keepeth instruction: but he that refuseth reproof erreth.* Tobit's 'do uprightly all thy life long' is the way of life Proverbs marks out for the one who keeps instruction.
cards.s_text: My son, be mindful of Yahuah (God), our Elohim (God) all your days, and let not your will be set to sin, or to transgress his commandments: do uprightly all your life long, and follow not the ways of unrighteousness.
cards.t_text: He is in the way of life that keeps instruction: but he that refuses reproof erreth.

cards.note: James 5:4 — *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* James hears the very wage-cry Tobit forestalls — kept-back hire reaching the ears of the Lord of hosts.
cards.s_text: Let not the wages of any man, which has wrought for you, tarry with you, but give him it out of hand: for if you serve Yahuah (God), he will also repay you: be circumspect my son, in all things you do, and be wise in all your conversation.
cards.t_text: Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, cries: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 24:15 — *At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it: lest he cry against thee unto Yahuah (LORD), and it be sin unto thee.* Deuteronomy makes the same-day wage a matter of the poor man's cry — the law behind Tobit's urgency.
cards.s_text: Let not the wages of any man, which has wrought for you, tarry with you, but give him it out of hand: for if you serve Yahuah (God), he will also repay you: be circumspect my son, in all things you do, and be wise in all your conversation.
cards.t_text: At his day you shall give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and sets his heart upon it: lest he cry against you unto Yahuah (LORD), and it be sin unto you.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:13 — *Thou shalt not defraud thy neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with thee all night until the morning.* The Torah command not to hold a hired man's wages overnight is precisely Tobit's 'give him it out of hand.'
cards.s_text: Let not the wages of any man, which has wrought for you, tarry with you, but give him it out of hand: for if you serve Yahuah (God), he will also repay you: be circumspect my son, in all things you do, and be wise in all your conversation.
cards.t_text: You shall not defraud your neighbour, neither rob him: the wages of him that is hired shall not abide with you all night until the morning.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* Love-thy-neighbour is the Torah seed of which Tobit's negative Golden Rule and the Sermon's positive one are both the flower.
cards.s_text: Do that to no man which you hatest: drink not wine to make you drunken: neither let drunkenness go with you in your journey.
cards.t_text: You shall not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Matthew 7:12 — *Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.* Yahusha's Golden Rule is Tobit's 'do that to no man which thou hatest' turned positive and named the sum of the law and the prophets.
cards.s_text: Do that to no man which you hatest: drink not wine to make you drunken: neither let drunkenness go with you in your journey.
cards.t_text: Therefore all things whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:3 — *Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).* The holiness code that names the mother first matches Tobit's stress on honouring the mother who bore him through danger.
cards.s_text: And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.
cards.t_text: You shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).

cards.note: Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* The Fifth Word itself; Tobit charges Tobias to honour his mother 'all the days of thy life,' the very commandment with promise.
cards.s_text: And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and your mother: that your days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you.

cards.note: Leviticus 19:10 — *And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).* The Torah law of the gleaning corners is the root of Tobit's 'give of thy bread to the hungry' — bread and garments owed to the poor.
cards.s_text: Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.
cards.t_text: And you shall not glean your vineyard, neither shall you gather every grape of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the poor and stranger: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).

cards.note: Luke 12:34 — *For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.* Tobit's unenvious eye toward the poor is the heart already lodged where its treasure is laid up — in mercy, not in hoarding.
cards.s_text: Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.
cards.t_text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

cards.note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.* (Luke 11:41). The Pharisees were careful about the outside of the cup; Yahusha (Jesus) told them the cleansing they needed was to give alms of what they had. Tobit had told his son the same long before: give of what you have, turn your face from no poor man, and the face of Yahuah (God) stays toward you.
