The King is not inventing a new rule; he is pointing a religious system back to the mercy the library had been teaching every son.
cards.s_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
cards.t_text: But rather give alms of such things as you have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.

cards.note: Luke 12:33 — *Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.* Yahusha lays up in heaven the same 'good treasure against the day of necessity' Tobit tells Tobias alms secures.
cards.s_text: For you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.
cards.t_text: Sell that you have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that fails not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth.

cards.note: Daniel 4:27 — *Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto thee, and break off thy sins by righteousness, and thine iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of thy tranquillity.* Daniel in exile, like Tobit in exile, urges mercy to the poor as the very thing that wards off death's sentence.
cards.s_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable unto you, and break off your sins by righteousness, and your iniquities by shewing mercy to the poor; if it may be a lengthening of your tranquillity.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:4 — *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* Proverbs repeats Tobit's deliverance-from-death word for word, naming the day of necessity Tobit calls 'the day of necessity.'
cards.s_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.
cards.t_text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivers from death.

cards.note: Proverbs 10:2 — *Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.* The very axiom Tobit hands his son — righteousness (alms) outlasts riches and pulls the giver back from death.
cards.s_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.
cards.t_text: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivers from death.

cards.note: Hebrews 1:14 — *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?* The angel who takes the name Azarias ('Yahuah-helps') to serve Tobias is the ministering spirit Hebrews describes, sent forth to minister for the heirs.
cards.s_text: Then he said, I am Azarias, the son of Ananias the great, and of your brothers.
cards.t_text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?

cards.note: Luke 1:19 — *And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.* Raphael, unrecognized and named Azarias, belongs to the same order of angels that stand in the presence of Elohim and are sent forth to households of the faithful.
cards.s_text: Therefore when he went to seek a man, he found Raphael that was an angel.
cards.t_text: And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto you, and to shew you these glad tidings.

cards.note: Exodus 23:14 — *Three times thou shalt keep a feast unto me in the year.* The pilgrim-journeys to Jerusalem to worship that Tobit recalls are the thrice-yearly feasts Torah appoints, kept by the faithful remnant in exile-prone days.
cards.s_text: Then Tobit said, You are welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know your tribe and your family; for you are my brother, of an honest and good stock: for I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brothers: my brother, you are of a good stock.
cards.t_text: Three times you shall keep a feast unto me in the year.

cards.note: Numbers 18:15 — *Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, which they bring unto Yahuah (LORD), whether it be of men or beasts, shall be thine: nevertheless the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem.* The firstborn that Tobit's kindred faithfully offered is the same firstborn the priestly law dedicates wholly to Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Then Tobit said, You are welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know your tribe and your family; for you are my brother, of an honest and good stock: for I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brothers: my brother, you are of a good stock.
cards.t_text: Every thing that opens the matrix in all flesh, which they bring unto Yahuah (LORD), whether it be of men or beasts, shall be yours: nevertheless the firstborn of man shall you surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shall you redeem.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 14:23 — *And thou shalt eat before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks; that thou mayest learn to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) always.* Tobit remembers going up to Jerusalem to offer the tenths of the fruits, the very tithe Torah commands be eaten before Yahuah in the place of his name.
cards.s_text: Then Tobit said, You are welcome, brother; be not now angry with me, because I have enquired to know your tribe and your family; for you are my brother, of an honest and good stock: for I know Ananias and Jonathas, sons of that great Samaias, as we went together to Jerusalem to worship, and offered the firstborn, and the tenths of the fruits; and they were not seduced with the error of our brothers: my brother, you are of a good stock.
cards.t_text: And you shall eat before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in the place which he shall choose to place his name there, the tithe of your corn, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstlings of your herds and of your flocks; that you may learn to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) always.

cards.note: Genesis 24:40 — *And he said unto me, Yahuah (LORD), before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:* Tobit's assurance that the good angel will prosper Tobias's journey and bring him back safe is word-for-word the hope of Abraham's servant.
cards.s_text: For the good angel will keep him company, and his journey shall be prosperous, and he shall return safe.
cards.t_text: And he said unto me, Yahuah (LORD), before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way; and you shall take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:

cards.note: Genesis 24:7 — *Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of heaven, which took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.* Tobit invokes the same God of heaven who sends his angel before a son's journey to kindred, as Tobias likewise rides toward Sara.
cards.s_text: So they were well pleased. Then said he to Tobias, Prepare thyself for the journey, and Yahuah (God) send you a good journey. And when his son had prepared all things for the journey, his father said, Go you with this man, and Yahuah (God), which dwells in heaven, prosper your journey, and the angel of Yahuah (God) keep you company. So they went forth both, and the young man’s dog with them.
cards.t_text: Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of heaven, which took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto your seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before you, and you shall take a wife unto my son from thence.

cards.note: Hebrews 1:14 — *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?* Raphael's promise to go with Tobias and lead the way is exactly this ministering-spirit office, sent forth to serve the heirs of the covenant.
cards.s_text: To whom the angel said, I will go with you, and I know the way well: for I have lodged with our brother Gabael.
cards.t_text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?

cards.note: Psalm 91:11 — *For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.* Tobit's prayer that the angel of Yahuah keep Tobias company echoes the psalm's charge over the traveller's every way.
cards.s_text: So they were well pleased. Then said he to Tobias, Prepare thyself for the journey, and Yahuah (God) send you a good journey. And when his son had prepared all things for the journey, his father said, Go you with this man, and Yahuah (God), which dwells in heaven, prosper your journey, and the angel of Yahuah (God) keep you company. So they went forth both, and the young man’s dog with them.
cards.t_text: For he shall give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways.

cards.note: Exodus 23:20 — *Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared.* The angel of Yahuah whom Tobit asks to keep his son company on the road to Rages is the same guide Yahuah pledged to send before Israel to keep them in the way.
cards.s_text: So they were well pleased. Then said he to Tobias, Prepare thyself for the journey, and Yahuah (God) send you a good journey. And when his son had prepared all things for the journey, his father said, Go you with this man, and Yahuah (God), which dwells in heaven, prosper your journey, and the angel of Yahuah (God) keep you company. So they went forth both, and the young man’s dog with them.
cards.t_text: Behold, I send an Angel before you, to keep you in the way, and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.

cards.note: Proverbs 19:14 — *House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from Yahuah (LORD).* The fair and wise maid joined to her kinsman by the right of inheritance is the very prudent wife that is the LORD's own gift, in Tobit 6:12.
cards.s_text: And the maid is fair and wise: now therefore hear me, and I will speak to her father; and when we return from Rages we will celebrate the marriage: for I know that Raguel cannot marry her to another according to the law of Moses, but he shall be guilty of death, because the right of inheritance does rather appertain to you than to any other.
cards.t_text: House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Genesis 24:15 — *And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.* The appointed bride given that same night without fail mirrors Rebekah appearing before the prayer was even finished, in Tobit 6:17.
cards.s_text: And the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more: but when you shall come to her, rise up both of you, and pray to Yahuah (God) which is merciful, who will have pity on you, and save you: fear not, for she is appointed to you from the beginning; and you shall preserve her, and she shall go with you. Moreover I suppose that she shall bear you children. Now when Tobias had heard these things, he loved her, and his heart was effectually joined to her.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.

cards.note: Genesis 24:14 — *And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.* Sara appointed to Tobias from the beginning answers the damsel the servant prays Yahuah has appointed for Isaac, in Tobit 6:17.
cards.s_text: And the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more: but when you shall come to her, rise up both of you, and pray to Yahuah (God) which is merciful, who will have pity on you, and save you: fear not, for she is appointed to you from the beginning; and you shall preserve her, and she shall go with you. Moreover I suppose that she shall bear you children. Now when Tobias had heard these things, he loved her, and his heart was effectually joined to her.
cards.t_text: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down your pitcher, I pray you, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give your camels drink also: let the same be she that you have appointed for your servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that you have shewed kindness unto my master.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:5 — *If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband's brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband's brother unto her.* The right of Sara appertaining to Tobias as her near kinsman echoes the kinsman's duty to raise up the dead man's name from his own house, in Tobit 6:11.
cards.s_text: For to you does the right of her appertain, seeing you only art of her kindred.
cards.t_text: If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife, and perform the duty of an husband’s brother unto her.

cards.note: Numbers 36:8 — *And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.* The right of inheritance that binds Sara to her kinsman Tobias is the very statute keeping a daughter's inheritance within her father's tribe, in Tobit 6:12.
cards.s_text: And the maid is fair and wise: now therefore hear me, and I will speak to her father; and when we return from Rages we will celebrate the marriage: for I know that Raguel cannot marry her to another according to the law of Moses, but he shall be guilty of death, because the right of inheritance does rather appertain to you than to any other.
cards.t_text: And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.

cards.note: Luke 8:29 — *(For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For oftentimes it had caught him: and he was kept bound with chains and in fetters; and he brake the bands, and was driven of the devil into the wilderness.)* The evil spirit that troubles and vexes a man or woman until it is driven off answers the unclean spirit cast out at the Master's command, in Tobit 6:7.
cards.s_text: And he said to him, Touching the heart and the liver, if a devil or an evil spirit trouble any, we must make a smoke thereof before the man or the woman, and the party shall be no more vexed.
cards.t_text: (For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For oftentimes it had caught him: and he was kept bound with chains and in fetters; and he brake the bands, and was driven of the devil into the wilderness.)

cards.note: James 4:7 — *Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.* The devil that smells the smoke and flees, never to return, is the same enemy that flees before submission to Elohim, in Tobit 6:17.
cards.s_text: And the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more: but when you shall come to her, rise up both of you, and pray to Yahuah (God) which is merciful, who will have pity on you, and save you: fear not, for she is appointed to you from the beginning; and you shall preserve her, and she shall go with you. Moreover I suppose that she shall bear you children. Now when Tobias had heard these things, he loved her, and his heart was effectually joined to her.
cards.t_text: Submit yourselves therefore to Elohim (God). Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

cards.note: Mark 16:18 — *They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.* The heart, liver, and gall kept safely for the recovery of the afflicted answer the laying on of hands by which the sick recover, in Tobit 6:4.
cards.s_text: To whom the angel said, Open the fish, and take the heart and the liver and the gall, and put them up safely.
cards.t_text: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.

cards.note: John 9:11 — *He answered and said, A man that is called Yahusha made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight.* The gall laid up to anoint whitened eyes and give sight prefigures the anointing of clay that opens the blind man's eyes, in Tobit 6:8.
cards.s_text: As for the gall, it is good to anoint a man that has whiteness in his eyes, and he shall be healed.
cards.t_text: He answered and said, A man that is called Yahusha (Jesus) made clay, and anointed my eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight.

cards.note: Ezekiel 47:12 — *And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.* The fish drawn from the river to feed and to heal answers the river whose very waters and fruit are medicine, in Tobit 6:3.
cards.s_text: Then the angel said to him, Take the fish. And the young man laid hold of the fish, and drew it to land.
cards.t_text: And by the river upon the bank thereof, on this side and on that side, shall grow all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed: it shall bring forth new fruit according to his months, because their waters they issued out of the sanctuary: and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* The fish that leaped up to devour is turned, like Joseph's harm, into the means of saving life, in Tobit 6:2.
cards.s_text: And when the young man went down to wash himself, a fish leaped out of the river, and would have devoured him.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Ruth 4:11 — *And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. Yahuah (LORD) make the woman that is come into thine house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Yashar'el (Israel): and do thou worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth-lehem:* the blessing turning Sara's sorrow to joy is the same bridal benediction the gate pronounces over Ruth.
cards.s_text: Be of good comfort, my daughter; Yahuah (God) of heaven and earth give you joy for this your sorrow: be of good comfort, my daughter.
cards.t_text: And all the people that were in the gate, and the elders, said, We are witnesses. Yahuah (LORD) make the woman that is come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, which two did build the house of Yashar'el (Israel): and do you worthily in Ephratah, and be famous in Beth-lehem:

cards.note: Genesis 24:60 — *And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.* Edna's *Yahuah (God) of heaven and earth give you joy* sends Sara out under the same household blessing pronounced over Rebekah as she leaves for Isaac.
cards.s_text: Be of good comfort, my daughter; Yahuah (God) of heaven and earth give you joy for this your sorrow: be of good comfort, my daughter.
cards.t_text: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, You are our sister, be you the mother of thousands of millions, and let your seed possess the gate of those which hate them.

cards.note: Genesis 24:54 — *And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.* Raguel's *Eat and drink, and make merry* matches the betrothal meal at Bethuel's house before the bride is led home.
cards.s_text: So he communicated the matter with Raguel: and Raguel said to Tobias, Eat and drink, and make merry:
cards.t_text: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that were with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.

cards.note: Genesis 29:22 — *And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.* Raguel's table after the sealed covenant — *Then they began to eat* — is the kinsman's wedding feast that Laban makes for Jacob and Rachel.
cards.s_text: Then they began to eat.
cards.t_text: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.

cards.note: Mark 10:7 — *For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;* the bride led away to the bridegroom's father after the law of Moses is the leaving-and-cleaving the Messiah grounds in the creation order.
cards.s_text: Then he called his daughter Sara, and she came to her father, and he took her by the hand, and gave her to be wife to Tobias, saying, Behold, take her after the law of Moses, and lead her away to your father. And he blessed them;
cards.t_text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;

cards.note: Ruth 4:10 — *Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: ye are witnesses this day.* The sealed instrument of covenants in Tobit is the same witnessed marriage-deed by which Boaz, the kinsman, secures the bride and the inheritance.
cards.s_text: And called Edna his wife, and took paper, and did write an instrument of covenants, and sealed it.
cards.t_text: Moreover Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, have I purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place: you are witnesses this day.

cards.note: Genesis 24:50 — *Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from Yahuah (LORD): we cannot speak unto thee bad or good.* Raguel's *the merciful Yahuah (God) give you good success in all things* reads the betrothal, like Rebekah's, as proceeding from Yahuah Himself.
cards.s_text: Raguel said, Then take her from henceforth according to the manner, for you are her cousin, and she is yours, and the merciful Yahuah (God) give you good success in all things.
cards.t_text: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceeds from Yahuah (LORD): we cannot speak unto you bad or good.

cards.note: Genesis 24:51 — *Behold, Rebekah is before thee, take her, and go, and let her be thy master’s son’s wife, as Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken.* Raguel taking Sara by the hand and saying *take her after the law of Moses, and lead her away to your father* echoes Bethuel and Laban giving Rebekah to be Isaac's wife.
cards.s_text: Then he called his daughter Sara, and she came to her father, and he took her by the hand, and gave her to be wife to Tobias, saying, Behold, take her after the law of Moses, and lead her away to your father. And he blessed them;
cards.t_text: Behold, Rebekah is before you, take her, and go, and let her be your master’s son’s wife, as Yahuah (LORD) has spoken.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The marriage made within the kindred is the obverse of the marriage forbidden with the nations — Tobias seeks Sara precisely because she is of the covenant seed.
cards.s_text: So he communicated the matter with Raguel: and Raguel said to Tobias, Eat and drink, and make merry:
cards.t_text: Neither shall you make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give unto his son, nor his daughter shall you take unto your son.

cards.note: Numbers 36:8 — *And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.* Sara, the only daughter, is given to her cousin so the inheritance of Nephthalim is not removed from the tribe.
cards.s_text: For it is meet that you should marry my daughter: nevertheless I will declare to you the truth.
cards.t_text: And every daughter, that possesseth an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), shall be wife unto one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) may enjoy every man the inheritance of his fathers.

cards.note: Numbers 36:6 — *This is the thing which Yahuah (LORD) doth command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.* Raguel's *it is meet that you should marry my daughter* obeys the same statute binding an heiress to a man of her father's tribe.
cards.s_text: For it is meet that you should marry my daughter: nevertheless I will declare to you the truth.
cards.t_text: This is the thing which Yahuah (LORD) does command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, Let them marry to whom they think best; only to the family of the tribe of their father shall they marry.

cards.note: Genesis 24:4 — *But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.* Raguel granting Sara because *you are her cousin* keeps Abraham's charge to seek the bride from his own kindred, not the nations.
cards.s_text: Raguel said, Then take her from henceforth according to the manner, for you are her cousin, and she is yours, and the merciful Yahuah (God) give you good success in all things.
cards.t_text: But you shall go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.

cards.note: Genesis 29:5 — *And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.* Raguel's *Do you know Tobit our kinsman? And they said, We know him* repeats Jacob's well-side recognition of the kindred verbatim in pattern.
cards.s_text: Then he said to them, Do you know Tobit our kinsman? And they said, We know him. Then said he, Is he in good health?
cards.t_text: And he said unto them, Know you Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know him.

cards.note: Genesis 29:14 — *And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.* Raguel's blessing — *You are the son of an honest and good man* — names the same bone-and-flesh kinship that binds Tobias into Raguel's house.
cards.s_text: And blessed him, and said to him, You are the son of an honest and good man. But when he had heard that Tobit was blind, he was sorrowful, and wept.
cards.t_text: And Laban said to him, Surely you are my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month.

cards.note: Genesis 29:13 — *And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.* Raguel leaping up to kiss and weep over Tobit's son re-enacts Laban running to embrace his sister's son Jacob.
cards.s_text: Then Raguel leaped up, and kissed him, and wept,
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister’s son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things.

cards.note: Tobit 13:18 — *And all her streets shall say, Alleluia; and they shall praise him, saying, Blessed be Yahuah (God), which has extolled it for ever.* Raguel’s call for saints, angels, and elect to praise forever is taken up in Tobit’s hymn of the regathered Jerusalem (Tobit 8:15).
cards.s_text: Then Raguel praised Yahuah (God), and said, O Yahuah (God), you are worthy to be praised with all pure and holy praise; therefore let your saints praise you with all your creatures; and let all your angels and your elect praise you for ever.
cards.t_text: And all her streets shall say, Alleluia; and they shall praise him, saying, Blessed be Yahuah (God), which has extolled it for ever.

cards.note: Psalms 148:5 — *Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.* All creatures praising their Maker is the ground of Tobias’s blessing of the holy and glorious name (Tobit 8:5).
cards.s_text: Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art you, O Yahuah (God) of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious name for ever; let the heavens bless you, and all your creatures.
cards.t_text: Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.

cards.note: Psalms 148:2 — *Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts.* The heavens and creatures Tobias bids bless Yahuah are the very hosts Psalm 148 musters (Tobit 8:5).
cards.s_text: Then began Tobias to say, Blessed art you, O Yahuah (God) of our fathers, and blessed is your holy and glorious name for ever; let the heavens bless you, and all your creatures.
cards.t_text: Praise you him, all his angels: praise you him, all his hosts.

cards.note: Ephesians 5:25 — *Husbands, love your wives, even as Messiah (Christ) also loved the church, and gave himself for it;* the sacrificial, lifelong love that Tobias prays to live out, to grow aged together (Tobit 8:7).
cards.s_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.
cards.t_text: Husbands, love your wives, even as Messiah (Christ) also loved the church, and gave himself for it;

cards.note: Malachi 2:14 — *Yet ye say, Wherefore? Because Yahuah (LORD) hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.* Yahuah is the witness of the marriage covenant Tobias makes openly before him (Tobit 8:7).
cards.s_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.
cards.t_text: Yet you say, Wherefore? Because Yahuah (LORD) has been witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously: yet is she your companion, and the wife of your covenant.

cards.note: *And now, O Yahuah (God), I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.* (Tobit 8:7). *And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.* (Malachi 2:15). Tobias tells Yahuah (God) why he is taking Sarah: not for lust but uprightly, that they may grow old together. Malachi asks why Yahuah (God) made the two one and answers it — that he might seek a godly seed — and warns the man not to deal treacherously with the wife of his youth. Tobias's prayer is that purpose spoken aloud at the start of a marriage. The seed of promise is carried through marriages entered this way, and the prophet and the young bridegroom agree on what marriage is for.
cards.s_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.
cards.t_text: And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.

cards.note: Genesis 1:27 — *So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him; male and female created he them.* The making of Adam and Eve that Tobit 8:6 recalls as the pattern of his own marriage.
cards.s_text: You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.
cards.t_text: So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him; male and female created he them.

cards.note: Genesis 2:24 — *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.* The one-flesh covenant Tobias and Sarah enter is the creation ordinance Tobit 8:6 invokes.
cards.s_text: You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.
cards.t_text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

cards.note: Genesis 2:18 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.* The very word Tobias prays back to Yahuah as the ground of his marriage (Tobit 8:6).
cards.s_text: You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

cards.note: Ephesians 5:32 — *This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Messiah (Christ) and the church.* The prayer-hallowed marriage of Tobias points beyond itself to the covenant union it figures (Tobit 8:4).
cards.s_text: And after that they were both shut in together, Tobias rose out of the bed, and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray that Yahuah (God) would have pity on us.
cards.t_text: This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Messiah (Christ) and the church.

cards.note: Ephesians 5:3 — *But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becometh saints;* the very holiness Tobias guards when he rises to pray rather than to lust (Tobit 8:4).
cards.s_text: And after that they were both shut in together, Tobias rose out of the bed, and said, Sister, arise, and let us pray that Yahuah (God) would have pity on us.
cards.t_text: But fornication, and all uncleanness, or covetousness, let it not be once named among you, as becomes saints;

cards.note: Luke 10:19 — *Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.* The authority that binds and treads the enemy is given to the faithful, as the angel exercised it for Tobias (Tobit 8:3).
cards.s_text: The which smell when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the utmost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound him.
cards.t_text: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

cards.note: Matthew 12:29 — *Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.* The binding of the enemy must come first before the household is freed — Asmodeus bound, the marriage delivered (Tobit 8:3).
cards.s_text: The which smell when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the utmost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound him.
cards.t_text: Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.

cards.note: Revelation 20:3 — *And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.* As the demon is driven to the utmost parts and shut away, so the dragon is sealed in the pit (Tobit 8:3).
cards.s_text: The which smell when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the utmost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound him.
cards.t_text: And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.

cards.note: Revelation 20:2 — *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years,* the same word over the enemy that Tobit 8:3 sees in small — the angel bound him.
cards.s_text: The which smell when the evil spirit had smelled, he fled into the utmost parts of Egypt, and the angel bound him.
cards.t_text: And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years,

cards.note: Genesis 24:67 — *And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.* The morning union and blessing of Tobias and his wife answers the same pattern — the appointed bride received in love, the covenant household made whole.
cards.s_text: And early in the morning they went forth both together, and came to the wedding: and Tobias blessed his wife.
cards.t_text: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

cards.note: Genesis 24:60 — *And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.* Tobias blessing his wife at the wedding echoes the kindred's covenant-blessing over Rebekah, the seed of the house carried forward.
cards.s_text: And early in the morning they went forth both together, and came to the wedding: and Tobias blessed his wife.
cards.t_text: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, You are our sister, be you the mother of thousands of millions, and let your seed possess the gate of those which hate them.

cards.note: Genesis 24:55 — *And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.* As Raguel swears Tobias shall not yet depart, so Rebekah's kin would keep the bride a season before sending her on her way.
cards.s_text: For Raguel has sworn that I shall not depart.
cards.t_text: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us a few days, at the least ten; after that she shall go.

cards.note: Tobit 12:15 — *I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.* The Azarias dispatched to Gabael is later revealed as Raphael himself, one who goes in and out before Yahuah's glory.
cards.s_text: Brother Azarias, take with you a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.
cards.t_text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.

cards.note: Luke 1:19 — *And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.* The companion who goes out and returns for Tobias is, like Gabriel, an angel sent forth from before the throne.
cards.s_text: So Raphael went out, and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting: who brought forth bags which were sealed up, and gave them to him.
cards.t_text: And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto you, and to shew you these glad tidings.

cards.note: Psalm 91:11 — *For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.* Tobias's long journey to Rages is kept safe by the very angel-charge the Psalm promises the trusting traveller.
cards.s_text: Brother Azarias, take with you a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.
cards.t_text: For he shall give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways.

cards.note: Genesis 24:40 — *And he said unto me, Yahuah (LORD), before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father's house:* The sealed bags pass freely to Raphael because the same promised angel goes with him to prosper the errand.
cards.s_text: So Raphael went out, and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting: who brought forth bags which were sealed up, and gave them to him.
cards.t_text: And he said unto me, Yahuah (LORD), before whom I walk, will send his angel with you, and prosper your way; and you shall take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father’s house:

cards.note: Tobit 12:14 — *And now Yahuah (God) has sent me to heal you and Sara your daughter in law.* The errand-runner of chapter 9 is unveiled three chapters on as the very angel Yahuah sent, carrying the household's good far beyond a sack of silver.
cards.s_text: So Raphael went out, and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting: who brought forth bags which were sealed up, and gave them to him.
cards.t_text: And now Yahuah (God) has sent me to heal you and Sara your daughter in law.

cards.note: Matthew 24:46 — *Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.* Raphael is found doing exactly his charge — lodging with Gabael and receiving the sealed bags — the blessed faithfulness the Master praises.
cards.s_text: So Raphael went out, and lodged with Gabael, and gave him the handwriting: who brought forth bags which were sealed up, and gave them to him.
cards.t_text: Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he comes shall find so doing.

cards.note: Matthew 24:45 — *Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?* Raphael, entrusted with the camels and the money for the wedding, is the very image of the trusted servant set over his lord's affairs.
cards.s_text: Brother Azarias, take with you a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.
cards.t_text: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord has made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?

cards.note: Genesis 24:56 — *And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing Yahuah (LORD) hath prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.* As Tobias frets that his father counteth the days, the faithful servant likewise refuses delay, pressing home the instant the charge is complete.
cards.s_text: But my father counteth the days; and if I tarry long, he will be very sorry.
cards.t_text: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing Yahuah (LORD) has prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.

cards.note: Genesis 24:33 — *And there was set meat before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.* Abraham's servant, like Raphael sent for Gabael's money, holds his commission above his own comfort until the errand is discharged.
cards.s_text: Brother Azarias, take with you a servant, and two camels, and go to Rages of Media to Gabael, and bring me the money, and bring him to the wedding.
cards.t_text: And there was set meat before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told my errand. And he said, Speak on.

cards.note: Ephesians 6:3 — *That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.* The promise attached to honouring parents — long life, well-being — answers Raguel's hope in Tobit 10:12 to "hear good report of you," the blessing of a household in covenant order.
cards.s_text: And he said to his daughter, Honour your father and your mother in law, which are now your parents, that I may hear good report of you. And he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, Yahuah (God) of heaven restore you, my dear brother, and grant that I may see your children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before Yahuah (God): behold, I commit my daughter to you of special trust; where are do not entreat her evil.
cards.t_text: That it may be well with you, and you may live long on the earth.

cards.note: Ephesians 6:2 — *Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)* Sha'ul names the very commandment Raguel presses upon his daughter in Tobit 10:12 as the first with promise, binding the apocryphal counsel to the apostolic word.
cards.s_text: And he said to his daughter, Honour your father and your mother in law, which are now your parents, that I may hear good report of you. And he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, Yahuah (God) of heaven restore you, my dear brother, and grant that I may see your children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before Yahuah (God): behold, I commit my daughter to you of special trust; where are do not entreat her evil.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)

cards.note: Exodus 20:12 — *Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee.* Raguel's charge to honour her parents in Tobit 10:12 is the fifth commandment itself, the covenant word carried into the household of the dispersion.
cards.s_text: And he said to his daughter, Honour your father and your mother in law, which are now your parents, that I may hear good report of you. And he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, Yahuah (God) of heaven restore you, my dear brother, and grant that I may see your children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before Yahuah (God): behold, I commit my daughter to you of special trust; where are do not entreat her evil.
cards.t_text: Honour your father and your mother: that your days may be long upon the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you.

cards.note: Psalms 128:6 — *Yea, thou shalt see thy children’s children, and peace upon Yashar'el (Israel).* Edna's longing in Tobit 10:12 to see her daughter's children before she dies is the very blessing of the Torah-faithful house — to see one's children's children, and peace upon Israel.
cards.s_text: And he said to his daughter, Honour your father and your mother in law, which are now your parents, that I may hear good report of you. And he kissed her. Edna also said to Tobias, Yahuah (God) of heaven restore you, my dear brother, and grant that I may see your children of my daughter Sara before I die, that I may rejoice before Yahuah (God): behold, I commit my daughter to you of special trust; where are do not entreat her evil.
cards.t_text: Yea, you shall see your children’s children, and peace upon Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Genesis 28:15 — *And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.* Raguel's prayer that the God of heaven give a prosperous journey in Tobit 10:11 echoes the promise spoken over Jacob's road — kept in all his ways and brought home again.
cards.s_text: And he blessed them, and sent them away, saying, Yahuah (God) of heaven give you a prosperous journey, my children.
cards.t_text: And, behold, I am with you, and will keep you in all places whither you go, and will bring you again into this land; for I will not leave you, until I have done that which I have spoken to you of.

cards.note: Genesis 24:60 — *And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou art our sister, be thou the mother of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.* As Rebekah was blessed and sent from her father's house to her bridegroom, so Raguel blesses Sara and sends the couple away with a prosperous journey in Tobit 10:11.
cards.s_text: And he blessed them, and sent them away, saying, Yahuah (God) of heaven give you a prosperous journey, my children.
cards.t_text: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, You are our sister, be you the mother of thousands of millions, and let your seed possess the gate of those which hate them.

cards.note: Genesis 42:38 — *And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which ye go, then shall ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.* Jacob's dread of mischief "by the way" mirrors the aged parents Tobias hurries home to in Tobit 10:9, lest grief bring down their gray hairs.
cards.s_text: But Tobias said, No; but let me go to my father.
cards.t_text: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which you go, then shall you bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

cards.note: Luke 15:20 — *And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.* The parents who "look no more to see" their son in Tobit 10:7 are the watching father of the parable, eyes fixed on the road for the child's return.
cards.s_text: But she said, Hold your peace, and deceive me not; my son is dead. And she went out every day into the way which they went, and did eat no meat on the daytime, and ceased not whole nights to bewail her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the wedding were expired, which Raguel had sworn that he should spend there. Then Tobias said to Raguel, Let me go, for my father and my mother look no more to see me.
cards.t_text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

cards.note: Genesis 42:36 — *And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have ye bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and ye will take Benjamin away: all these things are against me.* When a son delays, the bereaved-feeling father is the same voice that cries in Tobit 10:4, "My son is dead, seeing he stayeth long."
cards.s_text: Then his wife said to him, My son is dead, seeing he stayeth long; and she began to wail him, and said,
cards.t_text: And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have you bereaved of my children: Joseph is not, and Simeon is not, and you will take Benjamin away: all these things are against me.

cards.note: Genesis 37:35 — *And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.* Anna's ceaseless nightly weeping in Tobit 10:7 is Jacob's refusal to be comforted — a parent set on going down to the grave for a son not truly lost.
cards.s_text: But she said, Hold your peace, and deceive me not; my son is dead. And she went out every day into the way which they went, and did eat no meat on the daytime, and ceased not whole nights to bewail her son Tobias, until the fourteen days of the wedding were expired, which Raguel had sworn that he should spend there. Then Tobias said to Raguel, Let me go, for my father and my mother look no more to see me.
cards.t_text: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.

cards.note: Genesis 37:34 — *And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.* As Jacob mourned the son he thought lost, so Anna in Tobit 10:5 mourns Tobias as good as dead, her own eyes' light gone.
cards.s_text: Now I care for nothing, my son, since I have let you go, the light of my eyes.
cards.t_text: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.

cards.note: Psalm 147:2 — *Yahuah (LORD) doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel).* Yahuah's gathering of the outcasts of Israel is the larger hope behind the joy among Tobit's kindred at Nineveh in Tobit 11:17.
cards.s_text: But Tobias gave thanks before them, because Yahuah (God) had mercy on him. And when he came near to Sara his daughter in law, he blessed her, saying, You are welcome, daughter: Yahuah (God) be blessed, which has brought you to us, and blessed be your father and your mother. And there was joy among all his brothers which were at Nineve.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) does build up Jerusalem: he gathers together the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Isaiah 49:18 — *Lift up thine eyes round about, and behold: all these gather themselves together, and come to thee. As I live, saith Yahuah (LORD), thou shalt surely clothe thee with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them on thee, as a bride doeth.* The gathering joy among all Tobit's brethren mirrors the regathered children of restored Zion in Tobit 11:17.
cards.s_text: But Tobias gave thanks before them, because Yahuah (God) had mercy on him. And when he came near to Sara his daughter in law, he blessed her, saying, You are welcome, daughter: Yahuah (God) be blessed, which has brought you to us, and blessed be your father and your mother. And there was joy among all his brothers which were at Nineve.
cards.t_text: Lift up your eyes round about, and behold: all these gather themselves together, and come to you. As I live, says Yahuah (LORD), you shall surely clothe you with them all, as with an ornament, and bind them on you, as a bride does.

cards.note: Isaiah 60:4 — *Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side.* The sons and daughters gathered home is the great pattern of which Tobit's regathered household at the gate is a token in Tobit 11:16.
cards.s_text: Then Tobit went out to meet his daughter in law at the gate of Nineve, rejoicing and praising Yahuah (God): and they which saw him go marvelled, because he had received his sight.
cards.t_text: Lift up your eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to you: your sons shall come from far, and your daughters shall be nursed at your side.

cards.note: Luke 15:20 — *And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.* The father who runs and falls on the returning son's neck is the very gesture Anna makes over Tobias in Tobit 11:9.
cards.s_text: Then Anna ran forth, and fell upon the neck of her son, and said to him, Seeing I have seen you, my son, from henceforth I am content to die. And they wept both.
cards.t_text: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

cards.note: Psalm 30:5 — *For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.* Tobit's tears turn to joy at the sight of his son, the morning after the night of weeping in Tobit 11:15.
cards.s_text: For you have scourged, and have taken pity on me: for, behold, I see my son Tobias. And his son went in rejoicing, and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.
cards.t_text: For his anger endures but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy comes in the morning.

cards.note: Hebrews 12:6 — *For whom Yahuah (Lord) loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.* Tobit's scourging-then-pity is read as a Father's loving correction, not a curse, in Tobit 11:15.
cards.s_text: For you have scourged, and have taken pity on me: for, behold, I see my son Tobias. And his son went in rejoicing, and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.
cards.t_text: For whom Yahuah (Lord) loves he chastens, and scourgeth every son whom he receives.

cards.note: Job 5:18 — *For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.* The same hand that scourged Tobit now takes pity and heals, exactly as Job describes in Tobit 11:15.
cards.s_text: For you have scourged, and have taken pity on me: for, behold, I see my son Tobias. And his son went in rejoicing, and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.
cards.t_text: For he makes sore, and binds up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.

cards.note: Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* The son's striking of the gall on his father's eyes accomplishes the prophesied opening of the blind in Tobit 11:11.
cards.s_text: And took hold of his father: and he strake of the gall on his fathers’ eyes, saying, Be of good hope, my father.
cards.t_text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.

cards.note: Psalm 146:8 — *Yahuah (LORD) openeth the eyes of the blind: Yahuah (LORD) raiseth them that are bowed down: Yahuah (LORD) loveth the righteous:* The psalm names Yahuah as the One who opens blind eyes, the true healer behind the gall that peels the whiteness in Tobit 11:13.
cards.s_text: And the whiteness pilled away from the corners of his eyes: and when he saw his son, he fell upon his neck.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) opens the eyes of the blind: Yahuah (LORD) raiseth them that are bowed down: Yahuah (LORD) loves the righteous:

cards.note: Mark 8:25 — *After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.* The two-stage touch that ends in clear sight mirrors the rubbing and peeling of the whiteness in Tobit 11:8.
cards.s_text: Therefore anoint you his eyes with the gall, and being pricked with it, he shall rub, and the whiteness shall fall away, and he shall see you.
cards.t_text: After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

cards.note: John 9:7 — *And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.* The blind man comes seeing after the washing, as Tobit's whiteness falls away and he sees in Tobit 11:8.
cards.s_text: Therefore anoint you his eyes with the gall, and being pricked with it, he shall rub, and the whiteness shall fall away, and he shall see you.
cards.t_text: And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

cards.note: John 9:6 — *When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,* The Messiah anoints blind eyes by hand just as Tobias is told to anoint with the gall in Tobit 11:8.
cards.s_text: Therefore anoint you his eyes with the gall, and being pricked with it, he shall rub, and the whiteness shall fall away, and he shall see you.
cards.t_text: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,

cards.note: Isaiah 35:5 — *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* The prophet's promise of opened eyes is the very thing Raphael foretells over Tobit in Tobit 11:7.
cards.s_text: Then said Raphael, I know, Tobias, that your father will open his eyes.
cards.t_text: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.

cards.note: Hebrews 1:14 — *Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?* This defines the office of the angel sent to heal Tobit and Sara in Tobit 12:14 — a ministering spirit sent for the heirs of salvation.
cards.s_text: And now Yahuah (God) has sent me to heal you and Sara your daughter in law.
cards.t_text: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?

cards.note: Luke 1:49 — *For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.* Praising Elohim for the great things he has done is the very response Raphael calls for in Tobit 12:6.
cards.s_text: Then he took them both apart, and said to them, Bless Yahuah (God), praise him, and magnify him, and praise him for the things which he has done to you in the sight of all that live. It is good to praise Yahuah (God), and exalt his name, and honourably to shew forth the works of Yahuah (God); therefore be not slack to praise him.
cards.t_text: For he that is mighty has done to me great things; and holy is his name.

cards.note: Luke 1:46 — *And Mary said, My soul doth magnify Yahuah (Lord),* Mary magnifies Yahuah just as Raphael commands the household to magnify and praise him in Tobit 12:6.
cards.s_text: Then he took them both apart, and said to them, Bless Yahuah (God), praise him, and magnify him, and praise him for the things which he has done to you in the sight of all that live. It is good to praise Yahuah (God), and exalt his name, and honourably to shew forth the works of Yahuah (God); therefore be not slack to praise him.
cards.t_text: And Mary said, My soul does magnify Yahuah (Lord),

cards.note: Tobit 4:10 — *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Tobit had already taught his son the lesson Raphael now confirms from heaven in Tobit 12:9.
cards.s_text: For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:
cards.t_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.

cards.note: Proverbs 11:4 — *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* That righteousness, not hoarded gold, delivers from death echoes Raphael's counsel in Tobit 12:9 that alms is better than laying up gold.
cards.s_text: For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:
cards.t_text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivers from death.

cards.note: Proverbs 10:2 — *Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.* Solomon's word that righteousness delivers from death is the very promise Raphael attaches to alms in Tobit 12:9.
cards.s_text: For alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin. Those that exercise alms and righteousness shall be filled with life:
cards.t_text: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivers from death.

cards.note: Matthew 6:18 — *That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.* The fasting Raphael joins to prayer and alms in Tobit 12:8 is the secret fasting Yahusha teaches.
cards.s_text: Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:
cards.t_text: That you appear not unto men to fast, but unto your Father which is in secret: and your Father, which sees in secret, shall reward you openly.

cards.note: Matthew 6:6 — *But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.* The prayer Raphael calls good in Tobit 12:8 is the secret prayer Yahusha commends.
cards.s_text: Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:
cards.t_text: But you, when you prayest, enter into your closet, and when you have shut your door, pray to your Father which is in secret; and your Father which sees in secret shall reward you openly.

cards.note: Matthew 6:1 — *Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.* The good of almsgiving Raphael commends in Tobit 12:8 is the same alms Yahusha teaches, done before the Father not before men.
cards.s_text: Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness. A little with righteousness is better than much with unrighteousness. It is better to give alms than to lay up gold:
cards.t_text: Take heed that you do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise you have no reward of your Father which is in heaven.

cards.note: John 6:38 — *For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.* Raphael came not of his own favour but by the will of Elohim (Tobit 12:18), the very pattern of the Sent One.
cards.s_text: For not of any favour of mine, but by the will of our Elohim (God) I came; wherefore praise him for ever.
cards.t_text: For I came down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him that sent me.

cards.note: Revelation 1:11 — *Saying, I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last: and, What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia; unto Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamos, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.* The command to write all things in a book is given to John just as Raphael commands Tobit in Tobit 12:20.
cards.s_text: Now therefore give Yahuah (God) thanks: for I go up to him that sent me; but write all things which are done in a book.
cards.t_text: Saying, I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last: and, What you see, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia; unto Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamos, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.

cards.note: John 6:38 — *For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.* The posture of doing the will of the One who sent him, and returning to him, is Raphael's own word in Tobit 12:20.
cards.s_text: Now therefore give Yahuah (God) thanks: for I go up to him that sent me; but write all things which are done in a book.
cards.t_text: For I came down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him that sent me.

cards.note: Revelation 22:8 — *And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.* John falling at the angel's feet mirrors Tobit and Tobias falling on their faces before Raphael in Tobit 12:16.
cards.s_text: Then they were both troubled, and fell upon their faces: for they feared.
cards.t_text: And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.

cards.note: Revelation 22:9 — *Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship Elohim (God).* The same fellowservant who declines worship matches Raphael disclaiming any favour of his own in Tobit 12:18.
cards.s_text: For not of any favour of mine, but by the will of our Elohim (God) I came; wherefore praise him for ever.
cards.t_text: Then says he unto me, See you do it not: for I am your fellowservant, and of your brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship Elohim (God).

cards.note: Revelation 19:10 — *And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See thou do it not: I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren that have the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus): worship Elohim (God): for the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus) is the spirit of prophecy.* The angel refusing worship and redirecting it to Elohim is exactly Raphael's word in Tobit 12:18.
cards.s_text: For not of any favour of mine, but by the will of our Elohim (God) I came; wherefore praise him for ever.
cards.t_text: And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See you do it not: I am your fellowservant, and of your brethren that have the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus): worship Elohim (God): for the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus) is the spirit of prophecy.

cards.note: Luke 1:13 — *But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.* The prayer heard and answered by a sent angel is the pattern Raphael reveals to Tobit in Tobit 12:12.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, when you did pray, and Sara your daughter in law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One: and when you did bury the dead, I was with you likewise.
cards.t_text: But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for your prayer is heard; and your wife Elisabeth shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.

cards.note: Revelation 8:4 — *And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before Elohim (God) out of the angel’s hand.* The angel bearing the remembrance of prayers up to the throne matches Raphael bringing Tobit's prayers before the Holy One in Tobit 12:12.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, when you did pray, and Sara your daughter in law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One: and when you did bury the dead, I was with you likewise.
cards.t_text: And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before Elohim (God) out of the angel’s hand.

cards.note: Psalm 141:2 — *Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.* David asks that his prayer rise as incense before Yahuah, which is the very thing Raphael carried out in Tobit 12:12.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, when you did pray, and Sara your daughter in law, I did bring the remembrance of your prayers before the Holy One: and when you did bury the dead, I was with you likewise.
cards.t_text: Let my prayer be set forth before you as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.

cards.note: Luke 1:19 — *And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.* Gabriel self-identifies as one who stands before the glory of Elohim, the same station Raphael claims in Tobit 12:15.
cards.s_text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto you, and to shew you these glad tidings.

cards.note: Revelation 8:4 — *And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before Elohim (God) out of the angel’s hand.* The saints' prayers rising before the glory of the Holy One is exactly what Raphael did with Tobit's prayer in Tobit 12:15.
cards.s_text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: And the smoke of the incense, which came with the prayers of the saints, ascended up before Elohim (God) out of the angel’s hand.

cards.note: Revelation 8:3 — *And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne.* This is the heavenly office Raphael describes in Tobit 12:15 — an angel presenting the prayers of the saints at the throne.
cards.s_text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer; and there was given unto him much incense, that he should offer it with the prayers of all saints upon the golden altar which was before the throne.

cards.note: Revelation 8:2 — *And I saw the seven angels which stood before Elohim (God); and to them were given seven trumpets.* John beholds the very seven holy angels Raphael names himself among in Tobit 12:15.
cards.s_text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.
cards.t_text: And I saw the seven angels which stood before Elohim (God); and to them were given seven trumpets.

cards.note: Revelation 19:1 — *And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the Lord our God).* The "Alleluia" Tobit 13:18 puts on the streets of the rebuilt city is the very Alleluia of the heavenly multitude before the throne.
cards.s_text: And all her streets shall say, Alleluia; and they shall praise him, saying, Blessed be Yahuah (God), which has extolled it for ever.
cards.t_text: And after these things I heard a great voice of much people in heaven, saying, Alleluia; Salvation, and glory, and honour, and power, unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the Lord our God):

cards.note: Isaiah 60:19 — *The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but Yahuah (LORD) shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy Elohim (God) thy glory.* The streets of Tobit 13:18 that bless Yahuah "which has extolled it for ever" shine in Isaiah's city where Yahuah Himself is the everlasting light.
cards.s_text: And all her streets shall say, Alleluia; and they shall praise him, saying, Blessed be Yahuah (God), which has extolled it for ever.
cards.t_text: The sun shall be no more your light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto you: but Yahuah (LORD) shall be unto you an everlasting light, and your Elohim (God) your glory.

cards.note: Isaiah 54:12 — *And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones.* The sapphires, emeralds, and carbuncle of Tobit 13:16-17 are Isaiah's promised gemstone city, gate and border laid in precious stone.
cards.s_text: For Jerusalem shall be built up with sapphires and emeralds, and precious stone: your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold.
cards.t_text: And I will make your windows of agates, and your gates of carbuncles, and all your borders of pleasant stones.

cards.note: Revelation 21:18 — *And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass.* Tobit's walls and battlements of pure gold are John's New Jerusalem, her very wall jewelled and her city pure gold.
cards.s_text: For Jerusalem shall be built up with sapphires and emeralds, and precious stone: your walls and towers and battlements with pure gold.
cards.t_text: And the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass.

cards.note: Baruch 5:5 — *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).* Baruch's exile-vision of the children gathered home is the very gathering Tobit 13:13 bids the city rejoice over.
cards.s_text: Rejoice and be glad for the children of the just: for they shall be gathered together, and shall bless Yahuah (God) of the just.
cards.t_text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: Isaiah 60:4 — *Lift up thine eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to thee: thy sons shall come from far, and thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side.* The "children of the just" gathered together in Tobit 13:13 are Zion's sons and daughters brought home from afar.
cards.s_text: Rejoice and be glad for the children of the just: for they shall be gathered together, and shall bless Yahuah (God) of the just.
cards.t_text: Lift up your eyes round about, and see: all they gather themselves together, they come to you: your sons shall come from far, and your daughters shall be nursed at your side.

cards.note: Isaiah 60:3 — *And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising.* The many nations Tobit 13:11 sees coming from far with gifts are Isaiah's Gentiles and kings streaming to Jerusalem's risen light.
cards.s_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.
cards.t_text: And the Gentiles shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
