cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The headless tyrant shamed by one woman of the Hebrews in Judith 14:18 echoes the enmity by which the woman's seed bruises the head of the serpent's kingdom.
cards.s_text: These slaves have dealt treacherously; one woman of the Hebrews has brought shame upon the house of king Nabuchodonosor: for, behold, Holofernes lieth upon the ground without a head.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Exodus 14:25 — *And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Yashar'el (Israel); for Yahuah (LORD) fighteth for them against the Egyptians.* Israel pursuing and overthrowing the fleeing host in Judith 14:4 is Yahuah fighting for them, as the Egyptians confessed when they fled the face of Israel.
cards.s_text: So you, and all that inhabit the coast of Yashar'el (Israel), shall pursue them, and overthrow them as they go.
cards.t_text: And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Yashar'el (Israel); for Yahuah (LORD) fighteth for them against the Egyptians.

cards.note: Exodus 14:24 — *And it came to pass, that in the morning watch Yahuah (LORD) looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubled the host of the Egyptians,* The morning panic that falls on the Assyrians in Judith 14:3 is the same morning-watch terror Yahuah loosed upon the host that pursued His people.
cards.s_text: Then they shall take their armour, and shall go into their camp, and raise up the captains of the army of Assur, and shall run to the tent of Holofernes, but shall not find him: then fear shall fall upon them, and they shall flee before your face.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, that in the morning watch Yahuah (LORD) looked unto the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of the cloud, and troubled the host of the Egyptians,

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:35 — *And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* The Assyrians who run to the tent only to find death and flee in Judith 14:3 reprise Sennacherib's host, struck and scattered by Yahuah's hand alone.
cards.s_text: Then they shall take their armour, and shall go into their camp, and raise up the captains of the army of Assur, and shall run to the tent of Holofernes, but shall not find him: then fear shall fall upon them, and they shall flee before your face.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: Ruth 1:16 — *And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy Elohim (God) my Elohim (God):* As Ruth the Moabitess cast her lot with Israel's people and Israel's Elohim, so Achior in Judith 14:10 makes the stranger's covenant confession his own.
cards.s_text: And when Achior had seen all that Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had done, he believed in Yahuah (God) greatly, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to this day.
cards.t_text: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave you, or to return from following after you: for whither you go, I will go; and where you lodgest, I will lodge: your people shall be my people, and your Elohim (God) my Elohim (God):

cards.note: Isaiah 56:6 — *Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to Yahuah (LORD), to serve him, and to love the name of Yahuah (LORD), to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant;* Achior believing greatly and joining the house of Israel in Judith 14:10 is the foreigner Isaiah says Yahuah will bring to His holy mountain.
cards.s_text: And when Achior had seen all that Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had done, he believed in Yahuah (God) greatly, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to this day.
cards.t_text: Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to Yahuah (LORD), to serve him, and to love the name of Yahuah (LORD), to be his servants, every one that keeps the sabbath from polluting it, and takes hold of my covenant;

cards.note: Exodus 12:49 — *One law shall be to him that is homeborn, and unto the stranger that sojourneth among you.* The Ammonite joined to Israel in Judith 14:10 stands under the one law that knows no second tier for the grafted-in.
cards.s_text: And when Achior had seen all that Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had done, he believed in Yahuah (God) greatly, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to this day.
cards.t_text: One law shall be to him that is homeborn, and unto the stranger that sojourns among you.

cards.note: Exodus 12:48 — *And when a stranger shall sojourn with thee, and will keep the passover to Yahuah (LORD), let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: for no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.* Achior's circumcision and joining to the house of Israel in Judith 14:10 is exactly the Torah's door for the sojourner into the covenant.
cards.s_text: And when Achior had seen all that Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had done, he believed in Yahuah (God) greatly, and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) to this day.
cards.t_text: And when a stranger shall sojourn with you, and will keep the passover to Yahuah (LORD), let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: for no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The ancient enmity in which the head of the enemy is bruised through the woman echoes in Israel's praise of a deliverance wrought by a woman's hand (Judith 15:10).
cards.s_text: You have done all these things by yours hand: you have done much good to Yashar'el (Israel), and Yahuah (God) is pleased with it: blessed be you of the Almighty Yahuah (God) for evermore. And all the people said, So be it.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Judges 5:24 — *Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.* Deborah's song over Jael, who felled the captain by her hand, is the very pattern of Israel blessing Judith for what her hand wrought (Judith 15:10).
cards.s_text: You have done all these things by yours hand: you have done much good to Yashar'el (Israel), and Yahuah (God) is pleased with it: blessed be you of the Almighty Yahuah (God) for evermore. And all the people said, So be it.
cards.t_text: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 18:6 — *And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Yashar'el (Israel), singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.* The women running together with dance to honor the one who slew the enemy's champion is the same answering-song that hails Judith (Judith 15:12).
cards.s_text: Then all the women of Yashar'el (Israel) ran together to see her, and blessed her, and made a dance among them for her: and she took branches in her hand, and gave also to the women that were with her.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Yashar'el (Israel), singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.

cards.note: Exodus 15:20 — *And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.* As Miriam led the women in dance after the Sea, so Judith leads the women of Israel in the dance after Assur is broken (Judith 15:13).
cards.s_text: And they put a garland of olive upon her and her maid that was with her, and she went before all the people in the dance, leading all the women: and all the men of Yashar'el (Israel) followed in their armour with garlands, and with songs in their mouths.
cards.t_text: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.

cards.note: Judith 13:18 — *Then said Ozias to her, O daughter, blessed art you of the most high Yahuah (God) above all the women upon the earth; and blessed be Yahuah (God), which has created the heavens and the earth, which has directed you to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies.* The blessing first spoken in the gate is now ratified by priest and people, blessed of the Almighty for evermore (Judith 15:10).
cards.s_text: You have done all these things by yours hand: you have done much good to Yashar'el (Israel), and Yahuah (God) is pleased with it: blessed be you of the Almighty Yahuah (God) for evermore. And all the people said, So be it.
cards.t_text: Then said Ozias to her, O daughter, blessed art you of the most high Yahuah (God) above all the women upon the earth; and blessed be Yahuah (God), which has created the heavens and the earth, which has directed you to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies.

cards.note: Luke 1:52 — *He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.* The Magnificat names the very reversal the elders bless in Judith, the Almighty pleased to overthrow the mighty by a lowly hand (Judith 15:10).
cards.s_text: You have done all these things by yours hand: you have done much good to Yashar'el (Israel), and Yahuah (God) is pleased with it: blessed be you of the Almighty Yahuah (God) for evermore. And all the people said, So be it.
cards.t_text: He has put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.

cards.note: Luke 1:42 — *And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.* Elisabeth's cry over Mary unfolds the elders' acclamation of Judith as Jerusalem's exaltation and Israel's glory (Judith 15:9).
cards.s_text: And when they came to her, they blessed her with one accord, and said to her, You are the exaltation of Jerusalem, you are the great glory of Yashar'el (Israel), you are the great rejoicing of our nation:
cards.t_text: And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.

cards.note: Judges 4:23 — *So Elohim (God) subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* As Yahuah subdued Canaan's king after a woman drove the nail, so He breaks Assur before Israel after a woman takes the head (Judith 15:5).
cards.s_text: Now when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) heard it, they all fell upon them with one consent, and slew them to Chobai: likewise also they that came from Jerusalem, and from all the hill country, (for men had told them what things were done in the camp of their enemies) and they that were in Galaad, and in Galilee, chased them with a great slaughter, until they were past Damascus and the borders thereof.
cards.t_text: So Elohim (God) subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 15:9 — *The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; my lust shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.* The tyrant who meant to spoil Israel is spoiled instead, the great multitude's goods falling to the villages that had been besieged (Judith 15:7).
cards.s_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that returned from the slaughter had that which remained; and the villages and the cities, that were in the mountains and in the plain, got many spoils: for the multitude was very great.
cards.t_text: The enemy said, I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; my lust shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.

cards.note: Exodus 14:13 — *And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.* The astonishment in the tents is Israel beholding a salvation it did not fight for, the enemy seen no more (Judith 15:1).
cards.s_text: And when they that were in the tents heard, they were astonished at the thing that was done.
cards.t_text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear you not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom you have seen to day, you shall see them again no more for ever.

cards.note: Exodus 15:16 — *Fear and dread shall fall upon them; by the greatness of thine arm they shall be as still as a stone; till thy people pass over, O Yahuah (LORD), till the people pass over, which thou hast purchased.* The same supernatural dread that paralyzed Egypt and Canaan now scatters Assur, so that no man durst abide in his neighbour's sight (Judith 15:2).
cards.s_text: And fear and trembling fell upon them, so that there was no man that durst abide in the sight of his neighbour, but rushing out all together, they fled into every way of the plain, and of the hill country.
cards.t_text: Fear and dread shall fall upon them; by the greatness of your arm they shall be as still as a stone; till your people pass over, O Yahuah (LORD), till the people pass over, which you have purchased.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 16:15 — *Seven days shalt thou keep a solemn feast unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which Yahuah (LORD) shall choose: because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in all thine increase, and in all the works of thine hands, therefore thou shalt surely rejoice.* The people's joyful feasting before the sanctuary in Judith 16:20 is the appointed solemn feast of rejoicing Torah set at the chosen place.
cards.s_text: So the people continued feasting in Jerusalem before the sanctuary for the space of three months and Judith remained with them.
cards.t_text: Seven days shall you keep a solemn feast unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which Yahuah (LORD) shall choose: because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless you in all your increase, and in all the works of your hands, therefore you shall surely rejoice.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 16:16 — *Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before Yahuah (LORD) empty:* The people going up to worship at Jerusalem in Judith 16:18 keeps the very pilgrimage-feast Torah commands at the chosen place.
cards.s_text: Now as soon as they entered into Jerusalem, they worshipped Yahuah (God); and as soon as the people were purified, they offered their burnt offerings, and their free offerings, and their gifts.
cards.t_text: Three times in a year shall all your males appear before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before Yahuah (LORD) empty:

cards.note: Isaiah 66:24 — *And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.* Judith's 'fire and worms in their flesh' for the nations that rise up (Judith 16:17) speaks Isaiah's undying worm and unquenchable fire upon the transgressors.
cards.s_text: Woe to the nations that rise up against my kindred! Yahuah (God) Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment, in putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.
cards.t_text: And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.

cards.note: *Let all creatures serve you: for you spakest, and they were made, you did send forth your spirit, and it created them, and there is none that can resist your voice.* (Judith 16:14). *Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.* (Psalm 148:5). Judith says the whole creation was made by speaking, you spoke and they were made, you sent forth your spirit and it created them. The psalm says the same of the heavens and the host of them: he commanded, and they were created, and that is why they are to praise his name. Moses wrote it as *Elohim (God) said, Let there be* with the Spirit moving on the waters (Genesis 1:2–3), and David wrote that *by the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth* (Psalm 33:6). John names that Word: all things were made by him (John 1:3). What was made by a voice cannot resist that voice, and Judith says so.
cards.s_text: Let all creatures serve you: for you spakest, and they were made, you did send forth your spirit, and it created them, and there is none that can resist your voice.
cards.t_text: Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.

cards.note: Psalm 96:1 — *O sing unto Yahuah (LORD) a new song: sing unto Yahuah (LORD), all the earth.* Judith's resolve to 'sing to Yahuah a new song' (Judith 16:13) is the Psalter's own summons to the whole earth to sing it.
cards.s_text: I will sing to Yahuah (God) a new song: O Yahuah (God), you are great and glorious, wonderful in strength, and invincible.
cards.t_text: O sing unto Yahuah (LORD) a new song: sing unto Yahuah (LORD), all the earth.

cards.note: Luke 1:48 — *For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.* The low and weak of Israel lifted up in Judith 16:11 foreshadow the low-estate handmaiden Yahuah regards in the Magnificat.
cards.s_text: Then my afflicted shouted for joy, and my weak ones cried aloud; but they were astonished: these lifted up their voices, but they were overthrown.
cards.t_text: For he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.

cards.note: Luke 1:52 — *He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.* Judith's afflicted shouting for joy while the boasters are overthrown (Judith 16:11) is the very reversal Mary sings in the Magnificat.
cards.s_text: Then my afflicted shouted for joy, and my weak ones cried aloud; but they were astonished: these lifted up their voices, but they were overthrown.
cards.t_text: He has put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.

cards.note: Judges 5:24 — *Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.* Jael smiting Sisera in the tent is the nearest kin to Judith 16:9, where the fauchion passes through the enemy's neck by a woman's hand.
cards.s_text: Her sandals ravished his eyes, her beauty took his mind prisoner, and the fauchion passed through his neck.
cards.t_text: Blessed above women shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be, blessed shall she be above women in the tent.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The tyrant felled 'by the hand of a woman' (Judith 16:6) is an echo of Eden's first promise that the head of the proud enemy is bruised through the woman.
cards.s_text: But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 2:4 — *The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.* Hannah's song already declared what Judith 16:7 enacts — the mighty one falls not by young warriors but by Yahuah's reversal.
cards.s_text: For the mighty one did not fall by the young men, neither did the sons of the Titans smite him, nor high giants set upon him: but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her countenance.
cards.t_text: The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.

cards.note: *But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.* (Judith 16:6). *But Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;* (1 Corinthians 1:27). The Almighty Yahuah (God) brought a whole army to nothing by the hand of one widow, and Judith's song says so without apology. Paul tells the Corinthians this is how Elohim (God) works on purpose: he chooses the weak things to confound the mighty and the foolish things to confound the wise, so that no flesh can glory in his presence (1 Corinthians 1:29). Holofernes bragged of what he would do to Yashar'el (Israel); the next verse of the song says the mighty one did not fall by young men or giants but by a woman. The hand of a woman is the weak thing, and the weak thing is what he chose.
cards.s_text: But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;

cards.note: Psalm 137:9 — *Happy shall he be, that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the stones.* Holofernes' brag to dash the sucking children (Judith 16:5) is exactly the cruelty the Psalm pronounces back upon Babylon herself.
cards.s_text: He bragged that he would burn up my borders, and kill my young men with the sword, and dash the sucking children against the ground, and make my infants as a prey, and my virgins as a spoil.
cards.t_text: Happy shall he be, that takes and dasheth your little ones against the stones.

cards.note: Isaiah 10:5 — *O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation.* Assur in Judith 16:4 is the same proud northern instrument that boasts as if it were not a mere rod in Yahuah's hand.
cards.s_text: Assur came out of the mountains from the north, he came with ten thousands of his army, the multitude of which stopped the torrents, and their horsemen have covered the hills.
cards.t_text: O Assyrian, the rod of my anger, and the staff in their hand is my indignation.

cards.note: Psalm 46:9 — *He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.* The Psalm names the same Battle-Breaker Judith praises for delivering her out of the hand of the persecutor.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) breaks the battles: for among the camps in the midst of the people he has delivered me out of the hands of them that persecuted me.
cards.t_text: He makes wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaks the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burns the chariot in the fire.

cards.note: Judges 5:1 — *Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,* Judith 16's woman-led thanksgiving stands in the line of Deborah's song after another tyrant's army was undone.
cards.s_text: Then Judith began to sing this thanksgiving in all Yashar'el (Israel), and all the people sang after her this song of praise.
cards.t_text: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying,

cards.note: Exodus 15:3 — *Yahuah (LORD) is a man of war: Yahuah (LORD) is his name.* The One who 'breaks the battles' in Judith 16:3 is the very Man of War who threw Pharaoh's host into the sea.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (God) breaks the battles: for among the camps in the midst of the people he has delivered me out of the hands of them that persecuted me.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) is a man of war: Yahuah (LORD) is his name.

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* Judith's whole nation sings after her exactly as Israel sang after Moses at the Red Sea — the same redeemed-people chorus.
cards.s_text: Then Judith began to sing this thanksgiving in all Yashar'el (Israel), and all the people sang after her this song of praise.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: Esther 9:22 — *As the days wherein the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.* The same days of Adar that The Rest of Esther 10:13 fixes with assembly and gladness, the month turned from sorrow to joy.
cards.s_text: Therefore those days shall be to them in the month Adar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with an assembly, and joy, and with gladness before Yahuah (God), according to the generations for ever among his people.
cards.t_text: As the days wherein the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

cards.note: Leviticus 23:4 — *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.* The fixed assembly of the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar before Yahuah (The Rest of Esther 10:13) is feast-keeping in the pattern of the appointed convocations of Torah.
cards.s_text: Therefore those days shall be to them in the month Adar, the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the same month, with an assembly, and joy, and with gladness before Yahuah (God), according to the generations for ever among his people.
cards.t_text: These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their seasons.

cards.note: Matthew 25:32 — *And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:* The two lots that come at the day of judgment (The Rest of Esther 10:11) set the people of Elohim (God) apart from the nations; the shepherd's dividing goes further, sifting his own flock gathered out of all nations, the sheep from the goats.
cards.s_text: And these two lots came at the hour, and time, and day of judgment, before Yahuah (God) among all nations.
cards.t_text: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats:

cards.note: Isaiah 54:17 — *No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of Yahuah (LORD), and their righteousness is of me, saith Yahuah (LORD).* The nation saved when it cried (The Rest of Esther 10:9) is the heritage against which no weapon Haman forged could prosper.
cards.s_text: And my nation is this Yashar'el (Israel), which cried to Yahuah (God), and were saved: for Yahuah (God) has saved his people, and Yahuah (God) has delivered us from all those evils, and Yahuah (God) has wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
cards.t_text: No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against you in judgment you shall condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of Yahuah (LORD), and their righteousness is of me, says Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Psalm 124:3 — *Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us:* Without the hand that delivered them from all those evils (The Rest of Esther 10:9), the assembled nations would have swallowed Yashar'el alive.
cards.s_text: And my nation is this Yashar'el (Israel), which cried to Yahuah (God), and were saved: for Yahuah (God) has saved his people, and Yahuah (God) has delivered us from all those evils, and Yahuah (God) has wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
cards.t_text: Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us:

cards.note: Psalm 124:1 — *If it had not been Yahuah (LORD) who was on our side, now may Yashar'el (Israel) say;* The very confession of The Rest of Esther 10:9, that it was Yahuah and not the sword who saved His people.
cards.s_text: And my nation is this Yashar'el (Israel), which cried to Yahuah (God), and were saved: for Yahuah (God) has saved his people, and Yahuah (God) has delivered us from all those evils, and Yahuah (God) has wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
cards.t_text: If it had not been Yahuah (LORD) who was on our side, now may Yashar'el (Israel) say;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:19 — *Therefore it shall be, when Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath given thee rest from all thine enemies round about, in the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee for an inheritance to possess it, that thou shalt blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; thou shalt not forget it.* The fall of Aman and his assembled nations (The Rest of Esther 10:8) is the blotting-out of Amalek the covenant had sworn long before.
cards.s_text: And the nations were those that were assembled to destroy the name of the Yahudim (Jews):
cards.t_text: Therefore it shall be, when Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has given you rest from all your enemies round about, in the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you for an inheritance to possess it, that you shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven; you shall not forget it.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:17 — *Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;* The nations assembled to destroy the Name of the Yahudim (The Rest of Esther 10:8) are the standing order of Amalek that Torah commands Yashar'el never to forget.
cards.s_text: And the nations were those that were assembled to destroy the name of the Yahudim (Jews):
cards.t_text: Remember what Amalek did unto you by the way, when you were come forth out of Egypt;

cards.note: Exodus 17:8 — *Then came Amalek, and fought with Yashar'el (Israel) in Rephidim.* Aman the Agagite, the second dragon of The Rest of Esther 10:7, is the seed of the Amalek that first warred against Yashar'el at Rephidim.
cards.s_text: And the two dragons are I and Aman.
cards.t_text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Yashar'el (Israel) in Rephidim.

cards.note: Romans 8:28 — *And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.* The dream that failed in nothing (The Rest of Esther 10:5) is the same purpose by which all things work together for His called.
cards.s_text: For I remember a dream which I saw concerning these matters, and nothing thereof has failed.
cards.t_text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* Joseph and Mardocheus read the same Author behind the plot, that nothing of His dream had failed (The Rest of Esther 10:5).
cards.s_text: For I remember a dream which I saw concerning these matters, and nothing thereof has failed.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Esther 9:1 — *Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Yahudim (Jews) hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over them that hated them;)* The river that the little fountain became is the great reversal of Esther 9, the hidden hand of The Rest of Esther 10:6 made visible in history.
cards.s_text: A little fountain became a river, and there was light, and the sun, and much water: this river is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen:
cards.t_text: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Yahudim (Jews) hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over them that hated them;)

cards.note: Luke 1:52 — *He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.* Miriam's Magnificat carries the same covenant overturning — the lowly raised over the glorious — that crowns Mordecai's dream.
cards.s_text: The light and the sun rose up, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the glorious.
cards.t_text: He has put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 2:7 — *Yahuah (LORD) maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.* Hannah's song of the great reversal is exactly the lowly exalted and the glorious devoured in Rest of Esther 11:11.
cards.s_text: The light and the sun rose up, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the glorious.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) makes poor, and makes rich: he brings low, and lifts up.

cards.note: Isaiah 9:2 — *The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.* The sun rising after the day of darkness is the great light shining on the people of Rest of Esther 11:11.
cards.s_text: The light and the sun rose up, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the glorious.
cards.t_text: The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them has the light shined.

cards.note: Isaiah 60:1 — *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee.* The light and the sun rising up in Mordecai's dream is the risen glory of Yahuah over His delivered people.
cards.s_text: The light and the sun rose up, and the lowly were exalted, and devoured the glorious.
cards.t_text: Arise, shine; for your light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon you.

cards.note: Exodus 14:14 — *Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.* The flood of much water rising from a little fountain is Yahuah Himself fighting for the people who cried out, as at the sea.
cards.s_text: Then they cried to Yahuah (God), and upon their cry, as it were from a little fountain, was made a great flood, even much water.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.

cards.note: Psalms 18:6 — *In my distress I called upon Yahuah (LORD), and cried unto my Elohim (God): he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.* David's cry from distress heard by Yahuah is the very pattern of the righteous nation's cry in Rest of Esther 11:10.
cards.s_text: Then they cried to Yahuah (God), and upon their cry, as it were from a little fountain, was made a great flood, even much water.
cards.t_text: In my distress I called upon Yahuah (LORD), and cried unto my Elohim (God): he heard my voice out of his temple, and my cry came before him, even into his ears.

cards.note: Joel 2:32 — *And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of Yahuah (LORD) shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as Yahuah (LORD) hath said, and in the remnant whom Yahuah (LORD) shall call.* The nation crying to Yahuah and being delivered is the remnant calling on the Name unto deliverance.
cards.s_text: Then they cried to Yahuah (God), and upon their cry, as it were from a little fountain, was made a great flood, even much water.
cards.t_text: And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of Yahuah (LORD) shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as Yahuah (LORD) has said, and in the remnant whom Yahuah (LORD) shall call.

cards.note: Daniel 12:1 — *And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* The righteous nation troubled and ready to perish is the people delivered in the unequalled time of trouble.
cards.s_text: And the whole righteous nation was troubled, fearing their own evils, and were ready to perish.
cards.t_text: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which stands for the children of your people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.

cards.note: Zephaniah 1:15 — *That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness,* the prophet's day of darkness matching the day of darkness and obscurity of Rest of Esther 11:8.
cards.s_text: And lo a day of darkness and obscurity, tribulation and anguish, affliction and great uproar, upon earth.
cards.t_text: That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress, a day of wasteness and desolation, a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick darkness,

cards.note: Revelation 12:17 — *And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of Elohim (God), and have the testimony of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).* The nations prepared to fight against the righteous people are the dragon making war on the commandment-keeping seed.
cards.s_text: And at their cry all nations were prepared to battle, that they might fight against the righteous people.
cards.t_text: And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of Elohim (God), and have the testimony of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).

cards.note: Revelation 12:7 — *And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,* unveiling the heavenly front of the very dragon-war Mordecai foresaw in Rest of Esther 11:6.
cards.s_text: And, behold, two great dragons came forth ready to fight, and their cry was great.
cards.t_text: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,

cards.note: Daniel 7:3 — *And four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another.* The beasts rising from the sea are kin to the great dragons of Mordecai's dream, the kingdoms arrayed against the saints.
cards.s_text: And, behold, two great dragons came forth ready to fight, and their cry was great.
cards.t_text: And four great beasts came up from the sea, diverse one from another.

cards.note: Daniel 7:2 — *Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.* The troubled sea of the nations is the same churning waters from which Mordecai's two dragons come forth ready to fight.
cards.s_text: And, behold, two great dragons came forth ready to fight, and their cry was great.
cards.t_text: Daniel spake and said, I saw in my vision by night, and, behold, the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sea.

cards.note: Exodus 17:14 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.* The seed-war Haman renews in Rest of Esther 12:6 is the very Amalek whose remembrance Yahuah swore to blot out.
cards.s_text: Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:17 — *Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;* the Agagite's grudge in Rest of Esther 12:6 is the standing Torah-charge against Amalek breaking out again in Persia.
cards.s_text: Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.
cards.t_text: Remember what Amalek did unto you by the way, when you were come forth out of Egypt;

cards.note: 1 Samuel 15:2 — *Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), I remember that which Amalek did to Yashar'el (Israel), how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.* Haman the Agagite of Rest of Esther 12:6 is the line of Agag king of Amalek, carrying forward the ancient enmity Yahuah remembers.
cards.s_text: Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), I remember that which Amalek did to Yashar'el (Israel), how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.

cards.note: Esther 3:6 — *And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Yahudim (Jews) that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.* The grudge that begins against Mordecai's people in Rest of Esther 12:6 swells in the Hebrew into a decree to destroy the whole nation.
cards.s_text: Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.
cards.t_text: And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone; for they had shewed him the people of Mordecai: wherefore Haman sought to destroy all the Yahudim (Jews) that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even the people of Mordecai.

cards.note: Esther 10:3 — *For Mordecai the Yahudi (Jew) was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Yahudim (Jews), and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.* Mordecai's service-and-reward in Rest of Esther 12:5 ripens into the second seat of the kingdom and peace for his whole people.
cards.s_text: So the king commanded, Mardocheus to serve in the court, and for this he rewarded him.
cards.t_text: For Mordecai the Yahudi (Jew) was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Yahudim (Jews), and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

cards.note: Esther 6:11 — *Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delighteth to honour.* The reward promised in Rest of Esther 12:5 is paid by Haman's own hand in the Hebrew, the enemy parading the man he hated.
cards.s_text: So the king commanded, Mardocheus to serve in the court, and for this he rewarded him.
cards.t_text: Then took Haman the apparel and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and brought him on horseback through the street of the city, and proclaimed before him, Thus shall it be done unto the man whom the king delights to honour.

cards.note: Ecclesiastes 10:20 — *Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.* The eunuchs' devices in Rest of Esther 12:2 are the hidden voice that wings its way to the king's ear through the watchman who heard.
cards.s_text: And he heard their devices, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artexerxes the king; and so he certified the king of them.
cards.t_text: Curse not the king, no not in your thought; and curse not the rich in your bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which has wings shall tell the matter.

cards.note: Proverbs 24:12 — *If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?* The plot Mordecai searches out in Rest of Esther 12:2 cannot be feigned-ignorant, for the One who ponders the heart renders to each according to his works.
cards.s_text: And he heard their devices, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artexerxes the king; and so he certified the king of them.
cards.t_text: If you say, Behold, we knew it not; does not he that pondereth the heart consider it? and he that keeps your soul, does not he know it? and shall not he render to every man according to his works?

cards.note: Proverbs 24:11 — *If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;* Mordecai's certifying of the king in Rest of Esther 12:2 is exactly the deliverance from death the proverb forbids the righteous to withhold.
cards.s_text: And he heard their devices, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artexerxes the king; and so he certified the king of them.
cards.t_text: If you forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain;

cards.note: Esther 6:2 — *And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.* The record Mordecai writes in Rest of Esther 12:4 is the very page read on the sleepless night that begins his deliverance.
cards.s_text: And the king made a record of these things, and Mardocheus also wrote thereof.
cards.t_text: And it was found written, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s chamberlains, the keepers of the door, who sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.

cards.note: Esther 2:23 — *And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.* The strangling and the chronicling of Rest of Esther 12:3-4 is this same examination and record set down in the Hebrew.
cards.s_text: Then the king examined the two eunuchs, and after that they had confessed it, they were strangled.
cards.t_text: And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.

cards.note: Esther 2:21 — *In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.* The canonical book names the same two door-keepers whose plot Mordecai overhears in Rest of Esther 12:2.
cards.s_text: And he heard their devices, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artexerxes the king; and so he certified the king of them.
cards.t_text: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:18 — *How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not Elohim (God).* As Amalek struck the feeble hindmost, so Haman the Agagite targets the children and women of the scattered people — the same fearless cruelty.
cards.s_text: Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:
cards.t_text: How he met you by the way, and smote the hindmost of you, even all that were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he feared not Elohim (God).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:17 — *Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;* Haman's edict to slay "with their wives and children" is Amalek's old work, the very thing Israel is commanded never to forget.
cards.s_text: Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:
cards.t_text: Remember what Amalek did unto you by the way, when you were come forth out of Egypt;

cards.note: Exodus 17:16 — *For he said, Because Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn that Yahuah (LORD) will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.* Haman the Agagite, of Amalek's royal seed, is exactly the perpetual foe against whom Yahuah swore this generational war.
cards.s_text: Now when I asked my counsellors how this might be brought to pass, Aman, that excelled in wisdom among us, and was approved for his constant good will and steadfast fidelity, and had the honour of the second place in the kingdom,
cards.t_text: For he said, Because Yahuah (LORD) has sworn that Yahuah (LORD) will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

cards.note: Joel 2:13 — *And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.* Mordecai's appeal to be "merciful to your inheritance" and to "turn our sorrow into joy" leans on this very mercy that relents from the threatened evil.
cards.s_text: Hear my prayer, and be merciful to your inheritance: turn our sorrow into joy, that we may live, O Yahuah (God), and praise your name: and destroy not the mouths of them that praise you, O Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 9:26 — *I prayed therefore unto Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah (Lord) GOD, destroy not thy people and thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed through thy greatness, which thou hast brought forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand.* Mordecai's "despise not the portion delivered out of Egypt" is Moses' very intercession pleading the Exodus-redeemed inheritance against ruin.
cards.s_text: Despise not the portion, which you have delivered out of Egypt for your own self.
cards.t_text: I prayed therefore unto Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Adonai (Lord) GOD, destroy not your people and your inheritance, which you have redeemed through your greatness, which you have brought forth out of Egypt with a mighty hand.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:9 — *For the LORD'S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.* Mordecai's word "the inheritance, that has been yours from the beginning" rests on the Song of Moses' claim that Israel is Yahuah's own allotted portion.
cards.s_text: And now, O Yahuah (God) and King, spare your people: for their eyes are upon us to bring us to nought; yes, they desire to destroy the inheritance, that has been yours from the beginning.
cards.t_text: For the LORD’S portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:23 — *Sing, O ye heavens; for Yahuah (LORD) hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for Yahuah (LORD) hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Yashar'el (Israel).* The Maker of heaven and earth in Mordecai's prayer is the same who, having made all things, redeems Jacob — creation and salvation in one hand.
cards.s_text: For you have made heaven and earth, and all the wondrous things under the heaven.
cards.t_text: Sing, O you heavens; for Yahuah (LORD) has done it: shout, you lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, you mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for Yahuah (LORD) has redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Psalm 115:4 — *Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands.* Against the made-by-hands gods of the nations, Mordecai owns the living Yahuah whom no man can resist — the system of dead gods is empty, the Maker is not.
cards.s_text: You are Yahuah (God) of all things, and there is no man that can resist you, which are Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:6 — *Thou, even thou, art Yahuah (LORD) alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all things that are therein, the seas, and all that is therein, and thou preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth thee.* Mordecai's "you have made heaven and earth" is the same monotheist confession the Levites pray over the returned exiles.
cards.s_text: For you have made heaven and earth, and all the wondrous things under the heaven.
cards.t_text: You, even you, are Yahuah (LORD) alone; you have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all things that are therein, the seas, and all that is therein, and you preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth you.

cards.note: Psalm 115:1 — *Not unto us, O Yahuah (LORD), not unto us, but unto thy name give glory, for thy mercy, and for thy truth's sake.* Mordecai's refusal "to prefer the glory of man above the glory of Yahuah" is this psalm enacted — the Name keeps its glory.
cards.s_text: But I did this, that I might not prefer the glory of man above the glory of Yahuah (God): neither will I worship any but you, O Yahuah (God), neither will I do it in pride.
cards.t_text: Not unto us, O Yahuah (LORD), not unto us, but unto your name give glory, for your mercy, and for your truth’s sake.

cards.note: Daniel 3:18 — *But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.* Mordecai in Persia and the three in Babylon make the identical confession: no image, no man, gets the worship due to Elohim, whatever the cost.
cards.s_text: You know all things, and you know, Yahuah (God), that it was neither in contempt nor pride, nor for any desire of glory, that I did not bow down to proud Aman.
cards.t_text: But if not, be it known unto you, O king, that we will not serve your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.

cards.note: Exodus 20:5 — *Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) am a jealous Elohim (God), visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;* The very posture Mordecai withholds from Haman — bowing down and serving — is the act Sinai reserves for Yahuah alone.
cards.s_text: But I did this, that I might not prefer the glory of man above the glory of Yahuah (God): neither will I worship any but you, O Yahuah (God), neither will I do it in pride.
cards.t_text: You shall not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) am a jealous Elohim (God), visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;

cards.note: Exodus 20:3 — *Thou shalt have no other gods before me.* Mordecai's refusal to bow to Haman is simple obedience to the first commandment — no glory of man placed before the glory of Elohim.
cards.s_text: But I did this, that I might not prefer the glory of man above the glory of Yahuah (God): neither will I worship any but you, O Yahuah (God), neither will I do it in pride.
cards.t_text: You shall have no other gods before me.

cards.note: Psalm 83:4 — *They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Yashar'el (Israel) may be no more in remembrance.* Haman's plot to send a people "in one day" into the grave is one episode of the recurring confederate vow to erase Israel from the earth.
cards.s_text: That they, who of old and now also are malicious, may in one day with violence go into the grave, and so ever hereafter cause our affairs to be well settled, and without trouble.
cards.t_text: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Yashar'el (Israel) may be no more in remembrance.

cards.note: Esther 3:13 — *And the letters were sent by posts into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Yahudim (Jews), both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.* This is the same sword-without-mercy edict against wives and children that the rest-of-Esther letter publishes against the whole people.
cards.s_text: Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:
cards.t_text: And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Yahudim (Jews), both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.

cards.note: Esther 3:8 — *And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king's laws: therefore it is not for the king's profit to suffer them.* The Greek letter merely formalizes the very accusation Haman makes in the Hebrew Esther — a scattered people whose Torah-difference is cast as treason.
cards.s_text: Declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings, so as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us cannot go forward.
cards.t_text: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of your kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

cards.note: Psalm 25:16 — *Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.* Esther's joy 'only in Yahuah God of Abraham' amid the king's feast is the desolate one's single turning toward Him.
cards.s_text: Neither had yours handmaid any joy since the day that I was brought hither to this present, but in you, O Yahuah (God) of Abraham.
cards.t_text: Turn you unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.

cards.note: Psalm 119:46 — *I will speak of thy testimonies also before kings, and will not be ashamed.* Esther's abhorrence of heathen glory before a heathen throne is the psalmist's unashamed witness of the testimonies before kings.
cards.s_text: You know all things, O Yahuah (God); you know that I hate the glory of the unrighteous, and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised, and of all the heathen.
cards.t_text: I will speak of your testimonies also before kings, and will not be ashamed.

cards.note: Daniel 1:8 — *But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.* Esther's refusal of Aman's table and the king's wine is Daniel's same purposed-heart refusal of the king's defiling meat.
cards.s_text: And that yours handmaid has not eaten at Aman’s table, and that I have not greatly esteemed the king’s feast, nor drunk the wine of the drink offerings.
cards.t_text: But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.

cards.note: Judith 9:13 — *And make my speech and deceit to be their wound and stripe, who have purposed cruel things against your covenant, and your hallowed house, and against the top of Sion, and against the house of the possession of your children.* Judith too asks God to arm her speech against the enemy of the covenant, the sister-prayer to Esther's 'eloquent speech before the lion.'
cards.s_text: Give me eloquent speech in my mouth before the lion: turn his heart to hate him that fighteth against us, that there may be an end of him, and of all that are likeminded to him:
cards.t_text: And make my speech and deceit to be their wound and stripe, who have purposed cruel things against your covenant, and your hallowed house, and against the top of Sion, and against the house of the possession of your children.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:1 — *The king's heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.* Esther asks God to 'turn his heart' before the lion-king — the very thing Proverbs says is wholly in Yahuah's hand.
cards.s_text: Give me eloquent speech in my mouth before the lion: turn his heart to hate him that fighteth against us, that there may be an end of him, and of all that are likeminded to him:
cards.t_text: The king’s heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turns it whithersoever he will.

cards.note: Jeremiah 10:10 — *But Yahuah (LORD) is the true Elohim (God), he is the living Elohim (God), and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation.* The living everlasting King stands against the nothing-idols, the 'King of the nations' Esther invokes.
cards.s_text: Remember, O Yahuah (God), make thyself known in time of our affliction, and give me boldness, O King of the nations, and Yahuah (God) of all power.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (LORD) is the true Elohim (God), he is the living Elohim (God), and an everlasting king: at his wrath the earth shall tremble, and the nations shall not be able to abide his indignation.

cards.note: Psalm 115:4 — *Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands.* The 'them that be nothing' Esther begs God not to crown are the lifeless hand-made idols the psalm exposes.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (God), give not your sceptre to them that be nothing, and let them not laugh at our fall; but turn their device upon themselves, and make him an example, that has begun this against us.
cards.t_text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

cards.note: *And now we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies,* (The Rest of Esther 14:6). *And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:* (Leviticus 26:41). Esther's prayer follows the lines Moses laid down. Leviticus 26 said that if the people broke the covenant, Yahuah (God) himself would walk contrary to them and bring them into the land of their enemies, and that the way back would open when their uncircumcised hearts were humbled and they accepted the punishment as just. Esther does exactly that: we have sinned, you gave us into our enemies' hands, you are righteous. The enemy's hand is the covenant curse at work, not the covenant's end, and the next line in Leviticus is the promise, *then will I remember my covenant with Jacob* (Leviticus 26:42). Her humbled heart in Persia is the turn the Torah said would bring them home.
cards.s_text: And now we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies,
cards.t_text: And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:33 — *Howbeit thou art just in all that is brought upon us; for thou hast done right, but we have done wickedly:* Esther's 'O Yahuah, you are righteous' echoes the post-exile confession that God is just even in the hand of the enemy.
cards.s_text: Because we worshipped their gods: O Yahuah (God), you are righteous.
cards.t_text: Howbeit you are just in all that is brought upon us; for you have done right, but we have done wickedly:

cards.note: Daniel 9:5 — *We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from thy precepts and from thy judgments:* Daniel's confession in exile is Esther's 'we have sinned before thee,' the captive owning the covenant's justice.
cards.s_text: And now we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies,
cards.t_text: We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even by departing from your precepts and from your judgments:

cards.note: *From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.* (The Rest of Esther 14:5). *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* (Deuteronomy 7:6). Esther says she heard it in her youth, in the tribe of her family: Yahuah (God) took Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people for a perpetual inheritance. She is quoting Moses from memory in a Persian palace. Moses had said it to the whole people: chosen above all people on the face of the earth, a special people to himself. Esther is in exile, her people scattered under a foreign king and marked for slaughter, and nothing about that has cancelled what she heard in her tribe. A chosen people stays chosen in the lands of their scattering, and the inheritance is perpetual because the one who gave it does not take it back.
cards.s_text: From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.
cards.t_text: For you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has chosen you to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 19:5 — *Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:* The peculiar-treasure of Sinai is the 'perpetual inheritance' Esther was taught from her youth.
cards.s_text: From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, if you will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then you shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine:

cards.note: *For your power stands not in multitude nor your might in strong men: for you are a Yahuah (God) of the afflicted, an helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.* (Judith 9:11). *But deliver us with yours hand, and help me that am desolate, and which have no other help but you.* (The Rest of Esther 14:14). Two women, two prayers, the same confession. Judith says Yahuah (God) is the helper of the oppressed and the saviour of those without hope, that his power never stood in numbers or strong men. Esther says it as a plea rather than a creed: deliver us with your hand, help me that am desolate, I have no other help but you. Each one stands alone in front of a power that means to wipe out her people, and each one knows the only hand that can turn it. The strength of Yashar'el (Israel) in both books is a woman on her knees who has run out of every other help.
cards.s_text: But deliver us with yours hand, and help me that am desolate, and which have no other help but you.
cards.t_text: For your power stands not in multitude nor your might in strong men: for you are a Yahuah (God) of the afflicted, an helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.

cards.note: Psalm 25:16 — *Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.* David's desolate-and-afflicted plea is the same word Esther twice calls herself, the helpless turned wholly toward Yahuah.
cards.s_text: But deliver us with yours hand, and help me that am desolate, and which have no other help but you.
cards.t_text: Turn you unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted.

cards.note: Psalm 22:11 — *Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.* Esther's 'no helper but thee' is the Passion-psalm's own none-to-help, the righteous left utterly alone with God.
cards.s_text: And she prayed to Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, O my Elohim (God), you only art our King: help me, desolate woman, which have no helper but you:
cards.t_text: Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.

cards.note: Matthew 6:17 — *But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;* Esther's secret, ash-strewn fast — joy laid aside for the Father alone — is the very hiddenness the Messiah commands.
cards.s_text: And laid away her glorious apparel, and put on the garments of anguish and mourning: and instead of precious ointments, she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she humbled her body greatly, and all the places of her joy she filled with her torn hair.
cards.t_text: But you, when you fastest, anoint your head, and wash your face;

cards.note: Judith 9:1 — *Judith fell upon her face, and put ashes upon her head, and uncovered the sackcloth with which she was clothed; and about the time that the incense of that evening was offered in Jerusalem in the house of Yahuah (God) Judith cried with a loud voice, and said,* Esther's deliverer-sister begins her own intercession in the same ashes, fear of death turned into prayer.
cards.s_text: Queen Esther also, being in fear of death, resorted to Yahuah (God):
cards.t_text: Judith fell upon her face, and put ashes upon her head, and uncovered the sackcloth with which she was clothed; and about the time that the incense of that evening was offered in Jerusalem in the house of Yahuah (God) Judith cried with a loud voice, and said,

cards.note: Joel 2:13 — *And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.* Esther's humbled body and laid-away glory is the outward sign of the inward rending Joel demands.
cards.s_text: And laid away her glorious apparel, and put on the garments of anguish and mourning: and instead of precious ointments, she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she humbled her body greatly, and all the places of her joy she filled with her torn hair.
cards.t_text: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.

cards.note: Joel 2:12 — *Therefore also now, saith Yahuah (LORD), turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:* The prophet's call to fasting-and-mourning is the very rite Esther enacts in ashes and torn hair.
cards.s_text: And laid away her glorious apparel, and put on the garments of anguish and mourning: and instead of precious ointments, she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she humbled her body greatly, and all the places of her joy she filled with her torn hair.
cards.t_text: Therefore also now, says Yahuah (LORD), turn you even to me with all your heart, and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning:

cards.note: Exodus 34:29 — *And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.* The shining, grace-filled countenance the queen marvels at in Rest of Esther 15:14 echoes the radiant face that the divine presence gives in the Tanakh.
cards.s_text: For wonderful art you, lord, and your countenance is full of grace.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.

cards.note: Judges 13:6 — *Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of Elohim (God) came unto me, and his countenance was like the countenance of an angel of Elohim (God), very terrible: but I asked him not whence he was, neither told he me his name:* Manoah's wife describes the same fearful angel-like countenance the queen sees in the king in Rest of Esther 15:13.
cards.s_text: Then said she to him, I saw you, my lord, as an angel of Yahuah (God), and my heart was troubled for fear of your majesty.
cards.t_text: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, A man of Elohim (God) came unto me, and his countenance was like the countenance of an angel of Elohim (God), very terrible: but I asked him not whence he was, neither told he me his name:

cards.note: Nehemiah 2:8 — *And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my Elohim (God) upon me.* The king's granting of Nehemiah's request by the good hand of Elohim is the same hand that spares the queen and bids her come near in Rest of Esther 15:10.
cards.s_text: You shall not die, though our commandment be general: come near.
cards.t_text: And a letter unto Asaph the keeper of the king’s forest, that he may give me timber to make beams for the gates of the palace which appertained to the house, and for the wall of the city, and for the house that I shall enter into. And the king granted me, according to the good hand of my Elohim (God) upon me.

cards.note: Nehemiah 2:4 — *Then the king said unto me, For what dost thou make request? So I prayed to the Elohim (God) of heaven.* Nehemiah's prayer at the king's invitation to speak mirrors the king's word ‘Speak to me’ in Rest of Esther 15:12, where the request is borne on intercession.
cards.s_text: And embraced her, and said, Speak to me.
cards.t_text: Then the king said unto me, For what do you make request? So I prayed to the Elohim (God) of heaven.

cards.note: Esther 5:2 — *And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.* The golden sceptre laid upon the queen's neck in Rest of Esther 15:11 is the canonical sceptre of favour held out and touched.
cards.s_text: And so he held up his golden sceptre, and laid it upon her neck,
cards.t_text: And it was so, when the king saw Esther the queen standing in the court, that she obtained favour in his sight: and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre that was in his hand. So Esther drew near, and touched the top of the sceptre.

cards.note: Psalm 37:5 — *Commit thy way unto Yahuah (LORD); trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.* The psalm's counsel to commit the way and let Yahuah bring it to pass is fulfilled when He changes the king's spirit in Rest of Esther 15:8.
cards.s_text: Then Yahuah (God) changed the spirit of the king into mildness, who in a fear leaped from his throne, and took her in his arms, till she came to herself again, and comforted her with loving words and said to her,
cards.t_text: Commit your way unto Yahuah (LORD); trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.
