cards.t_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) will seek that which is well, pleasing to him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law.

cards.note: *They that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways* (Sirach 2:15). *The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way* (Psalm 25:9): the way Yahuah teaches the meek is His own way, and Sirach names what it is to be so taught — *they that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways*. To be taught of Yahuah is to be brought to keep His ways; the meek taught are the obedient.
cards.s_text: The meek will he guide in judgment: and the meek will he teach his way.
cards.t_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) will not disobey his Word; and they that love him will keep his ways.

cards.note: Romans 7:23 — *But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.* The mind's law against the passions of the members is the same contest 4 Maccabees frames as Reason over the passions.

cards.t_text: But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.

cards.note: Romans 7:22 — *For I delight in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man:* the inward delight in the Law is exactly the inner Reason 4 Maccabees sets over the passions.
cards.s_text: Philosophical in the highest degree is the question I propose to discuss, namely whether the Inspired Reason is supreme ruler over the passions; and to the philosophy of it I would seriously
cards.t_text: For I delight in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man:

cards.note: Genesis 49:5 — *Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.* This is the censure 4 Maccabees recalls as Jacob blaming the houses of Simeon and Levi.

cards.t_text: Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 5:21 — *Neither shalt thou desire thy neighbour's wife, neither shalt thou covet thy neighbour's house, his field, or his manservant, or his maidservant, his ox, or his ass, or any thing that is thy neighbour's.* Moses' second giving of the Tenth Word is the same command 4 Maccabees cites — "when the Law orders us not to covet."
cards.s_text: impulse not only of sexual desire, but of all sorts of covetings. For the Law says, 'Thou shalt not
cards.t_text: Neither shall you desire your neighbour’s wife, neither shall you covet your neighbour’s house, his field, or his manservant, or his maidservant, his ox, or his ass, or any thing that is your neighbour’s.

cards.note: Genesis 39:12 — *And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.* Joseph fleeing the temptation is the deed 4 Maccabees praises as Reason mastering the passion.

cards.t_text: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 5:11 — *Now when this that was done came to the king's ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms.* The plundering of the city before the decrees is the same furious return from Egypt and storming of Jerusalem the other sibling book records.
cards.s_text: And when he had plundered the city he made a decree denouncing the penalty of death upon any who should be seen to live after the Law of our fathers.
cards.t_text: Now when this that was done came to the king’s ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms,

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 1:62 — *Howbeit many in Yashar'el (Israel) were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean thing.* The men tortured to eat unclean meats answer the many resolved not to eat any unclean thing — the dietary law of Leviticus standing under threat of death.
cards.s_text: When therefore his decrees continued to be contemned by the mass of the people, he personally tried to force by tortures each man separately to eat unclean meats and thus abjure the Yahudi (Jewish) religion.
cards.t_text: Howbeit many in Yashar'el (Israel) were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean thing.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 1:60 — *At which time according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.* The women flung from the rocks for circumcising their sons are the same mothers slain for the covenant in the sibling chronicle.
cards.s_text: so that even women for circumcising their sons, though they knew beforehand what would be their fate, were flung, together with their offspring, headlong from the rocks.
cards.t_text: At which time according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 1:50 — *And whoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.* The death-penalty decree against living after the Law of the fathers is the king's edict the sibling book records.
cards.s_text: And when he had plundered the city he made a decree denouncing the penalty of death upon any who should be seen to live after the Law of our fathers.
cards.t_text: And whoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 1:20 — *And after that Antiochus had struck Egypt, he returned again in the hundred forty and third year, and went up against Yashar'el (Israel) and Jerusalem with a great multitude.* The same return from Egypt and march on Jerusalem that 4 Maccabees compresses into Antiochus marching back against the city.
cards.s_text: For when he was carrying on war with Ptolemy in Egypt and heard that the people of Jerusalem had rejoiced exceedingly over a report of his death, he immediately marched back against them.
cards.t_text: And after that Antiochus had struck Egypt, he returned again in the hundred forty and third year, and went up against Yashar'el (Israel) and Jerusalem with a great multitude,

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:33 — *Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake Yahuah (God) has granted you life.* Onias the high priest interceding so the spoiler is granted his life is the same mercy the sibling book records at the same altar.
cards.s_text: Moved by these words, Onias, the high-priest, although most scrupulous in other cases, made intercession for him lest King Seleucus should possibly think that Apollonius had been overthrown by a human device and not by divine justice.
cards.t_text: Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake Yahuah (God) has granted you life:

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:29 — *For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.* Apollonius fallen half-dead with hands stretched to heaven matches the king's agent cast down speechless by the hand of Elohim.
cards.s_text: And Apollonius fell down half-dead in the Court of the Gentiles, and stretched out his hands to heaven, and with tears he entreated the Hebrews that they would make intercession for him and stay the wrath of the heavenly host.
cards.t_text: For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:25 — *For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.* The heavenly horsemen flashing from heaven who terrify the raiders are the same apparition the sibling book describes striking the king's man down.

cards.t_text: For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.

cards.t_text: O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless you Yahuah (God): praise and exalt him above all for ever: for he has delivered us from hell, and saved us from the hand of death, and delivered us out of the midst of the furnace and burning flame: even out of the midst of the fire has he delivered us.

cards.note: *For he does scourge, and has mercy: he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again: neither is there any that can avoid his hand* (Tobit 13:2). *Thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit* (Psalm 30:3): the restored library prays the same brought-up motion in its own thanksgiving song — *he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again*. The God who can bring down to Sheol and lift back up is the One David thanks for his own deliverance from the pit.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (LORD), you have brought up my soul from the grave: you have kept me alive, that I should not go down to the pit.
cards.t_text: For he does scourge, and has mercy: he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again: neither is there any that can avoid his hand.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Sirach 2:10). *Let me never be ashamed* (Psalm 31:1): the wisdom tradition asks the never-confounded plea as a settled fact of all the generations — none who trusted Yahuah was ever confounded, none who feared Him forsaken. The psalmist's trust stands on that long record of faithfulness.
cards.s_text: In you, O Yahuah (LORD), do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in your righteousness.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him* (Sirach 2:6). *In thee, O Yahuah (LORD), do I put my trust* (Psalm 31:1): the wisdom call is the psalm's own posture — believe, and He will help; order your way and trust in Him. The trust the psalmist declares is the trust the wisdom tradition commends, the trust that is helped and never put to shame.
cards.s_text: In you, O Yahuah (LORD), do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in your righteousness.
cards.t_text: Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.

cards.note: *Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth* (Ecclesiasticus 5:7). *For this shall every one that is godly pray unto thee in a time when thou mayest be found* (Psalm 32:6): turn while He may be found, the wisdom warns — make no tarrying, put it not off. The time of finding is now, in confession, before the floods of great waters rise.
cards.s_text: For this shall every one that is godly pray unto you in a time when you may be found: surely in the floods of great waters they shall not come nigh unto him.
cards.t_text: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.

cards.note: *Be not ashamed to confess your sins; and force not the course of the river* (Ecclesiasticus 4:26). *I said, I will confess my transgressions unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 32:5): the restored wisdom presses the same charge — be not ashamed to confess, do not dam up what must flow out. David's silence wasted his bones (32:3) until he opened his mouth in confession.
cards.s_text: I acknowledged my sin unto you, and my iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto Yahuah (LORD); and you forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah.
cards.t_text: Be not ashamed to confess your sins; and force not the course of the river.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). *By the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth* (Psalm 33:6): the second-Temple prayer confesses the same — Yahuah *have made all things with your word*. The witness outside the canon sings the psalm's own confession: all things, the heavens and their host, made by the Word.
cards.s_text: By the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,

cards.note: *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him* (Sirach 2:6). *Blessed is the man that trusteth in him* (Psalm 34:8): the restored wisdom presses the same charge — believe, order thy way, and trust in Yahuah, and He will help. The blessedness of the psalm is the help promised to the one who trusts.
cards.s_text: O taste and see that Yahuah (LORD) is good: blessed is the man that trusts in him.
cards.t_text: Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?* (Sirach 2:10). *Blessed is the man that trusteth in him* (Psalm 34:8): the wisdom of old tests the promise against all the generations and finds none who trusted Yahuah were ever confounded — the blessed man who trusts is never put to shame.
cards.s_text: O taste and see that Yahuah (LORD) is good: blessed is the man that trusts in him.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *And weigh your words in a balance, and make a door and bar for your mouth* (Sirach 28:25). *Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile* (Psalm 34:13): the restored wisdom gives the same guard — weigh the words, set a door and bar upon the mouth. The kept tongue of the psalm is the barred door of Sirach, the same discipline of the lips unto life.
cards.s_text: Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking guile.
cards.t_text: And weigh your words in a balance, and make a door and bar for your mouth.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Sirach 2:10). *None of them that trust in him shall be desolate* (Psalm 34:22): the restored wisdom seals the promise against all the generations — none who trusted Yahuah were ever confounded or forsaken. The servants whose souls He redeems are never left desolate.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) redeemeth the soul of his servants: and none of them that trust in him shall be desolate.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it* (Sirach 27:26). *Without cause have they hid for me their net in a pit, which without cause they have digged for my soul* (Psalm 35:7): the restored wisdom of Sirach carries the same recoil — *he that sets a trap shall be taken in it*. The net hidden for the righteous one snares the one who hid it; the Judge lets the trap take its own maker.
cards.s_text: For without cause have they hid for me their net in a pit, which without cause they have digged for my soul.
cards.t_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it.

cards.note: *He that winketh with the eyes works evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him* (Sirach 27:22). *Neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause* (Psalm 35:19): the restored wisdom names the very gesture — *he that winketh with the eyes works evil*. The enemies who wink in scorn at the righteous one are the workers of evil Sirach warns against.
cards.s_text: Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause.
cards.t_text: He that winketh with the eyes works evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him.

cards.note: *They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die* (Sirach 27:29). *Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me* (Psalm 35:19): the wisdom of Sirach answers the cry — *they that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare*. The enemies who wrongfully rejoice over the hated-without-cause one are judged, taken in the very snare they set.
cards.s_text: Let not them that are my enemies wrongfully rejoice over me: neither let them wink with the eye that hate me without a cause.
cards.t_text: They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; and anguish shall consume them before they die.

cards.note: *For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26). *In thy light shall we see light* (Psalm 36:9): the light by which we see light is named the brightness of the everlasting light — the wisdom that flows from Yahuah, the unspotted mirror of His power and the image of His goodness. The psalm's light-within-light is that everlasting brightness.
cards.s_text: For with you is the fountain of life: in your light shall we see light.
cards.t_text: For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness.

cards.note: *You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom* (Baruch 3:12). *For with thee is the fountain of life* (Psalm 36:9): the fountain with Yahuah is the very spring Baruch warns Yashar'el (Israel) it has forsaken — the fountain of wisdom which is the fountain of life, length of days, and *the light of the eyes* (Baruch 3:14). To leave that spring is to perish in a strange land; to drink of it is life.
cards.s_text: For with you is the fountain of life: in your light shall we see light.
cards.t_text: You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom.

cards.note: *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:6). *Trust in Yahuah (LORD), and do good; so shalt thou dwell in the land, and verily thou shalt be fed.* (Psalm 37:3). Sirach is repeating David. Believe in him, order your way aright, trust in him, is the same counsel as trust in Yahuah (LORD) and do good, the trusting and the doing bound together in one breath. Neither verse lets a man trust Yahuah (God) while walking however he pleases, and neither lets him order his way as if his own ordering were what held him up. The whole life leans on his help, and the leaning shows up as a way set aright.
cards.s_text: Trust in Yahuah (LORD), and do good; so shall you dwell in the land, and verily you shall be fed.
cards.t_text: Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.

cards.note: *You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall* (Sirach 2:7). *Rest in Yahuah (LORD), and wait patiently for him* (Psalm 37:7): the psalm's patient waiting is the son of Sirach's — *wait for his mercy* and *go not aside* — the still trust that does not fret at the prospering wicked but waits on Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Rest in Yahuah (LORD), and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who brings wicked devices to pass.
cards.t_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Sirach 2:10). *Yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread* (Psalm 37:25): the son of Sirach makes the psalmist's witness a challenge to the generations — none who trusted Yahuah was ever confounded or forsaken. The righteous one is never abandoned.
cards.s_text: I have been young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life* (2 Maccabees 7:9). *Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter* (Psalm 44:22): the Maccabean martyr dies *for his laws* — innocent suffering FOR the covenant, not for sin — and looks past the slaughter to the King who raises the faithful to everlasting life. The sheep slain for His sake are the ones He raises.
cards.s_text: Yea, for your sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
cards.t_text: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.

cards.note: *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6). *Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death* (Psalm 44:19): the sore breaking is the furnace — the righteous tried as gold and received as an offering, the affliction itself the refining of the faithful, not the curse of the false.
cards.s_text: Though you have sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.
cards.t_text: As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.

cards.note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5). *Though thou hast sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death* (Psalm 44:19): the breaking is a proving, not a casting-off — a little chastening that ends in great reward; Yahuah proves the righteous and finds them worthy of Himself.
cards.s_text: Though you have sore broken us in the place of dragons, and covered us with the shadow of death.
cards.t_text: And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). *All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten thee, neither have we dealt falsely in thy covenant* (Psalm 44:17): the affliction is no proof of abandonment — the souls of the covenant-keeping righteous are held in Yahuah's hand, beyond the reach of the torment that seems to undo them.
cards.s_text: All this is come upon us; yet have we not forgotten you, neither have we dealt falsely in your covenant.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). *the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion... the city of the great King* (Psalm 48:2): the joy of the whole earth is the nations streaming from far to the Name, the ingathering to the city of the great King. Zion becomes the joy of the whole earth as the nations come up to praise.
cards.s_text: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *Give praise to Yahuah (God), for he is good: and praise the everlasting King, that his tabernacle may be builded in you again with joy, and let him make joyful there in you those that are captives* (Tobit 13:10). *the city of the great King* (Psalm 48:2): the restored wisdom of Tobit names the same King — *the everlasting King* whose tabernacle is builded again in Jerusalem with joy, gathering home the captives. The great King of the psalm rebuilds and rejoices over His city.
cards.s_text: Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.
cards.t_text: Give praise to Yahuah (God), for he is good: and praise the everlasting King, that his tabernacle may be builded in you again with joy, and let him make joyful there in you those that are captives, and love in you for ever those that are miserable.

cards.note: *Give, and take, and sanctify your soul; for there is no seeking of dainties in the grave* (Sirach 14:16). *Wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others* (Psalm 49:10): the restored wisdom presses the same — there is no enjoying of goods in the grave, and *Shall you not leave your travails to another?* (Sirach 14:15). The hoarded wealth is left; the grave seeks no dainties.
cards.s_text: For he sees that wise men die, likewise the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others.
cards.t_text: Give, and take, and sanctify your soul; for there is no seeking of dainties in the grave.

cards.note: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8-9). *Man being in honour abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish* (Psalm 49:12): the ungodly confess too late what the psalm taught — pride and riches profit nothing, all passed away like a shadow. The honour and the wealth abide not; only the verdict of the grave remains.
cards.s_text: Nevertheless man being in honour abides not: he is like the beasts that perish.
cards.t_text: What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?

cards.note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Sirach 11:19). *For when he dieth he shall carry nothing away* (Psalm 49:17), against the conceit that *their houses shall continue for ever* (49:11): the restored wisdom names the very thought — the man at rest among his goods who knows not he must leave them to others and die. He carries nothing away.
cards.s_text: For when he dies he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Sirach 35:1). *I will take no bullock out of thy house, nor he goats out of thy folds* (Psalm 50:9): the restored wisdom binds the offering to the obedience — to keep the law IS to bring offerings enough. Yahuah needs no bullock from a hand that has not first kept His commandment.
cards.s_text: I will take no bullock out of your house, nor he goats out of your folds.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise. To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation* (Sirach 35:2-3). *Offer unto Elohim (God) thanksgiving* (Psalm 50:14): the thanksgiving the psalm seeks is the alms that sacrifice praise and the wickedness departed from — Sirach makes the right walk itself the acceptable offering.
cards.s_text: Offer unto Elohim (God) thanksgiving; and pay your vows unto the El Elyon (most High):
cards.t_text: He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.

cards.note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted* (Sirach 34:18). *Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?* (Psalm 50:13): the psalm scorns the carcass offered from a corrupt life, and Sirach names it ridiculous — the offering of the wrongfully-gotten is no offering at all.
cards.s_text: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
cards.t_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.

cards.note: *The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices* (Sirach 34:19). *Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?* (Psalm 50:13): no multitude of sacrifices buys off the wicked — the El Elyon (most High) is not pleased with their offerings. The carcass cannot stand in for the heart the psalm demands.
cards.s_text: Will I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
cards.t_text: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.

cards.note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). The *man of sorrows... despised, and we esteemed him not* (Isaiah 53:3) is the persecuted righteous one the ungodly plot against — *let us lie in wait for the righteous*. The 2nd-Temple witness already reads the suffering of the righteous one as the world's hatred of the one who reproves its lawlessness.
cards.s_text: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
cards.t_text: Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.

cards.note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). The servant who *opened not his mouth* and was *numbered with the transgressors* (Isaiah 53:7,12) is foreshadowed in the righteous one tortured to test his meekness — *let us examine him with despitefulness and torture... and prove his patience*. The mockers' own words script the patient, silent suffering of the just.
cards.s_text: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he has poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
cards.t_text: Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.

cards.note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). The servant *poured out his soul unto death* and *was numbered with the transgressors* (Isaiah 53:12); the ungodly resolve *let us condemn him with a shameful death*. The shameful death of the righteous son who calls Yahuah his father (2:16-18) is the very pattern Isaiah 53 unfolds — the just one slain, then vindicated.
cards.s_text: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he has poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
cards.t_text: Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.

cards.note: *For you are my defender and helper, and has preserved my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lips that forge lies, and has been my helper against my adversaries* (Sirach 51:2). *For he hath delivered me out of all trouble* (Psalm 54:7): the restored wisdom sings the very contours of David's Ziphite betrayal — preserved from the slanderous tongue and the lips that forge lies, helped against the adversaries. The trouble David is delivered out of is the lying tongue of those who betrayed his hiding place.
cards.s_text: For he has delivered me out of all trouble: and my eye has seen his desire upon my enemies.
cards.t_text: For you are my defender and helper, and has preserved my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lips that forge lies, and has been my helper against my adversaries:

cards.note: *And have delivered me, according to the multitude of your mercies and greatness of your name, from the teeth of them that were ready to devour me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had* (Sirach 51:3). *For he hath delivered me out of all trouble* (Psalm 54:7): the deliverance is by the greatness of the Name (the very Name of 54:1) and is out of the hands of *such as sought after my life* — the oppressors who *seek after my soul* in 54:3. The Name that saves delivers out of the hand that hunts.
cards.s_text: For he has delivered me out of all trouble: and my eye has seen his desire upon my enemies.
cards.t_text: And have delivered me, according to the multitude of your mercies and greatness of your name, from the teeth of them that were ready to devour me, and out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the manifold afflictions which I had;

cards.note: *For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble* (Sirach 6:8). *But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance* (Psalm 55:13): the restored wisdom names the very wound — the friend for his own occasion who will not abide in the day of trouble. The trusted equal of the psalm is the fair-weather friend of Sirach, gone in the day of need.
cards.s_text: But it was you, a man my equal, my guide, and my acquaintance.
cards.t_text: For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.

cards.note: *Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction* (Sirach 6:10). *We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of Elohim (God) in company* (Psalm 55:14): the table-companion of Sirach is the company of the psalm — the one who shared the meal and the counsel, who will not continue in the day of affliction. The shared table makes the betrayal sharper.
cards.s_text: We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of Elohim (God) in company.
cards.t_text: Again, some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction.

cards.note: *If you be brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himself from your face* (Sirach 6:12). *The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart* (Psalm 55:21): the smooth friend of the psalm is the one Sirach warns of — when you are brought low he turns against you and hides his face. The butter-smooth words mask the heart that will be against you in the fall.
cards.s_text: The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.
cards.t_text: If you be brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himself from your face.

cards.note: *Is it not a grief to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?* (Sirach 37:2). *But it was thou, a man mine equal, my guide, and mine acquaintance* (Psalm 55:13): Sirach measures the wound of the psalm exactly — the companion and friend turned enemy is a grief unto death. The equal and acquaintance of the psalm, turned, is that very grief.
cards.s_text: But it was you, a man my equal, my guide, and my acquaintance.
cards.t_text: Is it not a grief to death, when a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?

cards.note: *There is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him* (Sirach 37:4). *We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of Elohim (God) in company* (Psalm 55:14): the companion of sweet counsel is the very figure Sirach names — glad in prosperity, against you in trouble. The shared walk to the house of Elohim turns, in the day of trouble, to enmity.
cards.s_text: We took sweet counsel together, and walked unto the house of Elohim (God) in company.
cards.t_text: There is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him.

cards.note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). The Servant who *gave my back to the smiters... I hid not my face from shame and spitting* (Isaiah 50:6) is the righteous one the wicked plot to torture — to *prove his patience*. The restored library witnesses the same pattern: the meek, righteous One examined with despite, who does not turn his face away.
cards.s_text: I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting.
cards.t_text: Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb* (Sirach 1:14). The restored witness carries the motto of *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge* (Proverbs 1:7) almost word for word: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom*. The same root runs the whole wisdom library — the fear of Yahuah is where wisdom begins, planted in the faithful from the womb.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). The restored witness binds the motto of *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge* (Proverbs 1:7) to the Torah outright: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments*. Wisdom is not earned apart from the commandments nor against them — the fear of Yahuah and the keeping of His word are the one path to her.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
cards.t_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.

cards.note: *Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yes, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:12). The Wisdom who *crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets* (Proverbs 1:20) is the same who is *easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her*. She does not hide — she cries aloud and shows herself to all who will seek; the failure is never in Wisdom's silence but in the simple ones' refusal to turn.
cards.s_text: Wisdom cries without; she utters her voice in the streets:
cards.t_text: Wisdom is glorious, and never fadeth away: yes, she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.

cards.note: *For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably to them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:16). The crying Wisdom of *she uttereth her voice in the streets* (Proverbs 1:20) is the seeking Wisdom who *goes about seeking such as are worthy of her... and meeteth them in every thought*. She is not waited upon in a temple but walks the streets seeking — the same Wisdom-figure who in chapter 8 was the Father's delight before the world was.
cards.s_text: Wisdom cries without; she utters her voice in the streets:
cards.t_text: For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably to them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.

cards.note: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever* (Sirach 1:1). The restored witness opens on the very truth of *For Yahuah (LORD) giveth wisdom* (Proverbs 2:6): *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever*. There is no wisdom apart from its Source; she is His to give.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (LORD) gives wisdom: out of his mouth comes knowledge and understanding.
cards.t_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.

cards.note: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). The opening charge to *receive my words, and hide my commandments with thee* (Proverbs 2:1) is kept whole by the restored witness: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments*. Wisdom is not loosed from the commandments but given through their keeping — the Torah is the path to her, never the burden laid aside.
cards.s_text: My son, if you will receive my words, and hide my commandments with you;
cards.t_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb* (Sirach 1:14). The restored witness keeps the very refrain Proverbs 2:5 reaches for — *Then shalt thou understand the fear of Yahuah (LORD)* — naming it *the beginning of wisdom*. The fear of Yahuah is the root the faithful are born to.
cards.s_text: Then shall you understand the fear of Yahuah (LORD), and find the knowledge of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). To seek wisdom *as silver* and *as for hid treasures* (Proverbs 2:4) is to esteem her above all treasure, as the restored witness does: *esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her*. The one who counts wisdom the true treasure has already begun to find her.
cards.s_text: If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hid treasures;
cards.t_text: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.

cards.note: *Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you: and when you have got hold of her, let her not go* (Sirach 6:27). The restored witness keeps the same charge as *If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as for hid treasures* (Proverbs 2:4): *Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you*. Wisdom is found by the diligent searcher, and once found she is to be held fast.
cards.s_text: If you seek her as silver, and search for her as for hid treasures;
cards.t_text: Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you: and when you have got hold of her, let her not go.

cards.note: *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:8). *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:* (Proverbs 3:9). Sirach is repeating Solomon almost word for word. Honour Yahuah (LORD) with what you have and with your firstfruits, Solomon says; give Yahuah (God) his honour and do not diminish the firstfruits of your hands, says Sirach, and he adds the good eye, the ungrudging eye, as the manner of it. The first and the best belong to Yahuah (God), and they are not to be cut short. The proverb came down whole, and Sirach handed it on whole.
cards.s_text: Honour Yahuah (LORD) with your substance, and with the firstfruits of all your increase:
cards.t_text: Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). The restored witness gives the reason not to *despise... the chastening* (Proverbs 3:11): *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity*. The correction is the refining furnace that proves the son acceptable, as gold is proved in the fire — adversity is the Father's assaying, not His rejection.
cards.s_text: My son, despise not the chastening of Yahuah (LORD); neither be weary of his correction:
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9). The restored witness sees the same Wisdom at the founding of the earth: *Yahuah (LORD) by wisdom hath founded the earth* (Proverbs 3:19) is *wisdom... was present when you madest the world*. Wisdom stood with the Father at creation, knowing His works — the expressed agent through whom the world was made.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) by wisdom has founded the earth; by understanding has he established the heavens.
cards.t_text: And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments.

cards.note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). The restored witness frames Wisdom — the One who was *by him, as one brought up with him* (Proverbs 8:30) — as *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty*. She proceeds FROM the Almighty's own glory, the expressed breath of the Formless Source: brought forth from the Father's being, not fashioned beside it.
cards.s_text: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;
cards.t_text: For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.

cards.note: *For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:26). The Wisdom *daily his delight, rejoicing always before him* (Proverbs 8:30) is *the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness* — the very language the gospel takes up of the Son, *the brightness of his glory* (Hebrews 1:3). The Formed One is the radiance and exact mirror of the Formless Father, his image perfectly drawn.
cards.s_text: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him;
cards.t_text: For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of Yahuah (God), and the image of his goodness.

cards.note: *And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments.* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9). When Wisdom says *When he prepared the heavens, I was there* (Proverbs 8:27), the restored witness agrees: she *was present when you madest the world*. The Formed Son was there at the making — present at the founding, the workman who knew the Father's works because he wrought them with him.
cards.s_text: When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth:
cards.t_text: And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in your sight, and right in your commandments.

cards.note: *I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud* (Sirach 24:3). Wisdom's *Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way* (Proverbs 8:22) is sung again as *I came out of the mouth of the Most High* — the expressed Word PROCEEDING from the Formless Father, drawn out of his own mouth. She is not made beside him but brought forth FROM him, the utterance of the Most High going out to cover the earth.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old.
cards.t_text: I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.

cards.note: *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail* (Sirach 24:9). Wisdom's *I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was* (Proverbs 8:23) is echoed in *He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail*. The "created/set up" is the bringing-forth before all worlds of the One who never fails — begotten of the Father before time, not a perishable thing fashioned within it; the everlasting Word who was there before the earth was.
cards.s_text: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.
cards.t_text: He created me from the beginning before the world, and I shall never fail.

cards.note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits* (Sirach 24:19). The restored witness keeps Wisdom's same banquet-cry as *Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled* (Proverbs 9:5): *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits*. Wisdom spreads her table in both books and bids the desirous come and eat; the next verses — *they that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty* (Sirach 24:21) — make the feast inexhaustible, the same table John's bread of life never empties.
cards.s_text: Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb* (Sirach 1:14). The restored witness restates Proverbs 9:10 nearly verbatim — *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom* — and roots it deeper still: *it was created with the faithful in the womb*. The fear of Yahuah as the beginning of wisdom is the one foundation the whole wisdom-library is built upon, planted in the faithful from the start.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life* (Sirach 1:20). The multiplied days of *by me thy days shall be multiplied* (Proverbs 9:11) are bound by the restored witness to the fear of Yahuah of the verse just before (9:10): *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life*. The long life is the branch that grows from the root — fear Yahuah, and the years are increased.
cards.s_text: For by me your days shall be multiplied, and the years of your life shall be increased.
cards.t_text: The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life.

cards.note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.* (Isaiah 55:1). Wisdom calls everyone who wants her to come and fill themselves; the prophet calls everyone who thirsts to come to the waters and eat without money. Both invitations go out to the desirous and the thirsty, and both offer what satisfies for nothing but the coming. There is no price at the door in either verse, only the call to come and be filled.
cards.s_text: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come you to the waters, and he that has no money; come you, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: *They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty* (Sirach 24:21). *Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good* (Isaiah 55:2) — Wisdom answers the same hunger: only she, the Word, satisfies; the bread that is not bread leaves the soul empty, but the desirous keep coming to be filled.
cards.s_text: Wherefore do you spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfies not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat you that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness.
cards.t_text: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.

cards.note: *So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?* (Sirach 34:26). *Is it such a fast that I have chosen?* (Isaiah 58:5) — Sirach names the same vanity: the fast that humbles the body while the man returns to his sin profits nothing, and his prayer is not heard. The afflicted soul without turned conduct is the empty fast Isaiah rebukes.
cards.s_text: Is it such a fast that I have chosen? a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? will you call this a fast, and an acceptable day to Yahuah (LORD)?
cards.t_text: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?

cards.note: *He that washeth himself after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it again, what availeth his washing?* (Sirach 34:25). *Ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high* (Isaiah 58:4) — the washing undone by re-touching the corpse is the fast undone by the fist of wickedness. The ritual cleansing that does not change the conduct avails nothing; the voice of such a fast is not heard on high.
cards.s_text: Behold, you fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: you shall not fast as you do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high.
cards.t_text: He that washeth himself after the touching of a dead body, if he touch it again, what availeth his washing?

cards.note: *He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:17). This is the same picture as *and was clad with zeal as a cloke* (Isaiah 59:17) — Yahuah arming Himself with His own jealousy/zeal to repay His adversaries. The restored library witnesses the divine warrior clothing Himself in zeal to bring judgment and salvation.
cards.s_text: For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke.
cards.t_text: He shall take to him his jealousy for complete armour, and make the creature his weapon for the revenge of his enemies.

cards.note: *He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of an helmet* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:18). Almost word for word with *he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head* (Isaiah 59:17). The whole armour of the LORD — breastplate of righteousness, helmet — is sung twice in the library, the warrior who saves by His own arm when no man is found.
cards.s_text: For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke.
cards.t_text: He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and true judgment instead of an helmet.

cards.note: *Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her* (Sirach 4:11). The promise *Exalt her, and she shall promote thee: she shall bring thee to honour, when thou dost embrace her* (Proverbs 4:8) is matched in the restored witness: *Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her*. He that exalts her is exalted by her; the embrace is mutual — Wisdom lays hold of those who lay hold of her.
cards.s_text: Exalt her, and she shall promote you: she shall bring you to honour, when you do embrace her.
cards.t_text: Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.

cards.note: *My son, gather instruction from your youth up: so shall you find wisdom till your old age* (Sirach 6:18). The father's *Hear, ye children, the instruction of a father* (Proverbs 4:1) is the same counsel the restored witness gives the son: *gather instruction from your youth up*. The instruction received in youth ripens into the wisdom of age — the lifelong fruit of the handed-down teaching.
cards.s_text: Hear, you children, the instruction of a father, and attend to know understanding.
cards.t_text: My son, gather instruction from your youth up: so shall you find wisdom till your old age.

cards.note: *He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless* (Sirach 4:13). *Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life* (Proverbs 4:13) is the very counsel of the restored witness: *He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory*. To take fast hold of Wisdom and not let her go is to inherit glory and the blessing of Yahuah; she is the holder's life.
cards.s_text: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is your life.
cards.t_text: He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless.

cards.note: *Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you: and when you have got hold of her, let her not go* (Sirach 6:27). The command *let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life* (Proverbs 4:13) is repeated word for word in the restored witness: *when you have got hold of her, let her not go*. Wisdom is sought, found, and held fast — the grip never loosened, for she is the seeker's life.
cards.s_text: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is your life.
cards.t_text: Search, and seek, and she shall be made known to you: and when you have got hold of her, let her not go.

cards.note: *Come to her with your whole heart, and keep her ways with all your power* (Sirach 6:26). To *Take fast hold of instruction* (Proverbs 4:13) is to come to Wisdom *with your whole heart, and keep her ways with all your power*. The fast hold is the whole-hearted keeping; Wisdom is grasped not with half a heart but with all one's power.
cards.s_text: Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is your life.
cards.t_text: Come to her with your whole heart, and keep her ways with all your power.

cards.note: *Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined to us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:6). *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble* (Proverbs 4:19) is the very confession the wicked make too late in the restored witness: *the light of righteousness has not shined to us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us*. They erred from the way of truth and walked in darkness; the light they refused never dawned upon their path.
cards.s_text: The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.
cards.t_text: Therefore have we erred from the way of truth, and the light of righteousness has not shined to us, and the sun of righteousness rose not upon us.

cards.note: *He that winketh with the eyes works evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him* (Sirach 27:22). The body-language of the worthless man — *He winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet, he teacheth with his fingers* (6:13) — is named almost verbatim in the restored witness: *He that winketh with the eyes works evil*. The wink is the secret signal of the deceiver; the wise man, knowing him, departs from him.
cards.s_text: He winketh with his eyes, he speaks with his feet, he teaches with his fingers;
cards.t_text: He that winketh with the eyes works evil: and he that knoweth him will depart from him.

cards.note: *Three sorts of men my soul hates, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth* (Sirach 25:2). The numbered form of *These six things doth Yahuah (LORD) hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him* (6:16) is kept by the restored witness, which counts its own list of the hated — *a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer*. The pride and the lying tongue Yahuah hates (6:17) stand at the head of both lists.
cards.s_text: These six things does Yahuah (LORD) hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:
cards.t_text: Three sorts of men my soul hates, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.

cards.note: *A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins* (Sirach 23:18). The lust warned against — *Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids* (6:25) — is traced to its root in the restored witness: the adulterer's secret reasoning, *Who seeth me? ... the walls cover me*. The heart that lusts hides behind imagined darkness; the proverb and Sirach alike strip the cover away.
cards.s_text: Lust not after her beauty in your heart; neither let her take you with her eyelids.
cards.t_text: A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins:

cards.note: *Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts* (Sirach 23:19). The adulterer who thinks he *shall not be innocent* yet unseen (6:29) is answered: *the eyes of Yahuah are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men*. No wall covers the deed; the secret toucher of the neighbour's wife stands already in the light that the commandment-lamp serves.
cards.s_text: So he that goes in to his neighbour’s wife; whosoever touches her shall not be innocent.
cards.t_text: Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.

cards.note: *Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he has kindled a fire* (Sirach 23:16). The proverb's fire — *Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?* (6:27) — is the very figure the restored witness keeps: *a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he has kindled a fire*. The adulterer carries the coal that consumes him; the burning of 6:27 is the burning of 6:28, *Can one go upon hot coals, and his feet not be burned?*
cards.s_text: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?
cards.t_text: Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicator in the body of his flesh will never cease till he has kindled a fire.

cards.note: *When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?* (Sirach 34:24). The restored witness asks the very question Proverbs 28:9 answers — *whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?* — when the one praying has turned his ear from the law. The unjust offering and the unhearkened Torah make the prayer no prayer Yahuah will hear.
cards.s_text: He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
cards.t_text: When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?

cards.note: *So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?* (Sirach 34:26). The abomination-prayer of Proverbs 28:9 is here the fast of the unrepentant: *a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer?* The ear turned from the law cannot be covered by ritual; the prayer of the one who will not hearken profits him nothing.
cards.s_text: He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
cards.t_text: So is it with a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer? or what does his humbling profit him?

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Sirach 35:1). Where Proverbs 28:9 makes the law-forsaker's prayer an abomination, the restored witness makes the law-keeper's very obedience an offering: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough*. The kept Torah IS the acceptable approach; the turned-away ear is the rejected one.
cards.s_text: He that turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins* (Sirach 3:30). The restored witness binds the giving of *He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack* (Proverbs 28:27) to atonement itself: *alms makes an atonement for sins*. Mercy to the poor is not a small prudence but a weighty thing before Yahuah — as water to fire, so alms to sin.
cards.s_text: He that gives unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hides his eyes shall have many a curse.
cards.t_text: Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1). The hidden eyes of *he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse* (Proverbs 28:27) are here the defrauding that *make[s] the needy eyes to wait long*. The same charge runs through the restored witness: do not turn the eye away from the poor man's need.
cards.s_text: He that gives unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hides his eyes shall have many a curse.
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him* (Sirach 4:6). The *many a curse* upon him that hides his eyes (Proverbs 28:27) is here made fearful: *if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him*. The poor man's cry is heard — the very heard-prayer of THREAD 2 — and the one who shut his hand stands under it.
cards.s_text: He that gives unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hides his eyes shall have many a curse.
cards.t_text: For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). The riddle of who *established all the ends of the earth* (Proverbs 30:4) is answered in the restored witness: the Father *have made all things with your word* — the Word being the Formed Son, the agent of creation, present when the world was made. The Son's name Agur sought is the Word by whom all things were made.
cards.s_text: Who has ascended up into heaven, or descended? who has gathered the wind in his fists? who has bound the waters in a garment? who has established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you can tell?
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,

cards.note: *To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?* (Sirach 18:4). Agur's *if thou canst tell* (Proverbs 30:4) is the same confession of the unsearchable Maker: *To whom has he given power to declare his works?* The works of the One who gathered the wind and established the earth are beyond the creature to declare — the riddle is not answered by man but by the descended-and-ascended Son.
cards.s_text: Who has ascended up into heaven, or descended? who has gathered the wind in his fists? who has bound the waters in a garment? who has established all the ends of the earth? what is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you can tell?
cards.t_text: To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?

cards.note: *As for the wondrous works of Yahuah (God), there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out* (Sirach 18:6). The restored witness keeps both halves of 30:5-6 at once — the unsearchable purity and the prohibition on adding: *there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out*. Nothing may be added, nothing taken; the works and the words of Yahuah are perfect and complete.
cards.s_text: Add you not unto his words, lest he reprove you, and you be found a liar.
cards.t_text: As for the wondrous works of Yahuah (God), there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out.

cards.note: *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double* (Sirach 26:1). The restored witness keeps the eshet chayil of *Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies* (Proverbs 31:10): *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double*. Her worth doubles her husband's days — a treasure above rubies.
cards.s_text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.

cards.note: *A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 26:3). The virtuous woman *far above rubies* (Proverbs 31:10) is, in the restored witness, the portion of the God-fearing: *A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah*. She is given to those who fear Yahuah — binding the eshet chayil to the fear that crowns her in verse 30.
cards.s_text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
cards.t_text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Forego not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold* (Sirach 7:19). The price *far above rubies* (Proverbs 31:10) is matched in the restored witness: *Forego not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold*. Rubies and gold alike fall short of her — let no man let her go.
cards.s_text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
cards.t_text: Forego not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold.

cards.note: *The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing* (Sirach 1:11). The praise of *a woman that feareth Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 31:30) is, in the restored witness, the crown itself: *The fear of Yahuah is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing*. Her fear of Yahuah is her true crown — the glory that does not fade as favour and beauty do.
cards.s_text: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that fears Yahuah (LORD), she shall be praised.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). Tobit's prayer, sung from the captivity of the scattered, sees the very flowing of Isaiah 2:2 — *all nations shall flow unto it*: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands*. The restored witness sees the gathering to Jerusalem the prophet foretold.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD’S house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). What Isaiah promised — death swallowed up, every tear wiped away (Isaiah 25:8) — the restored witness names as *hope full of immortality*. The death that looks like *utter destruction* to the unwise (3:2-3) is, to the righteous, the doorway to the resurrection Isaiah saw.
cards.s_text: He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) has spoken it.
cards.t_text: For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). The restored witness holds the same hope as Isaiah's swallowed death — *He will swallow up death in victory* (Isaiah 25:8): the righteous *are in the hand of Yahuah (God)*, untouched by torment, kept against the day the dead are raised.
cards.s_text: He will swallow up death in victory; and Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for Yahuah (LORD) has spoken it.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares* (Sirach 9:3). The honey-lipped strange woman of *the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb* (Proverbs 5:3) is the harlot the restored witness warns against: *Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares*. The wisdom is one — keep far, for the snare is set in the sweetness.
cards.s_text: For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:
cards.t_text: Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares.

cards.note: *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire* (Sirach 9:8). The smoother-than-oil mouth of Proverbs 5:3 deceives as the restored witness warns: *many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire*. The counsel matches the proverb's — *Remove thy way far from her* (5:8) is *Turn away your eye*.
cards.s_text: For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil:
cards.t_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.

cards.note: *A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins* (Sirach 23:18). The restored witness draws the very self-deceiving thought Proverbs 5:21 refutes — the wedlock-breaker who says *Who seeth me?* — against whom *the ways of man are before the eyes of Yahuah (LORD)* stands as the answer. The darkness he trusts is no cover at all.
cards.s_text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Yahuah (LORD), and he pondereth all his goings.
cards.t_text: A man that breaks wedlock, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darkness, the walls cover me, and no body seeth me; what need I to fear? the Most High will not remember my sins:

cards.note: *Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts* (Sirach 23:19). This is *the ways of man are before the eyes of Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 5:21) made vivid: *the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men*. The eye that beholds all the ways is the eye before which the strange-woman's path is laid bare.
cards.s_text: For the ways of man are before the eyes of Yahuah (LORD), and he pondereth all his goings.
cards.t_text: Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.

cards.note: *Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares* (Sirach 9:3). The restored witness gives the plain counsel the youth of Proverbs 7:7 did not heed: *Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares*. The young man *void of understanding* went the way to her house and fell into the very snare Sirach warns against.
cards.s_text: And beheld among the simple ones, I discerned among the youths, a young man void of understanding,
cards.t_text: Meet not with an harlot, lest you fall into her snares.
