cards.note: *Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent* (Sirach 19:2). The ox-to-slaughter of Proverbs 7:22 is the falling-away Sirach names: *he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent*. Even *men of understanding* are made to fall; how much more the young man void of understanding who goeth after her straightway.
cards.s_text: He goes after her straightway, as an ox goes to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks;
cards.t_text: Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away: and he that cleaveth to harlots will become impudent.

cards.note: *Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall* (Sirach 5:13). The restored witness weighs the wicked mouth of Proverbs 10:11: *the tongue of man is his fall*. The mouth that pours out violence is the man's own undoing — *the froward tongue shall be cut out* (10:31).
cards.s_text: The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
cards.t_text: Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall.

cards.note: *The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17). The violence that *covereth the mouth of the wicked* (Proverbs 10:11) strikes deeper than the lash: *the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones*. The wicked tongue is a weapon; the righteous tongue, by contrast, is *as choice silver* (10:20) and *feed[s] many* (10:21).
cards.s_text: The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
cards.t_text: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.

cards.note: *Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue* (Sirach 28:18). The wicked mouth of Proverbs 10:11 slays more than the sword does: *not so many as have fallen by the tongue*. Against this stands the well-of-life mouth — *The lips of the righteous feed many* (10:21) — the tongue that heals rather than kills.
cards.s_text: The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life: but violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
cards.t_text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.

cards.note: *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life* (Sirach 1:12). The restored witness binds the fear to long life exactly as *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days* (Proverbs 10:27) does: *The fear of Yahuah (God)... gives joy, and gladness, and a long life*. The fear of Yahuah is no old-covenant dread but the spring of a glad and lengthened life.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life.

cards.note: *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life* (Sirach 1:20). The restored witness draws the same tree as *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days* (Proverbs 10:27): *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life*. Fear at the root, long life on the branches — the very harvest the proverb promises.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days: but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
cards.t_text: The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life.

cards.note: *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity* (Sirach 10:7). The restored witness sets pride where Proverbs 11:2 does — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man* — the very thing that brings shame. What is hateful before Yahuah cannot but end in the shame the proverb foretells.
cards.s_text: When pride comes, then comes shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
cards.t_text: Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.

cards.note: *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker* (Sirach 10:12). Sirach traces the pride of Proverbs 11:2 to its root: *the beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker*. The lowly, by contrast, keep near their Maker — and *with the lowly is wisdom*.
cards.s_text: When pride comes, then comes shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
cards.t_text: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.

cards.note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly* (Sirach 10:13). The shame of *When pride cometh, then cometh shame* (Proverbs 11:2) is here drawn to its end — *Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly*. Pride is named *the beginning of sin*, and its wage is the overthrow the proverb warns of.
cards.s_text: When pride comes, then comes shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
cards.t_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

cards.note: *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected* (Sirach 7:32). The restored witness joins the open hand of *The liberal soul shall be made fat* (Proverbs 11:25) to a perfected blessing: *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected*. The scattering that increaseth is the hand stretched out, and the blessing it draws back is made full.
cards.s_text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
cards.t_text: And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.

cards.note: *Give to the Most High according as he has enriched you; and as you have gotten, give with a cheerful eye* (Sirach 35:10). The liberal soul of Proverbs 11:25 gives as the restored witness charges — *with a cheerful eye* — out of what the Most High has given. The withholder who *tendeth to poverty* (11:24) gives grudgingly or not at all; the cheerful giver is the watered waterer.
cards.s_text: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.
cards.t_text: Give to the Most High according as he has enriched you; and as you have gotten, give with a cheerful eye.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). The restored witness keeps the recompense of *the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth* (Proverbs 11:31): *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them*. The recompense of the righteous is safe-keeping in Yahuah's own hand.
cards.s_text: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). The recompense of Proverbs 11:31 is here made everlasting: *the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God)*. The "recompensed in the earth" opens onto a reward kept with the Most High Himself.
cards.s_text: Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner.
cards.t_text: But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High.

cards.note: *Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall* (Sirach 5:13). The restored witness weighs the tongue as Proverbs 12:17 does — *He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit* — for *the tongue of man is his fall*. Honour or shame, righteousness or deceit, hang on what the tongue speaks.
cards.s_text: He that speaks truth shows forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit.
cards.t_text: Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall.

cards.note: *Be not called a whisperer, and lie not in wait with your tongue: for a foul shame is upon the thief, and an evil condemnation upon the double tongue* (Sirach 5:14). The *lying tongue... but for a moment* (Proverbs 12:19) earns the restored witness's *evil condemnation upon the double tongue*. The deceitful, double tongue carries a foul shame; only the single, truthful lip is established for ever.
cards.s_text: The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment.
cards.t_text: Be not called a whisperer, and lie not in wait with your tongue: for a foul shame is upon the thief, and an evil condemnation upon the double tongue.

cards.note: *The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17). *There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health* (Proverbs 12:18) — and the restored witness names the wounding tongue: *the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones*. The piercing tongue does deeper harm than the whip; the wise tongue, by contrast, is health.
cards.s_text: There is that speaks like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.
cards.t_text: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.

cards.note: *Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace* (Sirach 28:13). The lying lips that are *abomination to Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 12:22) are the restored witness's *whisperer and doubletongued* — cursed because *such have destroyed many that were at peace*. The deceitful tongue is no light matter; it is an abomination that wrecks the peace of many.
cards.s_text: Lying lips are abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but they that deal truly are his delight.
cards.t_text: Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace.

cards.note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Sirach 11:19). *if riches increase, set not your heart upon them* (Psalm 62:10): the restored wisdom paints the very man — he rests in his goods, not knowing he must leave them all to others and die. The heart set on riches is set on what cannot be kept.
cards.s_text: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: *As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judges a man according to his works* (Sirach 16:12). *Also unto thee, O Yahuah (Lord), belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work* (Psalm 62:12): the restored wisdom binds the same two — mercy AND correction both great, for He judges a man according to his works. The psalm's mercy-and-recompense couplet is the wisdom's mercy-and-correction.
cards.s_text: Also unto you, O Adonai (Lord), belongs mercy: for you renderest to every man according to his work.
cards.t_text: As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he judges a man according to his works

cards.note: *Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works* (Sirach 16:14). *for thou renderest to every man according to his work* (Psalm 62:12): the restored wisdom seals the measure — every man shall find according to his works. What the psalm says Yahuah renders, the wisdom says every man shall find: the same Torah-consistent recompense.
cards.s_text: Also unto you, O Adonai (Lord), belongs mercy: for you renderest to every man according to his work.
cards.t_text: Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.

cards.note: *They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty* (Sirach 24:21). *My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is* (Psalm 63:1): the restored wisdom marks the contrast — even her own water leaves men thirsty still; the soul's thirst is finally filled not by Wisdom's draught but by the living Elohim Himself.
cards.s_text: O Elohim (God), you are my Elohim (God); early will I seek you: my soul thirsteth for you, my flesh longeth for you in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is;
cards.t_text: They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty.

cards.note: *The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17). *Who whet their tongue like a sword... even bitter words* (Psalm 64:3): the restored wisdom weighs the wound — the tongue strikes deeper than the whip, breaking the very bones. The bitter word is the sword that cuts beyond the flesh.
cards.s_text: Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words:
cards.t_text: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.

cards.note: *Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue* (Sirach 28:18). *Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words* (Psalm 64:3): the wisdom of old names the tongue the deadlier blade — more have fallen by it than by the sword. The psalm whets it like a sword because it kills like one.
cards.s_text: Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words:
cards.t_text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). *Unto thee shall all flesh come* (Psalm 65:2): the restored Tobit sings the same ingathering — many nations come from far to the Name, bearing gifts to the King of heaven. The all-flesh-come is the nations streaming to Zion to praise Yahuah with joy.
cards.s_text: O you that hear prayer, unto you shall all flesh come.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *By his commandment he makes the snow to fall aplace, and sends swiftly the lightnings of his judgment. Through this the treasures are opened: and clouds fly forth as fowls* (Sirach 43:13-14). *Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; and thy paths drop fatness* (Psalm 65:11): the restored wisdom watches the same hand over the seasons — by His commandment the snow falls and the treasures of the sky are opened. The crowned year, the dropping fatness, is Yahuah's ordering of cloud and season unto the harvest.
cards.s_text: You crownest the year with your goodness; and your paths drop fatness.
cards.t_text: By his commandment he makes the snow to fall aplace, and sends swiftly the lightnings of his judgment.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). *thou hast tried us, as silver is tried* (Psalm 66:10): the restored wisdom gives the same assay — as gold is tried in the fire, so acceptable men are proved in the furnace of adversity. The trial of the psalm is the furnace that makes men acceptable.
cards.s_text: For you, O Elohim (God), have proved us: you have tried us, as silver is tried.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself* (Wisdom 3:5). *For thou, O Elohim (God), hast proved us... but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place* (Psalm 66:10,12): the wisdom of Solomon names the proving — Yahuah proved them and found them worthy for Himself, the little chastening unto great reward. The proving of the psalm ends in the worthy ones brought out and rewarded.
cards.s_text: You have caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but you brought us out into a wealthy place.
cards.t_text: And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.

cards.note: *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering* (Wisdom 3:6). *we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place* (Psalm 66:12): the wisdom binds the fire to the offering — tried as gold in the furnace, received as a burnt offering. The fire of the psalm refines the people into an offering received, and joins the next breath of the psalm: *I will go into thy house with burnt offerings* (66:13).
cards.s_text: You have caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but you brought us out into a wealthy place.
cards.t_text: As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.

cards.note: *And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life* (2 Maccabees 7:9). The hope of *Thy dead men shall live* (Isaiah 26:19) steadies the martyred brother before the tyrant — *the King of the world shall raise us up... to everlasting life*. The resurrection of the dust is the answer of faith to death itself: he who keeps the laws is raised.
cards.s_text: Your dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, you that dwell in dust: for your dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.
cards.t_text: And when he was at the last gasp, he said, You like a fury takest us out of this present life, but the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life.

cards.note: *He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end* (Sirach 30:1). The restored witness states *He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes* (Proverbs 13:24) almost word for word: *He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod*. Love and the rod are bound together — the end is joy in the son, not harm.
cards.s_text: He that spareth his rod hates his son: but he that loves him chastens him betimes.
cards.t_text: He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end.

cards.note: *He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance* (Sirach 30:2). The fruit of the loved-and-chastened son of *he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes* (Proverbs 13:24) is here named: *He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him*. The discipline aimed at the son's good returns to the father as joy.
cards.s_text: He that spareth his rod hates his son: but he that loves him chastens him betimes.
cards.t_text: He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.

cards.note: *There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward* (Sirach 11:18). The self-made rich of *There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing* (Proverbs 13:7) is the man of Sirach who *waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching* — and the very next verse shows what his hoard comes to.
cards.s_text: There is that makes himself rich, yet has nothing: there is that makes himself poor, yet has great riches.
cards.t_text: There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:

cards.note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Sirach 11:19). This is *maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing* (Proverbs 13:7) drawn out to its end: the man boasts *I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods*, but *he must leave those things to others, and die*. The same picture Yahusha (Jesus) paints in the rich fool — full barns, an empty soul.
cards.s_text: There is that makes himself rich, yet has nothing: there is that makes himself poor, yet has great riches.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb* (Sirach 1:14). The restored witness sings the very confidence of Proverbs 14:26: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom*. The fear that gives strong confidence and a place of refuge is no late acquisition — *it was created with the faithful in the womb*.
cards.s_text: In the fear of Yahuah (LORD) is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life* (Sirach 1:20). The fountain of life of Proverbs 14:27 is here a tree: *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life*. The fear of Yahuah roots the wisdom whose very branches are the long life the fountain gives.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death.
cards.t_text: The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life.

cards.note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted* (Sirach 34:18). The restored witness states *The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD)* (15:8) outright: the offering of a thing wrongfully gotten *is ridiculous*, and *the gifts of unjust men are not accepted*. It is not the gift but the unjust hand that voids it.
cards.s_text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
cards.t_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.

cards.note: *The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices* (Sirach 34:19). The plain echo of *The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination* (15:8): *The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked*. Multiplied sacrifices cannot pacify for sin where the heart is wicked — the same verdict Isaiah and Amos pronounce.
cards.s_text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
cards.t_text: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Sirach 35:1). Where *the prayer of the upright is his delight* (15:8), the restored witness makes the kept Torah itself the acceptable approach: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough*. The upright's obedience IS the offering Yahuah delights in; the wicked's ritual without it is abomination.
cards.s_text: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?* (Sirach 34:24). The restored witness asks the question *Yahuah (LORD) is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous* (15:29) answers — *whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?* — and the answer is the righteous, not the wicked whose offering is built on wrong.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) is far from the wicked: but he hears the prayer of the righteous.
cards.t_text: When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb* (Sirach 1:14). The restored witness echoes *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the instruction of wisdom* (15:33): *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom*. The same motto that opens Proverbs runs through the restored wisdom-witness — the fear of Yahuah is wisdom's beginning and its teacher.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life* (Sirach 1:12). The restored witness names the root of *A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance* (15:13): *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy*. The cheerful countenance springs not from circumstance but from the fear of Yahuah — binding the merry heart back to the fear-motto of the chapter's close.
cards.s_text: A merry heart makes a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life.

cards.note: *As the clay is in the potter's hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best* (Sirach 33:13). The restored witness frames *Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps* (16:9) with the potter: *so man is in the hand of him that made him*. The clay does not direct its own shaping; the man does not direct his own steps — both rest in the hand of the One who made them.
cards.s_text: A man’s heart deviseth his way: but Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps.
cards.t_text: As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him, to render to them as liketh him best.

cards.note: *And above all this pray to the Most High, that he will direct your way in truth* (Sirach 37:15). Where *The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from Yahuah (LORD)* (16:1), the only wise response is to ask Him for it: *pray to the Most High, that he will direct your way in truth*. The heart cannot prepare itself; it must be prepared by the One from whom the answer comes.
cards.s_text: The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: And above all this pray to the Most High, that he will direct your way in truth.

cards.note: *Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins* (Sirach 3:30). The restored witness sets mercy beside the iniquity-purging of 16:6: *alms makes an atonement for sins*. As water to fire, so mercy to sin — the deed of mercy is no small thing but, with truth, a purging before Yahuah.
cards.s_text: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of Yahuah (LORD) men depart from evil.
cards.t_text: Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.

cards.note: *To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation* (Sirach 35:3). The second half of 16:6 — *by the fear of Yahuah (LORD) men depart from evil* — is here named a propitiation: *to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation*. The fear of Yahuah that turns a man from evil is itself part of the purging the proverb describes.
cards.s_text: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of Yahuah (LORD) men depart from evil.
cards.t_text: To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.

cards.note: *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity* (Sirach 10:7). The restored witness says of pride exactly what 16:5 says — *Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD)* — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man*. What Yahuah abhors in the proud heart, the witness names hateful to heaven and earth both.
cards.s_text: Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
cards.t_text: Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man: and by both does one commit iniquity.

cards.note: *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker* (Sirach 10:12). Before the destruction of 16:18 comes the pride; and before the pride, the witness says, comes the departing: *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God)*. The haughty spirit is first a turned-away heart, and the fall follows the turning.
cards.s_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
cards.t_text: The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker.

cards.note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly* (Sirach 10:13). The destruction that pride goes before (16:18) is spelled out: *pride is the beginning of sin... and therefore Yahuah (God)... overthrew them utterly*. The proud are not merely shamed but overthrown — the proverb's "destruction" made plain.
cards.s_text: Pride goes before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.
cards.t_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). The restored witness binds the figure of 17:3 tight: *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity*. The fining pot and the furnace of the proverb are the trials Yahuah brings on His own to prove and refine them acceptable.
cards.s_text: The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but Yahuah (LORD) trieth the hearts.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1). The restored witness charges the same care 17:5 commands: *defraud not the poor of his living*. To mock or defraud the poor is to wrong the One who made him; the needy eyes are not to be turned away.
cards.s_text: Whoso mocks the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished.
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure* (Sirach 6:14). The restored witness echoes 17:17: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence... a treasure*. The friend who loves at all times is no small thing but a defence and a treasure found.
cards.s_text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
cards.t_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.

cards.note: *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him* (Sirach 6:16). The brother born for adversity in 17:17 is here *the medicine of life* — and found by *they that fear Yahuah (God)*. The faithful friend who fears Yahuah is the one whose love holds when adversity comes.
cards.s_text: A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
cards.t_text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.

cards.note: *There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful* (Sirach 20:5). The restored witness states the chapter's close — *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise* (17:28) — outright: *one that keepeth silence, and is found wise*. The kept silence is counted wisdom; the babbling tongue becomes hateful.
cards.s_text: A merry heart does good like a medicine: but a broken spirit dries the bones.
cards.t_text: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). *O let the nations be glad and sing for joy* (Psalm 67:4): the restored Tobit sings the same ingathering — many nations coming from far to the Name of Yahuah, all generations praising with joy. The nations are drawn TO the Name, to Jerusalem restored, with His people.
cards.s_text: O let the nations be glad and sing for joy: for you shall judge the people righteously, and govern the nations upon earth. Selah.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (Tobit 13:5). *all the ends of the earth shall fear him* (Psalm 67:7): the restored Tobit names the two-house ingathering — Yahuah gathering His scattered people out of all the nations, His mercy after the chastening. As the dispersed are gathered home, the ends of the earth come to fear Him.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) shall bless us; and all the ends of the earth shall fear him.
cards.t_text: And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Sirach 2:10). *Let me never be put to confusion* (Psalm 71:1): the restored wisdom tests the plea against all the ages and finds none who trusted Yahuah were ever confounded — the aged servant's prayer is answered before it is prayed.
cards.s_text: In you, O Yahuah (LORD), do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of Yahuah (God) is their glory* (Sirach 25:6). *Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O Elohim (God), forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation* (Psalm 71:18): the restored wisdom crowns the very man the psalm pictures — the grayhead whose glory is the fear of Yahuah, whose long experience is given to teach the generation to come.
cards.s_text: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O Elohim (God), forsake me not; until I have shewed your strength unto this generation, and your power to every one that is to come.
cards.t_text: Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of Yahuah (God) is their glory.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom 3:1). *Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end* (Psalm 73:17): the restored wisdom shows the very end Asaph beheld — the righteous, who *seemed to die* (3:2) in the sight of the unwise, are in fact held safe in the hand of Yahuah, *and in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (3:7). The end the sanctuary reveals is not the prosperity of the wicked but the immortal hope of the righteous.
cards.s_text: Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *But the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken Yahuah (God)* (Wisdom 3:10). *Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end* (Psalm 73:17): set against the souls of the righteous held safe (3:1), the wisdom names the other end — the ungodly punished according to their own imaginations. The two ends seen together in the sanctuary: the righteous shining, the ungodly undone.
cards.s_text: Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end.
cards.t_text: But the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm... and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day* (Wisdom 5:14). *As a dream when one awaketh; so, O Yahuah (Lord), when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image* (Psalm 73:20): the wisdom names the ungodly's end in the same vanishing terms — dust on the wind, froth in the storm, the dream that dissolves on waking. The image of the prospering wicked is a thing that does not survive the dawn.
cards.s_text: As a dream when one awakes; so, O Adonai (Lord), when you awakest, you shall despise their image.
cards.t_text: For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.

cards.note: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a post that hasted by* (Wisdom 5:8-9). *Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction* (Psalm 73:18): the restored wisdom puts the confession in the mouth of the fallen — pride profited nothing, riches passed like a shadow. *Pride compasseth them about as a chain* (73:6) until the slippery place gives way, and then it is all a shadow hasting by.
cards.s_text: Surely you did set them in slippery places: you castedst them down into destruction.
cards.t_text: What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?

cards.note: *And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5). *I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction* (Isaiah 48:10) is the chastening that proves — *having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded* — the affliction by which Yahuah *proved them, and found them worthy for himself*. The restored witness names the furnace the assaying of the worthy.
cards.s_text: Behold, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
cards.t_text: And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.

cards.note: *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6). The *furnace of affliction* (Isaiah 48:10) is the very figure — *As gold in the furnace has he tried them* — and the tried ones are *received... as a burnt offering*, given back to Yahuah purified. The fire is acceptance, not rejection.
cards.s_text: Behold, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
cards.t_text: As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). The wisdom-witness restates Isaiah 48:10 as a proverb: *I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction* becomes *acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* — as *gold is tried in the fire*, so the chosen are proved by affliction and found acceptable. The furnace makes the man fit, it does not unmake him.
cards.s_text: Behold, I have refined you, but not with silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17). The restored witness weighs the death-power of Proverbs 18:21 against the whip: *the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones*. Worse than the lash on the flesh is the wound the tongue deals — death is truly in its power.
cards.s_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
cards.t_text: The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.

cards.note: *Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue* (Sirach 28:18). The tongue's death-power of Proverbs 18:21 is measured against the sword: *not so many as have fallen by the tongue*. More are slain by words than by steel — *Death... [is] in the power of the tongue*.
cards.s_text: Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.
cards.t_text: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue.

cards.note: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure* (Sirach 6:14). The restored witness echoes the friend that sticks closer than a brother (Proverbs 18:24): *A faithful friend is a strong defence... has found a treasure*. The true friend is no small thing but a fortress and a treasure found.
cards.s_text: A man that has friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
cards.t_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.

cards.note: *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him* (Sirach 6:16). The friend closer than a brother of Proverbs 18:24 is here *the medicine of life* — and given to *they that fear Yahuah (God)*. The faithful friend is a gift bound to the fear of Yahuah, healing as a balm.
cards.s_text: A man that has friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
cards.t_text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.

cards.note: *Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure* (Sirach 9:10). The friend that sticks closer than a brother (Proverbs 18:24) is the tried, old friend the restored witness will not let go: *Forsake not an old friend*. The friendship that has aged like wine is the one that sticks closest.
cards.s_text: A man that has friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.
cards.t_text: Forsake not an old friend; for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.

cards.note: *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double* (Sirach 26:1). The restored witness echoes *Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing* (Proverbs 18:22): *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife*. The good wife is a blessing that lengthens a man's very days.
cards.s_text: Whoso finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favour of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.

cards.note: *A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 26:3). The favour-of-Yahuah of Proverbs 18:22 is named here a portion *given... [to] them that fear Yahuah (God)*: *A good wife is a good portion*. The wife is a gift apportioned by Yahuah to those who fear Him.
cards.s_text: Whoso finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favour of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *He that getteth a wife begins a possession, a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest* (Sirach 36:24). The good thing of Proverbs 18:22 is here *a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest* — the very help meet of the garden (Genesis 2:18). The wife is a beginning of good, a help and a rest given of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Whoso finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains favour of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: He that getteth a wife begins a possession, a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest.

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1). The pity of *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 19:17) is the restored witness's charge too: *defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long*. To withhold from the poor is to default on a loan owed to Yahuah.
cards.s_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *Let it not grieve you to bow down your ear to the poor, and give him a friendly answer with meekness* (Sirach 4:8). The pity of *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 19:17) is more than coin — *bow down your ear to the poor, and give him a friendly answer with meekness*. The bowed ear and the open hand together make the loan to Yahuah.
cards.s_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.
cards.t_text: Let it not grieve you to bow down your ear to the poor, and give him a friendly answer with meekness.

cards.note: *Help the poor for the commandment's sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty* (Sirach 29:9). The restored witness grounds the pity of *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 19:17) in the Torah itself: *Help the poor for the commandment's sake*. The loan to Yahuah is commanded, not optional; it is the open hand of Deuteronomy 15.
cards.s_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.
cards.t_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.

cards.note: *Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction* (Sirach 29:12). The repayment of *that which he hath given will he pay him again* (Proverbs 19:17) is the restored witness's treasure: *Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction*. Alms given to the poor are laid up with Yahuah, who returns them as deliverance.
cards.s_text: He that has pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he has given will he pay him again.
cards.t_text: Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.

cards.note: *Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good* (Sirach 7:13). The restored witness keeps the charge behind *he that speaketh lies shall not escape* (Proverbs 19:5): *Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good*. The habit of lying is named no small thing — it leads where the proverb says, to not escaping.
cards.s_text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaks lies shall not escape.
cards.t_text: Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.

cards.note: *A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage* (Sirach 20:25). The perishing of *he that speaketh lies shall perish* (Proverbs 19:9) is the restored witness's verdict too: *they both shall have destruction to heritage*. The settled liar is worse than a thief, and both inherit the same ruin.
cards.s_text: A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaks lies shall perish.
cards.t_text: A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.

cards.note: *The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing* (Sirach 1:11). The restored witness sings the satisfied life of *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life... he shall abide satisfied* (Proverbs 19:23): *The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing*. The fear of Yahuah is no dread but a crown.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life: and he that has it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing.

cards.note: *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life* (Sirach 1:12). The tending-to-life of *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life* (Proverbs 19:23) is the restored witness's long life: *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life*. The same fear that satisfies also gladdens and lengthens days.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life: and he that has it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
cards.t_text: The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life.

cards.note: *Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope* (Sirach 34:14). The *he shall not be visited with evil* of Proverbs 19:23 is the restored witness's fearlessness: *Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope*. The fear of Yahuah casts out every other fear, and evil cannot touch the one whose hope is in Him.
cards.s_text: The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life: and he that has it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil.
cards.t_text: Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope.

cards.note: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). The restored witness binds wisdom to the kept commandment, as does *He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul* (Proverbs 19:16): *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments*. The way to wisdom and the keeping of the soul are one and the same — the kept Torah.
cards.s_text: He that keeps the commandment keeps his own soul; but he that despises his ways shall die.
cards.t_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.

cards.note: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance* (Sirach 28:1). The restored witness states the danger Proverbs 20:22 warns against: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God)*. To recompense evil is to invite the very recompense you sought to deal — better to wait on Yahuah, who saves.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will recompense evil; but wait on Yahuah (LORD), and he shall save you.
cards.t_text: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.

cards.note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest* (Sirach 28:2). The waiting of *wait on Yahuah (LORD), and he shall save thee* (Proverbs 20:22) is here forgiveness tied to your own pardon: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt... so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest*. The one who releases vengeance is the one whose own prayer is heard.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will recompense evil; but wait on Yahuah (LORD), and he shall save you.
cards.t_text: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.

cards.note: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance* (Sirach 28:7). The restored witness binds non-vengeance straight to the Torah: *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest*. To say not *I will recompense evil* (Proverbs 20:22) is to remember the commandments and the covenant.
cards.s_text: Say not you, I will recompense evil; but wait on Yahuah (LORD), and he shall save you.
cards.t_text: Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest, and wink at ignorance.

cards.note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted* (Sirach 34:18). The restored witness draws out *To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah (LORD) than sacrifice* (Proverbs 21:3): the offering brought without justice — *of a thing wrongfully gotten* — is *ridiculous*. The sacrifice itself is not condemned; the unjust man's sacrifice is.
cards.s_text: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah (LORD) than sacrifice.
cards.t_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.

cards.note: *The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices* (Sirach 34:19). Here is the dark side of Proverbs 21:3 in the restored witness — *the most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked* — exactly as the proverb sets justice above the wicked's sacrifice (21:27). Multiplied sacrifice cannot pacify where justice is refused; the doing of justice is the more acceptable thing.
cards.s_text: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah (LORD) than sacrifice.
cards.t_text: The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; neither is he pacified for sin by the multitude of sacrifices.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Sirach 35:1). The restored witness states the positive of Proverbs 21:3 plainest of all: the kept Torah IS the acceptable approach — *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough*. Obedience and offering are not rivals but one; the justice the law commands makes the offering acceptable, never abolishes it.
cards.s_text: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah (LORD) than sacrifice.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1). The restored witness names the stopped ear of Proverbs 21:13 as the defrauding that *make[s] the needy eyes to wait long*. To turn from the poor man's cry is to defraud him of his very living; the charge runs the same through the whole library.
cards.s_text: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him* (Sirach 4:6). Here is the exact reversal of Proverbs 21:13: the stopper *shall cry himself, but shall not be heard*, while the poor man he turned from — *if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him*. The cry stopped on earth is heard in heaven, and against the one who stopped it.
cards.s_text: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard.
cards.t_text: For if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.

cards.note: *Have regard to your name; for that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold* (Sirach 41:12). The restored witness makes the choice of 22:1 plain: the name *shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold*. Great riches are the very thing the name is to be chosen rather than — for the gold passes and the name remains.
cards.s_text: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
cards.t_text: Have regard to your name; for that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold.

cards.note: *A good life has but few days: but a good name endureth for ever* (Sirach 41:13). Here is the reason a good name is *rather to be chosen than great riches* (22:1): *a good name endureth for ever*. The body's days are few and the riches fewer; the good name alone abides past death.
cards.s_text: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
cards.t_text: A good life has but few days: but a good name endureth for ever.

cards.note: *Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 11:14). The restored witness states the ground of 22:2: *poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God)*. The rich and poor meet because the same Yahuah apportioned both estates; He is the maker of them all, and the giver of all they have.
cards.s_text: The rich and poor meet together: Yahuah (LORD) is the maker of them all.
cards.t_text: Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end* (Sirach 30:1). The restored witness binds love to the rod of training (22:6, 22:15): *He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end*. The discipline is for the end — the grown child who has not departed from the way.
cards.s_text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
cards.t_text: He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end.

cards.note: *He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance* (Sirach 30:2). The fruit of training the child in 22:6 is here named: *He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him*. The father who disciplines his son into the way reaps joy when the son, grown, keeps it.
cards.s_text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
cards.t_text: He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him, and shall rejoice of him among his acquaintance.

cards.note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1). The restored witness echoes *Rob not the poor, because he is poor* (22:22): *defraud not the poor of his living*. To rob the poor is to take the very living of the one who has least — and Yahuah pleads his cause.
cards.s_text: Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
cards.t_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.

cards.note: *The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood* (Sirach 34:21). The weight of robbing the poor (22:22) is here made plain: *The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood*. To rob the poor man's bread is to take his life — and Yahuah, who pleads his cause, will spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.
cards.s_text: Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
cards.t_text: The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.

cards.note: *And when they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned up, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest... they rent their clothes, and made great lamentation* (1 Maccabees 4:38-39). *They have burned up all the synagogues of Elohim (God) in the land* (Psalm 74:8) and *They have cast fire into thy sanctuary* (74:7): the restored history shows the lament realized — the gates burned up, the courts grown wild, the same great lamentation Asaph sings over the fire-stricken house.
cards.s_text: They said in their hearts, Let us destroy them together: they have burned up all the synagogues of Elohim (God) in the land.
cards.t_text: And when they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned up, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest, or in one of the mountains, yes, and the priests’ chambers pulled down;

cards.note: *And made up the sanctuary, and the things that were within the temple, and hallowed the courts* (1 Maccabees 4:48). *Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual desolations; even all that the enemy hath done wickedly in the sanctuary* (Psalm 74:3): the desolations Asaph lifts before Yahuah are answered in the Maccabean rededication — the sanctuary made up, the courts hallowed again. The lament over the ruined house holds the hope of the house restored.
cards.s_text: Lift up your feet unto the perpetual desolations; even all that the enemy has done wickedly in the sanctuary.
cards.t_text: And made up the sanctuary, and the things that were within the temple, and hallowed the courts.

cards.note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead* (Sirach 10:14). *He putteth down one, and setteth up another* (Psalm 75:7): the restored wisdom sings the abase-and-exalt outright — the thrones of the proud cast down, the meek set up in their place. The reversal of the psalm is the settled way of the Judge.
cards.s_text: But Elohim (God) is the judge: he puts down one, and sets up another.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.

cards.note: *Brought them through the Red sea, and led them through much water* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:18). *The waters saw thee, O Elohim (God), the waters saw thee; they were afraid: the depths also were troubled* (Psalm 77:16): the restored wisdom sings the same crossing the psalm rehearses — the people brought through the Red sea, led through much water; the deep that was troubled became the path of redemption.
cards.s_text: The waters saw you, O Elohim (God), the waters saw you; they were afraid: the depths also were troubled.
cards.t_text: Brought them through the Red sea, and led them through much water:

cards.note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels' food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). *Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full* (Psalm 78:25): the restored wisdom sings the very phrase — the people fed with angels' food, bread sent from heaven without their labour; the same manna the psalm names, the heavenly bread that contents every taste.
cards.s_text: Man did eat angels’ food: he sent them meat to the full.
cards.t_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.

cards.note: *And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine* (2 Esdras 5:23). The *vineyard in a very fruitful hill* of *my wellbeloved* (Isaiah 5:1) is the one chosen vine of all the trees of the earth — the restored witness names the election the vineyard-song assumes.
cards.s_text: Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved has a vineyard in a very fruitful hill:
cards.t_text: And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:

cards.note: *And now, O Yahuah (God), why have you given this one people over to many? and upon the one root have you prepared others, and why have you scattered your only one people among many?* (2 Esdras 5:28). The vineyard that is *the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 5:7) is the *one people* of the one root — Ezra's cry mourns the scattering the lawsuit's judgment brings, the two-house dispersion that awaits the gathering.
cards.s_text: For the vineyard of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the men of Yahudah (Judah) his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.
cards.t_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), why have you given this one people over to many? and upon the one root have you prepared others, and why have you scattered your only one people among many?

cards.note: *Shew not your valiantness in wine; for wine has destroyed many* (Ecclesiasticus 31:25). The *Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!* (Isaiah 5:11) is met by the restored wisdom-witness: wine pursued as valour *has destroyed many*.
cards.s_text: Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them!
cards.t_text: Shew not your valiantness in wine; for wine has destroyed many.

cards.note: *The furnace proves the edge by dipping: so does wine the hearts of the proud by drunkeness* (Ecclesiasticus 31:26). The *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink* (Isaiah 5:22) is the very proving of *the hearts of the proud by drunkeness* — strength boasted in the cup is strength laid bare.
cards.s_text: Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:
cards.t_text: The furnace proves the edge by dipping: so does wine the hearts of the proud by drunkeness.

cards.note: *And when he had taken the spoils of the city, he set it on fire, and pulled down the houses and walls thereof on every side* (1 Maccabees 1:31). *O Elohim (God), the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps* (Psalm 79:1): the restored history gives the scene the psalm mourns — the heathen taking the spoils, burning the city, pulling its houses and walls down on every side; Jerusalem laid on heaps by the hand of the stranger.
cards.s_text: O Elohim (God), the heathen are come into your inheritance; your holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.
cards.t_text: And when he had taken the spoils of the city, he set it on fire, and pulled down the houses and walls thereof on every side.

cards.note: *The flesh of your saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them* (1 Maccabees 7:17). *Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury them* (Psalm 79:3): the restored history quotes this psalm BY NAME — the flesh of the saints cast out, the blood shed round about Jerusalem, none to bury them; the very words of Asaph become the epitaph of the pious slain by Bacchides.
cards.s_text: Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury them.
cards.t_text: The flesh of your saints have they cast out, and their blood have they shed round about Jerusalem, and there was none to bury them.

cards.note: *But all was deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and struck it very sore, and destroyed much people of Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Maccabees 1:30). *The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth* (Psalm 79:2): the slaughter the psalm laments — much people of Yashar'el destroyed by deceit, the bodies of the servants of Yahuah left as meat for the fowls and the beasts; the history and the lament name one carnage.
cards.s_text: The dead bodies of your servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the heaven, the flesh of your saints unto the beasts of the earth.
cards.t_text: And spoke peaceable words to them, but all was deceit: for when they had given him credence, he fell suddenly upon the city, and struck it very sore, and destroyed much people of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: ★ *From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection* (Sirach 43:7) — the new moon of 81:3 set as the sign of the appointed feasts; the moon Yahuah made to mark His solemn days.
cards.s_text: Blow the trumpet at the dark new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.
cards.t_text: From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.

cards.note: *Then shouted the sons of Aaron, and sounded the silver trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the Most High* (Sirach 50:16) — the trumpet-blowing of 81:3 sounded by the priests for a remembrance: the feast-day blast before Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Blow the trumpet at the dark new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.
cards.t_text: Then shouted the sons of Aaron, and sounded the silver trumpets, and made a great noise to be heard, for a remembrance before the Most High.

cards.note: *For power is given you of Yahuah (God), and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:3). *Elohim (God) standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods* (Psalm 82:1): the restored wisdom names exactly what the psalm means — the rulers' power is GIVEN of Yahuah and from El Elyon (the Highest); the authority is borrowed, and the Most High will try the works of those He set in high places.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) stands in the congregation of the mighty; he judges among the gods.
cards.t_text: For power is given you of Yahuah (God), and sovereignty from the Highest, who shall try your works, and search out your counsels.

cards.note: *Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God)* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:4). *How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?* (Psalm 82:2): the same charge against the same office — ministers of His kingdom who have not judged aright nor kept the law; the unjust judgment of the psalm is the failure to keep the Torah's charge, and judgment will fall on them for it.
cards.s_text: How long will you judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked? Selah.
cards.t_text: Because, being ministers of his kingdom, you have not judged aright, nor kept the law, nor walked after the counsel of Yahuah (God);

cards.note: *Now when the nations round about heard that the altar was built and the sanctuary renewed as before, it displeased them very much* (1 Maccabees 5:1). *For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against thee* (Psalm 83:5): the restored history shows the same ring — the nations round about, displeased at the renewed sanctuary, consulting with one consent against the people of the covenant.
cards.s_text: For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against you:
cards.t_text: Now when the nations round about heard that the altar was built and the sanctuary renewed as before, it displeased them very much.

cards.note: *Wherefore they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that was among them, and thereupon they began to slay and destroy the people* (1 Maccabees 5:2). *Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation* (Psalm 83:4): the very plot the psalm names — to destroy the generation of Jacob, to cut off the people from being a nation; the confederacy's aim is always the erasing of the seed.
cards.s_text: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Yashar'el (Israel) may be no more in remembrance.
cards.t_text: Wherefore they thought to destroy the generation of Jacob that was among them, and thereupon they began to slay and destroy the people.

cards.note: *And let them know you, as we have known you, that there is no Yahuah (God) but only you, O Yahuah (God)* (Ecclesiasticus 36:5). *Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek thy name, O Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 83:16): the restored wisdom prays the same redemptive aim — that the nations know Yahuah as the covenant people have known Him, that there is no Elohim but only He; the seeking of the Name is the nations brought to the knowledge.
cards.s_text: Fill their faces with shame; that they may seek your name, O Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: And let them know you, as we have known you, that there is no Yahuah (God) but only you, O Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *That men may know that thou, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, art the most high over all the earth* (Psalm 83:18): the same prayer joins the knowing of the Name to the gathering of the tribes — the two houses gathered as from the beginning, the confederacy's plot to scatter and erase overturned in the ingathering of Jacob.
cards.s_text: That men may know that you, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, are the most high over all the earth.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God), hear the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all they which dwell upon the earth may know that you are Yahuah (God), the eternal Yahuah (God)* (Ecclesiasticus 36:17). *That men may know that thou, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, art the most high over all the earth* (Psalm 83:18): the prayer ends exactly where the psalm ends — that all who dwell upon the earth may know that He is Yahuah, the eternal One; the imprecation's crown is the whole earth's knowledge of the Name.
cards.s_text: That men may know that you, whose name alone is JEHOVAH, are the most high over all the earth.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God), hear the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron over your people, that all they which dwell upon the earth may know that you are Yahuah (God), the eternal Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Give praise to Yahuah (God), for he is good: and praise the everlasting King, that his tabernacle may be builded in you again with joy, and let him make joyful there in you those that are captives* (Tobit 13:10). *How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)!* (Psalm 84:1): the restored witness sings the same longing — the tabernacle of Yahuah builded again with joy, the captives made joyful in His dwelling; the ache for the amiable tabernacles is the ache for the house restored.
cards.s_text: How amiable are your tabernacles, O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)!
cards.t_text: Give praise to Yahuah (God), for he is good: and praise the everlasting King, that his tabernacle may be builded in you again with joy, and let him make joyful there in you those that are captives, and love in you for ever those that are miserable.

cards.note: *Shew not your valiantness in wine; for wine has destroyed many* (Sirach 31:25). The restored witness sets the same warning beside *Look not thou upon the wine when it is red... At the last it biteth like a serpent* (Proverbs 23:31-32): *wine has destroyed many*. The boast of strength at the cup — the valiantness in wine — is the very thing the proverb says bites like a serpent at the last.
cards.s_text: Look not you upon the wine when it is red, when it gives his colour in the cup, when it moves itself aright.
cards.t_text: Shew not your valiantness in wine; for wine has destroyed many.

cards.note: *Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminisheth strength, and makes wounds* (Sirach 31:30). The serpent-bite of *At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder* (Proverbs 23:32) is here named plain: drunkenness *makes wounds* — the very *wounds without cause* the proverb asks after (23:29). The restored witness measures the cup exactly as Proverbs does: gladness if drunk in season (31:27-28), but rage and wounds in excess.
cards.s_text: At the last it bites like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
cards.t_text: Drunkenness increaseth the rage of a fool till he offend: it diminisheth strength, and makes wounds.

cards.note: *If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it* (Sirach 31:12). The counsel *When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee* (Proverbs 23:1) finds its closest echo in the restored witness: *If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it*. The bountiful table of the great man calls not for appetite but for diligent restraint — the same wisdom in both books.
cards.s_text: When you sit to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before you:
cards.t_text: If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it.

cards.note: *Eat as it becometh a man, those things which are set before you; and devour not, lest you be hated* (Sirach 31:16). The knife at the throat of *put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite* (Proverbs 23:2) is this same bridle on the greedy eater: *devour not, lest you be hated*. The man given to appetite must rule himself at the table, eating as becometh a man and not as one whose throat needs a knife held to it.
cards.s_text: And put a knife to your throat, if you be a man given to appetite.
cards.t_text: Eat as it becometh a man, those things which are set before you; and devour not, lest you be hated.

cards.note: *Leave off first for manners' sake; and be not unsatiable, lest you offend* (Sirach 31:17). The deceitful dainties of *Be not desirous of his dainties: for they are deceitful meat* (Proverbs 23:3) are met with the same restraint the restored witness teaches: *Leave off first... and be not unsatiable*. To desire the ruler's dainties is to be drawn by deceitful meat; the wise leave off first and are not mastered by the unsatiable craving.
cards.s_text: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they are deceitful meat.
cards.t_text: Leave off first for manners’ sake; and be not unsatiable, lest you offend.

cards.note: *A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time* (Sirach 20:7). The restored witness names the discipline behind *A word fitly spoken* (Proverbs 25:11): *A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity*.
