The lost grain is not lost; it is sifted into the nations and kept for the gathering.
cards.s_text: For, lo, I will command, and I will sift the house of Yashar'el (Israel) among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David* (Sirach 47:22). The remnant possessed and the nations called by his name (Amos 9:12) rest on this kept word: *a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David*. The Davidic line is never abolished; from its root the tabernacle is raised again.
cards.s_text: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, says Yahuah (LORD) that does this.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David.

cards.note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols* (Tobit 14:6). The heathen *called by my name* (Amos 9:12), the residue of men seeking after Yahuah, are the all-nations that *turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly*. The rebuilt tabernacle of David draws the nations in — they bury their idols and seek the Name called upon them.
cards.s_text: That they may possess the remnant of Edom, and of all the heathen, which are called by my name, says Yahuah (LORD) that does this.
cards.t_text: And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land* (2 Esdras 13:40). The restored witness names the lost flock by name — the ten tribes of the northern house, scattered into the nations. Micah's *I will surely gather the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Micah 2:12) is the promise that this very scattered north — *the multitude with peace* (13:47) — comes home in the latter time.
cards.s_text: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of you; I will surely gather the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel); I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness comes in* (Wisdom 1:5). The restored witness frames the contrast of Micah 3: the Spirit who fills Micah — *full of power by the spirit of Yahuah (LORD)* (3:8) — *will flee deceit* and *will not abide* the lying prophet for hire. He cannot dwell with the hireling's falsehood; He fills the one sent to declare the people's sin.
cards.s_text: But truly I am full of power by the spirit of Yahuah (LORD), and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his sin.
cards.t_text: For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness comes in.

cards.note: *For the Spirit of Yahuah (God) filleth the world: and that which containeth all things has knowledge of the voice* (Wisdom 1:7). Micah is *full of power by the spirit of Yahuah (LORD)* (3:8); Wisdom declares that same *Spirit of Yahuah (God) filleth the world*. The Spirit who fills all things fills the true prophet with judgment and might to speak — opposite the bought mouths over whom the sun goes down.
cards.s_text: But truly I am full of power by the spirit of Yahuah (LORD), and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his sin.
cards.t_text: For the Spirit of Yahuah (God) filleth the world: and that which containeth all things has knowledge of the voice.

cards.note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted* (Sirach 34:18). They *build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity* (Micah 3:10) — and the restored witness weighs such gifts: *the gifts of unjust men are not accepted*. A Zion raised on blood and bribery brings an offering Yahuah will not receive.
cards.s_text: They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.
cards.t_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.

cards.note: *He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). To *build up Zion with blood* (Micah 3:10) is precisely this — the bloodshedder who *defraudeth the labourer of his hire*. The judges who *judge for reward* and priests who *teach for hire* (Micah 3:11) build a city whose every stone is another man's stolen life.
cards.s_text: They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.
cards.t_text: He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). The restored witness sings the same hope as Micah's *many nations shall come... let us go up to the mountain of Yahuah (LORD)* (Micah 4:2): the nations coming from far to the Name, to Jerusalem, with gifts — the in-gathering of the peoples to the house of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of Yahuah (LORD), and to the house of the Elohim (God) of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of Yahuah (LORD) from Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols* (Tobit 14:6). Micah's nations who say *he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths* (Micah 4:2) are Tobit's all-nations who turn and fear Yahuah truly, casting off their idols — the same Messianic-age conversion of the peoples to walk in Yahuah's ways.
cards.s_text: And many nations shall come, and say, Come, and let us go up to the mountain of Yahuah (LORD), and to the house of the Elohim (God) of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of Yahuah (LORD) from Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Sirach 35:1). The restored witness reads Micah's answer exactly: what Yahuah requires (*to do justly, and to love mercy* — Micah 6:8) is not more rams but the kept commandment — *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough*. Obedience IS the offering.
cards.s_text: He has shewed you, O man, what is good; and what does Yahuah (LORD) require of you, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your Elohim (God)?
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation* (Sirach 35:3). Beside *to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly* (Micah 6:8), Sirach names the same heart: *To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah*. The walk Yahuah requires is the true propitiation the heaped sacrifices could never be.
cards.s_text: He has shewed you, O man, what is good; and what does Yahuah (LORD) require of you, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your Elohim (God)?
cards.t_text: To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.

cards.note: *You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall* (Sirach 2:7). Micah's posture — *Therefore I will look unto Yahuah (LORD); I will wait for the Elohim (God) of my salvation* (Micah 7:7) — is the very counsel of Sirach: *wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall*. The waiting faith that looks up through judgment is the wisdom of the fathers.
cards.s_text: Therefore I will look unto Yahuah (LORD); I will wait for the Elohim (God) of my salvation: my Elohim (God) will hear me.
cards.t_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest you fall.

cards.note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (Tobit 13:5). Micah sees the coming home *from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain* (Micah 7:12); Tobit names it: *he will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us*. The flock fed *as in the days of old* (Micah 7:14) is the scattered two-house people gathered back to the heritage.
cards.s_text: In that day also he shall come even to you from Assyria, and from the fortified cities, and from the fortress even to the river, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
cards.t_text: And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

cards.note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (Tobit 13:5). *Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thine heritage, which dwell solitarily in the wood* (Micah 7:14): the Shepherd feeds the scattered flock, and the gathering Tobit names — *gather us out of all nations* — is that very feeding of the heritage brought home.
cards.s_text: Feed your people with your rod, the flock of your heritage, which dwell solitarily in the wood, in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
cards.t_text: And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction* (Sirach 2:11). Sirach answers Micah's *who is a Elohim (God) like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity* (Micah 7:18) in the same Sinai-words — *full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering... and forgiveth sins*. The fathers knew the incomparable pardoning Elohim.
cards.s_text: Who is a Elohim (God) like unto you, that pardoneth iniquity, and passes by the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delights in mercy.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction.

cards.note: *For he does scourge, and has mercy: he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again: neither is there any that can avoid his hand* (Tobit 13:2). Micah's turning — *He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities* (Micah 7:19) — is Tobit's *he does scourge, and has mercy*. The same hand that brings down brings up; the same Elohim who corrects has compassion.
cards.s_text: He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
cards.t_text: For he does scourge, and has mercy: he leadeth down to hell, and brings up again: neither is there any that can avoid his hand.

cards.note: *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it* (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus 43:23). The One *which hath made the sea and the dry land* (Jonah 1:9) is the One who rules the deep that swallows the prophet — *by his counsel he appeaseth the deep*. The storm and the great fish are alike under the hand of the Maker the Hebrew confesses.
cards.s_text: And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, which has made the sea and the dry land.
cards.t_text: By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.

cards.note: *For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created* (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus 43:25). The Creator of *the sea and the dry land* (Jonah 1:9) made also the deep's creatures — *all kinds of beasts and whales created* — among them the *great fish* He prepares to swallow Jonah (1:17). The confessed Maker holds the very fish of the sign in his hand.
cards.s_text: And he said unto them, I am an Hebrew; and I fear Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, which has made the sea and the dry land.
cards.t_text: For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.

cards.note: *From the depth of the belly of hell, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words* (Ecclesiasticus 51:5). The restored witness sings the same deliverance Jonah cried for — *out of the belly of hell cried I* (Jonah 2:2) — *from the depth of the belly of hell* the soul is drawn up. One cry from Sheol, one Yahuah who hears from the depths.
cards.s_text: And said, I cried by reason of my affliction unto Yahuah (LORD), and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and you heard my voice.
cards.t_text: From the depth of the belly of hell, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words.

cards.note: *I will praise your name continually, and will sing praises with thanksgiving; and so my prayer was heard* (Ecclesiasticus 51:11). Jonah's *he heard me... and thou heardest my voice* (Jonah 2:2) is the same answered cry — *so my prayer was heard*. The prayer from the depths reaches Yahuah and is heard; deliverance turns to thanksgiving.
cards.s_text: And said, I cried by reason of my affliction unto Yahuah (LORD), and he heard me; out of the belly of hell cried I, and you heard my voice.
cards.t_text: I will praise your name continually, and will sing praises with thanksgiving; and so my prayer was heard:

cards.note: *Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently* (Sirach 17:26). Nineveh's turning *from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands* (Jonah 3:8) is this double turning — *Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity.* The one who turns from the evil way is led *out of darkness into the light*; the relenting mercy meets the genuine turn.
cards.s_text: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto Elohim (God): yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
cards.t_text: Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.

cards.note: *Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less* (Sirach 17:25). The restored witness states Nineveh's very act — *let them turn every one from his evil way* (Jonah 3:8) — as the call to all: *Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins.* To repent is to return AND to forsake the sin; the prayer before His face joined to the turning of the way.
cards.s_text: But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily unto Elohim (God): yea, let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
cards.t_text: Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less.

cards.note: *But you have mercy upon all; for you can do all things, and winkest at the sins of men, because they should amend* (Wisdom of Solomon 11:23). The closing question — *should not I spare Nineveh?* (Jonah 4:11) — is this restored witness exactly: Yahuah *has mercy upon all... because they should amend*. The reprieve given Nineveh is mercy that withholds judgment that the sinner may repent.
cards.s_text: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
cards.t_text: But you have mercy upon all; for you can do all things, and winkest at the sins of men, because they should amend.

cards.note: *But you sparest all: for they are yours, O Yahuah (God), you lover of souls* (Wisdom of Solomon 11:26). Why spare Nineveh and its sixscore thousand? Because *you sparest all: for they are yours, O Yahuah (God), you lover of souls*. The gentile city is no less Yahuah's handiwork than Yashar'el (Israel); the lover of souls spares all that are his, and so the question of Jonah 4:11 answers itself.
cards.s_text: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
cards.t_text: But you sparest all: for they are yours, O Yahuah (God), you lover of souls.

cards.note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock* (Sirach 18:13). Jonah's mercy was toward his own; Yahuah's mercy — *should not I spare Nineveh?* (Jonah 4:11) — is *upon all flesh*. The shepherd who reproves and brings again gathers even the city Jonah would have seen burn.
cards.s_text: And should not I spare Nineveh, that great city, wherein are more than sixscore thousand persons that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand; and also much cattle?
cards.t_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.

cards.note: *And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Yahuah (LORD), she came to prove him with hard questions* (1 Kings 10:1). *The queen of the south... came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon* — she who came so far will rise to judge those who would not hear a greater than Solomon at hand.
cards.s_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
cards.t_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Yahuah (LORD), she came to prove him with hard questions.

cards.note: *The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.* (Ecclesiasticus 47:17). The library remembers how Solomon's wisdom drew the nations from afar — the very fame that brought the queen of the south; yet *a greater than Solomon is here* (Luke 11:31).
cards.s_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
cards.t_text: The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.

cards.note: *Then Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea at Arabattine, because they besieged Gael: and he gave them a great overthrow, and abated their courage, and took their spoils* (1 Maccabees 5:3). The recompense Obadiah foretold returns on the brother-line — *thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever* (Obadiah 1:10): centuries later *the children of Esau in Idumea* are given *a great overthrow*. The deed done to Jacob is repaid upon Esau's house.
cards.s_text: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.
cards.t_text: Then Judas fought against the children of Esau in Idumea at Arabattine, because they besieged Gael: and he gave them a great overthrow, and abated their courage, and took their spoils.

cards.note: *And say not His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners* (Sirach 5:6). The restored witness states Nahum's balance plainly — *mercy and wrath come from him* — answering the one who presumes on mercy alone. Nahum's *Yahuah (LORD) revengeth, and is furious* (Nahum 1:2) is the wrath that *resteth upon sinners*.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) is jealous, and Yahuah (LORD) revengeth; Yahuah (LORD) revengeth, and is furious; Yahuah (LORD) will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserveth wrath for his enemies.
cards.t_text: And say not His mercy is great; he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth upon sinners.

cards.note: *Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance* (Sirach 5:7). The slowness of *Yahuah (LORD) is slow to anger* (Nahum 1:3) is no acquittal — *he will not at all acquit the wicked*; the *day of vengeance* comes suddenly on the secure who would not turn.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked: Yahuah (LORD) has his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
cards.t_text: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Sirach 2:10). The restored witness presses Nahum's promise — *he knoweth them that trust in him* (Nahum 1:7): never once was the one who trusted Yahuah confounded or forsaken.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knows them that trust in him.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction* (Sirach 2:11). Nahum's *Yahuah (LORD) is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble* (Nahum 1:7) is the same — He *saves in time of affliction*; the goodness is the refuge of all who trust Him.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble; and he knows them that trust in him.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saves in time of affliction.

cards.note: *Go into Media my son, for I surely believe those things which Jonas the prophet spoke of Nineve, that it shall be overthrown... and that our brothers shall lie scattered in the earth from that good land: and Jerusalem shall be desolate, and the house of Yahuah (God) in it shall be burned* (Tobit 14:4). Nahum's *yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, shall they cry; but none shall look back* (Nahum 2:8) is the very overthrow Tobit, a captive in Nineveh, surely believed was coming — *that it shall be overthrown*. The restored witness of the exile confirms the prophet's word: the city of the emptiers will itself be emptied.
cards.s_text: But Nineveh is of old like a pool of water: yet they shall flee away. Stand, stand, shall they cry; but none shall look back.
cards.t_text: Go into Media my son, for I surely believe those things which Jonas the prophet spoke of Nineve, that it shall be overthrown; and that for a time peace shall rather be in Media; and that our brothers shall lie scattered in the earth from that good land: and Jerusalem shall be desolate, and the house of Yahuah (God) in it shall be burned, and shall be desolate for a time;

cards.note: *But before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineve, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineve* (Tobit 14:15). When Yahuah said *Behold, I am against thee, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Nahum 2:13), the doom was sure — and Tobit, carried captive into Nineveh itself, lived to hear *the destruction of Nineve* and *rejoiced over Nineve*. The captive's own testimony seals the oracle: the bloody city fell exactly as Yahuah had spoken.
cards.s_text: Behold, I am against you, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour your young lions: and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers shall no more be heard.
cards.t_text: But before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineve, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineve.

cards.note: *But before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineve, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineve* (Tobit 14:15). The restored witness records the very relief Nahum foretells — *all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee* (Nahum 3:19): faithful Tobit, who lived under Nineveh's cruelty, *rejoiced over Nineve* at her fall. Jonah's word (Tobit 14:4,8) is fulfilled; the oppressed are glad at the end of the perpetual oppressor.
cards.s_text: There is no healing of your bruise; your wound is grievous: all that hear the bruit of you shall clap the hands over you: for upon whom has not your wickedness passed continually?
cards.t_text: But before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineve, which was taken by Nabuchodonosor and Assuerus: and before his death he rejoiced over Nineve.

cards.note: *Go into Media my son, for I surely believe those things which Jonas the prophet spoke of Nineve, that it shall be overthrown* (Tobit 14:4). Nahum's *Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her?* (Nahum 3:7) is the certain overthrow Tobit stakes his counsel on — *I surely believe those things which Jonas the prophet spoke of Nineve, that it shall be overthrown*. The fall is so sure the righteous flee the city before it comes; none will be left to mourn.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon you shall flee from you, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? whence shall I seek comforters for you?
cards.t_text: Go into Media my son, for I surely believe those things which Jonas the prophet spoke of Nineve, that it shall be overthrown; and that for a time peace shall rather be in Media; and that our brothers shall lie scattered in the earth from that good land: and Jerusalem shall be desolate, and the house of Yahuah (God) in it shall be burned, and shall be desolate for a time;

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen; till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptre of the unrighteous* (Sirach 35:18). To Habakkuk's complaint that *the law is slacked* (Habakkuk 1:4), the restored witness answers in kind: *Yahuah (God) will not be slack... till he have judged the cause of his people* (35:18-19). The slackness is man's, not Yahuah's; the Judge's delay is not negligence, and His verdict is sure.
cards.s_text: Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment does never go forth: for the wicked does compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceeds.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen; till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptre of the unrighteous;

cards.note: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). The cry *how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear!* (Habakkuk 1:2) is the question the righteous souls themselves ask — *How long shall I hope on this fashion?* The wrestling with Yahuah's apparent silence is the saints' own faithful question, recorded and answered.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (LORD), how long shall I cry, and you will not hear! even cry out unto you of violence, and you will not save!
cards.t_text: Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?

cards.note: *For I have seen how you sufferest them sinning, and have spared wicked doers: and have destroyed your people, and have preserved your enemies, and have not signified it* (2 Esdras 3:30). Habakkuk's *Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance?* (Habakkuk 1:3) is the very lament Ezra pours out in the restored witness — that Yahuah seems to spare the wicked and let His own suffer. The same theodicy ache: the righteous bewildered that the Holy One holds His tongue while violence triumphs.
cards.s_text: Why do you shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there are that raise up strife and contention.
cards.t_text: For I have seen how you sufferest them sinning, and have spared wicked doers: and have destroyed your people, and have preserved your enemies, and have not signified it.

cards.note: *For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle; and as for their feet, they are slow to go* (Wisdom of Solomon 15:15). The restored witness names exactly Habakkuk's charge — the idol with *no breath at all in the midst of it* (Habakkuk 2:19). The made-thing has no breath to draw, no eyes, no ears; it cannot be a god, for *man made them.*
cards.s_text: Woe unto him that says to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.
cards.t_text: For they counted all the idols of the heathen to be gods: which neither have the use of eyes to see, nor noses to draw breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers of hands to handle; and as for their feet, they are slow to go.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). Habakkuk's stripped season — *the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat* (Habakkuk 3:17) — is the furnace the wise son is told to expect: *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity*. The barren year is the testing in which faith is proved acceptable.
cards.s_text: Although the fig tree shall not blossom, neither shall fruit be in the vines; the labour of the olive shall fail, and the fields shall yield no meat; the flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls:
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him* (Ecclesiasticus 2:6). Habakkuk's *I will joy in the Elohim (God) of my salvation* (Habakkuk 3:18) is the furnace-trust the restored wisdom teaches — *Believe in him, and he will help you... trust in him*. The rejoicing rests on Yahuah himself, the Elohim who helps and saves, not on the circumstances that have failed.
cards.s_text: Yet I will rejoice in Yahuah (LORD), I will joy in the Elohim (God) of my salvation.
cards.t_text: Believe in him, and he will help you; order your way aright, and trust in him.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Sirach 35:1). The second-Temple wisdom fuses faith and faithful doing exactly as Yahusha does — to keep the law IS the acceptable service, the offering *enough.* The servant who has *done that which was our duty* (Luke 17:10) has brought the very sacrifice that pleases; obedience and trust are never torn apart in the library.
cards.s_text: So likewise you, when you shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance* (Sirach 5:7). The restored witness rebukes the exact security Zephaniah names — the men settled on their lees who say *Yahuah will not do good* (Zephaniah 1:12). The wrath comes suddenly upon those at ease; the day of vengeance overtakes the secure.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, Yahuah (LORD) will not do good, neither will he do evil.
cards.t_text: Make no tarrying to turn to Yahuah (God), and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of Yahuah (God) come forth, and in your security you shall be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.

cards.note: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Sirach 11:19). Centuries before the parable of the rich fool, the wisdom-witness draws the same man Zephaniah judges: he hoards his goods in false rest, not knowing they shall *become a booty* (Zephaniah 1:13) and be left to others. The complacent man and his lost goods.
cards.s_text: Therefore their goods shall become a booty, and their houses a desolation: they shall also build houses, but not inhabit them; and they shall plant vineyards, but not drink the wine thereof.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: *They that fear Yahuah (God) will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight* (Ecclesiasticus 2:17). The *meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment* (Zephaniah 2:3) are those who *humble their souls in his sight* — the restored witness names the same posture: hearts prepared, souls humbled before Yahuah. The meekness Zephaniah commands is this self-humbling fear of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Seek you Yahuah (LORD), all you meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be you shall be hid in the day of the LORD’S anger.
cards.t_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) will prepare their hearts, and humble their souls in his sight,

cards.note: *They that fear Yahuah (God) will seek that which is well, pleasing to him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law* (Ecclesiasticus 2:16). The remnant *which have wrought his judgment* (Zephaniah 2:3) are *filled with the law* — to seek righteousness and meekness is to be filled with the Torah, not freed from it. The doers of his judgment are the ones who love him and are filled with his law.
cards.s_text: Seek you Yahuah (LORD), all you meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be you shall be hid in the day of the LORD’S anger.
cards.t_text: They that fear Yahuah (God) will seek that which is well, pleasing to him; and they that love him shall be filled with the law.

cards.note: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead* (Ecclesiasticus 10:14). The proud city that said *I am, and there is none beside me* (Zephaniah 2:15) is cast down — and in her stead the meek are set up, the very *meek of the earth* called to seek Yahuah in 2:3. The judgment on the careless city and the inheritance of the meek are one work: Yahuah throws down the proud and raises the lowly.
cards.s_text: This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation, a place for beasts to lie down in! every one that passes by her shall hiss, and wag his hand.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). The restored witness sees the very thing Zephaniah promised — that all peoples *call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD)* (Zephaniah 3:9): *many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God)*. The nations streaming to the one Name with praise.
cards.s_text: For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD), to serve him with one consent.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols* (Tobit 14:6). The pure language given so that *they may all call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD), to serve him with one consent* (Zephaniah 3:9) is the turning of all nations: *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly*, their idols buried. The one Name served with one consent.
cards.s_text: For then will I turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD), to serve him with one consent.
cards.t_text: And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.

cards.note: *Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God)* (Baruch 5:5). The restored witness sings Zephaniah's homecoming — *I will... gather you... when I turn back your captivity* (Zephaniah 3:20): *behold your children gathered from the west to the east... rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God)*. The driven-out children brought home.
cards.s_text: At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, says Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him* (Baruch 5:9). The captivity turned and the gathered made *a name and a praise* (Zephaniah 3:20) is the joyful procession home: *Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory*. The gathering home is led by Yahuah Himself, in mercy and righteousness.
cards.s_text: At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, says Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) shall lead Yashar'el (Israel) with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that comes from him.

cards.note: *So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory* (Ecclesiasticus 49:12). Haggai names the same high priest — *Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest* (Haggai 1:12) — and the restored witness records the outcome of the obedience: *who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God)*. The "I am with you" bore its fruit; the house that lay waste was raised.
cards.s_text: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God), and the words of Haggai the prophet, as Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) had sent him, and the people did fear before Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory.

cards.note: *How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand* (Ecclesiasticus 49:11). The restored witness honours the very man Haggai stirred — *Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel... with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God)* (Haggai 1:12). Sirach remembers Zerubbabel *as a signet on the right hand*, the prince of the rebuilding the prophet roused to the work.
cards.s_text: Then Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed the voice of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God), and the words of Haggai the prophet, as Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) had sent him, and the people did fear before Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand:

cards.note: *How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand* (Ecclesiasticus 49:11). The restored witness magnifies the very man Haggai sealed: Zerubbabel *was as a signet on the right hand* — echoing word for word *will I... make thee as a signet* (Haggai 2:23), and answering Jeremiah's plucked signet (Jeremiah 22:24). Ben Sira remembers him as the seal restored to the right hand of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: In that day, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), will I take you, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, says Yahuah (LORD), and will make you as a signet: for I have chosen you, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).
cards.t_text: How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand:

cards.note: *So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory* (Ecclesiasticus 49:12). The witness pairs Zerubbabel the signet with Joshua (Jesus) son of Josedech — the very pair addressed in Haggai 2:2 — who *builded the house, and set up an holy temple... prepared for everlasting glory*. This is Haggai's own promise remembered: the latter house *filled with glory* (Haggai 2:7), the glory *greater than of the former* (2:9), prepared for everlasting glory.
cards.s_text: In that day, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), will I take you, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, says Yahuah (LORD), and will make you as a signet: for I have chosen you, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).
cards.t_text: So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory.

cards.note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). Israel's own wisdom confessed it long before Joppa: life and death belong to Yahuah alone, who *bringest up again*. When *many believed in Yahuah* (Acts 9:42), they believed in the One who has always held that power.
cards.s_text: And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord.
cards.t_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.

cards.note: *Help the poor for the commandment's sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty* (Sirach 29:9). The second-Temple sages read the open-hand statute exactly as Antioch lived it — mercy to the poor done *for the commandment's sake*, Torah obeyed in love, not set aside.
cards.s_text: Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judæa:
cards.t_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.

cards.note: *Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. Call to remembrance what acts our fathers did in their time; so shall you receive great honour and an everlasting name* (1 Maccabees 2:50-51). Mattathias' charge to his sons is the pattern James fulfils — to give one's life for the covenant and win an everlasting name. The martyr does not die for a new thing but for the old faith of the fathers.
cards.s_text: And because he saw it pleased the Yahudim (Jews), he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)
cards.t_text: Now therefore, my sons, be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers.

cards.note: *Fear not then the words of a sinful man: for his glory shall be dung and worms. To day he shall be lifted up and to morrow he shall not be found, because he is returned into his dust* (1 Maccabees 2:62-63). Mattathias named the end of the proud tyrant — lifted up today, dung and worms tomorrow. Herod *eaten of worms* (Acts 12:23) is that word fulfilled to the letter, while the word of Elohim multiplies on.
cards.s_text: But the word of Elohim (God) grew and multiplied.
cards.t_text: Fear not then the words of a sinful man: for his glory shall be dung and worms.

cards.note: *The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.* (Sirach 34:21). The second-Temple sages weighed it the same: to withhold bread from the hungry at the very table is no light thing — it is bloodguilt. The whole library speaks with one voice on the poor.
cards.s_text: What? have you not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise you the assembly of Elohim (God), and shame them that have not? What shall I say to you? shall I praise you in this? I praise you not.
cards.t_text: The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Sirach 2:5). Ben Sira reads the Father's chastening just as Paul does: not wrath against the rejected but the refining of the accepted. The fire proves the son it loves.
cards.s_text: But when we are judged, we are chastened of Yahuah (the Lord), that we should not be condemned with the world.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *He seeks out the deep, and the heart, and considereth their crafty devices: for Yahuah (God) knoweth all that may be known, and he beholds the signs of the world* (Sirach 42:18). Ben Sira sings the same searching Elohim — he seeks out the heart, no thought escapes him. When prophecy makes "the secrets of his heart manifest," it is this all-knowing One at work in the gathered.
cards.s_text: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship Elohim (God), and report that Elohim (God) is in you of a truth.
cards.t_text: He seeks out the deep, and the heart, and considereth their crafty devices: for Yahuah (God) knoweth all that may be known, and he beholds the signs of the world.

cards.note: Out to the furnace of the upright: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). Job's *shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips* (Job 2:10) is the acceptable man in the furnace — the same image 1 Peter takes up as faith *tried with fire* (1 Peter 1:7), adversity refining rather than condemning the righteous.
cards.s_text: But he said unto her, You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. What? shall we receive good at the hand of Elohim (God), and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: Out to the wisdom of endurance: *Whatsoever is brought upon you take cheerfully, and be patient when you are changed to a low estate* (Ecclesiasticus 2:4). Job *took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes* (Job 2:8) — the man brought to the lowest estate, scraping his sores in the dust, embodies the patient bearing the second-Temple wisdom counsels.
cards.s_text: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
cards.t_text: Whatsoever is brought upon you take cheerfully, and be patient when you are changed to a low estate.

cards.note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). The restored wisdom library confesses Hannah's creed exactly — *Yahuah (LORD) killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up* (1 Samuel 2:6) — life and death held in one hand.
cards.s_text: Yahuah (LORD) kills, and makes alive: he brings down to the grave, and brings up.
cards.t_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.

cards.note: *By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision* (Ecclesiasticus 46:15). *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared again in Shiloh: for Yahuah (LORD) revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of Yahuah (LORD)* (1 Samuel 3:21) — the open vision restored — is what the witness names: *by his word he was known to be faithful in vision*. Where there had been *no open vision* (3:1), Yahuah now reveals Himself by His word through a true and faithful prophet.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) appeared again in Shiloh: for Yahuah (LORD) revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision.

cards.note: *Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah (God), beloved of his Elohim (God), established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people* (Ecclesiasticus 46:13). That *all Yashar'el (Israel) from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Yahuah (LORD)* (1 Samuel 3:20) is remembered by the restored witness: *Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah... established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people*. The child called in the night becomes the prophet who anoints Israel's kings.
cards.s_text: And all Yashar'el (Israel) from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah (God), beloved of his Elohim (God), established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.

cards.note: *By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision* (Ecclesiasticus 46:15). When *there was no open vision* (1 Samuel 3:1), the open vision is restored in Samuel — *by his word he was known to be faithful in vision*. The restored witness remembers him as the very man through whom the dearth of seeing was answered: a true prophet, faithful in vision, when vision had failed.
cards.s_text: And the child Samuel ministered unto Yahuah (LORD) before Eli. And the word of Yahuah (LORD) was precious in those days; there was no open vision.
cards.t_text: By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision.

cards.note: *Instead of which you gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably.* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:3). The guiding Moses recalls — Yahuah (God) *went in the way before you, to search you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day* (Deuteronomy 1:33) — is witnessed in the restored book: *a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey*. The fire by night that led the son through the wilderness.
cards.s_text: Who went in the way before you, to search you out a place to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to shew you by what way you should go, and in a cloud by day.
cards.t_text: Instead of which you gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey, and an harmless sun to entertain them honourably.

cards.note: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob* (Sirach 24:23). The 2nd-Temple sages already read Deuteronomy's claim — *statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law* (Deuteronomy 4:8) — as Wisdom herself: the divine Wisdom IS the Torah Moses gave for an heritage.
cards.s_text: And what nation is there so great, that has statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law, which I set before you this day?
cards.t_text: All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob.

cards.note: *Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of Yahuah (God), and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster* (Wisdom of Solomon 13:1). The warning against being *driven to worship... the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven* (Deuteronomy 4:19) is exactly the folly Wisdom names: mistaking the creature for the Creator.
cards.s_text: And lest you lift up your eyes unto heaven, and when you see the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, should be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.
cards.t_text: Surely vain are all men by nature, who are ignorant of Yahuah (God), and could not out of the good things that are seen know him that is: neither by considering the works did they acknowledge the workmaster;

cards.note: *But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 13:2). A direct gloss on Deuteronomy 4:19 — the *circle of the stars* and *the lights of heaven* are the very *sun, and the moon, and the stars... all the host of heaven* Moses forbids the people to worship.
cards.s_text: And lest you lift up your eyes unto heaven, and when you see the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, should be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.
cards.t_text: But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world.

cards.note: *Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men* (Baruch 3:37). The unseen One whose *similitude* Yashar'el could not behold — *ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude* (Deuteronomy 4:12) — is the same who would *shew himself upon earth,* the Formed Son made visible.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto you out of the midst of the fire: you heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude; only you heard a voice.
cards.t_text: Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men.

cards.note: *This is our Elohim (God), and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him* (Baruch 3:35). The restored witness repeats Moses' confession — *Yahuah (LORD) he is Elohim (God)... there is none else* (Deuteronomy 4:39) — none other to be accounted of beside Him.
cards.s_text: Know therefore this day, and consider it in your heart, that Yahuah (LORD) he is Elohim (God) in heaven above, and upon the earth beneath: there is none else.
cards.t_text: This is our Elohim (God), and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him

cards.note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved* (Baruch 3:36). The one Elohim of Deuteronomy 4:39 *there is none else* is the same who gave the way of knowledge — the Torah-wisdom — to Jacob and Yashar'el alone.
cards.s_text: Know therefore this day, and consider it in your heart, that Yahuah (LORD) he is Elohim (God) in heaven above, and upon the earth beneath: there is none else.
cards.t_text: He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.

cards.note: *There is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him* (Ecclesiasticus 37:4). Sirach diagnoses the fair-weather friend who fails in *the day of affliction*; this is the friend Job indicts — they came to comfort and dealt deceitfully (Job 6:14-15).
cards.s_text: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty.
cards.t_text: There is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him.

cards.note: *What is man, and to which serveth he? what is his good, and what is his evil? The number of a man's days at the most are an hundred years. As a drop of water to the sea, and a gravelstone in comparison of the sand; so are a thousand years to the days of eternity* (Ecclesiasticus 18:8-10). The wisdom library carries Job's very question — *What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him?* (Job 7:17) — and answers it with the measure that frames it: man's little span set against the days of eternity, a drop to the sea. Why should the Eternal set His heart on so small a thing? The library lets the wonder stand.
cards.s_text: What is man, that you should magnify him? and that you should set your heart upon him?
cards.t_text: What is man, and to which serveth he? what is his good, and what is his evil?

cards.note: *And our name shall be forgotten in time... and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, that is driven away with the beams of the sun... For our time is a very shadow that passeth away; and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:4-5). The wisdom library puts Job's very image — *as the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away... he shall come up no more* (Job 7:9) — in the mouth of the ungodly who reason WITHOUT hope. Job grieves it as a righteous man pressed to the wall; the ungodly seize it as license. The same shadow, the same vanishing cloud — but the heart that holds it makes all the difference.
cards.s_text: As the cloud is consumed and vanishes away: so he that goes down to the grave shall come up no more.
cards.t_text: And our name shall be forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, that is driven away with the beams of the sun, and overcome with the heat thereof.

cards.note: *Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learn understanding, and to give answer as need requires* (Sirach 8:9). Bildad appeals to the same inheritance: *For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers... Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?* (Job 8:8,10). The wisdom tradition honors the handed-down counsel of the fathers — yet the book of Job will show that the fathers' tidy retribution formula does not fit every righteous sufferer.
cards.s_text: For enquire, I pray you, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:
cards.t_text: Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learn understanding, and to give answer as need requires.

cards.note: *As for the wondrous works of Yahuah (God), there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out* (Ecclesiasticus 18:6). The ground of the Maker's works cannot be found out — exactly Job's *great things past finding out* (Job 9:10) — the same posture the Torah commands toward the perfect work of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.s_text: Which does great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
cards.t_text: As for the wondrous works of Yahuah (God), there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out.

cards.note: *To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?* (Ecclesiasticus 18:4). Ben Sira voices Job's wonder — the One *which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number* (Job 9:10) — the works of the Maker are beyond the reach of the creature to declare.
cards.s_text: Which does great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
cards.t_text: To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?

cards.note: *But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again* (2 Maccabees 7:23). The mother of the seven sons confesses the very Creator Job confesses — *Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit* (Job 10:12) — and carries it forward past the dust-fear: the One who formed will give breath and life AGAIN.
cards.s_text: You have granted me life and favour, and your visitation has preserved my spirit.
cards.t_text: But doubtless the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man, and found out the beginning of all things, will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again, as you now regard not your own selves for his laws’ sake.

cards.note: *And in my mother's womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:2). Solomon's wisdom describes the same hidden craft Job marvels at — *Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese? Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh* (Job 10:10-11): the flesh compacted, fashioned, clothed in the womb by the Creator's hand.
cards.s_text: You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and have fenced me with bones and sinews.
cards.t_text: And in my mother’s womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood, of the seed of man, and the pleasure that came with sleep.

cards.note: *Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity? Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom?* (Ecclesiasticus 1:2-3). The restored wisdom-tradition echoes Job 11:8-9 almost word for word — *high as heaven ... deeper than hell ... longer than the earth, and broader than the sea* — confessing that the height of heaven and the breadth of the earth and the deep cannot be found out by man.
cards.s_text: It is as high as heaven; what can you do? deeper than hell; what can you know?
cards.t_text: Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?

cards.note: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 1:1). Ben Sira opens with Job's very claim: *With him is wisdom and strength* (Job 12:13) — wisdom is not a human possession but is *with him* for ever, the Formed Word at the Maker's side.
cards.s_text: With him is wisdom and strength, he has counsel and understanding.
cards.t_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.

cards.note: *For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble* (Ecclesiasticus 6:8). The wisdom of Ben Sira draws the very portrait Job suffers: friends present in prosperity who, when the day of trouble comes, become *physicians of no value* (Job 13:4) — counsellors who abandon the man precisely when he bleeds.
cards.s_text: But you are forgers of lies, you are all physicians of no value.
cards.t_text: For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.

cards.note: *All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death* (Sirach 14:17). Ben Sira reads Job's frailty as the Eden-sentence -- man wears out like cloth. *He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow* (Job 14:2): the appointed end of all flesh.
cards.s_text: He comes forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continues not.
cards.t_text: All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death.

cards.note: *For our time is a very shadow that passeth away; and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again* (Wisdom 2:5). The ungodly in Wisdom say what Job feels in the dark -- the tree may sprout, *but man dieth, and wasteth away... and where is he?* (Job 14:7,10). Wisdom voices the despair that 14:14 will dare to question.
cards.s_text: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
cards.t_text: For our time is a very shadow that passeth away; and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again.

cards.note: *Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave* (Wisdom 2:1). This is the dark verdict Job wrestles -- *man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?* (Job 14:10). The canon records the darkness honestly before it answers it.
cards.s_text: But man dies, and wasteth away: yea, man gives up the ghost, and where is he?
cards.t_text: For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.

cards.note: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them* (2 Esdras 7:32). The Second-Temple hope speaks Job's answer plainly -- the dust that swallowed the dead gives them back. *If a man die, shall he live again?* (Job 14:14): the earth shall restore those asleep in her.
cards.s_text: If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
cards.t_text: And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom 3:1). Job's plea -- *thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands* (14:15) -- is met by Wisdom's assurance: the righteous are held in the hand of Yahuah, not abandoned to the grave.
cards.s_text: You shall call, and I will answer you: you will have a desire to the work of your hands.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom 3:4). Against the seeming destruction of the righteous, Wisdom answers Job's longing for reunion (14:15) -- their hope is *full of immortality*. The desire of the Creator for the work of his hands does not die with the body.
cards.s_text: You shall call, and I will answer you: you will have a desire to the work of your hands.
cards.t_text: For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality.

cards.note: Ben Sira sings the same dissolving wealth: *The goods of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in rain* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 40:13). Zophar's *The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath* (Job 20:28) is the river drying up — the wisdom tradition guards this truth even where Zophar misuses it.
cards.s_text: He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: Elohim (God) shall cast them out of his belly.
cards.t_text: The goods of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in rain.

cards.note: The library's own praise of Samuel echoes this verse: *And before his long sleep he made protestations in the sight of Yahuah (God) and his anointed, I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe: and no man did accuse him* (Ecclesiasticus 46:19) — the very farewell of *whose ox have I taken... or of whose hand have I received any bribe* (1 Samuel 12:3), remembered down the centuries as the mark of the true judge.
cards.s_text: Behold, here I am: witness against me before Yahuah (LORD), and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind my eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
cards.t_text: And before his long sleep he made protestations in the sight of Yahuah (God) and his anointed, I have not taken any man’s goods, so much as a shoe: and no man did accuse him.

cards.note: The library remembers this very thunder: *He called upon the mighty Yahuah (God), when his enemies pressed upon him on every side, when he offered the sucking lamb. And Yahuah (God) thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard* (Ecclesiasticus 46:16-17) — the heavenly answer to Samuel's prayer, *and Yahuah (LORD) sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared Yahuah (LORD) and Samuel* (1 Samuel 12:18).
cards.s_text: So Samuel called unto Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared Yahuah (LORD) and Samuel.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.

cards.note: The library's memorial of Samuel frames v.23 exactly: *Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah (God), beloved of his Elohim (God)... By the law of Yahuah (God) he judged the congregation* (Ecclesiasticus 46:13-14). Samuel's promise *I will teach you the good and the right way* (1 Samuel 12:23) is the Torah-way — *by the law of Yahuah he judged* — taught, never abolished.
cards.s_text: Moreover as for me, Elohim (God) forbid that I should sin against Yahuah (LORD) in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
cards.t_text: Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah (God), beloved of his Elohim (God), established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1). The wisdom of Yashar'el (Israel) reads Samuel exactly: the keeping of Torah IS the acceptable offering — obedience does not abolish the altar but fills it. *To obey is better than sacrifice* (1 Samuel 15:22) because obedience is the offering Yahuah was always after.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said, Has Yahuah (LORD) as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Yahuah (LORD)? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise* (Ecclesiasticus 35:2). Ben Sira binds righteous deeds to the sacrificial vocabulary itself, the same fusion Samuel makes when he weighs *obeying the voice of Yahuah (LORD)* against *burnt offerings and sacrifices* (1 Samuel 15:22) — the deed of obedience is the truer flour and praise.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said, Has Yahuah (LORD) as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Yahuah (LORD)? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
cards.t_text: He that requiteth a goodturn offers fine flour; and he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.

cards.note: *He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:1). Ben Sira reads the open-hand law of Deuteronomy 15:8 — *thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need* — as commandment-keeping itself: to lend in mercy is to keep the Torah, the strengthened hand and the kept commandment being the same act.
cards.s_text: But you shall open your hand wide unto him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.
cards.t_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.

cards.note: *Help the poor for the commandment's sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:9). Ben Sira echoes the enduring command of Deuteronomy 15:11 — *Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy* — naming its ground plainly: help the poor *for the commandment's sake*, the Torah itself the reason the hand stays open.
cards.s_text: For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command you, saying, You shall open your hand wide unto your brother, to your poor, and to your needy, in your land.
cards.t_text: Help the poor for the commandment’s sake, and turn him not away because of his poverty.

cards.note: Wisdom shows the wicked's too-late repentance at the day Job foretells: 'And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach' (Wisdom of Solomon 5:3). The wicked 'brought forth to the day of wrath' (Job 21:30) face there the righteous they once despised.
cards.s_text: That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath.
cards.t_text: And they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach:

cards.note: Wisdom seals the wicked's end the friends could not deliver on schedule: 'For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm... and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day' (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). Job's 'stubble before the wind... chaff that the storm carrieth away' (Job 21:18) is the same vanishing — at the end, not the middle.
cards.s_text: They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away.
cards.t_text: For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.

cards.note: Ben Sira draws the same lesson on the rich man's false security: 'Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die' (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). Where Job protests 'Elohim (God) layeth up his iniquity for his children' (Job 21:19), the reckoning is real but reserved.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) lays up his iniquity for his children: he rewardeth him, and he shall know it.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: Wisdom unmasks the same contempt: 'We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness... and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father' (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). The wicked who ask 'What is the Almighty, that we should serve him?' (Job 21:15) despise the knowledge of his ways as the deluded do who lie in wait for the righteous.
cards.s_text: What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?
cards.t_text: We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.

cards.note: The ungodly's own creed, given voice: 'Come on therefore, let us enjoy the good things that are present: and let us speedily use the creatures like as in youth' (Wisdom of Solomon 2:6). Job's wicked who 'take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ' (Job 21:12) are the same revellers who treat present pleasure as their whole portion.
cards.s_text: They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
cards.t_text: Come on therefore, let us enjoy the good things that are present: and let us speedily use the creatures like as in youth.

cards.note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). Ben Sira sets the proverb of the sufferer almost word for word beside Job: gold tried in the fire, acceptable men in the furnace of adversity. Job''s *I shall come forth as gold* (Job 23:10) is exactly this — the righteous proved acceptable by the affliction, not condemned by it.
