cards.s_text: But he knows the way that I take: when he has tried me, I shall come forth as gold.
cards.t_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.

cards.note: *He that takes away his neighbour's living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). The wisdom of Ben Sira names the crime of Job's oppressors for what it is — bloodshed. To *take a pledge of the poor* (Job 24:9) and strip the labourer is not mere theft; it is to slay a man by inches. The restored library keeps the Torah's verdict: the defrauder of the poor is a murderer.
cards.s_text: They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.
cards.t_text: He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.

cards.note: *The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the Most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:17). Where Job sees the groan of the wounded rise unanswered (Job 24:12), Ben Sira tracks that same cry upward — it *pierces the clouds* and does not rest until the Most High judges. The delay Job feels is the prayer still climbing; the answer is certain.
cards.s_text: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded cries out: yet Elohim (God) lays not folly to them.
cards.t_text: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the Most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:18). This is the direct answer to Job's complaint that *Elohim (God) layeth not folly to them* (Job 24:12). He is *not slack* — the patience is not impunity but the held breath before the loins of the unmerciful are struck in sunder.
cards.s_text: Men groan from out of the city, and the soul of the wounded cries out: yet Elohim (God) lays not folly to them.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) will not be slack, neither will the Mighty be patient toward them, till he have struck in sunder the loins of the unmerciful, and repayed vengeance to the heathen; till he have taken away the multitude of the proud, and broken the sceptre of the unrighteous;

cards.note: *For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:15). The wisdom-teacher voices the same creaturely lowliness Bildad presses — *how can he be clean that is born of a woman?* (Job 25:4) — the corruptible, earthy frame cannot reach up to the purity of the Most High.
cards.s_text: How then can man be justified with Elohim (God)? or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?
cards.t_text: For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.

cards.note: *To whom Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with Yahuah (God) of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company* (1 Maccabees 3:18). Generations later Yahudah Maccabee, facing a mighty host with a small company, confesses David's very creed — *Yahuah (LORD) saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD'S* (1 Samuel 17:47); the deliverance is reckoned to Yahuah, not to numbers.
cards.s_text: And all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saves not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’S, and he will give you into our hands.
cards.t_text: To whom Judas answered, It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with Yahuah (God) of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company:

cards.note: *For the victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; but strength comes from heaven* (1 Maccabees 3:19). This is the marrow of David's word to the assembly — *all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saveth not with sword and spear* (1 Samuel 17:47); the strength that wins the field comes down from Yahuah, and the host learns it.
cards.s_text: And all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saves not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’S, and he will give you into our hands.
cards.t_text: For the victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; but strength comes from heaven.

cards.note: *Who has seen him, that he might tell us? and who can magnify him as he is?... There are yet hid greater things than these be, for we have seen but a few of his works* (Sirach 43:31-32). Ben Sira closes his own creation-hymn exactly where Job does — *how little a portion is heard of him?* (Job 26:14). All the cosmic wonders are *but a few of his works*; the thunder of his power remains beyond the telling.
cards.s_text: Lo, these are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?
cards.t_text: Who has seen him, that he might tell us? and who can magnify him as he is?

cards.note: Ben Sira draws the same portrait of the man who heaps up silver: *There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:18-19). Job's wicked man who *heap[s] up silver as the dust* (Job 27:16) leaves it all behind — the silver passes to others, exactly as Job foretells.
cards.s_text: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay;
cards.t_text: There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:

cards.note: Job asks *what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when Elohim (God) taketh away his soul?* (Job 27:8), and Wisdom answers in the same breath of wind and storm: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; ... and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). The godless man's confidence has no anchor before Yahuah; when trouble comes (Job 27:9) it scatters like dust.
cards.s_text: For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he has gained, when Elohim (God) takes away his soul?
cards.t_text: For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.

cards.note: Baruch hears Job's very question and presses it: *Who has found out her place? or who has come into her treasures?* (Baruch 3:15). Job had cried *But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?* (Job 28:12) — and this restored witness in the wisdom-tradition is a near-paraphrase of the whole chapter, ransacking the earth, the sea, and the heathen princes and finding wisdom in none of them, until the answer comes home to Elohim alone.
cards.s_text: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
cards.t_text: Who has found out her place? or who has come into her treasures?

cards.note: Of the gold-hoarders Baruch asks *...they that hoarded up silver and gold, in which men trust, and made no end of their getting?* — and answers that they vanished and went down to the grave (Baruch 3:17-19). It is Job's verdict exactly: *The gold and the crystal cannot equal it... the price of wisdom is above rubies* (Job 28:17-18). The thing men trust to buy everything cannot buy her.
cards.s_text: The gold and the crystal cannot equal it: and the exchange of it shall not be for jewels of fine gold.
cards.t_text: They that had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and they that hoarded up silver and gold, in which men trust, and made no end of their getting?

cards.note: *Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?* (Baruch 3:30) — no one. Job had already weighed her against *pure gold* and *the topaz of Ethiopia* and found gold wanting: *neither shall it be valued with pure gold* (Job 28:19). Wisdom is not an article of trade; she is given, not bought.
cards.s_text: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it, neither shall it be valued with pure gold.
cards.t_text: Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?

cards.note: Ben Sira opens his whole book on Job's answer: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever* (Sirach 1:1). Job asked *where shall wisdom be found?* (Job 28:12); the wisdom-tradition replies in one line — her source and her home are with Yahuah, and from no mine, market, or sea is she dug or bought.
cards.s_text: But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?
cards.t_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.

cards.note: The wisdom-tradition confesses what Job glimpses: *Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting* (Sirach 1:4). When Elohim *prepared it, yea, and searched it out* (Job 28:27), wisdom was already brought forth — not a thing dug from the earth in time, but with Yahuah from everlasting, the firstborn of his way.
cards.s_text: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out.
cards.t_text: Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.

cards.note: *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:10). The wisdom tradition names exactly Job's deed — *I was a father to the poor* (Job 29:16) — and weighs it as the mark of a son of the Most High: covenant mercy is the fruit by which the righteous are known.
cards.s_text: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
cards.t_text: Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.

cards.note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). The wicked plot the testing of the just man with mockery and torment, the very contempt Job tastes — *And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword* (Job 30:9) — the abasement of the righteous as the wicked's sport.
cards.s_text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
cards.t_text: Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.

cards.note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). The shameful end appointed for the just man by his mockers gathers Job's reproach — *I am their byword* (Job 30:9) — forward toward the Man of Sorrows condemned by the very pattern.
cards.s_text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.
cards.t_text: Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.

cards.note: *The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the Most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment* (Ecclesiasticus 35:17). The humble man's prayer is not abandoned though it goes uncomforted — the very tension of Job's *I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me* (Job 30:20): the cry pierces the clouds and waits on the Most High's appointed regard.
cards.s_text: I cry unto you, and you do not hear me: I stand up, and you regard me not.
cards.t_text: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the Most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.

cards.note: *Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:17). The wicked wait to see calamity overtake the just man — and the just man himself is bewildered by it: *When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness* (Job 30:26).
cards.s_text: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
cards.t_text: Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him.

cards.note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). The taunt that no deliverance comes is the very darkness Job waited in — *when I waited for light, there came darkness* (Job 30:26) — the righteous sufferer's good hope met by evil, his trust held in the dark.
cards.s_text: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.
cards.t_text: For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.

cards.note: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:1). *Now therefore, my lord, as Yahuah (LORD) liveth, and as thy soul liveth, seeing Yahuah (LORD) hath withholden thee from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with thine own hand, now let thine enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.* (1 Samuel 25:26). Abigail met David on the road while he was riding to shed Nabal's blood, and she told him plainly that Yahuah (LORD) had held him back from avenging himself with his own hand. Sirach says why that mattered: the man who takes his own vengeance finds vengeance from Yahuah (God), and his sins are kept in remembrance. David was one hour from writing that sentence against himself, and a wise woman turned him from it. He blessed her for it, and Nabal died by the hand of Yahuah (God) ten days later without David lifting a finger.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, my lord, as Yahuah (LORD) lives, and as your soul lives, seeing Yahuah (LORD) has withholden you from coming to shed blood, and from avenging thyself with your own hand, now let your enemies, and they that seek evil to my lord, be as Nabal.
cards.t_text: He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God), and he will surely keep his sins in remembrance.

cards.note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest* (Ecclesiasticus 28:2). The advice David blesses — *which hast kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with mine own hand* (1 Samuel 25:33) — is the wisdom of Sirach made flesh: release the wrong, and you are released. Abigail's counsel is mercy that frees the giver no less than the spared.
cards.s_text: And blessed be your advice, and blessed be you, which have kept me this day from coming to shed blood, and from avenging myself with my own hand.
cards.t_text: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.

cards.note: *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double* (Ecclesiasticus 26:1). Nabal had *a woman of good understanding* (1 Samuel 25:3) and squandered her; David received her and was blessed. Sirach names the gift the churl despised: the virtuous wife who lengthens her husband's days — the very life Nabal forfeited and David gained.
cards.s_text: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
cards.t_text: Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.

cards.note: *The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fatten his bones* (Ecclesiasticus 26:13). Abigail's discretion is the whole engine of the chapter — *a woman of good understanding* (1 Samuel 25:3) whose quiet wisdom *kept me this day from coming to shed blood* (1 Samuel 25:33). Sirach names the grace she carried: the discreet wife whose understanding is the strength of the house.
cards.s_text: Now the name of the man was Nabal; and the name of his wife Abigail: and she was a woman of good understanding, and of a beautiful countenance: but the man was churlish and evil in his doings; and he was of the house of Caleb.
cards.t_text: The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fatten his bones.

cards.note: *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another's beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.* (Sirach 9:8). The same wisdom Job swore by — *why then should I think upon a maid?* (Job 31:1) — and the same fire-image Job uses two verses on, naming lust *a fire that consumeth to destruction* (Job 31:12). Turn the eye away before the fire is kindled.
cards.s_text: I made a covenant with my eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?
cards.t_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.

cards.note: *Whereas your servant works truly, entreat him not evil, nor the hireling that bestoweth himself wholly for you.* (Sirach 7:20). The wisdom of the fathers commands the same justice Job swore by — not to despise the manservant's cause: *If I did despise the cause of my manservant or of my maidservant, when they contended with me* (Job 31:13). The servant who labours truly is to be loved, never wronged.
cards.s_text: Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?
cards.t_text: Whereas your servant works truly, entreat him not evil, nor the hireling that bestoweth himself wholly for you.

cards.note: *Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms* (Tobit 4:16). Tobit's charge to his son is the very mercy Job swore by — *Or have eaten my morsel myself alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof* (Job 31:17); *If I have seen any perish for want of clothing* (Job 31:19). Bread to the hungry, garment to the naked: the Torah's mercy enacted.
cards.s_text: If I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or any poor without covering;
cards.t_text: Give of your bread to the hungry, and of your garments to them that are naked; and according to your abundance give alms: and let not your eye be envious, when you give alms.

cards.note: *But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world.* (Wisdom of Solomon 13:2). The folly Job stood clear of — to make *the lights of heaven* into gods — is the folly he names a judge-worthy iniquity: *If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness... This also were an iniquity to be punished by the judge: for I should have denied the Elohim (God) that is above* (Job 31:26,28).
cards.s_text: If I beheld the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in brightness;
cards.t_text: But deemed either fire, or wind, or the swift air, or the circle of the stars, or the violent water, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world.

cards.note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:7). Solomon embodies Job 32:8 — he did not grow wise by years but *prayed, and understanding was given* him; *the spirit of wisdom came* by calling on Yahuah, the very inspiration of the Almighty.
cards.s_text: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty gives them understanding.
cards.t_text: Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.

cards.note: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:1). Ben Sira opens his whole book on Elihu's premise: *the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding* (Job 32:8) — *all wisdom comes from Yahuah*. Age cannot manufacture what is *with him for ever* and given out of His breath.
cards.s_text: But there is a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty gives them understanding.
cards.t_text: All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever.

cards.note: *I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.* (Tobit 12:15) The restored library gives a picture of Elihu's *messenger... an interpreter, one among a thousand* (Job 33:23) — the angel who carries a man's prayers before the glory. It illuminates the office of intercession that Job 33 anticipates, fulfilled at last not by an angel but by the one Mediator who *render[s] unto man his righteousness* (Job 33:26).
cards.s_text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:
cards.t_text: I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels, which present the prayers of the saints, and which go in and out before the glory of the Holy One.

cards.note: 'But to Leviathan you gavest the seventh part, namely, the moist; and have kept him to be devoured of whom you will, and when' (2 Esdras 6:52). The great creature is reserved at the Maker's pleasure — exactly the sovereignty of Job 40:19, 'he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him': the Creator masters what no man can subdue.
cards.s_text: He is the chief of the ways of Elohim (God): he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.
cards.t_text: But to Leviathan you gavest the seventh part, namely, the moist; and have kept him to be devoured of whom you will, and when.

cards.note: The restored witness keeps Leviathan reserved for the Creator's judgment: *But to Leviathan you gavest the seventh part, namely, the moist; and have kept him to be devoured of whom you will, and when* (2 Esdras 6:52). The proud monster (Job 41:34, *a king over all the children of pride*) is held in hand against the appointed day — devoured at Yahuah's (God's) will, never man's.
cards.s_text: He beholds all high things: he is a king over all the children of pride.
cards.t_text: But to Leviathan you gavest the seventh part, namely, the moist; and have kept him to be devoured of whom you will, and when.

cards.note: *But seek ye first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you* (Matthew 6:33). The Messiah reorders desire exactly as Yahuah reorders Baruch's — *And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not* (Jeremiah 45:5). Seek not great things for self, but the kingdom and his righteousness; what is needful is added, while the grasping after greatness is laid down.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: But seek you first the kingdom of Elohim (God), and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

cards.note: *For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it* (Matthew 16:25). Baruch is given his life *for a prey* — snatched bare from the ruin — not as a possession to be grasped (Jeremiah 45:5). The Messiah names the law of it: the life clutched is lost, the life surrendered is found. He who seeks not great things for himself receives his life as a gift, not a prize.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

cards.note: *Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content* (Philippians 4:11). Paul learned the contentment Baruch is taught — to seek not great things for himself (Jeremiah 45:5) but to be content in whatsoever state. Abased or abounding, the heart that has let go of grasping rests in what Yahuah gives, even when it is only bare life preserved.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

cards.note: *But godliness with contentment is great gain* (1 Timothy 6:6). The great thing Baruch is told NOT to seek (Jeremiah 45:5) is answered by the great gain Paul names: not riches nor station, but godliness with contentment. To seek not great things for self is not loss but the true gain — the heart that needs nothing beyond what Yahuah grants.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.

cards.note: *And having food and raiment let us be therewith content* (1 Timothy 6:8). Baruch's reward is his life *for a prey in all places whither thou goest* (Jeremiah 45:5) — the bare necessity spared, and it is enough. Paul draws the same line: food and raiment, and therewith content. The one who seeks not great things for himself is satisfied with the little that sustains life.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.

cards.note: *And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth* (Luke 12:15). The Messiah strikes at the very thing Baruch is warned against — *seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not* (Jeremiah 45:5). Life is not measured by abundance of possessions; the soul that grasps after great things has mistaken what life is. The life given *for a prey* is life indeed.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

cards.note: *Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity* (Ecclesiastes 1:2). Baruch faints and finds no rest — *Woe is me now!... I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest* (Jeremiah 45:3). The Preacher names the reason the grasping after great things finds no rest: all of it is vanity, a chasing after wind. The cure is not more of what cannot satisfy, but contentment with the bare life Yahuah preserves.
cards.s_text: You did say, Woe is me now! for Yahuah (LORD) has added grief to my sorrow; I fainted in my sighing, and I find no rest.
cards.t_text: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.

cards.note: *And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) hath taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD)* (Job 1:21). Job receives both the gift and the stripping with blessing, grasping at nothing — the very posture Baruch is called to when told *seek them not* and given only his life *for a prey* (Jeremiah 45:5). What Yahuah gives is enough; what he takes was never ours to clutch.
cards.s_text: And seek you great things for thyself? seek them not: for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, says Yahuah (LORD): but your life will I give unto you for a prey in all places whither you go.
cards.t_text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) has taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.* (Baruch 2:34). Baruch confesses the exile and then pleads the Deut 30 promise — bringing again *into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers* and increasing them — exactly Moses' *bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed ... and multiply thee above thy fathers* (Deuteronomy 30:5).
cards.s_text: And Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it; and he will do you good, and multiply you above your fathers.
cards.t_text: And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.

cards.note: *All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:11). The added riches follow the wisdom, never the other way — *And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour* (1 Kings 3:13). Seek her first, and all good things come trailing after.
cards.s_text: And I have also given you that which you have not asked, both riches, and honour: so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto you all your days.
cards.t_text: All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.

cards.note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). Solomon's own first-person account confesses the choice Yahuah commends — *thou hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment* (1 Kings 3:11).
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) said unto him, Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked for thyself long life; neither have asked riches for thyself, nor have asked the life of your enemies; but have asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;
cards.t_text: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.

cards.note: *for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Matthew 12:42). *And Solomon's wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt* (1 Kings 4:30) — his fame *was in all nations round about* (1 Kings 4:31). That wisdom which surpassed every nation is the foreshadow; the greater than Solomon is the substance.
cards.s_text: And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east country, and all the wisdom of Egypt.
cards.t_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

cards.note: *The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Matthew 12:42). The very scene of 1 Kings — *there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth* (1 Kings 4:34) — Yahusha (Jesus) names as a witness against his generation: the nations came for Solomon's wisdom; here stands the greater Son in whom that wisdom dwells.
cards.s_text: And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom.
cards.t_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

cards.note: *Yea, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him* (Psalms 72:11). 1 Kings shows the firstfruits: *there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth* (1 Kings 4:34). The kings of the earth drawn to Solomon are a token of the psalm's word that *all nations shall serve him* — the nations gathered to the Son of David.
cards.s_text: And there came of all people to hear the wisdom of Solomon, from all kings of the earth, which had heard of his wisdom.
cards.t_text: Yea, all kings shall fall down before him: all nations shall serve him.

cards.note: *You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:8). Wisdom puts into Solomon's mouth the very theology of his dedication prayer: the temple is *a resemblance of the holy tabernacle* — an earthly likeness of the heavenly pattern, not a container for the uncontainable. So Solomon marvels, *the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded?* (1 Kings 8:27). The house is a shadow of the true dwelling Yahuah prepared from the beginning.
cards.s_text: But will Elohim (God) indeed dwell on the earth? behold, the heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have builded?
cards.t_text: You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning.

cards.note: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). Tobit sings what Solomon prayed: *that all people of the earth may know thy name* (1 Kings 8:43). The far country of Solomon's stranger becomes the *many nations... from far* who come to the Name — not Israel replaced, but the Name carried out and the nations drawn in to praise the King of heaven.
cards.s_text: Hear you in heaven your dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calls to you for: that all people of the earth may know your name, to fear you, as do your people Yashar'el (Israel); and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by your name.
cards.t_text: Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven; all generations shall praise you with great joy.

cards.note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols* (Tobit 14:6). The end of Solomon's petition — *that all people of the earth may know thy name, to fear thee* (1 Kings 8:43) — is Tobit's hope: all nations turning, fearing Yahuah, casting away their idols. The Name made known is not a tolerance of idols but their burial; the nations come to fear the one true El.
cards.s_text: Hear you in heaven your dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calls to you for: that all people of the earth may know your name, to fear you, as do your people Yashar'el (Israel); and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by your name.
cards.t_text: And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.

cards.note: *So shall all nations praise Yahuah (God), and his people shall confess Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) shall exalt his people; and all those which love Yahuah (God) in truth and justice shall rejoice* (Tobit 14:7). Solomon's stranger comes *that all people of the earth may know thy name* (1 Kings 8:43) — and Tobit completes the picture: the nations praise while *his people* are confessed and exalted. The ingathering of the stranger does not displace the people; both rejoice, those who love Yahuah in truth and justice.
cards.s_text: Hear you in heaven your dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calls to you for: that all people of the earth may know your name, to fear you, as do your people Yashar'el (Israel); and that they may know that this house, which I have builded, is called by your name.
cards.t_text: So shall all nations praise Yahuah (God), and his people shall confess Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) shall exalt his people; and all those which love Yahuah (God) in truth and justice shall rejoice, shewing mercy to our brothers.

cards.note: *For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves* (Baruch 2:30). Baruch echoes Solomon almost word for word — *yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives* (1 Kings 8:47). The *remember themselves* of Baruch is the *bethink themselves* of the dedication prayer: the first stirring of repentance in the land of exile.
cards.s_text: Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto you in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness;
cards.t_text: For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.

cards.note: *And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished* (Baruch 2:34). The return Solomon prays toward — *pray unto thee toward their land, which thou gavest unto their fathers* (1 Kings 8:48) — is the oath-bound regathering: brought again into the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The seed of promise, the paternal covenant line, gathered home and increased, no more diminished.
cards.s_text: And so return unto you with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, which led them away captive, and pray unto you toward their land, which you gave unto their fathers, the city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built for your name:
cards.t_text: And I will bring them again into the land which I promised with an oath to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and they shall be lords of it: and I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished.

cards.note: *The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Luke 11:31). The seeking heart of the queen — who *came to prove him with hard questions* (1 Kings 10:1) — judges the unseeking generation; the one who sought the lesser wisdom condemns those who spurn the greater.
cards.s_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Yahuah (LORD), she came to prove him with hard questions.
cards.t_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

cards.note: *The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Matthew 12:42). The Formed Son reads the queen of 1 Kings 10:1 forward: she crossed the uttermost parts to seek the wisdom *concerning the name of Yahuah (LORD)*, and so she rises to condemn those who ignore the greater Son standing before them.
cards.s_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of Yahuah (LORD), she came to prove him with hard questions.
cards.t_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

cards.note: *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp* (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus 48:1). Ben Sira's hymn to the fathers opens its Elijah praise on the very man of 1 Kings 17:1 -- the prophet who *stood* before Yahuah, whose *word* is the engine of the whole chapter, fire and lamp against the Baal of Ahab's house.
cards.s_text: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
cards.t_text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.

cards.note: *By the word of Yahuah (God) he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire* (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus 48:3). Second-Temple memory reads 1 Kings 17:1 with the right grammar: it was *by the word of Yahuah* that the heaven was shut -- Elijah's *according to my word* is Yahuah's word in the prophet's mouth, never the prophet exalting himself.
cards.s_text: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) lives, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
cards.t_text: By the word of Yahuah (God) he shut up the heaven, and also three times brought down fire.

cards.note: *Who did raise up a dead man from death, and his soul from the place of the dead, by the word of the Most High* (Sirach/Ecclesiasticus 48:5). Ben Sira remembers Zarephath: it was *by the word of the Most High* that Elijah raised the dead, the very confession the widow makes -- *the word of Yahuah (LORD) in thy mouth is truth* (1 Kings 17:24). The raising was Yahuah's, wrought through His prophet's word.
cards.s_text: And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that you are a man of Elohim (God), and that the word of Yahuah (LORD) in your mouth is truth.
cards.t_text: Who did raise up a dead man from death, and his soul from the place of the dead, by the word of the Most High:

cards.note: *Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit* (Ecclesiasticus 48:12). The same testimony the sons of the prophets give — *The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha* (2 Kings 2:15) — the succession of the prophetic Spirit named in the second-temple memory.
cards.s_text: And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah does rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.
cards.t_text: Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit: while he lived, he was not moved with the presence of any prince, neither could any bring him into subjection.

cards.note: *Who was taken up in a whirlwind of fire, and in a chariot of fiery horses* (Ecclesiasticus 48:9). The second-temple witness reads 2 Kings 2 exactly as the text gives it — *there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire... and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven* (2 Kings 2:11) — preserving the memory of the prophet translated, not buried.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
cards.t_text: Who was taken up in a whirlwind of fire, and in a chariot of fiery horses:

cards.note: *And when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.* (2 Kings 13:21). Ben Sira praises this very wonder: *No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:13) — Eliseus' (Elisha's) corpse still bearing the power of Yahuah, a witness in the second-temple library to the prophet whose bones gave life.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass, as they were burying a man, that, behold, they spied a band of men; and they cast the man into the sepulchre of Elisha: and when the man was let down, and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
cards.t_text: No word could overcome him; and after his death his body prophesied.

cards.note: *And Elisha died, and they buried him.* (2 Kings 13:20) — yet his grave was no end. *He did wonders in his life, and at his death were his works marvellous.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:14). The wonders did not cease at his burial; the dead man raised at his bones is the marvellous work wrought even in death.
cards.s_text: And Elisha died, and they buried him. And the bands of the Moabites invaded the land at the coming in of the year.
cards.t_text: He did wonders in his life, and at his death were his works marvellous.

cards.note: *For we are born at all adventure: and we shall be hereafter as though we had never been: for the breath in our nostrils is as smoke, and a little spark in the moving of our heart:* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:2). This is the ungodly's reasoning that Qoheleth voices to overturn it — life as mere *breath in our nostrils... as smoke*, the hevel of *all is vanity* (Ecclesiastes 1:2). The book of Wisdom answers it; so does the Preacher's conclusion in the fear of Elohim.
cards.s_text: Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity.
cards.t_text: For we are born at all adventure: and we shall be hereafter as though we had never been: for the breath in our nostrils is as smoke, and a little spark in the moving of our heart:

cards.note: *And our name shall be forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud...* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:4). The ungodly dread exactly what Qoheleth observes: *There is no remembrance of former things* (Ecclesiastes 1:11), the *name... forgotten in time.* Within the closed horizon this is despair; it is undone only by the One who remembers and makes all things new.
cards.s_text: The thing that has been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.
cards.t_text: And our name shall be forgotten in time, and no man shall have our works in remembrance, and our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud, and shall be dispersed as a mist, that is driven away with the beams of the sun, and overcome with the heat thereof.

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:14). Sirach, the wisdom-book that walks beside Ecclesiastes, names the cure for *much wisdom is much grief* (Ecclesiastes 1:18): *to fear Yahuah... is the beginning of wisdom.* The grief is the wisdom that forgot its beginning.
cards.s_text: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven: this sore travail has Elohim (God) given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: 'Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die' (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). Ben Sira sets the heaper-up beside Qoheleth: 'I hated all my labour... because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me' (Ecclesiastes 2:18) — and this same wisdom-saying stands behind the rich fool of Luke 12:19-20.
cards.s_text: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
cards.t_text: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die.

cards.note: 'There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward' (Ecclesiasticus 11:18). The wealth scraped together by anxious pinching is the 'portion' that must be left behind — exactly Qoheleth's 'great evil,' that the labourer 'shall leave it unto the man that shall be after me. And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool?' (Ecclesiastes 2:18-19,21).
cards.s_text: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me.
cards.t_text: There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:

cards.note: *By the knowledge of Yahuah (God) they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 33:8). The wisdom-tradition heir of Qoheleth roots the seasons in the appointed times themselves — the Hand that ordered *a time to plant, and a time to pluck up* (Ecclesiastes 3:2) is the Hand that set the feasts of Leviticus 23; the rhythm of providence and the calendar of Yahuah (LORD) are one.
cards.s_text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
cards.t_text: By the knowledge of Yahuah (God) they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.

cards.note: *He has garnished the excellent works of his wisdom, and he is from everlasting to everlasting: to him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he has no need of any counsellor* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 42:21). Ben Sira hears Qoheleth and answers him almost verbatim: *nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it* (Ecclesiastes 3:14) — the second-Temple wisdom tradition confessing the immutable, everlasting work of Elohim (God).
cards.s_text: I know that, whatsoever Elohim (God) does, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and Elohim (God) does it, that men should fear before him.
cards.t_text: He has garnished the excellent works of his wisdom, and he is from everlasting to everlasting: to him may nothing be added, neither can he be diminished, and he has no need of any counsellor.

cards.note: *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 6:16). The threefold cord is *not quickly broken* (Ecclesiastes 4:12) because the faithful friend is *the medicine of life* — and the wisdom tradition binds even this to the covenant: *they that fear Yahuah shall find him*. The companionship of Ecclesiastes 4 is Genesis 2:18's good, found by those who fear Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
cards.t_text: A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him.

cards.note: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 6:14). Ben Sira draws out the very strength the Preacher praises — *if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him* (Ecclesiastes 4:12): the faithful friend is *a strong defence*, the second hand that lifts the fallen, the treasure the solitary toiler of verse 8 never gained.
cards.s_text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
cards.t_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.

cards.note: *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof* (Ecclesiasticus 31:5). Ben Sira sets the lover of gold beside Qoheleth's lover of silver — *He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver* (Ecclesiastes 5:10): the love of gold cannot justify, and the one who follows it follows corruption.
cards.s_text: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loves abundance with increase: this is also vanity.
cards.t_text: He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.

cards.note: *Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified* (Ecclesiasticus 18:22). Ben Sira, the wisdom-witness nearest Qoheleth, echoes him almost word for word — *defer not to pay it* (Ecclesiastes 5:4): the vow paid in due time, never deferred, never left as a debt at death.
cards.s_text: When you vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay that which you have vowed.
cards.t_text: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.

cards.note: *A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul* (Sirach 14:9). Ben Sira diagnoses the same unfilled mouth: the covetous eye *is not satisfied with his portion*, just as *the appetite is not filled*. The craving does not rest the soul; it *drieth up his soul*.
cards.s_text: All the labour of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
cards.t_text: A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; and the iniquity of the wicked drieth up his soul.

cards.note: *He that gathers by defrauding his own soul gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously* (Sirach 14:4). Ben Sira reads the same evil the Preacher names: the hoarder who *wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth* yet has no power to eat thereof gathers only *for others* — *a stranger eateth it*. The next breath of Sirach seals it: *he shall not take pleasure in his goods* (14:5).
cards.s_text: A man to whom Elohim (God) has given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet Elohim (God) gives him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eats it: this is vanity, and it is an evil disease.
cards.t_text: He that gathers by defrauding his own soul gathers for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.

cards.note: *Whatsoever you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amiss.* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 7:36). Ben Sira distills the chapter: *Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit* (Ecclesiastes 7:8) — the wise keep the end in view, and so the house of mourning makes the heart better than the house of mirth.
cards.s_text: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: and the patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit.
cards.t_text: Whatsoever you take in hand, remember the end, and you shall never do amiss.

cards.note: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 1:14). The preacher warns against self-righteous excess and against wickedness alike, then names the one axis that escapes both: *for he that feareth Elohim (God) shall come forth of them all* (Ecclesiastes 7:18). Ben Sira places that fear where all wisdom begins — not lukewarm compromise but the reverence that holds the soul true.
cards.s_text: It is good that you should take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not your hand: for he that fears Elohim (God) shall come forth of them all.
cards.t_text: To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb.

cards.note: *For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.* (The Wisdom of Solomon 2:23). *Elohim (God) hath made man upright* (Ecclesiastes 7:29) — created in the image, made for eternity; the upright forming is exactly what the Wisdom of Solomon confesses before naming what undid it.
cards.s_text: Lo, this only have I found, that Elohim (God) has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (God) created man to be immortal, and made him to be an image of his own eternity.

cards.note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (The Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *But they have sought out many inventions* (Ecclesiastes 7:29) — the Wisdom of Solomon names the first invention sought, the envy of the serpent that brought death upon the upright creation (Genesis 3).
cards.s_text: Lo, this only have I found, that Elohim (God) has made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
cards.t_text: Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.

cards.note: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). The restored wisdom library says it almost word for word: where Qoheleth observes *the righteous... are in the hand of Elohim (God)* (Ecclesiastes 9:1), Wisdom presses past the under-the-sun horizon — *in the sight of the unwise they seemed to die... but they are in peace* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:2-3).
cards.s_text: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of Elohim (God): no man knows either love or hatred by all that is before them.
cards.t_text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.

cards.note: *A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 20:7). Ben Sira sets the wise tongue against the fool's exactly as Qoheleth does in *The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself* (Ecclesiastes 10:12) — the babbler of Ecclesiastes 10:11 is the very fool who *will regard no time*.
cards.s_text: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
cards.t_text: A wise man will hold his tongue till he see opportunity: but a babbler and a fool will regard no time.

cards.note: *Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 27:26). Ben Sira repeats Qoheleth's *He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it* (Ecclesiastes 10:8) almost verbatim — the restored wisdom witness confirms that the recoil of the evil deed was settled doctrine in Yashar'el (Israel)'s sages, the same creation-justice the apostles preach.
cards.s_text: He that digs a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaks an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
cards.t_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall in it: and he that sets a trap shall be taken in it.

cards.note: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). The same 2nd-Temple wisdom fusion as Ecclesiastes 12:13 — *Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments* — wisdom is not found apart from commandment-keeping; the fear of Yahuah and the keeping of his Torah are the one path to her.
cards.s_text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
cards.t_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.

cards.note: *For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words shall come to Yahuah (God) for the manifestation of his wicked deeds* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:9). The same library voice as Ecclesiastes 12:14 — *with every secret thing* — the hidden counsels searched out and the secret deeds manifested before Yahuah.
cards.s_text: For Elohim (God) shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.
cards.t_text: For inquisition shall be made into the counsels of the ungodly: and the sound of his words shall come to Yahuah (God) for the manifestation of his wicked deeds.

cards.note: *A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth* (Ecclesiastes 7:1). The bride says *thy name is as ointment poured forth* (Song of Solomon 1:3); the wisdom of Solomon weighs the two together — a name above ointment — so the Beloved's name, poured forth like fragrant oil, is the most precious thing, *therefore do the virgins love thee*.
cards.s_text: Because of the savour of your good ointments your name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love you.
cards.t_text: A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.

cards.note: *Yahuah (God) took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Sirach 47:11). Ben Sira remembers the covenant exactly — *I will stablish his throne for ever* (1 Chronicles 17:12) — a covenant of kings and a throne of glory given to David in Israel.
cards.s_text: He shall build me an house, and I will stablish his throne for ever.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (God) took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish... wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David* (Sirach 47:22). The covenant's mercy *his throne shall be established for evermore* (1 Chronicles 17:14) endures because Yahuah never leaves off His mercy — the root to David preserved, a remnant kept to Jacob.
cards.s_text: But I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom for ever: and his throne shall be established for evermore.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David.

cards.note: *David for being merciful possessed the throne of an everlasting kingdom* (1 Maccabees 2:57). Mattathias rehearses the fathers to his sons, and David's portion is named for what it is — *his throne shall be established for evermore* (1 Chronicles 17:14): the throne of an everlasting kingdom.
cards.s_text: But I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom for ever: and his throne shall be established for evermore.
cards.t_text: David for being merciful possessed the throne of an everlasting kingdom.

cards.note: *They brought also the priests' garments, and the firstfruits, and the tithes: and the Nazarites they stirred up, who had accomplished their days* (1 Maccabees 3:49). Centuries after Numbers, the Nazarite vow is still being kept and fulfilled in Yashar'el — the living testimony that *all the days of his separation he is holy unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Numbers 6:8) was never a dead letter.
cards.s_text: All the days of his separation he is holy unto Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: They brought also the priests’ garments, and the firstfruits, and the tithes: and the Nazarites they stirred up, who had accomplished their days.

cards.note: *Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for Yahuah (God) made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his name, and prepare his sanctuary for ever* (Sirach / Ecclesiasticus 47:13). Ben Sira reads the chronicler exactly: *a man of rest... I will give peace and quietness unto Yashar'el (Israel) in his days. He shall build an house for my name* (1 Chronicles 22:9-10). The rest given is the condition of the house being built — the man of peace builds the house of peace.
cards.s_text: Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of rest; and I will give him rest from all his enemies round about: for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness unto Yashar'el (Israel) in his days.
cards.t_text: Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for Yahuah (God) made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his name, and prepare his sanctuary for ever.

cards.note: *He set singers also before the altar, that by their voices they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs* (Sirach 47:9). The restored witness remembers exactly what this chapter records — David's establishing of the singers *who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals* (1 Chronicles 25:1): the appointed, daily, prophetic worship set in order at the altar.
cards.s_text: Moreover David and the captains of the host separated to the service of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals: and the number of the workmen according to their service was:
cards.t_text: He set singers also before the altar, that by their voices they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs.

cards.note: *for Yahuah (God) is witness of his reins, and a true beholder of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:6). The second-temple witness names the same heart-searching Elohim David sets before Solomon — *Yahuah (LORD) searcheth all hearts* (1 Chronicles 28:9); a beholder of the heart whom no doubled mind escapes.
cards.s_text: And you, Solomon my son, know you the Elohim (God) of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind: for Yahuah (LORD) searcheth all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts: if you seek him, he will be found of you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off for ever.
cards.t_text: For wisdom is a loving spirit; and will not acquit a blasphemer of his words: for Yahuah (God) is witness of his reins, and a true beholder of his heart, and a hearer of his tongue.

cards.note: *You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:8). The second-temple voice of Solomon names the house as a copy of the heavenly — fitting the pattern David handed him, *the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof... and of the place of the mercy seat* (1 Chronicles 28:11), the resemblance of what was prepared from the beginning.
cards.s_text: Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof, and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat,
cards.t_text: You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning.

cards.note: The congregation that *offered willingly* with great joy (1 Chronicles 29:9) keeps the counsel Ben Sira preserves: *In all your gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness* (Ecclesiasticus 35:9). The cheerful giver of 2 Corinthians 9:7 stands already in second-Temple Israel's wisdom.
cards.s_text: Then the people rejoiced, for that they offered willingly, because with perfect heart they offered willingly to Yahuah (LORD): and David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
cards.t_text: In all your gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness.

cards.note: David's rejoicing gift (1 Chronicles 29:9) answers Ben Sira's charge: *Give to the Most High according as he has enriched you; and as you have gotten, give with a cheerful eye* (Ecclesiasticus 35:10). We give back only out of what Yahuah first enriched us with — the same logic David confesses in 29:14.
cards.s_text: Then the people rejoiced, for that they offered willingly, because with perfect heart they offered willingly to Yahuah (LORD): and David the king also rejoiced with great joy.
cards.t_text: Give to the Most High according as he has enriched you; and as you have gotten, give with a cheerful eye.

cards.note: *David said, Blessed be thou, Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) our father, for ever and ever* (1 Chronicles 29:10). Tobit's prayer of rejoicing carries the same blessing into exile: *Blessed be Yahuah (God) that lives for ever, and blessed be his kingdom* (Tobit 13:1). The doxology that opens David's reign's close is the captive's confession too — Yahuah and his kingdom blessed for ever.
cards.s_text: Wherefore David blessed Yahuah (LORD) before all the congregation: and David said, Blessed be you, Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) our father, for ever and ever.
cards.t_text: Then Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing, and said, Blessed be Yahuah (God) that lives for ever, and blessed be his kingdom.

cards.note: Solomon's prayer for wisdom to judge the people (2 Chronicles 1:10) is unfolded in his own restored meditation: *You have chosen me to be a king of your people, and a judge of your sons and daughters* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:7). The throne is given for the sake of righteous judgment, not the king's own glory.
cards.s_text: Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this your people, that is so great?
cards.t_text: You have chosen me to be a king of your people, and a judge of your sons and daughters:

cards.note: When Solomon asks *who can judge this thy people, that is so great?* (2 Chronicles 1:10), the Wisdom of Solomon shows him pleading for the gift from above: *O send her out of your holy heavens, and from the throne of your glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing to you* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:10). Wisdom descends from Yahuah's throne to enable the shepherd-king's service.
cards.s_text: Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this your people, that is so great?
cards.t_text: O send her out of your holy heavens, and from the throne of your glory, that being present she may labour with me, that I may know what is pleasing to you.

cards.note: The whole aim of Solomon's request — *that I may go out and come in before this people* (2 Chronicles 1:10) — is voiced in his restored prayer: *So shall my works be acceptable, and then shall I judge your people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my father's seat* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:12). Wisdom is sought for the righteous judging of Yahuah's people.
cards.s_text: Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people: for who can judge this your people, that is so great?
cards.t_text: So shall my works be acceptable, and then shall I judge your people righteously, and be worthy to sit in my father’s seat.

cards.note: Solomon's choosing of wisdom over *riches, wealth, or honour* (2 Chronicles 1:11) is his own confession in the restored Wisdom of Solomon: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). The king weighed wisdom against every earthly treasure and chose wisdom.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) said to Solomon, Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches, wealth, or honour, nor the life of your enemies, neither yet have asked long life; but have asked wisdom and knowledge for thyself, that you may judge my people, over whom I have made you king:
cards.t_text: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.

cards.note: That the riches were *added* once wisdom was sought (2 Chronicles 1:12) is precisely Solomon's testimony: *All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:11). Wisdom came first and brought every other good in her train — the same order Yahuah honoured at Gibeon.
cards.s_text: Wisdom and knowledge is granted unto you; and I will give you riches, and wealth, and honour, such as none of the kings have had that have been before you, neither shall there any after you have the like.
cards.t_text: All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.

cards.note: Hiram marvels that Yahuah *hath given to David the king a wise son... that might build an house for Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 2:12); the son himself confesses the commission and its pattern: *You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount... a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:8). The wisdom given is wisdom to build by the appointed pattern.
cards.s_text: Huram said moreover, Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for Yahuah (LORD), and an house for his kingdom.
cards.t_text: You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning.

cards.note: Hiram blesses *Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that made heaven and earth* (2 Chronicles 2:12); the wisdom prayer addresses the same Maker: *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1). Even the king of Tyre, of the nations, confesses the Creator whom Solomon serves.
cards.s_text: Huram said moreover, Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for Yahuah (LORD), and an house for his kingdom.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,

cards.note: Solomon's own prayer in the wisdom tradition names the same charge: *You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:8). Where Solomon *determined to build an house for the name of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 2:1), the building is no innovation but a resemblance of the pattern Yahuah prepared from the beginning.
cards.s_text: And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of Yahuah (LORD), and an house for his kingdom.
cards.t_text: You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning.

cards.note: The queen who *came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 9:1) is the very sign the Messiah raises against his generation: *The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Matthew 12:42). The first of the nations drawn to the wisdom given the Davidic king becomes the witness against those who will not come to the greater Son of David.
cards.s_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
cards.t_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

cards.note: When the queen of Sheba *came to prove Solomon with hard questions* (2 Chronicles 9:1), she set the pattern the Messiah names: *The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here* (Luke 11:31). A foreign queen crossed the earth for Solomon's wisdom; how much more is owed to the King in whom that wisdom dwells without measure.
cards.s_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
cards.t_text: The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with the men of this generation, and condemn them: for she came from the utmost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.

cards.note: That a queen crossed the earth *to prove Solomon with hard questions* (2 Chronicles 9:1) is just what the restored praise of Solomon records of his reach: *The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations* (Ecclesiasticus 47:17). The nations marvelled at the wisdom Yahuah set in the king's heart.
cards.s_text: And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to prove Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great company, and camels that bare spices, and gold in abundance, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
cards.t_text: The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.

cards.note: That *all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom* (2 Chronicles 9:23) is sung in his restored praise: *Your name went far to the islands; and for your peace you were beloved* (Ecclesiasticus 47:16). The reach of the king's name to the ends of the earth is the fame the wisdom of Yahuah carried.
cards.s_text: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that Elohim (God) had put in his heart.
cards.t_text: Your name went far to the islands; and for your peace you were beloved.

cards.note: The kings who came *to hear his wisdom, that Elohim had put in his heart* (2 Chronicles 9:23) are the *countries* of the restored witness: *The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations* (Ecclesiasticus 47:17). The nations marvelled, drawn to the wisdom given the king — the very pull the greater Son of David inherits.
cards.s_text: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, that Elohim (God) had put in his heart.
cards.t_text: The countries marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.
