cards.note: The flood of gold *that came to Solomon in one year* (2 Chronicles 9:13) is exactly the order Solomon confesses in his restored meditation: *All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:11). The riches came WITH wisdom, in her train — the wealth follows the gift, it does not precede it.
cards.s_text: Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and threescore and six talents of gold;
cards.t_text: All good things together came to me with her, and innumerable riches in her hands.

cards.note: Though Solomon's vessels were all of gold and *silver was nothing accounted of in his days* (2 Chronicles 9:20), the king himself weighed it lightly: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). The gold that filled his house was nothing beside the wisdom that drew the nations.
cards.s_text: And all the drinking vessels of king Solomon were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold: none were of silver; it was not any thing accounted of in the days of Solomon.
cards.t_text: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.

cards.note: *Yahuah (God) took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Sirach 47:11). The second-Temple sage remembers David's grant exactly as Abijah does — *a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory... for ever* — the same perpetual Davidic settlement Abijah calls *a covenant of salt*.
cards.s_text: Ought you not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
cards.t_text: Yahuah (God) took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *According to the covenant made with David son of Jesse, of the tribe of Juda, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone* (Sirach 45:25). The sage couples the Davidic covenant with the priestly one — the very pairing in Abijah's speech (the throne in v.5, the Aaronic priests in v.10) — and like Abijah holds the kingly inheritance to David's *posterity alone*.
cards.s_text: Ought you not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
cards.t_text: According to the covenant made with David son of Jesse, of the tribe of Juda, that the inheritance of the king should be to his posterity alone: so the inheritance of Aaron should also be to his seed.

cards.note: *But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy... wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David* (Sirach 47:22). However the northern kingdom falls away, the *root to David* abides — the same indissoluble mercy Abijah leans on when he calls the throne *a covenant of salt* given *to David for ever*.
cards.s_text: Ought you not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Ecclesiasticus 2:10). The restored wisdom-witness puts the seek/forsake principle as a question that answers itself — none who truly sought were forsaken. It is the same promise as *if ye seek him, he will be found of you* (2 Chronicles 15:2), pressed home by the testimony of the generations of old.
cards.s_text: And he went out to meet Asa, and said unto him, Hear you me, Asa, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin; Yahuah (LORD) is with you, while you be with him; and if you seek him, he will be found of you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves* (Baruch 2:30). The restored witness traces the same arc — the desolation, then the remembering that begins the return. As *they in their trouble did turn unto Yahuah... and sought him, he was found of them* (2 Chronicles 15:4), so Baruch foresees the captive people remembering themselves, given a heart, and brought back.
cards.s_text: But when they in their trouble did turn unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and sought him, he was found of them.
cards.t_text: For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.

cards.note: *You that fear Yahuah (God), believe him; and your reward shall not fail* (Ecclesiasticus 2:8). The restored wisdom-witness sets the same promise beside the same call to courage. *Be ye strong... for your work shall be rewarded* (2 Chronicles 15:7) and *your reward shall not fail* are one assurance — the faithful who do not let their hands grow weak are never unrewarded.
cards.s_text: Be you strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.
cards.t_text: You that fear Yahuah (God), believe him; and your reward shall not fail.

cards.note: *He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician* (Sirach 38:15). The proverb is the exact shape of Asa's end: the king who had imprisoned the seer and oppressed the people, hardened against Yahuah, falls wholly *to the physicians* (2 Chronicles 16:12) with no recourse left to his Maker. The hand of the physician is no curse — but to fall into it ALONE, having forsaken Yahuah, is the judgment on the heart that departs.
cards.s_text: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians.
cards.t_text: He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician.

cards.note: *Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him* (Sirach 38:12). This guards the reading of Asa's sin: the physician is Yahuah's own creation, honourably consulted — the wrong is not seeking the physician but seeking him INSTEAD of Yahuah. Asa *sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians* (2 Chronicles 16:12); Sira would have him do both, in order, the heart turned first to its Maker.
cards.s_text: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians.
cards.t_text: Then give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him: let him not go from you, for you have need of him.

cards.note: *My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole* (Sirach 38:9). Ben Sira sets the order Asa inverted: in sickness, pray to Yahuah FIRST. Asa, *diseased in his feet... in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians* (2 Chronicles 16:12) — he was negligent of the prayer Sira commands, the same self-reliance that had hired Syria.
cards.s_text: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians.
cards.t_text: My son, in your sickness be not negligent: but pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.

cards.note: *Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?* (Sirach 2:10). Ben Sira appeals to the whole record of the fathers — including Asa's own earlier deliverance — to prove the rule Hanani states: Yahuah *shew[s] himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him* (2 Chronicles 16:9). None who trusted was ever confounded; Asa was confounded only when he stopped trusting.
cards.s_text: For the eyes of Yahuah (LORD) run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein you have done foolishly: therefore from henceforth you shall have wars.
cards.t_text: Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called upon him?

cards.note: *He gave to him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Yashar'el (Israel) in his laws.* (Ecclesiasticus 45:17) Ben Sira sets the teaching of the law at the heart of the priestly grant to Aaron — *that he should teach Jacob the testimonies* — the very office the Levites and priests of Jehoshaphat carry when they *had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them* (2 Chronicles 17:9).
cards.s_text: And they taught in Yahudah (Judah), and had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Yahudah (Judah), and taught the people.
cards.t_text: He gave to him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Yashar'el (Israel) in his laws.

cards.note: *An unwise king destroys his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.* (Ecclesiasticus/Sirach 10:3) Jehoram, *risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword* (2 Chronicles 21:4): the foolish king turning the sword on his own house, destroying the very princes of Yashar'el (Israel) given them by Jehoshaphat. The wisdom-tradition names the pattern — a king without the fear of Yahuah (LORD) is a devourer of his own people.
cards.s_text: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: An unwise king destroys his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.

cards.note: *But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David.* (Ecclesiasticus/Sirach 47:22) The wisdom-tradition states the very doctrine of 2 Chronicles 21:7 — Yahuah (LORD) *would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant*. He will not *abolish the posterity of his elect*; *a root to David* is kept, the lamp that buds into the Messiah.
cards.s_text: Howbeit Yahuah (LORD) would not destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he promised to give a light to him and to his sons for ever.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (God) will never leave off his mercy, neither shall any of his works perish, neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loves him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant to Jacob, and out of him a root to David.

cards.note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly* (Ecclesiasticus 10:13). Ben Sira gathers the whole lesson of Uzziah into a sentence — pride is *the beginning of sin*, and Yahuah *overthrew them utterly*. *When he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction* (2 Chronicles 26:16), and the destruction was a *strange calamity*: leprosy in the forehead of a king. The wisdom of the second-Temple sages reads the Chronicler exactly: the proud heart pours out abomination and is cast down.
cards.s_text: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
cards.t_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.

cards.note: *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands* (Ecclesiasticus 35:8). The Second-Temple wisdom keeps the same Torah measure Hezekiah's people met when they *brought in abundance the firstfruits* (2 Chronicles 31:5) — the firstfruits given whole, with a generous eye, not diminished or held back.
cards.s_text: And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly.
cards.t_text: Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye, and diminish not the firstfruits of yours hands.

cards.note: *In all your gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness* (Ecclesiasticus 35:9). The gladness of Hezekiah's givers, who *brought in abundance* and *laid them by heaps* (2 Chronicles 31:5-6), is the very spirit Sirach commends — tithes dedicated with gladness, the cheerful eye the apostle later names in *Elohim loveth a cheerful giver* (2 Corinthians 9:7).
cards.s_text: And Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answered him, and said, Since the people began to bring the offerings into the house of Yahuah (LORD), we have had enough to eat, and have left plenty: for Yahuah (LORD) has blessed his people; and that which is left is this great store.
cards.t_text: In all your gifts shew a cheerful countenance, and dedicate your tithes with gladness.

cards.note: *Now therefore I bow the knee of my heart, beseeching you of grace. I have sinned, O Yahuah (God), I have sinned, and I acknowledge my iniquities:* (Prayer of Manasseh 1:11–12). *And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that Yahuah (LORD) he was Elohim (God).* (2 Chronicles 33:13). The restored library preserves the very prayer attributed to him, and it goes on to call Yahuah (God) the God of them that repent. It is the inside of the humbling the Chronicler records — the bowed knee of the heart that the worst king found Yahuah (God) would not refuse.
cards.s_text: And prayed unto him: and he was intreated of him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that Yahuah (LORD) he was Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: Now therefore I bow the knee of my heart, beseeching you of grace.

cards.note: *And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem to his Elohim (God), and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month;* (1 Esdras 1:1). The restored Greek chronicle opens with the same scene, the same day — confirming the great passover *unto Yahuah (LORD) in Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 35:1) kept on the fourteenth exactly as Moses wrote.
cards.s_text: Moreover Josiah kept a passover unto Yahuah (LORD) in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
cards.t_text: And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem to his Elohim (God), and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month;

cards.note: *Offer the passover in order, and make ready the sacrifices for your brothers, and keep the passover according to the commandment of Yahuah (God), which was given to Moses.* (1 Esdras 1:6). 1 Esdras echoes Josiah's charge to do *according to the word of Yahuah (LORD) by the hand of Moses* (2 Chronicles 35:6) — the feast kept by the very commandment given to Moses, the Torah honoured to the letter.
cards.s_text: So kill the passover, and sanctify yourselves, and prepare your brethren, that they may do according to the word of Yahuah (LORD) by the hand of Moses.
cards.t_text: Offer the passover in order, and make ready the sacrifices for your brothers, and keep the passover according to the commandment of Yahuah (God), which was given to Moses.

cards.note: *And such a passover was not kept in Yashar'el (Israel) since the time of the prophet Samuel.* (1 Esdras 1:20). The restored witness agrees word for word with the chronicler: *there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet* (2 Chronicles 35:18) — the unrivalled feast remembered in both libraries.
cards.s_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: And such a passover was not kept in Yashar'el (Israel) since the time of the prophet Samuel.

cards.note: *The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary: it is sweet as honey in all mouths, and as musick at a banquet of wine.* (Ecclesiasticus 49:1). Ben Sira's praise of the fathers crowns Josiah's memory as sweet incense — the king of the great passover that *all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel)* could not match (2 Chronicles 35:18).
cards.s_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary: it is sweet as honey in all mouths, and as musick at a banquet of wine.

cards.note: *He directed his heart to Yahuah (God), and in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 49:3). The wisdom-praise names exactly what 2 Chronicles records: Josiah *set the priests in their charges, and encouraged them to the service of the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 35:2) — he re-established the true worship Yahuah commanded.
cards.s_text: And he set the priests in their charges, and encouraged them to the service of the house of Yahuah (LORD),
cards.t_text: He directed his heart to Yahuah (God), and in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *Now after all these acts of Josias it came to pass, that Pharaoh the king of Egypt came to raise war at Carchamis upon Euphrates: and Josias went out against him.* (1 Esdras 1:25). The restored chronicle tells it the same: after the great passover, *Necho king of Egypt came up to fight against Carchemish by Euphrates: and Josiah went out against him* (2 Chronicles 35:20) — the turn from the feast to the field.
cards.s_text: After all this, when Josiah had prepared the temple, Necho king of Egypt came up to fight against Carchemish by Euphrates: and Josiah went out against him.
cards.t_text: Now after all these acts of Josias it came to pass, that Pharaoh the king of Egypt came to raise war at Carchamis upon Euphrates: and Josias went out against him.

cards.note: *But joined battle with him in the plain of Magiddo, and the princes came against king Josias.* (1 Esdras 1:29). 1 Esdras names the same valley where Josiah, who *would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself... came to fight in the valley of Megiddo* (2 Chronicles 35:22), unheeding the word from the mouth of Elohim.
cards.s_text: Nevertheless Josiah would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself, that he might fight with him, and hearkened not unto the words of Necho from the mouth of Elohim (God), and came to fight in the valley of Megiddo.
cards.t_text: But joined battle with him in the plain of Magiddo, and the princes came against king Josias.

cards.note: *And in all Jewry they mourned for Josias, yes, Jeremy the prophet lamented for Josias, and the chief men with the women made lamentation for him to this day...* (1 Esdras 1:32). The restored witness preserves the very lament: *Jeremiah lamented for Josiah: and all the singing men and the singing women spake of Josiah in their lamentations* (2 Chronicles 35:25) — the prophet's grief for the good king carried in both records.
cards.s_text: And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah: and all the singing men and the singing women spake of Josiah in their lamentations to this day, and made them an ordinance in Yashar'el (Israel): and, behold, they are written in the lamentations.
cards.t_text: And in all Jewry they mourned for Josias, yes, Jeremy the prophet lamented for Josias, and the chief men with the women made lamentation for him to this day: and this was given out for an ordinance to be done continually in all the nation of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Also they held the feast of tabernacles, as it is commanded in the law, and offered sacrifices daily, as was meet* (1 Esdras 5:51). The restored Greek account of the same return witnesses the same fact in the same words — the feast of tabernacles kept *as it is commanded in the law*, exactly as Ezra 3:4 says *as it is written*. Two witnesses, one testimony: the appointed worship of Torah resumed first thing in the restoration.
cards.s_text: They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;
cards.t_text: Also they held the feast of tabernacles, as it is commanded in the law, and offered sacrifices daily, as was meet:

cards.note: *Also of the priests and Levites, and of the chief of their families, the ancients who had seen the former house came to the building of this with weeping and great crying* (1 Esdras 5:63). The restored Greek witness records the same mingled scene — *the ancients who had seen the former house... with weeping and great crying* against *many with trumpets and joy* (1 Esdras 5:64), so that *the trumpets might not be heard for the weeping* (1 Esdras 5:65). It confirms Ezra 3:12-13 detail for detail: the joy and the grief of the day of small things sounded as one.
cards.s_text: But many of the priests and Levites and chief of the fathers, who were ancient men, that had seen the first house, when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, wept with a loud voice; and many shouted aloud for joy:
cards.t_text: Also of the priests and Levites, and of the chief of their families, the ancients who had seen the former house came to the building of this with weeping and great crying.

cards.note: *And thus was the holy house finished in the three and twentieth day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of Darius king of the Persians* (1 Esdras 7:5). The restored library's own record of the same hour: *this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king* (Ezra 6:15). Two witnesses to the one finishing — the second-temple memory preserved that the house was completed in Darius's sixth year.
cards.s_text: And this house was finished on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
cards.t_text: And thus was the holy house finished in the three and twentieth day of the month Adar, in the sixth year of Darius king of the Persians

cards.note: *And to the dedication of the temple of Yahuah (God) they offered an hundred bullocks two hundred rams, four hundred lambs* (1 Esdras 7:7). The restored library preserves the same dedication, the same numbers: *an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Yashar'el (Israel), twelve he goats* (Ezra 6:17). The second-temple witness confirms the offering verse for verse.
cards.s_text: And offered at the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Yashar'el (Israel), twelve he goats, according to the number of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And to the dedication of the temple of Yahuah (God) they offered an hundred bullocks two hundred rams, four hundred lambs;

cards.note: *And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God), for that he had turned the counsel of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Esdras 7:14-15). The restored library's own account matches Ezra word for word: *kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them* (Ezra 6:22). Two witnesses to the joy of the restored feast.
cards.s_text: And kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of Elohim (God), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God),

cards.note: *But he that gives his mind to the law of the Most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies* (Ecclesiasticus 39:1). Ben Sira's portrait of the scribe — the man who gives his mind to *the law of the Most High* — is drawn from this very Ezra, *a ready scribe in the law of Moses* (Ezra 7:6): the office of the Torah-scribe held in honour in the second-Temple library.
cards.s_text: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) upon him.
cards.t_text: But he that gives his mind to the law of the Most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.

cards.note: *And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory* (2 Esdras 14:40). The Ezra-tradition itself remembers him as the one whose heart was filled to recover and write the law — the same ready scribe whom Yahuah's hand made fruitful in *the law of Moses* (Ezra 7:6).
cards.s_text: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) upon him.
cards.t_text: And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory:

cards.note: *He shall shew forth that which he has learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of Yahuah (God)* (Ecclesiasticus 39:8). Ben Sira's ideal scribe teaches only what he has first learned and lived, and his glory is *the law of the covenant* — the same fusion of doing and teaching grounded in the Torah that Ezra embodied when he *prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah, and to do it, and to teach* (Ezra 7:10).
cards.s_text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.
cards.t_text: He shall shew forth that which he has learned, and shall glory in the law of the covenant of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments* (Ecclesiasticus 29:1). The wisdom of the second-Temple house reads merciful lending as commandment-keeping itself — the very Torah Nehemiah enforces when he indicts those who *exact usury, every one of his brother* (Nehemiah 5:7).
cards.s_text: Then I consulted with myself, and I rebuked the nobles, and the rulers, and said unto them, You exact usury, every one of his brother. And I set a great assembly against them.
cards.t_text: He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.

cards.note: *The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood* (Ecclesiasticus 34:21). When the poor confess *we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants* (Nehemiah 5:5), the wisdom of the house declares that stripping the needy of their living is no small matter but bloodguilt.
cards.s_text: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.
cards.t_text: The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.

cards.note: *He that takes away his neighbour's living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). The mortgaged fields and enslaved children of Nehemiah 5:5 are precisely the neighbour's living taken away — the second-Temple house names it bloodshed, as Nehemiah's anger (Nehemiah 5:6) testifies.
cards.s_text: Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our brethren, our children as their children: and, lo, we bring into bondage our sons and our daughters to be servants, and some of our daughters are brought unto bondage already: neither is it in our power to redeem them; for other men have our lands and vineyards.
cards.t_text: He that takes away his neighbour’s living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.

cards.note: *And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory* (2 Esdras 14:40). The same Ezra-tradition: the restorer of the Word filled with understanding so the lost Scripture might be recovered — the heart of the Levites' work to *cause them to understand the reading* (Nehemiah 8:8).
cards.s_text: So they read in the book in the law of Elohim (God) distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
cards.t_text: And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory:

cards.note: *For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge* (2 Esdras 14:47). The recovered books are named the very spring of understanding — what Nehemiah's assembly drank when the Levites *gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading* (Nehemiah 8:8).
cards.s_text: So they read in the book in the law of Elohim (God) distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
cards.t_text: For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.

cards.note: *Let your mind be upon the ordinances of Yahuah (God) and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish yours heart, and give you wisdom at your owns desire* (Sirach 6:37). The joy that becomes the people's strength flows from the Word meditated and understood — the heart established and made glad by the commandments, not crushed by them.
cards.s_text: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be you sorry; for the joy of Yahuah (LORD) is your strength.
cards.t_text: Let your mind be upon the ordinances of Yahuah (God) and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish yours heart, and give you wisdom at your owns desire.

cards.note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels' food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). The restored witness names the manna the Levites confess — *withheldest not thy manna from their mouth* (Nehemiah 9:20) — as heaven's own bread.
cards.s_text: You gave also your good spirit to instruct them, and withheldest not your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.
cards.t_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.

cards.note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:26). The manna and the *good spirit to instruct them* (Nehemiah 9:20) teach the same lesson Deuteronomy 8:3 taught — man lives by the word.
cards.s_text: You gave also your good spirit to instruct them, and withheldest not your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.
cards.t_text: That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.

cards.note: *Therefore is Yahuah (God) patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them* (Ecclesiasticus 18:11). The restored wisdom witnesses the same patience the Levites confess — *gracious and merciful, slow to anger... and forsookest them not* (Nehemiah 9:17).
cards.s_text: And refused to obey, neither were mindful of your wonders that you did among them; but hardened their necks, and in their rebellion appointed a captain to return to their bondage: but you are a Elohim (God) ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and forsookest them not.
cards.t_text: Therefore is Yahuah (God) patient with them, and poureth forth his mercy upon them.

cards.note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock* (Ecclesiasticus 18:13). Sirach names the very pattern of Nehemiah 9 — Yahuah reproves yet brings again, *not utterly* consuming (9:31), as a shepherd gathers the strayed.
cards.s_text: Nevertheless for your great mercies’ sake you did not utterly consume them, nor forsake them; for you are a gracious and merciful Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:39 — *For he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defendeth it; and he beateth and destroys them that come to hurt it.* The Greatest Elohim the priests implore to come and help is the same Defender who beat back every man that came to hurt His house — deliverance as the Father's mercy, not reward.
cards.s_text: And when the priests fell down in their sacred vestments imploring the Greatest Elohim (God) to come and help in time of need, and to avert the violence of the fierce aggressor, and when they filled the temple with lamentations and tears,
cards.t_text: For he that dwells in heaven has his eye on that place, and defendeth it; and he beateth and destroys them that come to hurt it.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:19 — *And the women, girt with sackcloth under their breasts, abounded in the streets, and the virgins that were kept in ran, some to the gates, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows.* The virgins and mothers pouring into the streets in 3 Macc 1:18 mirror the very uproar of the city when Heliodorus came.
cards.s_text: Virgins, who had been shut up within their chambers, came out with their mothers, scattering dust and ashes on their heads, and filling the streets with outcries.
cards.t_text: And the women, girt with sackcloth under their breasts, abounded in the streets, and the virgins that were kept in ran, some to the gates, and some to the walls, and others looked out of the windows.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:15 — *But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called to heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to be kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept.* The priests prostrate in their vestments and crying to heaven is the same response that met Heliodorus' assault on the temple.
cards.s_text: And when the priests fell down in their sacred vestments imploring the Greatest Elohim (God) to come and help in time of need, and to avert the violence of the fierce aggressor, and when they filled the temple with lamentations and tears,
cards.t_text: But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests’ vestments, called to heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to be kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept.

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 26:21 — *And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, being a leper; for he was cut off from the house of Yahuah (LORD): and Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.* He who would usurp the house is shut out of it forever — the just end of the trespass Ptolemy is set upon.
cards.s_text: He, in his hardened mood, insensible to all persuasion, was going onwards, with the view of carrying out this design.
cards.t_text: And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death, and dwelt in a several house, being a leper; for he was cut off from the house of Yahuah (LORD): and Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 26:19 — *Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of Yahuah (LORD), from beside the incense altar.* The presuming king is answered by Yahuah Himself, not by men — the fate the hardened Ptolemy is courting.
cards.s_text: He, in his hardened mood, insensible to all persuasion, was going onwards, with the view of carrying out this design.
cards.t_text: Then Uzziah was wroth, and had a censer in his hand to burn incense: and while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of Yahuah (LORD), from beside the incense altar.

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 26:18 — *And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto Yahuah (LORD), but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed; neither shall it be for thine honour from Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God).* As Azariah's priests withstood Uzziah, so the priests read the law and forbid Ptolemy the inner room.
cards.s_text: Then they read the law to him; but he persisted in obtruding himself, exclaiming, that he ought to be allowed: and saying, Be it that they were deprived of this honour, I ought not to be.
cards.t_text: And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto you, Uzziah, to burn incense unto Yahuah (LORD), but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for you have trespassed; neither shall it be for your honour from Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God).

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 26:16 — *But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense.* Uzziah's lifted-up heart is the pattern of Ptolemy's haughty, hardened design to force the sanctuary.
cards.s_text: The elders who surrounded the king strove in many ways to divert his haughty mind from the design which he had formed.
cards.t_text: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense.

cards.note: Ezekiel 44:7 — *In that ye have brought into my sanctuary strangers, uncircumcised in heart, and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to pollute it, even my house, when ye offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and they have broken my covenant because of all your abominations.* The king reasons from the open doors of heathen temples, but admitting the uncircumcised stranger is named here as the very pollution of Yahuah's house.
cards.s_text: And he put the question, Why, when he entered all temples, none of the priests who were present forbad him?
cards.t_text: In that you have brought into my sanctuary strangers, uncircumcised in heart, and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in my sanctuary, to pollute it, even my house, when you offer my bread, the fat and the blood, and they have broken my covenant because of all your abominations.

cards.note: Ezekiel 44:9 — *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Ptolemy's demand to enter with or without consent runs straight into Yahuah's flat refusal of any stranger within the sanctuary.
cards.s_text: Well; since I have done this, said he, be the cause what it may, shall I not enter with or without your consent?
cards.t_text: Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 18:4 — *And they shall be joined unto thee, and keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, for all the service of the tabernacle: and a stranger shall not come nigh unto you.* When they read the law to Ptolemy (3 Macc 1:12), this is the word that barred him — the stranger comes not nigh.
cards.s_text: Then they read the law to him; but he persisted in obtruding himself, exclaiming, that he ought to be allowed: and saying, Be it that they were deprived of this honour, I ought not to be.
cards.t_text: And they shall be joined unto you, and keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, for all the service of the tabernacle: and a stranger shall not come nigh unto you.

cards.note: Numbers 18:3 — *And they shall keep thy charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, that neither they, nor ye also, die.* If even the ministering Levites die for nearing the holy vessels, a Greek king has no claim at all.
cards.s_text: And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
cards.t_text: And they shall keep your charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, that neither they, nor you also, die.

cards.note: *And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.* (3 Maccabees 1:11). *Therefore thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and ye shall serve: I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.* (Numbers 18:7). Ptolemy saw the temple, admired it, and decided he would walk into the sanctuary itself. The priests told him the rule: no one of the nation, not even the priests, only the high priest, and he only once a year. The king called that an honour he was being denied; the Torah calls it a death sentence for anyone else who comes near. Yahuah (God) gave the priesthood to Aaron and his sons as a gift, within the vail as well as at the altar, and said the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. The high priest's one entry a year on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:2) was not a privilege to be extended; it was the boundary Yahuah (God) set on his own dwelling, and Ptolemy was pressing against the boundary and its penalty.
cards.s_text: And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
cards.t_text: Therefore you and your sons with you shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and you shall serve: I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that comes nigh shall be put to death.

cards.note: Daniel 4:37 — *Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.* The King of heaven who abases the proud — the same hand that shook Ptolemy to and fro like a reed.
cards.s_text: Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech.
cards.t_text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:29 — *For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.* Cast down powerless and deprived of speech — the identical righteous judgment that paralyzed Ptolemy and silenced his boast.
cards.s_text: Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech.
cards.t_text: For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:26 — *Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.* The same scourging of a proud intruder at the holy place — Heliodorus then, Ptolemy now.
cards.s_text: At that time Elohim (God), who seeth all things, who is beyond all Holy among the holy, heard that prayer, so suitable; and scourged the man greatly uplifted with scorn and insolence.
cards.t_text: Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.

cards.note: Isaiah 37:16 — *O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: thou hast made heaven and earth.* The unapproachable dwelling-place, the heaven of heavens — the same Father whose throne is above the cherubim, against whom no king may presume.
cards.s_text: Thy dwelling-place, the heaven of heavens, is indeed unapproachable to men.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:19 — *Now therefore, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God), I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), even thou only.* The deliverance Simon seeks is for the Father's Name — that none may boast he trampled his house like an idol's.
cards.s_text: We have trampled upon the holy house, as idolatrous houses are trampled upon.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God), I beseech you, save you us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), even you only.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:15 — *And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.* Simon prays as Hezekiah prayed — appealing to the sole Creator against the lawless boaster who would trample the holy house.
cards.s_text: Punish us not by means of the uncleanness of their men, nor chastise us by means of their profanity; lest the lawless ones should boast in their rage, and exult in exuberant pride of speech, and say,
cards.t_text: And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: Daniel 4:34 — *And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the El Elyon (most High), and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation.* The Most High who blots out iniquity and restores — the One whose mercy Simon implores.
cards.s_text: Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and shew forth thy compassion in this hour.
cards.t_text: And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up my eyes unto heaven, and my understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the El Elyon (most High), and I praised and honoured him that lives for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:3 — *And they stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) one fourth part of the day; and another fourth part they confessed, and worshipped Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God).* Simon's plea is the same covenant posture — sin confessed at the holy place, the Father faithful to hear.
cards.s_text: And thou didst promise, out of love to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that should we fall away from thee, and become afflicted, and then come to this house and pray, thou wouldest hear our prayer.
cards.t_text: And they stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) one fourth part of the day; and another fourth part they confessed, and worshipped Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God).

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:11 — *And thou didst divide the sea before them, so that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; and their persecutors thou threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters.* Simon's rolling of the depths over the pursuer with his chariots, and the safe passage for those who trust — the same deliverance, the same Deliverer.
cards.s_text: And thou rolledst the depths of the sea over him, when he made pursuit with chariots, and with a multitude of followers, and gavest a safe passage to those who put their trust in thee, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation.
cards.t_text: And you did divide the sea before them, so that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; and their persecutors you threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:10 — *And shewedst signs and wonders upon Pharaoh, and on all his servants, and on all the people of his land: for thou knewest that they dealt proudly against them. So didst thou get thee a name, as it is this day.* The same bold Pharaoh, the enslaver who dealt proudly, brought low by the Father's hand.
cards.s_text: Thou didst make known thy power when thou causedst the bold Pharaoh, the enslaver of thy people, to pass through the ordeal of many and diverse inflictions.
cards.t_text: And shewedst signs and wonders upon Pharaoh, and on all his servants, and on all the people of his land: for you knew that they dealt proudly against them. So did you get you a name, as it is this day.

cards.note: Daniel 4:37 — *Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.* The righteous Governor who judges all who act with pride and insolence — the very lesson the humbled king learned.
cards.s_text: It is thou, the Creator of all, Yahuah (Lord) of the universe, who art a righteous Governor, and judgest all who act with pride and insolence.
cards.t_text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:6 — *Thou, even thou, art Yahuah (LORD) alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all things that are therein, the seas, and all that is therein, and thou preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth thee.* The same confession Simon makes — the one Creator-Father, King of the heavens, before whom the oppressor's strength is nothing.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord), King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who exulteth in his confidence and strength.
cards.t_text: You, even you, are Yahuah (LORD) alone; you have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all things that are therein, the seas, and all that is therein, and you preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth you.

cards.note: Exodus 1:10 — *Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.* Pharaoh's slander that the people are a disloyal danger in war is exactly Ptolemy's charge that they are *hostile to the king's interests* (3 Macc 3:7) and might *turn traitors* (3 Macc 3:24).
cards.s_text: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Yahudim (Jews) in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
cards.t_text: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falls out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.

cards.note: Exodus 1:9 — *And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:* Ptolemy's dread of the Yahudim is the first Pharaoh's dread — the king of Egypt who again turns on the seed dwelling in his land.
cards.s_text: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Yahudim (Jews) in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
cards.t_text: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:

cards.note: Daniel 3:28 — *Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).* The deliverance promised over the slandered seed of 3 Macc 3 is the deliverance already shown in the furnace — the Father sends his angel to those who will not bow.
cards.s_text: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Yahudim (Jews) with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them.
cards.t_text: Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).

cards.note: Daniel 3:12 — *There are certain Yahudim (Jews) whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.* As the three were charged for serving Elohim alone, so the Egyptian Yahudim are charged because *they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law* (3 Macc 3:4).
cards.s_text: yet, as they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium;
cards.t_text: There are certain Yahudim (Jews) whom you have set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded you: they serve not your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.

cards.note: Daniel 3:8 — *Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Yahudim (Jews).* The *invidious rumour... uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Yahudi race* (3 Macc 3:2) is the same malicious accusation the Chaldeans brought in Babylon.
cards.s_text: While this was going on, an invidious rumour was uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Yahudi (Jewish) race. The purport of their charge was, that the Yahudim (Jews) kept them away from the ordinances of the law.
cards.t_text: Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Yahudim (Jews).

cards.note: The Rest of Esther 13:6 — *Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:* The Greek text of Artaxerxes' decree matches 3 Macc 3:25 phrase for phrase — total destruction of the people *with wives and children*.
cards.s_text: As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Yahudim (Jews) who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected.
cards.t_text: Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:

cards.note: Esther 3:13 — *And the letters were sent by posts into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Yahudim (Jews), both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.* Ptolemy's letter to *destroy* with *wives and children* is the very decree of Esther 3:13 — the same extermination-edict, the same enemy.
cards.s_text: As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Yahudim (Jews) who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected.
cards.t_text: And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Yahudim (Jews), both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.

cards.note: Psalm 2:4 — *He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: Yahuah (Lord) shall have them in derision.* The king who thinks the people *lift up their heads against kings* (3 Macc 3:19) is himself the one held in derision by the enthroned Father.
cards.s_text: And thus, exhibiting their enmity against us, they alone among the nations lift up their heads against kings and benefactors, as men unwilling to submit to any thing reasonable.
cards.t_text: He that sits in the heavens shall laugh: Adonai (Lord) shall have them in derision.

cards.note: Psalm 2:2 — *The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,* The king who writes against Yahuah's people writes, in truth, against Yahuah and his Anointed.
cards.s_text: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of Elohim (God), but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,

cards.note: Psalm 2:1 — *Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?* Ptolemy's letter-writing rage against the Yahudim is the empty raging of the heathen against the covenant.
cards.s_text: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of Elohim (God), but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?

cards.note: The Rest of Esther 13:4 — *Declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings, so as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us cannot go forward.* The Greek decree of Artaxerxes frames the same accusation as 3 Macc 3:7 — a people whose laws set them apart is named an enemy of the realm.
cards.s_text: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Yahudim (Jews) with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them.
cards.t_text: Declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings, so as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us cannot go forward.

cards.note: Esther 3:8 — *And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king's laws: therefore it is not for the king's profit to suffer them.* Haman's slander is word-for-word the charge laid against the Yahudim of Egypt — Torah-fidelity read as disloyalty.
cards.s_text: yet, as they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium;
cards.t_text: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of your kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

cards.note: Psalm 44:23 — *Awake, why sleepest thou, O Yahuah (Lord)? arise, cast us not off for ever.* The apparent silence before heaven's interference in 3 Macc 4:21 matches the psalmist's plea against the Deliverer's seeming sleep.
cards.s_text: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
cards.t_text: Awake, why sleepest you, O Adonai (Lord)? arise, cast us not off for ever.

cards.note: Psalm 44:26 — *Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.* The unconquerable Providence that assists from heaven in 3 Macc 4:21 answers the cry to be redeemed for mercy's sake, not for merit.
cards.s_text: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
cards.t_text: Arise for our help, and redeem us for your mercies’ sake.

cards.note: Psalm 44:22 — *Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.* The registration of the whole nation for destruction in 3 Macc 4:17 is the covenant people counted as slaughter-sheep — yet, as here, not abandoned.
cards.s_text: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Yahudim (Jews) was too great for registration,
cards.t_text: Yea, for your sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

cards.note: Exodus 1:9 — *And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:* the king who herds the multitude to the hippodrome in 3 Macc 4:11 shares the first Pharaoh's dread of the multiplying people.
cards.s_text: They were conveyed accordingly in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces; nay, were deemed unworthy of any civilized accommodation.
cards.t_text: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:

cards.note: Exodus 1:13 — *And the Egyptians made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to serve with rigour:* the merciless treatment of 3 Macc 4:9 echoes Egypt's first rigour against the covenant seed.
cards.s_text: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
cards.t_text: And the Egyptians made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to serve with rigour:

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The chains and fetters of 3 Macc 4:9 are the bitter Egyptian bondage returning upon the same people.
cards.s_text: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:6 — *And he hath violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden: he hath destroyed his places of the assembly: Yahuah (LORD) hath caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and hath despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.* Feasting and jollity turned to wailing in 3 Macc 4:8 as the solemn joy of Zion was likewise forgotten.
cards.s_text: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand.
cards.t_text: And he has violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden: he has destroyed his places of the assembly: Yahuah (LORD) has caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and has despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:21 — *The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; thou hast slain them in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, and not pitied.* The young brides and bridegrooms hurried to misery in 3 Macc 4:6-8 match Zion's fallen virgins and young men.
cards.s_text: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled, and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn.
cards.t_text: The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; you have slain them in the day of your anger; you have killed, and not pitied.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:10 — *The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.* The streets filled with wailing in 3 Macc 4:3 echo the dust-strewn mourning of Zion's daughter.
cards.s_text: What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation?
cards.t_text: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

cards.note: Esther 4:1 — *When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;* the loud bitter cry of grief that fills 3 Macc 4:2-3 has its pattern in Mordecai's own.
cards.s_text: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
cards.t_text: When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;

cards.note: Esther 4:3 — *And in every province, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Yahudim (Jews), and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.* The identical mourning of the covenant people under a royal decree of destruction, ch4:2 in Egypt mirroring Persia.
cards.s_text: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
cards.t_text: And in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Yahudim (Jews), and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:20 — *Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.* The hands stretched out in mournful strains are heard by the same God who answered Hezekiah's prayer against the blasphemer.
cards.s_text: The Yahudim (Jews), breathless with momentary suspense, stretched forth their hands, and prayed the Greatest Elohim (God), in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.
cards.t_text: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), That which you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:34 — *For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake.* The Father overthrows the evil purpose for his own sake and for David's line, the same covenant ground on which Egypt's remnant casts its plea.
cards.s_text: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah (Lord), and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim (God) and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah (Lord) of every power,
cards.t_text: For I will defend this city, to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.

cards.note: Esther 6:1 — *On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.* The spirit of oblivion that empties this king's memory of his own decree mirrors the sleepless night that began Haman's undoing — providence governing a king's restless or clouded mind.
cards.s_text: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unwonted exit; and, overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, enquired the object of this earnest preparation.
cards.t_text: On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.

cards.note: Esther 6:1 — *On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.* As one king is kept from sleep to save the Yahudim, this king is sent into sleep to the same providential end — the small turning that overthrows the gallows and the hippodrome alike.
cards.s_text: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time, by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion thereof [now] upon the king.
cards.t_text: On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:31 — *The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of Yahuah (LORD).* Hermon may ready the elephants for the day of slaughter, but the safety of the covenant people rests with Yahuah, not the strength of the beasts.
cards.s_text: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
cards.t_text: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 21:30 — *There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD).* The king's repeated counsel to destroy keeps collapsing because no plotting can stand against the Father's purpose to deliver.
cards.s_text: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Yahudim (Jews). He swore a fruitless oath, and determined forthwith to send them to Hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.
cards.t_text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 21:1 — *The king's heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.* The king's unflinching resolve is held fast and turned aside by the hand that channels every royal will.
cards.s_text: By this sweet and profound influence of Yahuah (Lord) he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.
cards.t_text: The king’s heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turns it whithersoever he will.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:35 — *And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* Hermon's five hundred enraged beasts are no match for the One who alone can rout an army in a night.
cards.s_text: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: Exodus 14:28 — *And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.* The friends and army gathered to hate and destroy stand in the place of Pharaoh's vanished host.
cards.s_text: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Yahudim (Jews) the most.
cards.t_text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

cards.note: Exodus 14:27 — *And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.* The host massed for execution will, like Pharaoh's, be turned back upon itself in the morning.
cards.s_text: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine and handfuls of incense [infused] to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious draughts of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
