cards.note: Exodus 14:30 — *Thus Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Yashar'el (Israel) saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.* The cry for Yahuah to reveal himself at the gates of Hades looks for the same hand that once saved Israel out of Egypt's own grip.
cards.s_text: sent up an exceeding great cry, entreating Yahuah (Lord) of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of Hades.
cards.t_text: Thus Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Yashar'el (Israel) saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.

cards.note: Exodus 14:14 — *Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.* As they invoke the Almighty Yahuah and beseech the Lord of every power, the battle is the Father's, not the captives'.
cards.s_text: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah (Lord), and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim (God) and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah (Lord) of every power,
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.

cards.note: Exodus 14:13 — *And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.* Hemmed in by chains and beasts, the bound remnant of Egypt is set in the same posture Moses commanded at the sea — wait and watch for a salvation no hand of theirs can earn.
cards.s_text: The heathen believed the Yahudim (Jews) to be destitute of all protection; for chains fettered them about.
cards.t_text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear you not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom you have seen to day, you shall see them again no more for ever.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:26 — *Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.* The two angels of 3 Macc 6:18 echo the two manifest deliverers at the temple — it ain't new.
cards.s_text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:24 — *Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, Yahuah (God) of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.* The same Prince of all power who routed Heliodorus' guard opens heaven over Ptolemy's host (3 Macc 6:18).
cards.s_text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, Yahuah (God) of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.

cards.note: Psalms 34:7 — *The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.* The two dreadful angels of 3 Macc 6:18 are the standing promise of the angel-armies about the faithful.
cards.s_text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivers them.

cards.note: Jonah 2:10 — *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.* 'Recover him to the sight of his own' (3 Macc 6:8) — the deep gives Jonah back at the Deliverer's word.
cards.s_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

cards.note: Jonah 2:6 — *I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Yahuah (LORD) my Elohim (God).* The Father who 'looked upon him' (3 Macc 6:8) brought his life up from corruption.
cards.s_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
cards.t_text: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet have you brought up my life from corruption, O Yahuah (LORD) my Elohim (God).

cards.note: Jonah 2:1 — *Then Jonah prayed unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) out of the fish's belly,* The 'pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster' of 3 Macc 6:8 is Jonah's cry from the deep.
cards.s_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
cards.t_text: Then Jonah prayed unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) out of the fish’s belly,

cards.note: Daniel 6:22 — *My Elohim (God) hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.* Daniel 'hurled through slander and envy as a prey to lions' (3 Macc 6:7) was brought back unhurt by the sent angel.
cards.s_text: It was thou who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, didst bring him back again unhurt to light.
cards.t_text: My Elohim (God) has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before you, O king, have I done no hurt.

cards.note: Daniel 3:28 — *Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).* The three 'rather than serve vain things' (3 Macc 6:6) were delivered by the angel the Father sent.
cards.s_text: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.
cards.t_text: Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).

cards.note: Daniel 3:25 — *He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of Elohim (God).* The 'dewy coolness' of 3 Macc 6:6 is the presence of the Formed-Son in the furnace with the three.
cards.s_text: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.
cards.t_text: He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Isaiah 37:36 — *Then the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* Isaiah seals the same deliverance Eleazar pleads in 3 Macc 6:5 — the boaster against the holy city undone.
cards.s_text: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah (Lord), didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.
cards.t_text: Then the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:35 — *And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* The demolishing of Sennacherim (3 Macc 6:5) was wrought by one angel of the Father's hosts.
cards.s_text: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah (Lord), didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: Exodus 14:28 — *And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.* 'His proud army' overwhelmed (3 Macc 6:4) leaves not so much as one — the same Egypt twice undone.
cards.s_text: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.
cards.t_text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

cards.note: Exodus 14:27 — *And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.* The overthrow Eleazar rehearses in 3 Macc 6:4 is the very deed of the Sea.
cards.s_text: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

cards.note: Psalms 111:9 — *He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name.* The wonders wrought for their salvation in 3 Macc 7:22 are the sent redemption of the covenant Redeemer whose name is holy.
cards.s_text: Every man received back his own, according to inventory; those who had obtained their goods, giving them up with the greatest terror. For the greatest Elohim (God) wrought with perfectness wonders for their salvation.
cards.t_text: He sent redemption unto his people: he has commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:22 — *I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.* The Redeemer of Yashar'el is the one who redeems by blotting out sin and calling His people home, the salvation celebrated in 3 Macc 7:22-23.
cards.s_text: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) unto everlasting. Amen.
cards.t_text: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed you.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:6 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).* The Redeemer of Yashar'el blessed unto everlasting in 3 Macc 7:23 is the King and Redeemer who is the first and the last.
cards.s_text: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) unto everlasting. Amen.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).

cards.note: Exodus 12:14 — *And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.* The first memorial of deliverance out of Egypt stands behind the seven-day feast of deliverance kept at Ptolemais in 3 Macc 7:17.
cards.s_text: Having arrived at Ptolemais, called from the specialty of that district Rose-bearing, where the fleet, in accordance with the general wish, waited for them seven days,
cards.t_text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and you shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; you shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

cards.note: Esther 9:28 — *And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Yahudim (Jews), nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.* The deliverance registered as sacred on a pillar in 3 Macc 7:20 is the same kind of perpetual memorial the Jews ordained for Purim — a freely instituted remembrance, not a commanded feast of the law.
cards.s_text: These they registered as sacred upon a pillar, when they had dedicated the place of their festivity to be one of prayer. They departed unharmed, free, abundant in joy, preserved by the king's command, by land, by sea, and by river, each to his own home.
cards.t_text: And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Yahudim (Jews), nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

cards.note: Esther 9:22 — *As the days wherein the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.* The days of joyfulness kept in 3 Macc 7:19 mirror the Purim days of feasting and joy the people themselves appointed.
cards.s_text: They were accordingly brought back in peace, while they gave utterance to becoming thanks; and they determined to keep these days during their sojourn as days of joyfulness.
cards.t_text: As the days wherein the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

cards.note: Psalms 111:4 — *He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: Yahuah (LORD) is gracious and full of compassion.* The deliverance is set to song and remembrance precisely because His wonders are made to be remembered, as in 3 Macc 7:16.
cards.s_text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: He has made his wonderful works to be remembered: Yahuah (LORD) is gracious and full of compassion.

cards.note: Isaiah 49:7 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel), and his Holy One, to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of Yahuah (LORD) that is faithful, and the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), and he shall choose thee.* The Redeemer of Yashar'el — the same title sung in 3 Macc 7:16 and sealed in 7:23.
cards.s_text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel), and his Holy One, to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of Yahuah (LORD) that is faithful, and the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), and he shall choose you.

cards.note: Isaiah 49:26 — *And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I Yahuah (LORD) am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.* The eternal Saviour of Yashar'el whom they hymn in 3 Macc 7:16 is the one who repays the oppressor and redeems His own.
cards.s_text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And I will feed them that oppress you with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I Yahuah (LORD) am your Saviour and your Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.

cards.note: Esther 9:16 — *But the other Yahudim (Jews) that were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,* The same pattern of striking down the enemies and then having rest that closes the deliverance in 3 Macc 7:15-16.
cards.s_text: slaying thus, in that day, above three hundred men, and esteeming this destruction of the wicked a season of joy.
cards.t_text: But the other Yahudim (Jews) that were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

cards.note: Esther 9:2 — *The Yahudim (Jews) gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.* The same authorized self-defence of the covenant people that 3 Macc 7:10-12 grants against the apostates.
cards.s_text: When they had received this letter, they were not forward to depart immediately. They petitioned the king to be allowed to inflict fitting punishment upon those of their race who had willingly transgressed the holy Elohim (God), and the law of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: The Yahudim (Jews) gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.

cards.note: Esther 9:25 — *But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Yahudim (Jews), should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.* The evil designed against the covenant people falls back on its author, as Ptolemy warns it would in 3 Macc 7:9.
cards.s_text: For know ye, that should we conceive any evil design against, or in any manner aggrieve them, we shall ever have as our opposite, not man, but the highest Elohim (God), the ruler of all might. From Him there will be no escape, as the avenger of such deeds. Fare ye well.
cards.t_text: But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Yahudim (Jews), should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

cards.note: Esther 9:1 — *Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Yahudim (Jews) hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over them that hated them;)* The day appointed for destruction is turned to the contrary, exactly as the king's letter reverses his own decree in 3 Macc 7.
cards.s_text: King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders throughout Egypt, and to all who are set over affairs, joy and strength.
cards.t_text: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Yahudim (Jews) hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over them that hated them;)

cards.note: *But those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders. Now when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he shall defend his people that remain. And then shall he shew them great wonders.* (2 Esdras 13:48-50). The vision sets the wrath and the keeping in one hour: *he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together,* and in that same hour *he shall defend his people that remain.* So *Yahusha (Lord) himself shall descend from heaven with a shout* (1 Thessalonians 4:16) into the day of wrath on the gathered nations: the dead in Messiah (Christ) raised, and the living remnant defended while the wrath falls.
cards.s_text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of Elohim (God): and the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first:
cards.t_text: Now when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he shall defend his people that remain.

cards.note: *Whereas you have spoken of them that are left behind, this is the interpretation: He that shall endure the peril in that time has kept himself: they that be fallen into danger are such as have works, and faith toward the Almighty. Know this therefore, that they which be left behind are more blessed than they that be dead.* (2 Esdras 13:22-24). Paul speaks of the same company: *we which are alive and remain unto the coming of Yahusha (Lord)* (1 Thessalonians 4:15). Esdras is told that those *left behind* in that time are the ones who endured the peril and kept themselves, a people with *works, and faith toward the Almighty,* and that they *are more blessed than they that be dead.* To remain is not to be left out: the living remnant who endure to his coming are kept through the peril and gathered.
cards.s_text: For this we say unto you by the word of the Lord, that we which are alive and remain unto the coming of the Lord shall not prevent them which are asleep.
cards.t_text: Know this therefore, that they which be left behind are more blessed than they that be dead.

cards.note: *And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* (2 Esdras 7:30). *I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.* (Jeremiah 4:23). Esdras is told the world returns to the old silence for seven days, no man remaining. Jeremiah was shown the like: the earth *without form, and void,* the heavens without light, and, as he goes on, *lo, there was no man* (Jeremiah 4:25). These are the words of the earth before the first day, when *the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep* (Genesis 1:2); the old silence is the earth returned to that first stillness, no man remaining, before *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her* (2 Esdras 7:32).
cards.s_text: And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.
cards.t_text: I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.

members.member_note: The Hebrew library's own celebration of the genealogical line — *Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.* Ecclesiasticus 44 walks the same line Matthew opens his gospel with.

Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* John comes preaching in the wilderness at Matthew 3:1 with the same fire in his word; he is the Elijah who was to come.

Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* The Elijah errand ends in the restoring of the tribes of Jacob; the voice in the wilderness at Matthew 3:3 is its beginning.
Ecclesiasticus 48:1 carried again — the fire-baptism Yochanan (John) announces at Matt 3:11 sits inside the prophet-as-fire register.

Ecclesiasticus 48:12 — *Elias it was, who was covered with a whirlwind: and Eliseus was filled with his spirit.* The spirit passed from Elijah to Elisha at the Jordan; at Matthew 3:13 Yahusha (Jesus) comes to the same river and the Spirit descends.
Wisdom of Solomon 7:22 — the Hebrew library's twenty-one-attribute characterization of the Ruach (Spirit) holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled.

Wisdom 7:25 — *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* The Ruach as the Father's own breath; the dove-descent is the visible form of the breath landing on the Formed in flesh.
Wisdom 7:27 — *in all ages entering into holy souls, she makes them friends of Yahuah (God), and prophets.* The Spirit-anointing of the Servant-Prophet-King the Father will name at v.17.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The ungodly test the righteous one's claim to be the child of Yahuah (God); the tempter at Matthew 4:3 says if thou be the Son.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* The boast the ungodly resent is the claim the tempter dares him to prove at Matthew 4:6.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly's test is the devil's dare at Matthew 4:6, down to the cut quotation of Psalm 91.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The plot's end; Matthew 4:11's *Then the devil leaveth him* is only the end of its first round.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* Where the persecuted of Matthew 5:10 end up — theirs is the kingdom.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:9 — *grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect.* The reward laid up for the persecuted at Matthew 5:12, who join the line of the prophets.
Ecclesiasticus 23:9 — *Accustom not your mouth to swearing.* The casual oath Sirach warns against is what Matthew 5:33 begins to cut away.
Ecclesiasticus 23:10 — *he that sweareth and nameth Yahuah (God) continually shall not be faultless.* The mark habitual swearing leaves; *Swear not at all; neither by heaven* (Matthew 5:34).
Ecclesiasticus 23:11 — *A man that useth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity.* The iniquity that fills the swearer is the evil Matthew 5:37 names at the root.

Wisdom of Solomon 12:19 — *by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful.* Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44) is the lesson the Father taught by his own mercy on enemies.

Wisdom of Solomon 12:20 — *giving them time and place, by which they might be delivered from their malice.* Sun on the evil and rain on the unjust (Matthew 5:45) is the time and place the Father gives enemies to turn.

Tobit 12:8 — *prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.* The Hebrew library names the triad explicitly as a single righteous-life register; Matt 6:1-18 walks the same three at the motive-level.
Ecclesiasticus 35:6 — *the sweet savour thereof is before the Most High.* Alms in secret (Matthew 6:4) reach the same Most High who receives the righteous offering.
Ecclesiasticus 35:7 — *the memorial thereof shall never be forgotten.* The Father who sees in secret (Matthew 6:4) keeps the memorial men never saw.

Ecclesiasticus 28:2 — *so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* Forgiveness asked for and forgiveness given in one prayer; *forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors* (Matthew 6:12).

Sirach 28:3 — *one man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?* The diagnostic in question-form; Matt 6:14's *if ye forgive men their trespasses* walks the same architecture in proposition-form.

Ecclesiasticus 28:4 — *He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself.* No mercy to the man like yourself, no forgiveness to ask; *if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive* (Matthew 6:15).

Tobit 4:9 — *for you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The Hebrew library's precise *lay up treasure* phrasing; Matt 6:20's *lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven* walks the same architecture directly.
Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* The deliverance the open hand brings, stored where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt (Matthew 6:20).

Ecclesiasticus 29:11 — *Lay up your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High.* The treasure laid up by the open hand of the commandment keeper is the *treasures in heaven* of Matthew 6:20.

Sirach 29:12 — *shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.* The Hebrew library's direct *storehouse* image; Matt 6:20 walks the same storehouse-of-treasure architecture at the heavenly-treasure level.

*Provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not... For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.* The treasure-in-heaven substance — same architecture as Matthew 6:19-21 and the Tobit / Sirach wisdom-stream witness.
Ecclesiasticus 35:8 — *Give Yahuah (God) his honour with a good eye.* The good eye in giving is the single eye of Matthew 6:22.
Ecclesiasticus 14:8 — *The envious man has a wicked eye.* Sirach's wicked eye of envy is the evil eye that darkens the body at Matthew 6:23.
Ecclesiasticus 14:9 — *A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion.* The unsatisfied eye that dries the soul is the evil eye of Matthew 6:23.
Ecclesiasticus 14:10 — *A wicked eye envies his bread, and he is a niggard at his table.* The niggard's table is the darkness of Matthew 6:23 with bread on it.

Ecclesiasticus 31:5 — *He that loves gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption.* The gold-lover cannot stand justified because *ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon* (Matthew 6:24).
Ecclesiasticus 31:6 — *Gold has been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.* Where gold leads; the choice between Elohim (God) and mammon at Matthew 6:24 is the fork before that ruin.
Ecclesiasticus 31:7 — *It is a stumblingblock to them that sacrifice to it.* Gold as a master men sacrifice to; *Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon* (Matthew 6:24).
Wisdom of Solomon 5:15 — *the care of them is with the Most High.* The Father who feeds the birds (Matthew 6:26) is the Most High whose care the righteous are already in.

Wisdom of Solomon 5:16 — *Therefore shall they receive a glorious kingdom, and a beautiful crown from the hand of Yahuah (God).* Seek the kingdom first (Matthew 6:33); the kingdom and the crown come from the Father's hand, and all the rest is added.
Ecclesiasticus 11:14 — *Prosperity and adversity, life and death, poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God).* Because both come of Yahuah (God), the citizen can seek first the kingdom at Matthew 6:33.
Tobit 4:15 — *Do that to no man which you hatest.* The golden rule in negative form, generations before *this is the law and the prophets* (Matthew 7:12).
Ecclesiasticus 27:30 — *Malice and wrath, even these are abominations.* The heart condition that has to go before a brother is weighed; *judge not, that ye be not judged* (Matthew 7:1).
Ecclesiasticus 28:1 — *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God).* Measure for measure: *with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again* (Matthew 7:2).

Ecclesiasticus 28:5 — *If he that is but flesh nourish hatred, who will intreat for pardon of his sins?.* The beam that comes out first (Matthew 7:5); hatred nursed in the heart leaves no one to plead for the man's own pardon.

*Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven: give, and it shall be given unto you.* The Lukan judge-not architecture is the same Sirach 27-28 just-judgment substance Matthew 7:1 anchors.
Ecclesiasticus 22:7 — *Whoso teaches a fool is as one that glueth a potsherd together.* The futility of teaching the one who cannot receive; *neither cast ye your pearls before swine* (Matthew 7:6).
Ecclesiasticus 22:8 — *He that telleth a tale to a fool speaks to one in a slumber.* Discernment of the hearer, made a kingdom rule in Matthew 7:6.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:12 — *she is easily seen of them that love her, and found of such as seek her.* Seek and ye shall find (Matthew 7:7) is the promise Solomon wrote about wisdom first.

Wisdom of Solomon 6:13 — *She preventeth them that desire her, in making herself first known to them.* Wisdom goes before those who desire her; the Father answers ask, seek, knock (Matthew 7:7) because he came out to meet the seeker first.

Wisdom 6:16 — *she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably to them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.* The Father's active pursuit of the seeker; Matt 7:8's *every one that asketh receiveth* walks the same.

Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* The fruit shows the tree, the speech shows the heart; the same test Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 7:16, *ye shall know them by their fruits*.
Ecclesiasticus 27:7 — *Praise no man before you hear him speak.* The man is tried in his speaking; *by their fruits ye shall know them* (Matthew 7:20), and a teacher's teaching is his fruit.
Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* Good tree, good fruit; corrupt tree, corrupt fruit (Luke 6:43), and the mouth is the heart's fruit.

Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed.* The tree is known by what it brings forth and the heart by what its mouth speaks; *every tree is known by his own fruit* (Luke 6:44).

*For every tree is known by his own fruit... A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good.* The Lukan tree-and-fruit teaching ties the fruit-diagnostic to the heart-utterance — Sirach 27:6 substance directly. The mouth speaks the heart's abundance; the fruit reveals the tree.
Ecclesiasticus 22:16 — *so the heart that is stablished by advised counsel shall fear at no time.* The hearer and doer who built on the rock (Matthew 7:24) has the heart Sirach describes.
Ecclesiasticus 22:17 — *A heart settled upon a thought of understanding.* The settled heart is the hearer and doer of Matthew 7:24.
Ecclesiasticus 22:18 — *so a fearful heart in the imagination of a fool cannot stand against any fear.* The wind of Matthew 7:25 that cannot move the house on the rock blows the pales flat.
Ecclesiasticus 22:16 — *As timber girt and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking.* Luke 6:48's builder *digged deep*, and the stream *could not shake* the house.
Ecclesiasticus 22:18 — *Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind.* The hearer who does not do, *without a foundation*, falls and the ruin is great (Luke 6:49).

The Lukan wise-and-foolish-builders carries the same Sirach 22:16-18 heart-stablished substance Matthew 7:24-27 anchors. Luke uniquely names the *deep* — *digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock.*

Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning..* The many from east and west (Matthew 8:11) are the tribes coming home to their fathers' table.
Ecclesiasticus 36:12 — *Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* The firstborn's scattered children sit down with the fathers in Matthew 8:11.

Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn.* The righteous one of Wisdom 2 is Isaiah's servant; at Matthew 8:17 he bears our sicknesses while the ungodly lie in wait for him.

Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* The help came as bearing, not escape — *Himself took our infirmities, and bare our sicknesses* (Matthew 8:17).

Wisdom 2:20 — *let us condemn him with a shameful death.* The lawless plot against the just-man; the wider Hebrew-library backdrop to Matt 8:17's Servant-credential operative across the Messianic ministry.

Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea.* The one who rebuked the winds and the sea (Matthew 8:26) is the one whose providence governs it.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:4 — *Shewing that you can save from all danger.* Lord, save us, we perish (Matthew 8:25) is answered by the one who can save from all danger at sea (Matthew 8:26).
Ecclesiasticus 35:1 — *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough.* Mercy and not sacrifice (Matthew 9:13) is the commandment kept, which is the offering.
Ecclesiasticus 35:2 — *he that gives alms sacrificeth praise.* Alms as sacrifice; *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13).
Ecclesiasticus 35:3 — *to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.* The turning is the offering; Matthew 9:13 calls sinners to that repentance.

Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice, which the Pharisees at the table had forgotten (Matthew 9:13).
Tobit 4:9 — *you layest up a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* The treasure laid up by mercy, the thing Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).
Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy is what delivers, and mercy is what Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).
Tobit 12:9 — *alms does deliver from death, and shall purge away all sin.* Mercy with the weight of life and death, the mercy Hosea asked for in place of sacrifice (Matthew 9:13).
Ecclesiasticus 12:4 — *Give to the godly man, and help not a sinner.* Sirach guards the hand from strengthening the ungodly; the King's table at Matthew 9:10 calls sinners to turn.

Ecclesiasticus 12:5 — *hold back your bread, and give it not to him, lest he overmaster you thereby.* Bread held back from the one who would overmaster you is not the table the Pharisees question at Matthew 9:11.
Ecclesiasticus 12:7 — *Give to the good, and help not the sinner.* Help not the sinner and call sinners to repentance (Matthew 9:13) meet at the word repentance.

*And Levi made him a great feast in his own house: and there was a great company of publicans and of others that sat down with them. But their scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples, saying, Why do ye eat and drink with publicans and sinners?* The Lukan call of Levi and the table-fellowship that follows is the same Sirach-12-inverse the Matthew 9:10 catch names.
Tobit 12:8 — *Prayer is good with fasting and alms and righteousness.* Fasting belongs with prayer, alms, and righteousness, not alone; the King keeps it in that place (Matthew 9:14).

Ecclesiasticus 34:26 — *a man that fasteth for his sins, and goes again, and doeth the same: who will hear his prayer?.* Fasting that turns is heard; *then shall they fast* (Matthew 9:15) is fasting with the loss truly felt.
Ecclesiasticus 9:10 — *a new friend is as new wine; when it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.* Sirach's new wine that ages well sits beside the new wine and new bottles of Matthew 9:17.
Ecclesiasticus 38:9 — *pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole.* The woman who touched the hem (Matthew 9:20) made that prayer with her hand.

Ecclesiasticus 38:12 — *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him.* The bleeding woman gave place to physicians for twelve years; at Matthew 9:22 she reached past them to the one who made them, and her faith made her whole.

Ecclesiasticus 38:14 — *they shall also pray to Yahuah (God), that he would prosper that, which they give.* The physician prays that his remedy would prosper; at Matthew 9:25 the one he prays to takes the dead girl by the hand himself.

Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The maid not dead but sleeping (Matthew 9:24) is raised by the one who leads to the grave and brings up again.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:14 — *the spirit, when it is gone forth, returns not.* What no man can do, the King does with his hand on a dead girl (Matthew 9:25).
2 Esdras 12:31 — *the lion, whom you sawest rising up out of the wood, and roaring.* The lion named as the anointed is the Son of David the blind men cry to at Matthew 9:27.
2 Esdras 12:32 — *This is the anointed, which the Highest has kept for them.* The anointed kept to the end is the Son of David met on the road at Matthew 9:27.
2 Esdras 12:34 — *the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders.* The blind men ask the Son of David for that same mercy at Matthew 9:27.
2 Esdras 7:28 — *my son the Messiah shall be revealed with those that be with him.* The blind men of Matthew 9:27 confess as present the one Ezra was told would be revealed.

2 Baruch 35:1 — *the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The apocalyptic-stream names the harvest of the age explicitly; Matt 9:37's *the harvest truly is plenteous* names the present-tense fulfillment at the King's arrival.

2 Baruch 35:1 (extended) — the same eschatological-harvest-of-the-age verse also anchors Matt 9:38's *pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers.* The Lord-of-the-harvest is the Mighty One the apocalyptic-stream had named; the labourers being prayed-for are about to be commissioned at Matt 10:1.
2 Esdras 4:35 — *How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?.* The living are sent into the harvest the sleeping righteous wait for (Matthew 9:37).
2 Esdras 4:36 — *Even when the number of seeds is filled in you: for he has weighed the world in the balance.* The labourers sent into the harvest (Matthew 9:38) are how the number is filled.

2 Baruch 38:4 — *all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* The apocalyptic-stream's twelve-tribes-bound-by-one-bond architecture; the scattered-shepherdless multitudes Yahusha (Jesus) sees at Matt 9:36 are the same one-father-born twelve-tribe-body the wisdom-stream had named.

2 Baruch 38:7 — *with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* The apocalyptic-stream's explicit gathering-of-the-dispersed-with-much-mercy architecture; the same mercy-substance Hosea 6:6 names at Matt 9:13, now operative as the gathering-architecture of Matt 9:36's scattered-shepherdless multitudes.
2 Esdras 13:40 — *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) the twelve are sent to at Matthew 10:6.
2 Esdras 13:41 — *they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country.* The remnant went out to keep the statutes; the twelve are sent after them (Matthew 10:6).

2 Esdras 13:47 — *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through.* The way home opens at the latter time; the mission runs till the Son of Adam comes (Matthew 10:23).

Tobit 13:5 — *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations.* The gathering Tobit prayed for is the mission to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 10:6).

Tobit 13:3 — *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.* The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King confesses them before his Father (Matthew 10:32).

Tobit 14:5 — *afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously.* Two returns, the second still to come; the mission runs till the Son of Adam comes (Matthew 10:23).
Ecclesiasticus 2:1 — *if you come to serve Yahuah (God), prepare your soul for temptation.* The endurance to the end Yahusha (Jesus) asks of the twelve at Matthew 10:22.
Ecclesiasticus 2:5 — *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* The furnace the twelve are sent into at Matthew 10:22.
Ecclesiasticus 2:18 — *We will fall into the hands of Yahuah (God), and not into the hands of men.* The fear moved off men and onto Yahuah (God) at Matthew 10:28.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *there shall no torment touch them.* The persecutor kills the body but cannot kill the soul held in the Father's hand (Matthew 10:28).
Wisdom of Solomon 3:5 — *Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself.* The proving is the hatred of all men; *he that endureth to the end shall be saved* (Matthew 10:22).

Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The one who confesses the King before his afflicters (Matthew 10:32) is the one who stands in boldness before them on that day.

4 Maccabees (edition ch 8, v.4 = std 4 Macc 9:4) — *apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.* The Hebrew library's most direct verbal-anchor for Matt 10:28's *not able to kill the soul* — the third son under torture names the diagnostic explicitly at the martyrdom-witness.

4 Maccabees (edition ch 11, v.3 = std 4 Macc 15:3) — *her seven sons ... loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God).* The priority of eternal-stakes-religion over the tyrant's present-life-promise; Matt 10:28's fear-redirect names the same priority at the commissioning.

4 Maccabees (edition ch 13, v.13 = std 4 Macc 17:13) — *virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* The wisdom-stream's endurance-prize architecture; Matt 10:22's endure-to-the-end is the same diagnostic at the kingdom-citizens commissioning.

4 Maccabees (edition ch 13, v.18 = std 4 Macc 17:18) — *the endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* The wisdom-stream's post-martyrdom station; the Red Line #11 first-resurrection-firstfruits architecture at the wisdom-stream witness.

4 Maccabees (edition ch 8, v.18 = std 4 Macc 9:18) — *even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.* The wisdom-stream's direct operative-fact for Matt 10:20's *Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you* — the Father's direct-hearing of the persecuted-disciple does not depend on the disciple's organ of speech.
2 Esdras 4:33 — *How, and when shall these things come to pass? wherefore are our years few and evil?.* John's question from prison (Matthew 11:3) is the same question from the same distress.
2 Esdras 4:34 — *Do not you hasten above the most Highest: for your haste is in vain to be above him.* Blessed is he who is not offended in the waiting (Matthew 11:6).
2 Esdras 4:35 — *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The one who waits without being offended is blessed (Matthew 11:6).
Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *to restore the tribes of Jacob.* Yahusha (Jesus) names John as Elias at Matthew 11:14, and Sirach says what Elijah comes to do: restore the tribes of Jacob, all twelve.
1 Maccabees 2:58 — *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* John came in that same zeal; this is Elias which was for to come (Matthew 11:14).

Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* The contradictory complaints of Matthew 11:19 hide the real grievance Wisdom 2:12 names: the righteous one reproves their lawbreaking.

Wisdom of Solomon 2:15 — *his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion.* The life of another fashion is what the slander of Matthew 11:19 was aimed at — a glutton and winebibber for sitting with sinners.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* The end of the road whose first step is the slander of Matthew 11:19.
Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Wisdom's invitation; *wisdom is justified of her children* who came (Matthew 11:19).
Baruch 3:36 — *has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* Wisdom's children at Matthew 11:19 are the people she was given to.
Baruch 4:1 — *the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life.* Wisdom is the Torah; her children keep it (Matthew 11:19).

Wisdom of Solomon 6:5 — *a sharp judgment shall be to them that be in high places.* Chorazin and Bethsaida (Matthew 11:21) saw the mighty works and did not repent; the more shown, the sharper the judgment.

Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 — *mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* More tolerable for Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:22): the judgment is real and weighed by what each was shown.
Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 — *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Capernaum, exalted unto heaven and brought down to the grave (Matthew 11:23), is the mighty under the sore trial.
Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 — *a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Sodom, the standing monument of unbelief, is the floor the King measures Capernaum against (Matthew 11:24).
Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *The greater you are, the more humble thyself.* Revealed unto babes, hidden from the wise and prudent (Matthew 11:25).
Ecclesiasticus 3:19 — *mysteries are revealed to the meek.* Hid from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes (Matthew 11:25).

Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Understanding is given to the one who prays; the Father reveals to babes what the wise cannot reach (Matthew 11:25).

Ecclesiasticus 51:23 — *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* Sirach's closing invitation is the one Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28; come near, and find the rest in the house of learning.

Ecclesiasticus 51:26 — *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction.* The yoke is the instruction and the rest is found under it, not away from it; Matthew 11:29 says take my yoke, learn of me.
Ecclesiasticus 51:27 — *I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* Sirach's little labour and much rest under the yoke is Matthew 11:30, my yoke is easy and my burden is light.
Ecclesiasticus 6:28 — *at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* The rest found under the yoke at Matthew 11:29.

Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The same call Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*; Wisdom speaking before she came in flesh.
1 Maccabees 2:41 — *Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him.* Preserving life on the sabbath is doing well on it (Matthew 12:12).
Ecclesiasticus 35:1 — *he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* Heeding the commandment is the offering; mercy over sacrifice at Matthew 12:7.
Ecclesiasticus 34:18 — *the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* Sacrifice while condemning the guiltless (Matthew 12:7) is the gift Yahuah (God) does not take.
Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy carries eternal weight; the Sabbath condemnation showed a system that had lost it (Matthew 12:7).

Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the verdict this age renders; the day of judgment reverses it in front of them.

Wisdom of Solomon 5:4 — *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the judgment of fools that the day of judgment turns into their own confession.
Ecclesiasticus 4:1 — *defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* The bruised reed not broken at Matthew 12:20, asked of the son first.
Ecclesiasticus 4:4 — *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* The face the Messiah keeps toward the bruised reed at Matthew 12:20.
Ecclesiasticus 35:14 — *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow.* The bruised reed not broken (Matthew 12:20) is the same mercy toward the ones who cry.

Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The cogitation that would never be changed is the heart behind the word against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) that is not forgiven (Matthew 12:32).
Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Words as the fruit of the heart; *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh* (Matthew 12:34).

Ecclesiasticus 27:7 — *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* Speech as the trial of a man; at Matthew 12:36 that trial reaches the day of judgment, where *every idle word* is given account of.
Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought.* No word goes for nothing; Matthew 12:36 says every idle word is accounted for in the day of judgment.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The sign of Jonah walks that road: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, then up (Matthew 12:40).
2 Esdras 7:48 — *though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.* The swept but empty house of Matthew 12:45 is a son of Adam without a new heart.

Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life of another fashion; Matthew 12:50 says the same, whoever does the will of my Father.

Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly test sonship by rescue; Yahusha (Jesus) marks his family by doing the Father's will (Matthew 12:50).
Ecclesiasticus 4:10 — *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother.* The doing of the Father's will by which the family is known at Matthew 12:50.
2 Esdras 5:9 — *then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber.* To some it is given to know the mysteries; to others it is not (Matthew 13:11).
Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 — *into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter.* Wisdom does not enter a soul set against her; at Matthew 13:13 the parables meet eyes that have closed themselves.

Ecclesiasticus 39:6 — *he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences.* Understanding is given when Yahuah (God) wills; the blessed eyes and ears of Matthew 13:16 are given the same way.
2 Esdras 4:30 — *the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning.* The parable of the good seed sown in the field (Matthew 13:24) runs to the same threshing.
2 Esdras 3:21 — *the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome.* The field of Adam's sons is where the enemy sowed tares while men slept (Matthew 13:25).
2 Esdras 8:6 — *give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it.* The sower of Matthew 13:24 is the answer to this prayer.

Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* The harvest scene of Matthew 13:43 — tares to the fire, *then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun.*

Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 — *I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you.* Things kept secret from the foundation of the world uttered in parables (Matthew 13:35) is the same refusal to hide mysteries.
2 Esdras 6:26 — *the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.* The parables of Matthew 13:35 open what was kept secret to a heart turned toward their meaning.
Ecclesiasticus 20:30 — *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both.* The treasure hid in the field is found and bought with everything (Matthew 13:44).
Ecclesiasticus 6:14 — *he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* The one pearl worth all the merchant had, Matthew 13:45.

Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 — *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* The merchant who sells all for one pearl (Matthew 13:45) is doing Solomon's arithmetic: sceptres and riches are nothing beside wisdom.

Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God).* The treasure hid in a field worth selling all for (Matthew 13:44) is the treasure that never fails and makes friends of Yahuah (God).

2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:33 — *the Most High shall appear upon the seat of judgment ... judgment only shall remain, truth shall stand, and faith shall wax strong.* The seat of judgment at the last end, after the reign; the angels severing the wicked from among the just at Matt 13:49 is the severing at the end of the age, before the reign.
2 Esdras 8:3 — *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* The angels sever the wicked from among the just at Matthew 13:49; the few are what remains.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* After the angels sever the wicked from among the just (Matthew 13:49), the just are the ones who judge.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 — *through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side.* The enemy who sowed the tares (Matthew 13:39) is the one whose envy let death in.
Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *his word burned like a lamp.* Elijah's fire at Ahab's court is John's word to Herod at Matthew 14:3–4; the king answers the prophet by binding him.
Ecclesiasticus 48:2 — *by his zeal he diminished their number.* Elijah's zeal against Ahab's court brought famine; John's zeal against Herod's court brought his imprisonment at Matthew 14:3.

Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God).* The multitude at Matthew 14:5 counted John a prophet; Sirach describes which prophet, the Elijah ordained for reproofs and the restoring of Jacob.

Ecclesiasticus 48:11 — *Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* John's disciples at Matthew 14:12 bury the Elijah of their day and go to Yahusha (Jesus), the one in whom we shall surely live.
2 Esdras 1:19 — *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat.* The same pity fed the multitude in the desert place of Matthew 14:13.

Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour.* Bread without labour again, blessed and broken in a desert place and handed out by the disciples (Matthew 14:19).

Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word.* The loaves blessed and broken point past themselves to the word that nourishes (Matthew 14:19).

Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* In the desert place *they did all eat, and were filled* (Matthew 14:20); Wisdom feeding her children, with twelve baskets left for the twelve tribes.

Ecclesiasticus 43:23 — *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.* The one who stills the deep by his counsel walks on it at Matthew 14:25; Job 9:8 said he alone treads upon the waves of the sea.

Ecclesiasticus 43:25 — *in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* The sea is the Creator's storehouse of wonders; at Matthew 14:25 the Creator walks on it and tells them, it is I.
Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The King walking on the sea in the fourth watch (Matthew 14:25) is walking the way the Father made in the sea.

Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 — *Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne.* The Word who came down on Passover night speaks across the dark water, *it is I; be not afraid* (Matthew 14:27).
Ecclesiasticus 24:3 — *I came out of the mouth of the Most High, and covered the earth as a cloud.* The Word from the Father's mouth is the one on the water saying *it is I* (Matthew 14:27).
Wisdom of Solomon 9:1 — *who have made all things with your word.* The Word all things were made with walks on the sea and says it is I (Matthew 14:27).
Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* John upbraids Herod with the law at Matthew 14:3–4 and is bound for it, the ungodly lying in wait for the righteous.
Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness.* Herod's heart toward John, held back only by fear of the multitude (Matthew 14:5).
Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* John beheaded in the prison on a birthday oath (Matthew 14:10) is the death Wisdom describes.
Ecclesiasticus 3:1 — *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* The fifth commandment Yahusha (Jesus) quotes against the tradition at Matthew 15:4.
Ecclesiasticus 3:8 — *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed.* The word without the deed the corban tradition allowed, against Matthew 15:4.
Ecclesiasticus 7:27 — *Honour your father with your whole heart.* The whole heart the corban tradition divided, against Matthew 15:4.
Ecclesiasticus 3:16 — *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer.* The weight behind the voided commandment at Matthew 15:6.

Tobit 4:3 — *despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life.* The commandment to honour father and mother, kept to the end of her days, which the gift tradition voided (Matthew 15:4).
Ecclesiasticus 15:11 — *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away.* The fall is not from Yahuah (God), and the defilement is not from the food (Matthew 15:11); both come from the man.
Ecclesiasticus 15:20 — *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* No licence to sin from Yahuah (God); the sin comes out of the heart at Matthew 15:18.

Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* The heart's conceit comes out in the mouth; *those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart* (Matthew 15:18).
Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* The lying mouth of Wisdom 1:11 and the false witness of Matthew 15:19 come from the same place, the heart.
Ecclesiasticus 36:1 — *Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us.* The prayer for mercy that the mission to the lost sheep (Matthew 15:24) answers.
Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in Matthew 15:24 are the tribes Sirach prayed home.
2 Esdras 13:40 — *whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) the King says he was sent to (Matthew 15:24).

2 Esdras 13:48 — *those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.* The remnant that stayed; the King's mission reaches them and the scattered alike (Matthew 15:24).

Tobit 13:5 — *will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* The lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) Yahusha (Jesus) was sent to are the scattered Tobit said would be gathered (Matthew 15:24).
Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* Said in mockery here; confessed by Peter at Matthew 16:16 as *the Son of the living Elohim (God).*
Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *let us lie in wait for the righteous.* The plot of Wisdom 2 ends in a shameful death; at Matthew 16:21 Yahusha (Jesus) names the same end and adds the third day.

Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness.* The grievance of the religious seat, which is why he must suffer of the elders and chief priests and scribes (Matthew 16:21).

Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* The shameful death is the cross Yahusha (Jesus) said he must die at Matthew 16:21, hung on the tree of Deuteronomy 21:23.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).* The other half of the shameful death — killed, *and be raised again the third day* (Matthew 16:21).

Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Killed and raised the third day (Matthew 16:21) is where the righteous man's standing before his afflicters begins.

Wisdom of Solomon 1:13 — *Yahuah (God) made not death: neither has he pleasure in the destruction of the living.* Death is not of Yahuah's (God's) making, so the gates of the grave at Matthew 16:18 have no lasting claim on the assembly he builds.
Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The gates that could not hold the raised King will not prevail against his assembly (Matthew 16:18).

2 Esdras 4:35 — *the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers.* The chambers hold the righteous until the resurrection; the gates of hell shall not prevail (Matthew 16:18).
Ecclesiasticus 16:12 — *he judges a man according to his works.* Judged according to his works is the Son of Adam's reward at Matthew 16:27.
Ecclesiasticus 16:14 — *Make way for every work of mercy: for every man shall find according to his works.* Every man finds according to his works when the Son of Adam comes at Matthew 16:27.
Ecclesiasticus 35:19 — *Till he have rendered to every man according to his deeds.* Reward according to works at the Son of Adam's coming (Matthew 16:27).
2 Esdras 7:32 — *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her.* Resurrection first, then reward according to works, as the Son of Adam says at Matthew 16:27.
2 Esdras 7:35 — *the work shall follow, and the reward shall be shewed.* At Matthew 16:27 the Son of Adam rewards every man according to his works.
Who is there alive that hath not sinned — the leveling baseline before Paul
No man... but he hath dealt wickedly — the universal verdict pre-Paul
Howbeit neither are they to be pardoned — the Romans 1 argument before Romans 1
How did they not sooner find out Yahuah (the Lord) — without-excuse, source argument
We are all worthy of punishment — the universal verdict in wisdom register
Righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces — Baruch echoes Daniel verbatim
I have sinned, I acknowledge mine iniquities — the model return-prayer matches the new heart's loathing
Forgive me, I humbly beseech thee — Manasseh's confession in Daniel-style posture
Ecclesiasticus 19:13 — *Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it.* The private first step of Matthew 18:15 — go to him alone, and he may be gained.
Ecclesiasticus 19:17 — *Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him.* The order and the temper of the private word in Matthew 18:15 — admonish first, and not in anger.
Ecclesiasticus 19:15 — *for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.* The two or three witnesses of Matthew 18:16 guard against the slander Sirach warns of.
Ecclesiasticus 20:2 — *It is much better to reprove, than to be angry secretly.* The open reproof before the assembly in Matthew 18:17 — the alternative to secret anger that restores no one.

Ecclesiasticus 27:30 — *even these are abominations; and the sinful man shall have them both.* Malice and wrath as the sinful man's portion; Peter's *till seven times?* (Matthew 18:21) is still counting, and the King's answer leaves the count behind.

Ecclesiasticus 28:2 — *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you.* The one line behind the King's *seventy times seven* (Matthew 18:22) and the parable that follows it: forgive, and be forgiven.

Ecclesiasticus 28:3 — *One man bears hatred against another, and does he seek pardon from Yahuah (God)?.* Sirach's question is the lord's question at Matthew 18:33, *shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant*; the pardon that was not passed on was taken back.

Ecclesiasticus 28:7 — *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour.* Torah remembered and malice laid down as one thing; at Matthew 18:35 the Father deals the same way with the one who will not forgive *from your hearts*.
Ecclesiasticus 10:7 — *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man.* The pride Sirach names is the disposition behind who is the greatest at Matthew 18:1.
Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* The humbling that is the kingdom's entry at Matthew 18:3.
Ecclesiasticus 10:14 — *cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead.* The meek set up in the proud's stead is the child who is greatest at Matthew 18:4.

Tobit 8:6 — *You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay.* The creation prayed over a marriage bed; *What therefore Elohim (God) hath joined together, let not man put asunder* (Matthew 19:6).

Wisdom of Solomon 3:14 — *to him shall be given the special gift of faith, and an inheritance in the temple of Yahuah (God).* The gift behind Matthew 19:12's *he that is able to receive it, let him receive it.*
Ecclesiasticus 7:23 — *Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their neck from their youth.* The parents bringing their children to Yahusha (Jesus) at Matthew 19:13.
Ecclesiasticus 3:1 — *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter.* The children who come when called, of whom the kingdom is, at Matthew 19:14.
Tobit 4:3 — *My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother.* A father handing covenant life to his son; the King laying hands on the children brought to him (Matthew 19:15).
Ecclesiasticus 17:11 — *the law of life for an heritage.* The law of life is the keep the commandments that enters into life at Matthew 19:17.

Ecclesiasticus 29:1 — *he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments.* Mercy to the neighbour as commandment keeping; *if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments* (Matthew 19:17), and the test that followed was the poor.
Ecclesiasticus 29:11 — *and it shall bring you more profit than gold.* The treasure laid up by the commandments is the *treasure in heaven* the King offers the young man at Matthew 19:21.
Tobit 4:9 — *a good treasure for thyself against the day of necessity.* Give to the poor and have treasure in heaven (Matthew 19:21), the treasure Tobit told his son to lay up.

*But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* The Lukan Woes are the 1 Enoch 94-100 woes-on-the-rich register in the King's own mouth — the reversal-architecture Wisdom of Solomon 3 and 5 also carry. The woes are paired with the blessings so the reader hears both sides of the post-harvest sifting at once.
Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together.* Twelve thrones for twelve tribes (Matthew 19:28); the tribes gathered whole.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* The outer ring of the kingdom whose inner ring is the twelve thrones over the twelve tribes (Matthew 19:28).

Ecclesiasticus 24:8 — *Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).* Wisdom planted in Yashar'el (Israel), the vineyard the householder hires labourers into (Matthew 20:1).
Ecclesiasticus 24:12 — *I took root in an honourable people.* The honourable people is the vineyard of Matthew 20:1 — Yashar'el (Israel), the Father's own inheritance.
Ecclesiasticus 33:13 — *As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his pleasure.* The householder's right over his own (Matthew 20:15) is the potter's right over the clay.

2 Esdras 5:23 — *of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine.* The householder's vineyard at Matthew 20:1 is that one chosen vine, and the labourers are hired into it.
2 Esdras 9:22 — *let my grape be kept, and my plant; for with great labour have I made it perfect.* The grape kept out of the cluster is the few chosen of Matthew 20:16.
2 Esdras 8:1 — *The most High has made this world for many, but the world to come for few.* Many called, few chosen (Matthew 20:16) is the same count.
2 Esdras 8:3 — *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* Many called, few chosen (Matthew 20:16); the few are the sheep who hear and keep.
Wisdom of Solomon 3:1 — *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God).* What held the sons of Zebedee while they drank the cup they said they could drink (Matthew 20:22).

Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The cup the sons of Zebedee will drink (Matthew 20:23) comes first; the standing in boldness before the afflicters comes after.
Wisdom of Solomon 5:15 — *their reward also is with Yahuah (God).* The seats that are the Father's to give (Matthew 20:23) are the reward kept with Yahuah (God) for the righteous.
2 Maccabees 7:37 — *offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers.* The cup the sons of Zebedee said they could drink (Matthew 20:22).
Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* Greatness as service, against the domination of the princes, at Matthew 20:26.
2 Maccabees 10:7 — *they bare branches, and fair boughs, and palms also, and sang psalms.* Branches and psalms before a cleansed temple, as at the entry (Matthew 21:8).
Ecclesiasticus 36:14 — *Fill Sion with your unspeakable oracles, and your people with your glory.* The glory entered the city at Matthew 21:9 to the cry of Hosanna.
1 Maccabees 4:43 — *cleansed the sanctuary, and bare out the defiled stones into an unclean place.* The King cast out what defiled the same house (Matthew 21:12).
2 Maccabees 10:3 — *having cleansed the temple they made another altar.* The temple cleansed of a defilement from outside; the King cleansed it from inside (Matthew 21:12).

Ecclesiasticus 35:12 — *Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for such he will not receive.* The den of thieves (Matthew 21:13) was gifts and sacrifices turned to trade, and the judge will not take them.
1 Maccabees 4:46 — *until there should come a prophet to shew what should be done with them.* The prophet came and spoke for the house: my house shall be called the house of prayer (Matthew 21:13).
Wisdom of Solomon 4:4 — *though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last.* Leaves without fruit at Matthew 21:19 is the same show of life with nothing under it.

Wisdom of Solomon 4:5 — *The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable.* The fig tree with leaves and no fruit (Matthew 21:19) is the leadership, not the people; the branch that bears nothing is broken off.

Ecclesiasticus 23:25 — *Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit.* Leaves without fruit; the fig tree told *Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever* (Matthew 21:19).
Ecclesiasticus 17:24 — *to them that repent, he granted them return.* Return granted to them that repent is the son who afterward repented, and went at Matthew 21:29.
Ecclesiasticus 1:28 — *come not to him with a double heart.* The second son's *I go, sir: and went not* (Matthew 21:30).
Ecclesiasticus 1:29 — *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men.* The second son's public yes and absent obedience at Matthew 21:30.
Ecclesiasticus 21:1 — *have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* The repentance John preached — the publicans and harlots did it, the office refused it (Matthew 21:32).
2 Esdras 9:11 — *when as yet place of repentance was open to them, understood not, but despised it.* The chief priests who would not repent when John came (Matthew 21:32) walked past that open place.
2 Esdras 1:32 — *I sent to you my servants the prophets, whom you have taken and slain.* The husbandmen who beat, killed, and stoned the servants (Matthew 21:35) are the same story.
2 Esdras 1:33 — *Your house is desolate, I will cast you out as the wind does stubble.* The sentence falls when the husbandmen cast out the son and slay him (Matthew 21:39).
Ecclesiasticus 36:11 — *inherit you them, as from the beginning.* The one nation bringing forth fruit (Matthew 21:43) is the gathered tribes of Jacob, not a replacement.
2 Esdras 2:38 — *behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of Yahuah (God).* The servants sent into the highways gather them to the marriage (Matthew 22:9).
2 Esdras 2:42 — *a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised Yahuah (God) with songs.* The wedding furnished with guests (Matthew 22:10) is the same gathered crowd.
