threads.summary_md: The chapter's final keystone: *Behold, the righteous shall be recompensed in the earth: much more the wicked and the sinner* (Proverbs 11:31). Peter quotes it nearly word for word from the Greek shape, turning the "much more" into a question: *And if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?* (1 Peter 4:18) — the recompense of the righteous measures the far heavier reckoning of the wicked. The same book states it plainly — *Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed* (Proverbs 13:21) — and the Psalter opens the whole Psalter on it: *the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous* (Psalm 1:5); *Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish* (1:6). The restored witness keeps the recompense sure and everlasting: *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1); *the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High* (5:15). Each is paid in his own coin — the righteous recompensed and kept, the wicked and the sinner answered with a far heavier reckoning.

threads.title: The lip of truth established for ever — the lying tongue but for a moment
threads.summary_md: The chapter gathers a cluster on the tongue: *He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit* (Proverbs 12:17); *There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health* (12:18); *The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment* (12:19); *Lying lips are abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but they that deal truly are his delight* (12:22). The lying tongue is among the very things Yahuah hates — *a proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood... A false witness that speaketh lies* (Proverbs 6:17,19). The one who may abide in Yahuah's tabernacle *speaketh the truth in his heart* (Psalm 15:2); and the covenant-conduct of the restored Jerusalem is *Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour... and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Zechariah 8:16-17). The New Testament keeps the same measure, never loosening it: *putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another* (Ephesians 4:25); *Lie not one to another, seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds* (Colossians 3:9). And at the end the lying tongue, established only for a moment, is shut out of the city — *all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death* (Revelation 21:8); *whosoever loveth and maketh a lie* is without (Revelation 22:15). The restored witness weighs the tongue the same way: *Honour and shame is in talk: and the tongue of man is his fall* (Sirach 5:13); *an evil condemnation upon the double tongue* (Sirach 5:14); *the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17); *Curse the whisperer and doubletongued: for such have destroyed many that were at peace* (Sirach 28:13). From Torah-rooted Proverbs to the prophets to the apostles to the restored witnesses, one verdict stands: the lip of truth is established for ever, and the lying tongue is but for a moment.

threads.title: If riches increase, set not your heart upon them
threads.summary_md: The psalm warns where the heart must not go: *Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them* (Psalm 62:10). Yahusha (Jesus) draws the very line: *Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man's life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth* (Luke 12:15) — and tells of the rich man whose barns could not save him: *Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). Paul charges the same: *Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living Elohim (God), who giveth us richly all things to enjoy* (1 Timothy 6:17). And the restored wisdom paints the very man: *I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Sirach 11:19). The heart set on increasing riches is the heart not waiting upon Elohim; riches cannot ransom the soul that trusts in them.

threads.title: Thou renderest to every man according to his work — the measure across the whole library
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes on a couplet that holds power and mercy together: *Elohim (God) hath spoken once; twice have I heard this; that power belongeth unto Elohim (God). Also unto thee, O Yahuah (Lord), belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work* (Psalm 62:11-12). This last line is woven across the entire library. Yahusha (Jesus): *the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works* (Matthew 16:27). Paul, as the rule of the righteous judgment of Elohim: *Who will render to every man according to his deeds* (Romans 2:6). The risen Messiah at the very end of the book: *behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be* (Revelation 22:12). Paul again, leaving the coppersmith to the rule: *Yahuah (Lord) reward him according to his works* (2 Timothy 4:14). The proverb asks it as a question that answers itself: *shall not he render to every man according to his works?* (Proverbs 24:12). And the restored wisdom doubles it: *he judges a man according to his works* (Sirach 16:12); *every man shall find according to his works* (Sirach 16:14). This is not works-righteousness but the Torah-consistent measure: power AND mercy both belong to Yahuah, and He renders to each according to his work — the standard that runs from David through the apostles to the throne.

threads.title: My soul thirsteth for thee in a dry and thirsty land — the living water
threads.summary_md: David in the wilderness sings the master thirst of the psalter: *O Elohim (God), thou art my Elohim (God); early will I seek thee: my soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh longeth for thee in a dry and thirsty land, where no water is* (Psalm 63:1). It is the panting of the sister-psalm — *As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after thee, O Elohim (God). My soul thirsteth for Elohim (God), for the living Elohim (God)* (Psalm 42:1-2). The Formed Son answers that thirst in the flesh: *whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life* (John 4:14); and at the feast He cried, *If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink* (John 7:37). It is the wide call of Yahuah through Isaiah — *Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters... without money and without price* (Isaiah 55:1) — and the last word of the whole library: *I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely* (Revelation 21:6); *let him that is athirst come... take the water of life freely* (Revelation 22:17). The restored wisdom marks the contrast — even her own draught never finally fills: *They that eat me shall yet be hungry, and they that drink me shall yet be thirsty* (Sirach 24:21). Only the living Elohim quenches the thirst of the dry land.

threads.title: Who whet their tongue like a sword — the tongue-as-weapon
threads.summary_md: *Who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words: That they may shoot in secret at the perfect* (Psalm 64:3-4). The tongue is the weapon, whetted and bent against the upright. The psalter sings the same wound again and again — *whose teeth are spears and arrows, and their tongue a sharp sword* (Psalm 57:4); *his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords* (Psalm 55:21); *Thy tongue deviseth mischiefs; like a sharp razor, working deceitfully* (Psalm 52:2). The restored wisdom weighs the wound: *The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh: but the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17); *Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue* (Sirach 28:18). And the apostolic word carries the same weapon whole — *the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity... and it is set on fire of hell* (James 3:6); *the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison* (James 3:8) — gathered into Paul's catena of the unrenewed mouth: *with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness* (Romans 3:13-14). One weapon across the whole library: the tongue whetted like a sword, the bitter word shot in secret at the perfect.

threads.title: O thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come — the ingathering of the nations with Yashar'el
threads.summary_md: *O thou that hearest prayer, unto thee shall all flesh come* (Psalm 65:2). This all-flesh-come is no replacement of Yashar'el (Israel) by the nations; it is the ingathering of the nations WITH His people, gathered to the One who hears prayer in Zion. Isaiah gives it its appointed-times shape: *from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 66:23) — and names the gathering: *I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory* (Isaiah 66:18). Paul presses that the Gentiles come not INSTEAD of but alongside His people: *Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people* (Romans 15:10); *There shall be a root of Jesse, and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles; in him shall the Gentiles trust* (Romans 15:12) — they trust IN the root of Jesse, grafted to the one covenant root, for *Elohim (God) hath not cast away his people* (Romans 11:2). And the restored Tobit sings it: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands, even gifts to the King of heaven* (Tobit 13:11). All flesh comes — to the One who hears prayer, the two houses and the nations together at His holy mountain.

threads.title: Thou crownest the year with thy goodness — the harvest of His providence
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes in the crowned-year harvest: *Thou crownest the year with thy goodness; and thy paths drop fatness. They drop upon the pastures of the wilderness: and the little hills rejoice on every side. The pastures are clothed with flocks; the valleys also are covered over with corn; they shout for joy, they also sing* (Psalm 65:11-13). The providence of the seasons is sung again in the great creation-psalm — *He watereth the hills from his chambers: the earth is satisfied with the fruit of thy works. He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man; that he may bring forth food out of the earth* (Psalm 104:13-14); *and wine that maketh glad the heart of man... and bread which strengtheneth man's heart* (Psalm 104:15). The restored wisdom of Sirach watches the same hand over snow and cloud and season — *By his commandment he makes the snow to fall aplace, and sends swiftly the lightnings of his judgment. Through this the treasures are opened: and clouds fly forth as fowls* (Sirach 43:13-14). The crowned year, the dropping fatness, the singing valleys — all are the goodness of Yahuah poured out over the whole earth.

threads.title: Thou hast tried us, as silver is tried — the furnace of affliction
threads.summary_md: *For thou, O Elohim (God), hast proved us: thou hast tried us, as silver is tried. Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins... we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place* (Psalm 66:10-12). The prophets name the furnace as Yahuah's own refining of His people. *Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction* (Isaiah 48:10); and it is the two-house ingathering — *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried: they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people* (Zechariah 13:9); *he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver* (Malachi 3:3); and the heart itself is the metal — *The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but Yahuah (LORD) trieth the hearts* (Proverbs 17:3). Peter carries the fire forward — *the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory* (1 Peter 1:7). And the restored wisdom sings it twice: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5); *Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering* (Wisdom 3:5-6). The fire is not the curse but the refining: the tried people are brought out into a wealthy place, received as an offering, owned again as His own — *It is my people.*

threads.title: Thy dead men shall live — the resurrection of the dust, the first and the great
threads.summary_md: After the travail that brought forth only wind (26:17-18), the prophet breaks into the resurrection keystone of the whole canon: *Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead* (Isaiah 26:19). Daniel speaks the LATERAL twin: *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2). The Formed Son owns the voice that raises them, and names the last hour, when all the graves give up their dead: *the hour is coming, in the which all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life* (John 5:28-29) — the voice of the Son who *hath life in himself*, who has a Father. It is bodily, and it comes in its order. Isaiah sets the rising in the indignation: *Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers... until the indignation be overpast. For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity* (Isaiah 26:20-21) — and Paul comforts with it: *the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first* (1 Thessalonians 4:16), the first resurrection, of the righteous seed only; of the others Isaiah says *they are deceased, they shall not rise* (Isaiah 26:14). The reign follows, and at the end the last trump, the seventh: *the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible* (1 Corinthians 15:52), and then *Death is swallowed up in victory* (1 Corinthians 15:54) — the very promise Isaiah sang one chapter before, *He will swallow up death in victory* (Isaiah 25:8). And the first rising is the TWO-HOUSE resurrection — *Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezekiel 37:12), the dry bones of *the whole house of Yashar'el (Israel)* raised and the two sticks made one. The restored witnesses sing the same rising: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1); and the martyred brother answers the tyrant, *the King of the world shall raise us up, who have died for his laws, to everlasting life* (2 Maccabees 7:9). Two resurrections, bodily — the first at his coming, the great one at the end — the one hope the whole library carries, never a secret rapture.

threads.title: He that spareth his rod hateth his son — the Father's loving chastening
threads.summary_md: The chapter binds discipline to love: *He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes* (Proverbs 13:24). The rod is not cruelty but care — and the pattern is the Father's own with His sons. Proverbs says it again and again: *despise not the chastening of Yahuah (LORD)... for whom Yahuah (LORD) loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth* (3:11-12); *the rod of correction shall drive it far from him* (22:15); *Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell* (23:14); *The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame* (29:15). The seeming hardness is mercy at its root — the rod is wielded to deliver the soul, and the father who withholds it does not love but hates, abandoning the son to a worse end. The restored witness keeps the same word: *He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end* (Sirach 30:1); *He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him* (30:2). And the NT lifts the proverb straight up to the Father: *whom Yahuah (Lord) loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth* (Hebrews 12:6); *what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?* (12:7) — the unchastened is no true son. The counter-charge guards the measure: *ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of Yahuah (Lord)* (Ephesians 6:4) — neither sparing the rod (which is hate) nor provoking to wrath (which is cruelty), but raising the child in the Father's own admonition.

threads.title: Rich yet nothing, poor yet great riches — and the wealth of the sinner laid up for the just
threads.summary_md: The chapter weighs true riches against false: *There is that maketh himself rich, yet hath nothing: there is that maketh himself poor, yet hath great riches* (Proverbs 13:7), with *Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase* (13:11) and *A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just* (13:22). Qoheleth groaned over the heaped wealth he must surrender: *I hated all my labour... because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me* (Ecclesiastes 2:18) — and he named the very transfer the proverb foretells: *to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before Elohim (God)* (2:26). Job saw the same: *He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver* (27:17). The self-made rich man trusts what he cannot keep — *He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch* (Proverbs 11:28). The restored witness draws the hoarder's portrait: *now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Sirach 11:19). And Yahusha (Jesus) tells the parable plain — *So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward Elohim (God)* (Luke 12:21) — while the risen Master rebukes the church that boasts its goods: *thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor* (Revelation 3:17). Paul holds the whole paradox: *as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things* (2 Corinthians 6:10). To be rich before men and bare before Yahuah is to have nothing; to be poor before men and rich toward Elohim is to possess all.

threads.title: In the fear of Yahuah is strong confidence — a fountain of life
threads.summary_md: The chapter carries the book's great motto in two couplets: *In the fear of Yahuah (LORD) is strong confidence: and his children shall have a place of refuge* (Proverbs 14:26), and *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death* (14:27). The fear of Yahuah is no cringing dread but the ground of confidence and the very fountain of life. It is the book's inclusio — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge* (1:7), *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom* (9:10), *the fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days* (10:27). And the fountain-of-life clause is word-for-word the Torah-clause of *The law of the wise is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death* (13:14): the fear of Yahuah and His law are the SAME fountain, departing the SAME snares of death — the Torah is not the curse but the very fountain of life. The restored witness sings it in one voice: *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom: and it was created with the faithful in the womb* (Sirach 1:14); *The root of wisdom is to fear Yahuah (God), and the branches thereof are long life* (Sirach 1:20). The fear that begins wisdom is the root whose branches are the long life the fountain gives.

threads.title: The sacrifice of the wicked an abomination — the prayer of the upright his delight
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets acceptable worship squarely on righteousness, framed by twin verses: *The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the prayer of the upright is his delight* (15:8), and *Yahuah (LORD) is far from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous* (15:29). This is obedience-above-ritual, NOT anti-sacrifice and NOT antinomian — the offering and the prayer alike are weighed by the heart and walk that bring them. The chapter itself frames the verses: *The way of the wicked is an abomination unto Yahuah (LORD): but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness* (15:9); *The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): but the words of the pure are pleasant words* (15:26). The same book states the measure twice more — *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?* (21:27) — and names the anti-antinomian twin: *He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination* (28:9). The prophets pronounce it over whole nations: *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me?... I delight not in the blood of bullocks* (Isaiah 1:11); *when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood* (Isaiah 1:15); *I hate, I despise your feast days... But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (Amos 5:21,24). Samuel sets the principle flat — *to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams* (1 Samuel 15:22) — and David sings it from the inside — *thou desirest not sacrifice... The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (Psalm 51:16-17). And the New Testament keeps the SAME rule, never abolishing it: *Now we know that Elohim (God) heareth not sinners: but if any man... doeth his will, him he heareth* (John 9:31); *whatsoever we ask, we receive of him, because we keep his commandments* (1 John 3:22). The restored witness states it whole — *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted* (Sirach 34:18); *The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked* (34:19); *When one prayeth, and another curses, whose voice will Yahuah (God) hear?* (34:24); *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough* (35:1). From Torah to prophets to Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witnesses the testimony is one: acceptable worship — sacrifice and prayer alike — flows from a righteous, Torah-keeping heart; the worship of the wicked is abomination.

threads.title: The fear of Yahuah the instruction of wisdom — before honour is humility
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes on the book's great motto and its humility-refrain in one verse: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility* (15:33). The whole chapter's reproof-and-instruction strand resolves here — *A fool despiseth his father's instruction: but he that regardeth reproof is prudent* (15:5); *The ear that heareth the reproof of life abideth among the wise* (15:31); *He that refuseth instruction despiseth his own soul: but he that heareth reproof getteth understanding* (15:32) — for the instruction of wisdom is the fear of Yahuah, and the teachable ear is the humble one. The motto is the book's recurring frame: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction* (1:7); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom* (9:10). And the humility-half is its own refrain: *Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility* (18:12); *By humility and the fear of Yahuah (LORD) are riches, and honour, and life* (22:4). The New Testament carries the humility-before-honour whole — *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6); *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* (James 4:10); *be clothed with humility: for Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble* (1 Peter 5:5); *Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of Elohim (God), that he may exalt you in due time* (1 Peter 5:6). The restored witness keeps the fear-half — *To fear Yahuah (God) is the beginning of wisdom* (Sirach 1:14). The way to honour runs down through humility; the way to wisdom runs through the fear of Yahuah. (Cross-lateral to the fear-of-Yahuah motto threads.)

threads.title: A merry heart hath a continual feast
threads.summary_md: The chapter twins the heart and the countenance through the joy that springs from within: *A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken* (15:13); *All the days of the afflicted are evil: but he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast* (15:15); *The light of the eyes rejoiceth the heart: and a good report maketh the bones fat* (15:30). The same book says it again: *A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones* (17:22) — the glad heart heals, the broken heart wastes. And the source of the feast is named where the Torah was read aloud and the people wept: *neither be ye sorry; for the joy of Yahuah (LORD) is your strength* (Nehemiah 8:10) — the continual feast is no idle mirth but the strength that joy in Yahuah gives. The restored witness roots that joy in the fear of Yahuah itself: *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life* (Sirach 1:12) — binding the merry heart back to the fear-motto that closes the chapter. The cheerful countenance is the overflow of a heart glad in Yahuah.

threads.title: A man's heart deviseth his way — but Yahuah directeth his steps
threads.summary_md: The chapter's spine is the sovereignty of Yahuah over man — man proposes, Yahuah disposes. It opens the theme: *The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from Yahuah (LORD)* (16:1); it states it bare at its center: *A man's heart deviseth his way: but Yahuah (LORD) directeth his steps* (16:9); and it seals it at the close, down to the cast lot: *The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of Yahuah (LORD)* (16:33). This is no fatalism but the Father's rule over the steps of the one who walks. Jeremiah confesses it as a prayer: *O Yahuah (LORD), I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps* (10:23). The same book of Proverbs says it twice more: *There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of Yahuah (LORD), that shall stand* (19:21); *Man's goings are of Yahuah (LORD); how can a man then understand his own way?* (20:24). And David sings the comfort hidden in it: *The steps of a good man are ordered by Yahuah (LORD): and he delighteth in his way* (Psalm 37:23) — the directing is not a cold decree but a delight. The chapter gives man his part too: *Commit thy works unto Yahuah (LORD), and thy thoughts shall be established* (16:3); and even the enemy's peace is His doing — *When a man's ways please Yahuah (LORD), he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him* (16:7), as Abimelech confessed to Isaac, *We saw certainly that Yahuah (LORD) was with thee... they departed from him in peace* (Genesis 26:28-31). The New Testament never abolishes this rule but presses it: *ye ought to say, If Yahuah (Lord) will, we shall live, and do this, or that* (James 4:15); *it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of Elohim (God) that sheweth mercy* (Romans 9:16); *it is Elohim (God) which worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure* (Philippians 2:13). Even the very lot of 16:33 falls as He disposes — *the lot fell upon Matthias* (Acts 1:26). The restored witness frames it with the potter: *As the clay is in the potter's hand, to fashion it at his pleasure: so man is in the hand of him that made him* (Sirach 33:13), and counsels the only safe response — *pray to the Most High, that he will direct your way in truth* (Sirach 37:15). From Torah-history to the prophets to the psalmist to the apostles to the restored witnesses, the testimony is one: man may devise, but the Father is sovereign over the heart, the tongue, the steps, and the lot.

threads.title: By mercy and truth iniquity is purged
threads.summary_md: *By mercy and truth iniquity is purged: and by the fear of Yahuah (LORD) men depart from evil* (16:6). The two — mercy and truth — are bound together through the canon: *Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart* (Proverbs 3:3); *Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other* (Psalm 85:10); and Micah gathers the whole walk into them — *what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (6:8). In the Formed Son the pair takes flesh: *the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us... full of grace and truth* (John 1:14); *the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (John 1:17) — which does not unseat the Torah given by Moses, but names the One in whom the iniquity-purging mercy and truth come to the people. And the purging itself is consummated in the blood: *the blood of Messiah (Christ), who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to Elohim (God), purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living Elohim (God)* (Hebrews 9:14). The restored witness sets mercy and the departing-from-evil beside the purging: *alms makes an atonement for sins* (Sirach 3:30); *to depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to Yahuah (God); and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation* (Sirach 35:3). The second half of the proverb is its own road home — *by the fear of Yahuah (LORD) men depart from evil* — and the highway of the upright is the same: *to depart from evil: he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul* (16:17).

threads.title: Pride goeth before destruction
threads.summary_md: *Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall* (16:18) — the chapter's famous warning, framed by *Every one that is proud in heart is an abomination to Yahuah (LORD): though hand join in hand, he shall not be unpunished* (16:5) and answered by *Better it is to be of an humble spirit with the lowly, than to divide the spoil with the proud* (16:19). The same book sounds the sequence again and again: *When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom* (11:2); *Before destruction the heart of man is haughty, and before honour is humility* (18:12); *A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit* (29:23). The archetype is the fall behind all falls: *I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of Elohim (God)... Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit* (Isaiah 14:13-15); *Thine heart was lifted up because of thy beauty... I will cast thee to the ground* (Ezekiel 28:17). And it is made flesh in a king brought low and restored, who confessed it from the far side: *those that walk in pride he is able to abase* (Daniel 4:37). The New Testament keeps the rule unbroken, twice setting down the same standing word: *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble* (1 Peter 5:5); *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6); and Yahusha states the exchange plain — *whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted* (Luke 14:11). The restored witness traces the root: *Pride is hateful before Yahuah (God) and man* (Sirach 10:7); *The beginning of pride is when one departs from Yahuah (God), and his heart is turned away from his Maker* (10:12); *pride is the beginning of sin... and therefore Yahuah (God)... overthrew them utterly* (10:13). The haughty spirit is first a turned-away heart; the fall follows the turning.

threads.title: The fining pot for silver — but Yahuah trieth the hearts
threads.summary_md: The chapter turns to the inner man and the One who proves it: *The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but Yahuah (LORD) trieth the hearts* (Proverbs 17:3). As metal is proved in the fire, so the heart is proved by Yahuah Himself — and the same book says it twice more: *Yahuah (LORD) weigheth the spirits* (16:2); *Yahuah (LORD) pondereth the hearts* (21:2). The man whose ways are clean in his own eyes cannot try himself; only Yahuah can. David, far from dreading the furnace, asks for it: *Examine me, O Yahuah (LORD), and prove me; try my reins and my heart* (Psalm 26:2). Jeremiah states it as Yahuah's declared office: *I Yahuah (LORD) search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways* (17:10). And the figure runs forward to the Formed Son: He comes *like a refiner's fire* (Malachi 3:2), to *sit as a refiner and purifier of silver... and purge them as gold and silver* (3:3); the covenant remnant is brought through — *I will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried... It is my people* (Zechariah 13:9). The NT keeps the furnace whole and names its purpose: *the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (1 Peter 1:7); *the fire shall try every man's work of what sort it is* (1 Corinthians 3:13). The risen Messiah claims the heart-trying as His own: *I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts* (Revelation 2:23). The restored witness binds the figure tight: *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). From Proverbs to the prophets to the apostles, the trying is not destruction but refining — Yahuah proves the heart to bring the true gold through.

threads.title: Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker
threads.summary_md: The proverb joins the poor man to Yahuah so tightly that what is done to him is done to his Maker: *Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker: and he that is glad at calamities shall not be unpunished* (Proverbs 17:5) — the verbatim near-twin of *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31). The ground is creation itself: *The rich and poor meet together: Yahuah (LORD) is the maker of them all* (22:2); *So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him* (Genesis 1:27). Job knew it toward his own servants: *Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?* (31:15). Because the poor man bears the image of his Maker, mercy to him is a loan to Yahuah — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD)* (19:17) — and mockery of him is reproach to Yahuah. The Formed Son seals it: *Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me* (Matthew 25:40), and its withholding — *Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me* (25:45). Yaakov rebukes the very mockery: *ye have despised the poor* (2:6), whom *Elohim (God) chosen... rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom* (2:5). The restored witness charges the same care: *defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1). To mock the poor is to reproach Yahuah; to be glad at his calamity shall not go unpunished.

threads.title: A friend loveth at all times — a brother born for adversity
threads.summary_md: The proverb names the friendship that holds when everything else gives way: *A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity* (Proverbs 17:17). The same book knows this friend who outlasts even kin — *there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother* (18:24) — and Ruth lives it in her bitterest hour: *Intreat me not to leave thee... for whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy Elohim (God) my Elohim (God)* (1:16). The Formed Son crowns the figure: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends* (John 15:13) — the love that loves at all times is the love that lays down its life. The restored witness treasures the same friend: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure* (Sirach 6:14); *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him* (6:16). The brother born for adversity is the faithful friend who fears Yahuah — a defence, a treasure, and the very medicine of life.

threads.title: A merry heart doeth good like a medicine — and the wise restrained tongue
threads.summary_md: The proverb knows the body and the spirit are bound together: *A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones* (Proverbs 17:22). The same book twins it — *A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance: but by sorrow of the heart the spirit is broken* (15:13); *he that is of a merry heart hath a continual feast* (15:15) — and Nehemiah names the source of the healing gladness: *neither be ye sorry; for the joy of Yahuah (LORD) is your strength* (8:10). The merry heart that does good like a medicine is not idle mirth but joy in Yahuah, strength against the broken spirit. The chapter closes on the wise, restrained tongue that the same glad-hearted wisdom keeps: *He that hath knowledge spareth his words: and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit* (17:27); *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding* (17:28). The book teaches it elsewhere — *In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin: but he that refraineth his lips is wise* (10:19) — and so does Yaakov: *let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath* (James 1:19). The fool is unmasked the moment he opens his mouth — *a fool's voice is known by multitude of words* (Ecclesiastes 5:3) — and the restored witness states the close outright: *There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise* (Sirach 20:5). The merry heart heals; the kept silence is counted wisdom.

threads.title: Thy saving health among all nations — the seed-promise: the nations praise WITH his people
threads.summary_md: The blessing on Yashar'el (Israel) turns outward into the saving of the nations — the missionary heart of the psalm: *That thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations. Let the people praise thee, O Elohim (God); let all the people praise thee. O let the nations be glad and sing for joy: for thou shalt judge the people righteously, and govern the nations upon earth* (Psalm 67:2-4). This is the Abrahamic promise unfolding. The blessing reaches the nations THROUGH the seed, never around it: *in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed* (Genesis 12:3); *in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice* (Genesis 22:18). Isaiah names the servant who carries it — and notice the order: *to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Yashar'el (Israel): I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth* (Isaiah 49:6) — the restoration of the houses and the light to the nations are ONE work. Paul takes the servant-word as his commission (*I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles... unto the ends of the earth*, Acts 13:47) and then stacks a catena that names the frame exactly: *that the Gentiles might glorify Elohim (God) for his mercy* (Romans 15:9); *Rejoice, ye Gentiles, with his people* (Romans 15:10); *Praise Yahuah (Lord), all ye Gentiles; and laud him, all ye people* (Romans 15:11). The nations praise WITH his people, not instead of them — for Yahuah has not cast away his people (Romans 11:1-2). The restored Tobit sings the same ingathering: *Many nations shall come from far to the name of Yahuah (God) with gifts in their hands... all generations shall praise you with great joy* (Tobit 13:11). The nations are gathered TO the Name, alongside Yashar'el, never displacing her.

threads.title: All the ends of the earth shall fear him — the ingathering of the scattered
threads.summary_md: The psalm closes with the farthest reach of the blessing: *Elohim (God) shall bless us; and all the ends of the earth shall fear him* (Psalm 67:7). The psalter elsewhere sees the same end — *All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto Yahuah (LORD): and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee* (Psalm 22:27) — and Isaiah issues the very call the psalm foresees answered: *Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am Elohim (God), and there is none else* (Isaiah 45:22). The restored Tobit binds this ends-of-earth fear to the two-house ingathering: *he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us* (Tobit 13:5). As Yahuah gathers His scattered people home out of all the nations, the ends of the earth themselves come to fear Him — the dispersion regathered and the nations turning, one harvest.

threads.title: In thee do I put my trust; let me never be confounded — the Rock, the stone in Zion
threads.summary_md: The prayer of the aged servant opens with the very words of an earlier psalm: *In thee, O Yahuah (LORD), do I put my trust: let me never be put to confusion. Deliver me in thy righteousness* (Psalm 71:1-2); *Be thou my strong habitation... thou art my rock and my fortress* (71:3). It is the twin of *In thee, O Yahuah (LORD), do I put my trust; let me never be ashamed: deliver me in thy righteousness* (Psalm 31:1) — one prayer taken up again at the close of a life. The Rock he makes his fortress is the Formed Son — *that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Messiah (Christ)* (1 Corinthians 10:4); *He is the Rock, his work is perfect* (Deuteronomy 32:4). And the never-confounded trust is the stone laid in Zion: *Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste* (Isaiah 28:16) — quoted by Paul and Peter as the standing promise — *whosoever believeth on him shall not be ashamed* (Romans 9:33; Romans 10:11); *he that believeth on him shall not be confounded* (1 Peter 2:6). The restored wisdom tests the plea against all the ages — *did ever any trust in Yahuah (God), and was confounded?* (Sirach 2:10). To trust the Rock is never to be put to shame.

threads.title: Forsake me not in old age — until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation
threads.summary_md: *Cast me not off in the time of old age; forsake me not when my strength faileth* (Psalm 71:9); *Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O Elohim (God), forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come* (71:18). The plea rests on the standing covenant word — *he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee* (Hebrews 13:5). And the grayheaded servant's task is the commanded work of transmission: *We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of Yahuah (LORD), and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done* (Psalm 78:4); *thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way* (Deuteronomy 6:7) — the Torah handed down. The restored wisdom crowns the very man the psalm pictures: *Much experience is the crown of old men, and the fear of Yahuah (God) is their glory* (Sirach 25:6). The aged are not cast off; their long experience is given to declare His strength to the generation to come.

threads.title: Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim — then understood I their end
threads.summary_md: This is the hinge of the whole psalm, the turning of the theodicy: *When I thought to know this, it was too painful for me; Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end* (Psalm 73:16-17). The riddle of the prospering wicked cannot be solved by staring at the prosperity; it is broken in the appointed place of worship, where the latter-end is seen. The neighbouring psalm declares that end: *Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace. But the transgressors shall be destroyed together: the end of the wicked shall be cut off* (Psalm 37:37-38). The proverb names it: *There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death* (Proverbs 14:12). And Malachi promises the day when all will see it — answering the very despair (*It is vain to serve Elohim (God)... we call the proud happy*, 3:14-15) — *Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth Elohim (God) and him that serveth him not* (Malachi 3:18). The restored wisdom of Solomon sets the two ends side by side: *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (Wisdom 3:1) — they only *seemed to die* (3:2), and *in the time of their visitation they shall shine* (3:7) — while *the ungodly shall be punished according to their own imaginations, which have neglected the righteous, and forsaken Yahuah (God)* (Wisdom 3:10). The end is the answer the sanctuary gives.

threads.title: The furnace of affliction — I have refined thee, not cast thee off
threads.summary_md: Yahuah's lawsuit against an obstinate people does not end in their rejection but in their refining: *Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction* (Isaiah 48:10). The affliction is the assaying of the CHOSEN — the fire that proves and purifies, not the wrath that discards. Peter says it of the scattered strangers: *though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations* (1 Peter 1:6), *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (1 Peter 1:7). Malachi names the Refiner at his work: *he shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver... that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness* (Malachi 3:3). And Zechariah names the far side of the fire — the restored two-house bond: *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined... they shall call on my name, and I will hear them: I will say, It is my people; and they shall say, Yahuah (LORD) is my Elohim (God)* (Zechariah 13:9). The restored wisdom-witnesses say it twice over: *having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for Yahuah (God) proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:5-6); *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). The furnace is the love of the One who chose, refining a people he will not give up.

threads.title: Death and life are in the power of the tongue
threads.summary_md: The chapter gathers its mouth-sayings to a head at v.21: *Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof* (Proverbs 18:21) — drawing up the talebearer's words *as wounds* (18:8), the fool's mouth that is *his destruction* (18:7), and the belly *satisfied with the fruit of his mouth* (18:20). The book states the double power many ways: *The mouth of a righteous man is a well of life* (10:11), yet *he that refraineth his lips is wise* (10:19); *The tongue of the just is as choice silver* (10:20); *There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health* (12:18); *He that keepeth his mouth keepeth his life: but he that openeth wide his lips shall have destruction* (13:3); *A wholesome tongue is a tree of life: but perverseness therein is a breach in the spirit* (15:4). The Formed Son raises the proverb to the day of judgment: *every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment* (Matthew 12:36); *by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (12:37) — death and life in the tongue, weighed at the bar. And James draws the death-power out in full: *the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity* (3:6), *an unruly evil, full of deadly poison* (3:8). The restored witness measures it against the sword: *the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones* (Sirach 28:17); *Many have fallen by the edge of the sword: but not so many as have fallen by the tongue* (28:18). From Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witness the testimony is one — the tongue holds death and life, and a man eats the fruit of his own.

threads.title: A friend that sticketh closer than a brother
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets true friendship against a wounded brotherhood: *A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle* (Proverbs 18:19), and then *A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother* (18:24). The book defines the friend it praises — *A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity* (17:17); *Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful* (27:6); *Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not... better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off* (27:10). The history shows the friend in the flesh: *the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul* (1 Samuel 18:1), and the two *made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul* (18:3) — the king's own son loving David above his house. Ruth cleaves to Naomi past all natural claim: *whither thou goest, I will go... thy people shall be my people, and thy Elohim (God) my Elohim (God)* (Ruth 1:16). And the Formed Son is Himself the friend that sticks closest of all, showing the proverb's full measure: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends* (John 15:13); *I have called you friends* (15:15) — opening His Father's counsel to His own. The restored witness sings the same treasure: *A faithful friend is a strong defence... has found a treasure* (Sirach 6:14); *A faithful friend is the medicine of life; and they that fear Yahuah (God) shall find him* (6:16); *Forsake not an old friend* (9:10).

threads.title: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing — a favour of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: *Whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing, and obtaineth favour of Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 18:22). The good thing reaches all the way back to the garden, where the wife is Yahuah's own remedy for the single thing in creation He named *not good*: *It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him* (Genesis 2:18); *they shall be one flesh* (2:24). The favour-of-Yahuah is no figure of speech — the same book names the wife a gift, not a chance: *House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from Yahuah (LORD)* (19:14); and weighs the finding above all price: *Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies* (31:10). The NT carries the one-flesh ordinance unbroken, quoting the garden — *they two shall be one flesh* (Ephesians 5:31) — and upholds it as honourable, never a concession: *Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled* (Hebrews 13:4). The restored witness keeps the same blessing: *Blessed is the man that has a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double* (Sirach 26:1); *A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear Yahuah (God)* (26:3); *He that getteth a wife begins a possession, a help like to himself, and a pillar of rest* (36:24) — the very help meet of Eden. The wife found is a good thing because she is a favour apportioned by Yahuah to them that fear Him.

threads.title: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah
threads.summary_md: The keystone of the chapter makes mercy to the poor a transaction with Yahuah Himself: *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again* (Proverbs 19:17). The gift handed to the poor is not lost; it is a loan to Yahuah, and He is no man's debtor — *that which he hath given will he pay him again*. This is the Torah's own open-hand command set as a couplet: *thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother* (Deuteronomy 15:7); *Thou shalt surely give him, and thine heart shall not be grieved... Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in all thy works* (15:10); *Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy* (15:11). The same book sings the loan twice over — *he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31), *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor* (22:9), *He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack* (28:27) — and David opens it: *Blessed is he that considereth the poor: Yahuah (LORD) will deliver him in time of trouble* (Psalm 41:1). The New Testament makes the loan personal and names when it is repaid: the poor man received is Yahuah received — *Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me* (Matthew 25:40); the repayment is at the last day — *call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind... thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just* (Luke 14:13-14); and the manner is glad — *he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully* (2 Corinthians 9:6), *Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver* (9:7), *he hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever* (9:9). The restored witness binds the same charge to the commandment and to a treasure laid up: *defraud not the poor of his living* (Sirach 4:1), *bow down your ear to the poor* (4:8), *Help the poor for the commandment's sake* (29:9), *Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction* (29:12). From Torah to Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witnesses, the testimony is one: the open hand to the poor is a loan to Yahuah, and Yahuah repays. (The poor man honoured runs the whole chapter — *Better is the poor that walketh in his integrity, than he that is perverse in his lips* (19:1), *a poor man is better than a liar* (19:22) — against a world where *Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour* (19:4).)

threads.title: A false witness shall not be unpunished — the ninth word
threads.summary_md: Twice over, almost word for word, the chapter pronounces the doom of the lying witness: *A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall not escape* (Proverbs 19:5); *A false witness shall not be unpunished, and he that speaketh lies shall perish* (Proverbs 19:9). This is the ninth word of the Ten carried into a proverb: *Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour* (Exodus 20:16; Deuteronomy 5:20), *Thou shalt not raise a false report: put not thine hand with the wicked to be an unrighteous witness* (Exodus 23:1). The Torah even names the false witness's exact sentence — the judges *make diligent inquisition* (Deuteronomy 19:18), and *Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother* (19:19): the liar perishes by the very harm he meant for another, which is why he shall not escape. Proverbs numbers him among the things Yahuah hates — *A false witness that speaketh lies* (6:19) — and repeats the verdict — *a false witness deceit* (12:17), *A false witness shall perish* (21:28). The New Testament keeps the same measure, never abolishing it: false witnesses are the weapon raised against Stephen — *And set up false witnesses, which said, This man ceaseth not to speak blasphemous words against this holy place, and the law* (Acts 6:13) — and the end of all liars is sealed at the last — *all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death* (Revelation 21:8). The restored witness agrees: *Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good* (Sirach 7:13), *A thief is better than a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage* (Sirach 20:25). The ninth word stands; the chapter closes on it still — *An ungodly witness scorneth judgment* (19:28).

threads.title: The fear of Yahuah tendeth to life
threads.summary_md: The chapter gathers the book's great motto and binds it to life itself: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) tendeth to life: and he that hath it shall abide satisfied; he shall not be visited with evil* (Proverbs 19:23). The fear of Yahuah is not a dread that shrinks life but the very fountain of it — it tends to life, satisfies, and keeps from evil. This is the refrain of the whole book: *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of knowledge* (1:7); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom* (9:10); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) prolongeth days* (10:27); *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is a fountain of life, to depart from the snares of death* (14:27); *By humility and the fear of Yahuah (LORD) are riches, and honour, and life* (22:4). The restored witness sings it most fully of all: *The fear of Yahuah (God) is honour, and glory, and gladness, and a crown of rejoicing* (Sirach 1:11); *The fear of Yahuah (God) makes a merry heart, and gives joy, and gladness, and a long life* (1:12); and the *he shall not be visited with evil* of the proverb is its fearlessness — *Whoso fears Yahuah (God) shall not fear nor be afraid; for he is his hope* (34:14). The satisfied, evil-unvisited life of the proverb is precisely the life the fear of Yahuah opens, from the first chapter of Proverbs to the restored witness that sings the same.

threads.title: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul
threads.summary_md: The chapter sets the kept commandment as the keeping of one's own life: *He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die* (Proverbs 19:16). The Torah is no bondage; to keep it is to keep the soul, and to despise one's ways is death. The chapter circles the same truth from every side — *He that getteth wisdom loveth his own soul: he that keepeth understanding shall find good* (19:8), *Hear counsel, and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end* (19:20), and the guarded ear of *Cease, my son, to hear the instruction that causeth to err from the words of knowledge* (19:27). It is the Torah's own promise of life: *keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply* (Deuteronomy 30:16). The same book states both halves again — *Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed: but he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded* (Proverbs 13:13) — and charges the holding-fast — *Take fast hold of instruction; let her not go: keep her; for she is thy life* (4:13). And the New Testament keeps the bond unbroken, never severing love from the commandment: *If ye love me, keep my commandments* (John 14:15); so too the restored witness — *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you* (Sirach 1:26). The kept commandment keeps the soul; the despised way is death — the anti-antinomian couplet of the chapter.

threads.title: Say not, I will recompense evil — wait on Yahuah, and he shall save thee
threads.summary_md: The chapter leaves vengeance where it belongs: *Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on Yahuah (LORD), and he shall save thee* (Proverbs 20:22). The reason is Yahuah's own claim in the Song of Moses: *To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time* (Deuteronomy 32:35). The proverb is the Torah's love-command turned toward the one who wronged you: *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 19:18). The same book repeats it almost word for word — *Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me* (Proverbs 24:29) — and turns non-vengeance into active mercy: *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink* (Proverbs 25:21). The New Testament keeps the measure whole and grounds it by quoting the Torah by name: *avenge not yourselves... for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith Yahuah (Lord)* (Romans 12:19); *Recompense to no man evil for evil* (Romans 12:17); *See that none render evil for evil unto any man* (1 Thessalonians 5:15); *Not rendering evil for evil... but contrariwise blessing* (1 Peter 3:9). And Yahusha (Jesus) lifts it to its summit: *Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you* (Matthew 5:44) — the non-recompense fulfilled as active love, not erased. The restored witness states the danger and the way: *He that revengeth shall find vengeance from Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 28:1); *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest* (Sirach 28:2) — the one who releases vengeance is the one whose own prayer is heard; *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour: remember the covenant of the Highest* (Sirach 28:7). From Torah to prophets to Proverbs to the apostles to the restored witnesses, the word is one: do not recompense; wait on Yahuah, and He shall save.

threads.title: To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah than sacrifice
threads.summary_md: The framework heavyweight of the chapter is a key, not a key to the lock of the Torah: *To do justice and judgment is more acceptable to Yahuah (LORD) than sacrifice* (Proverbs 21:3). This is obedience-and-mercy set ABOVE empty ritual — NOT the abolition of the sacrificial system. The SAME Torah commands both the justice and the offering; the prophets and Yahusha (Jesus) rebuke ritual divorced from obedience, never the appointed worship itself. Samuel set the measure first, to a king who kept the spoil and disobeyed the voice: *Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams* (1 Samuel 15:22). Hosea sang it — *For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* (6:6). Micah weighed *thousands of rams* against the requirement and found it: *what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (6:8). Isaiah set the courts full of sacrifice against the un-done justice — *To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me?* (1:11) — and sent the people back to it: *seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow* (1:17). David named the acceptable heart-posture beneath the offering — *The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (51:17). Amos thundered it — *let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (5:24). And the same chapter gives the dark twin: *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?* (21:27) — it is the WICKED man's sacrifice, the rite in place of justice, that is loathed. The New Testament keeps the SAME measure, never abolishing it: Yahusha quotes Hosea twice — *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13; 12:7) — sending the Pharisees to *learn what that meaneth*; and the scribe who saw that love *is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices* (Mark 12:33) was answered as not far from the kingdom. The restored witness states both sides plainest: the unjust offering refused — *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous... The most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked* (Sirach 34:18-19) — and the kept Torah accepted — *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough* (Sirach 35:1). From Samuel to the prophets to Proverbs to Yahusha to the restored witness, the testimony is one: the justice and the offering both belong to Yahuah, and the doing of justice is the more acceptable approach — the empty offering of the unjust is the only sacrifice refused.

threads.title: Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor shall cry himself, but shall not be heard
threads.summary_md: The chapter binds the heard prayer to a heard poor man: *Whoso stoppeth his ears at the cry of the poor, he also shall cry himself, but shall not be heard* (Proverbs 21:13). The stopped ear is answered in kind — the measure is given back. To shut the ear to the poor is to reproach Yahuah Himself — *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31) — and the same book twins the stopped ear with the hidden eye that inherits the curse: *he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse* (28:27). The Torah warned the very cry: shut not thine hand, *and he cry unto Yahuah (LORD) against thee, and it be sin unto thee* (Deuteronomy 15:9). Yahusha (Jesus) drew the whole law of it in the servant who would not show the mercy he had received, *delivered... to the tormentors* (Matthew 18:34); and Ya'aqob (James) states it as a verdict — *he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment* (James 2:13). The restored witness names the stopped ear as the defrauding that *make[s] the needy eyes to wait long* (Sirach 4:1) and gives the exact reversal of the proverb — the stopper's cry goes unheard, but the poor man's is heard: *if he curse you in the bitterness of his soul, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him* (Sirach 4:6). The other side of the chapter is the same mercy pursued instead of stopped — *He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour* (21:21).

threads.title: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens with a weighing: *A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold* (Proverbs 22:1). What endures is not the silver and gold but the name and the favour a man keeps before Yahuah and before men. Qoheleth weighs it the same: *A good name is better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth* (Ecclesiastes 7:1). The loving favour set above gold is named in the book itself — *So shalt thou find favour and good understanding in the sight of Elohim (God) and man* (Proverbs 3:4) — and its endurance against the wealth that perishes: *The memory of the just is blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rot* (Proverbs 10:7). The restored witness presses the choice home: *Have regard to your name; for that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold* (Sirach 41:12); *A good life has but few days: but a good name endureth for ever* (Sirach 41:13). Riches are few and the days fewer; the good name alone abides past death.

threads.title: The rich and poor meet together — Yahuah is the maker of them all
threads.summary_md: At the heart of the chapter's poor-cluster stands the levelling truth: *The rich and poor meet together: Yahuah (LORD) is the maker of them all* (Proverbs 22:2). Because ONE Maker formed both, the treatment of the poor is bound directly to the honour of Yahuah: *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (14:31); *Whoso mocketh the poor reproacheth his Maker* (17:5); *The poor and the deceitful man meet together: Yahuah (LORD) lighteneth both their eyes* (29:13). Job grounds it in the womb, as the ground of justice to his servant: *Did not he that made me in the womb make him? and did not one fashion us in the womb?* (31:15); and Elihu draws the verdict: Yahuah *accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands* (34:19). The chapter's own couplets turn on this: *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor* (22:9), and *He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches... shall surely come to want* (22:16). The NT makes the one-Maker truth the law's own measure: *if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors* (James 2:9); *Hath not Elohim (God) chosen the poor of this world rich in faith* (James 2:5); *Of a truth I perceive that Elohim (God) is no respecter of persons* (Acts 10:34). And the restored witness: *poverty and riches, come of Yahuah (God)* (Sirach 11:14). The rich and the poor meet on one ground — the one Maker who shows no partiality.

threads.title: Train up a child in the way he should go — the covenant handed down
threads.summary_md: The chapter carries the generational covenant charge: *Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it* (Proverbs 22:6). The *way he should go* is not generic parenting but the covenant way — the way of Yahuah, the Torah handed down father to son. It is the Shema's own command: *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children* (Deuteronomy 6:6-7); *ye shall teach them your children* (Deuteronomy 11:19). It is the very thing Abraham was chosen for: *I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of Yahuah (LORD)* (Genesis 18:19) — the discipling of the seed into the covenant. Asaph sings the handing-down: *We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 78:4); *he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Yashar'el (Israel)... that the generation to come might know them* (Psalm 78:5), *that they might set their hope in Elohim (God)... but keep his commandments* (Psalm 78:7). The other face of the proverb — *Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him* (22:15) — is the loving discipline that holds the child to the way: *He that spareth his rod hateth his son: but he that loveth him chasteneth him betimes* (13:24); *Withhold not correction from the child... shalt deliver his soul from hell* (23:13-14). The NT keeps the charge whole, never abolished: *bring them up in the nurture and admonition of Yahuah (Lord)* (Ephesians 6:4); and shows it fulfilled in Timothy — *from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures* (2 Timothy 3:15), the Tanakh trained into him young. The restored witness binds love to the rod: *He that loves his son causeth him oft to feel the rod, that he may have joy of him in the end* (Sirach 30:1); *He that chastiseth his son shall have joy in him* (Sirach 30:2). The way trained in from a child is the way not departed from when old — the covenant carried into the next generation.

threads.title: Rob not the poor — Yahuah will plead their cause
threads.summary_md: The words of the wise turn to the defenceless: *Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate: For Yahuah (LORD) will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them* (Proverbs 22:22-23). Yahuah Himself is the poor man's advocate, exactly as the Torah warned: *Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child. If thou afflict them in any wise, and they cry at all unto me, I will surely hear their cry* (Exodus 22:22-23). The prophets make Him the swift witness who pleads that cause: *I will be a swift witness against... those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless* (Malachi 3:5); and the judge of the grinders: *What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor?* (Isaiah 3:15). The same book sets the open hand against the robbing hand — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again* (Proverbs 19:17). The restored witness weighs the robbing as bloodshed: *defraud not the poor of his living* (Sirach 4:1); *The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood* (Sirach 34:21). To rob the poor is to take a life Yahuah Himself will avenge — He pleads their cause and spoils the soul of those that spoiled them.

threads.title: They have cast fire into thy sanctuary — the burned-house lament and its rededication
threads.summary_md: The heart of the lament is the ruined house: *They have cast fire into thy sanctuary, they have defiled by casting down the dwelling place of thy name to the ground. They said in their hearts, Let us destroy them together: they have burned up all the synagogues of Elohim (God) in the land* (Psalm 74:7-8). The twin Asaph psalm sings the same ruin: *O Elohim (God), the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps* (Psalm 79:1). Jeremiah's dirge names the abhorred house: *Yahuah (Lord) hath cast off his altar, he hath abhorred his sanctuary... they have made a noise in the house of Yahuah (LORD), as in the day of a solemn feast* (Lamentations 2:7). And the restored history of the Maccabees shows the lament both realized and answered: *when they saw the sanctuary desolate, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned up, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest... they rent their clothes, and made great lamentation* (1 Maccabees 4:38-39); then *made up the sanctuary, and the things that were within the temple, and hallowed the courts* (1 Maccabees 4:48). The desolations Asaph lifts before Yahuah — *Lift up thy feet unto the perpetual desolations* (74:3) — hold the hope of the house rebuilt and the courts hallowed again.

threads.title: He putteth down one, and setteth up another — the One who abases and exalts
threads.summary_md: *For promotion cometh neither from the east, nor from the west, nor from the south. But Elohim (God) is the judge: he putteth down one, and setteth up another* (Psalm 75:6-7). Promotion is from no quarter of earth but from the hand of the Judge alone. Hannah sang the spring of it: *Yahuah (LORD) maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes... for the pillars of the earth are the LORD'S* (1 Samuel 2:7-8) — and the One who bears the pillars (*I bear up the pillars of it*, 75:3) is the One who casts down and sets up. Daniel saw the same hand over the thrones: *he removeth kings, and setteth up kings* (Daniel 2:21). Miryam sang it again at the door of the gospel: *He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree* (Luke 1:52). James turns it to a charge: *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* (James 4:10). And the restored wisdom sings the same reversal: *Yahuah (God) has cast down the thrones of proud princes, and set up the meek in their stead* (Sirach 10:14). The abased He exalts; the proud He casts down — this is the settled way of the Judge.

threads.title: Thou leddest thy people like a flock — the Shepherd who led them through the sea
threads.summary_md: The second deed remembered is the Red Sea, and the psalm paints the theophany of the crossing: *The waters saw thee, O Elohim (God), the waters saw thee; they were afraid: the depths also were troubled... Thy way is in the sea, and thy path in the great waters, and thy footsteps are not known. Thou leddest thy people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron* (Psalm 77:16-20). The history is the Exodus crossing — *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left* (Exod 14:22). Isaiah names the unseen One who did it: *Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock?... That led them by the right hand of Moses with his glorious arm, dividing the water before them* (Isaiah 63:11-12); *Art thou not it which hath dried the sea... that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?* (Isaiah 51:10). The led-like-a-flock Shepherd is the same who *made his own people to go forth like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock* (Psalm 78:52) and who *shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom* (Isaiah 40:11) — the Formed Son who led His people through the deep. The restored wisdom sings the same crossing — *Brought them through the Red sea, and led them through much water* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:18). The dark night that opened the psalm is answered by the Shepherd who has already led His flock through the great waters.

threads.title: He rained down manna — angels' food, the bread from heaven
threads.summary_md: In the wilderness rehearsal Yahuah feeds them from above: *Though he had commanded the clouds from above, and opened the doors of heaven, And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them of the corn of heaven. Man did eat angels' food: he sent them meat to the full* (Psalm 78:23-25). This is the Exodus gift — *Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you... that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no* (Exodus 16:4). The restored wisdom sings the very phrase: *thou feddest thy own people with angels' food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20).
