Through this sealed line runs the genealogy of the Messiah: *Salathiel begat Zorobabel* (Matthew 1:12), *Zorobabel begat Abiud* (Matthew 1:13), *the son of Zorobabel, which was the son of Salathiel* (Luke 3:27) — the royal seed preserved from the curse all the way to the Formed Son who took flesh. The shaken kingdoms give way to the throne that cannot fall: *the Elohim (God) of heaven shall set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed... and it shall stand for ever* (Daniel 2:44). And the restored witness magnifies the very pair Haggai addressed: *How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand: So was Jesus the son of Josedec: who in their time builded the house, and set up an holy temple to Yahuah (God), which was prepared for everlasting glory* (Ecclesiasticus 49:11-12) — Zerubbabel the signet and Joshua the high priest, builders of the latter house *prepared for everlasting glory*, the very glory *greater than of the former* (Haggai 2:9) that Haggai foretold.

threads.title: Tabitha, Arise — the Father Raises the Dead, Once Through the Prophets, Now Through His Son's Name
threads.summary_md:
Come and see that the power to raise the dead has always been Yahuah's. *But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up* (Acts 9:40). Peter kneels first — the prophet bows, the Father raises — and *many believed in Yahuah* (Acts 9:42).

Elijah walked this path: *And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto Yahuah (LORD)... let this child's soul come into him again* (1 Kings 17:21); *And Yahuah (LORD) heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived* (1 Kings 17:22). So did Elisha: *And he went up, and lay upon the child... and the flesh of the child waxed warm* (2 Kings 4:34); *Then the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes* (2 Kings 4:35) — the very gesture Tabitha makes, the dead opening their eyes.

And the promise runs to a whole nation: *Son of Adam, can these bones live? And I answered, O Yahuah (Lord) GOD, thou knowest* (Ezekiel 37:3); *Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live* (Ezekiel 37:5). Israel's own wisdom confessed it: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). Through Elijah, through Elisha, through Peter in Yahusha's name, and at the last over all the slain of His people — the Father is the giver of breath and life.

threads.title: Acts 11:27-30 — Agabus, the dearth, and the Torah of the open hand
threads.summary_md: *And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world... Then the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren which dwelt in Judæa* (Acts 11:28-29). Two old patterns meet here. First the prophet forewarns: as Yoseph was shown the famine — *Behold, there come seven years of great plenty* (Genesis 41:29) and *there shall arise after them seven years of famine* (Genesis 41:30) — and laid up bread to keep a household alive, so Agabus signifies the dearth that the body may prepare. Then the body answers in the very words of the Torah: *thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother* (Deuteronomy 15:7); *thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him* (Deuteronomy 15:8). The commandment was never abolished — it breathes. *The liberal soul shall be made fat* (Proverbs 11:25); *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 19:17). The second-Temple sages kept the same reading: *Help the poor for the commandment's sake* (Sirach 29:9) — mercy done for the commandment's sake, not in place of it. And the apostle who carried this relief later wrote how it is given: *Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver* (2 Corinthians 9:7). One people caring for one people across the distance — the Torah of the open hand, alive. The library is one, and it ain't new.

threads.title: James slain with the sword — the blood of the just, the feast still kept
threads.summary_md: **Come and see** — the first of the twelve to fall. *And he killed James the brother of John with the sword* (Acts 12:2); and because it pleased the people, Herod took Peter also, *(Then were the days of unleavened bread.)* (Acts 12:3). This is no new grief. *Their blood have they shed like water round about Jerusalem; and there was none to bury them* (Psalm 79:3) — Asaph's lament rises under it, the same *how long?* (Psalm 79:5) Peter would need that night. It falls in the city *that have shed the blood of the just in the midst of her* (Lamentations 4:13), the long lament continued. The sword itself was foreseen: *Awake, O sword, against my shepherd... smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered* (Zechariah 13:7) — the word the Formed Son had already taken over His own twelve, *for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad* (Matthew 26:31). He drank the cup first; James drinks after Him, going up to the altar where the martyrs wait — *I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of Elohim (God)... How long, O Yahuah (Lord)... dost thou not judge and avenge our blood?* (Revelation 6:9-10). And mark the season Luke is careful to give: *ye shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations... by an ordinance for ever* (Exodus 12:14). Decades after the resurrection the days of unleavened bread are still being KEPT — *Therefore let us keep the feast... with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth* (1 Corinthians 5:8). The Torah is not abolished by the gospel; the apostles live it. And the martyr dies for that same old faith: *be you zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers... so shall you receive great honour and an everlasting name* (1 Maccabees 2:50-51). James wins the everlasting name — not for a new thing, but for the covenant of the fathers, the library that is one and ain't new.

threads.title: But the word of Elohim grew and multiplied — the tyrant struck, the word unstoppable
threads.summary_md: **Come and see** the contrast that closes the chapter. The king is hailed *It is the voice of a god, and not of a man* (Acts 12:22), and the same hour *the angel of Yahuah (Lord) smote him, because he gave not Elohim (God) the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost* (Acts 12:23). Then one line, quiet and unstoppable: *But the word of Elohim (God) grew and multiplied* (Acts 12:24). The tyrant returns to dust; the Father's word does not return void — *it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it* (Isaiah 55:11). It is the oldest law of His people under a tyrant: *the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew* (Exodus 1:12). Pharaoh could not stop Yashar'el; Herod cannot stop the word — *grew and multiplied* echoes Egypt word for word, and echoes the Creator's first blessing: *Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth* (Genesis 1:28). What He blessed at the beginning He blesses still. And the proud king on his throne? *Why do the heathen rage... The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed* (Psalm 2:1-2) — yet *He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: Yahuah (Lord) shall have them in derision* (Psalm 2:4). The throne in Caesarea is nothing before the throne in heaven. Luke sounds the refrain again later — *So mightily grew the word of Elohim (God) and prevailed* (Acts 19:20). And Mattathias named the end of every such tyrant long before: *Fear not then the words of a sinful man: for his glory shall be dung and worms. To day he shall be lifted up and to morrow he shall not be found* (1 Maccabees 2:62-63). Herod eaten of worms is that word to the letter — while the word of Elohim multiplies on. The library is one, and it ain't new.

threads.title: When Ye Come Together Not for the Better: The Table That Shames the Poor
threads.summary_md:
*Now in this that I declare unto you I praise you not, that ye come together not for the better, but for the worse* (1 Corinthians 11:17). The trouble: *in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken* (11:21). And Paul's sharpest word: *or despise ye the assembly of Elohim (God), and shame them that have not?* (11:22). A gathering meant to embody the covenant has become a place where the poor are humiliated.

This is a Torah failure at the table. *If there be among you a poor man of one of thy brethren... thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother* (Deuteronomy 15:7); *Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land* (Deuteronomy 15:11). The open-hand statute is being trampled where the bread is broken.

Isaiah names the fast Yahuah actually chooses: *Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house?* (Isaiah 58:7); *And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity* (Isaiah 58:10). Feed the afflicted and light rises; shame them and the meal turns *for the worse.*

And the injustice strikes upward: *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor* (Proverbs 14:31). The second-Temple sages weighed it the same — *The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood* (Sirach 34:21).

Most piercing of all, Amos pronounces the verdict over an empty feast: *I hate, I despise your feast days, and I will not smell in your solemn assemblies* (Amos 5:21) — *But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream* (Amos 5:24). Paul's *I praise you not* IS Amos's verdict spoken over the Corinthian supper. The remedy is not more ceremony but justice and mercy: tarry one for another, shame no one. Come and see: the whole library guards the poor at the table.

threads.title: Let a Man Examine Himself: Reverence at the Meal, the Father's Chastening
threads.summary_md:
*Wherefore whosoever shall eat this bread, and drink this cup of Yahusha (the Lord), unworthily, shall be guilty of the body and blood of Yahusha (the Lord)* (1 Corinthians 11:27). The covenant meal is not common, and to handle it carelessly is grave.

The ancient ground is Nadab and Abihu: *And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, took either of them his censer... and offered strange fire before Yahuah (LORD), which he commanded them not* (Leviticus 10:1). The holy thing approached unworthily. And the word over it: *I will be sanctified in them that come nigh me, and before all the people I will be glorified* (Leviticus 10:3). To *discern the body* is to come nigh in awe.

So Paul says, *let a man examine himself* (11:28) — David's own prayer: *Examine me, O Yahuah (LORD), and prove me; try my reins and my heart* (Psalms 26:2); and the turning of Lamentations, *Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to Yahuah (LORD)* (Lamentations 3:40). Self-examination unto repentance: *if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged* (11:31).

And here is the gospel comfort in the warning. *But when we are judged, we are chastened of Yahuah (the Lord), that we should not be condemned with the world* (11:32). This is not wrath against the rejected. *My son, despise not the chastening of Yahuah (LORD); neither be weary of his correction: for whom Yahuah (LORD) loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth* (Proverbs 3:11-12). The weak and sickly are not cast off — they are SONS being corrected by a Father who delights in them. Ben Sira read it the same: *gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Sirach 2:5). The fire proves the son it loves. Come and see: the chastening is a Father's, never a judge's condemnation.

threads.title: Elohim is in you of a truth — the convicting word draws the outsider in
threads.summary_md:
**Come and see** — "But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not... the secrets of his heart are made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship Elohim, and report that Elohim is in you of a truth" (1 Corinthians 14:24-25). The prophetic word lays a stranger's heart bare, and he confesses that the Father is among his people — and that confession is the prophets' own hope.

Isaiah saw the nations bow toward Yashar'el (Israel) with these very words: *they shall fall down unto thee, they shall make supplication unto thee, saying, Surely Elohim (God) is in thee; and there is none else, there is no Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 45:14). Zechariah painted the two-house gathering: *ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Yahudi (Jew), saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that Elohim (God) is with you* (Zechariah 8:23). Solomon had prayed for exactly this stranger: *do according to all that the stranger calleth to thee for: that all people of the earth may know thy name* (1 Kings 8:43).

The heart is laid open because Yahuah already knows it: *O Yahuah (LORD), thou hast searched me, and known me* (Psalms 139:1). Ben Sira sings the same searching Elohim: *He seeks out the deep, and the heart... for Yahuah (God) knoweth all that may be known* (Sirach 42:18). And the word that does the convicting is living: *For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful... and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart* (Hebrews 4:12). The outsider falling down is the nations drawn home — not Israel cast off, but the stranger grafted into the people where Elohim dwells.

threads.title: Shall We Receive Good and Not Receive Evil — the Furnace of the Upright
threads.summary_md: The accuser *smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown* (Job 2:7), and the perfect man is reduced to scraping himself with a potsherd among the ashes (Job 2:8). His wife voices despair — *curse Elohim (God), and die* (Job 2:9) — but Job answers with the heart that had already blessed the Name when all was taken (*Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) hath taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD)* — Job 1:21): *What? shall we receive good at the hand of Elohim (God), and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips* (Job 2:10). The "evil" received is ADVERSITY from Yahuah's sovereign hand, never moral evil charged against Him — the same confession Isaiah makes (*I make peace, and create evil: I Yahuah (LORD) do all these things* — Isaiah 45:7) and Lamentations asks (*Out of the mouth of the El Elyon (most High) proceedeth not evil and good?* — Lamentations 3:38). This is the testing of the righteous, not its punishment. The restored library names the pattern: *be patient when you are changed to a low estate... For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Ecclesiasticus 2:4-5). And the New Testament fills it forward: Paul's *thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me* (2 Corinthians 12:7); Peter's *trial of your faith... though it be tried with fire* (1 Peter 1:7); and James' own naming — *Ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of Yahuah (Lord); that Yahuah (Lord) is very pitiful, and of tender mercy* (James 5:11). The end is not a prosperity payout but Yahuah's tender mercy, and the proven faith of the man who would not sin with his lips.

threads.title: Yahuah killeth and maketh alive — he bringeth down to the grave and bringeth up
threads.summary_md: Hannah confesses the resurrection in seed-form: *Yahuah (LORD) killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up* (1 Samuel 2:6). It is the Song of Moses already heard: *I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand* (Deuteronomy 32:39); a power the king of Yashar'el (Israel) knows is Yahuah's alone — *Am I Elohim (God), to kill and to make alive?* (2 Kings 5:7). The restored wisdom library says the same: *you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). It opens forward to Daniel's plain sight — *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life* (Daniel 12:2) — and to the work the Father gives the Formed Son: *as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will* (John 5:21).

threads.title: The word of Yahuah was precious — there was no open vision
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens on a dearth: *And the child Samuel ministered unto Yahuah (LORD) before Eli. And the word of Yahuah (LORD) was precious in those days; there was no open vision* (1 Samuel 3:1). The word is *precious* because it is scarce — revelation had grown rare and costly, the open vision withdrawn. This is the very famine Amos names, not of bread but of hearing: *Behold, the days come, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Yahuah (LORD)* (Amos 8:11), in which men *shall run to and fro to seek the word of Yahuah, and shall not find it* (Amos 8:12). Into that silence Yahuah breaks His own famine and speaks afresh — to a child. And the restored witness remembers the man through whom the open vision is restored: *by his word he was known to be faithful in vision* (Ecclesiasticus 46:15). The precious, rare word becomes, in Samuel, the open vision again.

threads.title: Let none of his words fall to the ground — Samuel established a prophet
threads.summary_md: *And Samuel grew, and Yahuah (LORD) was with him, and did let none of his words fall to the ground* (1 Samuel 3:19). This is the very mark of the true prophet — that every word stands and comes to pass — the same unfailing faithfulness of Yahuah's own word: *There failed not ought of any good thing which Yahuah (LORD) had spoken unto the house of Yashar'el (Israel); all came to pass* (Joshua 21:45); *not one thing hath failed of all the good things... all are come to pass unto you, and not one thing hath failed thereof* (Joshua 23:14); *there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant* (1 Kings 8:56). So *all Yashar'el (Israel) from Dan even to Beer-sheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Yahuah (LORD)* (3:20) — the whole land, north and south, acknowledges him. He is the head of the prophetic line: *all the prophets from Samuel and those that follow after, as many as have spoken, have likewise foretold of these days* (Acts 3:24) — so the child called at Shiloh is the first witness of the whole chorus that testifies of the Messiah. The restored witness remembers him: *Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah (God)... established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people* (Ecclesiasticus 46:13), *by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision* (Ecclesiasticus 46:15). And the chapter closes where it began, the silence broken: *And Yahuah (LORD) appeared again in Shiloh: for Yahuah (LORD) revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the word of Yahuah (LORD)* (3:21). The open vision that was absent in verse 1 is restored in the faithful prophet.

threads.title: As a man doth bear his son — the Father carrying Yashar'el through the wilderness
threads.summary_md: Against the murmuring that Yahuah *hated* them, Moses sets the truth of the wilderness: *And in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place* (Deuteronomy 1:31) — He *went in the way before you... in fire by night, to shew you by what way ye should go, and in a cloud by day* (1:33). This is the Father carrying His son. Hosea draws the same picture: *When Yashar'el (Israel) was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt* (Hosea 11:1), *I taught Ephraim also to go, taking them by their arms* (11:3) — the northern house too carried like a son learning to walk. From Sinai it was the same word: *how I bare you on eagles' wings, and brought you unto myself* (Exodus 19:4); and the carrying never ends — *which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb... even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you* (Isaiah 46:3-4). The same book holds the discipline that belongs to a father's love: *as a man chasteneth his son, so Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) chasteneth thee* (Deuteronomy 8:5). Paul rehearses the forty-year forbearance — *about the time of forty years suffered he their manners in the wilderness* (Acts 13:18) — for to bear a son is to suffer his manners. And the restored witness names the guiding fire: *thou gavest them a burning pillar of fire, both to be a guide of the unknown journey* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:3). Yashar'el is the SON whom the Father loved, carried, taught, disciplined, and led — the two-house people borne the whole way home.

threads.title: This is your wisdom — the Torah draws the nations
threads.summary_md: Moses calls the Torah Yashar'el (Israel)'s wisdom in the eyes of the watching world: *Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations... Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people* (Deuteronomy 4:6), *what nation is there so great, who hath Elohim (God) so nigh unto them* (Deuteronomy 4:7), *what nation is there so great, that hath statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law* (Deuteronomy 4:8). David sings the same: *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul... The statutes of Yahuah (LORD) are right, rejoicing the heart* (Psalm 19:7-8); and *He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Yashar'el (Israel). He hath not dealt so with any nation* (Psalm 147:19-20). The apostolic verdict agrees — *the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good* (Romans 7:12) — and the Messiah binds it as light to the nations: *Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid* (Matthew 5:14); *whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven* (Matthew 5:19). The 2nd-Temple sages already named the Torah as Wisdom herself: *All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high Yahuah (God), even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the congregations of Jacob* (Sirach 24:23). The Torah is never the curse — it is the righteousness that draws the nations to Yahuah.

threads.title: Ye heard the voice, but saw no similitude — the Formless and the Formed
threads.summary_md: At Horeb Yashar'el (Israel) met Yahuah by hearing, not by sight: *ye heard the voice of the words, but saw no similitude; only ye heard a voice* (Deuteronomy 4:12); *ye saw no manner of similitude on the day that Yahuah (LORD) spake unto you* (Deuteronomy 4:15). Therefore make no image — not *the likeness of male or female* (Deuteronomy 4:16), no beast, fowl, fish (Deuteronomy 4:17-18), and do not be *driven to worship... the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven* (Deuteronomy 4:19). The reason is the Formless Source Himself: *Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live* (Exodus 33:20); *Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image* (Exodus 20:4); *To whom then will ye liken Elohim (God)?* (Isaiah 40:18). The New Testament makes the lens explicit: *No man hath seen Elohim (God) at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him* (John 1:18); *Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape* (John 5:37). The Father is heard and never beheld in form — He is declared and made visible only in the Formed Son, the One Baruch foresaw: *Afterward did he shew himself upon earth, and conversed with men* (Baruch 3:37). And the warning against worshipping the host of heaven is the folly Wisdom names — *deemed... the circle of the stars, or the lights of heaven, to be the gods which govern the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 13:1-2): the creature mistaken for the Creator.

threads.title: Yahuah he is Elohim; there is none else beside him
threads.summary_md: The sermon rises to the great confession that will be sealed as the Shema: *Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that Yahuah (LORD) he is Elohim (God); there is none else beside him* (Deuteronomy 4:35); *Know therefore this day, and consider it in thine heart, that Yahuah (LORD) he is Elohim (God) in heaven above, and upon the earth beneath: there is none else* (Deuteronomy 4:39). Two chapters on it becomes the watchword of Yashar'el: *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD)* (Deuteronomy 6:4). Isaiah carries the same oracle whole — *I am Yahuah (LORD), and there is none else, there is no Elohim (God) beside me* (Isaiah 45:5); *there is no Elohim (God) else beside me; a just Elohim (God) and a Saviour... Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth* (Isaiah 45:21-22). The scribe confesses it back to the Messiah, who commends him: *there is one Elohim (God); and there is none other but he* (Mark 12:32). And the restored witness repeats it: *This is our Elohim (God), and there shall none other be accounted of in comparison of him* (Baruch 3:35), the same One who *has given* the way of knowledge *to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved* (Baruch 3:36). One Yahuah, none else — the Father the formless Source, made known in the Formed Son.

threads.title: To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend
threads.summary_md: Here is the indictment, and it falls on the friends, not on Job: *To him that is afflicted pity should be shewed from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty* (Job 6:14). They came to comfort and brought no comfort — *for now ye are nothing; ye see my casting down, and are afraid* (Job 6:21). This is the wound the suffering righteous know well; the Psalmist names it word for word: *Reproach hath broken my heart; and I am full of heaviness: and I looked for some to take pity, but there was none; and for comforters, but I found none* (Psalm 69:20). Job himself will give them their name: *I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all* (Job 16:2). They failed the very standard wisdom sets — *a man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother* (Proverbs 18:24) — and Sirach has already drawn their portrait: *there is a companion, which rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, but in the time of trouble will be against him* (Ecclesiasticus 37:4). The fear of the Almighty is forsaken not by the man who laments, but by the friend who withholds pity in the day of affliction.

threads.title: As the Cloud Is Consumed: He Shall Return No More
threads.summary_md: *As the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no more. He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more* (Job 7:9-10). Here Job speaks within the limit of his own sight — the grief of a man who sees only the grave swallowing the life and the place forgetting the man. Moses sings the same turning, but in the mouth of the One whose word it is: *Thou turnest man to destruction; and sayest, Return, ye children of men* (Psalm 90:3); *thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep: in the morning they are like grass which groweth up... in the evening it is cut down, and withereth* (Psalm 90:5-6). And Job's plea echoes David's: *O spare me, that I may recover strength, before I go hence, and be no more* (Psalm 39:13). The restored library shows the danger of this same image when it is seized WITHOUT hope — the ungodly reason, *our life shall pass away as the trace of a cloud... For our time is a very shadow that passeth away; and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:4-5), and from there they turn to oppress the poor and the righteous. Job grieves the vanishing cloud as a faithful man pressed to the wall; the ungodly twist it into license. The same shadow — but the heart that holds it makes all the difference, and Job's heart will yet rise to the Redeemer (Job 19:25).

threads.title: What Is Man, That Thou Shouldest Magnify Him: The Dark Inversion of Psalm 8
threads.summary_md: *What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him? And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?* (Job 7:17-18). This is one of the Tanakh's most piercing turns. David sang the question as pure wonder and honor: *What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of Adam, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour* (Psalm 8:4-5). The same word — *visitest* — David adores as Yahuah's tender mindfulness, the dignity of the son of Adam crowned. Job, on the ash-heap, feels that very nearness as relentless scrutiny: the divine *visiting* becomes a watch set over him, a trial renewed *every morning... every moment*. He does not deny the attention; he reels under its weight. David asks again in another psalm: *Yahuah (LORD), what is man, that thou takest knowledge of him! or the son of Adam, that thou makest account of him! Man is like to vanity: his days are as a shadow that passeth away* (Psalm 144:3-4) — that the Eternal should take account of so frail a shadow at all is the wonder. And the wisdom library carries it too: *What is man, and to which serveth he?... so are a thousand years to the days of eternity* (Ecclesiasticus 18:8-10). The honor of Psalm 8 does not silence Job's cry, and Job's cry does not cancel the honor. Both are kept whole — the righteous sufferer wrestling honestly with the unbearable, undeniable nearness of Yahuah.

threads.title: Enquire of the former age — the tradition of the fathers
threads.summary_md: Bildad grounds his speech not in fresh revelation but in inherited counsel: *For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers: (For we are but of yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth are a shadow:) Shall not they teach thee, and tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?* (Job 8:8-10). The wisdom tradition prizes exactly this handed-down instruction: *Miss not the discourse of the elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you shall learn understanding* (Sirach 8:9). The fathers' wisdom is a real inheritance and is rightly honored. Yet the book of Job presses a hard edge against it: the fathers' tidy formula — that the righteous prosper and the wicked perish in this life — does not fit every case, and a righteous man can suffer without secret guilt. Tradition is a gift, not an infallible verdict; the search of the fathers must bow to the living God who alone weighs the heart.

threads.title: Great Things Past Finding Out
threads.summary_md: Job closes the doxology with the confession of the unsearchable: the One *which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number* (Job 9:10). The restored library sings the same posture — *To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall find out his noble acts?* (Ecclesiasticus 18:4), and *As for the wondrous works of Yahuah (God), there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out* (Ecclesiasticus 18:6). Isaiah seals it in the canon: *Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that El Olam (the everlasting God), Yahuah (LORD), the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding* (Isaiah 40:28). The ground of the Maker's works cannot be found out; the creature's only wisdom is the fear of him.

threads.title: Thine Hands Have Made Me: the Creator Who Formed Me as the Clay in the Womb
threads.summary_md: Even in the bitterness of his soul Job does not deny the hand that made him — he pleads WITH it. *Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me* (Job 10:8); *Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay* (Job 10:9); *Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews. Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit* (Job 10:11-12). This is the womb-forming Creator — the Formed Son the agent of all making — the same hand that *covered me in my mother's womb* (Psalm 139:13), that knew Jeremiah *before I formed thee in the belly* (Jeremiah 1:5), the *potter* of whom *we are the clay... and we all are the work of thy hand* (Isaiah 64:8), who *formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life* (Genesis 2:7). The restored witnesses marvel at the same hidden craft: *in my mother's womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months, being compacted in blood* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:2). And it does not end in dust: *the Creator of the world, who formed the generation of man... will also of his own mercy give you breath and life again* (2 Maccabees 7:23). The hand that fashioned the clay holds the power to raise it.

threads.title: Canst Thou by Searching Find Out Elohim — the Unsearchable Depth
threads.summary_md: Zophar the Naamathite, the third friend, opens with a premise that is wholly TRUE: *Canst thou by searching find out Elohim (God)? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection? It is as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know? The measure thereof is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.* (Job 11:7-9). No creature can audit the Most High to the bottom. This is the very confession Yahuah (LORD) presses on his scattered people: *that El Olam (the everlasting God), Yahuah (LORD), the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding.* (Isaiah 40:28); *Great is Yahuah (LORD), and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable.* (Psalm 145:3). The height and depth Zophar measures is Isaiah's same gulf: *For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways ... For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways* (Isaiah 55:8-9). It runs FORWARD into Paul's doxology — *O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of Elohim (God)! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of Yahuah (Lord)? or who hath been his counsellor?* (Romans 11:33-34) — and OUT into the restored wisdom-tradition: *Who can find out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom?* (Ecclesiasticus 1:2-3). The tragedy of the speech is that Zophar takes this true and glorious premise and bends it into a weapon — that the unsearchable El must therefore be hiding Job's secret sin (Job 11:6). The premise is sound; the application is the error Yahuah will rebuke (Job 42:7).

threads.title: With him is wisdom and strength
threads.summary_md: At the heart of Job's reply stands the confession his friends mouthed but he believes: *With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding* (Job 12:13), and again *With him is strength and wisdom* (Job 12:16). This is the wisdom personified throughout the canon — the Formed Word at the Maker's side, who says *Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength* (Proverbs 8:14). Daniel blesses Yahuah (LORD) in Job's own words: *Blessed be the name of Elohim (God) for ever and ever: for wisdom and might are his... and he changeth the times and the seasons: he removeth kings, and setteth up kings: he giveth wisdom unto the wise* (Daniel 2:20-21). Ben Sira opens his book the same way: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 1:1) — wisdom is never a human credential, it is *with him*. And it is gathered up at last in the Messiah (Christ): *Messiah (Christ) the power of Elohim (God), and the wisdom of Elohim (God)* (1 Corinthians 1:24). The wisdom and strength Job confesses to be *with him* is the Formed Son himself.

threads.title: Forgers of Lies, Physicians of No Value
threads.summary_md: Job turns on his three comforters with a verdict: *But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value* (Job 13:4). They have prescribed doctrine to a wound they never felt, and Job wishes their silence were their wisdom — *O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom* (Job 13:5). Three chapters later he says it again: *I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all* (Job 16:2). The wisdom of Ben Sira had already painted the type — *some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble* (Ecclesiasticus 6:8) — the companion who vanishes the moment trouble comes. And the book itself renders the final verdict in Job's favour: *Yahuah (LORD) said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath* (Job 42:7). The false physicians spoke wrongly of Elohim (God); the suffering man, who held his integrity, spoke right.

threads.title: Man of Few Days, as a Flower Cut Down
threads.summary_md: *Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not* (Job 14:1-2). Job names the universal frailty, and the whole canon sings it back. Moses: *they are like grass which groweth up; in the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up; in the evening it is cut down, and withereth* (Psalm 90:5-6). David: *As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth. For the wind passeth over it, and it is gone* (Psalm 103:15-16) -- yet held by Him who *remembereth that we are dust*. Isaiah turns the lament into comfort: *All flesh is grass... The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our Elohim (God) shall stand for ever* (Isaiah 40:6,8). James and Peter carry Job's flower into apostolic teaching -- *as the flower of the grass he shall pass away* (James 1:10); *all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass* (1 Peter 1:24). Ben Sira reads it as the Eden-sentence: *All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the covenant from the beginning is, You shall die the death* (Sirach 14:17). Frail man fades; the word of Yahuah does not.

threads.title: Is There Hope of a Tree, If It Be Cut Down
threads.summary_md: *For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease. Though the root thereof wax old in the earth... yet through the scent of water it will bud* (Job 14:7-9). The tree has hope: cut down, it sprouts again at the scent of water. Then the contrast cuts: *But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where is he?* (Job 14:10). *So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake* (14:12). Job stands in genuine darkness here -- the tree's sprouting only sharpens the question of man's silence. The same despairing voice is recorded in Wisdom on the lips of the ungodly: *Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave* (Wisdom 2:1); *our time is a very shadow that passeth away; and after our end there is no returning: for it is fast sealed, so that no man comes again* (Wisdom 2:5). The canon does not hide the darkness; it lets the sufferer ask honestly, before the resurrection answer breaks (14:14; Job 19:25-26).

threads.title: If a Man Die, Shall He Live Again -- the Resurrection Question
threads.summary_md: *O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave... until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me! If a man die, shall he live again? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come* (Job 14:13-14). This is the great question, asked in the dark -- Job has just said man *lieth down, and riseth not* (14:12). He does not yet know the answer; he waits for it. And the canon answers him forward. From his own mouth, chapters later: *I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth... yet in my flesh shall I see Elohim (God)* (Job 19:25-26). Daniel sees the awakening: *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life* (Daniel 12:2). The Formed Son declares the hour: *all that are in the graves shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life* (John 5:28-29). Paul names the change Job waited for: *We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump... and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed* (1 Corinthians 15:51-52). The Second-Temple hope says it plainly: *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence* (2 Esdras 7:32). *My change* is the resurrection transformation -- the answer to a question asked across the grave.

threads.title: He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up
threads.summary_md: Zophar pictures the wicked man's gain as food that betrays the body: *Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue... Yet his meat in his bowels is turned, it is the gall of asps within him. He hath swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again: Elohim (God) shall cast them out of his belly* (Job 20:12-15). Solomon used the same image of fare that will not stay down: *The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words* (Proverbs 23:8), and named the reason plainly: *Treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death* (Proverbs 10:2). Ben Sira sings the same dissolving wealth: *The goods of the unjust shall be dried up like a river, and shall vanish with noise, like a great thunder in rain* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 40:13) — which is Zophar's own *The increase of his house shall depart, and his goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath* (Job 20:28). Across the Tanakh and the wisdom witnesses the verdict on ill-gotten gain holds: sweet in the mouth, gall in the belly, vomited up. The wisdom is real; Zophar's sin is pressing it as proof that Job's losses convict Job of wickedness.

threads.title: The portion of a wicked man — true doctrine, false application
threads.summary_md: Zophar closes with the retribution formula in its bare form: *This is the portion of a wicked man from Elohim (God), and the heritage appointed unto him by Elohim (God)* (Job 20:29). Taken as a statement about the truly wicked, it is true — the whole chapter's wisdom-laterals (Psalm 37, Psalm 73, Proverbs, Sirach) affirm that the wicked's portion is ruin. But Zophar has aimed every word of it at Job, treating Job's suffering as evidence of hidden wickedness. The book itself reverses the verdict in the mouth of Yahuah (LORD): *My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath* (Job 42:7). The mechanical doctrine — every sufferer must be a sinner getting his portion — is the lie. Yahuah (LORD) does not deny that the wicked have a portion; he denies that Job is the wicked man. This is the frame guard for the whole chapter: thread the truth, name the misapplication, and let Job's vindication stand.

threads.title: Whose Ox Have I Taken — the Clean-Handed Judge
threads.summary_md:
Samuel sets his whole record before Yahuah and his anointed and asks the people to convict him if they can: *whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you* (1 Samuel 12:3). They answer, *Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man's hand* (12:4), and he seals it: *Yahuah (LORD) is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that ye have not found ought in my hand* (12:5).

The contrast is sharp and deliberate. It was not Samuel's hand but his sons' that forced the king: *And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment* (1 Samuel 8:3). The bribe Samuel refused is the very evil the psalmist sets against the righteous — the throne *which frameth mischief by a law* and they that *condemn the innocent blood* (Psalm 94:20-21). And the restored library remembers him by this very mark: *I have not taken any man's goods, so much as a shoe: and no man did accuse him* (Ecclesiasticus 46:19). Paul gathers the whole age into one line: *he gave unto them judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years, until Samuel the prophet* (Acts 13:20). The clean-handed judge closes the era; the king opens the next.

threads.title: Thunder and Rain in Wheat Harvest — the Sign
threads.summary_md:
Samuel seals the lawsuit with a sign out of season: *Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto Yahuah (LORD), and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), in asking you a king* (1 Samuel 12:17). At harvest the sky is dry; thunder and rain then are no accident but Yahuah's own answer to his prophet. *So Samuel called unto Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared Yahuah (LORD) and Samuel* (12:18).

It is the same heavenly thunder that answered him at Mizpeh, when his lamb and his cry routed the Philistines — *And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto Yahuah (LORD): and Samuel cried unto Yahuah (LORD) for Yashar'el (Israel); and Yahuah (LORD) heard him* (1 Samuel 7:9), and *Yahuah (LORD) thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them* (1 Samuel 7:10). The restored library remembers this very thunder: *He called upon the mighty Yahuah (God)... when he offered the sucking lamb. And Yahuah (God) thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard* (Ecclesiasticus 46:16-17). The same intercessor, the same answering thunder — first to save Israel, now to bring her to fear.

threads.title: I Will Teach You the Good and the Right Way — Ceaseless Intercession
threads.summary_md:
Samuel will not lay down either office Yahuah gave him. He binds his prayer to a holy obligation: *Moreover as for me, Elohim (God) forbid that I should sin against Yahuah (LORD) in ceasing to pray for you* (1 Samuel 12:23) — and to that he joins the teaching of the way: *but I will teach you the good and the right way: Only fear Yahuah (LORD), and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you* (12:23-24). The prophet who will not cease to intercede is the same prophet who keeps teaching the Torah-way.

The office of the praying prophet is the very one Paul names: *Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to Elohim (God)* (Romans 11:2) — the line that runs forward to the Formed Intercessor who ever liveth to plead for his people. And *the good and the right way* is no new law: the library remembers that *Samuel, the prophet of Yahuah (God), beloved of his Elohim (God)... by the law of Yahuah (God) he judged the congregation* (Ecclesiasticus 46:13-14); it is the Torah Moses commanded be read to all the people *that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and observe to do all the words of this law* (Deuteronomy 31:12). And it is the single, standing demand with which Joshua too sealed his farewell: *Now therefore fear Yahuah (LORD), and serve him in sincerity and in truth... and serve ye Yahuah (LORD)* (Joshua 24:14). The way is taught, learned, and kept — never abolished.

threads.title: To obey is better than sacrifice
threads.summary_md: Saul spared the best of the flocks and named it worship: *the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (1 Samuel 15:15,21). Samuel answers with the verse that anchors the whole sacrificial Torah: *Hath Yahuah (LORD) as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Yahuah (LORD)? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams* (1 Samuel 15:22). This is not the abolition of the altar but its heart. Hosea sings it: *For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* (Hosea 6:6). Micah presses the same: *shall I come before him with burnt offerings... thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil?... He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:6-8). David — the *neighbour... better than thou* (15:28) about to receive the kingdom — knows it from the ash of his own sin: *thou desirest not sacrifice... The sacrifices of Elohim (God) are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O Elohim (God), thou wilt not despise* (Psalm 51:16-17). Jeremiah grounds it in the founding charge itself: *I spake not unto your fathers... concerning burnt offerings or sacrifices: But this thing commanded I them, saying, Obey my voice* (Jeremiah 7:22-23). The wisdom of Yashar'el (Israel) says it plainly: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1-2) — obedience IS the offering, not its replacement. And the Formed Son, walking in flesh, twice sends the Pharisees back to Hosea's word: *I will have mercy, and not sacrifice* (Matthew 9:13; 12:7), commending the scribe who saw that obedient love *is more than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices* (Mark 12:33). The thread is one law of the altar from Moses to Messiah — the sacrifice was always meant to flow from an obeying heart, and severed from it, it is rejected.

threads.title: Open Thine Hand Wide — The Poor Shall Never Cease
threads.summary_md: The promise and the realism sit side by side. *Save when there shall be no poor among you; for Yahuah (LORD) shall greatly bless thee in the land* (Deuteronomy 15:4) — but only *if thou carefully hearken unto the voice of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (15:5); and where the people fall short, the truth stands: *For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee... Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy* (15:11). The command is the open hand: *thou shalt not harden thine heart, nor shut thine hand from thy poor brother* (15:7), but *open thine hand wide... and surely lend him sufficient for his need* (15:8), and *thine heart shall not be grieved when thou givest* (15:10). Proverbs names the unseen creditor: *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again* (Proverbs 19:17). Ben Sira makes it Torah itself: *He that is merciful will lend to his neighbour; and he that strengtheneth his hand keepeth the commandments* (Ecclesiasticus 29:1); *Help the poor for the commandment's sake* (29:9). Yahusha (Jesus) cites this very verse — *For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always* (Matthew 26:11; John 12:8) — not to dismiss the poor but to press the clause that follows in Moses: the poor remain, therefore the hand stays open. Paul carries the same heart forward — *not grudgingly, or of necessity: for Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver* (2 Corinthians 9:7) — and Luke records the shemittah ideal lived out in the first assembly: *Neither was there any among them that lacked* (Acts 4:34). John makes the closed fist the test of love: *whoso... seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of Elohim (God) in him?* (1 John 3:17). The command and the heart are one Torah.

threads.title: Wherefore Do the Wicked Live? — Job Demolishes the Retribution Lie
threads.summary_md: The friends preached a tidy ledger: the righteous prosper, the wicked perish — suffering proves sin, wealth proves righteousness. Job answers with the one thing their doctrine cannot survive, the plain fact: *Wherefore do the wicked live, become old, yea, are mighty in power?* (Job 21:7). He spreads the evidence out — *Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes* (Job 21:8); *Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of Elohim (God) upon them* (Job 21:9); their children dance, *They take the timbrel and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ* (Job 21:12); and the verdict, *They spend their days in wealth, and in a moment go down to the grave* (Job 21:13). This is not the speech of a doubting man but of an honest one, and Yahuah will vindicate it (Job 42:7). The canon names the same scandal again and again. Asaph: *For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked* (Psalm 73:3); *Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches* (Psalm 73:12). Jeremiah: *Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper? wherefore are all they happy that deal very treacherously?* (Jeremiah 12:1). Malachi: *And now we call the proud happy; yea, they that work wickedness are set up* (Malachi 3:15). And the restored library gives the wicked's own creed: *Come on therefore, let us enjoy the good things that are present: and let us speedily use the creatures like as in youth* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:6). The prosperity-gospel — that wealth is a sign of favour and affliction a sign of guilt — is the friends' error, and Scripture refutes it from its own mouth.

threads.title: Depart From Us — The Creed of the Prospering Wicked
threads.summary_md: Prosperity, untested by adversity, breeds contempt for the One who gives it. Job hears the wicked say it openly: *Therefore they say unto Elohim (God), Depart from us; for we desire not the knowledge of thy ways* (Job 21:14); *What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? and what profit should we have, if we pray unto him?* (Job 21:15). It is a cost-accounting of obedience: they weigh serving Yahuah by present gain alone, and finding their barns already full, they dismiss him. Asaph caught the same arrogance: *And they say, How doth Elohim (God) know? and is there knowledge in the El Elyon (most High)?* (Psalm 73:11). Malachi caught it among the covenant people themselves: *Ye have said, It is vain to serve Elohim (God): and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinance?* (Malachi 3:14) — the very same profit-and-loss reasoning Job's wicked use. And the restored Wisdom of Solomon unmasks where it leads: the ungodly esteem the righteous a counterfeit, despise that he *makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16), and lie in wait for him. Note carefully: the offense is not Torah-keeping but its abandonment. These are men who *desire not the knowledge of thy ways* — the ways being Yahuah's instruction, his covenant walk. The prosperity that should have drawn them to thanksgiving has instead taught them to push El away.

threads.title: How Oft Is the Candle of the Wicked Put Out? — The Reckoning Is Reserved, Not Immediate
threads.summary_md: The friends insisted the wicked are punished promptly and visibly — so Job turns their own slogan into a question: *How oft is the candle of the wicked put out! and how oft cometh their destruction upon them!* (Job 21:17). Not nearly so oft as their doctrine requires. He grants that judgment is real — *They are as stubble before the wind, and as chaff that the storm carrieth away* (Job 21:18); *Elohim (God) layeth up his iniquity for his children* (Job 21:19) — but insists it is *laid up*, reserved, not handed out on the friends' timetable. Asaph confirms both halves: the wicked do fall, *Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction* (Psalm 73:18); *How are they brought into desolation, as in a moment! they are utterly consumed with terrors* (Psalm 73:19) — but suddenly, in Yahuah's hour, not on demand. The restored library teaches the same patience. Ben Sira on the secure rich man: *he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). And Wisdom on the wicked's end: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind... and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). Job's chaff and stubble vanish — but at the appointed end, which is precisely why present prosperity proves nothing about a man's standing before Yahuah.

threads.title: Reserved to the Day of Wrath — The End, Not the Middle, Is the Measure
threads.summary_md: Job gives the answer his friends never reached: present prosperity is no verdict, because the verdict is reserved for *the day of destruction*. *That the wicked is reserved to the day of destruction? they shall be brought forth to the day of wrath* (Job 21:30). The man who flourishes now still answers later — *Yet shall he be brought to the grave* (Job 21:32) — and so Job's closing rebuke lands: *How then comfort ye me in vain, seeing in your answers there remaineth falsehood?* (Job 21:34). Their whole comfort was built on a measure the canon rejects. Asaph found the same resolution only when he stopped counting the present: *Until I went into the sanctuary of Elohim (God); then understood I their end* (Psalm 73:17). Malachi promises that discernment is coming: *Then shall ye return, and discern between the righteous and the wicked, between him that serveth Elohim (God) and him that serveth him not* (Malachi 3:18). Messiah tells the reversal in full — the rich man who fared sumptuously and the beggar at his gate trade places beyond death: *Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented* (Luke 16:25). And Wisdom of Solomon shows the wicked's too-late awakening at that very day: *they repenting and groaning for anguish of spirit shall say within themselves, This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:3). Job is vindicated (Job 42:7): wealth is no proof of righteousness, and affliction no proof of sin — the books are balanced at the end.

threads.title: Tried, I Shall Come Forth as Gold
threads.summary_md: From the depth of his ordeal Job utters one of the great confessions of the suffering righteous: *But he knoweth the way that I take: when he hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold* (Job 23:10). The fire is not the proof of guilt his friends insist on — it is a refining, and Job trusts the assayer. *The fining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold: but Yahuah (LORD) trieth the hearts* (Proverbs 17:3). The prophets carry the figure into the covenant people: *he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto Yahuah (LORD) an offering in righteousness* (Malachi 3:3); *I will bring the third part through the fire, and will refine them as silver is refined, and will try them as gold is tried... I will say, It is my people* (Zechariah 13:9) — the trial brings the remnant forth owned, not consumed. Ben Sira sets the proverb beside Job almost word for word: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). And the apostles fill it: *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (1 Peter 1:7); *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him* (James 1:12). The fire purifies the faithful; it does not prove them guilty.

threads.title: The widow and the fatherless — the Torah's protected poor
threads.summary_md: Verse by verse Job names the exact classes the covenant fences round, and verse by verse he shows them stripped: *They drive away the ass of the fatherless, they take the widow's ox for a pledge* (Job 24:3); *They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor* (Job 24:9). Every clause is a Torah clause turned inside out. *Ye shall not afflict any widow, or fatherless child* (Exodus 22:22) — and the statute arms itself: *my wrath shall wax hot... and your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless* (Exodus 22:24). The pledge-law is precise: *Thou shalt not pervert the judgment of the stranger, nor of the fatherless; nor take a widow's raiment to pledge* (Deuteronomy 24:17); and the withheld wage is given a cry — *lest he cry against thee unto Yahuah (LORD), and it be sin unto thee* (Deuteronomy 24:15). Isaiah pronounces the woe over Job's very scene — *that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless!* (Isaiah 10:2) — and asks *what will ye do in the day of visitation?* (Isaiah 10:3). Malachi seals the answer: Yahuah (the LORD) becomes *a swift witness... against those that oppress the hireling in his wages, the widow, and the fatherless* (Malachi 3:5). The restored library keeps the same verdict: *he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22), and the cry of the wronged *pierces the clouds... till the Most High shall behold to judge* (Ecclesiasticus 35:17), for *Yahuah (God) will not be slack* (Ecclesiasticus 35:18). Job's lament that *Elohim (God) layeth not folly to them* (Job 24:12) is answered from every shelf: the folly is laid to their charge, the witness only delayed.

threads.title: How Can He Be Clean That Is Born of a Woman: The No-Man-Clean Theme Reaching Its Final Form
threads.summary_md: Three times in this book the friends circle the same gulf, and here Bildad states it in its starkest form: *How then can man be justified with Elohim (God)? or how can he be clean that is born of a woman? Behold even to the moon, and it shineth not; yea, the stars are not pure in his sight* (Job 25:4-5). Eliphaz had said it first in the visions of the night — *Shall mortal man be more just than Elohim (God)? shall a man be more pure than his maker? Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly* (Job 4:17-18) — and again plainly: *What is man, that he should be clean? and he which is born of a woman, that he should be righteous? ... yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight* (Job 15:14-15). The psalmist pronounces the same verdict over all flesh: *They are all gone aside, they are all together become filthy: there is none that doeth good, no, not one* (Psalm 14:3). And the wisdom-teacher voices the creature's weight: *For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:15). This is true — gloriously, terribly true. Paul gathers it all up: *As it is written, There is none righteous, no, not one* (Romans 3:10), and *Therefore by the deeds of the law there shall no flesh be justified in his sight: for by the law is the knowledge of sin* (Romans 3:20). Mark the framework carefully: no flesh is justified by its own *works of merit*, for the Torah exposes sin — but the Torah itself is not abolished; it is the very mirror that shows the creature his uncleanness. Bildad's error is not his doctrine but his use of it: he wields the gulf as a final dismissal of his suffering friend, offering only the distance and never the mercy that, in the Besorah (good news), closes it.

threads.title: The battle is Yahuah's: he saveth not with sword and spear
threads.summary_md:
When Goliath comes with sword and spear and shield, David answers with the Name: *Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), whom thou hast defied* (1 Samuel 17:45). He tells the whole assembly why the giant will fall — *all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands* (1 Samuel 17:47). The deliverance is Yahuah's, and so is the glory.

This is the canon's recurring grammar of deliverance, woven through both houses and beyond. Zechariah hears it over the rebuilding of the house: *Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Zechariah 4:6). Jehoshaphat hears it in Yahudah (Judah) when a great multitude comes up: *Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but Elohim's (God's)* (2 Chronicles 20:15) — *set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 20:17). Jonathan ventured against the garrison on it: *there is no restraint to Yahuah (LORD) to save by many or by few* (1 Samuel 14:6). And generations later Yahudah Maccabee confesses the same creed against a mighty host: *It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with Yahuah (God) of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company* (1 Maccabees 3:18) — *for the victory of battle stands not in the multitude of an host; but strength comes from heaven* (1 Maccabees 3:19). The sword and the spear are nothing; the battle is Yahuah's.

threads.title: The thunder of his power who can understand
threads.summary_md: Job ends the hymn not with mastery but with awe at how little he has seen: *Lo, these are parts of his ways: but how little a portion is heard of him? but the thunder of his power who can understand?* (Job 26:14). The whole cosmic survey — the hung earth, the bound waters, the subdued serpent — is only the fringe. The apostle reaches the same confession: *O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of Elohim! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!* (Romans 11:33). Isaiah had already said it of the Creator of the ends of the earth — *there is no searching of his understanding* (Isaiah 40:28) — and Qoheleth of his works — *no man can find out the work that Elohim maketh from the beginning to the end* (Ecclesiastes 3:11). Ben Sira closes his own creation-hymn on the very same note: *Who has seen him, that he might tell us?... There are yet hid greater things than these be, for we have seen but a few of his works* (Sirach 43:31-32). The thunder of his power remains beyond all telling; the Maker who fills the sky is himself unsearchable to the mind he made.

threads.title: What Is the Hope of the Hypocrite — the Godless Without Anchor
threads.summary_md: Against his friends' assumption that the godless can rest secure in his gain, Job asks the question that exposes the hollowness of it: *For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained, when Elohim (God) taketh away his soul? Will Elohim (God) hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him? Will he delight himself in the Almighty? will he always call upon Elohim (God)?* (Job 27:8-10). The man who never sought Yahuah in the day of ease has no anchor in the day of trouble; his cry has nowhere to land. The restored wisdom-witness paints exactly this hope dissolving in wind and storm: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). The hypocrite's confidence scatters like dust the moment El takes his soul.

threads.title: He Heapeth Up Silver, but the Just Shall Put It On
threads.summary_md: Job now declares *the portion of a wicked man with Elohim (God), and the heritage of oppressors* (Job 27:13) — affirming, against the friends' mechanical timetable, that the wicked DO face a reckoning, but on Yahuah's timing. The oppressor *heap[s] up silver as the dust, and prepare[s] raiment as the clay* (Job 27:16), yet the gain is only stored: *He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver* (Job 27:17). The same verdict runs through wisdom: *A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just* (Proverbs 13:22); *but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before Elohim (God)* (Ecclesiastes 2:26). And Ben Sira draws the same portrait of the hoarder who never reckons his hour: *There is that waxeth rich by his wariness and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward: Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:18-19). The wicked labours; Yahuah hands the wealth to the upright.

threads.title: But Where Shall Wisdom Be Found? — Not Minable, Not Buyable
threads.summary_md:
Job has just watched man tear the earth open for every buried treasure — *Surely there is a vein for the silver, and a place for gold... Iron is taken out of the earth, and brass is molten out of the stone* (Job 28:1-2) — sinking shafts where no fowl or lion has trod, *and his eye seeth every precious thing* (28:10). Then the turn that names the whole chapter: *But where shall wisdom be found? and where is the place of understanding?* (Job 28:12), repeated at *Whence then cometh wisdom?* (28:20). And the verdict: *Man knoweth not the price thereof; neither is it found in the land of the living. The depth saith, It is not in me: and the sea saith, It is not with me* (28:13-14). She cannot be dug and she cannot be bought: *It cannot be gotten for gold, neither shall silver be weighed for the price thereof... the price of wisdom is above rubies* (28:15,18).

The restored wisdom-tradition takes up Job's very words. Baruch is almost a paraphrase of this chapter: *Who has found out her place? or who has come into her treasures?* (Baruch 3:15) — ransacking the silver-hoarders *in which men trust* (3:17), the merchants, the heathen princes, and finding wisdom in none, asking at last *Who has gone over the sea, and found her, and will bring her for pure gold?* (3:30) — and answering that only Yahuah *has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved* (3:36). Ben Sira opens his whole book on the same note: *All wisdom comes from Yahuah (God), and is with him for ever* (Sirach 1:1). And Wisdom herself, in Proverbs, lifts the curtain on where she dwelt all along: *Yahuah (LORD) possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old* (Proverbs 8:22) — not buried ore but the firstborn of Yahuah's way, the Formed Word brought forth before the earth was. She is never mined or marketed; she is given to those who fear him.

threads.title: Elohim Knoweth Her Place — Wisdom Present at Creation
threads.summary_md:
Where man's deepest shaft cannot reach, Elohim alone has the map: *Elohim (God) understandeth the way thereof, and he knoweth the place thereof. For he looketh to the ends of the earth, and seeth under the whole heaven* (Job 28:23-24). And the proof that he knows her place is that he was wielding her when he set the world in order: *To make the weight for the winds; and he weigheth the waters by measure. When he made a decree for the rain, and a way for the lightning of the thunder: Then did he see it, and declare it; he prepared it, yea, and searched it out* (Job 28:25-27).

Proverbs lets that same Wisdom speak from inside the act: *Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth* (Proverbs 8:25); *When he prepared the heavens, I was there: when he set a compass upon the face of the depth* (8:27); *Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight, rejoicing always before him* (8:30). The measured winds, the weighed waters, the decree for the rain are not blind force — they are laid by the Formed Wisdom, the expressed Word brought forth before the works of old, the agent of creation who is Yahuah's daily delight and who has a Father. The wisdom-tradition confesses the same: *Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting* (Sirach 1:4). She was never dug out of the earth in time; she was with Yahuah from everlasting — the firstborn of his way, not a created goddess and not a co-equal rival to the Most High, but the Formed Son who would one day take flesh.

threads.title: I delivered the poor and the fatherless — covenant-justice enacted
threads.summary_md: Here is the heart of Job's defence, and the flat refutation of his accusers. Eliphaz had slandered him: *Thou hast sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken* (Job 22:9). Job answers not with argument but with the record of his life: *Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him... I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out. And I brake the jaws of the wicked, and plucked the spoil out of his teeth* (Job 29:12,16-17). This is the Torah's justice walked out in a man. Yahuah Himself *doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment* (Deuteronomy 10:18), and Job is His image enacted. Isaiah commands of Yashar'el (Israel) precisely what Job already lived: *Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow* (Isaiah 1:17). The wisdom tradition weighs the same deed as the mark of a true son: *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shalt thou be as the son of the Most High* (Ecclesiasticus / Sirach 4:10). These are not works hoarded as flesh-merit against the Almighty; they are the fruit that grows from the fear of Yahuah — the covenant-mercy by which the righteous are known.

threads.title: Now Am I Their Song — the Once-Honored Made a Byword
threads.summary_md: The chief who once sat in honor is now mocked by the basest: *But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock* (Job 30:1), until *And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword* (Job 30:9) and *They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face* (Job 30:10). It is the reversal the righteous sufferer knows by heart. The psalmist sings it: *I made sackcloth also my garment; and I became a proverb to them* (Psalm 69:11), *and I was the song of the drunkards* (Psalm 69:12); *the abjects gathered themselves together against me... they did tear me, and ceased not* (Psalm 35:15), *with hypocritical mockers in feasts, they gnashed upon me with their teeth* (Psalm 35:16). Lamentations takes up the same line — *I was a derision to all my people; and their song all the day* (Lamentations 3:14) — and Job had already felt it from his own household: *young children despised me; I arose, and they spake against me* (Job 19:18), *all my inward friends abhorred me: and they whom I loved are turned against me* (Job 19:19). The wicked's scheme against the just man names it plainly: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19), *let us condemn him with a shameful death* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). And the whole pattern foreshadows the Man of Sorrows: *He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief... he was despised, and we esteemed him not* (Isaiah 53:3) — fulfilled when *they spit upon him, and took the reed, and smote him on the head* (Matthew 27:30). The abasement of the righteous is never the verdict on his righteousness.

threads.title: I Cry, and Thou Dost Not Hear — the Hidden Face
threads.summary_md: Job comes to the hardest place a believer knows: the cry that seems to fall back unanswered. *I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not. Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me* (Job 30:20-21). This is not the speech of an unbeliever but of faith in the dark — the same anguish the psalm of the righteous sufferer pours out: *My Elohim (God), my Elohim (God), why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?* (Psalm 22:1), *I cry in the daytime, but thou hearest not; and in the night season, and am not silent* (Psalm 22:2). Lamentations groans the same shut door: *Also when I cry and shout, he shutteth out my prayer* (Lamentations 3:8). Yet the cry is never truly lost — *The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds: and till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the Most High shall behold to judge righteously* (Ecclesiasticus 35:17). The forsaken cry finds its fullest voice and its answer in the Formed Son: *Yahusha (Jesus) cried with a loud voice, saying... My Elohim (God), my Elohim (God), why hast thou forsaken me?* (Matthew 27:46) — the One who entered the silence and was heard.

threads.title: When I Waited for Light, There Came Darkness
threads.summary_md: Job's deepest bewilderment is that his own compassion was repaid with calamity: *Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor? When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness* (Job 30:25-26). The psalmist had walked the same road — *when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth: I humbled my soul with fasting; and my prayer returned into mine own bosom* (Psalm 35:13), *I behaved myself as though he had been my friend or brother: I bowed down heavily, as one that mourneth for his mother* (Psalm 35:14) — and met only adversity from those he mourned for. The wicked's test of the just man frames the darkness from the other side: *Let us see if his words be true: and let us prove what shall happen in the end of him* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:17), *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). The righteous waits for light and is given darkness — not as the wage of his sin, but as the furnace in which his trust is proven.

threads.title: Is there any thing too hard for me? — the field bought as a sign restoration is sure
